Biological evaluations demonstrated that DPDMN-DC-DOX effectively suppresses osteosarcoma progression by enhancing intracellular reactive oxygen species generation and inducing apoptosis, while maintaining good biocompatibility. Compared to the DPDMN-DC, DPDMN-DC-DOX shows significantly enhanced antitumor efficacy, attributed to the synergistic effect of photothermal ablation and chemotherapy. In summary, this work presents a rationally designed benzobisthiazole polymer nanocarriers with temperature-responsive controlled drug release behavior, offering a promising platform for synergistic chemo-photothermal cancer therapy.

title: Cracking suppression in powder bed fusion-laser beam of CM247LC Ni-based superalloy
abstract: • Achieved virtually crack-free (0.04 mm/mm 2 ) CM247LC without preheating. • Unidirectional scanning yields a twofold smoother surface finish (Ra = 7.39 µm). • 10 × 10 mm 2 island size lowers bulk cooling rate by ∼3×, mitigating thermal stress. • Optimised strategy shifts grain boundaries from HAGBs to LAGBs (<15°). • Strong <0 0 1> texture (11.9 MUD) correlates with reduced cracking susceptibility. High γ′ Ni-based superalloys, such as CM247LC studied here, suffer from a high propensity for crack formation during additive manufacturing, hampering mission-critical applications due to poor weldability. In this work, crack suppression was achieved in CM247LC processed via Powder Bed Fusion-Laser Beam (PBF-LB) through systematic control of scanning strategies. Without compositional modification or substrate preheating, cracking density was reduced from 3.14 mm/mm 2 in the default sample to a virtually crack-free microstructure of 0.04 mm/mm 2 in the optimised sample. A twofold enhancement in surface finish was also achieved by employing a unidirectional scanning strategy, which avoids laser turn-around-induced heat accumulation and thermal stresses. The optimal strategy was designed based upon a systematic evaluation of island size, shift, rotation angle, and meander, with their impact on heat input and cooling rates rationalised using a transient finite volume temperature field simulation. The thermal model reveals that increasing island size promotes higher heat retention and lower thermal gradients, significantly mitigating cracking susceptibility. The ratio of active to inactive laser scan times was identified as a key descriptor governing crack reduction. Our work suggests that tuning scanning strategies offers a promising alternative to alloy redesign or preheating for processing crack-susceptible Ni-based superalloy CM247LC via PBF-LB

title: Inverse design of high-entropy superalloys using machine learning and generative artificial Intelligence
abstract: • End-to-end inverse design yields decision-grade HESA shortlists from data. • Creep (LMP) and oxidation ( log K A ) are optimized as first-class objectives. • Composition-only, physics-informed surrogates with descriptor and outlier control. • Feasibility floor + Pareto + Ward-medoids deliver a diverse experimental shortlist. • Conditional VAE explores new alloys under feasibility and sustainability filters. We introduce a structure-agnostic inverse-design workflow that turns heterogeneous literature and database evidence into experiment-prioritized shortlists of high-temperature high-entropy superalloy candidate chemistries. Unlike most data-driven high-entropy alloy (HEA) design studies that optimize a small set of proxies, we provide an end-to-end, reproducible decision-support loop that treats high-temperature creep and oxidation as first-class objectives and outputs compact shortlists for downstream validation. From curated multi-source data, we learn structure-agnostic, physics-informed surrogate models for the key high-temperature objectives – creep resistance (Larson–Miller parameter), oxidation kinetics (parabolic rate constant), melting point, density and elastic properties – and map predictions to “desirability” normalized scores. Candidate alloys are screened by a uniform feasibility floor and Pareto non-domination, then compressed by Ward–medoid clustering to yield compact, diversity-preserving shortlists for downstream validation. To explore beyond brute-force enumeration under the same admissibility rules, we couple the screening stage to a constraint-conditioned variational autoencoder, and retain only generated candidates that pass the full surrogate stack. The resulting compressed Pareto sets extend the occupied property envelope of legacy Ni-based superalloys while remaining interpretable through elemental-role analyses and Ashby-style trade-off maps. An external thermodynamic plausibility cross-check further shows that higher microstructure-oriented scores enrich the candidate space in single-phase HEA-compatible chemistries with wider stability windows and more favorable transition classes. Finally, we show how the same pipeline can be restricted to sustainability-compatible element pools, enabling performance-aware exploration under supply-risk and footprint constraints.

title: The effect of temperature on the mechanical properties of metal organic framework HKUST-1
abstract: This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to reveal that temperature influences the mechanical properties of HKUST – 1. • Identified three-stage stretching behavior of HKUST-1 under thermal response. • All mechanical parameters of HKUST-1 decrease with rising temperature. • High-stress atoms concentrated around Cu-centered H3BTC linkers. • Young’s modulus maximum along < 111>, minimum in < 001 > direction. • Shear modulus shows broader maximum distribution range than Young’s modulus. Elucidating the mechanical behavior of HKUST-1 under thermal response is essential for its practical applications, yet remains incompletely explored. This study employed molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the mechanical properties of HKUST-1 in response to temperature changes. The tensile process of HKUST-1 involves three distinct stages: elastic deformation, plastic deformation dominated by pore collapse and bond rupture, and fracture. While HKUST-1 exhibits flexibility, its wear and scratch resistance is weak. Elevated temperatures consistently reduce all mechanical properties of HKUST-1, including ultimate tensile strength. Under thermal stress, the HKUST-1 framework undergoes progressive degradation, where higher temperatures intensify interatomic stresses, ultimately collapsing its porous architecture. Besides, the atoms experiencing high stress are primarily located around the H 3 BTC organic linker centered on Cu. The maximum Young’s modulus of HKUST-1 is observed along the < 111 > crystallographic direction, whereas the minimum occurs along the < 001 > orientation. The shear modulus exhibits its maximum value between the < 001 > and < 011 > directions, displaying a broader distribution range of maximum compared with the Young’s modulus. This study provides insights into the mechanical mechanisms of HKUST-1 under thermal stress by analyzing parameter evolution and microscale stress distributions. The obtained results provide numerical predictions for its engineering applications in different temperatures.

title: Additive manufacturing of polymer-derived SiOC(Fe) ceramic composites as a catalyst support exhibiting magnetic heating capability
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) of advanced functional ceramics using preceramic polymers (PCPs) is gaining attention due to its processability and tailorable properties. A photosensitive resin with iron-modified polysiloxanes was developed for vat photopolymerization (VPP) to create porous SiOC(Fe) catalytic supports with magnetic heating capability. Ferric acetylacetonate and ferrocene were examined as iron precursors, leading to the formation of Fe-based magnetic particles (α-Fe, Fe 3 C, Fe x Si y ) within the silicon oxycarbide (SiOC) ceramic matrix after pyrolysis at 800 to 1500 °C. Depending on the Fe-based precursor used and the applied pyrolysis temperature, the obtained monoliths exhibited magnetic nanoparticle (MNP) contents ranging from 0.9 to 7.9 wt%, with particle sizes from 17 to 96 nm. The monolithic catalyst supports fabricated from ferric acetylacetonate modified PCP-based resin formulations, pyrolyzed at 900 °C, exhibited the highest specific absorption rate and resulted in magnetic heating up to 200 °C at an applied external magnetic field of 60 kA·m −1 . While catalyst supports fabricated from ferrocene modified PCP-based resin formulations had lower heating capabilities, they offered better printability and higher ceramic yield. In situ formed MNPs impart magnetic properties advantageous for catalyst support heating, highlighting AM’s design flexibility and PCPs’ role in creating tailored, lightweight structures with controlled porosity.

title: A new approach to enhance the efficiency of local squeezing during high pressure die casting of aluminum alloys
abstract: • New approach to squeeze pin parameters enhances queezing efficiency in high pressure die casting. • The stroke of the squeeze pin provides details of solid fraction in the squeezed region. • Squeeze pin velocity is more important than the delay time for EN AC 46000 alloy during squeezing. • Reduced squeeze velocity can provide stable mechanical properties independent of delay time. High Pressure Die Casting (HPDC) produces near-net-shape components with varying wall thicknesses, leading to heterogeneous solidification conditions. These effects led to inhomogeneities, which significantly affect mechanical properties. Local squeezing is a standard approach for minimising shrinkage porosity. We applied local squeezing at the industrial standard and at two magnitudes lower speeds: 27.5 mm/s and 0.7 mm/s. We varied the delay time, a typically used parameter in industrial practice, between 0.0 and 3.0 s. During the intervention, we recorded the complete motion curve of the squeezing pin. We took a sample from the squeezed volume and characterised its porosity distribution by density measurements, computed tomography, and scanning electron microscopy. The tensile strength of the squeezed volume was also measured. From the results, we concluded that the squeeze pin movement speed has a much stronger effect on the success of squeezing, i.e., the reduction of porosity. Based on microstructural examinations, we showed that the key to successful squeezing is selecting the optimal melt-to-solid ratio, which correlates with the maximum distance the squeeze pin travels. These results contribute significantly to the development of a monitoring system that can increase squeezing efficiency by orders of magnitude compared to current industrial practice.

title: Self-Sensing SMA-Textile Composite Actuator for Multi-Mode Actuation
abstract: In this study, a self-sensing soft actuator was developed by integrating shape memory alloy (SMA) wires and conductive fabric into a PDMS matrix, enabling simultaneous actuation and sensing. Bending, twisting and combined deformation modes were achieved by varying the SMA wire arrangement and the fabric sensor pattern, and the corresponding resistance changes are quantitatively characterized. The results demonstrate a consistent correlation between resistance change and both bending curvature and twist angle, with stable response characteristics maintained under repeated actuating conditions. Sensor performance was further evaluated based on response time, gauge factor, and hysteresis. Moreover, the proposed actuator was applied as a soft gripper and gripping experiments on various objects were conducted and it was confirmed that real-time resistance change can be detected concurrently with actuation. This study provides a technical foundation for soft robotic and smart material applications requiring deformation detection and real-time feedback control.

title: Low temperature hot melt extrusion of polycaprolactone/polyethylene oxide/chitosan ternary blends for biocompatible implantable device development
abstract: Rising demand for biomedical devices requires manufacturing approaches suitable for processing thermally-sensitive materials. Hot-melt extrusion may cause thermal degradation of polymers and bioactives. This study examines low-temperature hot-melt extrusion (LT-HME) as an alternative processing method for blends of polycaprolactone, polyethylene oxide, and chitosan (PCL/PEO/Cs), fabricated using a twin-screw extruder under reduced temperatures. Extrudates were characterised using scanning electron microscopy, gel permeation chromatography, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, and rheology. LT-HME enabled melt-blending with reduced torque and no chemical degradation or adverse intermolecular interactions. Thermal analysis revealed a modest reduction in PCL melting temperature and crystallinity across blended systems without evidence of complete amorphisation miscibility. Composition-dependent morphological variations were demonstrated, including phase separation and void formation in blends containing PEO and/or Cs, with ternary blends exhibiting comparatively improved structural uniformity and interfacial adhesion relative to binary blends. Rheological measurements showed enhancements in storage and loss moduli and complex viscosity, particularly for the A3 ternary composition, indicating altered melt behaviour during extrusion. The results provide an initial insight into the processing behaviour of PCL/PEO/Cs ternary blends via LT-HME. This supports further investigation into multi-component polymer systems including optimising formulation parameters, robust structural validation and biocompatibility studies for potential biomedical applications.

title: Machine learning–enabled intelligent hydrogels: applications and future perspectives
abstract: Hydrogels are increasingly used in flexible electronics, biomedicine, and soft robotics due to their tissue-like mechanics, high water content, stimuli responsiveness, and programmable structures. At the same time, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) are accelerating hydrogel design, signal processing, and intelligent control. This review presents an integrated framework linking hydrogel materials, flexible/wearable sensing, and ML-enabled analysis and optimization, distinguishing it from previous reviews on general hydrogel design or isolated ML applications. Recent progress is summarized in flexible sensing, health monitoring, drug delivery, cell behavior analysis, and soft robotics. Current challenges and future opportunities are discussed, particularly in data standardization, model generalizability, multimodal fusion, and closed-loop intelligent systems.

title: Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids: rational structural design and structure-property relationships for biomedical applications
abstract: Achieving nanoscale precision in structural design remains a formidable challenge for traditional non-structural delivery systems. Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (tFNAs), characterized their the atomically precise 10-nm pyramidal architecture, have emerged as a versatile molecular chassis to overcome these constraints. Herein, we elucidate the structural design and structure–property relationships of tFNA. Initial discussions define the physicochemical foundation of tFNA, focusing on how their programmable self-assembly dictates mechanical rigidity and enzymatic stability. Building on these attributes, the engineering of bio-nano interfaces is analyzed, detailing how tFNA scaffolds exercise out-of-plane entropic control to optimize probe orientation and in-plane spatial patterning to orchestrate multivalent recognition in diagnostic sensing. Furthermore, therapeutic strategies are categorized by cargo requirements and material evolution, spanning static scaffolds, dynamic responsive systems, and integrated macroscopic hydrogels. Finally, critical hurdles in clinical translation are discussed, along with proposed material-based countermeasures to facilitate the transition of these nanostructures from laboratory research to clinical paradigms.

title: Effect of sintering process on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the B4C ceramics with Si additive
abstract: The effects of sintering temperature, pressure and content of Si on the phase composition, microstructure and mechanical properties of the B 4 C ceramics sintered by spark plasma sintering (SPS) were investigated. Results show that the sintering temperature illustrates the ultimate effect of relative density and microhardness, the Si content shows the maximum effect of bending strength and the pressure shows the most effect on fracture toughness. The optimal comprehensive mechanical properties of the B 4 C ceramics reached when the sintering temperature is 1800℃ and the pressure is 60 MPa with 15 vol% Si, The fracture toughness could reach 6.89 MPa·m 1/2 , which is improved 130%-245% than pure B 4 C ceramics. Partial decomposition of B 4 C occurred during the sintering process, resulting in the precipitation of carbon, which in-situ react to Si generating the SiC. The sintering could be divided into the initial (0–600 s), mid (600–1200 s) and final stages (after 1200 s), where the mid stage shows the fastest densification. The combination of transgranular and intergranular fractures illustrates during the bending fracture of B 4 C, while the stacking fault in the formed SiC. Both of which could consume more energy during the prolongation of cracks, resulting in the improvement of fracture toughness.

title: Microstructural effects of tungsten deposition on 415 steel during PBF-LB/M additive manufacturing of plasma facing components
abstract: Microstructure and mechanical properties of tungsten/415 stainless steel samples manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion (PBF-LB/M) were investigated. The effect of W processing parameters on the microstructure development at and in the vicinity of the steel-W interface was studied by chemical imaging techniques, in particular scanning micro X-ray diffraction (µXRD) and micro X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) imaging. The microstructure at the interface between tungsten and steel was analyzed using Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) and XRD, and the formation of crytalline phases in the area of the interface was also analyzed by operando XRD measurements. Finally, neutron Bragg-edge imaging (NBEI) was used to investigate the residual strains in the steel domain of the resulting multimaterial components. Using this complementary array of physical and chemical imaging techniques allowed to identify distinct zones with characteristic dimensions and properties depending on the laser manufacturing parameters. XRD scanning imaging showed the formation of retained austenite (RA) within the lower interface region, reaching up to 1 wt.\% locally and 0.4wt.\% average. The NBEI measurements probing full size samples revealed that lattice expansion was visible further from the interface, in the region where no chemical changes could be observed.

title: Preparation and comprehensive characterisation of microwave heat treated soft magnetic Fe@MgO composites
abstract: Soft magnetic composites (SMCs) are essential for electromagnetic devices requiring high electrical resistivity and low magnetic losses. The current demand for cost-effective and energy-efficient materials drives research to enhance their characteristics towards more sustainable solutions. Fe@MgO composites were prepared by dry particle coating and subjected to microwave heat treatment at 600°C with varying MgO contents (2–5 wt%), Both preparation techniques represent the progressive – ecologically and economically beneficial ones. Microstructural analyses revealed the formation of a non-stoichiometric magnesia-ferrite spinel interphase. Increasing MgO content decreased elastic moduli and permeability while enhancing electrical resistivity and coercivity, affecting magnetic domain wall movability and losses. Microwave-treated composites exhibited improved complex permeability and frequency stability compared to conventionally treated samples, indicating a presence of a ferrimagnetic phase as well, which enables magnetic flux continuity at the insulation layer. Notably, 2–3 wt% MgO yielded low DC hysteresis losses and higher permeability, whereas 5 wt% MgO optimised AC losses and DC-bias stability (∼80% at 40 Oe). These findings demonstrate that microwave processing effectively tailors microstructure and magnetic properties, offering a versatile approach to optimise Fe@MgO SMCs for specific electromagnetic applications.

title: Carburisation and oxidation driven erosion of electroplated chromium in a large-calibre artillery barrel
abstract: Chromium electroplating is widely used to enhance erosion resistance and extend service life-time of artillery barrels. In the present study, the mechanism for premature erosion of an electroplated artillery layer was systematically investigated after firing tests by using a combination of electron and ion microscopy. Spallation of chromium layer is closely related with propagation of erosion attack along the chromium-steel interface and the underlying steel matrix upon growth of erosion damage. The pre-existing micro-cracks in electroplated chromium act as the preferential pathways for penetration of erosive propellant gas, facilitating rapid crack propagation. Growth and coalescence of pre-existing micro-cracks further lead to formation of micro-cracks penetrating through the entire thickness of chromium layer, facilitating erosion attack along the chromium-steel interface and the underlying steel matrix upon the presence of erosive propellant gas. Propagation of erosion attack along the interface was initiated by preferential carburisation of chromium layer leading to non-equilibrium M 7 C 3 carbides formation. This further facilitates rapid propagation of erosion attack along the interface and in the adjacent steel matrix via a combination of non-equilibrium carburisation and oxidation processes. The growth of interfacial erosion damage and subsurface erosion pits both contribute to spallation of chromium layer via a decohesion mechanism.

title: Excellent superplasticity at 800 ℃ achieved via Low-temperature rolling in a novel Ti-44Al-1.5Cr-0.5Re alloy
abstract: This study investigates the microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of a novel Ti-44Al-1.5Cr-0.5Re alloy sheet processed by hot rolling at temperatures ranging from 1050°C to 1250°C. Results demonstrate that rolling at 1050°C, near the eutectoid temperature, leads to significant grain refinement with an average grain size of 2.31 μm, attributed to the combined effects of particle-stimulated nucleation (PSN) and α₂ twinning-induced fragmentation. The refined microstructure contributes to exceptional superplasticity at 800°C, exhibiting an elongation of 140% alongside a tensile strength of 472 MPa. Microstructural analysis reveals that the grain refinement mechanism under low-temperature, high-stress rolling involves the decomposition of α2 and βo phases into finely dispersed particles, which promote dynamic recrystallization of the γ phase via PSN effect, while repeated α2 twinning leads to continuous grain subdivision. This work provides a viable low-temperature rolling strategy for producing fine-grained TiAl sheets with excellent superplasticity, offering significant potential for energy-efficient forming of aerospace components.

title: A comprehensive DFT study of XFe3H8 (X = Mg, Na, Sr) intermetallic hydrides for hydrogen storage applications
abstract: The structural, electronic, elastic, phonon, and thermodynamic properties of intermetallic hydrides XFe3H8 (X = Mg, Na, and Sr) were comprehensively analyzed using ab-initio calculations. The investigated intermetallic hydrides are stable in the cubic phase with space group Pm3m. For these intermetallic hydride compounds, which adopt a stable cubic configuration, the spin-polarized band structure exhibits a pronounced metallic character, characterized by the complete absence of a band gap. A detailed analysis of the total and partial density of states (PDOS) corroborates this metallicity by revealing a pronounced peak at the Fermi level. The mechanical stability of the compounds studied here is verified by the calculated elastic constants satisfying the Born stability criteria. These compounds demonstrate ductile behavior, as evidenced by the predicted values of Pugh’s ratio, Poisson’s ratio, and Cauchy pressure. In addition, the 2D and 3D plots of Young’s modulus (E), shear modulus (G), and Poisson’s ratio (ν) reveal anisotropy for XFe3H8. The analysis of phonon dispersion relations and the corresponding density of states reveals that all compounds possess only positive phonon frequencies, confirming their dynamical stability in the cubic phase. Owing to their moderate gravimetric hydrogen densities—3.887 wt%, 3.902 wt%, and 2.972 wt% for MgFe3H8, NaFe3H8, and SrFe3H8, respectively—these hydrides may be employed in hydrogen-storage applications. The evaluated mechanical characteristics indicate that these materials could serve as promising candidates for hydrogen storage applications.

title: Temperature-dependent deformation mechanisms influenced by the μ phase TCP in a Ni-based single crystal superalloy
abstract: The influence of the plate-like μ phases precipitates in Ni-based single-crystal superalloys on their mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms was systematically investigated over a range of temperatures (25–700 °C) using multi-scale mechanical testing together with electron microscopy-based microstructure analysis. Macro-scale compression tests provided insights into the bulk mechanical performance, whereas in situ scanning electron microscope (SEM) micropillar tests enabled direct comparison of local deformation behaviors between μ phase-containing and μ phase-free regions. The results demonstrated that at room temperature, the μ phase remained undeformed and acted as an effective barrier to { 111 } γ / γ ′ slip propagation. However, at elevated temperatures ( ≥ 500 °C), the μ phase exhibited distinct deformation modes, including bending and shearing along non-basal planes. In contrast to the temperature-dependent deformation behavior, the critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) of micropillars consistently decreased in the presence of μ phases, irrespective of temperature. This indicates that the observed CRSS reduction likely originated from microstructural changes in the surrounding γ/γ’ rather than from deformation of the μ phase itself. This work clearly demonstrates temperature-dependent deformation behavior of the μ phase formed in Ni-based single-crystal superalloys and provides insights into a guidance for microstructural control and enhanced material reliability in high-temperature applications.

title: Ultralight electrospun nanofibrous aerogels as shape-stabilizing matrices for high-loading paraffin-based phase change materials
abstract: Electrospun nanofibrous aerogels (NFAs) were strategically employed as a lightweight, porous supporting matrix to fabricate shape-stabilized composite phase change materials (PCMs) with exceptionally high paraffin wax (PW) loading. NFAs of tunable density were fabricated via a synergistic process combining high-speed emulsification, freeze-drying, and thermal crosslinking, using electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN)/benzoxazine (BA-a) nanofibrous membranes integrated with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) as precursors. The microstructure, shape stability, thermal energy storage capacity, thermal reliability, and thermal conductivity of the resulting PW/NFA composites were systematically evaluated. The NFAs exhibit an ultralow-density, hierarchically interconnected three-dimensional porous architecture, which enables effective control over PW incorporation by adjusting aerogel density. Notably, a maximum PW mass fraction of 98% was achieved without any leakage. Thermal analysis confirms that the composite PCMs exhibit excellent thermal energy storage and release capabilities, with phase change enthalpies approaching those of pure PW, along with outstanding thermal reliability and stability. Furthermore, the incorporation of CNT-reinforced NFAs enhances the thermal conductivity of the composite by 125.30% relative to pure PW. Infrared thermal imaging and time–temperature response tests collectively validate the superior heat transfer efficiency and practical applicability of these shape-stabilized PCMs in thermal management systems.

title: Parametric control of Poisson’s ratio in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) based re-entrant auxetic structures for stretchable devices application
abstract: Auxetic structures have significant potential for stretchable devices, such as flexible displays, circuits, and sensors, due to their remarkable self-deformation characteristics. However, in practical embedded systems, the mechanical response is governed not solely by the auxetic structure (AS). The mechanical behavior mismatch due to the interaction between the AS and the surrounding matrix can degrade the desired auxetic effect. Therefore, this study proposes an effective methodology to investigate a matrix-embedded Re-entrant Auxetic Cellular Structure (RACS) design, focusing on the parametric influence of key geometrical factors to achieve the desired and controlled mechanical performance for stretchable devices. A comprehensive parametric analysis, using single-unit RACS and multiple-cell RACS array configurations, is performed through simulation and experimental comparison. The results identify horizontal rib thickness as the dominant design parameter significantly affecting Poisson’s ratio, while other geometric parameters contribute comparatively minor effects. The findings provide a practical design strategy for tailoring AS in matrix-embedded systems, addressing scalability challenges and advancing their applicability in next-generation flexible devices.

title: Unexpectedly large intra-grain crystal rotations in CVD-grown (Ti,Al)N coatings and their relation to internal nanolamella structures
abstract: The crystal growth direction within a single grain is typically assumed to be uniform. However, this study presents the first observation of spontaneous intra-grain crystal rotations in (Ti,Al)N grains with an internal nanolamella structure. The rotation occurs during grain growth in a chemical vapor deposition process. The crystal rotations exhibit a highly symmetrical pattern linked to the (Ti,Al)N grain morphology: a pyramid comprising three {001}-faceted domains. The crystal lattices systematically rotate within each domain toward the pyramid tip, with the largest rotations concentrated at the pyramid edges. Within a single (Ti,Al)N grain, the crystal orientation can shift up to 15° from base to tip, with a typical gradient of 1°/µm. The gradient reaches a peak of 3 – 4 °/µm in the horizontal direction near the pyramid edges. This is attributed to the high density of grown-in dislocations, arising from interface mismatches between the (Ti,Al)N grain domains and hexagonal AlN nano-precipitates that form at the domain boundaries. Analysis of (Ti,Al)N samples with varying nanolamella structures reveals that the presence of more nanolamellae corresponds to larger crystal rotations. These findings provide useful insights into controlling crystal rotation and its potential influence on material properties, opening new avenues for materials design..

title: Influence of wood hardness on the shear strength performance of friction stir spot welding joints with a Nylon-66 interlayer
abstract: To address the challenge of interfacial incompatibility and brittle failure in wood-metal hybrid structures, this study investigates a friction-based joining method using Nylon-66 as a thermoplastic bridging agent between AA6061 aluminum alloy and various wood species. The joints were fabricated via Friction Stir Spot Welding techniques, focusing on the mechanical interlocking and chemical bonding facilitated by the nylon interface. The research revealed that the optimized AA6061-Beech joint achieved a peak shear tensile strength of 10.43 MPa. A transition from brittle separation to a controlled, ductile-like failure mode was discovered. Unlike conventional joints, the nylon-bridged interface maintained a sustained load-bearing capacity exceeding 400 N even after the initial peak load. This phenomenon is attributed to the elongation of the nylon bridge, which effectively absorbs energy and prevents sudden structural collapse. This study demonstrates that thermoplastic bridging is a viable strategy for creating high-strength, safety-enhanced wood-metal joints for green manufacturing.

title: Laser-scanning of induction-melted Al-Zr-Er-Ni alloys: are they representative of additively manufactured ones?
abstract: The alloy design for powder-based additive manufacturing (AM) bottlenecks at customized powder production, which is expensive and slow, hindering closed-loop AM alloy development. This study evaluates multi-track laser scanning of induction-melted samples as a rapid experimental workflow to down-select the design space and assesses whether they reproduce AM-like rapid-solidification microstructures across different length scales. A newly developed coarsening-resistant AM Al-Zr-Er-Ni alloy is used as a model system, and multiscale characterizations compare laser-scanned and LPBF samples. Although differences appear at the microscale, higher-resolution SEM (∼10 1 µm) and TEM (nanometer scale) reveal similar phase morphology and distribution, particularly the nearly identical composition and size of L1 2 phase which contributes to ∼80% of the strength. Microhardness was 23% lower in laser-scanned samples. A similar trend was observed in an Al-Ni-Zr-Er-Y-Yb benchmark alloy, with a 29% microhardness reduction in the laser-scanned sample. We demonstrate that laser scanning is effective for screening of phase formation, nanoscale strengthening features, and comparative microhardness trends, but does not reproduce LPBF-equivalent melt-pool geometry, grain structure, or the direct value of mechanical properties. This work evaluates a rapid, cost-effective pathway for early-stage AM alloy development in the Al-Zr-Er-Ni alloy system and motivates validation across broader alloy systems and processing conditions.

title: Optimizing austempering for lower bainite formation in DC53 steel: mechanisms for enhanced strength and toughness
abstract: This study aims to enhance the strength-toughness properties of DC53 cold work die steel by optimizing the austempering process. Compared to high-temperature tempering, the optimal austempering process increases unnotched impact toughness from 32.8 J/cm 2 to 41.3 J/cm 2 while maintaining a hardness of 61.9 HRC. The simultaneous reduction of the coefficient of friction from 0.674 to 0.621 and the decrease of the volume wear rate from 5.52 × 10 −8 to 3.80 × 10 −8 mm 3 ·N −1 ·m −1 suggest an enhancement in wear resistance. It was attributed to the formation of lower bainite, which exhibited in an acicular morphology and partitioned the prior austenite grains. It can disperse stress concentration similar to the prior austenite grain boundary, thereby reducing the formation of secondary cracks. The film-like retained austenite, distributs along the sides of lower bainite, exhibits high thermodynamic stability. The microstructural features exhibit a synergistic interaction resulting in superior comprehensive performance.

title: Preparation of the high mechanical and damping performance Mg-Y-Zn alloys with three Y/Zn ratios using the hot extrusion deformation process
abstract: To develop magnesium alloys with both excellent mechanical and damping properties, three Mg–Y–Zn alloys with varying Y/Zn ratios (Mg 95 Y 3 Zn 2 , Mg 95 Y 3.5 Zn 1.5 , Mg 95 Y 3.8 Zn 1.2 (at.%)) were innovatively designed based on an arithmetic progression. Correspondingly, three different contents of the long-period stacked ordered (LPSO) phase were introduced. The alloys were prepared and deformed, followed by microstructural characterization and evaluation of mechanical and damping properties. The results show that the extruded Mg 95 Y 3.5 Zn 1.5 alloy demonstrates superior mechanical performance with UTS of 461 MPa and elongation of 10.3%. For the damping capacity, under testing conditions of ε = 0.1% and f = 1 Hz, the Q⁻ 1 value of all three as-cast alloys exceeds 0.05, while that of the three extruded alloys also exceeds 0.01. The alloy achieves a balance between damping and mechanical properties, driven by four synergistic mechanisms: dislocation dynamics, bimodal grain structure, interfacial characteristics, and intrinsic deformation of the LPSO phase. This work provides valuable guidance for the design of lightweight magnesium alloys with high properties, which are promising candidates for vibration-damping components in aerospace and transportation applications.

title: PCN-224 engineered self-amplifying nanoplatform for TME responsive multimodal imaging and in situ vaccinated combined therapy
abstract: Breast cancer remains a major clinical challenge due to its high incidence, tumor heterogeneity, hypoxia, and limited treatment specificity. In this study, we developed PMDH, a six-in-one integrated nanoplatform for targeted multimodal imaging and combined therapy. PMDH was constructed by sequentially coating a MnO 2 shell on PCN–224, loading doxorubicin (DOX), and conjugating hyaluronic acid (HA). The system features complementary tumor microenvironment (TME) responsive imaging modalities, including fluorescence imaging, magnetic resonance imaging, and photoacoustic imaging for precise diagnostics. Therapeutically, PMDH enables controlled DOX release for chemotherapy, self-enhanced photodynamic therapy (PDT) through intratumoral oxygen generation, and PDT-triggered immunotherapy. These integrated capabilities were comprehensively validated through in vitro and in vivo studies, underscoring PMDH’s potential as a versatile and precise platform for oncology treatment.

title: Binder-free 3D printing of ceramics via shear-induced colloidal assembly
abstract: Shaping ceramics with complex geometries using low-cost and simple additive processes is interesting for many applications but remains challenging. One simple known process is the direct ink writing, which relies on extrusion of a paste deposited layer by layer to create an object. However, the upstream formulation of the ink is often complicated and usually requires polymer additives. In this study, a novel extrusion printing process based on dynamic colloidal assembly in a microfluidic channel is introduced. The raw materials consist of two colloidal suspensions, one containing positively charged particles and the other containing negatively charged particles. When introduced into a microfluidic channel, they naturally self-assemble to form a printable filament. Numerical simulations reveal that this filament results from complex dynamic effects due to suspension flows. This new process uses feedstock prepared with no or few polymer additives, which offers a cost-effective and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional methods.

title: IF steel shim-assisted process to improve mechanical behaviour of Sn-containing hot stamping steel resistance spot weld joint
abstract: The steel industry’s shift towards scrap-based, low-carbon steelmaking introduces residual Sn, which compromises the resistance spot weldability of advanced hot-stamping steels essential for automotive lightweighting. This study investigates the impact of Sn on the mechanical properties of such welds and evaluates a shim-assisted RSW (SA-RSW) process using an interstitial-free steel shim for mitigation. Increasing Sn content degraded the cross-tension performance, with a critical content of 0.05% causing a transition from the desirable pull-out fracture to partial interface fracture and a 20% reduction in peak load, primarily due to Sn segregation. The SA-RSW process effectively diluted Sn concentration in the fusion zone by ∼66%, restoring the pull-out fracture mode. However, it concentrated residual stress near the fusion line, leading to cleavage brittle fracture and reduced displacement, which diminished energy absorption despite Sn-induced strengthening increasing the peak load. Based on these results, a practical selection strategy is proposed. Using conventional RSW for Sn content below 0.05%, and adopting the SA-RSW process for Sn content at or above 0.05%. This work provides insights into Sn-induced embrittlement and a viable joining strategy for sustainable manufacturing.

title: A novel transforming mechanical metastructure capable of shape morphing and locking
abstract: Shape morphing structures are rapidly appearing at the frontiers of sciences and technologies, yet it is challenging for them to retain their shapes and sustain loads. This paper introduces a novel transforming mechanical meta structure (TMMS) capable of shape morphing and locking. Periodically arranging unit cells and modularly assembling, the TMMS can be fabricated into the customized array in a fast and simple way. Deformation actuating and state switching are imposed through mechanical mechanisms for high reliability. For the morphing behaviors, theoretical analysis is carried out to address the kinematical properties, which shows good agreements with experiments. Meanwhile, mechanical tests are performed to validate the shape locking capacities. The analytical models provide a feasible scheme to determine the configuration of the TMMS, and thereby an optimization scheme for accurate shape fitting is developed. This TMMS concept offers a promising viewpoint to develop shape morphing structures and demonstrates outstanding potentials in a wide range of industrial applications.

title: A salidroside-mediated injectable hydrogel microsphere combining immunomodulatory and reactive oxygen species scavenging for delaying intervertebral disc degeneration
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD)-associated low back pain represents a substantial global health challenge with profound socioeconomic consequences. The dysregulated immune microenvironment in degenerated discs creates a hostile milieu that suppresses tissue repair. In this study, we engineered a hierarchical delivery platform where salidroside (SAL)-functionalized Prussian blue analogues (PBA) were electrostatically assembled into gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel microspheres. The system enables spatiotemporally controlled SAL release by combining PBA-mediated molecular loading with GelMA microsphere-based sustained delivery reservoirs. These functionalized hydrogel microspheres serve as fundamental regulatory units for the IVDD immune microenvironment, enabling minimally invasive treatment of IVDD. In vitro experiments revealed that functionalized hydrogel microspheres effectively promoted the activation of macrophages towards the reparative sentinel M2 phenotype, scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), and improved extracellular matrix (ECM) metabolism. In vivo studies further revealed that the functionalized hydrogel microspheres significantly restored intervertebral disc height, water content, and tissue structure in a rat IVDD model, while also enhancing ECM repair and suppressing inflammation. This study provides a novel therapeutic strategy for immunomodulation and tissue repair in degenerative disc diseases, with potential for future clinical translation.

title: Tailoring intermetallic compounds for corrosion resistance of AlSi10MnMg aluminum alloy via different cooling media after solution treatment
abstract: AlSi10MnMg (AA365) alloy is valued for its corrosion resistance, castability, excellent mechanical properties, and low density, making it attractive for high-pressure die-cast (HPDC) automotive structural components. Despite its broad industrial adoption, the behavior of AA365 in corrosive environments remains comparatively underexplored, particularly with respect to the roles of heat treatment and intermetallic compounds in governing localized corrosion. This work addresses that gap by investigating the electrochemical response of AA365 in conjunction with microstructural evolution controlled by different cooling media after solution treatment. The influence of cooling condition on the type, distribution, and electrochemical activity of intermetallic compounds at or near the surface is evaluated, and these features are linked to corrosion initiation and propagation via micro-galvanic interactions in marine-relevant environments. The findings elucidate the relationships among processing, microstructure, and corrosion mechanisms in AA365, providing guidance for alloy and process optimization. Ultimately, this study supports more reliable applications of AA365 in automotive and marine applications by linking microstructural control to improved corrosion performance.

title: Design and fabrication of 3D-printed structural supercapacitors with vertically aligned carbon nanotube-enhanced carbon fibers
abstract: This study presents a novel hierarchical strategy for the design and manufacture of sustainable complex-shaped Structural Supercapacitors (SSCs) via an additive manufacturing approach using vertically aligned carbon nanotube (VACNT)-functionalized carbon fiber electrodes. The SSC core, based on a poly(vinyl alcohol)-NaCl gel polymer electrolyte, is integrated within a load-bearing polyethylene terephthalate glycol-modified carbon fiber (PETG-CF) reinforcement hull. While the VACNT functionalization effectively boosted the component-level integral specific capacitance to 5.75F/g, the process induced a 70% reduction in fiber’s tensile strength. This limitation was mitigated through topology optimization, which minimized the composite reinforcement hull mass while ensuring the required structural integrity for complex geometries. Additive-manufacturing successfully overcomes the geometric constraints of traditional lamination methods. However, the study identifies a manufacturing bottleneck: device performance (415 µF/g) was limited by process losses, specifically high current collector contact resistance and gel polymer swelling-induced short-circuiting. A demonstrated closed-loop system, including the mechanical recycling of the PETG-CF hull and chemical recovery of the water-soluble PVA, establishes a strong sustainability profile for this novel multifunctional composite system. This work provides a scalable pathway for designing weight-efficient, energy-storing structures in aerospace and automotive applications.

title: Adobe-inspired hydrogel with antibacterial and angiogenic functions for osteoporotic bone defect repair
abstract: Nowadays, the rapid development of tissue engineering technology has provided more treatment options for bone defect repair, but the osteoporotic bone defect repair remains a major challenge. In this study, QTH@PPO (QCS/TA/HA@PCL/PLGA/OGP) hydrogel for osteoporotic bone defect repair was developed. In ancient times, sand or lime was added to traditional straw-adobe to make the adobe stronger. Inspired by this adobe improvement method, novel composite hydrogel was prepared in this study by incorporating coaxial electrospun fibers and HA particles into the hydrogel. This method endows the hydrogel with enhanced mechanical properties and drug release functionality that meets the requirements for bone defect repair, while the hydrogel still maintains excellent porosity and biocompatibility. In vitro experiments showed that QTH@PPO exhibited the ability to promote cell proliferation and migration, also had excellent antibacterial activity and angiogenic ability. In vivo experiments demonstrated that QTH@PPO promoted immunomodulation, angiogenesis, and osteogenic differentiation under osteoporotic conditions, ultimately facilitated bone defect repair. QTH@PPO can meet the mechanical strength requirements for osteoporotic bone defect repair and the temporal requirements for drug release, while also exhibiting excellent antibacterial properties. Therefore, the design of QTH@PPO provides a promising strategy for osteoporotic bone defect repair.

title: Mechanism of carbon anode sticking during baking: Effect of volatile partial pressure
abstract: In primary aluminum production, anode sticking is a recurrent problem in carbon anode baking, characterized by adhesion of adjacent anodes or sticking of packing coke to anode surfaces. One explanation involves local variation in the efficiency of volatile extraction, where increased volatile residence time and partial pressure in the packing coke might promote their condensation. This study investigates the influence of volatile partial pressure on condensation behavior within a coke bed during pitch pyrolysis. Nitrogen was injected into a closed system at controlled flow rates to regulate volatile partial pressure. Gas composition was measured using Micro-GC, while the processed coke was evaluated through visual inspection, physical characterization, and surface chemical analysis. Results showed severe coke sticking, substantial mass gain from condensed volatiles, and the lowest pycnometer and real densities under high volatile partial pressure. Thick deposits of condensed volatiles were observed within coke pores, with their thickness decreasing as volatile partial pressure decreased. Baking experiments on cored anodes using different chamber sizes and packing coke permeabilities further confirmed the direct role of volatile partial pressure in anode sticking. These findings demonstrate that volatile partial pressure governs volatile condensation and constitute a key mechanism contributing to anode sticking.

title: Tunable elastic modulus of Ti6Al4V bio-inspired lattices fabricated by laser powder bed fusion for biomedical applications
abstract: Conventional metallic bone implants often suffer from stress-shielding and limited mechanical adaptability, necessitating the development of biomimetic lattice structures with tunable properties. In this study, a novel Ti6Al4V bio-inspired lattice, termed RaLak, was proposed to mimic bone architecture. The corresponding lattices, with relative densities of 20% and 30% and unit cell sizes of 2–4 mm, were fabricated using laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) technology. Through experimental investigations, a comprehensive analysis was conducted to evaluate the mechanical behaviour of the proposed lattice in comparison with conventional triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattices. The results indicate that the RaLak lattice exhibits enhanced mechanical performance, achieving an improved balance between stiffness and energy absorption relative to gyroid and diamond TPMS lattices. In particular, the energy absorption of RaLak shows an improvement of approximately 50% compared to the gyroid lattice at 30% RD with a 4 mm cell size. This behaviour is attributed to its hybrid architecture, which promotes more uniform stress distribution and progressive deformation. Furthermore, modified Gibson-Ashby based models were developed to establish relationships between lattice geometry and mechanical response. The proposed design strategy enables effective tuning of mechanical properties, demonstrating strong potential for load-bearing biomedical applications.

title: Inverse design of a thermally self-adaptive carbon fiber acoustic metastructure using a residual MLP architecture
abstract: To address the dual challenges of low-frequency and broadband noise mitigation in variable-temperature aerospace environments, this study proposes an intelligent inverse design framework that integrates a deep residual multilayer perceptron (Res-MLP) surrogate model with a genetic algorithm (GA) optimizer. The resulting thermally self-adaptive carbon-fiber acoustic metastructure (TS-CFAM) employs embedded shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators to convert ambient thermal stimuli into controlled mechanical displacement, thereby enabling real-time reconfiguration of its resonant microarchitecture and overcoming the fixed-bandwidth limitation inherent to conventional passive acoustic metamaterials. Numerical and experimental results confirm that the Res-MLP surrogate model accurately captures the high-dimensional, strongly nonlinear acoustic–thermal–mechanical coupling, achieving a test-set coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.99. Validation further demonstrates that TS-CFAM delivers a continuous thermal frequency-tuning range of 1240 Hz—spanning 620 Hz to 1860 Hz—over the 30–50 °C operational range. Under weighted multi-objective optimization, the framework attains a 14.23% reduction in total structural mass and a 33.30% decrease in radial thickness, while sustaining an average sound absorption coefficient above 0.88 across the target band. Collectively, this work establishes a scalable, physics-informed digital design paradigm for structural–functional integration in next-generation aviation noise-mitigation systems.

title: Nanozymes in cardiovascular diseases: from mechanisms to translational applications
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the main cause of death and disability worldwide. Existing drug treatments have limitations such as poor targeting, limited efficacy, safety problems, and low patient compliance. Nanozymes, a type of nanomaterial with natural enzyme-like catalytic activity, have shown considerable promise in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases in recent years due to their high stability, designability, and good biocompatibility. This review offers a comprehensive overview of the therapeutic mechanisms and the progress in the application of nanozymes in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Nanozymes can efficiently scavenge ROS, regulate oxidative stress and inflammatory response, inhibit apoptosis and abnormal fibrosis, and promote angiogenesis and myocardial repair by mimicking the activities of antioxidant enzymes such as SOD and CAT. Nanozymes can also be utilized as intelligent drug delivery vehicles to achieve targeted thrombolysis, regulate the plaque microenvironment, and integrate diagnosis and treatment. Here, we systematically reviewed and analyzed the related studies in recent years, and introduced the development, classification, and role of nanozymes in a variety of CVDs. In addition, the potential of nanozymes in clinical applications is discussed, hoping to provide new strategies for the precision treatment of CVDs in the future.

title: Influence of molecular weight on the printability and piezoelectric morphology of melt-based 3D printed poly-L-lactic acid
abstract: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printing has been demonstrated capable of directly producing tailored piezoelectric morphology in poly-L-lactide (PLLA). This technique has shown strong potential for developing complex and highly customized smart structures, but relationships between polymer printability, microstructure, and piezoelectric response remain largely unexplored. The molecular weight of the polymer and the printing trajectory critically impact the resulting shear piezoelectric coefficient of 3D-printed laminates. This is accomplished by printing PLLA from two raw sources with well-differentiated molecular weight and using either linear or concentric infill patterns. Results indicate that printing following concentric patterns enhances both crystallization and its orientation, associated with a faster cooling rate that minimizes chain relaxation. Besides, high molecular weight PLLA showed much higher piezoelectric responses, despite its slightly lower values for crystalline fraction and orientation. The role of molecular chain entanglements in limiting crystal disorientation is discussed, along with the effect of the size and periodicity of the crystalline lamellas, whose geometric arrangement is revealed here as a new key feature of the piezoelectric morphology of PLLA. Uncovering the polymer 3D printing-microstructure-property relationships has allowed to fully leverage the capabilities of this additive manufacturing strategy to realize complex, high-performance piezoelectric polymeric structures.

title: Low-hazard fabrication of natural zeolite @NiO composite for Pb2+ removal from industrial wastewater: toxicity assessment
abstract: The presence of heavy metals in water and industrial wastewater has become a major environmental concern due to their harmful effects on human health and other living organisms. In this study, a Zeolite/NiO composite was employed to investigate its potential for the removal of lead (Pb 2+ ) from aqueous solutions. NiO nanoparticles (∼20 nm) were green-synthesized and loaded onto zeolite to prepare Zeolite@NiO nanocomposites. XRD analysis confirmed that the crystalline structure of zeolite was preserved after NiO incorporation, while uniform dispersion of NiO nanoparticles was achieved. FESEM images demonstrated homogeneous NiO distribution while maintaining the zeolite framework. The Pb 2+ adsorption performance of the composites was evaluated in aqueous solutions. Zeta potentials displayed the highest Pb 2+ removal efficiency, attributed to an optimal balance between zeolite ion-exchange sites and NiO dispersion. The adsorption mechanism involves a synergistic combination of electrostatic interactions, ion exchange, surface complexation with −Ni-OH groups, and Pb 2+ stabilization/precipitation. Cytotoxicity assessment using the MTT assay showed that at a realistic residual catalyst concentration of 0.75 µg/mL, A549 cells maintained ≥90–115% viability. The IC 50 values for NiO, zeolite, and Zeolite: NiO = 1:1 were approximately 1.74, 1.87, and 1.90 µg/mL, indicating negligible biological risk under practical exposure conditions.

title: Mechanical enhancement and microstructural evolution of fiber–binder stabilized loess: experimental evaluation and multi-objective mix design optimization
abstract: Loess, widely distributed across the Loess Plateau and possessing substantial engineering potential, requires effective stabilization due to its inherently loose structure, high silt content, and low natural cohesion. This study investigates fiber–binder stabilization of loess and develops a performance-driven optimization framework to enhance mechanical behavior and microstructural compactness while improving material efficiency. Laboratory experiments were conducted on mixtures incorporating cement, polyethylene fibers, and a polymer-based binder. Significant improvements in compressive strength and shear resistance, together with a reduction in average pore size, were observed. SEM and mercury intrusion porosimetry analyses revealed that cement hydration products form a continuous load-bearing skeleton, binder gels enhance interparticle bonding and pore densification, and fibers bridge microcracks and subdivide large pores, thereby refining the internal structure. Response surface modeling and global sensitivity analysis quantified nonlinear interactions among components, showing that fiber and binder contribute more substantially to performance variance once structural continuity is established. A multi-objective optimization framework integrating NSGA-II and entropy–AHP-weighted TOPSIS identified an optimal mixture with validation errors below 6.5%. This study provides a quantitative and interpretable pathway for performance-oriented and sustainable loess stabilization design.

title: A stochastic damage-tolerant framework for fatigue strength prediction in additively manufactured alloys
abstract: Widespread adoption of Additively Manufactured (AM) components requires reliable characterisation of their fatigue properties to meet safety–critical standards. Damage-tolerant models offer an attractive avenue for alleviating intensive process-specific testing while retaining the inherent benefits of the AM manufacturing path. These models integrate principles of fracture mechanics, allow for non-uniform defect populations, and can incorporate process-specific attributes. In this study, we develop a computational framework that integrates population statistics, Monte Carlo defect sampling, and a modified NASGRO damage-tolerant solver to quantify the stochastic relationship between defect population statistics and fatigue strength. The approach provides a transferable modelling architecture for defect-sensitive design in AM. Specifically, we include statistical representations of multiple features (defect size, shape, location, and clustering of volumetric and surface roughness equivalent defects) to estimate fatigue strength distributions, which are shown to facilitate the formation of subtle, unexpected fatigue failures that better reflect the scatter in real fatigue behaviour. Overall, the nuance of defect population statistics as a source of fatigue scatter is underscored, revealing critical aspects for the design and modelling of AM component fatigue life.

title: Microstructure-informed creep model for 30CrMoNiV11-5 steel
abstract: 30CrMoNiV11-5 is a high-strength rotor steel used in turbine shafts, where creep governs long-term performance under elevated temperature and stress. In this work, a physics-based mean-field creep (MFC) framework is developed, in which dislocation populations (mobile, immobile, and boundary) are coupled with precipitate-kinetics inputs and damage evolution arising from precipitate coarsening and cavitation. The precipitate state is obtained from thermo-kinetic simulations based on the alloy heat-treatment history. The model is calibrated against 7 standard creep tests at 550 °C over a stress range of 283–450 MPa. It successfully reproduces the primary–secondary–tertiary creep behaviour, captures the stress dependence of the minimum creep strain rate, and predicts rupture time with good fidelity. The predicted microstructural evolution is consistent with TEM and EBSD observations, and the model allows analysis of the respective roles of intragranular and boundary-related precipitates. The proposed framework provides a mechanism-based approach for creep-life assessment of 30CrMoNiV11-5 and related rotor steels.

title: Dimensionally hybrid architecture-property relations in carbon nanotubes and silicon carbide nanoparticles reinforced aluminum matrix composites
abstract: Achieving an optimal strength-ductility synergy in aluminum matrix composites (AMCs) requires intelligent architectural design of multi-dimensional reinforcements. This study focuses on distinctive dimensional characteristics of hybrid reinforcements, combining one-dimensional multi-walled carbon nanotubes (1D CNTs) with zero-dimensional silicon carbide nanoparticles (0D SiCnp) in 6013Al matrix. By fixing volume ratio at 1:1 and varying total reinforcement content from 2 to 8 vol%, we systematically elucidate how the interplay between 1D and 0D reinforcements governs microstructural evolution and mechanical responses. The composite with 2 vol% CNTs and 2 vol% SiCnp exhibits the most balanced performance, delivering a tensile strength of 662 MPa and an elongation of 8.6%. This optimum is attributed to a spatially partitioned architecture wherein over 50% of reinforcements are encapsulated within Al grains, enabling efficient Orowan looping, load transfer and dislocation storage. Beyond this threshold, severe agglomeration redistributes reinforcements to grain boundaries, transforming them into stress concentrators and degrading both strength and ductility. Quantitative analysis confirms that the deterioration of reinforcement-related strengthening outweighs the continued benefits of grain refinement and geometrically necessary dislocations. This work emphasizes that preserving uniform dispersion and dimensional complementarity is key to harnessing the potential of hybrid nanocomposites, providing a microstructure-guided design principle for high-performance AMCs.

title: Atomic-scale study of Cu3Sn and Cu6Sn5 intermetallic layers growth after soldering
abstract: Advanced microscopy and elemental analysis techniques were employed to investigate the atomic-scale characteristics of intermetallic compound (IMC) layers of Cu 3 Sn and Cu 6 Sn 5 , which commonly form on copper-based surfaces during reflow soldering with lead-free Sn-based alloys in electronic packaging applications. The study also focused on the influence of iron nanoparticles—introduced via the soldering flux and localized at the interface during solidification—on the growth and coarsening behavior of these IMCs during both reflow and aging processes. High-resolution analyses, comprising atom probe tomography (APT) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), were used to characterize nanoscale precipitates at interfaces between Cu 3 Sn and Cu 6 Sn 5 , as well as between Cu 6 Sn 5 and the solder joint. These analyses aimed to elucidate the mechanisms by which iron nanoparticles suppress IMC growth during thermal processing. In addition, nanobeam diffraction mapping (NBDM) was used to quantify nanoscale strain distributions at intermetallic interfaces resulting from solid-state phase transformations during soldering. In the thin, fine-grained Cu 3 Sn layer, the dominant suppression mechanism was identified as nanoscale segregation of elemental iron. Conversely, in the thicker, coarse-grained Cu 6 Sn 5 layer, multiple mechanisms were observed. These included solid-solutioning of iron within the complex Cu 6 Sn 5 crystal structure and in-situ reactions with tin, leading to nanoscale FeSn 2 precipitates both within the Cu 6 Sn 5 layer and extending into the solder matrix. Together, these mechanisms contribute to inhibiting IMC growth during soldering and subsequent thermal aging.

title: Precision design of dissolving microneedles via mechanically induced micro-vent and Capillary-Controlled Molding: From fabrication to mechanical characterization
abstract: • Rheology-guided pre-curing physically suppresses capillary failures. • Mechanically induced micro-vents enable reliable microneedle casting. • A piecewise linear model defines coupled microneedle-skin mechanics. • Tip diameters below 25 µm enabled reliable insertion in layered skin. Dissolving microneedles with controlled geometry are difficult to fabricate reproducibly because liquid polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) molding is prone to meniscus failure and bubble entrapment. Here, we formed a PDMS master mold by directly inserting metal needles into thermally pre–cured PDMS and used rheology to identify the insertion window for stable cavity replication. A modified Young–Laplace model described the capillary-dominated failure of liquid PDMS, whereas successful meniscus suppression occurred after PDMS entered a gel-like viscoelastic regime. Under our conditions, pre–curing for 6 min on a 100 °C hotplate enabled faithful cavity replication and the fabrication of gelatin microneedle arrays with heights of 500–1500 µm. As the gelatin concentration increased from 25 to 40 % (w/v), Young’s modulus increased from 0.286 to 1.826 GPa. Compression and insertion tests using a multilayer artificial skin model identified distinct insertion phases and showed that microneedles with tip diameters of up to 25 µm reliably penetrated the model. These results provide a simple PDMS mold fabrication route and a rheology-guided basis for designing and mechanically evaluating dissolving gelatin microneedles.

title: Numerical analysis of microstructural characteristics on the hydrogen susceptibility of pipeline steels
abstract: Hydrogen-induced degradation challenges the safe operation of pipeline steels. However, the quantitative influence of complex microstructural features on hydrogen transport and mechanical response is not well understood. This study presents a two-way coupled crystal plasticity–hydrogen diffusion framework for analyzing the hydrogen susceptibility of two API X70 pipeline steel grades with different microstructures: ferritic–pearlitic (=X70-T14) and predominantly bainitic (=X70-T19). Statistically representative three-dimensional microstructure models were generated using EBSD-based data enhanced by a Wasserstein generative adversarial network to capture realistic morphological and crystallographic distributions. The models were calibrated using macroscopic tensile tests and phase-specific macro-indentation data. The hydrogen transport, trapping, and degradation were evaluated under various stress states using a fracture indicator parameter that accounts for HELP (hydrogen-enhanced localized plasticity) and HEDE (hydrogen-enhanced decohesion) mechanisms. The results demonstrate that bainitic X70-T19 steel accumulates higher plastic strain, stress triaxiality, and hydrogen concentration. This leads to increased hydrogen susceptibility under uniaxial loading. In contrast, X70-T14 steel is more vulnerable under plane strain and biaxial tension. Additional parametric case studies reveal that non-metallic inclusions, voids, grain size, phase fraction, and banded pearlite-structures significantly influence hydrogen kinetics and local damage initiation. The proposed framework establishes a data-driven foundation for microstructure design toward hydrogen-resistant pipeline steels. • At low stress triaxiality, both X70 grades exhibit similar hydrogen resistance. • Ferritic-pearlitic X70 shows higher FIP values at elevated stress triaxialities. • Inclusions, voids and phase fraction control hydrogen localization. • HELP/HEDE coupling accelerates hydrogen-assisted damage evolution.

title: Corrigendum to “Investigation on hot deformation behavior of a novel Ti-5Mo-20Nb-10Zr-5Ta-1Fe titanium alloy using constitutive equations, artificial neural network and processing maps” [Mater. Des. 265 (2026) 115918]
Zinc bioactive glass modified with an organic resin for pulp capping in comparison to other bioceramic cements: biological fluid -mediated performance
abstract: This study evaluated the mechanical and biological performance of a zinc‑modified bioactive glass–resin pulp‑capping agent (NPA) under clinically relevant conditions and compared it with MTA Angelus and Biodentine in the presence of blood and phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS). Setting time (n = 4; ISO 9917) and Vickers microhardness (n = 10) were measured after exposure to blood‑ or PBS‑moistened pellets. Dental pulp stem cell (DPSC) adhesion (n = 6) was examined by scanning electron microscopy, and DPSC migration (n = 6) was assessed using a scratch assay with material extracts diluted at 1:1, 1:4, and 1:8. The results showed that blood exposure significantly prolonged setting times for all materials (p < 0.05), with NPA showing the longest and Biodentine the shortest. NPA demonstrated the highest microhardness in both media (p < 0.01), although blood reduced hardness across groups. At 1:1 dilution, no measurable cell migration was observed; therefore, statistical analysis was limited to diluted concentrations. Lower concentrations enhanced cell migration, reaching 124% for MTA, 104.5% for NPA, and 86% for Biodentine at 1:8. SEM confirmed DPSC adhesion on all materials, with improved spreading on MTA and NPA. Despite slower setting, NPA showed superior microhardness and favorable cellular responses, suggesting its potential as a candidate material for vital pulp therapy.

title: Crack suppression and directional grain growth in M247 nickel-based superalloy via synchronous induction-assisted laser directed energy deposition
abstract: Additive manufacturing of nickel-based superalloys, particularly for aeroengine blade repair, faces challenges such as cracking and uncontrolled microstructure due to high thermal gradient and rapid cooling. This study presents a synchronous induction-assisted laser directed energy deposition (SIA-LDED) method to address these issues in M247 superalloy. By integrating a moving disk-shaped induction coil with the laser heat source, precise control of the local temperature field was achieved, enabling crack suppression and enhancing directional grain growth. Numerical simulation uncovered that preheating and slow-cooling effects induced by synchronous induction heating effectively reduced thermal gradients, thereby suppressing crack formation. It can also be employed to predict directional grain growth capability for process parameters optimization. The optimized induction parameters (268 A, 10 kHz) promoted the directional grain growth with the length exceeding 31 mm. The numerical simulation revealed that the synchronous induction heating minimized the solidification rate and enhanced the directional grain growth capability. It breaks through the inherent limitation of LDED in achieving directional grain growth on the ordinary substrate (non-directional grain). Mechanical testing showed that the SIA-LDED can prevent premature fracture of the sample, which primarily originates from the defect elimination and γ′ phase refinement.

title: Bio-hydrogelated structured sensors of high-performances for degradable bioelectronics
abstract: Compared with state-of-the-art polymeric counterparts, proteinic self-assemblies may bridge the gap between device performances and biocompatibility/biodegradability requirement, showing promising potentials in implantable bioelectronic scenarios. Nevertheless, stochastic behaviors due to lack of structural design severely restrict the reliability of proteinic sensors, along with hindering their miniaturization for in vivo applications. Herein, proteinic hydrogelation-based structured implantable sensors of intrinsic biodegradability with enhanced stability and sensing behaviours are engineered. Upon enzymatic crosslinking, the bio-hydrogels can boost mechanical elasticity and lead to minimal swelling side-effects for bioelectronics. Followingly, an interlocking sawtooth structure is designed to convert external loading into tensile strain, based on which a miniaturized implantable tactile sensor of high-performances is developed, showing an ultrahigh sensitivity integrated with fast dynamic responses, high resolutions towards varied amplitudes, frequencies and types, as well as reliable repeatability and intrinsic biodegradability. Our findings exemplify the feasibility of developing bio-hydrogelated structured sensors as biodegradable bioelectronics

title: Significant improvement of magnetic properties in LiZn ferrite ceramics via hot-pressing sintering technique
abstract: In prior research on LiZn ferrite ceramics, efforts primarily focused on reducing porosity through solid-state sintering methods to reduce magnetic loss. However, the influence of structural factors such as grain size and grain uniformity on ferromagnetic resonance linewidth (Δ H ) and spin wave linewidth ( Δ H k ), governed by hot-pressing sintering techniques, has received less attention. Here hot-pressing sintering techniques are employed to optimize these structural factors, aiming to enhance Δ H k and minimize Δ H in LiZn ferrite ceramics. Compared with solid-state sintering results, hot-pressing sintering technique yields significant improvements in addition to superior densification, achieving a remarkable 110.7% enhancement in Δ H k and a notable 22.2% reduction in Δ H . Besides, theoretical calculations are conducted to deeply analyze the loss mechanisms by decoupling magnetocrystalline anisotropy linewidth and pore linewidth, thereby elucidating their contributions to the total loss. Our results contribute to the fundamental understanding of the correlation between loss mechanisms and structural factors which can be further exploited to optimize LiZn ferrite properties.

title: Mechanical behaviour of additively manufactured CoCrWMo gyroid metamaterials using numerical modelling including mesostructure defects based on X-ray microtomography
abstract: This paper concerns the numerical modelling of the mechanical properties of metamaterials with a gyroid mesostructure and various relative densities, obtained using the additive laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) method from CoCrWMo alloy. The paper presents and compares two approaches to modelling the deformation process of the investigated metamaterials. The first was based on nominal geometric models of gyroid mesostructures, while the second involved mapping realistic mesostructure shapes using X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). The use of tomographic measurements made it possible to take into account the imperfections and defects of the studied gyroid structures resulting from the characteristics of the production process and its parameters. Using both approaches, numerical modelling of the deformation process of the investigated metamaterials was carried out using the finite element method (FEM). Based on the numerical calculations, stress and strain distributions in the studied metamaterials were obtained, and after their analysis, the influence of the shape of the tested mesostructures and their imperfections on their mechanical properties was determined. It was also indicated how external and internal technological defects can affect the mechanism of material fracture. A verification of the developed computational models was also performed using the results of experimental studies.

title: A process–structure–property ICME framework for additive friction stir deposition repair of aluminum alloys
abstract: Additive Friction Stir Deposition (AFSD) is a novel solid-state additive manufacturing process that is particularly suitable for repair of aluminum alloys. In this study, an Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework is developed to establish process–structure–property (PSP) relationships for AFSD repair of aluminum alloys, with a demonstration example of through-hole repairs in AA7050-T7451. Stationary Tool Head (STH) and Moving Tool Head (MTH) approaches are examined for straight and beveled geometries with diameters of 0.25 and 0.5-inch. Thermal histories during deposition are obtained using in-situ thermocouple measurements supplemented by COMSOL simulations and serve as inputs for precipitation simulations using the TC-Prisma module in Thermo-Calc. The predicted microstructural evolution is coupled with a physics-based yield strength model that shows good agreement with experimentally estimated yield strength derived from hardness measurements calibrated using AFSD-specific regression model. Results show that strength evolution during AFSD is primarily governed by precipitate dissolution and coarsening under STH conditions, while MTH processing results in lower thermal exposure, enabling alternative strengthening pathways. The ICME framework presented provides a predictive foundation for AFSD process optimization supporting its broader adoption as an advanced solid-state manufacturing and repair technology for aluminum alloys

title: NIR-enhanced HCuS-Pt nanozymes based hydrogel dressing accelerates chronic infected wound healing via synergistic antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities
abstract: Chronic infectious wounds often delayed in healing due to their complex pathogenic factors. Currently, multifunctional hydrogel dressings offer a cost-effective and efficient therapeutic strategy to accelerate chronic wound healing by overcoming healing barriers. In this study, a multifunctional hydrogel named HOCP2 was developed by incorporating ultrasmall platinum (Pt) nanoparticles-loaded hollow HCuS (HCuS-Pt) nanozymes into a hydrogel matrix composed of adipic acid dihydrazide modified hyaluronic acid (HA-ADH) and oxidized sodium alginate (OSA), which were crosslinked via Schiff base bonds.
