The higher burn-up specimen exhibits a more pronounced size effect when indent load is lower than 20 mN. Size effect correction models are also calculated by plots fitting, which predicts the true microhardness without size effect. Results shows that the hardness of the Al matrix near the ZrN coating has the highest value, then decreases moving away from the coating and become stable when the distance reaches ∼10 µm. The hardness starts increasing again getting closer to the next fuel particle, which makes the hardness distribution between two fuel particles to be “U” shape.

title: A novel medium-carbon steel adapted to laser powder bed fusion: Microstructure, mechanical and wear properties
abstract: • New medium-carbon steel for laser powder bed fusion was developed. • Process parameters for crack-free fabrication of components were identified. • As-built steel possesses hierarchical microstructure. • Deformation-induced martensitic transformation occurred during compressive testing. • Friction-induced martensitic transformation occurred during abrasive wear testing. Laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is designed for the near-net-shape fabrication of complex tool steel parts. In high-carbon steels, however, its broader application is limited by crack formation arising from severe thermal gradients and from stresses induced by austenite-to-martensite transformation. In this work, a materials design-driven strategy is presented to overcome these limitations through the development of a lean medium-carbon tool steel (Fe94.1Cr0.8Mo0.5Mn1.1Ni3.0C0.5) adapted to PBF-LB/M processing. By reducing the carbon content, transformation-induced stresses are mitigated, enabling the fabrication of crack-free components with a relative density of 99.7% without substrate preheating. The as-built microstructure consists predominantly of α ′-martensite containing MnS precipitates, ε -martensite, and retained austenite, which undergoes deformation-induced transformation to martensite during mechanical loading and friction. The transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effect promotes work hardening and contributes to a favorable combination of strength and wear resistance. The additively manufactured steel exhibits a yield strength of 1317 MPa and an ultimate compressive strength of 2061 MPa. Benchmarked against commercial H11 tool steel, superior abrasive wear resistance is achieved despite lower macrohardness, which is attributed to a friction-induced austenite-to-martensite transformation at the worn surface. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of alloy design for enhanced processability and performance in additively manufactured tool steels.

title: Compressible two-phase VOF simulation of turbulent mold filling in high-pressure die casting and a quantitative evaluation approach
abstract: Air entrapment during mold filling critically affects porosity and overall casting quality in High-Pressure Die Casting (HPDC). This study assesses the feasibility of applying the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method within OpenFOAM to simulate compressible, turbulent mold filling in a thin-walled geometry. Three-dimensional simulations with the compressibleInterFoam solver were carried out under ambient initial cavity conditions, using both laminar flow and the k - ε turbulence model. The free surface dynamics were examined across a range of inlet velocities to evaluate their influence on interface morphology, cavity pressurization, and gas entrapment. To quantify these effects, three evaluation criteria were introduced: the Time-Integrated Free Surface Area (TIFSA) as a geometric exposure metric associated with oxidation potential, the Temporal Mean Volume Fraction (TMVF) as an indicator of filling continuity and air entrapment, and the Time-Integrated Volumetric Flow (TIVF) as a proxy for surface loading. Results show that turbulence modeling accelerates pressurization and limits the persistence of entrapped gas, with velocity governing the balance between smooth filling, turbulent breakup, and exposure duration. Comparison with experimental casting trials on a thin-walled HPDC plate in aluminum alloy AlSi10MnMg, including CT-based porosity analysis and photogrammetric surface evaluation, supported the interpretation that the water-based simulations capture key defect-relevant flow features in this geometry and provide a transferable methodological framework for process optimization.

title: Glass transition temperature prediction in lignin polyurethanes using machine learning on small experimental dataset
abstract: Lignin-based polyurethanes (PUs) offer a compelling route towards sustainable material development, yet the challenge of designing chemical formulations with targeted properties, such as glass transition temperature (T g ), remains unresolved. In this work, we present a systematic approach to explore key structural parameters – such as lignin content, co-polyol chain length, isocyanate functionality, and mixing ratios – across 136 unique formulations, creating a diverse dataset of lignin-based PUs. By harnessing this small dataset, we develop a machine learning (ML) stacking ensemble model capable of reliably predicting T g , with a mean absolute error of 13.41 °C on the validation set, surpassing the performance of all individual models. Additionally, we enhance model interpretability by integrating advanced mapping techniques and employ an adaptive grid search algorithm to explore extrapolative scenarios. Our workflow, paired with a user-friendly interface, enables rapid discovery and optimization of formulations with desired properties. This study not only deepens the understanding of structure–property relationships in lignin-PUs but also provides a scalable ML-driven tool for designing sustainable materials with precision, highlighting the transformative potential of artificial intelligence in green chemistry and materials innovation.

title: Strengthening properties of glass-ceramics with near-zero thermal expansion
abstract: The hydrogen atomic clock microwave cavity serves as the interaction site between electromagnetic fields and hydrogen atoms, requiring materials with low coefficient of thermal expansion, high temperature variation resistance, and superior mechanical strength. Although quartz glass is currently widely used for manufacturing hydrogen atomic clock microwave cavities, there remains room for improving overall performance and reliability. This study focuses on investigating the effects of different physical strengthening and chemical strengthening processes on the properties of Li2O-Al2O3-SiO2 system glass-ceramics. We successfully developed glass-ceramics exhibiting a near-zero expansion coefficient, exceptional thermal stability, high bending strength, and verified the feasibility of the fracture mechanics analysis method for glass materials using finite element simulation. The coefficient of thermal expansion of this material achieved (0 ± 0.2) × 10-7 / ℃. After chemical strengthening, the material demonstrated a bending strength of 208.61 MPa, representing a 22.52 % enhancement compared to the strengthening before. This advanced glass-ceramic shows promising applications in manufacturing hydrogen atomic clock microwave cavities, with significant implications for aerospace engineering, space tracking, navigation systems, radio astronomy, timekeeping, and frequency metrology.

title: Stem cells from apical papilla-derived exosomes alleviate bisphosphonate-related osteonecrosis of the jaw by promoting angiogenesis
Mesoporous carbon/Co composites with optimized impedance matching for enhanced microwave absorption and radar stealth performance
abstract: Composites of carbon and magnetic metals are attractive candidates for microwave absorbing materials (MAMs) due to their synergistic loss mechanisms and tailorable electromagnetic properties. In this work, magnetic Co nanoparticles were coupled with mesoporous carbon (MC) to enhance microwave absorption. Electromagnetic analysis reveals that Co nanoparticles fulfill dual functions: they introduce significant magnetic loss while moderately modulating the dielectric loss of the MC framework, thereby optimizing the impedance matching characteristics of the hybrid. Specifically, the MC/Co-2 sample achieves a minimum reflection loss of −37.55 dB at 9.24 GHz and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 3.3 GHz. The practical potential of the optimized sample is further validated by RCS simulations. Specifically, a maximum RCS reduction of 33.84 dB·m2 was achieved at a 0° incident angle, with an average RCS value of –22.8 dB·m2 across the entire detection range, demonstrating reliable radar stealth capability under simulated far-field conditions. This study not only provides a comprehensive evaluation of carbon/metal composites as potential MAMs, but also offers valuable insights into the synergistic mechanisms that guide the rational design of magnetic carbon-based absorbers for future stealth applications.

title: Tailored graphene quantum dots for heavy metal stabilization in MSW incineration fly ash: A potential scalable engineering pathway
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) have attracted increasing attention as emerging carbon-based nanomaterials due to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and abundant surface functional groups. However, their practical use in large-scale engineering systems remains limited. Meanwhile, municipal solid waste incineration fly ash (IFA), a hazardous byproduct containing leachable heavy metals, requires effective treatment to reduce environmental risks. In this study, amino-functionalized graphene quantum dots (A-GQDs) were synthesized and incorporated into a cement-based solidification/stabilization (S/S) system for IFA treatment, and their effects on heavy metal immobilization and the underlying mechanism were systematically investigated. The results show that the addition of 0.2 wt% A-GQDs significantly reduced the leaching concentrations of Pb, Cd, and Zn by 50-90%. Sequential extraction further confirmed that A-GQDs promoted the transformation of heavy metals from unstable fractions to more stable forms. Microstructural characterization suggests that A-GQDs enhanced the formation of dense hydration products and refined the cement matrix, while their surface functional groups may also contribute to heavy metal immobilization through chemical interactions. Overall, A-GQDs show promise as multifunctional nano-additives for improving the cement-based treatment of IFA and provide a potential application pathway for carbon dots in hazardous waste management.

title: Cuttlebone-inspired cellular ceramics with Ti3C2Tx MXene for structural and functional integration
abstract: This work presents additively manufactured bioinspired, cuttlebone-like cellular ceramics with a conformal multilayer coating of Ti3C2Tx MXene and epoxy to improve mechanical performance, energy absorption, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding. Several cuttlebone-inspired cellular architectures with S-shaped walls and varying curvatures were designed to systematically evaluate the role of structural geometry on mechanical response and functional performance. The application of the conformal epoxy coating substantially enhances the compressive behavior of the cellular ceramics, yielding a 540% increase in compressive strength. An increase in wall curvature from flat to sinusoidal geometries leads to approximately 95% improvement in specific energy absorption and induces a transition in failure mechanism from brittle fracture to stable, progressive layer-by-layer collapse. EMI shielding measurements indicate that MXene-coated structures display mostly absorption-dominated shielding, achieving a maximum total shielding effectiveness (SET) of about 59–60 dB at the optimal MXene coating cycle. Low–curvature and flat geometries achieve the highest peak absorption, while highly curved structures provide more gradual increases in shielding effectiveness (SE) across coating cycles. The synergistic combination of bioinspired geometry, ceramic rigidity, and MXene conductivity yields a lightweight, multifunctional material system with enhanced mechanical resilience and strong EMI shielding, making it suitable for advanced aerospace and electronic protection applications.

title: Phase transformation and microstructural evolution of tantalum carbide coatings on graphite in a TaCl5-H2-Ar gas–solid CVD system
abstract: This study investigates the phase transformation and microstructural evolution of TaC coatings formed on graphite in a TaCl5-H2-Ar gas–solid CVD system without an external carbon precursor. The as-deposited coating consisted of a mixed Ta2C/TaC layer, indicating that limited and spatially non-uniform carbon availability during deposition favored the formation of a Ta-rich intermediate carbide together with TaC. After annealing, the coating evolved into a TaC-dominant state, accompanied by carbon redistribution and microstructural rearrangement within the coating. A second deposition–annealing cycle preserved the TaC-dominant phase and further modified the surface morphology. Combined structural, interfacial, and mechanical characterizations clarified the relationship among processing route, phase evolution, interfacial/microstructural development, and local mechanical response in this no-external-carbon-precursor system. The final coating exhibited a hardness of 16.4 ± 1.5 GPa and an elastic modulus of 240.3 ± 24.5 GPa. This study provides a basis for the design of refractory carbide coatings on carbon-based substrates.

title: Strengthening the hall-petch relationship of 316LN by chemical short-range order
abstract: 316LN stainless steel is a key structural alloy for cryogenic applications, valued for its excellent low-temperature mechanical properties. While intrinsic chemical short-range order (CSRO) has been recognized for enhancing strength and toughness in multi-principal element alloys, its specific role in the deformation and strengthening of 316LN remains unclear. In this work, molecular dynamics simulations were performed to examine the Hall-Petch relationship and underlying deformation mechanisms in 316LN, focusing on the effect of CSRO and temperature. The results show that the Hall-Petch response proceeds through three distinct stages: strengthening, plateau, and inverse Hall-Petch softening. Notably, CSRO segregated at grain boundaries (GBs) strengthens the material by hindering dislocation transmission and nucleation. It also suppresses GB activity, extending the plateau stage to finer grains and improving preparation robustness. Since GB-mediated plasticity dominates the inverse Hall-Petch stage, CSRO exerts its most pronounced strengthening effect in this stage. Furthermore, at cryogenic temperatures, a synergistic strengthening interaction between thermal effects and CSRO is observed. These findings advance the understanding of CSRO-mediated strengthening in 316LN stainless steel.

title: Electrophoretic deposition of SiO2 coatings on nitinol: The effect of suspension pH on tailoring film properties
abstract: Nickel–titanium alloys are widely used in cardiovascular implants because of their shape-memory behavior and superelasticity, yet they can release nickel ions that trigger inflammation and hinder endothelialization. In this study, amorphous SiO2 nanopowders were deposited onto NiTi substrates using electrophoretic deposition (EPD), and the effect of suspension pH on coating structure, physicochemical properties, and biological response was investigated. Zeta potential measurements showed consistently positive values at all pH levels, confirming effective charge masking by polyethylenimine (PEI). Despite similar electrokinetic behavior, scanning electron microscopy revealed clear pH-dependent differences in morphology. At pH 4, coatings were dense, compact, and exhibited nearly complete surface coverage with local microcracks, whereas coatings produced at pH 8 were more heterogeneous and showed directional agglomeration. FT-IR and SEM–EDS analyses confirmed the coexistence of SiO2 and PEI, along with greater elemental uniformity at pH 4. These coatings were also thicker, more cohesive, and offered superior wear resistance and barrier performance compared to those formed at pH 8. Biological tests demonstrated that SiO2-modified surfaces reduced cell adhesion and viability relative to bare NiTi. The results indicate the need to balance protective functionality with biocompatibility, providing guidance for further optimization of SiO2-based coatings for NiTi cardiovascular implants.

title: On the microstructural strategies adopted for achieving improved machinability in commercial brass alloys
abstract: Commercially available lead-free brasses with improved machinability were investigated to elucidate the microstructural mechanisms responsible for their enhanced interrupted chip formation. The study examines the microstructure and chip characteristics of alloys belonging to the Cu–Zn–Si (CW724R) and Cu–Zn–Mg (CW732R) lead-free systems and compares them with the standard CuZn42 (CW510L) and CuZn39Pb3 (CW614N) brasses. The results indicate that improved machinability in these lead-free alloys is achieved either by increasing the amount and hardness of the β phase through precipitation strengthening, as in the Mg-bearing CW732R alloy, or by promoting the formation of hard constituents capable of replacing the β phase, as observed in the Si-bearing CW724R alloy. Chip analyses from rough and fine turning tests revealed that CW724R develops a deformed chip microstructure characterized by periodic deep cracks and localized shear bands traversing the entire chip thickness, resulting in a discontinuous morphology comparable to that of the lead-bearing CW614N alloy. In contrast, the Mg-bearing CW732R alloy, despite its higher hardness and larger β phase fraction, displayed a chip morphology similar to the standard lead-free CW510L alloy under the machining conditions adopted here. These findings appear to contradict earlier reports showing superior machinability in similar Mg-bearing brasses, highlighting that the microstructural design of free-machining alloys must be carefully tailored to the specific chip-removal technology and machining parameters.

title: Microstructural evolution and surface integrity Enhancement of SLM fabricated FeCoCrNiMn High-Entropy alloys by Single-Point diamond turning technology
abstract: Selective laser melted (SLM) FeCoCrNiMn high-entropy alloys exhibit inadequate surface quality and microstructural features unfavorable for machining, which limit their functional performance. This study comprehensively investigates the surface integrity, microstructural change and mechanical properties of FeCoCrNiMn high-entropy alloy fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) with machined by single point diamond turning (SPDT). Results show that shallower cutting depths and higher cutting speeds significantly improve surface uniformity and finish, while promoting the formation of nano-laminated, grain-refined layers. SPDT transforms coarse columnar grains into nanocrystalline structures with an increased density of twins, stacking faults, and dislocations, resulting in up to a 16.9% increase in surface nano-hardness and wear resistance, and a reduction in friction coefficient to 0.226. Furthermore, adhesive wear is identified as the primary diamond tool wear mechanism in SPDT of high entropy alloys, which can be effectively mitigated by optimizing key machining parameters. These findings demonstrate that SPDT is an effective approach for enhancing both surface quality and mechanical performance of SLM-fabricated high-entropy alloys, and provide insights into the interplay between machining conditions, microstructural changes, and functional performance.

title: Interface engineering of 2D V2C MXene/APTES modified PVDF membranes with enhanced hydrophilicity, permeability, and antifouling properties for methylene blue removal
abstract: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) membranes are widely used in water purification because of their chemical resistance and thermal stability, but their hydrophobic nature makes them prone to fouling and limits water permeability. In this study, PVDF membranes were modified with vanadium carbide (V2C) MXene and 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES)-V2C to address these shortcomings. V2C was selected due to its layered structure, conductivity, and hydrophilic surface chemistry, while APTES was introduced to stabilize the MXene and add functional groups that improve compatibility and antifouling behavior. In the 120-min filtration test, the modified membranes showed clear improvements compared to pristine PVDF. The addition of 2 wt% V2C in PVDF/V2C 2% (MMV2) reduced the water contact angle from 73° to 46° (MMV2), increased pure water flux from 20.99 m−2h−1 (PVDF) to 91.44 L m−2h−1 (MMV2), dye removal efficiency from 88.30 (PVDF) to 96.51% (MMV2), and recovery ratio from 58.2% (PVDF) to 84.4% (MMV2). With APTES functionalization (MMV2A-2), the removal efficiency reached 97.77% and flux recovery ratio improved markedly to 93.8% (MMV2A-2), indicating excellent resistance to fouling. These results confirm that V2C and its APTES-modified form were effective fillers for tailoring PVDF membranes, providing both higher permeability and stronger antifouling properties. The fabricated membranes fell within the ultrafiltration (UF) classification, as confirmed by molecular weight cut-off (MWCO) values of 52.2–77.6 kDa. The approach offered a practical route to improve PVDF membranes for dye removal and related ultrafiltration processes.

title: Corrigendum to “Metabolically targeted NIR-II theranostic nanoplatform enabling efficient synergistic phototherapy and chemotherapy for alveolar echinococcosis” [Mater. Des. 263 (2026) 115597]
A critical review of the recent biomaterial innovations for pelvic organ prolapse treatment: materials and design
abstract: • Biomaterials strategies for pelvic organ prolapse are critically reviewed. • Structure–property relationships govern mechanics and tissue integration. • Bioactive designs enhance regeneration while reducing inflammation. • Translational challenges include biomechanics, longevity, and scalability. • Emerging tools enable patient-specific and durable prolapse therapies.

title: Atom probe informed persistent homology analysis of precipitation topology and hardening
abstract: • Application of persistent homology enables quantitative analysis of precipitate structure evolution during ageing of maraging stainless steel, revealing a multi-stage three-dimensional topological transformation. • Topological descriptors correlate with mechanical property trends, with H2 topology (void-like 3D features) showing a strong correlation to precipitation hardening (R 0.9). • Wasserstein and bottleneck distances quantify topological changes in precipitate structures, linking them to observed hardening behaviour: the VR bottleneck distance shows a strong negative correlation with hardness difference, while the Alpha Wasserstein distance exhibits a strong positive correlation. • Topological descriptors reveal a non-monotonic relationship between spatial heterogeneity and peak hardening. • A unified topology-microstructure-strength framework is established, demonstrating the superior predictive potential of topological descriptors over conventional structural metrics.

title: Enhancing the mechanical performance of DLP-printed HAp scaffolds: Impact of 72.5 wt% solid loading on achieving cortical-bone-level strength
abstract: This work establishes a new performance benchmark for DLP-printed hydroxyapatite (HAp) scaffolds by realizing a record-tier solid loading of 72.5 wt%, yielding an unprecedented compressive strength of ∼ 130.08 MPa and hardness of 3.59 GPa, surpassing all previously reported 3D-printed HAp materials. To overcome the rheological challenges of ultra-high ceramic loading, we developed a tailored slurry using 5 wt% BYK-180 and a black photoabsorber to achieve optimal flowability and precise light-scattering control. A strategic two-stage thermal protocol was engineered to ensure complete organic removal and near-theoretical densification (0.8% porosity) while preserving phase purity. The resulting scaffolds exhibit superior dimensional accuracy and structural integrity across complex architectures. Biological evaluations with MC3T3-E1 cells confirm robust cell adhesion, sustained proliferation, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. By redefining the upper limits of both solid loading and structural integrity, this work provides a validated, scalable route for manufacturing high-performance, patient-specific bioceramic implants for advanced bone repair.

title: Effects of grain size, crystal texture, and misorientation on thermoelectric properties of (Bi0.1Sb0.9)2Te3 based compounds
abstract: • We study how grain size, boundary misorientation, and texture affect the thermoelectric behavior of (Bi 0 . 1 Sb 0 . 9 ) 2 Te 3 processed by controlled ball–milling and hot–pressing. • The coarse-grained structure observed for the as-grown (Bi 0.1 Sb 0.9 ) 2 Te 3 compound decreases to ca. 3 µm due to hand-grinding, then decreases down to sub-µm size upon ball-milling. • The fractions of highly misoriented and twin grain boundaries increase with ball–milling duration and level off at approximately 90% and 10%, respectively, accompanied by a reduction in electrical conductivity • Lattice thermal conductivity peaks in as–grown samples and reaches its minimum in hand–ground ones, with ball–milled samples exhibiting similar intermediate values, due to preferred orientations with Te-Te van der Waals bonds parallel to the {0001} basal planes that reduce thermal conductivity along the c-axis.

title: Superior strength and ductility synergy at elevated temperatures of LPBF-fabricated IN718 + HfB2 through cooperative microbands and microtwins
abstract: Laser-powder bed fusion (LPBF) fabricated IN718 superalloy is often constrained by its inferior high-temperature performance beyond 650 °C. While ceramic reinforcement is a widely adopted strategy to address this limitation, conventional ceramics (e.g., ZrB 2 , Y 2 O 3 ) often suffer from interfacial instability and insufficient effectiveness at elevated temperatures. This study presents a superior alternative by incorporating nano-scale HfB 2 particles to develop a high-performance IN718 composite via LPBF. The novel IN718 + HfB 2 composite demonstrates an exceptional balance between ultra-high strength and ductility at both ambient and elevated temperatures. At 650 °C, the composite exhibits a high ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 1178.2 MPa and elongation of 8.6%. At 800 °C, the composite maintains an ultra-high UTS of 732.5 MPa and elongation of 6.6%, surpassing most reported IN718-based composites. The outstanding strength is attributed to the in-situ formation of a continuous cellular network of borides and intermetallics during LPBF, which synergistically enhanced grain boundaries, dislocations, and precipitates strengthening capabilities. Moreover, these uniformly distributed precipitates facilitated a unique cooperative deformation behaviors of microbands and microtwins at elevated temperatures. Consequently, this study offers a new pathway for achieving superior mechanical properties for nickel-based superalloys beyond conventional reinforcement strategies.

title: A strong and ductile medium-entropy alloy with a thermally stable cellular heterostructure by additive manufacturing
abstract: Microstructural thermal stability usually defines the upper limit of the mechanical properties of an alloy. Many complex alloys such as high- and medium-entropy alloys (HEAs and MEAs) often suffer from low microstructural thermal stability. For instance, the cellular structures formed in many additively manufactured HEAs/MEAs, which are beneficial to both strength and ductility, could be eliminated in a post-process heat treatment or thermal exposure while brittle topologically closed-packed (TCP) phases such as σ phase can form during this process. In this study, we design a novel MEA based on calculation of phase diagram, (CoNi) 71 Cr 20 Ti 3 Al 5 Mo 0.5 Ta 0.5 (at.%), which upon selective laser melting and heat treatment forms no TCP phase but a cellular heterostructure that can remain up to 1000 °C, demonstrating extraordinary thermal stability. The cellular heterostructure comprising clusters of large γ′ precipitates at the cell boundaries and ultrafine γ′ particles in the cell interior, induces effective precipitate strengthening and back stress strengthening during deformation. The clusters of large γ′ particles decorated cell boundaries effectively impede dislocation motion while the gaps between the clusters allow straight and uniform slip across cellular structures. Consequently, the cellular heterostructure imparts the material with an excellent combination of strength and ductility.

title: Virtual CT analysis of pore structure in DEM-generated granular media: Application to porous asphalt
abstract: • Voxel resolution controls pore structure quantification in granular media. • Global properties converge at coarse resolution, unlike pore-scale features. • Increased resolution improves pore detection but induces over-segmentation. • Optimal voxel size should balance particle scale, accuracy, and cost.

title: Injectable hydrogel with sequential drug release for synergistic antibacterial activity and osteogenesis in infected bone defects
abstract: The treatment of infected bone defects (IBD) remains challenging due to persistent infection, inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis. Traditional antibiotic-centered strategies suffer from limited therapeutic efficacy, high risks of bacterial resistance and systemic toxicity, and a requirement for multiple invasive surgeries. To overcome these drawbacks, we fabricated a bifunctional hydrogel (Gel/LB) based on polyethylene glycol and oxidized dextran backbones, via lysozyme physical blending and bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) derived peptide grafting, to achieve sequential drug release for early rapid antibacterial activity and long-term sustained osteogenesis. In vitro characterization revealed the hydrogel had a three-dimensional porous structure, excellent injectability, and self-healing capacity. It exerted potent anti- Staphylococcus aureus effects via rapid lysozyme release, while sustained BMP-2-derived peptide release significantly promoted adhesion, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, as verified by elevated alkaline phosphatase activity, upregulated osteogenic gene expression, and enhanced mineralized nodule formation. In vivo , Gel/LB eradicated infection in mouse femoral infected defect models, markedly promoted new bone formation and collagen deposition, improved bone-related parameters, and regulated inflammatory and osteogenic markers. Collectively, this bifunctional hydrogel enables effective antibacterial and pro-osteogenic effects via sequential release, providing a novel biomaterial strategy for clinical IBD management.

title: PLGA/nanofibrillated chitosan-coated titanium nanotube arrays with sequential release capabilities for enhanced antibacterial performance, cell viability, and osteo/angio-genesis
abstract: Designing an antimicrobial implant that also facilitates sustained drug release and supports cell proliferation remains a challenge. Hence, this study aimed to develop a titanium nanotube (TNT)-based implant to overcome these barriers. Human placenta extract (HPE) was loaded into TNTs, coated with poly lactic-co-glycolic acid (PLGA) via electrospray deposition, and then overlaid with alendronate (ALN) encapsulated in nanofibrillated chitosan (CSNF). This system is engineered for sequential drug release, promoting initial bone attachment through ALN and reducing bacterial biofilm formation via CSNF. Additionally, it stimulates osteoblast activity, osteogenesis, and angiogenesis. Drug release profiles showed initial ALN release followed by sustained long-term HPE release. The highest bacterial inhibition zone against S. aureus was 19.68 ± 0.99 mm. The implants demonstrated high cell viability. Immunofluorescence images of Osteopontin (OPN) validated enhanced osteogenic activity, with HPE and ALN encapsulation and bilayer coating leading to increased OPN concentration and osteogenesis. HPE encapsulation in TNTs upregulated VEGFR-2 and angiogenic activity. Furthermore, CSNF and ALN further increased VEGFR-2 expression, demonstrating the effectiveness of our multifunctional implant in promoting bone regeneration and antimicrobial activity.

title: Corrigendum to “An advanced modeling framework for capturing elastic/thermoelastic responses and gradual creep progression in graphene nanoplatelet-magnesium nanocomposites” [Mater. Design 265 (2026) 115945]
Evaluating buckling stability in multiscale design: a comparative study of shell- and truss-based lattices
abstract: • Comparative analysis of buckling behavior between shell-based and truss-based lattices reveals the superior buckling resistance of shell-based designs due to their smooth, continuous geometry. • A three-dimensional buckling-constrained multiscale topology optimization framework is developed using different lattice microstructures and both macrostructural and microstructural buckling are considered in optimization • Shell-based lattices demonstrate clear advantages in multiscale optimization, significantly improving global stability.

title: FeSO4-Vitamin C co-loaded active targeting liposome inhibits liver cancer through synergistic ferroptosis mechanism
abstract: Ferroptosis is an emerging regulated cell death pattern characterized by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and has enormous potential in tumor therapy. Given that iron ions are the key mediator of ferroptosis, we hypothesized that targeted delivery-mediated selective elevation of intracellular iron ion concentrations in tumor cells would promote the Fenton reaction, thereby inducing tumor cell death via lipid peroxidation. In this study, we engineered a galactose (Gal) residues-modified liposome (Fe-Vc-LIP-Gal) with active targeting capability toward hepatoma cells, which co-encapsulated FeSO 4 (Fe 2+ ) and vitamin C (Vc) to enhance the intracellular delivery efficiency of both agents. During storage, Vc maintains the stability of Fe 2+ . Within hepatoma cells, Vc reacts with Fe 3+ to generate dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) and Fe 2+ ; DHA then depletes glutathione (GSH) continuously to regenerate reduced Vc. This redox cycle not only sustains Fe 2+ availability but also positively drives the Fenton reaction, amplifying ferroptosis-associated oxidative stress and triggering robust lipid peroxidation that ultimately leads to cell death. Thus, high-concentration Fe 2+ and Vc exert a synergistic ferroptosis effect, and the active targeted delivery of these two agents into tumor cells offers a novel strategy for the application of ferroptosis in cancer therapy.

title: The fabrication and characterization of chitosan/polyvinylpyrrolidone/surfactin/platensimycin composite film for the treatment of MRSA-infected skin wounds
abstract: • The combination of chitosan, polyvinylpyrrolidone, adjuvant surfactin, and the antimicrobial agent platensimycin (PTM) enables the formation of a crosslinked film. • The crosslinking mechanism arises from the formation of hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions among the components. • The prepared film exhibited synergistic anti-MRSA performance, with a greater than 64-fold rise in its bacterial kill rate. • The PTM-loaded composite film exhibited significant efficacy in ameliorating MRSA infection and promoting skin wound repair.

title: Thiamazole-loaded nanohybrid hydrogel microneedles for treating hyperthyroidism
abstract: Hyperthyroidism treatment with antithyroid drugs such as Thiamazole is often limited by systemic adverse effects and poor therapeutic specificity during long-term oral administration. To overcome these limitations, we designed Thiamazole-loaded mesoporous carbon nanohybrid microneedles (MN-T@MCN) as a minimally invasive, locally enhanced transdermal delivery platform. The MN-T@MCN system exhibited strong mechanical integrity, high transparency, rapid dissolution, and near-infrared-triggered photothermal-enhances drug diffusion. In vitro, MN-T@MCN effectively reduced reactive oxygen species and suppressed lipid peroxidation and apoptosis in PMA-induced thyroid epithelial cells. In vivo, it restored thyroid follicular structure, normalized serum T3/T4/TSH levels, and mitigated hepatic injury in L-thyroxine–induced hyperthyroid rats. Notably, NIR stimulation further improved transdermal delivery efficiency and accelerated local drug diffusion, enhancing therapeutic efficacy. Additionally, MN-T@MCN attenuated oxidative stress and regulated apoptosis-related proteins (Bax, Bcl-2, Caspase-3) in thyroid and liver tissues. Overall, this study presents a safe, responsive microneedle-based strategy for hyperthyroidism treatment, offering a promising alternative to conventional oral therapy while reducing hepatotoxicity risks

title: Corrigendum to “Morphology-dependet electrical response of CO2-foamed conductive TPU filaments fabricated by foam additive manufacturing” [Mater. Design 266 (2026) 116091]
Application and translation of biodegradable metals in cardiovascular and neurovascular interventional devices
abstract: • Biodegradable metallic stents are reviewed as translational vascular devices, with emphasis on Mg, Fe, Zn, and Mo systems and their distinct mechanical, degradation, biological, and clinical profiles. • Cardiovascular applications provide the major evidence base for biodegradable metals, including material optimization, device-level performance, preclinical validation, and clinical experience in coronary intervention. • Neurovascular translation requires dedicated re-engineering beyond coronary stent adaptation, due to intracranial vessel tortuosity, fragile arterial walls, perforator-rich anatomy, blood–brain barrier-related safety concerns, and stricter imaging requirements.

title: Achieving exceptional Strength-Ductility at 4.2 K in High-Manganese Steels: The influence of pre-strain and aging on Manipulating microstructure and deformation behavior
abstract: Pre-strain and aging (PA) treatment is essential in manufacturing Nb 3 Sn magnets and must be performed together with the outer jacket material. This imposes strict requirements on the aging resistance and cryogenic performance of the jacket material, making it crucial to understand the effects of PA treatment. This study investigates the effect of pre-strain and aging (PA) treatment on Fe-Mn-xAl-C high-Mn austenitic steels for 4 K application, which shows promise for replacing 316LN and JK 2 LB stainless steels in 4 K applications as a new cryogenic material. The findings reveal that: PA treatment triggers detrimental carbide precipitation in 0Al and 2Al steels, causing embrittlement and reduced ductility. The 5Al steel maintains microstructural stability during PA, achieving a 165 MPa yield strength increase through Taylor lattice and dislocation strengthening. PA alters deformation mechanisms: lower Al steels show enhanced twinning due to reduced SFE, while 5Al steel combines microband- and twinning-induced plasticity. 5Al steel exhibits an excellent combination of yield strength and ductility compared to existing cryogenic materials for 4.2 K applications. The research provides crucial insights into how PA processing manipulates microstructure and cryogenic deformation behaviour, establishing a theoretical foundation for designing advanced cryogenic materials with superior strength-ductility synergy at 4.2 K.

title: A neural network-based hardening model for plastic anisotropy evolution in a face centered cubic material
abstract: This study presents a data-driven approach for modelling the hardening behavior of polycrystalline materials using artificial neural networks (ANNs) integrated within a crystal plasticity (CP) framework. A dataset of slips and hardening parameter combinations was extracted from crystal-level simulations. This dataset contained some contradictory points where similar inputs produced significantly different outputs, and a filtering process was introduced to selectively eliminate these points for aiding the neural network to better capture representative data. Multiple ANN architectures were evaluated, with a network comprising 5 hidden layers identified as the most accurate for predicting the work hardening behavior. The final model was implemented as a hardening rule in the CP model. The ANN outperformed the Voce hardening rule with stress prediction errors reduced to below 2%. Texture evolution, stress-strain curves, and strain ratios were also analyzed across different material orientations for uniaxial and plane strain tension. Despite some limitations, such as strain ratio predictions, the proposed model shows significant promise. It offers improved predictive accuracy in stress-strain curves, providing a viable alternative to traditional hardening functions in CP modeling. This work highlights the potential of well-trained neural networks to effectively capture the complex, non-linear hardening behavior of polycrystalline materials.

title: Ultrasound-triggered “piezoelectric-chemical” synergy in a smart hydrogel for enhanced craniomaxillofacial bone regeneration
abstract: • Smart hydrogel integrates BaTiO3 and naringin for bone regeneration. • Enables ultrasound-triggered synergy of physical and chemical signals. • The system realizes on-demand sustained release of osteogenic drugs. • Promotes robust bone formation in rat critical-sized calvarial defects.

title: Tailoring Ablation-Resistant ZrCN composites with strategically designed chopped carbon fibers
abstract: This study presents a strategic approach to enhancing both the ablation resistance and thermal shock resistance of zirconium carbonitride (ZrCN) through the architectural design of chopped carbon fibers. A series of Csf/ZrCN composites with systematically varied fiber lengths and volume fractions were fabricated via spark plasma sintering. The composite incorporating 0.5 mm fibers at 30 vol% demonstrated optimal performance, exhibiting a uniform microstructure and maintaining structural integrity without macroscopic fracture after oxyacetylene ablation at 3000 °C, of which linear and mass ablation rates were significantly reduced to –0.67 μm/s and –0.45 mg/s, respectively. Integrated experimental and ab initio molecular dynamics analysis reveals that the superior performance originates from the in-situ formation of a dual-protective Zr–C–N–O cluster network around 2500 K, which enhances oxide viscosity to suppress erosion and forms a dense diffusion barrier. This work provides fundamental insights into the design of fiber-reinforced ultra-high-temperature ceramics for extreme thermal environments.

title: Linear friction welding of Haynes 282 Ni superalloy
abstract: • First-time LFW investigation of Haynes 282 Ni superalloy at 100–500 MPa. • Joints achieved 100% efficiency with fracture in the base metal. • High pressures (300, and 500 MPa) promote grain growth and twinning during PWHT. • Stored strain energy dominates the driving force during PWHT.

title: Injectable hydrogel with immune regulation, anti-inflammation, and angiogenesis for accelerating diabetic wound healing
abstract: • An injectable immunomodulatory hydrogel (CGHP) was developed for accelerating diabetic wound healing. • CGHP is capable of adapting to irregular wounds while overcoming short half-life and burst release of platelet-rich plasma. • Gallic acid and platelet-rich plasma synergistically regulate immunity, promoting M2 macrophage polarization. • This multifunctional hydrogel accelerates wound healing through combined immunomodulation, anti-inflammation, and pro-angiogenesis.

title: Architectural and interfacial effects on texture development and structure–property relationships in wire-drawn multilayer HSLA steel/Ti composites
abstract: The design of heterogeneous materials that activate multiple strengthening mechanisms simultaneously offers a promising route for developing advanced structural composites. In this study, multilayer wire systems were fabricated by combining microalloyed high-strength steel with titanium layers and subjected to multi-stage wire drawing. This process imposed very large plastic strains, driving grain refinement through continuous recrystallization, typical of severe plastic deformation (SPD). Numerical simulations were employed to analyze mechanical inhomogeneity within the layered architecture. The substantial divergence in plasticity between bcc steel and hcp titanium promoted decohesion and fragmentation of titanium layers in 0.3 mm-diameter wires, producing dispersed particles ranging from nanometers to micrometers. These particles contribute to dispersion strengthening. The combined effects of drawing were assessed through mechanical testing and microstructural characterization (optical microscopy, SEM, TEM), supported by synchrotron X-ray diffraction and texture studies. These analyses revealed the interplay of strain hardening, texture evolution, and dislocation-interface interactions. The results demonstrate that strengthening in bcc–hcp heterostructures arises from the synergy of grain refinement, dispersion strengthening, and interface-mediated dislocation pile-up. The study identifies critical processing conditions for achieving high strain accumulation in layered bcc–hcp systems and emphasizes the pivotal role of interphase boundaries between materials with such drastically different plastic properties in controlling their mechanical performance.

title: Fabrication of macroporous amorphous calcium phosphate ceramic scaffolds by pressure-driven sintering at sub-zero temperature using ice microspheres as space holders
abstract: Controlled porosity in pressure-assisted sintered ceramics can be introduced using space holders, which are subsequently removed by heat or dissolution. For some materials, such as the biomaterial amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP), which can be pressure-sintered at room temperature but is sensitive to heat and moisture, finding a suitable space holder is challenging. Here we report that under a uniaxial pressure of 1500 MPa, ACP can be densified to more than 94% of its true density at ∼ -50 to −40 °C, allowing the use of solid substances at sub-zero temperatures as space holders. ACP samples compacted at 1500 MPa at sub-zero temperature had slightly lower density, and their Vickers hardness, biaxial flexural, and splitting tensile strengths reached approximately 80% of those compacted at room temperature. Nevertheless, their mechanical properties were similar to those reported for conventionally sintered hydroxyapatite. Ice microspheres were successfully used as space holders. However, due to crack formation, the highest splitting tensile strengths were exhibited by scaffolds fabricated at 190 and 500 MPa, rather than at 1500 MPa. The feasibility of using ice particles for the fabrication of porous scaffolds was also demonstrated using an alternative method, freeze isostatic pressing, and was shown in other bioceramic systems.

title: Dihydromyricetin-loaded nanofiber membranes accelerate diabetic wound repair via PI3K/AKT-mediated immune regulation
abstract: • Dihydromyricetin-loaded membranes sustain local delivery in diabetic wounds. • The membranes reduce inflammation and promote fibroblast migration. • Repair is linked to phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B signaling. • Treatment speeds wound closure, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis.

title: Real-time stereo vision for in-situ 3D reconstruction and realistic numerical simulation for GTA-WAAM
abstract: • Generate 3D model in real time during the GTA-WAAM process. • Demonstrated high geometric fidelity in geometric modeling. • Achieved realistic numerical simulation to enhance simulation reliability.

title: Analysis of graded cellular solids in static and fatigue compression
Multi-fidelity physics-guided graph neural networks for predicting structure–property relationships in polycrystalline metals
abstract: • Multi-fidelity PGNN is developed for prediction of structure–property linkage. • Introducing physics-guided HP module improves accuracy and sample efficiency. • PGNN rapidly and accurately predicts anisotropic properties and yield loci. • PGNN shows high efficiency and well generalizes across diverse microstructures.

title: Replenishing the oxidation-induced Al-depletion in Cr2AlC MAX phase coatings
abstract: Cr 2 AlC MAX phase coatings are known to form a protective alumina scale upon high temperature oxidation. Scale formation causes Al depletion, which results in the formation of Cr-carbides and pores that, in turn, cause coating failure. Here, we show that the oxidation-driven Al depletion of the coating is prevented by Al-replenishment using an Al-reservoir (Al-containing substrate), thereby extending the coating lifetime. Cr 2 AlC substrates with coarse and fine grain distributions were produced by spark plasma sintering and coated with Cr 2 AlC by magnetron sputtering. Upon oxidation at 1100 °C the Cr 2 AlC coatings, deposited onto a coarse-grained reservoir and onto MgO without an Al-reservoir, showed no significant change in Al content of the coating post-oxidation, and hence no evidence for Al-replenishment from the substrate. However, in the case of a Cr 2 AlC coating, deposited onto a fine-grained substrate, the Al content of the coating post-oxidation remained close to the initial concentration (∼23 at.%). This replenishment is rationalized by the presence of more grain boundaries in the fine-grained substrate, versus the coarse-grained one, enabling sufficient Al diffusion across the substrate/coating interface to offset the Al losses to the scale.

title: A shape memory composite sponge loaded with kaolin for non-compressive traumatic hemostasis
abstract: Effective bleeding control is crucial in surgical procedures and trauma management to ensure patient safety. However, most currently available hemostatic materials perform poorly in cases of noncompressible bleeding. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an innovative composite shape memory sponge loaded with kaolin, consisting of hydroxypropyl cellulose, an acellular dermal matrix, and polycaprolactone (PDX@G 0.5 ), as an effective strategy for non-compressible hemostasis. The introduction of hydroxypropyl cellulose enhances the hydrophilicity of the acellular dermal matrix and polycaprolactone, improving the porous structure of the sponge and its liquid-triggered shape memory capabilities. Additionally, the incorporation of kaolin significantly enhanced the coagulation-promoting ability of the sponge. The experimental results indicated that the PDX@G 0.5 sponge exhibited a porosity of up to 80%, enabling it to rapidly and effectively absorb and activate the endogenous coagulation pathway, thus quickly initiating the intrinsic coagulation cascade. In various rat bleeding models, the PDX@G 0.5 sponge demonstrated significant hemostatic efficacy, with significantly reduced bleeding times and total blood loss compared with traditional hemostatic materials. Furthermore, the shape memory properties of the sponge allowed it to conform closely to irregular wound surfaces. In summary, the PDX@G 0.5 sponge offers a novel and effective solution for trauma hemostasis with broad potential for medical applications.

title: DSC curve fingerprints directly encode mechanical properties of aluminum alloys
abstract: • Full thermogram outperforms hand-crafted DSC features as ML model input. • Linear models match or outperform Random Forest and Gradient Boosting. • β” precipitation region (230–270°C) dominates predictive feature importance. • Cross-alloy transfer achieved with as few as one anchor condition. • DSC established as rapid proxy replacing tensile testing for alloy screening.

title: Cover_266
Editorial Board
Microstructural design and 1100 °C oxidation resistance of a multiphase high entropy alloy
abstract: This study addresses the dual requirements of lightweight and high-temperature oxidation resistance for aircraft engine hot-end components. A multi phase, multi scale high-entropy alloy (HEA) in the NiCoFeCrAlMo system was designed by benchmarking GH4169, achieving a density of only 7.55 g/cm 3 . Its microstructure is based on an interdendritic(ID) FCC/intradendritic(DR) B2 dual-matrix skeleton combined with multi scale precipitates of Laves phase and MC type carbides. It shows excellent oxidation resistance at 1100 °C, with steady-state oxidation kinetics following a sub-parabolic law. The primary oxidation-resistance mechanisms involve the formation of an Al 2 O 3 -based composite protective scale, together with element redistribution and interfacial reconstruction induced by the B2 → FCC phase transformation. MC decomposition, Laves-phase evolution, and the formation of nanoscale (Ti,Nb)O 2 serve as secondary synergistic factors, promoting local oxide-scale densification and increasing the tortuosity of oxygen diffusion paths. In addition, the refinement of B2 grains to 17.3 ± 3.3 μm and the reconstruction of FCC grain boundaries reflect the adjustment of grain-boundary networks during high-temperature oxidation. Together with the Al 2 O 3 -dominated protective scale and the auxiliary densification effect of nanoscale (Ti,Nb)O 2 , these microstructural responses contribute to improved interfacial stability between the oxide scale and the alloy matrix.

title: Nonlinear mechanics of living cells uncovered by multistep amplitude-controlled atomic force microscopy
abstract: Nonlinear viscoelasticity governs the mechanical response of living cells and plays a central role in mechanotransduction, cytoskeletal remodeling, and disease progression. However, experimental approaches capable of systematically probing amplitude-dependent viscoelastic responses at the cellular scale remain limited. Here, we introduce an atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based framework that extends conventional microrheology beyond the linear regime through two complementary protocols: multi-step stress relaxation (SIS-FCs) and multi-step creep force curves (SFS-FCs). We investigated three cell lines: mouse osteoblasts (OFCOLII), mouse myoblasts (C2C12), and human osteosarcoma (MG63), systematically varying step amplitudes to probe distinct deformation regimes. In SIS-FCs, two regimes emerged: small indentation increments (30 nm) induced pronounced cortical softening and increased fluidity, whereas larger increments ( ≥ 50 nm) consistently triggered stress stiffening. In contrast, SFS-FCs exhibited stress stiffening across all force amplitudes, accompanied by characteristic fluidization dynamics with kinetics distinct from those observed in SIS-FCs. Single-curve analysis revealed nonlinear transitions between softening and stiffening, as well as between solidification and fluidization, reflecting dynamic cytoskeletal reorganization under load. Population-level analysis confirmed that these amplitude-dependent mechanical signatures are reproducible across cell types. This framework establishes AFM-based amplitude-controlled microrheology as a strategy to quantify nonlinear cellular mechanics.

title: Refractive index modulation in PS/TiO2 polymer nanocomposites via nanoparticle Dimension control
abstract: The effect of titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanoparticle size on the refractive index (RI) of polystyrene (PS), one of the most important physicochemical parameters of polymer materials, was investigated. TiO₂ nanoparticles (NPs) of three distinct sizes, approximately 5 nm, 10 nm, and 14 nm, were synthesized via a controlled hydrothermal method by varying the precursor composition, solvent ratio, surfactants, and reaction conditions, incorporated into polystyrene matrix at different concentrations, and subsequently fabricated into thin films via spin coating. The effect of particle size, filler loading and UV-curing was systematically investigated. An ~18% increase in the refractive index was observed for UV-cured composites containing large-sized, high-loading TiO₂, accompanied by minimal transparency loss. Surface modification could improve nanoparticle dispersion and interfacial adhesion, reduce light scattering and enhance optical homogeneity. The experimental refractive index was further analyzed theoretically using the linear mixing rule (Agro-Biot rule) and extended Lorentz-Lorentz (L-L) equations.

title: Multiscale elemental segregation and post-HIP microstructural evolution in the laser powder bed fusion of IN738LC nickel-based superalloy
abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) of the medium- γ ′ nickel-based superalloy IN738LC is strongly affected by multiscale elemental segregation, which promotes low-melting interdendritic constituents, defect sensitivity, and a heterogeneous heat-treatment response. However, the mechanistic relationship between rapid solidification-induced segregation in the as-printed condition and subsequent post-HIP microstructural evolution remains insufficiently clarified. In this work, that link is addressed through a correlative multiscale approach combining optical profilometry, SEM/EDS, TEM, EBSD, and μ XCT before and after HIP, together with velocity-dependent solidification modeling. CALPHAD equilibrium/Scheil calculations were further augmented with Aziz solute trapping to capture LPBF nonequilibrium partitioning and phase formation. Guided by this framework, a modified subsolidus–supersolvus hot isostatic pressing (SSHIP) route at 1200 ∘ C , 125 MPa , for 4 h , followed by controlled cooling at 35 – 40 ∘ C min − 1 , was applied. SSHIP eliminated resolvable porosity above the 6 μ m XCT detection limit, reduced the nonrecrystallized fraction from 46.9 % to 22.6 % in the XY plane, and increased the Σ 3 + Σ 9 boundary fraction to 8.5 % in the XZ plane without strong texture development ( J ≈ 1.7 – 2.0 ). These changes were accompanied by marked improvements in yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, strain at maximum stress, and microhardness, providing a mechanistic basis for postprocessing crack-prone γ ′ -strengthened nickel-based superalloys.

title: Fabrication of laser-machined hair-on-a-chip for long-term culture of hair tissue
abstract: Hair loss caused by stress, hormonal changes, medications, genetics, and burns is increasing annually, yet treatment options remain limited. Here we developed a laser-machined hair-on-a-chip model by laser-drilling 150 μm holes into a scaffold and sealing one side with a HUVEC-based hole capping layer to enable long-term, contraction-free culture. Dermal papilla cell (DPCs)–based spheroids with or without LEF1 and Wnt1 transfection (TKH and DKH, respectively) were sequentially combined with fibroblasts (FBs) and keratinocytes (KCs) and cultured for up to 90 days to reconstruct hair-bearing skin tissue. Over prolonged culture, spheroids gradually transformed into hair peg–like structures, with more pronounced morphological maturation observed after 60–90 days. Hair formation was evaluated using SEM, H&E, and immunofluorescence staining. Chips containing growth factor-transfected spheroids exhibited thicker hair structures and increased expression of hair-related proteins K17, K75, and K25, which were further modulated in a time-dependent manner by minoxidil supplementation. Minoxidil treatment also promoted tissue thickening and cellular distribution, likely by improving nutrient and oxygen supply through the HUVEC layer. These results demonstrate that the proposed hair-on-a-chip platform supports progressive HF-like tissue maturation under long-term culture and provides a promising human cell–based in vitro system for studying hair regeneration and evaluating scalp-targeted therapeutic candidates.

title: Cartilage-affinity tea polyphenol liposomes alleviate osteoarthritis by suppressing the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway
abstract: Tea polyphenols are natural antioxidant compounds, yet their function and mechanisms in osteoarthritis (OA) remain unclear. In OA, prolonged inflammation activates chondrocyte inflammation, triggering a series of regulatory axes, while mitochondria, as key effector organelles of inflammation, may play a role in the regulation of OA-related inflammation. However, it remains uncertain whether tea polyphenols impact mitochondrial function. In this study, we utilized transcriptomic sequencing, western blotting (WB), and drug intervention to demonstrate that tea polyphenols alleviate oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in chondrocytes via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, thereby ameliorating chondrocyte phenotype alterations and slowing OA progression. Additionally, we developed a tea polyphenol-based chondrocyte-targeted nanoparticle drug delivery system (Lip-TP-T), which significantly enhanced the in vivo therapeutic efficacy of tea polyphenols.

title: A thermally robust and flexible PDMS monolithic microfluidic device for integrated thermal management and safety of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: The intrinsic trade-off between efficient thermal management and instant safety intervention remains a fundamental bottleneck for advanced lithium-ion battery (LIB) systems. To transcend the limitations of bulky, multi-component designs, we introduce a flexible and monolithic microfluidic platform that synergistically unifies active cooling, passive flame-retardancy, and on-demand fire suppression. This system is fabricated via scalable molding of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), integrating an embedded piezoelectric micropump and a serpentine micromixer. The device achieves a high-precision flow (up to 88.76μL/min) and rapid mixing efficiency (>80% within 8mm), ensuring an optimal coolant-suppressant ratio for operation. Uniquely, the PDMS matrix itself serves as a first-line thermal barrier, forming a stable silica char layer upon flame exposure that maintains structural integrity with a steep 400°C thermal gradient for over 42 minutes. More critically, during nail penetration abuse, the microchannels function as predetermined failure points, enabling immediate, targeted release of fire suppressant to mitigate thermal runaway—reducing peak temperature and electrolyte ejection. With a compact footprint (47×27×6mm3), this work demonstrates a cross-disciplinary paradigm that bridges microfluidic engineering and battery safety, offering a scalable, integrated solution for safe LIBs in high-density and wearable applications.

title: Towards oxidative aging-resistant design of SBS-modified asphalt mixtures: Role of oxygen diffusion and pore structure
abstract: • Physical pore pathways outweigh thermal effects in driving oxygen diffusion of asphalt mixture. • Oxygen permeability directly dictates the rate and severity of long-term thermal-oxidative degradation. • Quantitative predictive models accurately forecast asphalt durability based on oxygen diffusion coefficient.

title: Metal-phenolic networks: a favorable combination for disease treatment
abstract: Metal ions and polyphenols possess special pharmacological activities and are widely researched for various disease treatments. When they undergo a favorable combination, metal-phenolic networks (MPNs) are formed through the coordination-driven self-assembly between polyphenols and metal ions. MPNs are widely used as multifunctional nanoplatforms, combining the pharmacological properties of metal ions with the biological functions of polyphenols, as well as possessing targeted delivery and microenvironment-responsiveness. This review provides a systematic summary of the physicochemical properties and pharmacological mechanisms of polyphenolic compounds (e.g., EGCG, TA) and metal ions (Fe 3+ , Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ , etc.), and elaborates on the fabrication strategies of MPNs and their applications in the treatment of tumors, infections, inflammation, degenerative disorders, and other diseases. The synergistic mechanisms of MPNs for disease treatment are emphasized, including ferroptosis, cuproptosis, and immunomodulation. We also address the challenges and improvement strategies of MPNs for their clinical translation. This work provides a foundation for the rational design and expansion of biomedical applications of MPNs.

title: A photocrosslinked micelle-hydrogel hybrid loaded with human dental pulp stem cells for cartilage defect repair
abstract: • A photocrosslinked micelle-hydrogel hybrid (GMKFM) for cartilage defect repair. • GMKFM provides mechanical stability and enables sustained KGN release. • GMKFM supports chondrogenesis of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs). • hDPSCs-laden GMKFM enhances cartilage repair in a rat model.

title: Bone-targeted carbon dots coordinate osteo–angiogenic coupling and antibacterial defense to promote periodontal regeneration
abstract: • Carbon quantum dots with catalase-like and peroxidase-like nanozyme activities; bone-targeting rate: 75.57%. • Membrane depolarization–induced antibacterial activity; bactericidal efficiency exceeding 95%. • Multifunctional carbon quantum dots coupled with angiogenesis, regulation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, balance of bone homeostasis.

title: Inoculation of heterogeneous nucleation site on microstructure and mechanical properties of A7003 aluminum alloy manufactured by wire-type directed energy deposition
abstract: In this study, the effects of Al 3 (Ti 1-x Zr x ) heterogeneous nucleation site particles on the formability, microstructure and mechanical properties of A7003 (Al-Zn-Mg) alloy samples manufactured by the wire-type directed energy deposition (DED) method were studied. The lattice matching between the Al 3 (Ti 1-x Zr x ) heterogeneous nucleation site particles and the primary crystal of A7003 Al alloy at solidification temperature is found to be good. The formability of wire-type DED can be improved and the occurrence of defects can be suppressed by addition of the heterogeneous nucleation site particles. The grain size and aspect ratio of the samples manufactured using the inoculated wire were found to be smaller than those of the uninoculated wire. It is also found that samples manufactured using uninoculated wire without heterogeneous nucleation site particles (uninoculated samples) show strong anisotropy and position dependence in mechanical properties. However, those containing heterogeneous nucleation site particles (inoculated samples) have higher mechanical properties without anisotropy and position dependence. It is concluded that the parts of the A7003 Al alloy with higher mechanical properties can be additively manufactured by inoculation of Al 3 (Ti 1-x Zr x ) heterogeneous nucleation site particles.

title: Design of a novel scanning strategy for formation of extremely strong textures in hexagonal materials through laser powder bed fusion
abstract: While crystallographic texture control in cubic metals via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) has been demonstrated in recent years, achieving such control in hexagonal metals remains a significant challenge. In the present work we present a novel route for the development of a very strong texture in a hexagonal close-packed (hcp)-structured Mg alloy through LPBF. It was achieved by employing reciprocal scanning with a 120° rotation between layers, aligning with the symmetry of Mg’s hcp crystal structure. This unique scanning strategy was designed through computational simulation of the heat flux in the melt pool and consideration of the six-fold rotational symmetry along the [0001] axis of the hcp structure. The texture formation was driven by preferential < 11 2 ¯ 0 > crystal growth along a direction inclined at approximately 60° to each scanning direction (0°, 120°, and 240°). The LPBF-fabricated specimens showed an anisotropic stress–strain responses in compression test owing to the crystal orientation-dependent selection of operative slip systems, similar to the behavior in a Mg single crystal. These findings highlight the potential in optimizing the scanning strategy by reflecting the symmetry of the crystal structure. This is particularly crucial for LPBF manufacturing non-cubic metals with prominent textures.

title: Exploring the addition of Fe3O4 coated carbonyl iron powder to FeSi Soft magnetic composites: advantages and challenges
abstract: • Carbonyl Iron Powder (CIP) oxidation is an easy way to vary magnetic properties. • Oxidation time is an effective technique for controlling coating thickness of CIP. • Oxygen content of coated powders was measured and coating thickness calculated. • Higher coating thickness does not always lead to lower losses at high frequencies. • Optimum coating thickness depends majorly on intended application frequency range.

title: Camphorquinone, a popularly-used photoinitiator, induced ER responses in dental pulp cells: Association with MAPK signaling, cytotoxicity, 8-isoprostane and PGE2 production
abstract: Composite resin and photoinitiator camphorquinone (CQ) are used in dentistry to restore tooth decay, but potentially affect pulpal viability and inflammation. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress molecules, such as Grp78, PERK, IRE1α and ATF6, are responsible for cellular adaptive response to toxicants. This study aimed to clarify the ER stress molecules in CQ toxicity of human dental pulp cells (HDPCs). CQ exposure increased ER and mitochondrial density. CQ stimulated mRNA expression of key ER stress markers, including Grp78, PERK, IRE1α, ATF6, eIF2α, XBP1 and ATF4. CQ promoted Grp78, PERK, IRE1α and ATF6 protein expression. U0126 (a MEK/ERK inhibitor) blocked the expression of most CQ-induced mRNA markers, but not Grp78 and XBP1. Five common ER stress inhibitors (NKP1339, Kira6, GSK2606414, phenylbutyrate, and Ceapin-A7) failed to prevent CQ’s cytotoxicity to HDPCs. Kira6 (IRE1α inhibitor) attenuated CQ-induced 8-isoprostane and PGE2 production, whereas others showed no consistent benefit. These results indicate that HDPCs expressed ER stress molecules. CQ stimulates ER stress response’s molecules. MEK/ERK signaling is associated with CQ-induced ER stress responses. Moreover, IRE1α signaling mediates CQ-induced 8-isoprostane and PGE2 production, but not directly involved in CQ-induced cytotoxicity. IRE1α signaling may represent a potential target for mitigating pulp inflammation and oxidative responses after operative restoration.

title: Bioactive metal-organic framework with efficient ROS supply ability for enhanced ferroptosis-like cancer cell death
abstract: • Engineered a novel Cu-TCPP MOF-based nanoparticle to induce ferroptosis. • Enhanced ferroptosis via synergistic ROS generation and GSH depletion-triggered lipid peroxidation. • Provides a promising strategy to boost ferroptosis therapy efficacy in vivo .

title: Modeling intramuscular fat infiltration in the engineered skeletal muscle myobundles
abstract: Intramuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) infiltration is primarily induced by aging, trauma, metabolic disorders, which is associated with various musculoskeletal diseases. However, a model that can simulate the pathological changes of this disease is lacking. In this manuscript, we developed an engineered skeletal muscle myobundle that enables the recapitulation of physiological structure, function, and contractile force in vitro. Human primary myoblasts were seeded into PDMS molds containing 3D-printed micropillars. After induced myogenic differentiation, myobundles with physiological structure and function were generated between the micropillars. By co-culturing with adipocyte spheroids derived from mesenchymal stem cells, IMAT-infiltrated myobundles can be recapitulated in vitro. With this model, we demonstrate that IMAT infiltration leads to structural and functional deterioration of the engineered myobundles. Transcriptomic analysis revealed IMAT-induced alterations in gene expression of myobundle, involving immune activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and metabolic reprogramming. Moreover, vitamin D intervention markedly improved both the structural integrity and contractile performance of IMAT-infiltrated myobundles. This work establishes a physiologically relevant model of IMAT-infiltrated myobundles, offering a promising platform for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic evaluation in human skeletal muscle.

title: Lattice anharmonic dynamics induced ultra-low thermal conductivity of Si doped Ag2S thermoelectric materials
abstract: Thermoelectric materials hold broad application prospects in waste heat recovery, yet the understanding of the thermal conduction mechanism remained insufficient and limited their development. Si doped Ag 2 S thermoelectric materials had prepared by vacuum electromagnetic induction melting technique with holding temperature at mushy zone, and the thermal transfer mechanism were investigated through anharmonic lattice dynamic analysis. The Ag 2-x Si x S alloys were prepared in one step, with the preparation time reduced to less than 40 min. X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy indicated the formation of major α -Ag 2 S phase and minor Ag 3 S phase. With the increase of Si content, the thermal conductivity ( κ l ) decreased from 0.87 Wm −1 K −1 to 0.38 Wm −1 K −1 at 603 K, exhibited a significant reduction of over 56%. The lowest κ l of 0.29 Wm −1 K −1 was achieved at 431 K with the Si concentration of 15 at%. The anharmonic lattice dynamic calculation revealed Si atoms promoted the high order anharmonicity, the weakening of the optical branch vibration mode caused the ultra-low κ l . The electronic structure calculation showed that doping led to the carriers more localized and reduced the electronic thermal transfer. The overall measurements indicated that Si doping enhanced carrier mobility and suppressed the thermal conductivity without reducing the Seebeck coefficient significantly.

title: Multiscale micromechanical modeling of the elastic properties of the S2 layer in archaeological wood cell walls
abstract: Predicting the elastic properties of archaeological wood is challenging because chemically driven degradation, including constituent loss and compositional change, is coupled across scales with microstructural evolution such as porosity development and moisture variation. This study develops a parameterized multiscale composition–structure–property framework for the secondary-wall S2 layer based on Voigt–Reuss mixing relations. Constituent-loss coefficients are introduced to translate chemical analyses of archaeological Chinese fir into a micromechanical model of the S2 layer, and molecular dynamics simulations are used to provide the moisture-dependent elastic and shear moduli of crystalline cellulose, amorphous cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin as constitutive inputs. The model predicts the elastic properties of the S2 layer in both modern and archaeological Chinese fir with good agreement with nanoindentation measurements. The results suggest that stiffness reduction in archaeological wood is governed by the coupled effects of constituent degradation, moisture-induced matrix softening, and porosity development. The proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for relating chemical composition and microstructural change to the effective mechanical response of degraded wood cell walls, and may support the mechanical assessment and conservation of archaeological wood.

title: Injectable rhNGF-functionalized silk hydrogels derived from transgenic silkworms accelerate sciatic nerve regeneration in rats
abstract: Peripheral nerve injury is a major clinical challenge that often results in incomplete functional recovery. Although nerve growth factor is a promising therapeutic molecule for nerve repair, its clinical application is limited by the high cost of recombinant protein production and the burst release associated with conventional post-loading delivery strategies. In this study, we developed an integrated design strategy termed source functionalization. Transgenic silkworms were generated to express recombinant human nerve growth factor in the silk gland under the control of the fibroin heavy chain promoter. This enabled the co-production of recombinant human nerve growth factor with endogenous silk fibroin and its physical entrapment within the fibroin matrix, allowing sustained release. Direct processing of these glands yielded an intrinsically functionalized injectable hydrogel, avoiding complex purification and reconstitution steps. In vitro , the hydrogel promoted neuronal proliferation and differentiation. In a rat sciatic nerve crush model, it significantly improved functional recovery and enhanced axonal regeneration and remyelination. These results demonstrate a cost-effective and scalable one-step strategy for preparing bioactive silk-based materials for peripheral nerve repair.

title: Recent progress in green synthesis of bioinspired nanoceria for therapeutic applications
abstract: With the rapid development of nanobiotechnology, green synthesis of cerium oxide nanoparticles (CeNPs) and their hybrid systems has emerged as a promising strategy for designing functional materials with tunable physicochemical and biological properties. This review focuses on the relationships among structure, processing, properties, and function of green and hybrid nanoceria, emphasizing how synthesis routes derived from plant, food, and microbial sources govern surface chemistry, defect states, and redox behavior. Particular attention is given to the Ce 3+ and Ce 4+ redox cycling, which enables catalytic regulation of oxidative stress and underlies key functionalities such as antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative effects. In addition, bio-derived surface coatings and hybrid architectures are discussed as critical design parameters that enhance interfacial interactions, stability, and biological performance. By integrating insights from synthesis strategies, material structure, and functional outcomes, this review highlights the design principles that distinguish green-synthesized CeNPs from conventional counterparts. Finally, current challenges, including toxicity evaluation, biodistribution, and scalability, are critically analyzed to outline future directions for the rational design of CeNP-based materials in advanced biomedical and engineering applications.

title: Thermal cycling-driven microstructural changes of eutectic Al–Si phase change materials in SS304 containers revealed by multi-modal imaging
abstract: Aluminum-based Al–Si alloys are widely used as phase change materials (PCMs) in thermal energy storage (TES) systems owing to their high volumetric latent heat and superior thermal conductivity. However, their long-term reliability is limited by degradation processes that remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we employ a multimodal, correlative characterization framework to systematically resolve the degradation behavior of eutectic Al–Si PCMs in contact with SS304 containers under repeated thermal cycling. By integrating high-resolution electron microscopy, three-dimensional X-ray fluorescence (3D XRF) imaging, and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), we directly link spatially resolved compositional and microstructural evolution to changes in thermophysical properties.
