After specific accumulation at tumor sites and with photoacoustic imaging guidance for HIFU surgery, the nanosystem rapidly dissociates and releases loaded drugs into the postoperative TME. Hypoxia-adaptive AQ4N is then metabolically activated, mediating the antitumor immunity associated with immunogenic cell death. Meanwhile, NLG919 suppresses the IDO pathway, and CaCO 3 depletes lactate to mitigate the immunosuppressive TME that was worsened following the surgery. As a result, the nanosystem greatly enhances antitumor immune responses after HIFU, showing excellent efficacy against tumor recurrence and metastasis. This offers a successful paradigm for improving the postoperative immunotherapy with immune enhancers for all surgical procedures.

title: Revolutionizing oral and maxillofacial region: the Promise of multiscale composite materials
abstract: The oral and maxillofacial region is characterized by a complex structure and a high functional density, performing critical functions. Its unique characteristics encompass complex anatomical structures, intensive motor functions, unique microbial environment, a warm, humid, pH-fluctuating environment, and aesthetic requirements, which impose stringent requirements on biomaterials. Multiscale composite materials, which leverage synergistic design and multifunctional integration across nano-, micro-, and macro-scales, have become a major focus of materials for the oral and maxillofacial region. Multiscale composite materials for oral and maxillofacial region must possess five core e properties: mechanical adaptability requires match hard and soft tissue; surface interfacial properties can regulate cellular behavior, enabling the material to rapidly integrate with the host organism; environmental responsiveness can intelligently respond to multiple stimuli, thereby triggering functional activation; aesthetic properties aim for biomimicry in morphology, transparency, and color stability; and comprehensive biological properties balances biosafety, functionality, and degradation/persistence profiles. At present, multiscale composite materials in the oral and maxillofacial regions still face numerous challenges, including limited functionality, insufficient long-term stability, and unbalanced functional integration. Future research should prioritize the introduction of artificial intelligence-assisted design to develop materials with more comprehensive properties and accelerate their clinical translation.

title: Incoherent interfacial energy from first-principles
abstract: Incoherent interfaces are ubiquitous in materials, yet their interfacial properties remain poorly understood. Due to the high computational cost, density functional theory (DFT) studies are typically restricted to coherent or semicoherent interfaces. In this work, we propose a novel approach to estimate incoherent interfacial energies within a DFT-accessible supercell size. Based on the so-called “incoherent -surface” concept, we first develop a classical-model-potential-based framework to capture the evolution of the one-dimensional (1D) incoherent -surface with increasing cell size. The method is then extended to the Ni/Ni 3 Nb interface in a quasi-1D configuration, and further to a fully two-dimensional case of the Cu–Nb incoherent interface possessing very different lattice mismatch along the two in-plane directions. All investigated systems exhibit a consistent smoothing behavior of the -surface with increasing cell size. Moreover, the average value of the incoherent -surface is demonstrated to be a robust estimator for the incoherent interfacial energy, which is shown to converge rapidly even at small cell sizes. This work extends the applicability of first-principles methods to ideal incoherent interfaces and deepens the understanding of the coherent versus incoherent -surface concepts.

title: Interphase engineering in carbon black–reinforced piezoelectric nanocomposites: A combined experimental and micromechanical modeling study
abstract: Piezoelectric polymer–ceramic composites are promising for sensors, energy-harvesting, and flexible electronics. However, their performance is often limited by weak filler–matrix coupling. To address this challenge, carbon black (CB) nanoparticles with controlled surface modification were introduced to engineer the interphase in KNN–epoxy composites. A physics-based micromechanical model was developed to systematically investigate the role of interphase characteristics on the electro-mechanical response. The model captures the coupled effects of filler dispersion, interphase properties, and conductive network formation, and successfully reproduces the experimentally observed non-monotonic dependence of piezoelectric performance on CB content. Experimentally, three CB types—untreated (CB0), mildly oxidized (CB1), and heavily oxidized (CB2)—were evaluated. CB1-based composites achieved the best balance of mechanical, dielectric, and piezoelectric properties, showing improved dispersion, adhesion, and polarization. By integrating experimental results with predictive modeling, this study reveals that interphase engineering governs charge transport and polarization behavior, and establishes a design framework for optimizing piezoelectric performance in multi-scale hybrid nanocomposites.

title: Topology-driven hydrogel microspheres for cartilage repair
abstract: Cartilage defects arise from localized loss or disruption of the articular cartilage layer, typically accompanied by extracellular matrix (ECM) depletion, chondrocyte dyshomeostasis, and progressive joint degeneration. Owing to the avascular and aneural nature of cartilaginous tissue, intrinsic self-repair is limited, and no available clinical treatments are effective for complete rehabilitation of articular cartilage function. Injectable hydrogel microsphere (HMS) filling strategies have recently emerged as a promising modality that enables precise control over microarchitecture, biochemical presentation, and mechanical cues within cartilage lesions. By enabling finely tunable microarchitecture, broad payload versatility, and precise spatiotemporal responsiveness, HMS-based scaffolds offer an advanced bioengineering platform for orchestrating cell recruitment, immune modulation, and ECM remodeling during cartilage regeneration. Herein, we systematically focus on topology-centric and mechanism-oriented material design principles, fabrication technologies, and representative HMS architectures, with particular emphasis on how micro-/nano-scale topological functionalization synergistically regulates the biological microenvironment throughout the cartilage repair cascade. Furthermore, rationally tailored HMS topologies are delineated in alignment with cartilage-specific demands, including cellular regulation, bioactive factor delivery, lubrication restoration, and microenvironment crosstalk. Future perspectives highlight refined smart HMS architectures, scalable manufacturing, and translational potential, ultimately aiming to establish a programmable and practicable cartilage tissue engineering platform.

title: Unraveling the mechanisms for high-temperature mechanical properties of a high-manganese austenitic steel at 500 °C
abstract: Conventional construction steel suffers severe softening at 500 ℃ under short-term fire exposure (the decrease of ultimate strength on reduction of 50 %, less than 500 MPa), while traditional austenitic steel exhibits drastically elevated stacking fault energy (SFE) at high temperature, which restricts Shockley partial dislocation dissociation and twinning, resulting in deterioration of high-temperature mechanical properties. This study compared high-manganese austenitic steel (HAMS, Fe-17.85Mn-5.21Al- 0.52C-0.18Si wt.%) tensile properties at 500 ℃ with and without prior 10 h thermal exposure. High-temperature tensile tests conducted at 500 ℃ demonstrate that 10 h thermal exposure creates favorable thermodynamic conditions for (Fe,Mn) 3 AlC precipitation which reduced 40 mJ·m −2 SFE and facilitating the dissociation of Shockley 1/6 < 112 > partial dislocations. Moreover, the thermal exposure creates microstructural evolution is characterized by an increment in low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) from 61.9%±1.9% to 69.9%±2.2%, a fragmented distribution of Schmid factors. The synergy between Lomer-Cottrell (L-C) locks and twins optimizes the properties of Fe-17.85Mn-5.21Al-0.52C-0.18Si alloy at 500 ℃, it achieves a yield strength (YS) of 416 MPa and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 532 ± 1.5 MPa (a reduction of 39%, surpassing the unexposed state 487 ± 2.0 MPa,), with ductility only decreasing by 5.3% (from 36.0%±0.6% to 34.1%±0.4%).

title: Direct ink writing of ammonium perchlorate propellants for solid rockets using a dual-cure approach
abstract: This work investigates the fabrication of ammonium perchlorate composite propellants using a dual-cure (ultraviolet and thermally curable) binder via direct ink writing and compares their performance with conventionally cast counterparts. The dual-cure approach enables rapid solidification during printing through ultraviolet irradiation, followed by thermal curing to ensure complete network formation. Propellants with 70 wt% solids loading, with and without aluminum, were fabricated and evaluated in terms of mechanical properties, thermal decomposition, and combustion behavior. Dynamic mechanical analysis revealed comparable crosslink density and glass transition temperature between printed and cast binders, indicating similar network development. Mechanical property testing showed improved tensile properties for printed non-aluminized propellants, while aluminized formulations exhibited comparable behavior between manufacturing methods likely due to ultraviolet attenuation by aluminum particles. Thermal analysis confirmed similar decomposition characteristics across all formulations. Burning rate measurements demonstrated that manufacturing method had negligible influence on combustion performance. These results demonstrate that dual-cure DIW enables the fabrication of AP propellants with performance comparable to cast materials, while providing enhanced geometric flexibility and manufacturing capability.

title: Improving the biocompatibility of photo-crosslinkable poly(2-oxazoline)-based hydrogels for stem cell research
abstract: Poly(2-oxazoline) (POx)-based hydrogels were developed as a biocompatible, tunable alternative to poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-based materials for cell-instructive biomaterials. Using cationic ring-opening polymerization, photo-crosslinkable POx macromonomers were synthesized and processed into hydrogels with adjustable cross-linking density, stiffness and swelling behavior. The intrinsic “stealth” character of poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (PEtOx) was systematically modified through incorporation of monomers bearing methyl ester functionalities (MestOx) to enable the subsequent covalent coupling of integrin-binding motifs like the RGD-peptide sequence to the formed hydrogels, transforming the inert matrix into a bioactive scaffold. The RGD motif describes the core-sequence of three-amino acids with an Arginine-Glycine-Aspartic acid sequence, found in many ECM proteins like fibronectin, vitronectin or fibrinogen. Human mesenchymal stem cells (huMSCs) cultured on these RGD-functionalized POx-based hydrogels exhibited enhanced adhesion, spreading, proliferation and osteogenic differentiation compared with non-functionalized controls. Increasing RGD content correlated positively with focal adhesion formation and alkaline phosphatase activity, while softer hydrogel formulations further supported cell proliferation. These findings demonstrate that RGD-modified POx-based hydrogels provide a versatile, cytocompatible and tunable platform for the engineering of defined microenvironments in stem cell research and regenerative medicine.

title: Polyolefin–Based Bitumen Modifiers for Durable Asphalt Pavements: Structure–Property Relationships, Compatibilization Strategies, and Design Implications
abstract: Polyolefin-based bitumen modifiers are emerging as cost-effective, circular alternatives to styrene-based elastomers in road construction. Their tunable mechanical performance and saturated backbone suit diverse climates, however, the chemical inertness and poor affinity to asphaltenes often compromise binder compatibility and storage stability. This review describes recent advances in polyolefin-modified bitumen from polymer- and bitumen-science perspectives, emphasizing how modifier architecture, functionalization route, and binder hybridization strategies influence phase structure and rheological response. The physicochemical nature of bitumen-polyolefin interactions is first addressed to elucidate underlying incompatibility mechanisms. The discussion provides insight into metallocene-catalyzed polyolefin elastomers, vulcanizable polyolefin rubbers, and functionalized polyolefins prepared via reactive extrusion, high-pressure polymerization, or catalytic functionalization. Further, more complex hybrid systems combining crumb rubber from post-consumer tires and polyolefin-based compatibilizers are critically reviewed. For each presented modifier class, microstructure, storage stability, and linear/nonlinear rheological assessments are evaluated to identify structure–property correlations and effective bitumen modification and compatibilization strategies. This work synthesizes literature reports into a unified framework that systematically catalogues recognized compatibilization approaches for enhancing the miscibility and performance of polyolefin–based binders. It concludes with design implications and research priorities for translating these insights into high–performance, sustainable paving materials approaching the performance targets set by styrene–based elastomer technologies.

title: Ultra-precision grinding process and compensation of cylindrical structure array mold
abstract: WC-Co carbide cylindrical array molds are essential for the high-efficiency manufacturing of high-precision optical lenses. However, due to the extreme hardness, brittleness, and complex dynamic mechanical response of the material, achieving high-efficiency and high-precision machining while suppressing surface damage remains a critical challenge. By utilizing a calibrated JH-2 constitutive model, this work analyzes the material removal mechanisms of WC-Co to disclose dynamic failure behaviors and define the critical depth threshold for ductile-regime removal. Subsequently, a hybrid grinding strategy is developed by integrating rough grinding via a profile diamond wheel with fine compensation using an ultra-thin diamond wheel, complemented by a constant material removal rate global path planning method. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a form accuracy PV of 2.43 μm and a surface roughness Sa of 17.025 nm for the array mold, with excellent morphological uniformity. These results indicate that the proposed strategy is beneficial not only for deterministic form generation, but also for suppressing brittle damage and preserving the surface integrity required for functional structured molds.

title: Phase field modeling of thermal-mismatch induced fracture in glass-ceramic sealing of solid oxide cell stacks
abstract: Thermal mismatches during cooling of solid oxide cell (SOC) stacks generate stresses in glass–ceramic sealings, driving cracks that may threaten gas tightness. Conventional strength-based or linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM) approaches are limited by geometry sensitivity or the requirement for predefined crack paths. To overcome these limitations, a phase-field fracture model with stack homogenization is developed and validated. This approach is insensitive to geometric irregularities and eliminates the need of predefined crack paths, and can be applied to full stacks.The study quantifies the impact of sealing thickness, thermal expansion coefficient (TEC), and external compression: for a typical stack design, crack growth remains localized; failure risk rises for thicker seals (\(>=\!1500\,\si{\micro\meter}\)) or severe mismatch with smaller TEC of seals (\(\approx 9\times10^{-6}\,\si{\per\kelvin}\)), while moderate compression suppresses propagation. To guide engineering, thickness–TEC design maps are introduced, rendering smooth iso-damage contours and a single failure boundary derived from energy scaling; external load appears as a translation of the TEC axis, shifting the boundary accordingly. The design maps allow for the rapid identification of optimal material-geometry combinations that ensure structural integrity under operational loads. This work provides a non-existing pathway for the reliable design and failure prevention of brittle sealants in SOC stacks.

title: Inverse design of acoustic topological insulators based on physics-informed neural network
abstract: Research on acoustic topological insulators has advanced, with their topologically protected edge states enabling dissipationless sound transmission and showing potential in anti-interference acoustic devices and communication. However, precise and efficient design remains a challenge due to the complexities of geometric configurations and the sporadic nature of phase transitions. This study proposes a Topological-evaluation Network, a physics-informed neural network framework that integrates physical band structure information into the network as an embedding structure. Through convolutional operations for feature separation, it enables the inverse design and mechanistic analysis of acoustic topological insulators. A symmetry-related Core and Perturbation Design Strategy was discovered through this framework. Compared to traditional trial-and-error methods based on numerical simulation, this strategy simplifies the acquisition of acoustic structures with topological insulation properties. It effectively optimizes the design efficiency for systems with complex physical mechanisms. By integrating physical band information, the framework achieves a 12-fold reduction in training data volume. The proposed model achieves a 95 % prediction accuracy in identifying topological phases, significantly accelerating the design of complex acoustic insulators. This approach offers extensive applications for future analysis and design of complex acoustic topological systems.

title: Performance of a broadband biconical-shaped metamaterial absorber with left-handed response for sensing chemical constituents in skincare products
abstract: This study proposes a broadband metamaterial absorber for sensing chemical constituents in skincare products. The designed unit cell comprises a gold core and a polytetrafluoroethylene dielectric layer, with an overall dimension of 20 µm × 20 µm. The absorber exhibits a left-handed electromagnetic response, with 99.9% absorption at resonance frequencies and a bandwidth of 1.97 THz. The polarisation spectrum indicates stable performance from 0° to 45°. The absorber’s surface current and impedance yield near-unity absorption at resonance frequencies, indicating good agreement. Most commonly used hydroquinone, ethanolamine, and parabens are selected as the chemical constituents for sensing applications. The permittivity of these chemicals, based on their terahertz dielectric properties, is determined using Lorentz dispersion parameters. The resonance frequency changed as the chemical concentration increased from 1% to 5%, yielding a maximum sensitivity of 2.12 THz/RIU, a quality factor up to 70.13, and a figure of merit of 25.36. Overall, the study highlighted that the uniquely designed metamaterial absorber can be used in terahertz chemical sensing for cosmetic safety monitoring

title: Potential use of Rigid 10K in VPP-UVL additive-manufactured mold inserts for injection molding of plastic parts: Opportunities and challenges
abstract: In recent years, additive manufacturing (AM) has gained increasing attention for its integration with injection molding (IM), specifically through the production of mold inserts. In the case of mold inserts produced by vat photopolymerization (VPP), this integration is limited by the thermal-insulating nature and anisotropic shrinkage of photocurable resins. This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of Rigid 10 K, a photocurable resin glass-filled (55–75 wt%), assessing its suitability for hybrid IM. The work includes thermal, rheological, chemical, and morphological analyses, besides examining the effects of print orientation on mechanical properties, dimensional accuracy, and shrinkage. ANOVA results confirmed that print orientation is critical for mechanical properties such as flexural modulus, tensile stress, and strain (p < 0.001), whereas its influence on flexural stress was moderate (p = 0.03), and Young’s Modulus was unaffected (p = 0.45). Z-orientation maximized structural integrity, increasing tensile strength by 29.4 % and reducing the shrinkage by 30.4–52.0 % compared to flat orientations. Numerical IM simulations revealed heat accumulation and associated defects in parts molded with the Rigid 10 K insert. In physical trials, the insert withstood 50 injection cycles without catastrophic failure. This study establishes design-oriented guidelines for improving insert longevity and provides a framework for the integration of highly filled VPP resins in IM applications.

title: Explainable machine learning reveals orbital design rules for reversible H2 adsorption on single-atom-doped TiO2 nanoparticles
abstract: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier for decarbonized technologies, but reversible on-board storage remains challenging because efficient uptake and release under near-ambient conditions require a narrow adsorption-energy window. Here, we combine high-throughput electronic-structure calculations with explainable machine learning to uncover the governing factors of molecular hydrogen adsorption on single-atom-doped TiO 2 nanoparticles. Screening 30 dopants across perpendicular and parallel H 2 adsorption geometries reveals substantial variation in adsorption strength and clear configuration-dependent behavior. From a broad descriptor space, a three-stage feature-selection strategy identifies eight robust predictors, which are further reduced through symbolic regression to an analytical and interpretable model. The resulting descriptor space is governed by H–H activation, dopant–H 2 distance, and -electron rearrangement. Adsorption within the target window is associated with balanced -donation and -back-donation, with Group 4 and 5 transition metals emerging as the most robust candidates across geometries. Combined with Langmuir-based desorption estimates, these results provide a mechanism-based screening rule for reversible hydrogen storage on doped TiO 2 .

title: A healing-constrained multi-objective design strategy for self-healing thermal barrier coatings: A modeling and simulation study
abstract: Conventional thickness design of thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) is mainly governed by thermal insulation and fracture-mechanics-based delamination resistance. As for self-healing thermal barrier coatings (SH-TBCs), such thermo-mechanical criteria alone are insufficient, because they do not determine whether a given architecture can provide adequate healing-agent supply to satisfy crack-sealing demand. In this study, a dimensionless healing sufficiency index, H , is introduced into the thickness design of an APS TiC-containing SH-TBC system to quantify the matching between healing-agent supply and crack-filling demand. On this basis, a healing-constrained multi-objective design strategy is established to balance thermal insulation, interfacial delamination resistance and self-healing functionality. The results show that, after considering the risks associated with insufficient healing and constrained crack-body expansion caused by excessive filling, approximately 80 % of the thickness designs previously regarded as feasible under conventional thermo-mechanical criteria are excluded. This indicates that thermo-mechanical criteria alone can substantially overestimate the true feasible design domain of SH-TBCs. A favorable thickness window is identified, corresponding to a TiC–Al 2 O 3 –YSZ (TAZ) layer thickness of 30–40 μm and a YSZ top-coat thickness of 160–200 μm. High-temperature oxidation experiments further show that the optimized thin-TAZ architecture retains effective crack-sealing capability and excellent thermo-mechanical match.

title: Synergistic crack suppression mechanism of high-temperature preheating assisted laser cladding for MAR-M247 turbine blades
abstract: MAR-M247, a Hf-rich nickel-based superalloy, is widely used for turbine blades, but its high thermal cracking sensitivity limits laser cladding repair, which traditionally requires preheating above 1000 °C. To address this, a synergistic strategy combining process parameter control and induction preheating was proposed to achieve crack-free laser cladding. The effects of preheating temperature and linear energy density on crack formation, microstructure evolution, and dendritic spacing were investigated using optical microscopy, SEM, EDS, and industrial CT. The solidification path and elemental segregation were analyzed to reveal the thermal cracking mechanism. A random forest model with interval-based data augmentation was developed to predict crack probability for small sample sets. Results indicate that thermal cracks include both solidification and liquation cracks, initiated by segregation at grain boundaries forming MC carbides and γ/γ′ eutectic phases, which reduce cohesion. Preheating temperature shows a non-monotonic effect on substrate dendritic spacing, with optimal crack suppression at 948–990 °C and linear energy density of 23.1–27.8 J/mm. This study clarifies the micro-mechanisms of thermal cracking and provides a reliable intelligent prediction method for process parameter optimization in MAR-M247 laser cladding.

title: Biomimetic hydrogel delivers engineered exosomes to attenuate cell senescence by AKG-mediated mitochondrial function restoration for osteoarthritis
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common chronic degenerative joint disease. The disruption of intracellular homeostasis driven by chondrocyte senescence represents a major challenge in current clinical management of OA. Herein, we developed a mitochondrial function‑modulating strategy to disrupt the oxidative stress–inflammation–senescence network in osteoarthritic chondrocytes. In this approach, scutellarin was loaded into stem cell‑derived exosomes (Exosomes–Scutellarin, ES) to mitigate oxidative stress‑induced mitochondrial damage and exert anti‑inflammatory effects. The ES were further modified with macrophage membranes to form MES nanoparticles, enhancing their targeting capability to inflammatory sites. The MES nanoparticles were then encapsulated in a sodium alginate–hyaluronic acid hydrogel, yielding a multifunctional composite hydrogel (Sodium alginate −Hyaluronic acid hydrogel @Macrophage membrane −Exosomes–Scutellarin, SH@MES). SH@MES not only suppressed oxidative stress but also prolonged nanoparticle retention within the joint cavity. In vitro results showed that Macrophage membrane–Exosomes–Scutellarin (MES) enhanced chondrocyte uptake and alleviated senescence through α‑ketoglutarate (AKG)‑mediated regulation of mitochondrial function. In vivo experiments revealed that SH@MES exhibited excellent joint retention and cartilage repair capacity in a mouse OA model, effectively delaying disease progression. In summary, SH@MES disrupts the oxidative stress–inflammatory–senescence network in chondrocytes via AKG‑driven modulation of mitochondrial function, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for osteoarthritis.

title: Impact of temperature on C-S-H properties: Chemical composition, density, porosity, and specific surface area
abstract: A comprehensive investigation of the impact of temperature on C-S-H properties over 5-90℃ was conducted using six model cement systems prepared with different C 3 S/C 2 S ratios. A fast DTG deconvolution method and a novel algorithm based on water–vapor adsorption were proposed to guarantee the accuracy and accessibility of the derived C-S-H properties. Test results indicate that the Ca/Si ratio of C-S-H generated by hydration of silicate cement with different C 3 S/C 2 S ratios increases with increasing C 3 S content. The Ca/Si ratio (1.73–1.93) and the chemically bound water content (H 2 O/Si ratio of 1.56–1.89) of C-S-H remain relatively stable within 30-70℃. The total water (H 2 O/Si ratio of 2.57–4.10), gel water (H 2 O/Si ratio of 1.01–1.96), and intrinsic porosity (0.18–0.29) of saturated C-S-H are found to decrease with rising temperature, exhibiting a density range of 2.11–2.38 g/cm 3 , with maxima at 5 °C and 90 °C and minima at 30℃ and 70℃. The density of C-S-H solid phase is determined to be 2.59 ± 0.12 g/cm 3 . The water–vapor adsorption results indicate that dried C-S-H possesses a specific surface area ranging from 91 to 502 m 2 /g. The obtained C-S-H parameters at varying temperatures provide essential inputs for analyzing the engineering properties of a wide range of cement systems.

title: Neural network and spectral characterization of diffusion-limited nanostructured hillock growth in physical vapor-deposited binary immiscible alloy films
abstract: Hillock formation in metallic thin films is commonly attributed to stress relaxation; however, in phase-separating alloy systems, surface instabilities can emerge purely from diffusion-limited processes during vapor deposition. While phase field modeling has previously captured such morphological evolution, quantitative classification and predictive mapping of diffusion-limited hillock modes remain unresolved. In this work, we introduce a spectral characterization framework based on structure factor analysis derived from Fast Fourier Transform to rigorously distinguish vertically aligned, partially ordered, and disordered hillock morphologies that cannot be reliably separated using real-space metrics. Building on this physics-based classification, a supervised neural network is developed to map deposition rate and diffusion kinetics directly to hillock growth modes, generating probability density maps that reveal clear transitions in kinetic parameter space. Phase field simulations are used to systematically vary deposition rate and atomic diffusion coefficients, confirming that hillock morphology is governed by the competition between atomic diffusion and deposition flux, with lower deposition rates enabling diffusion-limited surface reorganization. The integrated spectral and machine learning framework provides a quantitative and predictive pathway for classifying and controlling diffusion-driven surface instabilities in vapor-deposited immiscible alloy thin films.

title: Laser-engineered microtopographies for probabilistic control of cell shape and adhesion: from predictability to exploration
abstract: Fibroblast shape directs cell function and tissue organization, yet systematically controlling cell morphology requires highly reproducible surface topographies, which have so far been lacking. Here, we demonstrate a strategy to precisely guide fibroblast cell shapes and adhesion through design of simple and reproducible microtopographies fabricated by laser direct writing via two-photon polymerization of IP-Dip photopolymer. The engineered microtopographies consisted of parallel lines (2–4 μm spacing and 1028 ± 68 nm in height) and sets of intersecting lines spaced 2 μm apart and overlapped at 11.5°, 22.6 and 33.4°, respectively. Single-cell analysis of murine L929 fibroblasts revealed clear geometry-dependent phenotypes: flat substrates promoted polygonal shapes (circularity 0.65 ± 0.07; solidity 0.89 ± 0.04; vinculin 511,867 ± 68,060 a.u.), parallel lines induced elongated spindle-like morphologies (circularity 0.49 ± 0.05; solidity 0.93 ± 0.04; vinculin 469,604 ± 111,409 a.u.), and intersecting lines generated stellate cells (circularity 0.48 ± 0.07; solidity 0.77 ± 0.05; vinculin 336,256 ± 94,193 a.u., p < 0.01 vs parallel). The microtopographies also induced rounded transient morphologies in the seeded fibroblasts, with a higher number of rounded cells with filopodia-like protrusions (15.4 and 14 cells/100 μm 2 on parallel and overlapped lines, respectively) relative to flat surfaces (6.2 cells/100 μm 2 ), whereas rounded cells with bleb-like protrusions predominated on flat substrates (7.8 cells/100 μm 2 ) as compared to all other topographies investigated. Unlike conventional approaches focused on predictable geometry-driven cell behavior, our study proposes a semi-predictive model in which microtopographies influence cellular adaptation without fully determining it.

title: Additive manufacturing of barium titanate-aluminum oxide piezoelectric ceramic composites using fused deposition modeling
abstract: Barium titanate (BT) is a key lead-free piezoelectric ceramic, but conventional forming methods limit its structural design freedom and performance regulation. This work proposes an additive manufacturing route for BT-Al 2 O 3 composites via fused deposition modeling (FDM) with a solution-based PVB/PEG feedstock. The process included filament extrusion, FDM printing, staged debinding, and sintering. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed homogeneous ceramic dispersion and interfacial compatibility, enabling complex architectures. Sintering temperature (1100–1300 ∘ C) and Al 2 O 3 particle size (1–100 µ m) significantly influenced microstructure and phase evolution, allowing the piezoelectric coefficient ( d 33 ) to be tuned from 14.3 to 96.1 pC/N. Optimized composites sintered at 1200 ∘ C with 10 µ m Al 2 O 3 exhibited a compressive strength of 4.16 ± 0.31 MPa and a flexural strength of 0.96 ± 0.23 MPa. A four-sensor-integrated component fabricated via FDM demonstrated the capability of monitoring impact areas. This work establishes a generalized AM strategy for BT-based ceramics with tunable piezoelectric and mechanical properties, offering significant potential for smart ceramic systems.

title: Enhanced photochemical stability of hydrophobic TiO2 via covalently anchoring near-monolayer octadecyl brushes and its robust superhydrophobic photocatalytic coatings
abstract: Conventional TiO 2 -based superhydrophobic coatings suffer from ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodegradation. Here, we prepared a modified TiO 2 (ODS@TiO 2 ) using octadecyltrimethoxysilane (ODS) via non-hydrolytic grafting. Fourier-transform infrared, X-ray photoelectron and 29 Si nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy confirm a near-monolayer octadecyl brush (4.6 ± 0.2 chains nm −2 ) anchored onto TiO 2 via robust Ti–O–Si bonds, whereas a hydrolytic product (ODS/TiO 2 -EW) contains a polysiloxane overlayer with sparse Ti–O–Si linkages. The Tauc plot shows that ODS@TiO 2 retains the bandgap of pristineTiO 2 . Nitrogen adsorption reveals an effective specific surface area of 42 m 2 ·g −1 for ODS@TiO 2 (vs 9 m 2 ·g −1 for ODS/TiO 2 -EW) and sufficient mesopores for mass transfer. Following UV exposure, the component of ODS@TiO 2 keeps constant, attributed to the synergy of Ti–O–Si bonds and octadecyl brushes that promote charge separation and provide steric shielding. A superhydrophobic coating was fabricated by mixing ODS@TiO 2 with ODS@SiO 2 prepared via analogous non-hydrolytic grafting. Scanning electron microscopy and 3D profilometry disclose a hierarchical structure featuring with 39% porosity and an average roughness of 5.8 μm. The coating exhibits superhydrophobicity, excellent photochemical stability, mechanical durability, and antibacterial properties, while the hydrolytic counterpart fails within 100 min of UV exposure. This work provides a scalable, fluorine-free strategy for fabricating UV-stable superhydrophobic coatings.

title: An origin of superelasticity in Fe–Mn–Al–Ni alloy: A phase-field study
abstract: Phase-field simulations are performed to investigate the martensitic transformation (MT) from body-centered-cubic-α to face-centered-cubic-γ′ when external compressive stress is applied along the [100] α direction, as well as the reverse MT from γ′ to α during the unloading of the external stress. The objective is to gain fundamental insights into the reversibility of the MT in Fe–Mn–Al–Ni alloy with a microstructure containing nanoscale β-NiAl precipitates in the α phase. The stress-induced MT from α to γ′ occurred under a compressive loading of approximately 400 MPa, resulting in a martensite microstructure composed of two of the three crystallographic orientation variants. The elastic energy in the β phase increased owing to the MT, which slightly increased the structural density of martensite and consequently increased the chemical free energy of the β phase. Moreover, the structural density of martensite in the γ′ phase decreased near the β-phase boundary, where a compositional gradient was present, resulting in an increase in the chemical free energy of the γ′ phase. A complete reverse MT occurred when the total free-energy change, determined by the balance between the elastic-energy change and chemical free-energy change, temporarily became positive during the unloading of external stress.

title: High-strength, electrochemically efficient RuO2-MXene/CNTs hybrid fibres via nanostructure design for flexible electronics and energy storage
abstract: Demand for smart textiles in wearables spotlights MXene fibres, but their use is limited by mechanical robustness, electrochemical activity, and electrical stability challenges. In this paper, a three-dimensional network-structured hybrid fibre with high tensile strength, flexibility, electrical conductivity, and superior electrochemical characteristics was successfully fabricated by combining hydrothermal synthesis and wet-spinning techniques. Initially, an in-situ hydrothermal method was used to uniformly anchor hydrated RuO 2 nanoparticles onto MXene nanosheets. These RuO 2 -MXene composites were subsequently combined with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to construct RuO 2 -MXene/CNTs hybrid fibres via a wet-spinning process. RuO 2 prevents MXene re-lamination and adds pseudocapacitance, improving ion access and charge storage. Meanwhile, CNTs create a strong 3D conductive network, boosting charge transport and mechanical strength. As a result, the RuO 2 -MXene/CNTs hybrid fibres achieved a superior specific volumetric capacitance reaching 77.9F/cm 3 , along with outstanding cyclic stability, maintaining 88.1 % of the capacitance after 1000 charge–discharge operations. Additionally, the hybrid fibres displayed outstanding flexibility and electrical stability, with a resistance variation of less than 0.7 % under continuous rapid bending over 8000 s. These findings clearly demonstrate that RuO 2 -MXene/CNTs hybrid fibres possess high potential for application as electrode materials in the domain of future flexible electronics.

title: Low-voltage micro-arc discharge-grinding hybrid machining: Discharge energy regulation for high-surface-quality machining of Inconel 718
abstract: Electric arc machining (EAM) of Inconel 718 often produces thick recast layers and severe thermal damage because of sustained high-energy discharge. This study proposes low-voltage micro-arc discharge-grinding hybrid machining (LV-MADG), in which low-voltage micro-arc discharge, diamond-abrasive grinding, and gap renewal are coupled in the same machining zone. Synchronized high-speed imaging, voltage-current acquisition, waveform statistics, surface and cross-sectional morphology, elemental and phase analyses, and microhardness testing were used to link discharge-state evolution with surface-layer integrity. LV-MADG changed the discharge from concentrated continuous conduction to more discrete intermittent events by disturbing the discharge channel and renewing the gap medium. The peak current decreased from 830 A to 498 A, the average residual-conduction duration shortened from 0.268 ms to 0.194 ms, and high-current events above 500 A were nearly eliminated. Compared with EAM, LV-MADG increased the material removal rate by 24.66%, reduced areal surface roughness and relative electrode wear ratio by 88.54% and 55.00%, respectively, and improved groove profile accuracy. It also suppressed deep craters, retained resolidified products, continuous recast-layer formation, surface oxidation, reaction-product accumulation, and abnormal hardening. A stable low-damage window was identified by balancing material removal rate, areal surface roughness, and average recast-layer thickness.

title: Puzzle-like auxetic lattice architectures employing dovetail joints: Experimental investigation of the structural dynamic behaviour
abstract: This paper introduces a puzzle-like modular auxetic lattice architecture based on re-entrant unit cells and mechanically interlocking dovetail joints. The proposed concept decomposes a three-dimensional auxetic lattice into two repeatable two-dimensional components, enabling scalable assembly, disassembly, repair, and potential fabrication by conventional sheet-based manufacturing methods. The dynamic behavior of the assembled auxetic cube is experimentally investigated using instrumented impact-hammer testing, accelerometers, and laser vibrometry. The measurement and modal-identification workflow is first validated on a cantilever beam through comparison with analytical and numerical reference solutions. The validated procedure is then applied to the dovetail-jointed lattice to identify its dynamic behavior, modal participation, and equivalent damping characteristics. The results show repeatable global modes in the low-frequency range, strong direction-dependent modal participation, and additional higher-frequency modal groups captured by laser vibrometry. The damping response is shown to be method-dependent and frequency-dependent, reflecting the combined influence of base-material dissipation, joint compliance, frictional micro-slip, and contact effects. The study establishes experimental dynamic behaviour for modular auxetic lattices and provides a basis for future modelling, optimization, and vibration-oriented design of assembled mechanical metamaterials.

title: Crack suppression in additively manufactured non-weldable γ′ Ni-based superalloys by tailoring the melt-pool flank shape
abstract: To address solidification cracking in non-weldable γ′-strengthened Ni-based superalloys fabricated by powder bed fusion-laser beam (PBF-LB), this study achieves crack suppression through tailoring the melt-pool flank shape. Using Mar-M247 alloy as a representative, nearly crack-free PBF-LB specimens were successfully fabricated. Compared to conventionally additively manufactured Mar-M247 alloys, the optimized specimens show a 31.6% (from 1075 MPa to 1414.7 MPa) increase in strength and a 200% (from 5.4% to 16.2%) improvement in elongation. A moderate reduction in linear energy input (LED) increased the melt-pool width-to-depth ratio and produced a shallower melt pool with less steep melt-pool flanks, thereby aligning the local thermal-gradient direction more closely with the build direction (BD). This promoted columnar grains with < 001 > orientations nearly parallel to the BD, reduced inter-columnar misorientation, and suppressed crack initiation and propagation. Meanwhile, refined grains near the melt-pool flanks further alleviated local strain concentration and contributed to crack inhibition. In addition, the higher solidification rate restricted solute diffusion and promoted Hf trapping in the γ matrix, narrowing the solidification temperature range and decreasing crack susceptibility. Serrated grain boundaries further increased resistance to intergranular crack propagation. This work provides guidance for suppressing cracking in PBF-LB non-weldable γ′-strengthened Ni-based superalloys.

title: Synergistic antioxidant and inherited bioactivities of tremella fuciformis polysaccharide derived carbon dots for multi-layer skin aging therapy
abstract: To meet the substantial global demand for skin anti-aging, particularly for effectively against ultraviolet radiation (the primary exogenous driver of skin aging), this study successfully developed a novel tremella fuciformis polysaccharide derived carbon dots (TFP-CDs) via a hydrothermal method. The skin barrier function of the epidermis and the dense extracellular matrix of the dermis, poses a significant delivery challenge. It limits the penetration and bioavailability of most skincare agents, which would affect their intended multi-layer efficacy. To address this, the prepared TFP-CDs with ultrasmall size (∼2.4 nm) and amphiphilic functional groups, have been designed to sequentially overcome the barriers. As biologically responsive nanomaterials, they integrate the inherent bioactivity of herbal extract with excellent antioxidant properties, exhibiting superior efficacy over positive control drug. Through efficiently scavenging ROS, TFP-CDs may help break the vicious cycle of mitochondrial morphological and functional disorders, endoplasmic reticulum stress, and abnormal organelle contacts exacerbated. This study effectively achieves synergistic anti-aging repair in multi-layered skin repair, ranging from epidermal barrier repair and pigmentation inhibition to dermal collagen regeneration. This work provides a potential strategy for the intervention of skin aging, showing preliminary application promise.

title: Mechanical properties of graphene reinforced high-density polyethylene nanocomposites: a comprehensive review
abstract: Graphene-based high-density polyethylene (HDPE) nanocomposites have lately emerged as a promising route to enhance the mechanical properties of HDPE for high-performance engineering applications. This review critically examines the mechanical properties of HDPE/graphene nanocomposites, with emphasis on the influence of graphene size, type, concentration, and surface modification. Results indicate that the addition of graphene, even at very low concentrations, can enhance HDPE mechanical properties, including tensile and flexural moduli, and to a lesser extent the tensile and flexural strength. However, these enhancements depend on uniform dispersion and strong interfacial interactions within the polymer, where agglomeration can lead to significant reductions in mechanical properties. While ductility and impact resistance generally decrease with graphene addition, strategies such as graphene functionalization and compatibilizers can mitigate these drawbacks. Results also show that although larger graphene flake sizes better enhance the mechanical properties at lower concentrations, they lead to reductions in properties at higher concentrations due to increased agglomeration of graphene. Contrarily, impact resistance is higher with smaller graphene flake sizes. Finally, current challenges, including scalable dispersion methods, property trade-offs, and industrial processing compatibility, are discussed, and future research directions are outlined to facilitate their broader adoption in commercial applications, such as packaging and pipes.

title: Selective removal of Fe-rich intermetallics in AA8079 by mixed HNO3/HF pretreatment: Implications for aluminum–polypropylene interfacial integrity
abstract: Fe-containing intermetallic compounds (Fe-IMCs) in 8xxx aluminum alloys act as cathodic sites that promote localized corrosion and generate defects in anodic oxide films. A combined pretreatment—alkaline etching followed by mixed HNO 3 /HF pickling under ultrasonication (NH-U)—was applied to selectively remove Fe-rich Al 13 Fe 4 from AA8079 before phosphoric acid anodizing. Alkaline etching exposed and partially oxidized Fe-IMCs, whereas single-acid pickling (HNO 3 or HF) left residual cathodic inclusions at the surface. Mixed HNO 3 /HF without ultrasonication partially reduced the surface IMC population, whereas NH-U eliminated detectable surface Fe-IMCs and produced a micro-roughened surface. Anodizing on the IMC-free substrate yielded a uniform porous oxide, while untreated AA8079 formed heterogeneous films locally perturbed by Fe dissolution and incorporation. Cross-sectional elemental mapping confirmed Fe incorporation into the anodic oxide above residual IMCs, creating thinner and compositionally altered regions that can disrupt film uniformity and interfacial integrity. As an application-level indicator of film quality, lap-shear strength of anodized Al–polypropylene joints increased from ∼9 MPa to ∼21 MPa after NH-U pretreatment. Selective Fe-IMC dissolution is therefore identified as a prerequisite for mechanically robust and structurally uniform anodic films on AA8079. The pretreatment offers a scalable route to suppress cathodic-particle-driven film breakdown in battery-foil processing and joining applications.

title: Data-efficient optimization of LPBF 316 L stainless steel via domain knowledge-guided hybrid modeling
abstract: Parameter optimization in laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) remains challenging due to the high dimensionality of process variables and the cost of extensive experimentation. Here, a hybrid strategy synergizing physical insight with data-driven modelling is proposed to address the data scarcity. A central composite design (31 runs) with rotatable and symmetric characteristics was constructed and constrained within an intermediate laser volumetric energy density regime to fabricate 316 L stainless steel via LPBF. An iterative stepwise regression model with adaptive α-level tuning was developed to model the complex and nonlinear relationships between the key parameters (laser power, scanning speed, hatch spacing, layer thickness) and the resulting properties (relative density, tensile strength, yield strength, elongation), achieving R 2 values from 82.19% to 91.72%. The findings, derived from model analyses based on the specific experimental design range, unveil a transition in parameter dominance: from geometric factors alone governing density, to the set expanding to include energy inputs for mechanical properties. Experimental validation demonstrates optimized properties, including 99.96% relative density, 834 MPa tensile strength, 685 MPa yield strength, and 44% elongation. This work provides a resource-efficient and physically informed machine-learning framework for LPBF process optimization, offering practical guidance for high-performance additive manufacturing.

title: Nanoplatform-mediated dual-strategy cholesterol depletion for potentiating tumor chemodynamic-immunotherapy
abstract: Regulating cholesterol metabolism presents a promising multi-pronged strategy in cancer therapy, targeting its roles in tumor growth, immune suppression, and treatment resistance. To overcome the limitations of single-target approaches, a novel nanoplatform was engineered. This system utilizes hyaluronic acid-coated mesoporous polydopamine to co-deliver a dual-metabolic modulator: simvastatin (a synthesis inhibitor, Sim) and cholesterol oxidase (Chox), alongside Mn 2+ ions. The platform orchestrates a coordinated attack: Simvastatin blocks de novo cholesterol synthesis, while Chox depletes existing membrane cholesterol. This depletion disrupts oncogenic signaling and reverses immunosuppression. Furthermore, the enzymatic reaction of Chox generates H 2 O 2 , which Mn 2+ ions convert into highly cytotoxic hydroxyl radicals via Fenton-like reactions, initiating self-amplifying chemodynamic therapy. The mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA) core ensures high cargo loading and stability and enables spatiotemporal coordination of these actions. The hyaluronic acid (HA) shell promotes active cluster of differentiation 44 (CD44)-targeting and enzyme-triggered payload release within the tumor. This paradigm-shifting approach not only disrupts cholesterol-driven oncogenesis but also leverages its metabolic byproducts to fuel a synergistic anti-tumor cascade, offering a powerful strategy for tumor-selective metabolic reprogramming and immunotherapy.

title: Synergistic fabrication of FeSiAl/Si3N4 soft magnetic composites by two-step plasma-assisted ball milling and magnetic-field-induced orientation
abstract: To overcome the rapid permeability degradation, high eddy-current loss, and poor thermal management of FeSiAl soft magnetic composites under high-frequency and high-power conditions, a combined strategy of two-step plasma-assisted ball milling and magnetic-field-induced orientation was developed. The first plasma-assisted milling step transformed near-spherical FeSiAl powders into high-quality flakes, while the second step constructed a dense Si 3 N 4 coating layer, forming a tightly bonded core–shell structure. Interfacial analyses revealed the formation of Si–N, Si–O–N, and Fe–N/Al–N bonds. First-principles calculations further demonstrated interfacial charge transfer from FeSiAl to Si 3 N 4 , leading to strong Al–N covalent bonding, a built-in electric field, and a Schottky barrier, which effectively suppressed interparticle charge transport and reduced high-frequency eddy-current loss. Meanwhile, magnetic-field-induced orientation promoted the ordered arrangement of flaky particles, improving magnetic-flux continuity and heat-transfer pathways. The optimized composite containing 4 wt% Si 3 N 4 achieved an effective permeability of 93.4 at 1 MHz, a total core loss of 72.2 kW/m 3 at 50 mT and 100 kHz, and a thermal conductivity of 25.9 W·m −1 ·K −1 . This work provides a new route for designing soft magnetic composites for high-frequency, high-power-density power electronic devices.

title: Contrasting effect of compositional tuning and FCC-Al nanocrystals on stochastic shear-band behavior in Al-Ni-MM metallic glasses
abstract: Initiation and propagation of shear bands govern the deformation behavior of metallic glasses (MGs), yet how compositional variation and nanoscale heterogeneity tune stochastic yielding in MGs has not been systematically clarified. Here, we analyze pop-in statistics from a large number of nanoindentation tests on Al 100-x Ni 10 MM x MG ribbons (x = 2, 4, and 6; MM = Ce-rich misch metal) to investigate shear band behaviors. Despite pronounced composition-dependent changes in hardness and thermal properties, the stochastic signatures of shear bands remain largely insensitive in the fully amorphous Al 86 Ni 10 MM 4 and Al 84 Ni 10 MM 6 MGs. These alloys exhibit bimodal distributions of first pop-in loads with nearly invariant apparent Weibull moduli, together with similar pop-in size statistics. In contrast, as-spun and heated Al 88 Ni 10 MM 2 MGs, which contain FCC-Al nanocrystals, shows a trimodal distribution of the first pop-in loads, suggesting an additional shear band nucleation pathway associated with FCC-Al nanocrystals and a reduced nucleation barrier. Moreover, reduced interparticle spacing together with FCC-Al nanocrystal growth enhances nanoscale spatial heterogeneity and suppresses shear band propagation, shifting strain bursts toward smaller sizes and lowering their Weibull characteristic scale. Overall, compositional tuning in Al-based MGs primarily modifies macroscopic properties without substantially changing the stochastic characteristics of shear bands. In contrast, FCC-Al nanocrystals and reduced interparticle spacing govern the statistical behavior of shear band initiation and propagation. These changes are expected to promote enhanced plasticity in the MG composites.

title: Multi-model machine learning framework for predicting material properties of BaTiO3-based ferroelectric ceramics
abstract: Predicting multiple functional properties of ferroelectric ceramics simultaneously remains challenging due to complex nonlinear interactions between composition, processing conditions, and microstructural evolution. This study presents a unified machine learning framework for predicting four key properties of BaTiO 3 ceramics: piezoelectric coefficient ( ), dielectric constant ( ), dielectric loss tangent ( ), and density ( ). The framework integrates an in-house experimental dataset from ten independent fabrication runs, augmented to 10,000 instances using Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGAN), with statistical fidelity validated through KL divergence and Wasserstein distance analyses. Domain-specific features comprising compositional ratios, dopant-site descriptors, and processing parameters are synthesized to capture nonlinear structure–property relationships. A consensus-based feature selection strategy combining Random Forest importance and SHAP values confirms that all fourteen engineered descriptors carry meaningful predictive information. Seven models comprising three baselines (Linear Regression, Random Forest, SVR) and four gradient boosting algorithms (AdaBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) are benchmarked using Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and five-fold cross-validation. CatBoost achieves the highest performance across all targets, with of 0.922 for , 0.933 for , 0.855 for , and 0.674 for . Ablation studies confirm that domain-specific feature synthesis contributes approximately 38 percentage points of improvement, establishing a reproducible and interpretable pipeline for multi-property prediction in ferroelectric ceramics.

title: Process-dependent phase evolution in thermally sprayed Li4Ti5O12 thin-film anodes revealed by synchrotron and surface analysis
abstract: Understanding process-induced phase evolution in thermally sprayed Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO) thin-films is critical for developing scalable battery electrodes with stable electrochemical performance. This study comparatively investigates Atmospheric Plasma Spraying (APS), Suspension Plasma Spraying (SPS), and High-Velocity Oxy-Fuel (HVOF) processing of LTO thin-film anodes using SEM/EDS, laboratory XRD, synchrotron µXRD/µXRF mapping, XPS, and electrochemical characterization. Synchrotron µXRD revealed distinct process-dependent phase evolution governed by thermal exposure and quenching behavior. HVOF retained the highest spinel LTO fraction (66.8 %), APS retained 65.1 %, while SPS showed the strongest decomposition with only 53.5 % LTO together with increased Li 2 TiO 3 (43.5 %) and TiO 2 formation (3.0 %). XPS analysis identified Li 2 CO 3 surface formation in APS and HVOF coatings, whereas SPS exhibited strong surface lithium depletion. Electrochemical measurements showed that APS-LTO exhibited the most favorable electrochemical response, with a working voltage of ∼1.56 V vs. Li/Li + and lower polarization resistance (∼18.7 kΩ) compared with SPS and HVOF coatings. The results establish process–structure–property relationships linking thermal spray conditions with lithium retention, phase stability, and electrochemical behavior in thermally sprayed LTO thin-films.

title: Biomaterial-based ocular drug delivery: strategies, challenges, and future perspectives
abstract: Traditional ocular drug delivery methods suffer from low bioavailability, short precorneal residence time, and poor patient adherence due to ocular physiological and anatomical barriers. This review systematically summarizes biomaterial-based platforms for ocular drug delivery, focusing on controlled release, targeting, permeability, and synergistic therapy. The review also discusses key clinical features of ocular disorders, including dry eye disease, infectious keratitis, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration. It also evaluates the therapeutic performance and clinical translation of key systems, and identifies current challenges and future directions. This paper aims to provide theoretical foundations and innovative approaches for developing more efficient and safer ophthalmic drug delivery strategies.

title: Integrated wearable sensor modality for real-time monitoring of agro-ecological and human systems A review
abstract: Wearable sensor technologies are poised to transform real-time environmental and health monitoring by enabling non-invasive investigations of biofluids, i.e. plant sap, animal saliva, and human sweat, to address global challenges in food security and healthcare. This review synthesizes advancements in flexible microfluidic systems, multimodal sensor arrays, and low-power detection circuits to propose a unified platform for simultaneous monitoring of agricultural and human health. Despite shared technical challenges, such as microfluidic stability under variable biofluid flow rates of 0.1–5 µL/min, sensor sensitivity for low-concentration biomarkers e.g., glucose at 10 µM, cytokines at 1 pg/mL, and circuit power efficiency of more than 100 µA; current research gap remains siloed, with no integrated framework leveraging sweat sensor innovations for agricultural applications. By integrating these technologies with AI-driven analytics including hybrid CNN-LSTM models and IoT protocols, the potential use of the dual-purpose platform can be explored that may support predictive modeling broadly ranged 85–93 % for related tasks, and further validation on cross-domain datasets is required before higher performance can be claimed. By fostering cross-disciplinary synergy, this manuscript aims to advance sustainable agriculture and proactive health management, offering a roadmap for future research and deployment of unified wearable sensor systems.

title: Microscopic mechanisms underlying strength degradation in Alkali-activated slag-based plugging fluids under high-temperature curing
abstract: In this study, the microscopic mechanisms underlying strength degradation during the hydration process of metallurgical waste slag-based plugging fluids cured at high temperatures were investigated. Static gel strength analysis, X-ray diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy were employed to illustrate the effects of phase transformation, microstructure, and morphology evolution during hydration on mechanical performance. The results show that the optimized formulation system using 3% NaOH as the alkali activator exhibited rapid growth in strength during the early curing stage, reaching a peak of 22.70 MPa at 5 h, followed by a continuous strength declining trend as the hydration process progressed. Newly formed hydration products, calcium silicate (aluminate) hydrate, promote early-stage strength development owing to their relatively high crosslinking density and Ca 2+ bridging. However, phase transformations and the conversion of four-coordinated aluminum to six-coordinated aluminum led to a reduction in the crosslinking density between microstructural units and an increase in the pore (crack) size, thereby weakening the macroscopic load-bearing capacity of the hardened body. Furthermore, in the later stages of hydration, the hardened body lacked newly generated hydration products to fill internal pores (cracks). Consequently, the crack network structure became interconnected and deteriorated, which further accelerated strength degradation.

title: Bioadhesive ZnO2@BCG synergizing chemodynamic-immunotherapy enhances bladder cancer treatment
abstract: For patients with high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) is a well-established first-line therapy. However, disease recurrence and progression remain major clinical challenges. In this study, leveraging the inherently negative charge of biofilms, we constructed a ZnO 2 @BCG conjugate via charge-driven self-assembly of polyethyleneimine-modified ZnO 2 and BCG. ZnO 2 @BCG enhances its adhesion to the bladder wall through its own positive charge, thereby promoting sustained tumor killing. Mechanistically, ZnO 2 @BCG activates the pyroptosis pathway through the canonical inflammasome signaling cascade. The synergistic interplay between ZnO 2 -induced immunogenic cell death (ICD) and BCG immunotherapy promotes dendritic cell (DC) maturation and M1 macrophage polarization, effectively inhibiting tumor progression and extending a prolonged survival in an orthotopic murine bladder cancer model. Furthermore, the formulation exhibits an enhanced tolerability and biosafety. Thus, our work proposes a novel therapeutic strategy for bladder cancer by integrating ZnO 2 -based chemodynamic therapy with BCG immuno-instillation.

title: Mitigation of interfacial brittleness and property enhancement in WA-DED SS316L–NAB structures using an IN718 buffer layer
abstract: Wire arc directed energy deposition (WA-DED) enables the fabrication of multi-material structures for demanding marine applications; however, direct deposition of SS316L and nickel-aluminium bronze (NAB) creates a brittle, crack-prone interface due to thermodynamic incompatibility in the Fe–Cu binary system. This study investigates the influence of an intermediate IN718 buffer layer on mitigating interfacial Fe–Cu brittleness in SS316L–NAB structures via Fe–Ni and Ni–Cu sequential transitions. Bimetallic (BM) SS316L–NAB and trimetallic (TM) SS316L–IN718–NAB architectures were fabricated and compared through microstructural and mechanical analysis. The BM interface is reaction-dominated, exhibiting a submicron transition width (∼0.3 μm), a continuous AlNi intermetallic, elevated micro-strain (5.1–8.8 × 10 −3 ), and interfacial cracking. The TM architecture produces a crack-free interface with an extended compositional transition width (∼1 μm), stabilised FCC phase fraction (∼90%), refined crystallite size (14–21 nm), reduced microstrain (2.3–5.4 × 10 −3 ), and progressive interfacial hardness (up to 331 HV 0.5 ). Mechanically, TM achieves an average yield strength of ∼362 MPa, approximately 46% higher than BM (∼248 MPa), attributed to dislocation strengthening (∼110–130 MPa), solid-solution, mismatch-induced strengthening, and Orowan dispersoid strengthening. These results establish IN718 as a metallurgically active diffusion mediator that ensures crack-free graded compositional accommodation.

title: Defect-engineered biphasic calcium phosphate scaffolds from Nile tilapia bone: Calcination-controlled phase evolution and structure–bioactivity coupling
abstract: Porous biphasic calcium phosphate (BCP) scaffolds were fabricated from Nile tilapia bone waste via microwave-assisted processing. The extracted powders were subsequently calcined at 500–1000 °C to tailor precursor characteristics, phase evolution, and defect chemistry. Increasing calcination temperature promoted particle coarsening and carbonate removal. Below 700 °C, single-phase hydroxyapatite (HAp) was retained. At ≥ 700 °C, HAp/β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) compositions emerged, with β-TCP content increasing from 7.6 % to 16.9 %. Scaffolds fabricated via polyurethane sponge replication and sintered at 1250 °C exhibited highly interconnected porous architectures with porosities ranging from 77.5 % to 89 %. Carbonate-rich precursors promoted shrinkage, microcracking, and finer pore fractions, whereas higher-temperature calcined powders yielded crack-free scaffolds with improved structural stability. Sintering further increased β-TCP content (15–24.4 %) and promoted dehydroxylation, as confirmed by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), indicating the formation of OH − vacancies. In vitro evaluation revealed that scaffolds calcined at 500 °C exhibited the highest direct cell proliferation due to a favorable micropore fraction, while those calcined at 1000 °C demonstrated superior bioactivity attributed to the greatest OH − vacancy concentration (ΔOH − = 10.77 %). These findings establish calcination temperature as a critical processing parameter governing phase evolution, defect chemistry, and biological performance in sustainable biowaste-derived BCP scaffolds.

title: A self-heating-based physics-guided neural network for fatigue life prediction of polymer matrix composites
abstract: Great efforts have been made to obtain accurate and reliable fatigue life models for polymer matrix composites (PMCs) that encompass their complexity in a short time frame. This investigation employs a physics-guided neural network (PGNN) with self-heating behavior embedded as soft physics constraints to predict the fatigue life of different PMCs reported in the literature. Due to the limited data size, which ranges from 12 to 21 samples, Monte-Carlo simulations were used to generate synthetic data (up to 1000 samples) that adhere to the distribution of the experimental data. Comprehensive k-fold cross-validation is performed by varying k from 2 up to leave-one-out (LOOCV) on the proposed PGNN architecture to ensure robust prediction and generalization. This model was applied to four distinct PMCs subjected to cyclic loading under stress ratios (R = -1 and R = 0.1) and cyclic frequencies (5, 10 and 50 Hz). The results demonstrate that stabilized surface temperature can predict fatigue life within a factor of two, maintaining reasonable accuracy even for materials that exhibit scatter up to a factor of four. Ultimately, this framework can successfully guide early-stage material screening phase for structural design of PMCs, even when the available experimental data is scarce.

title: A multi-layer approximation framework for contact analysis of functionally graded quasicrystal coatings
abstract: This paper presents a multi-layer approximation framework for the frictionless contact analysis of functionally graded one-dimensional hexagonal quasicrystal (FGQC) coatings bonded to elastic substrates. The proposed approach aims to provide a computationally efficient and generalized analytical framework capable of modeling arbitrary material gradation profiles and complex contact interactions while accounting for phonon-phason coupling effects and anisotropic characteristics of quasicrystals. The FGQC coating is discretized into homogeneous sublayers to accurately approximate the continuous material gradation. The contact formulation is established by combining existing fundamental solutions for layered quasicrystals with continuity conditions imposed at interfaces between adjacent sublayers. A collocation technique based on finite element basis functions is employed to determine the unknown contact pressures. The framework is applicable to both complete and partial contact problems involving various indenter geometries. Numerical examples are presented to investigate the effects of material gradations, coating thickness, and phonon-phason coupling on the contact pressure and apparent indentation resistance of FGQC coating systems. Results indicate that concentrating the hard constituent near the coating surface provides the most effective enhancement in apparent indentation resistance. The proposed framework provides an effective analytical tool for contact analysis, material tailoring, and optimal design of advanced FGQC coating systems in engineering applications.

title: Thermoelastic optimisation of fibre-steered composite mirrors for space-based laser communication systems
abstract: Lightweight, dimensionally stable mirrors are essential for space-based laser communication, requiring concurrent optimisation of mass, stiffness, and environmental stability. This study presents a novel design–manufacture–validation framework that explicitly links variable-stiffness laminate design, manufacturing-induced effects, and experimentally validated optical performance under identical conditions. The novelty lies in providing the first experimentally validated, like-for-like comparison between conventional straight-fibre and Rapid Tow Shearing (RTS) laminates for precision composite mirrors under identical geometry, loading conditions, manufacturing assumptions, and validation procedures. The framework combines finite-element structural, thermoelastic, and hygroscopic analyses with Cure Hardening Instantaneously Linear Elastic (CHILE)-based process modelling and demonstrator-level validation for a 0.50 m composite mirror. Both designs satisfy the > 140 Hz fundamental frequency requirement and exhibit large safety margins. The straight-fibre laminate achieves ∼ 153 Hz and ∼ 69 µm RMS, while the RTS laminate achieves ∼ 145 Hz with comparable deformation and ∼ 11% lower mass. Hygroscopic effects are modest, and cure-induced distortion is dominated by low-order modes. The results demonstrate that RTS enables mass-efficient stiffness tailoring without degrading first-order thermoelastic performance and establish a validated methodology linking modelling predictions, manufacturing variability, and measured surface figure for next-generation lightweight space optics.

title: Towards deeper carburizing by DEDp and L-PBF additive manufacturing of in-situ TiC-reinforced steel composites: powders and processability
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) of iron-based metal matrix composites (IMMCs) enables the fabrication of more complex geometries than conventional processes for applications such as brake discs, transmission shafts, cutting tools, and gears. Current challenges associated with AM of IMMCs, including homogeneous reinforcement distribution and reinforcement/matrix interfacial decohesion, have been mitigated in the context of deep carburizing for gear applications. In situ reinforcement by Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) was achieved using nano-TiC (35–55 nm) dry coating onto spherical steel powder particles (15–45 µm) through Cyclomix® blade mixing, with a reinforcement content of 5 vol% (3.2 wt%). Powder rheology, powder density measurements, single-track experiments, high-speed imaging, and 3D builds revealed improved flowability due to coating, an increasing of spatters amount despite a low porosity rate (0.26 vol%). Directed Energy Deposition using powder (DEDp) enables additional functionalities such as repair and compositional gradients while accounting for process-induced constraints. However, the powder must be coarser to ensure efficient stream. Turbula® premixed composite powders were used with spherical steel particles (45–125 µm) mixed and 3.2 wt% of micrometric TiC particles (3–8 µm and 15–30 µm). Video imaging, single-track experiments and 3D build showed that unmelted TiC particles could not be completely eliminated and create defects. Hardening comparable to carburizing was achieved, increasing from 350 HV to 600 HV throughout the volume in L-PBF samples and at the surface in DED-p samples. Strengthening was likely induced by carbon diffusion from the reinforcement phase; however, the strong thermal cycling associated with DED-p caused softening in previously deposited layers.

title: Advances in biodegradable metallic materials and its applications: A comprehensive review
abstract: Biodegradable metallic materials (BMMs) are increasingly being explored as temporary implants because they can provide mechanical support during healing without requiring secondary removal surgery. This review summarizes recent advances in Mg-, Zn-, Fe- and Mo-based alloys, with emphasis on their mechanical performance, in vivo degradation behavior and biocompatibility. Mg alloys are attractive for bone repair but are limited by rapid corrosion and gas evolution. Zn alloys exhibit a more moderate resorption profile and show antibacterial and osteogenic potential, although their relatively low strength restricts use in highly loaded regions. Fe alloys provide excellent structural support, yet their extremely slow degradation may lead to prolonged retention of corrosion products. Mo-based alloys combine high strength, relatively uniform corrosion and promising biosafety, but their dose-dependent toxicity and long-term systemic effects still require further clarification. Recent advances in additive manufacturing, microstructural regulation and surface functionalization have created new opportunities to better balance mechanical reliability with controlled bioresorption. This review also identifies major challenges, including nanoscale interface engineering and standardized in vivo evaluation and discusses future directions for the clinical translation of biodegradable metallic implants.

title: Designing and optimizing the galvanized quenching and partitioning process: Evolution of microstructure and transformation behavior
abstract: This work explores key aspects of designing and optimizing the quenching and partitioning process integrated with galvanizing (GI Q&P) for developing next-generation automotive steels. A conventional CMnSi steel was quenched below the martensite-start temperature, followed by partitioning at 460 °C for time durations (t P ) between 3 and 60 s, to simulate the GI Q&P process using a dilatometer. Carbon redistribution between martensite and remaining austenite was observed during initial quenching, which continued during isothermal holding at the quenching temperature (T Q ) and subsequent partitioning at 460 °C, leading to the stabilization of austenite. Transition carbides and/or cementite and bainite formation were observed during different stages of Q&P. Transition carbides formed during initial quenching and holding at T Q , and then dissolved during partitioning at 460 °C after 30 s, followed by precipitation of cementite. The amount of retained austenite increased with increasing T Q , while its carbon content was not affected much. With increasing t P , both the amount and carbon content of retained austenite first increased, attained a maximum value (∼15 vol pct after t P of 10 s and ∼0.82 wt pct carbon after t P of 30 s), and then decreased, due to austenite decomposition into bainite, and ferrite and cementite.

title: 4D printing of transformable re-entrant auxetic metastructures using shape memory polymers for wearable protective devices
abstract: 4D printing on shape memory polymers (SMPs) enables transformable structures capable of programmable and reversible shape morphing, offering significant potential for adaptive wearable protection. In this study, transformable re-entrant auxetic metastructures based on SMP were designed and fabricated via 4D printing to simultaneously achieve high stretchability and reliable shape recoverability. Finite element analyses incorporating a thermo-viscoelastic constitutive model were conducted to accurately capture temperature-dependent deformation during thermal programming. Both numerical and experimental results demonstrate that the re-entrant auxetic structure exhibits superior stretchability and recovery performance, owing to its bending-dominated deformation mechanism, which enables large ligament rotation while mitigating stress concentration. Compared with conventional porous structures, the re-entrant design achieved substantially larger recoverable deformation and improved structural integrity during repeated transformations. A transformable wrist splint was developed as a representative application, which can be programmed from a compact 2D configuration (50 × 60 mm) into a personalized 3D shape and subsequently recovered within 10 s at 60°C, maintaining a recovery ratio exceeding 97% over repeated cycles. These results demonstrate that combining SMPs with 4D-printed re-entrant auxetic metastructures provides an effective strategy for developing lightweight, portable, and reusable wearable protective devices with enhanced transformability and mechanical robustness.

title: Rice husk cellulose fiber-derived vitrimers: dynamic covalent network design via transesterification exchange with hierarchical structure preservation
