abstract: Bio-based vitrimers have gained considerable attention for their potential to replace fossil derived plastics, address end-of-life recycling issues through dynamic covalent chemistry, and ultimately align materials science with sustainable development principles. However, conventional bio-based vitrimers necessitate the complete depolymerization of natural polymers into small-molecule precursors, disrupting the native supramolecular architecture that underpins their mechanical performance. This study introduces a strategy that preserves the intrinsic fibrous structure of rice husk cellulose to create high-performance, reprocessable vitrimers. Rice husk fibers were activated via steam explosion-alkaline treatment and functionalized through in-situ esterification to incorporate acetyl and phthaloyl groups, while largely preserving the polymerization degree. Crosslinking with bisphenol A diglycidyl ether generated a β-hydroxyester dynamic network. In contrast to a control vitrimer made from cellulose acetate phthalate (CAP) small molecules, the fiber-reinforced vitrimer (ERH-Vitrimer) exhibited superior mechanical properties and thermal stability, owing to the preserved cellulose framework. The ERH-Vitrimer demonstrated reprocessability without external catalyst addition, maintaining over 90% of its tensile strength after 5 cycles, significantly outperforming CAP-Vitrimer, in addition to offering advantages in cost efficiency and biomass content. This work thus demonstrates that preserving native supramolecular structures in bio-based vitrimers leads to a combination of enhanced thermal stability, mechanical robustness, and sustainable reprocessability.

title: Residual Strength–Porosity master curve for thermally damaged composite materials via Arrhenius-Based Time–Temperature Equivalence: A porous solid approach
abstract: A physically grounded model is presented to establish a master curve relating residual compressive strength to porosity ratio in polymer-matrix composites subjected to thermal exposure. Leveraging the Arrhenius law of thermally activated processes, an equivalent damage time t e q = t . e x p ( - E a / ( R . T ) ) , is defined to collapse experimental data across diverse time–temperature histories onto a single monotonic function of residual strength σ as a function of the porosity ϕ . This model derives from the idea that the mechanical strength of a porous solid decreases as porosity ϕ grows because pores interrupt load-bearing cross-sections and act as local stress concentrators. Applied to an independent set of experimental data (heterogeneous kerosene flame exposure), the model captures this behavior through a critical-porosity power law, which is widely used in porous materials science and micromechanics of porous solids. A major practical advantage of the proposed framework is its ability to significantly reduce the experimental burden. Once the master curve is established from a limited set of isothermal tests, residual properties after arbitrary thermal/fire scenarios can be predicted from a single post-exposure porosity measurement. This approach is readily extensible to other polymer-matrix composites.

title: Active learning-driven inference of mesoscale material heterogeneity from acoustic resonance
abstract: Mesoscale material heterogeneity critically influences component performance but remains difficult to quantify using rapid, non-destructive approaches such as vibration sensing. Here, we establish an active learning-driven, physics-guided framework that links heterogeneity to acoustic resonance and enables inference of heterogeneity descriptors from frequency responses. Eigenmode finite element simulations define a nonlinear mapping between heterogeneity descriptors (geometry, location, and material type of dissimilar domains) and vibrational responses across deformation types (elongation, bending, and twisting). To enable efficient forward prediction, surrogate models are constructed to rapidly generate datasets of frequency response–heterogeneity pairs. Trained on these datasets, a coupled inverse–forward neural network architecture is developed to perform inverse prediction while enforcing spectral consistency. Compared to uniform sampling, active learning-guided forward modeling significantly improves data fidelity, which in turn improves the inverse prediction accuracy—increasing the average coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) from 0.75 to 0.82. Mode-specific analyses of forward prediction accuracy and sensitivity suggest that inverse prediction accuracy is governed not only by data but also by the underlying physics. Leveraging this insight, we optimally select informative modes in the input frequency response and further increase R 2 to 0.89. Our findings establish a direct link between forward-model fidelity, physics-based sensitivity, and heterogeneity identifiability.

title: Machine learning–assisted grain boundary segmentation reveals nanoscale heat treatment behavior of additively manufactured 316L stainless steel
abstract: Additive manufacturing produces inhomogeneous and anisotropic microstructures that differ from those in conventionally processed materials. Heat treatment is a crucial process to regulate the microstructural properties. Although estimating the resultant microstructure is a challenging issue, visualizing grain boundaries (GBs) would provide fundamental understanding of the mechanism during heat treatment. In this study, we developed a visualization method using electron diffraction mapping in transmission electron microscopy combined with machine learning. By extracting the area where the feature of electron diffraction patterns varies in the mapping data, GB region was successfully visualized. The developed image processing was applied to ex-situ heating observation of an additively manufactured 316L stainless steel (316L SS), and the curvature variation of GB before and after heat treatment was discussed. It is shown that existing sub-GBs likely attracts GBs, causing unevenness in GB migration.

title: Microstructural evolution and solid-state sintering behavior of SiC during laser-beam directed energy deposition
abstract: Solid-state sintering of SiC powder under various laser scanning regimes was investigated using laser-beam directed energy deposition (DED-LB). The applied laser power input, combined with localized thermal gradients, generates a high-temperature sintering zone that promotes rapid densification of SiC particles. The results demonstrate that the average local sintering temperature is the dominant parameter controlling the sintering response through its direct influence on diffusion kinetics. The X-ray diffraction analysis confirms that evaporation-condensation is the primary densification mechanism under the applied DED-LB conditions, consistent with the high thermal flux and short laser-material interaction time. The microstructural characterization reveals the formation of continuous SiC necks, with consistent observations across complementary analytical techniques. The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis indicates partial surface oxidation, which is expected for SiC processed under atmospheric conditions. Overall, the findings confirm that the DED-LB process provides sufficient thermal energy and diffusion rates to enable localized densification of SiC powder and clarify the process-structure relationships controlling solid-state sintering. These findings provide insight into the sintering mechanisms of dark ceramics processed by DED-LB and highlight the potential of this technique for localized deposition, coating, and repair of SiC-based components.

title: Polycaprolactone microspheres promote hyaluronic acid synthesis in fibroblasts via FOXA1 O-GlcNAcylation
abstract: Polycaprolactone (PCL) microspheres, widely recognized for their biocompatibility and collagen-stimulating properties, have been employed as skin fillers in plastic surgery. However, their broader impact on the synthesis of other extracellular matrix (ECM) components in the skin remains poorly understood. Hyaluronic acid (HA), a critical ECM constituent, is tightly regulated by multiple factors, including metabolic intermediates and epigenetic modifications. Herein, we confirmed that 6-hydroxyhexanoic acid (6-HHA), degradation metabolite of PCL microspheres, significantly enhances HA synthesis in skin fibroblasts. Specifically, PCL microspheres upregulate the expression of hyaluronic acid synthases (HAS), activate the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway (HBP) in fibroblasts. This metabolic shift leads to elevated levels of O-linked N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) and increased O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT)-mediated protein glycosylation (O-GlcNAcylation). Mechanistically, we identify forkhead box A1 (FOXA1) as a key transcriptional regulator of HAS expression. Notably, PCL microspheres facilitate O-GlcNAcylation of FOXA1 at serine 151 (S151) in an OGT-dependent manner, enhancing the transcriptional activity of HAS genes and promoting HA synthesis. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel mechanism by which PCL microspheres stimulate HA production through FOXA1 O-GlcNAcylation, providing new insights into the role of post-translational modification in ECM remodeling in skin aging and skin regeneration.

title: Multifunctional injectable hydrogel loaded with sheep placenta and copper-tannic acid nanozyme for facilitating spinal cord regeneration
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) can lead to severe oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration in the local microenvironment, which hinders spinal cord regeneration. Injectable hydrogels have been investigated as potential therapeutic strategies for SCI. However, the microenvironment of an injured spinal cord is complex, as hemorrhage, ischemia, glial scar formation, and demyelination occur at different times and locations. In this study, a novel injectable functional hydrogel based on sheep placenta powder (SSP), hyaluronic acid methacrylate (HAMA) and copper-tannic acid (CuTA) nanozyme was developed to provide strong reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging ability, inhibition of macrophage polarization, and angiogenesis sequentially. After implantation, the multifunctional hydrogel alleviated local oxidative stress, inhibited the infiltration of M1 macrophages, accelerated the switching of M1 macrophages to the M2 type, and promoted local microvessel regeneration, thereby established a satisfactory foundation for spinal cord reconstruction and further improved behavioral phenotypes and motor abilities. Therefore, the multifunctional hydrogel offers a promising approach for SCI treatment.

title: Interfacial and bonding characteristics of low-temperature Cu–Cu joints with an Au passivation layer
abstract: As the three-dimensional (3D) integrated circuit technology advances toward finer-pitch structures, hybrid Cu bonding has emerged as a superior alternative to conventional microbumps. However, Cu oxidation and the high thermal budgets required for bonding present significant technical hurdles. This study proposes depositing a uniform Au thin film on Cu surfaces via electroless plating to act as an oxidation barrier to overcome these limitations. To enable systematic investigation of interfacial evolution, bonding was conducted at 220 °C under 30 MPa for 1.5 h. The specific activation energies of Au–Cu interdiffusion causes the Au passivation layer to remain localized at the bonding interface, effectively suppressing Cu oxidation even under atmospheric pressure. The resulting joints exhibited excellent mechanical integrity, achieving a maximum shear strength of 57.8 MPa with minimal void formation and a low surface roughness. Compared to nonpassivated joints, the Au-passivated samples demonstrated superior reliability and performance even after postbonding annealing. These findings provide mechanistic insights into thickness-dependent interfacial diffusion, void evolution, and reliability behavior in Au-passivated Cu–Cu bonding systems.

title: IN625–CuCrZr multi-material joints by PBF-LB/M: Process–structure–property relationships
abstract: 3D-printed multi-material components represent a major advancement in additive manufacturing, allowing the combination of dissimilar materials to achieve tailored properties and functionalities. Recent developments in Laser Powder Bed Fusion (PBF-LB/M) with Selective Powder Deposition modules have enabled the creation of multi-material powder beds, paving the way for complex and functionally graded structures. This study explores the interfacial features of IN625–CuCrZr components produced by PBF-LB/M, with emphasis on the effects of interface orientation and deposition sequence on microstructure, mechanical, and thermal properties. Results demonstrate the formation of dense interfaces with continuous metallurgical bonding. The morphology and width of the transition zone vary with both orientation and deposition sequence. EBSD analyses reveal a columnar-to-equiaxed grain transition when moving from IN625 to CuCrZr. Mechanical tests, especially in-situ SEM tensile tests, suggest that joint strength and crack development strongly depend on interface orientation and loading direction. Laser flash analysis highlights enhanced thermal diffusivity in CuCrZr–IN625 joints, exceeding that of monolithic IN625, thus suggesting potential for high-performance applications. These findings clarify deposition-sequence effects on interfacial bonding, intermixing, defects, and performance in IN625/CuCrZr architectures.

title: Effect of varying trunnion geometry of hip implant on contact mechanics under walking gait cycle: A finite element study
abstract: This study investigates the contact parameters at the trunnion by analyzing the effects of four key geometric factors: distal and proximal chamfer geometry, contact length and surface geometry, and acetabular head diameter, to identify designs that reduce the risk of contact-related failures. The forces are exerted in the F x , F y , and F z directions on hip implant acetabular head. The chamfer cut improve the contact stress distribution, micromotion, and penetration, whereas trunnions without a chamfer exhibit stress concentration that can lead to edge damage and joint failure. Increasing the contact length from 10 to 17.5 mm improves contact stress, micromotion and penetration and contributes to a lower wear rate. The acetabular head diameter variation has very negligible effect on the contact parameters at trunnion. Furthermore, angular mismatches at trunnion create a shielding effect, resulting in contact stress concentration and potential damage at the trunnion edges. Notably, spur gear trunnion models with 4 and 8 teeth show superior performance by reducing sliding distance and wear rate. These findings offer valuable insights for optimizing trunnion design to improve implant longevity and performance.

title: Enhancing corrosion rate prediction under data scarcity with virtual sample generation and heterogeneous transfer learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of corrosion rates is essential for optimizing the alloy composition of structural metals and evaluating their service lifetimes. However, corrosion datasets for newly developed structural metals are typically of limited size, and significant differences in alloy composition, environmental conditions, and data dimensionality between existing and new material datasets often prevent direct knowledge reuse. In this paper, we propose a structural metal corrosion rate prediction framework that combines virtual sample generation and heterogeneous transfer learning (VSG-HTL). We first apply three topology-based virtual sample generation strategies to augment the limited training data and compare their effectiveness. We then utilize heterogeneous transfer learning to transfer knowledge from large-scale corrosion datasets of existing materials to the new dataset, selecting appropriate fine-tuning strategies based on the similarity between datasets. Experiments on multiple structural metal corrosion datasets under different environmental conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms a baseline artificial neural network and other existing methods in predictive accuracy, validating its effectiveness in scenarios with limited samples and heterogeneous data.

title: A performance-customized design framework for the hydraulic quadruped robot leg limb unit based on additive manufacturing
abstract: A B S T R A C THydraulic quadruped robots are considered to have the potential to surpass their biological counterparts due to their exceptional terrain adaptability and high power-to-weight ratio. As the core component of hydraulic quadruped robots, the motion characteristics of the leg limb unit (LLU) directly determine the upper performance limits of the entire robot. This study proposes a performance-customized design framework for the hydraulic quadruped robot LLU based on additive manufacturing. First, the requirements for the LLU were analyzed, leading to defined design objectives: lightweight, tubeless, and integrated construction. Next, an accurate mechanical model was developed through bionic structural design and key parameter matching. Finally, a performance-customized design process incorporating topology optimization and lattice filling methods was implemented for the structural components. Following this framework, an LLU for the Spurlos II quadruped robot was designed and manufactured. The thigh part achieved extreme lightweighting (37.2% mass reduction from 1574.09 g to 988.56 g) while maintaining hydraulic functionality. The LLU was successfully fabricated via additive manufacturing and was assembled. Comparative experiments validated the superior dynamic performance of the proposed LLU, demonstrating smaller trajectory tracking errors and better dynamic performance than the previous generation.

title: AlB2 nanosheets as energetic boosters: enhancement of energetic performance of AlB2 fuels
abstract: AlB 2 has been a focused candidate for applying as a solid fuel in energetics. However, the limited energy release rate of AlB 2 fuel restricts its wider adoption. To address this limitation, we prepared AlB 2 nanosheets containing nanoscale AlB 2 by liquid-phase exfoliation to improve the energetic performance of AlB 2 fuel. The microstructure and exfoliation principle of fuels were characterized and investigated. The oxidation kinetics and corresponding oxidation process of the AlB 2 nanosheets were explored. The superiority of AlB 2 nanosheets in terms of combustion release rate was verified by using laser ignition experiments and combustion pressure tests. Additionally, the combustion mechanism of AlB 2 nanosheets was investigated through an analysis of combustion products. The research findings indicate that the peak pressure of the AlB 2 nanosheet/AP composite exhibits a significantly enhanced energy release capacity—2.53 times greater—compared to the bulk AlB 2 /AP composite. The pressure rise rate and burning rate of the former are 3.38 times and 1.46 times those of the latter, respectively, which can be attributed to the existence of two-dimensional AlB 2 and the larger surface area of the AlB 2 nanosheets. This work provides a promising high-energy fuel for energetic materials.

title: Designing heterogeneous microstructure in PM nickel superalloys via dual-alloy powder blending: A combined experimental and computational study
abstract: Heterogeneous microstructure design holds promise to overcome the inherent trade-off between high-temperature strength and dwell crack growth (DCG) resistance in powder metallurgy (PM) nickel-based superalloys for aero-engine disks. Herein, a dual-alloy powder blending strategy is presented to engineer and control microstructure heterogeneity. Two master alloy powders with distinct compositions and γ’ solvus temperatures—a low-solvus alloy (S1) and a high-solvus alloy (S2)—were blended (20 wt.% S1), consolidated via hot isostatic pressing, and subjected to supersolvus solution treatment. Multi-scale characterization revealed that compositional inheritance produced a stable heterogeneous microstructure: S1-derived regions containing finer γ’ precipitates (~190 nm, ~53 vol.%) and coarse grains (~76 µm) embedded within an S2 matrix featuring coarser γ’ (~310 nm, ~63 vol.%) and finer grains (~38 µm). This heterogeneity originates from differential γ’ dissolution kinetics and limited interdiffusion of slow-diffusing elements (Cr, W, Mo, Ta), as validated by thermodynamic and kinetic simulations. The degree of heterogeneity is highly sensitive to initial powder size and cooling rate: simulations established a critical S1 particle radius of ~20 µm below which compositional inheritance is lost, while rapid cooling (3 °C/s) intensified non-equilibrium precipitation. These findings provide quantitative design criteria for engineering heterogeneous PM superalloys with enhanced damage tolerance.

title: Tailoring phase formation and mechanical properties of low-temperature-grown Al-rich CrAlWN films by selective metal-ion bombardment during high-power impulse magnetron sputtering
abstract: Conventional physical vapor deposition of CrAlN coatings on carbon-rich steels (e.g., 100Cr6) is restricted to <∼160 °C to preclude processes deleterious to the mechanical properties of steel. Here, we present a two-step pulsed substrate-biasing strategy in reactive high-power impulse magnetron sputtering to deposit Al-rich, single-phase cubic Cr 1−x−y Al x W y N (x > 0.5, 0 < y < 0.24) films under <∼160 °C. Pulsed substrate biasing favors selective Al⁺ ion bombardment during early stages of film growth (< 200 nm) and subsequently enables Al⁺ and Cr⁺ bombardment by extending the bias pulse width. This approach stabilizes rocksalt CrAlN by suppressing phase separation without interrupting the deposition process. The resultant films are dense, exhibit ∼ 30 GPa indentation hardness, and high residual compressive stress of 4.2 GPa. Introducing W + ions with Cr + and Al + at ion energies of ∼ 30–100 eV lowers compressive stress by up to 0.97 GPa while retaining high hardness and increased film density. These attributes cannot be realized by conventional direct current magnetron sputtering at 500 °C. Such W alloying combined with two-step substrate biasing do not induce grain coarsening and strain relaxation due to tempering in 100Cr6 substrates. This can be adapted for growing low-temperature nitride films on temperature-sensitive substrates.

title: Hydrogel-based regulation of neutrophil extracellular traps: from wound healing to multi-system disease management
abstract: Inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases represent a major global health challenge, urgently demanding novel therapeutic targets. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are reticular structures released by neutrophils. As a vital component of innate immunity, NETs physically trap and eliminate invading pathogens. However, excessive NETs activation or impaired clearance drives the pathogenesis of various diseases. These aberrant processes exacerbate inflammation, trigger autoimmune disorders, impair wound healing, and promote thrombosis. Furthermore, they create a microenvironment that facilitates cancer metastasis and immune evasion. Consequently, targeted interventions against NETs have emerged as promising therapeutic strategies for these conditions. In this context, hydrogels exhibit enormous application potential due to their excellent biocompatibility and superior drug controlled-release capabilities. This review introduces NETs formation pathways, comprehensively summarizes cutting-edge hydrogel-based NETs-targeting therapies across various diseases, and discusses integrated hydrogel design strategies, aiming to provide new insights for the development of more efficient and intelligent targeted NETs therapy.

title: Mg2+ loaded heparin functionalized injectable gelatin hydrogel promotes bone defect repair
abstract: Hydrogels have emerged as promising materials for bone tissue engineering applications. However, a significant challenge in osteogenic hydrogels lies in insufficient osteogenic activity, limiting efficacy in bone defect repair. During hydrogel construction, the selection of appropriate cross-linking molecules to impart enhanced biological properties remains a critical factor for effective bone defect repair. Herein, a hydrogel constructed using methacrylated gelatin, methacrylated heparin, alendronic acid, and Mg 2+ was used to promote the repair of bone defects. HepMA was successfully prepared by the methacrylic anhydride. The carboxyl groups of HepMA were modified to synthesize HepMA-BP. The incorporation of HepMA-BP reduced the injection resistance of GelMA, and upon photo-crosslinking, the hydrogel demonstrated the capacity for Mg 2+ loading and sustained release of phosphorus (P) and magnesium (Mg). In addition, heparin functionalized hydrogels significantly promoted angiogenesis, inhibited osteoclastic differentiation, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs after binding Mg 2+ . At 8 weeks, the Mg 2+ loaded hydrogel could significantly repair bone defects in rats. GelMA-BP-Mg hydrogel enhances osteogenesis by promoting Vascular Cell Adhesion Molecule 1(VCAM1) overexpression via the TNF-α pathway, representing a potential underlying mechanism. Therefore, Mg 2+ loaded heparin functionalized hydrogel, with high osteogenic activity, may offer a reliable solution for bone defect repair in the near future.

title: Plant-derived vesicle-like nanoparticles: current applications in systemic conditions and future horizons in oral diseases
abstract: Plant-derived vesicle-like nanoparticles (PDVLNs) refer to nanoscale vesicular structures isolated from plants. They can be internalized by human cells, deliver functional molecules, and exert biological effects. Substantial progress was made in exploring the biomedical application of PDVLNs. However, these studies primarily focus on various systemic diseases, with limited attention given to oral diseases. Oral diseases affect both oral and systemic health, and their treatment modalities are compromised by the dynamic oral environment, underscoring the need for innovative therapeutic approaches. The natural biocompatibility, modifiability, and diverse functionality of PDVLNs make them promising new strategies. Systematically exploring the potential of PDVLNs in oral diseases represented by dental diseases, periodontal diseases, oral mucosal diseases, and maxillofacial bone diseases is of critical importance for expanding the application of PDVLNs into the field of oral medicine. This review briefly introduces the overview of PDVLNs, including their biogenesis, isolation, and characterization. It then demonstrates the distribution and safety profile of PDVLNs following cellular and systemic uptake. Importantly, it provides a detailed summary of research findings on the application of PDVLNs treating systemic and oral conditions. Finally, it discusses the challenges PDVLNs face in clinical translation and highlights their potential applications in oral disease treatment.

title: Dissimilar fabrication of Ti/TiAl bimetal via wire arc directed energy deposition
abstract: The pronounced mismatch in thermal and mechanical properties between titanium alloys and titanium aluminide alloys presents significant challenges for achieving high-quality metallurgical bonding. In this study, a Ti6Al4V and high-niobium TiAl alloy (Ti45Al8Nb) bimetal were fabricated via wire arc directed energy deposition (wire arc DED). The results demonstrate that a transition zone exists between Ti6Al4V and Ti45Al8Nb. This region comprises five distinct sublayers with a continuous composition gradient from Ti6Al4V to Ti45Al8Nb, and the microstructure evolves progressively from a basket‑weave α structure, to a tweed‑like α 2 structure, then to a rod‑like α 2 + B2 mixture, and finally to fine α 2 /γ lamellar colonies. The formation of this gradient transition zone is attributed to the plasma arc heat source, which induces interlayer remelting and promotes melt pool convection, leading to elemental mixing and the establishment of a compositional gradient. Tensile tests revealed an ultimate tensile strength of 341.2 MPa and elongation of 0.82 %, with fracture occurring in the third sublayer. The fracture was primarily caused by the synergistic effects of brittle α 2 /B2 phase precipitation, strong texture, and local stress concentration. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of wire arc DED for fabricating crack‑free Ti/TiAl bimetal and elucidate the microstructural evolution and fracture mechanisms within the gradient transition zone.

title: Coupling surface vibratory extrusion and carburizing heat treatment to improve the surface microstructure and mechanical properties of powder metallurgy steel
abstract: Surface integrity is critical to the reliability of powder metallurgy steels in service environments. However, surface densification, although necessary for structural support, reduces the pore-assisted pathways available for carbon transport during carburizing, making it difficult to achieve both a dense surface layer and effective thermochemical strengthening. To address this issue, a coupled processing route consisting of surface vibratory extrusion and carburizing heat treatment was proposed for Fe-Mo-Cu-C powder metallurgy steel. Surface vibratory extrusion produced a 620 μm densified layer and promoted continuous dynamic recrystallization, generating a high density of grain boundaries and dislocations. These microstructural features increased the effective diffusion coefficient by about 51 % compared with steady-state extrusion. The treated surface developed high-carbon fine-grained martensite and fine dispersed carbides, increasing the surface peak hardness to 882 HV 1.0 , corresponding to a 3.95-fold increase over the untreated state, and extending the effective case depth to 1265 μm. The carbon concentration gradient also contributed to a surface compressive residual stress of 277 MPa. Tribological investigations showed improved friction and wear behavior through a transition from severe pore-induced spalling to mild abrasive wear with frictional oxidation. These results provide useful guidance for designing surface strengthening processes for high-performance powder metallurgy components.

title: Geometric determinants of monotonic and fatigue performance in additively manufactured TPMS lattice structures: Decomposing scale effects
abstract: Additively-manufactured lattice structures are increasingly used in biomedical, automotive, and aerospace applications, where scale strongly influences structural integrity. In TPMS gyroid lattices, even though scaling involves simultaneous changes in unit-cell size and wall thickness, their combined effects on manufacturing fidelity and mechanical performance remain unclear. This study investigates these effects in AlSi10Mg gyroid lattices under monotonic and fatigue loading by decomposing scale into three cases: variation in scale, variation in unit-cell size at constant wall thickness, and variation in wall thickness at constant unit-cell size. As-printed geometric deviations altered key attributes governing mechanical performance, including relative density, slenderness, and surface-to-volume ratio Wall thickness showed the strongest influence on geometric deviation, whereas unit-cell size showed comparatively stable geometric fidelity. Monotonic properties were governed primarily by relative density and slenderness. Fatigue behaviour was controlled by the coupled effects of relative density and surface-to-volume ratio, reflecting a competitive damage mechanism between deformation mode and surface roughness. Both yield strength and fatigue limit decreased with increasing unit-cell size or decreasing wall thickness, with mechanical performance showing greater sensitivity to unit-cell size than to wall thickness. Decomposing scale effects offers a clearer interpretation of geometry–process–performance relationships beyond trends observed for individual geometric parameters.

title: Regulatory network–oriented design of stimuli-responsive biomaterials for oral and craniofacial bone regeneration
abstract: Oral and craniofacial bone regeneration is regulated by a dynamically evolving defect microenvironment in which microbial dysbiosis, persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, extracellular matrix degradation, and altered mechanical signaling are closely interconnected. These convergent pathological cues act on shared regulatory pathways coupling immune activation with bone remodeling, resulting in sustained osteoclastogenesis and impaired osteogenic differentiation. Conventional biomaterials, primarily designed for structural support, have limited capacity to modulate this temporally shifting signaling network. Stimuli-responsive biomaterials provide a microenvironment-adaptive intervention strategy by sensing pathological alterations and translating them into defined biological responses. Responsiveness to chemical and physical cues enables spatiotemporal regulation of interconnected processes governing inflammation, osteoclast activity, immunometabolic homeostasis, and mechanotransductive signaling. Modulation of these regulatory pathways supports restoration of osteoimmune balance and regenerative remodeling. This review establishes a network-based framework linking microenvironmental pathology to pathway-level material design in oral and craniofacial bone repair. Responsive systems are organized according to activation mechanisms and regulatory targets, and translational considerations related to response precision, long-term safety, and scalable manufacturing are critically assessed.

title: Displacement modeling for liquid cast forming process development considering microstructure evolution
abstract: This study presents a liquid cast forming process enabling thin-walled aluminum structures (1–3 mm) by combining sand casting flexibility with controlled melt displacement above the liquidus temperature. Unlike semi-solid processing requiring forces of 40–80 MPa, this liquid-phase approach achieves wall thicknesses below the conventional sand-casting limit of 4–6 mm with negligible forces (<10 N), preserving sand mold integrity. An energy balance model predicts transient temperature fields during punch-induced displacement, incorporating a characteristic displacement ratio ζ relating surface-to-volume geometry to process window duration. Experimental validation using EN AC-AlSi7Mg0.3 demonstrated reliable production of 1–3 mm wall thicknesses at punch velocities of 2.5–15 mm/s and casting temperatures of 680–745 °C. Model predictions showed excellent agreement with experimental data (<5 % deviation) for processes above the liquidus temperature (615 °C). Microstructural analysis revealed secondary dendrite arm spacing predominantly influenced by wall thickness (16 % increase from 1 to 3 mm) and punch velocity. The forming zone exhibited 29 % finer microstructure compared to non-deformed regions due to enhanced heat extraction through direct punch contact.

title: Phase-dependent thermoelectric performance of MnIn2Te4
abstract: We investigate the thermoelectric properties of MnIn 2 Te 4 in both experimentally characterized phases. The tetragonal phase undergoes a pressure-induced transition to an orthorhombic phase at 1.3 GPa. First-principles calculations reveal for both phases a small energy difference between antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic states. The band gap is 1.04 (0.70) eV in the tetragonal phase and 1.25 (1.10) eV in the orthorhombic phase for the antiferromagnetic (ferromagnetic) state. A higher power factor is achieved for n -type than for p -type carriers. At 700 K, for example, the more densely packed orthorhombic phase exhibits a 57% reduction in the lattice thermal conductivity compared with the tetragonal phase, yielding high thermoelectric figures of merit of 1.23 for n -type carriers and 0.96 for p -type carriers at optimal carrier concentration.

title: Ameliorative effect of surface-functionalized polymeric@selenium-bioflavonoid nanoparticles on cognition
abstract: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a comorbid condition associated with diabetes mellitus affecting senior citizens worldwide. Many therapies, including nanotechnology, are targeted at ameliorating cognitive functions by inhibiting neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. Hesperidin (HSP) is a bioflavonoid that possesses a variety of pharmacological effects, including neuroprotection; however, its short plasma half-life and poor aqueous solubility limit its use in clinical settings. The present work is designed to enhance the stability, permeability, and bioavailability of HSP in the brain by conjugating it with selenium nanoparticles (HSNPs). Furthermore, the functionalization of selenium-conjugated HSP with chitosan (CSHNPs) aims to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of HSP. The nanoparticles are synthesised and characterised by several spectroscopic and microscopic techniques. The neurobehavioral studies assess the efficacy of HSP in nanoformulations (HSNPs and CSHNPs) in vitro and in vivo oxidative stress parameters, nitrite levels, and acetylcholinesterase levels in the streptozotocin-induced diabetic cognitive impairment rat model. The nanoformulations enhance the antioxidant enzyme levels, nitrite, and acetylcholinesterase by reducing lipid peroxidation, improving memory and learning in the diabetes-induced cognitively impaired rats. The neuroprotective activity of the polymer-selenium conjugated HSP is more than that of HSP and HSNPs; hence, it may offer an alternate management for neurodegenerative diseases like CI and Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Critical review of recent advancements of mxene in diabetic wound healing
abstract: Diabetic wounds constitute a significant worldwide health issue due to chronic inflammation, heightened oxidative stress, compromised angiogenesis, hypoxia, and persistent infections. Traditional wound dressings and antibiotics often fail to overcome these complex obstacles, underscoring the need for sophisticated, multifaceted biomaterials. MXenes, an innovative class of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides, have recently emerged as viable options for diabetic wound treatment due to their unique physicochemical, electrical, and biological properties. This study rigorously assesses recent developments in MXene-based hydrogels, microneedles, nanozymes, composite membranes, and biosensors for the treatment of diabetic wounds.MXenes exhibit significant antibacterial properties, remarkable photothermal responsiveness, robust antioxidant activity, and efficient immunomodulation, including the facilitation of M2 macrophage polarization. Their superior conductivity and adjustable surface chemistry facilitate improved angiogenesis, collagen deposition, reactive oxygen species scavenging, oxygen transport, and bioelectrical signaling. Moreover, MXene-integrated wearable and implantable biosensors enable real-time surveillance of wound microenvironmental parameters, including pH, moisture, temperature, and biochemical markers pertinent to diabetic foot problems. Notwithstanding considerable advances, obstacles remain regarding long-term biological compatibility, biodegradability, stability, and scalable production. Mitigating these restrictions could expedite the clinical adoption of MXene-enabled technologies for precision-oriented diabetic wound treatments.

title: Progress in binder jet 3D printing of advanced ceramics: An insightful review
abstract: Binder jetting (BJ) is one of the most scalable additive manufacturing (AM) technologies with advantages such as: (i) high throughput, (ii) amenable to printing a wide variety of materials, viz. metals, polymers, ceramics & composites, and (iii) the ability to produce complex geometries without the need for support structures. In addition, BJ uses significantly less quantity of additives compared to other AM methods and has the flexibility of handling both dry and wet powder beds. This timely, in-depth review aims to provide a holistic powder-to-product excursion of binder jetting of ceramics, elaborating on various aspects such as powder/binder design, their desired characteristics, print parameter optimisation, and post-processing (binder removal and sintering). The progressive developments of BJ of advanced ceramics have been examined, critically analysed and evaluated from the perspectives of innovations in both printer and part manufacturing. The epilogue highlights the new directions for pushing the research boundaries of the BJ of advanced ceramics, a roadmap for emerging applications and the opportunities for industrial take-up.

title: Data-driven trend assessment of glass-forming ability in metallic glasses using experimental characteristic temperatures
abstract: The industrial application of Metallic glasses (MGs) is seriously limited by their glass-forming ability (GFA), typically quantified by the critical casting diameter (Dmax). Traditional empirical methods for predicting GFA are often system-specific and lack general applicability. Data-driven modeling based on experimentally accessible descriptors offers an alternative route for GFA evaluation across different alloy systems. In recent years, data-driven approaches has emerged as a promising tool for GFA prediction, but challenges such as data imbalance, model homogeneity, and dependence on extensive feature engineering remain. To address these issues, this study develops develops a hierarchical ensemble modeling framework that integrates stacking and blending strategies. Using a standardized dataset of 712 samples with three experimentally measurable characteristic temperatures (Tg, Tx, and Tl) and corresponding Dmax, KNN, XGBoost, and Random Forest were selected as base learners. The resulting model demonstrates stable agreement between predicted and experimentally measured Dmax values on independent test data, showing improved robustness under imbalanced data conditions, and provides practical data-driven tool for GFA trend assessment and composition screening, offering model-assisted guidance for optimizing alloy compositions rather than replacing experimental validation.

title: Adaptive material properties tailoring for stress concentration
abstract: Avoiding stress concentrations is essential to prevent engineering failures. Advanced manufacturing methods like multi-material additive manufacturing are enabling the realization of structures with intricate spatially varying mechanical properties, offering an attractive pathway for redistributing the stress by adjusting mechanical properties in selected locations. This work effectively marries the concepts of material properties and stress distribution, and addresses the issue of what material properties minimize stress concentration by adaptive design of Young’s modulus, Poisson’s ratio, shear modulus and yield strength for both isotropic and anisotropic materials. Regions of adjustable material properties are created around areas of high stress to alter the stress distribution. The accurate mechanical properties distributions are calculated using adaptive design method in a finite element analysis framework. The effectiveness of the much-enhanced material properties on reducing stress concentrations is demonstrated for thin plate with circular hole and L-shaped thin plate. Results show that the peak stress can be reduced by up to about 70 % in isotropic designs and up to over 80 % in anisotropic designs.

title: Evaluation method for the interfacial strength of thermally grown Al2O3 scale and Ni-Al alloy
abstract: Nanoindentation techniques are useful for evaluating the critical load for crack initiation on interface between Ni-Al alloy and thin surface Al 2 O 3 scale formed at high temperature, since interfacial cracking can be clearly detected as a pop-in event. However, actual interfacial stress applied during loading and when cracked is unclear, due to the multiaxial stress field. Here we analyzed interfacial stress distribution during the nanoindentation using finite element analysis. Elastoplastic simulations of nanoindentation were performed with local stress–strain curves for oxide scale and the Al depletion zone. Local stress–strain curves were inversely analyzed from experimental load-penetration depth curves, obtained using separate nanoindentation tests. Interfacial stress was obtained as a function of indentation load, clarifying that shear stress acting on interface contributed significantly to crack initiation. The two-parameter Weibull plots of interfacial strength σ I n t , m a x c were converted from pop-in load P c obtained in experimental nanoindentation tests for samples with different amounts of impurity S segregation. Largest differences appear where fracture probability F is low; for F = 4 %, difference of approximately 780 MPa between the sample with higher S segregation level (high S interface alloy, σ I n t , m a x c =1.73 GPa) and lower S segregation level (low S interface alloy, σ I n t , m a x c =2.51 GPa) were obtained.

title: Advanced spectroscopic investigation of lunar highland simulant (LHS-1) geopolymer for in-situ resource utilization
abstract: In situ resource utilization (ISRU) is essential for sustainable lunar infrastructure, where geopolymers provide a promising pathway to reduce dependence on Earth-supplied materials. This study evaluates Lunar Highland Simulant-1 (LHS-1) as a geopolymer precursor, comparing as-received and screened fractions activated with sodium hydroxide. While the general effects of alkali concentration on geopolymerization are established, the spectroscopic characteristics and mineralogical effects of LHS-1 remain insufficiently understood and are systematically investigated here. Screening reduced the median particle size by about 33 percent, increasing surface area and reactivity. Multi-technique spectroscopic analyses (FT-IR, NMR, XPS, Raman) confirmed enhanced aluminosilicate network formation in screened and high-alkali systems, accompanied by the development of crystalline sodalite and garronite phases. Mechanical testing showed that compressive strength improved by 42 to 44 percent with screening, achieving up to 29.7 MPa in the 10 M mixture after screening. Thermal and microstructural evaluations (TGA, MIP, calorimetry) further demonstrated greater N-A-S-H gel formation, refined pore structure, and accelerated reaction kinetics. These findings provide new information into the geopolymerization characteristics of LHS-1, providing a laboratory-scale reference for ISRU material screening.

title: Data-driven process maps for functionally graded foams in foam additive manufacturing: Accuracy and interpretability across six models
abstract: Abstract Foam Additive Manufacturing (FAM) couples gas-assisted foaming with material extrusion to produce lightweight PLA components, yet the combined influence of solubilization and extrusion variables remains poorly quantified. We analyze 528 experiments on PLA foamed with CO₂ and model strand density (ρ) as a function of six controllable parameters (Pₐ, tₐ, t_d, Tₑ, Sₑ, Dₙ). We compare six regressors (polynomial, PCA + polynomial, SVR-RBF, Random Forest, RF-distilled polynomial surrogate, and MLP) using an identical 80/20 held-out test partition and a standardized map-generation protocol. The Bayesian-regularized MLP attains the highest nominal accuracy(MAE = 0.0925 g/cm³, RMSE = 0.1216 g/cm³, R² = 0.832),while the Random Forest provides the most reliable non-neural baseline(R² = 0.41, RMSE = 0.141 g/cm³). To reconcile accuracy and interpretability, we distill the Random Forest into a degree-2 polynomial surrogate that yields a closed-form, differentiable mapping with competitive error and enables analytic process maps and gradient-based optimization. The resulting maps quantify interactions among Tₑ and Sₑ at fixed (Pₐ, tₐ, t_d), revealing physically consistent trends (density decreases with increasing Sₑ; mild increase with Tₑ). This study delivers a hybrid framework—ensemble accuracy plus polynomial transparency—for predictive design and multivariable control in FAM, and establishes reproducible benchmarks and artifacts (code, splits, figures) to support deployment in digital twins and closed-loop process planning.

title: Critical evaluation and thermodynamic modeling of the BaO-TiO2-Ti2O3 system for MLCC applications
abstract: The critical evaluation and thermodynamic modeling of the BaO-TiO 2 -Ti 2 O 3 system was carried out with a special emphasis on BaTiO 3 perovskite solid solution. All reliable thermodynamic data, phase equilibria, and non-stoichiometries of BaTiO 3 perovskite under both oxidizing and reducing conditions were well reproduced by the thermodynamic model with optimized parameters. In particular, the proper defect structure of BaTiO 3 perovskite solid solution was employed in the present thermodynamic model to accurately explain the variation of oxygen deficiency and non-stoichiometry of BaTiO 3 depending on oxygen partial pressure and temperature. The developed thermodynamic database was applied to the Ni/BaTiO 3 Multilayered Ceramic Capacitor (MLCC) sintering process calculations, and the contour map of oxygen vacancy formation in BaTiO 3 and Ni oxidation depending on sintering conditions was successfully predicted.

title: FracFlowFormer: Generative forecasting of microstructural evolution in thermal barrier coatings
abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) during thermal-shock durability testing of thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) is limited to a few checkpoints, which limits microstructural evolution analysis due to sparse imaging data. Here we present FracFlowFormer, a data-efficient forecasting framework that learns from limited early-stage SEM observations and predicts late-stage fracture and pore evolution in TBCs. To address the issue of coarse temporal sampling, we reconstruct more densely sampled temporal sequences employing TV-L1 dense optical-flow interpolation, thereby generating intermediate states that maintain fracture- and pore-relevant morphology. FracFlowFormer forecasts subsequent microstructural evolution using a hybrid architecture that combines a U-Net encoder–decoder and a spatio-temporal fusion transformer for long-range temporal SEM image generation, enabling high-fidelity predictions that capture microstructural evolution in TBCs during thermal-shock cycling, with 89.95% SSIM, 0.049 LPIPS, and 23.18 dB PSNR. An optical-flow branch provides a microstructural evolution cue that complements grayscale appearance and temporal aspects information. The framework reconstructs high-fidelity, time-resolved image sequences from sparse early-stage observations and demonstrates descriptor-based characterization of microstructural evolution, thereby transforming TBC characterization from static inspection into evolution-aware analysis of degradation and failure.

title: Advances in nanocellulose hydrogels for wound dressing and healing therapy: a review
abstract: With accelerating advances in regenerative medicine and wound-healing technologies, developing materials that are biocompatible, effective, and that enhance tissue regeneration has become a pivotal focus. Nanocellulose, an emerging natural polymer nanomaterial with high specific surface area, tunable surface chemistry, excellent mechanical properties, and good biocompatibility, is an ideal scaffold for functional hydrogel dressings. This review discusses the main types of nanocellulose, including Cellulose Nanocrystals (CNC), Cellulose Nanofibers(CNF), and Bacterial Nanocellulose (BNC), their preparation methods, and structural characteristics. Given the unique advantages of nanocellulose-based hydrogels in wound treatment, this review summarizes construction strategies, performance-tuning mechanisms, and multifunctional applications in wound healing, focusing on accelerating wound closure, antimicrobial and antioxidant properties, promoting angiogenesis, and controlled drug release. It also compares the biological properties of different nanocellulose hydrogels, highlighting that by rationally adjusting network structures, introducing functional components, and constructing composite systems, their mechanical stability and bioactivity can be significantly improved. Finally, this review discusses challenges in large-scale preparation, long-term biocompatibility assessment, and clinical translation, and looks forward to future development toward smart, personalized wound management and tissue regeneration.

title: PLA/CNT for plate lattice architectures: Experiments and constitutive modeling for mechanical and piezoresistive characterization
abstract: This study presents an integrated experimental and numerical framework for the mechanical and piezoresistive characterization of plate lattices fabricated via filament deposition modeling. Material-level tensile and compressive tests are conducted on polylactic acid doped with carbon nanotubes, considering multiple printing orientations. The results reveal pronounced print-induced anisotropy (up to 70% variation in tensile strength), tension–compression asymmetry, and direction-dependent sensing behavior. Body-centered cubic (BCC) and face-centered cubic (FCC) plate lattices with varying relative densities and printing directions are fabricated and tested under compression. The FCC lattices achieve a maximum strength of 11.8 MPa, while BCC lattices reach a stiffness of 588 MPa. A constitutive model is calibrated using the material-level data: elastic behavior is described with a reduced transversely isotropic formulation, and inelastic behavior is captured using either the Hill anisotropic yield criterion or Drucker–Prager plasticity. Piezoresistive response is modeled linearly, assuming operation within a non-damaging loading regime. Model calibration is performed through closed-loop optimization across all printing orientations and loading cases. The calibrated models are validated against BCC lattice experiments, showing excellent agreement. This framework provides not only global material models but also a robust foundation for the design and characterization of multifunctional lattice materials.

title: Biomechanical and anatomical optimization of iliosacral screw corridors based on statistical shape modeling, CT density mapping and finite element analysis
abstract: Sacral fractures are associated with severe morbidity and prolonged recovery, with screw internal fixation serving as the primary treatment. However, standardized sacral screw corridors that simultaneously account for individual anatomical variability and biomechanical load transmission are lacking. Current corridor selection relies heavily on surgeon experience. This study aims to establish a standardized sacral screw corridor that unifies anatomical adaptability and mechanical stability. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to identify major sacral morphological variations. Based on these variations, two statistically distinct sacral statistical shape model subtypes were constructed according to screw corridor morphology. The characteristics and shared features of S1 corridors were comparatively analyzed between subtypes. To enhance mechanical stability, grayscale values of cortical bone regions in the first sacral vertebra were measured to assess local bone density around different screw corridors. A distinct high-density cortical bone corridor was identified in the S1 vertebral body, from which the principal stress transmission direction was inferred. Screw placement along this corridor significantly improved biomechanical performance, reducing maximum screw and sacral stresses by 7.28% and 57.75%, respectively, decreasing screw shear force by 37.52%, and improving stress distribution and interfacial micromotion. This study provides critical theoretical evidence for standardized sacral screw fixation corridors.

title: Multi-phase kinetic precipitation model for the aging process design of Al-Mg-Si alloys
abstract: A new kinetic precipitation model capable of predicting the microstructural features in Al-Mg-Si alloys has been developed based on the Kampmann-Wagner Numerical (KWN) methodology coupled with an automated phase transformation algorithm between precipitate phases. The new algorithm automatically calculates gradual phase evolution of forward transformation and degeneration between metastable and stable phases like GP zone, β ″ , β ′ and β in Al-Mg-Si alloy, based on the Gibbs energy and interface energy of precipitates and diffusions of solute elements. Experimental precipitate evolution data during the aging process of a wide range of Al-Mg-Si alloys are successfully predicted by the present kinetic model with one set of thermodynamic and physical property data. Based on the model, precipitation maps for the aging process of Al-Mg-Si alloy are generated for new alloy design and process optimization.

title: Microstructure-driven terahertz absorption in single-layer graphene: Statistical insights from random grain-boundary networks
abstract: Polycrystalline graphene exhibits stochastic grain morphologies that strongly affect its terahertz (THz) electromagnetic absorption, yet most existing models rely on idealized or periodic assumptions that overlook the statistical nature of grain–boundary networks. Here, we develop a statistically grounded framework that quantitatively links microscopic randomness to macroscopic THz absorption. Voronoi–generated morphologies with independently tunable grain size, grain–boundary resistance, and structural regularity are combined with a frequency–dispersive surface–conductivity model. An L9(3 3 ) orthogonal design with K = 10 realizations per configuration enables systematic evaluation of multivariate effects and their variability. Absorption arises from the interplay between scattering-induced field confinement and boundary-mediated dissipation, both governed by grain–network topology. Large grains and moderate–to–high boundary resistance promote continuous dissipative pathways, whereas excessive structural perturbation disrupts connectivity and weakens absorption. Field maps confirm that strong absorption corresponds to extended high-intensity channels along grain boundaries. Scale–up validation using 3 × 3 supercells agree closely with unit–cell ensemble averages, demonstrating that the identified mechanisms persist across larger domains. This study establishes statistically validated structure–property relationships for THz absorption in polycrystalline graphene and identifies the microstructural conditions required for forming continuous dissipative pathways, providing a practical basis for microstructure–engineered absorber design and for understanding dissipation in disordered two–dimensional materials.

title: Isogeometric level-set topology optimization for the design of geometrically nonlinear auxetic metamaterials with AM experimental analysis
abstract: Auxetic metamaterials have garnered significant attention in advanced industrial manufacturing due to their superior mechanical properties, which are characterized by a counterintuitive Negative Poisson’s Ratio (NPR). However, traditional design approaches often rely on linear elasticity assumptions, which fail to accurately predict structural behavior under substantial strain. To satisfy stringent engineering requirements, it is imperative to integrate geometric nonlinearity into the topology optimization framework. In this work, we propose an isogeometric level set topology optimization method specifically tailored for designing geometrically nonlinear auxetic metamaterials. Firstly, the isogeometric level set method is introduced, which seamlessly integrates Computer-Aided Design (CAD) with Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) to ensure smooth boundary representation and numerical stability. Secondly, the geometric nonlinearity isogeometric analysis (IGA) formulation is derived. By adopting the Total Lagrangian approach, we accurately model the behavior of structures under the large deformation assumption. Thirdly, the generation theory of auxetic metamaterials based on the stretching-dominated assumption is analyzed, and a robust objective function is formulated to maximize the auxetic effect. Moreover, the corresponding topology optimization model is developed, and a comprehensive sensitivity analysis scheme is utilized to guide the structural evolution. Optimization results demonstrate robust performance under large deformation conditions, while the integration of the level set method with isogeometric analysis yields smooth and well-defined structural boundaries. Comprehensive CAE analyses are performed to evaluate the mechanical responses of the optimized configurations. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated through a combination of high-fidelity numerical simulations and experimental testing of models fabricated via Additive Manufacturing (AM), where the experimental results demonstrate strong consistency with the simulation predictions, confirming its superior performance and practical feasibility in geometric nonlinear design.

title: Mesoporous hollowed Mn-Ca hybrid nanostimulator with ICG encapsulation for precise breast tumor ablation via synergistic photothermal-chemodynamic and Ca2+ overloading
abstract: In this research, a synergistic nanotherapeutic system was developed, which employs fluorescence imaging, enhanced hyperthermia-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and Ca 2+ overloading (CO) to achieve a multi-modal therapeutic effect on breast cancer. This innovative nanotherapeutic approach was designed to specifically target and effectively eradicate breast cancer. The nanostimulator was engineered with surface folic acid (FA) conjugation, ensuring selective targeting of tumor cells, and adsorbed indocyanine green (ICG), which leverages the high surface area for efficient interaction. FA enhancement promoted tumor cell recognition and accumulation, while ICG release post-internalization facilitated near-infrared II (NIR II, (1000–1700 nm) fluorescence imaging and photothermal therapy. Notably, the presence of Mn ions within the nanostimulator enhanced the Fenton-like reaction, enabling chemodynamic therapy under NIR laser irradiation. Additionally, the hollow mesoporous MnCa (mhMnCa) nanostimulator induced artificial calcium ions overload stress in the cytoplasm. Both in vitro and in vivo experiments have confirmed the effectiveness of this MnCa based nanostimulator in breast tumor targeting, NIR II fluorescence imaging, and synergistic therapeutic efficacy. Thus, this multi-modal nano-system presented a straightforward and adaptable strategy for the diagnosis and treatment of breast tumors.

title: Cover_267
Editorial Board
Patient-specific hard contact lenses fabricated by vat photopolymerization printing and non-contact fluidization coating
abstract: Patient-specific hard contact lenses offer significant advantages for vision correction and corneal health, yet their fabrication remains constrained by limited geometric customization and surface-processing strategies. Here, we report a digital manufacturing platform for the fabrication of hard contact lenses with programmable thickness gradients and conformal surface modification. Cornea-specific lens geometries are computationally designed using MATLAB-based algorithms that translate corneal topography into spatially resolved thickness maps, with validation using both real patient-derived data and representative corneal geometries. The lenses are fabricated using DLP-based 3D printing from functional hydrophilic silicone-acrylate formulations and subsequently surface-modified via a non-contact fluidization coating technique. This coating approach enables uniform surface treatment without mechanical contact, preserving lens geometry. The resulting lenses are designed for myopia and hyperopia correction and exhibit controlled thickness variation, mechanical robustness, high oxygen permeability, and excellent cytocompatibility with human corneal epithelial cells. Confocal 3D slicing and scanning electron microscopy confirm precise thickness gradients throughout the lens cross-section. This work establishes a scalable route for a digital manufacturing platform for patient-specific design-capable hard contact lenses, integrating computational design, additive manufacturing, and non-contact surface engineering.

title: Autonomous closed-loop optimization for MAX-phase synthesis via image-based quality evaluation and sequence learning
abstract: MAX-phase synthesis is highly sensitive to composition and thermal history, making manual exploration inefficient and batch quality difficult to stabilize. In this work, a characterization-driven closed-loop framework is established by coupling a programmable logic controller (PLC)-supervised synthesis robot with image-guided quality assessment and sequence-based process planning. SEM and XRD data are used to classify synthesis outcomes into non-layered, layered-with-impurities, and layered impurity-free regimes, while batch metadata and encoded furnace profiles are integrated to recommend updated synthesis routes. The quality-assessment model yields a micro-averaged receiver operating characteristic curve area (ROC–AUC) of 0.941 on the held-out test set, and the sequence-based planner achieves an out-of-fold ROC–AUC of 0.953 with an average precision of 0.994. Representative Rietveld refinements and EDS mapping further strengthen the experimental interpretation by providing diffraction-based phase analysis and microscale compositional support. Under identical hardware constraints, the closed-loop workflow delivers roughly three times more clean batches within eight experimental cycles and increases the weekly screening rate from 8 to 24 candidate recipes. These results demonstrate an effective route toward autonomous optimization of MAX-phase synthesis under experimentally grounded feedback.

title: Binder Jetting – Influence of shell printing on sintering densification and microstructure of 17-4 PH stainless steel
abstract: The shell printing strategy was utilized for Binder Jetting of 17-4 PH stainless steel to investigate the impact of the binder on green density, sintering densification, phase transformations and microstructure gradients. Green parts with 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% shell volume were printed and sintered in a dilatometer under Ar and H 2 atmospheres. The green density increased from 4.46 g/cm 3 for 25% shell volume to 4.82 g/cm 3 for 100% shell volume due to binder-induced particle rearrangement. The sintering densification in H 2 was primarily influenced by the powder packing, as higher shrinkages compensated for lower green densities, resulting in comparable sintered densities between 99.7% and 99.9%. Debinding in H 2 ensured low sintered carbon levels, resulting in high δ-ferrite fractions during sintering and martensite formation during cooling. In contrast, sintering in Ar was mainly impacted by carbon introduced by the binder since debinding efficiency was low. The increasing shell volume reduced the δ-ferrite fractions during sintering due to carbon pickup, which decreased the sintered densities from 99.3% for 25% shell volume to 93.4% for 100% shell volume. The binder-free core exhibited less porosity, higher microhardness and higher δ-ferrite fractions than the binder-affected shell, as carbon pickup stabilizes austenite during sintering and cooling.

title: Phase-specific deformation mechanisms in a Ti2AlNb-based alloy revealed by stepwise microstructural decoupling
abstract: A microstructure-dependent deformation framework was established for a Ti-22Al-24Nb-0.5Mo alloy by systematically decoupling the roles of the α 2 phase, primary O (O pri ) phase, and secondary O (O sec ) precipitates through a stepwise heat-treatment strategy. This phase-by-phase microstructural design enables a direct elucidation of their individual and synergistic contributions to tensile deformation. Three representative microstructures, namely B2+α 2 , B2+α 2 +O pri , and B2+α 2 +O pri +O sec , were constructed and investigated by room-temperature load-unload tensile testing combined with SEM, EBSD, and TEM characterizations. The results show that the slip behavior of the B2 matrix evolves from single slip to duplex slip and finally to cross-slip with increasing strain. In the B2+α 2 microstructure, intragranular α 2 shows a limited blocking effect on slip-trace continuity, whereas grain-boundary α 2 acts as the dominant obstacle to long-range slip propagation. In the B2+α 2 +O pri microstructure, the O pri phase promotes orientation-dependent slip transfer and slip deflection, thereby enhancing deformation compatibility and strain-hardening. Further introduction of fine acicular O sec precipitates effectively suppresses continuous slip propagation, leading to a marked increase in tensile strength and work-hardening capacity. These findings clarify the distinct deformation roles of the constituent phases over different strain regimes and provide mechanistic guidance for phase engineering and microstructural design of Ti 2 AlNb-based alloys.

title: Interpretable transfer learning accelerates the design of high-temperature-resistant copper alloys with limited data
abstract: Copper alloys are critical for high-temperature applications, including rocket combustion chamber linings and nuclear reactor deflectors, yet traditional smelt-cast alloys struggle under extreme thermal conditions. Recent advances in big data and machine learning have enabled the efficient design of high-performance copper alloys. Here, we propose a novel interpretable transfer learning model–the electrical conductivity-hardness artificial neural network (ECH–ANN)–that integrates feature and model transfer to accurately predict properties of dispersion-strengthened copper alloys via powder metallurgy. We further established a feature screening pipeline comprising correlation screening, recursive elimination, recursive addition, and exhaustive screening. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we quantified the importance and impact of key features on performance. Guided by these insights, a high-performance Cu-5.0 vol% Cr 2 O 3 composite was designed and fabricated through in-situ internal oxidation, achieving a strength of 570 MPa, electrical conductivity of 73.6 % IACS, and a softening temperature of 1000 °C, approaching copper’s melting point. This work provides a data-efficient framework for designing advanced materials, while elucidating the relationships between component characteristics and material properties.

title: Biomimetic Self-Assembled Chlorin e6/Capsaicin nanoparticles for Hypoxia-Alleviated photodynamic therapy of Triple-Negative breast cancer
abstract: The hypoxic tumor microenvironment and its oxidative stress defense mechanisms are core bottlenecks restricting the therapeutic efficacy of photodynamic therapy (PDT) for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Therefore, simultaneously ameliorating tumor hypoxia and targeted inhibition of oxidative stress defense pathways has emerged as a critical strategy to enhance the anti-tumor potency of PDT. Based on the unique roles of capsaicin (Cap) in regulating the above two aspects, this study constructed a biomimetic-targeted enhanced photodynamic nanodelivery system (M1@Ce6/Cap NPs). Cellular experimental results demonstrated that the system could significantly increase intracellular oxygen concentration via capsaicin release and downregulate the expression of Nrf2, a key transcription factor in the oxidative stress defense pathway, thereby synergistically enhancing the PDT effect mediated by the photosensitizer Ce6. Further experiments using TNBC tumor-bearing mouse models validated this synergistic enhancement. These findings provide a novel theoretical basis and technical support for integrating hypoxia alleviation, oxidative stress amplification, and biomimetic targeting strategies to optimize PDT efficacy against TNBC.

title: Advancing breakthrough design of superior strength-ductility synergy of lead-free solder alloys via interpretable machine learning and iterative optimization
abstract: The miniaturization, high-density integration, and multifunctionalization of electronic devices impose increasingly stringent performance requirements on solder alloys employed in microelectronic packaging. In this study, an interpretable machine-learning-based design strategy is developed by integrating element importance ranking, a small experimental dataset, and iterative optimization, with the objective of simultaneously enhancing the strength and ductility of SnAgCu (SAC)-based solder alloys. After four iterative optimization cycles, a novel Sn-Ag-Cu-Zr-Al-Ti (SACZAT) solder alloy is successfully designed, exhibiting an ultimate tensile strength of 48.26 ± 1.64 MPa and an elongation of 83.42 ± 8.94%, corresponding to improvements of 9.98% in strength and 42.02% in ductility, respectively, relative to the conventional Sn3Ag0.5Cu alloy. Microstructure analyses combined with first‑principles calculations reveal that the exceptional ductility of the SACZAT alloy originates from accelerated dynamic recrystallization (DRX) of β-Sn during deformation and β-Sn grain refinement. Meanwhile, the enhanced strength is attributed to the precipitation strengthening from newly formed intermetallic compounds and grain-refinement strengthening of the β-Sn. This study provides a machine learning framework for designing high-performance lead-free solder alloys with tunable mechanical properties by adjusting feature weights, thereby offering materials support for the development of high-reliability packaging devices.

title: Comparative study of flax, glass, and carbon textile reinforced concrete: experimental and machine learning evaluation of tensile and flexural behaviour
abstract: Direct comparative studies on the mechanical performance of flax textile-reinforced concrete and conventional textile systems under consistent experimental conditions remain limited. This study investigates the tensile and flexural behaviour of concrete reinforced with flax, carbon, and alkali-resistant (AR) glass textiles. Experimental testing was combined with machine learning approaches, including artificial neural networks (ANN) and random forests (RF), to assess the relative importance of key input parameters. Uniaxial tensile tests showed that mesh size had no significant effect on tensile properties when reinforcement ratios were constant. Flax- and AR-glass reinforced concretes exhibited comparable tensile strengths. ANN analysis further indicated that reinforcement arrangement, particularly the number of layers and reinforcement ratio, had a greater influence on tensile strength than mesh size or the intrinsic tensile properties of the reinforcement. Four-point bending tests highlighted the dominant role of textile type in flexural performance, with flax textile-reinforced concrete exhibiting significantly lower flexural strength and toughness than carbon- and AR-glass systems. Consistent with experimental observations, RF modelling identified reinforcement tensile strength as the most influential parameter governing flexural strength. Overall, flax textile reinforced concrete shows promise for tensile applications but remains less suitable for flexural structural use within the scope of this study.

title: Neural inverse design of self shaping composites
abstract: Self-shaping fiber-reinforced polymer ( FRP ) sheets offer a moldless method for generating complex 3D geometries by leveraging internal stresses. This innovative process enables sustainable fabrication of curved forms but presents a challenging inverse design problem: determining the fiber orientations that will produce a desired geometry. A data-driven approach is introduced for the inverse design of self-shaping FRP sheets, leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks ( CNNs ) trained on a large synthetic dataset generated from physically informed simulations. Two strategies are evaluated: (i) a direct prediction model that predicts fiber layouts from target surfaces, and (ii) an optimization method based on a trained surrogate model. The models are validated against physical prototypes and integrated into the Grasshopper design environment, facilitating accessible use within design workflows. It is demonstrated that the direct prediction model offers rapid, accurate predictions within the training distribution, while the optimization method generalizes better and is able to approximate freeform geometries. This work highlights the potential of machine learning to streamline moldless fabrication processes for complex architectural components.

title: Interfacial engineering of polyamide 1012 composites with balanced toughness and strength using ethylene-propylene-diene monomer ionomer
abstract: This study proposes a multi-bridge coordination strategy to construct layered sacrificial bonds in carboxylated ethylene-propylene diene monomer (EPDM) ionic polymers through lanthanum ions (La 3+ ), aiming to address the balance between toughness and strength in polyamide/elastomer blends. Unlike low-coordination polymers, La 3+ ionomer can form more coordination bonds (coordination number 8–10, while Lithium ion (Li + ) is only 2–3 and Zinc ion (Zn 2+ ) is 4). In addition to forming micro-crosslinked elastomers through regulated coordination reactions, La 3+ ionomer may provide additional available coordination sites that promote possible interfacial interactions with amide groups in polyamide 1012 (PA1012), thereby contributing to elastomer reinforcement and enhanced interfacial adhesion between the elastomer and polyamide matrix. The PA1012/La 3+ -ionomer blends exhibit breakthrough mechanical synergy: an impact strength of 100.9 kJ/m 2 (3.8 × higher than MAH-compatibilized PA1012) and a tensile strength of 55.4 MPa (1.3 × enhancement), while maintaining melt processability. Further confirmation of the existence of multiple cross-linked network structures was achieved through dynamic rheological performance and toughening reinforcement mechanism analysis. A design method is proposed for synergistic toughening and reinforcing modifiers that enhance the mechanical properties of polyamide composites via molecular-level coordination control.

title: Grain-scale origins of PLC banding in Al-9Mg sheet revealed by in-situ EBSD and DIC
abstract: High-Mg containing aluminum alloy sheet (Al-9Mg) was produced by horizontal twin-roll casting (TRC), yielding a ~6 m strip with uniform thickness and a centerline segregation-free microstructure. After homogenization, 75% cold rolling, and full annealing, the sheet exhibited a fully recrystallized grain structure (~40 μm) and an excellent strength–ductility balance (YS ≈ 162 MPa, UTS ≈ 343 MPa, elongation ≈ 25%). Serrated flow was investigated by correlative full-field DIC and in-situ tensile EBSD. PLC activity initiated at ε ≈ 0.13 and manifested as propagating B-type stretcher-strain marks inclined ~55–60° to the rolling direction. In-situ EBSD revealed that macroscopic PLC bands originate from intragranular shear bands (~45° traces) that preferentially developed in grains oriented between ⟨001⟩ and ⟨101⟩, where {111}⟨110⟩ slip showed high Schmid factor, low Taylor factor, and low initial KAM/GND.
