Progressive straining produced strong substructure refinement: the LAGB boundary-length density (2–15°) increased from 3.34 to 153.29 mm⁻¹ and the mean KAM rose from ~0.18° to ~0.39°, while GOS classification shifted from fully recrystallized to predominantly deformed. Texture changes remained modest (PF max 4.28→4.34 m.r.d.; ODF max 15.6→17.5 m.r.d.), indicating that PLC deformation is governed primarily by orientation-dependent slip localization and was accommodated by rapid substructure refinement.

title: Advancements and applications of magnetic nanoparticles in facilitating the repair and regeneration of the nervous system
abstract: Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), primarily superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), play a significant role in modern biomedicine, including drug delivery, magnetothermal therapy, and magnetic resonance imaging. MNPs are appropriate for repairing nerve injuries because of these uses. The specific mechanisms of nerve injury are first explained in this review from the viewpoints of peripheral nerve injuries, such as excitotoxicity, inflammatory reactions, oxidative stress, cell death, and glial scar formation, as well as central nervous system injuries, such as brain and spinal cord injuries. Second, the present state of MNP research is included in this review, along with surface modification, synthesis techniques, and basic biomedical applications. Lastly, this review describes the numerous ways that MNPs are utilized to repair nerve injuries and presents the unique mechanisms and applications of MNPs in this regard. The multimodal application tactics of SPIONs in nerve injury repair, including magnetic targeted administration, magnetic stimulation, and integrated diagnostic and treatment, are all methodically reviewed in this work. It offers new insights for the future use of MNPs in nerve injury repair and, for the first time, suggests a future development path from the standpoint of a “physical-chemical-biological” synergistic mechanism, building intelligent responsive MNPs systems to overcome present bottlenecks in nerve repair

title: Low-stress-splitting process for connecting rods with prefabricated notches
abstract: This paper presents a novel low-stress splitting process for connecting rods. Furthermore, a theoretical formula for calculating the critical load of the splitting process is derived. For a 500 mm cantilever, the maximum critical load required for the JD52 connecting rod is only 0.257 times that required for conventional fracture splitting. The analytical and experimental results reveal that crack evolution during this process is divided into three distinct stages: crack initiation, crack propagation, and instantaneous fracture. The material failure progresses through four successive stages:shear stress-dominated ductile failure, mixed shear-tensile stress-dominated ductile failure, tensile stress-dominated ductile–brittle failure, and tensile stress-dominated brittle failure. The cross-sectional horizontal error and maximum unevenness are ≤ 3 mm , both of which satisfy industrial production requirements. Additionally, a loading strategy is proposed to reduce the force required during the instantaneous fracture stage. This optimized control strategy, informed by the crack evolution characteristics, reduces the cross-sectional horizontal error to 0.27 mm and maximum unevenness to 736.5 μ m , while increasing the total processing time by less than 1%. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in significantly improving connecting rod quality with minimal impact on processing efficiency.

title: A one-way mechanics–electromagnetics coupled finite element approach for stress-driven magnetic response in architected Fe–Co magnetostrictive structures
abstract: In recent years, the rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has increased the demand for maintenance-free power sources for sensors. Magnetostrictive energy harvesting is a promising candidate due to its durability. However, its low power output remains a major challenge for practical use. Although architectural optimization has been shown to enhance performance, the physical mechanisms by which complex structures influence energy conversion efficiency are still not fully understood. In this study, we propose a one-way stress-driven mechanics–electromagnetics coupled approach for architected magnetostrictive materials. The approach captures architecture-dependent magnetic flux redistribution arising from stress-dependent magnetic property changes. Using this approach, three Fe–Co configurations, namely Bulk, Cubic lattice, and Cubic-auxetic lattice, were systematically investigated. The numerical results suggest that the Cubic-auxetic structure shows the largest quasi-static linked-flux-change response among the three configurations. By transferring stress distributions from structural analysis to electromagnetic simulations, the proposed approach quantified inverse-magnetostrictive, stress-driven flux redistribution and showed that, unlike the Bulk, the Cubic and Cubic-auxetic lattices produce local stress concentration and altered internal magnetic field distributions, leading to larger magnetic flux changes. Experiments were used only to confirm ranking-level and trend-level consistency with the numerical analysis. The present approach provides a practical basis for pre-fabrication design and architecture screening of magnetostrictive energy harvesters.

title: Tunable quantum transport and thermodynamic response in bilayer β-graphyne: interplay of stacking symmetry and external fields
abstract: A comprehensive theoretical investigation of the electronic, thermodynamic, and thermoelectric properties of bilayer β-graphyne is presented within a tight-binding framework combined with Green’s function formalism and Kubo transport theory. The effects of interlayer stacking geometry, external bias voltage, and perpendicular magnetic field are systematically examined for four representative bilayer configurations, namely AA, AB1, AB2, and AB3. The results reveal that the low-energy electronic spectrum is highly sensitive to the stacking arrangement, leading to pronounced differences in the electronic and thermoelectric responses. The calculated DOS reveals a strong stacking dependence, where AA configuration remains metallic, while the AB stackings exhibit a small gap near the Fermi level. The application of bias voltage redistributes the low-energy DOS around the Fermi level, whereas the perpendicular magnetic field modulates the VHSs through Zeeman splitting. These field-induced electronic modifications directly influence thermodynamic and transport behavior. In particular, the electronic specific heat and electrical conductivity display strong field‑dependent responses with increasing temperature. Furthermore, the Seebeck coefficient and Lorenz number exhibit pronounced enhancements under strong bias voltage, accompanied by noticeable deviations from the Wiedemann-Franz law. These results demonstrate that stacking‑dependent interlayer coupling provides an efficient mechanism for tuning the electronic and thermoelectric properties of bilayer β‑graphyne.

title: Study on multi-stage kinetics and main dissipation interval of magnetization reversal of nanocrystalline alloys under high-frequency excitation
abstract: To quantify the time-domain concentration of hysteretic dissipation in FINEMET-type nanocrystalline alloys, a three-dimensional amorphous/nanocrystalline micromagnetic model is developed under prescribed sinusoidal magnetic-field excitation. The model is validated against measured static magnetic properties and dynamic hysteresis-loop areas in the 1–20 kHz range. The magnetization reversal half-cycle is segmented into five stages for time-domain analysis: initial stability, energy pre-accumulation and magnetization relaxation, domain nucleation and early expansion, domain-wall-dominated rapid reversal, and saturation approaching with structural adjustment. These stages correspond to established micromagnetic processes and are used to correlate magnetization, magnetization rate, domain evolution, energy terms, and damping-related dissipation. A q -dependent main dissipation interval ( q -MDI) is introduced as the shortest time interval in which a prescribed fraction q of the half-cycle dissipated energy is accumulated. The representative 60%-MDI and threshold-sensitivity results indicate that the most concentrated dissipation occurs mainly near the transition from domain nucleation to rapid domain-wall propagation. Within the present equivalent model, increasing field amplitude produces a model-dependent transition near 28 mT, while increasing frequency shifts the 60%-MDI toward earlier stages of the half-cycle and gradually stabilizes its location. These results provide guidance for material-level micromagnetic analysis and microstructure-informed design of nanocrystalline soft magnetic alloys.

title: Control of nitrogen content in SPS-consolidated Nb-matrix composites via pressure-assisted mechanical alloying
abstract: Niobium-matrix composites reinforced with nitrides exhibiting superior mechanical properties have been developed. Nb powder was mechanically activated by high-energy ball milling under 3 bar N 2 . Longer milling times (2–40 h) increased nitrogen uptake and enabled the control of a Nb–nitride amount after spark plasma sintering (1500 °C, 10 min). The microstructure comprises a niobium matrix with β -Nb 4.62 N 2.14 , which gradually transforms into γ –Nb 4 N 3 as milling time increases. Moreover, as the β -phase content rises from 3 vol% to 26 vol%, precipitates evolve from thin platelets along grain boundaries to spheroidal particles. Among the tested conditions, the composite milled for 2 h showed the best balance of strength and ductility, achieving a plastic strain of 17.6%, a yield strength of 1294 MPa, and a compressive strength of 2170 MPa. Prolonged milling (above 5 h) maintains a high compressive strength (2185 MPa) but reduces plasticity, consistent with the higher fraction of brittle nitride phases. Moreover, composites milled for 2–5 h and then SPS-ed revealed superior performance at 800 °C, resulting from an optimized two-phase microstructure, in which a continuous and ductile α -Nb matrix cooperates with a moderate fraction of hard β -Nb 4.62 N 2.14 nitride reinforcement.

title: Fe impurity control in secondary aluminum alloys: a critical review of purification and upcycling
abstract: Secondary aluminum alloys (SAAs) are vital for lowering the aluminum industry’s energy use and carbon emissions, but their high-value recycling is limited by impurity buildup. Iron is especially harmful because of its very low solubility in aluminum and its strong tendency to form brittle Fe-rich intermetallics during solidification. These phases, often appearing as plate-like or Chinese-script structures, degrade castability, corrosion resistance, and mechanical properties. This review summarizes the sources of Fe contamination in scrap and remelting, and examines the phases, morphologies, and damage mechanisms of Fe-rich intermetallics in major aluminum alloy systems. It also explains why conventional refining methods such as oxidation and volatilization are generally ineffective for Fe removal. Key purification and phase-control strategies, including segregation, selective liquation, vacuum distillation, and electro-refining, are critically evaluated in terms of mechanism, efficiency, limitations, and industrial potential. In addition, emerging computational approaches such as CALPHAD, numerical simulation, and machine learning are discussed for predicting impurity behavior and optimizing processing. Overall, effective upgrading of complex SAAs will require integrated impurity control, phase regulation, alloy design, and data-driven optimization.

title: Shear transformation zone mechanics-based machine learning surrogates for designing ductile dual-phase metallic glasses
abstract: Metallic glasses (MGs) exhibit exceptionally high strength but suffer from limited ductility due to strain localization and shear banding. Designing dual-phase amorphous nanostructures offers a promising route to overcome this limitation; however, rational design of their constitutive response remains challenging due to complex structure–property relationships. Here, we develop a shear transformation zone (STZ) mechanics-based, data-driven framework for the design of ductile dual-phase MGs by integrating mesoscale STZ dynamics simulations with artificial neural networks (ANNs) and genetic algorithms (GAs). STZ dynamics simulations are performed on microstructures with various inclusion moduli, sizes, volume fractions, and nanoscale modulus heterogeneity to quantify their effects on stress–strain behavior and strain localization. An ANN surrogate model accurately predicts stress–strain responses and key mechanical properties, with mean absolute percentage errors of 2.95 % for yield stress, 1.96 % for flow stress, and 8.31 % for stress drop, enabling rapid evaluation across the design space. Coupling the ANN model with GA identifies microstructural configurations that minimize stress drop and enhance ductility. By integrating STZ-based deformation modeling, surrogate machine learning, and optimization, this framework provides an efficient route to the microstructural design of dual-phase MGs and offers a general strategy for accelerating the development of heterogeneous amorphous materials.

title: Microstructure, defects, and superconductivity of high-power impulse magnetron sputtered NbTiN thin films
abstract: Superconducting NbTiN thin films, one of the promising candidates for quantum and superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) cavity applications, were deposited using high-power impulse magnetron sputtering (HiPIMS), a high-quality thin film deposition technique. The effects of deposition pressure, duty cycle, substrate temperature, and substrate bias on microstructure, vacancy-type defects, and superconducting properties were systematically studied. Using positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy (PALS) from the radiation source ELBE combined with Doppler broadening spectroscopy (DBS), together with XRD, SEM, and AFM, a direct correlation between defect landscape and the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) was experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The results indicate that higher Tc values are typically associated with films exhibiting lower defect concentration, denser microstructures, and a preferred (200) orientation of NbTiN. We also found cases where Tc improved even in the presence of higher defect concentrations, as long as the films exhibited dense microstructure and well-connected grains. This highlights the complex interplay between defects, microstructure, and superconducting properties. Optimal deposition conditions yielded the highest Tc of ~ 15.49 K in this work. These findings suggest that minimising open volumes in the material, combined with microstructural refinement through coordinated parameter optimisation, is a key to optimising the superconducting properties of NbTiN films.

title: Achieving strength-corrosion synergy in a CoCrNi-based medium-entropy alloy via an electrochemically compatible hierarchical heterostructure
abstract: Achieving high strength without sacrificing corrosion resistance remains challenging, as strengthening-induced microstructural heterogeneity often triggers local electrochemical mismatch and destabilizes passivation. Here, we design a CoCrNiAl 3 Ti 3 Cu 6 Nb 0.8 medium-entropy alloy with an electrochemically compatible hierarchical heterostructure comprising multiscale coherent L1 2 precipitates, stacking faults (SFs), and long-period stacking ordered (LPSO) structures. The optimally processed alloy delivers a yield strength of 1108.4 MPa, ultimate tensile strength of 1446.6 MPa, and elongation of 23.8%, alongside the lowest passive current density, highest pitting potential, and largest low-frequency impedance among all aged states. Local surface potential mapping reveals that L1 2 precipitates and LPSO structures are only ∼ 10 mV nobler than the matrix, while SF-containing regions are only slightly less noble, indicating weak micro-galvanic coupling. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and cross-sectional TEM further reveal a compact ∼ 6 nm passive film with a Cr-rich inner barrier layer. The superior combination of properties arises from a hierarchical heterostructure that simultaneously delivers effective strengthening and strain hardening while preserving electrochemical compatibility and promoting stable passivation. This work establishes a practical microstructure design principle for overcoming the strength–corrosion trade-off in high-strength medium-entropy alloys.

title: Aged Bi-supersaturated Sn–5Bi–3In alloy for strengthening, corrosion resistance, and corrosion protection for FeCoNiMnCu substrate
abstract: Low-melting Sn–Bi alloys are attractive for metallic joining but suffer from Bi precipitation–induced micro-galvanic corrosion. This study investigates a Sn–5Bi–3In alloy (SBI53) to clarify the role of minor In addition in controlling microstructural evolution, mechanical properties, corrosion behavior, and soldering performance, using Sn–5Bi (SB5) as a reference. After aging at 150 °C, SB5 develops a fine Bi-dispersion microstructure, whereas SBI53 transforms into a stable Bi-supersaturated single-phase β-Sn solid solution, as confirmed by EBSD. This structure remains stable after long-term storage (5000 h), resulting in enhanced hardness (∼28 HV). Aged SBI53 shows localized grain-boundary corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, unlike the widespread Sn/Bi micro-galvanic corrosion in aged SB5, owing to suppressed Bi-rich precipitation and reduced Sn activity. XPS analysis confirms corrosion products consistent with the proposed mechanism. SBI53 also demonstrates excellent wettability and forms robust joints with FeCoNiMnCu (FCNMC), achieving shear strengths of ∼31 MPa. Furthermore, SBI53 acts as a sacrificial anode, effectively protecting FCNMC from corrosion. These results highlight SBI53 as a promising low-temperature solder and corrosion-protection material for HEA systems.

title: Al/Cr compositional effects on nanomechanical creep behavior in lightweight refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
abstract: Improving the surface mechanical performance of titanium alloy components without sacrificing lightweight design is a key requirement for protective coating development. Here, laser-cladded MoNbTiV-based lightweight refractory high-entropy alloy coatings on TC4 substrates were studied to clarify how Al/Cr alloying regulates phase constitution, interfacial structure, local nanomechanical response, and indentation creep behavior. TEM observations show that AlMoNbTiV forms a single BCC solid solution, whereas AlCrMoNbTiV develops a BCC + C15 Laves dual-phase microstructure with dense misfit dislocations near the phase interfaces. Nanoindentation mapping demonstrates that Al/Cr alloying increases nanohardness from 7.69 to 8.94 GPa and elastic modulus from 146.51 to 179.90 GPa, Among the investigated coatings, AlCrMoNbTiV exhibits the highest hardness–modulus combination, representing the most favorable local mechanical response. The coatings also display clear strain-rate-dependent indentation behavior; possible depth-dependent hardness effects are discussed cautiously because the tests were not designed as a dedicated quantitative indentation-size-effect study. The total strain recovery ratio decreases with Al addition but increases with Cr addition. Indentation creep analysis gives effective activation volumes comparable to those reported for BCC high-entropy alloys, suggesting thermally activated dislocation-mediated deformation. These results provide a composition–microstructure–property basis for designing lightweight protective coatings on titanium alloys.

title: Experimental investigation and multi-response optimization of electrical discharge machining parameters for EN24 steel using response surface methodology
abstract: Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) is a nonconventional machining process used for machining difficult-to-cut materials and can produce complex geometries. However, maintaining a balance between productivity, surface integrity, and dimensional accuracy has always been an issue in high-precision manufacturing. This research aims to evaluate the impact of three parameters, which include Pulse-ON Time (T ON :100–200 µs), Pulse-OFF Time (T OFF :40–60 µs), and Peak Current (I P :10-20A), on six responses, which include maximizing the Material Removal Rate (MRR), minimizing Electrode Wear Rate (EWR), Dimensional Deviation (DD), Cylindricity (Cyl), Taper Angle (TA), and Surface Roughness (Ra). Experiments were carried out using Response Surface Methodology on EN24 steel using copper electrodes. This study innovates in simultaneously optimizing metrology-related responses in the context of productivity and surface integrity. The experimental results revealed that discharge energy significantly influences machining efficiency, surface integrity, and dimensional precision. Higher T ON and I P improved MRR, whereas lower discharge energy conditions enhanced surface finish and geometrical accuracy. The optimal parameters are: T ON = 171.731 µs, T OFF = 60 µs, and I P = 16.8101 A. Apart from being technically innovative, this work supports SDGs, which include SDG 9 in relation to precision manufacturing and SDG 12 regarding minimized waste of materials and energy.

title: Magnetic hyperthermia properties of biogenic cockle shell waste-derived hydroxyapatite/magnetite nanocomposite synthesized using green approach
abstract: Magnetic hyperthermia therapy was developed as a more selective and localized-targeting approach for cancer therapy, utilizing magnetic nanoparticles internalized into cancer cells and heated through alternating magnetic-field exposure. Efficient heat generation combined with biocompatibility remains a major challenge in magnetic hyperthermia applications. In this study, Fe 3 O 4 /hydroxyapatite (HAp) nanocomposites were synthesized through a green approach using Moringa oleifera extract, with HAp derived from Cockle shell waste. The influence of HAp mass fractions (10%, 20%, and 30%) on structural, magnetic, and thermal properties was systematically investigated. X-ray diffraction and High-resolution transmission electron microscopy analysis confirmed the formation of two-phase nanocomposites with a crystallite size of 13.4–14.8 nm and a particle size of 6–14 nm, supporting superparamagnetic behavior. The nanocomposites exhibit moderate colloidal stability, with zeta potentials of − 21 to −28 mV. Magnetic characterization revealed a decrease in saturation magnetization with an increase in HAp content, indicating a magnetic dilution effect. The specific absorption rate values range from 0.3 to 2.56 W/g, with the highest performance demonstrated by the Fe 3 O 4 /HAp10% sample in ethylene glycol at a frequency of 20 kHz. These results show that the efficiency of heat generation is governed by the balance between magnetic response and colloidal stability.

title: Substrate geometry-controlled microstructure-stress-property relationships in nanocrystalline thin films
abstract: The functional properties of nanocrystalline thin films are governed by cross-sectional gradients in microstructure and residual stress. However, despite decades of intensive research, thin-film science has focused predominantly on planar substrates, leaving the influence of substrate geometry on films’ process-microstructure-stress-property relationships largely underexplored. Here, we demonstrate that thin-film growth on sharp cutting edges produces microstructural states and micromechanical responses that differ fundamentally from those formed on planar substrates. A nanocrystalline Al 0.6 Ti 0.4 N film was deposited on WC–Co inserts by DC magnetron sputtering and characterized using cross-sectional X-ray nanodiffraction combined with analytical scanning and transmission electron microscopy. Hardness, Young’s modulus, and fracture behavior were evaluated by nanoindentation and in situ microcantilever bending. Measurements reveal pronounced grain refinement at the cutting edge, accompanied by compressive residual stresses that are up to 500 MPa higher than those observed in the planar regions. Electron microscopy further identifies a previously unreported bimodal microstructure localized to the edge region, arising from superimposed self-shadowing effects. This manifests as a periodic grain size modulation with sharply demarcated coarse- and fine-grained regions and associated residual stress oscillations. Microcantilever bending tests performed directly at the cutting edge show that the fracture response is governed by the dominant grain morphology, producing distinctive fracture surface characteristics and load–deflection behavior. These results establish cutting edges as microscale platforms in which substrate geometry fundamentally governs thin-film microstructural evolution and the resulting mechanical properties. They reveal substrate curvature as a controllable design parameter for engineering spatially resolved microstructure-stress states, providing a framework for tailoring nanocrystalline films in performance-critical, non-planar regions.

title: Photothermal drug delivery via SPIO@C@PDA nanocomposites for targeted colorectal cancer treatment
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC), a common and lethal malignancy, has been a major global health challenge, as current clinical treatments are constrained by poor precision, severe side effects, and the complex tumor microenvironment. It is noteworthy that nanotechnology has brought about significant breakthroughs in traditional medicine, enabling the development of intelligent nanoscale systems tailored to specific requirements to overcome the drawbacks of clinical CRC treatments. Herein, a versatile nanotherapeutic agent is developed via integrating superparamagnetic iron oxide (SPIO) nanoparticles (NPs), carbon (C) intermediate layer, and outermost polydopamine (PDA) layer for CRC therapy. The as-designed SPIO@C@PDA NPs effectively serve as a photothermal therapy (PTT) agent for thermal ablation and a carrier for cisplatin delivery. The combination of PTT and chemotherapy holds promise in overcoming the limitations of monotherapy, which can avoid the administration of high-dose cisplatin, mitigate side effects, and achieve synergistic antitumor effectiveness. Hence, this innovative platform leverages the combination of functional materials to eradicate CRC and validate the feasibility of synergistic chemo-photothermal therapy.

title: Quantitative unraveling of spinodal decomposition in Cu-15Ni-8Sn alloys via small-angle neutron scattering: Kinetics and strengthening mechanisms
abstract: Cu-Ni-Sn alloys are widely used in electrical and other fields owing to their excellent mechanical properties. Spinodal decomposition (SD) plays a critical role in strengthening these alloys. However, its early-stage kinetics and quantitative evolution remain insufficiently characterized by conventional techniques. Here, small-angle neutron scattering (SANS), combined with transmission electron microscopy, is used to resolve the early-stage SD quantitatively and statistically in a Cu-15Ni-8Sn alloy aged at 400 °C. The results show that as aging time extends from 0.5 h to 8 h, the SD wavelength ( λ S D ) increases from 52.1 to 102.9 Å and its amplitude ( A SD ) from 16.6 to 22.3 at.%, following a diffusion-controlled coarsening law λ SD ∝ t 0.25 . Concurrently, L1 2 /D0 22 ordered phases precipitate within NiSn-rich regions. Through quantitative strengthening analysis, it is revealed for the first time that ordered phase strengthening (∼449 MPa) is the dominant mechanism, contributing approximately twice the effect of SD strengthening (∼235 MPa). This work not only demonstrates the unique capability of SANS in deciphering nanoscale phase separation but also establishes a quantitative microstructure-property relationship for designing high-performance Cu-Ni-Sn alloys.

title: Predicting ice adhesion of fluid-containing elastomers from surface tension/energy and crosslink density
abstract: The incorporation of silicone fluids in elastomeric coatings is often presented as a simple way to improve ice-release properties. However, understanding which fluid effectively improves the ice-release properties, and what quantity is needed, still remains challenging. To solve this challenge, a model has been proposed by Golovin and Tuteja to predict the ice-release properties of fluid-containing elastomers. Yet, this method relies on knowledge of the maximum swelling capability of the elastomer, which requires tedious experiments. In this work, we propose an original protocol to predict the swelling capability from the primary physical characteristics of the fluids and elastomers. In short, we characterize the surface tension/energy of the fluid and elastomer to obtain their solubility parameters ( δ ). These are then exploited, along with the crosslink density and fluid molecular weight, to predict the swelling capability of the elastomer from a mixing theory proposed by Harper and Liu, which allows the determination of swelling capability of the elastomer without tedious swelling measurements. Finally, this predicted swelling capability is then employed to predict the ice adhesion of the fluid-containing coating. The relevance of every step (from swelling to adhesion prediction) was verified by observations made with carefully controlled experimental coatings.

title: Powder mode in laser direct energy deposition repair of AlSi7Mg revealed by in-situ X-ray imaging
abstract: Directed energy deposition (DED) technology holds great potential for metal repair and remanufacturing. However, in powder-based laser directed energy deposition (L-DED), the complex interactions between the laser, powder, and melt pool under coupled process parameters make it challenging to control deposition quality and porosity. Using in situ X-ray imaging, we identified three powder behaviors: (I) droplet mode, where excessive powder accumulation leads to molten pool oscillation and lack of fusion defects; (II) free incidence mode, where excessive heat input causes substrate overheating, discrete powder incident, and circular pores; and (III) short-chain mode, a transitional state. We introduced the dimensionless number Π LPS to quantify the powder mode boundary, with increasing Π LPS values indicating a shift from droplet to free incidence mode. At a medium Π LPS value (short-chain mode), optimal process and powder feed parameters yielded minimal porosity and superior repair properties, with strength and ductility comparable to those of the substrate. Moreover, the impact of irregular lack-of-fusion defects in droplet mode is paramount, whereas the influence of densely distributed circular pores in free incidence mode is secondary. This study elucidates the laser-powder-substrate interaction and its influence on defect formation and property enhancement, which provides a valuable basis for further optimization.

title: Microstructural evolution and defect formation in aluminium alloy 4043 during molten metal deposition
abstract: Molten metal deposition (MMD) offers a promising approach to metal additive manufacturing due to its relatively low and controllable cooling rates compared with laser or arc-based processes. However, most investigations related to MMD remain as simulation studies with limited microstructural and defect-based studies. In this work, the microstructural and porosity defects of MMD-fabricated aluminium alloy 4043 are systematically examined across varying process parameters. The results show that high substrate temperatures combined with higher nozzle temperatures result in reduced cooling rate, thereby increasing grain size and defect levels. Conversely, both average grain size and defect levels decrease progressively along the build direction as interlayer height increases, reflecting an enhancement in the effective cooling rate with successive layer deposition. Hardness and nanoindentation testing revealed mechanical properties comparable to those achieved through conventional manufacturing routes, highlighting the promising applicability of MMD technology. When overall optimising is considered, lowering the substrate temperature and energy input tend to increase the cooling rate; this enables fewer defects and finer grain structures in MMD specimens. The present study provides quantitative process-microstructure-defect relationships to enable promising enhancements in MMD of aluminium alloy components.

title: From defects to Performance: A Dual-Framework approach to Post-Processing optimization in additively manufactured stainless steel
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the production of stainless-steel components with unprecedented geometric complexity; however, industrial adoption remains constrained by process-induced defects, including porosity, residual stresses, microstructural heterogeneity, and poor surface integrity. Although numerous post-processing technologies have been developed, current selection approaches remain largely empirical and insufficiently linked to defect mechanisms and targeted performance outcomes. This review critically analyses 110 studies published between 2015 and 2025 and proposes a Dual-Framework Decision Architecture for the rational selection of post-processing strategies in additively manufactured stainless steels. The first framework maps technologies according to bulk integrity and surface functionality, while the second links AM defects to engineering objectives, processing routes, expected benefits, and trade-offs. The analysis demonstrates that no individual technology can optimise all performance domains. Hot Isostatic Pressing provides near-complete densification but may reduce strength through microstructural coarsening. Electropolishing and advanced electrochemical routes improve surface quality and corrosion resistance, whereas severe shot peening enhances fatigue performance through deep compressive residual stresses. The findings show that optimal performance depends on hybrid post-processing chains combining complementary technologies. By integrating defect mitigation, process selection, and performance engineering, the proposed architecture establishes post-processing as a strategic design variable for next-generation AM systems.

title: Intranasal delivery of curcumin via biomimetic microglial membrane-coated chitosan nanoparticles alleviates depressive-like behaviors in LPS models
abstract: Accumulating evidence has shown that chronic neuroinflammation underlies the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder, and anti-inflammatory strategies represent a promising therapeutic direction. Curcumin (Cur), a natural compound with antidepressant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties, has emerged as a candidate for depression treatment. However, its clinical translation is limited by poor bioavailability and inefficient delivery across the blood–brain barrier. Here, we developed a responsive biomimetic nanomedicine system for enhanced delivery of curcumin. Phenylboronic acid-modified chitosan nanoparticles were used to encapsulate Cur with high loading efficiency and stimulus-responsive release properties. These cores were further coated with microglia-derived membranes to form biomimetic nanomedicine (mCBC). mCBC demonstrated good biocompatibility and was efficiently internalized by target cells. Following intranasal administration, mCBC significantly reduced neuroinflammation and attenuated neuronal damage in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced model of depression. These neuroprotective effects were associated with the amelioration of anhedonia and depressive-like behaviors in LPS models, suggesting that mCBC treatment is a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for inflammation-related depression.

title: Ethyl oleate-based in situ forming gel for long-term peptide delivery via water-triggered lamellar phase transition
abstract: Peptide therapeutics are increasingly attractive due to their high potency and specificity, yet their clinical application is often limited by short systemic half-life, enzymatic instability, and rapid clearance. Here, we report a minimally invasive injectable in situ forming gel (ISG) composed of phospholipids dissolved in ethyl oleate (EO), replacing conventional hydrophilic organic solvents, which rapidly forms a depot upon exposure to aqueous environments. By adjusting the phospholipid-to-EO ratio, we systematically characterized the ISG’s microstructural evolution, rheological behavior, water absorption, and drug release profile, revealing a water-triggered phase transition mechanism toward a lamellar gel structure. Compared with conventional hydrophilic organic solvent-based formulations, the EO-based ISG exhibited superior biocompatibility and enhanced protection of encapsulated peptides. Sustained in vivo release of peptides with distinct physicochemical properties was maintained for over one month, and the liraglutide-loaded ISG demonstrated prolonged glucose-control efficacy in a diabetic mouse model. Collectively, this study establishes a simple, scalable ISG platform for long-term peptide delivery, offering a promising strategy to enhance peptide stability and therapeutic performance.

title: Beyond the magnetic paradigm: Unveiling the dominant role of electron injection and heterointerface polarization for CoNi@C with enhanced microwave absorption
abstract: Developing microwave absorbing materials that integrate a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) with superior angular and polarization stability is a key research direction in the field. In particular, MOF derived magnetic metal/carbon composites (MMOF-MM/C) that integrate both magnetic and electric loss mechanisms, have attracted widespread attention. To date, the role of the high content of magnetic metal in MMOF-MM/C for microwave absorption awaits systematic investigation. In this work, a microwave-assisted fast calcination strategy was proposed to synthesize well-dispersed, welded, homogenous CoNi@C-MW micro/nano hierarchical structure. Analysis of impedance matching ratios and attenuation constants reveals that the permeability of CoNi@C-MW contributes only minimally to microwave absorption in the 2.0–18.0 GHz frequency range. GA|NLLS fitting shows that CoNi metal enhances conduction and polarization losses in CoNi@C-MW, increasing polarization loss by nearly 50 % and conduction loss by up to three times. This is attributed to thicker, more graphitized carbon layers that facilitate electron injection from CoNi to carbon, and a well-dispersed, uniform particle structure that promotes heterogeneous interface polarization. Furthermore, a magnetic-dielectric-magnetic (M 1 –D–M 2 ) sandwich-structured absorber was further constructed, delivering an EAB covering 7.7–18.0 GHz at an angular stability up to 60° under both TE and TM polarizations.

title: Immune-reprogramming electrospun membrane integrating EGCG and cerium-doped mesoporous bioactive glass for infected diabetic wound remodeling
abstract: Infected diabetic wounds are refractory lesions that often progress to chronic non-healing states. Beyond bacterial colonization, repair failure is driven by a persistently dysregulated microenvironment marked by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired angiogenesis. Conventional dressings mainly control infection but rarely restore the immune and vascular imbalance underlying regenerative failure. Here, we develop an immune-programmed electrospun membrane (PA-Ce@EG) integrating epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and cerium-doped mesoporous bioactive glass (Ce-MBG) within a poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) nanofibrous matrix. PA-Ce@EG exhibits strong antibacterial activity and efficiently reduces excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). It reprograms macrophages toward a reparative M2 phenotype with suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. This immune shift enhances endothelial activation and network formation under hyperglycemic conditions, indicating coordinated immune–vascular restoration. In diabetic mice, PA-Ce@EG reduces bacterial burden, alleviates inflammation, restores neovascularization, and accelerates high-quality wound repair without detectable systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, rapid EGCG release attenuates early inflammatory signaling, whereas sustained Ce-MBG-mediated redox regulation contributes to oxidative stress rebalancing and macrophage phenotype modulation. The ECM-mimicking fibrous architecture further supports immune–vascular crosstalk and tissue remodeling. Collectively, this study establishes immune rebalancing as a central design principle and presents a time-programmed electrospun platform for integrated infection control and regenerative repair in infected diabetic wounds.

title: Redox-responsive copper-based nanoplatform enables efficient pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma therapy via icaritin-enhanced cuproptosis
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic options, largely due to its metabolic adaptability and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Cuproptosis has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy; however, its efficacy in solid tumors is constrained by intracellular redox buffering and insufficient bioavailable copper. Here, we developed a redox-responsive copper-based nanoplatform (ICMNs) by integrating Icaritin (ICA) into a copper metal–organic framework to synergistic induce cuproptosis and immunotherapy. After cell internalization, ICMNs underwent glutathione (GSH)-triggered disassembly, co-releasing Cu 2+ and ICA. Mechanistically, ICMNs elevated intracellular reactive oxygen species levels by ∼ 145-fold while depleted GSH by 56%, thereby amplifying oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, Furthermore, ICMNs triggered prominent immunogenic cell death, evidenced by a 5.4-fold increase in calreticulin exposure, enhanced HMGB1 release, and ATP secretion, which promoted dendritic cell maturation and CD8 + T-cell activation. In patient-derived organoids, ICMNs reduced organoid viability by over 85%. In PDAC KPC subcutaneous transplant tumor mouse models, ICMNs achieved an 85.6% tumor inhibition rate and significantly prolonged median survival (41.5 vs. 15 days) without obvious systemic toxicity. Collectively, our findings demonstrates that redox potentiates copper-induced tumor cell death and antitumor immunity, offering a promising nanotherapeutic strategy for PDAC treatment.

title: Nanomaterials facilitating optical therapy for thyroid cancer: research progress and prospects
abstract: Thyroid cancer is the most common malignant tumor of the endocrine system, and Papillary Thyroid Cancer (PTC) is the most common. For differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC), surgery is the most important treatment modality, which is most widely used in clinical practice, and 131 I therapy and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) suppression therapy also play an important role in the comprehensive treatment of DTC. However, for advanced disease states, particularly radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (RAIR-DTC) and Anaplastic Thyroid Cancer (ATC), which is characterized by rapid progression and extremely poor prognosis, conventional therapeutic strategies have shown limited efficacy. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop more precise and effective treatment approaches, especially for ATC. In recent years, novel therapeutic strategies based on nanomaterials have demonstrated groundbreaking potential in cancer treatment through photothermal therapy, photodynamic therapy, targeted delivery drug, and multimodal combined therapy. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the latest advances in nanomaterial-mediated optical therapy for thyroid cancer, with a particular focus on ATC, and discuss their potential in precision treatment as well as the current challenges and future perspectives for clinical translation.

title: Structure–performance linkage in thickness-tailored steel tubes: energy partitioning and predictive design under axial impact
abstract: Thin-walled steel tubes with axially tailored thickness offer significant potential for improving crash energy absorption at constant mass; however, current design strategies largely rely on numerical optimization and lack physically grounded predictive tools capable of capturing general thickness morphologies. In this work, thickness-tailored square steel tubes manufactured through variable gauge rolling are systematically investigated under axial impact through experiments and high-fidelity finite element simulations. The results reveal that continuous thickness tailoring enhances crash performance by simultaneously enlarging the plastically engaged material area and increasing the effective strain level within that region. To rationalize these observations, an extended folding-based energy framework is developed in which bending, membrane stretching, conical transition and rolling-strip contributions are explicitly partitioned. A layer-wise formulation and eight morphology descriptors are then introduced to link the axial thickness history directly to the mean crushing load and initial peak force. The unified framework demonstrates strong agreement with numerical simulations across 132 tailored configurations and supports rapid multi-objective exploration of the thickness design space. The proposed approach provides a mechanism-informed and optimization-ready methodology for the design of thickness-tailored steel crash components, bridging material tailoring capability and structural performance prediction.

title: Derivative-free optimization for crystal plasticity parameter calibration: benchmarking, non-uniqueness, and transferability
abstract: Crystal plasticity (CP) models are widely used to describe anisotropic deformation in metallic materials, yet their predictive capability relies on accurate calibration of numerous material parameters. This calibration task constitutes a high-dimensional, computationally expensive black-box optimization problem strongly affected by prior parameter uncertainty. Here, CP parameter calibration is formulated as a budget-constrained optimization problem, and four derivative-free algorithms, namely Nelder-Mead, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Bayesian Optimization, are benchmarked under a unified protocol. Three representative CP models are considered: a BCC phenomenological model, an FCC dislocation-density model, and an HCP slip-twinning model. Performance is evaluated by minimum normalized root-mean-square error under a fixed evaluation budget across narrow, medium, and wide prior domains. Bayesian Optimization shows the highest sample efficiency and robustness under wide priors and complex landscapes, whereas Genetic Algorithm provides the most stable surrogate-free baseline. Nelder-Mead performs satisfactorily only in low-dimensional settings with restricted priors. Calibration difficulty is governed primarily by parameter-error landscape structure rather than nominal dimensionality: FCC under wide priors is the most challenging regime, whereas the higher-dimensional HCP model remains tractable. Low fitting error does not guarantee parameter identifiability because near-optimal regions may involve substantial parameter trade-offs.

title: Curvature as a cue guides biomaterial design for corneal tissue engineering
abstract: Corneal curvature is a fundamental determinant of optical function and tissue structural stability. With the development of biomaterials and biofabrication technologies, great progress has been made in promoting transparent repair and replacement of corneal tissue. However, the strategic incorporation of biomimetic curvature design remains underdeveloped, potentially limiting the restoration of visual quality. This review systematically collates research on corneal curvature, from its geometric description, clinical relevance, and cellular responses to applications in tissue engineering and in vitro models, while highlighting the crucial role of biomaterials as investigative platforms and enabling substrates for implementing biomimetic curvature. Through this integrated perspective, this review aims to bridge the gap between basic research and clinical applications, offering inspiration for biomaterial design and manufacturing strateges to advance corneal regenerative medicine from simply restoring light transmission to recovering precise refractive function.

title: Disordered metamaterials and network architectures: towards sustainability‑by‑design and functional applications
abstract: With the growing interest in synthetic and advanced materials for sustainable applications, there is increasing demand for design‑driven, multifunctional performance from metamaterials and architected networks. While metamaterials are typically periodic, introducing controlled disorder as a sustainability‑by‑design strategy can enhance functionality compared to ordered architectures, enabling application‑focused structure–property optimization with improved resource efficiency and durability. The rapid integration of artificial intelligence and data‑driven materials design is driving a new paradigm in materials‑by‑design, where machine learning facilitates efficient exploration of complex design spaces. This perspective examines emerging materials and design approaches for disordered metamaterials, emphasizing structure–processing–property–performance relationships relevant to materials sustainability. It highlights potential for vibration attenuation, acoustics, wave control, and tailored mechanical behavior. The advantages of these periodic counterparts are critically discussed from the perspectives of reliability, robustness, and environmental sustainability. Recent studies show disordered architectures can deliver enhanced mechanical performance, including auxeticity, high stiffness‑to‑weight, impact resistance, reduced brittleness, and superior attenuation, while being less dependent on strict symmetry and more tolerant to defects, supporting sustainable manufacturing. Consequently, disordered metamaterials emerge as damage‑tolerant, performance‑oriented sustainable systems offering superior responses under realistic conditions. The article reviews advanced manufacturing routes, summarizes the state of the art, and outlines future directions for data‑enabled, life‑cycle‑informed design compatible with circular economy objectives.

title: Carbon based composite nanostructures for ammonia sensing: comprehensive review on mechanisms, design principles, and emerging strategies
abstract: NH 3 is a hazardous atmospheric pollutant in excessive concentrations and an important biomedical marker, requiring sensitive, low-power, and real-time monitoring for environmental safety. Chemiresistive gas sensors are attractive for NH 3 detection due to their simple design, high signal efficiency, and compatibility with flexible electronics. Most of these sensors based on pristine metal oxide semiconductors, which operates at high temperatures, leading to high power consumption and limiting wearable applications, while conducting polymer based sensors suffer from long term stability and humidity. Compared to these materials, carbon nanomaterials have emerged as promising room-temperature sensing materials due to their high surface area, excellent conductivity, and enviromental friendliness·NH 3 sensing in various type of carbon materials is governed by physisorption and chemisorption, enabling fast and reversible sensing performance. However, pristine carbon often shows limited selectivity toward certain gas molecules and poor cyclablity. In this review, we comprehensively analyze recent advances in binary and ternary carbon-based composites for chemiresistive NH 3 sensors, focusing on synergistic effects such as heterojunction formation and surface functionalization. Furthermore, investigate various morphologies and structures, alongside key challenges and future directions, and examine their relationships to gas-sensing performance, demonstrating their promise for robust, flexible, and wearable NH 3 sensor applications.

title: Enhanced impedance matching with graded interphases for CFRP-steel FMLs with embedded sensors – A numerical investigation
abstract: Innovative composites with superior mechanical properties have been developed through the combination of various materials. Steel and carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) have each become well-known materials in a variety of engineering applications. Their combination of these materials has led to a remarkable class of composites known as CFRP-steel fibre metal laminates (FML). For the advancement of structural health monitoring (SHM) using guided ultrasonic waves in FML, effective testing methods are under research and require further improvement. The integration of sensors into the FML structure enhances damage detection capabilities. However, integrated sensors act as obstacles and disturb the wave field which may result in over- or underestimation of a damage. In a previous study it was observed that introducing a functionally graded material as an interphase can reduce wave field distortion. This paper presents a comprehensive numerical study on a two-dimensional model of an FML with integrated sensor and surrounding interphase, to optimise impedance matching and thereby reduce distortions of the wave field. Investigations are conducted on sensor and interphase dimensions as well as on different wave modes. The optimised integration of sensor and interphase demonstrates promising potential for further enhancing the reliability of SHM systems.

title: Performance improvement and friction reduction mechanism of Al2O3/Ti(C,N)/CaF2@Al2O3 self-lubricating ceramic tool for machining Cr15Ni60 alloy
abstract: Nickel-based alloys commonly used in spacecraft and wear-resistant coatings have excellent hardness and corrosion resistance. However, their high strength presents great machining challenges. Conventional metal cutting tools suffer severe friction and wear when machining these alloys, resulting in poor cutting performance. Ceramic tools feature high hardness, heat resistance, and excellent chemical stability. They also exhibit low metal affinity and little adhesion, making them widely used for machining difficult to cut materials. Using spark plasma sintering (SPS), Al 2 O 3 /Ti(C,N)/CaF 2 @Al 2 O 3 self-lubricating ceramic tools were produced and tested against commercial Al 2 O 3 /Ti(C,N) cutters for machining the Ni-based alloy Cr15Ni60. Compared with the commercial tools, self-lubricating inserts reduced axial, radial, circumferential and overall cutting forces by 17.0 %, 13.1 %, 9.7 % and 11.4 % on average, and lowered rake-face friction coefficient and cutting temperature by 4.1 % and 25.8 %. Analysis of the friction reduction mechanism in self-lubricating ceramic tools machining nickel-based alloys reveals under cutting forces and friction, solid lubricants continuously precipitate from the tool and uniformly distribute across tool-workpiece contact zone. This forms a dynamically balanced lubricating film that reduces friction between the tool, workpiece, and chips. Consequently, cutting forces, cutting temperatures, and coefficient of friction are lowered while machining performance is enhanced.

title: Conformal acoustic holographic lenses for wavefront control via geometry-encoded design
abstract: We present a conformal acoustic holographic lens as a functional material system that integrates geometric architecture, acoustic response, and fabrication for subject-specific wave manipulation. Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) enables noninvasive neuromodulation, but its performance is limited by skull-induced impedance mismatch, phase distortion, and energy loss across multilayer interfaces. Existing approaches mitigate these effects through electronic or computational correction, yet they remain limited by point-focused wave control and do not fully exploit material and interfacial design for subject-specific volumetric tFUS control. Here, we introduce a skull-conforming acoustic holographic lens that embeds wavefront engineering into a conformal interface. Within a subject-specific volumetric holography (SSVH) framework, skull geometry, acoustic properties, and therapeutic constraints guide a hierarchical optimization pipeline to generate phase-encoded structures. The resulting device integrates a conformal holographic lens with a coupling layer to improve tissue-interface compatibility, support skull-conforming contact, and eliminate complex sealing designs required for fluidic coupling. Across 20 cases, simulations demonstrate robust volumetric focusing and consistent target coverage, while ex vivo human skull experiments confirm fabrication accuracy and acoustic field reconstruction. This work establishes a scalable, materials-driven strategy for geometry-aware wave manipulation and patient-adaptive therapeutic ultrasound.

title: Impedance decouple conceptual design of multifunctional electromagnetic metasurface for anti-icing applications
abstract: Ice accumulation in severe environment degrades radome functionality, making the integration of electrothermal capabilities a critical challenge. Therefore, Impedance Decouple Conceptual Design (IDCD) is put forward to construct a multifunctional composite electromagnetic metasurface with independently tunable electrothermal and microwave transmission performance. This design utilizes the real impedance for heating and absorption, and the imaginary impedance for transmission. Furthermore, Equivalent circuit analysis is employed to mathematically decouple the real and imaginary impedances by strictly constraining the reactive components. Also, the design is characterized by electromagnetic wave simulation and thermal simulation. To explain the operating principle, a two-layer periodic structure is engineered. The measured results show that the IDCD structure can get an absorption band in the 2.4–4 GHz range for at least 10 dB reflectivity reduction at the normal incidence. It also exhibits a transmission band with insertion loss less than 1 dB from 8 GHz to 8.9 GHz. Furthermore, it delivers substantial heating power over 1.93 kW/m 2 with a 150 V bias and exhibits efficient heating capabilities at −10 °C. A new design for radome is established for extreme environments and it provides a practical technical solution for integrating anti-icing and electromagnetic wave transmission in advanced aerospace materials.

title: Detection of thin corrosion layers on steel using an electromagnetic jet (EMJ) lens for microwave non-destructive testing
abstract: This study explores the use of an electromagnetic jet lens (EMJ) operating at 30 GHz as a cost-effective near-field microwave imaging technique to detect and characterize thin corrosion layers on steel. The reflection coefficient between rust and steel is affected by variations in relative permittivity and thickness. The electromagnetic jet lens measures this variation using a locally concentrated focus, enabling precise detection of corroded and non-corroded areas and estimation of average thickness. A theoretical model based on transmission-line equations and numerical simulation has been used to quantify how rust thickness affects the reflected signal. Experiments were performed on a partially corroded steel plate, whose average rust thickness was first determined by a mechanical micrometer. Using the EMJ lens, high-resolution line scans of the plate surface were obtained. The EMJ measurements identified corroded and non-corroded areas from changes in reflected amplitude and phase and provided average rust thickness estimates closely matching micrometer measurements. Thus, the EMJ method provides a contactless and economical approach to evaluate corrosion, highly sensitive to geometric and dielectric changes. The results demonstrate that EMJ-based microwave non-destructive testing is a viable method for early corrosion detection.

title: Preparation of advanced copper-based brake pad material via multi-component powder metallurgy technology
abstract: To prepare high-performance copper-based brake pad materials that meet mine safety and braking requirements, a new brake pad material (BPM) was fabricated via multi-component powder metallurgy sintering. Copper powder and cemented carbide were mixed at a mass ratio of 1:2, sintered at 1100 °C for 30 min, and compared with German copper-based brake pad materials for mining (GBPM). Microstructure and phase composition were characterized by optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy dispersive spectrometry and X-ray diffraction, while friction properties were tested on a reciprocating dry friction tester. The results show that BPM and GBPM have identical phase composition, consisting of Cu, WC and AlCoCrW phases, W, Co significantly improve wear resistance, and Si helps enhance material density. Although BPM has slightly lower sintering density than GBPM, it exhibits strong interfacial bonding and a stable friction coefficient above 0.3 (up to over 0.5), with no sparks during braking, meeting mine explosion-proof and application requirements. BPM has been mass-applied on mining trucks in Chinese coal mines, meeting performance targets with lower cost, providing a feasible solution for the domestic production of copper-based mine brake pads.

title: Dual oxidized glycosaminoglycans crosslinked type II collagen hydrogel for in-situ full-thickness cartilage defect repair: in vitro and in vivo experiments
abstract: Hyaline articular cartilage (HAC) defects exhibit extremely limited self-repair capacity, while standard microfracture treatment tends to form inferior fibrocartilage. This study aimed to develop a dual oxidized glycosaminoglycan-crosslinked type II collagen (COL II) chondro-bionic hydrogel for in-situ repair of full-thickness articular cartilage defects. The hydrogel was prepared via Schiff base crosslinking at an optimized COL II/oxidized chondroitin sulfate/oxidized hyaluronic acid ratio of 80:15:5. It achieved rapid gelation within 5–10 min and exhibited mechanical properties consistent with native cartilage. In vitro , the hydrogel significantly promoted the proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. In vivo , the hydrogel induced complete hyaline cartilage regeneration with biomechanical properties close to healthy cartilage at 6 months, and no systemic toxicity was detected. This hydrogel provides a safe, effective, and clinically translatable strategy for articular cartilage defect treatment

title: Structural and oxidation behavior of Ti3AlC2 in extreme environments
abstract: MAX phase (Ti 3 AlC 2 ) is a promising material for high-temperature applications due to its atomic structure, which features alternating Ti-C and Ti-Al layers. This unique bonding pattern gives it characteristics of both metals and ceramics. Understanding its microstructural behavior and chemistry under extreme conditions is essential for its use in various applications. In this work, Ti 3 AlC 2 is processed using shock waves generated in a shock tube. The shock waves heat Ti 3 AlC 2 to the desired high temperature in inert argon and air for 2–3 ms, with heating and cooling rates of 10 6 K/s. The shock-processed Ti 3 AlC 2 is characterized using various analytical techniques to investigate its shock resistance, microstructural changes, structural stability, and high-temperature oxidation behavior. The results indicate that Ti 3 AlC 2 didn’t exhibit complete structural decomposition under shock conditions in argon, even at temperatures up to ∼6278 K. In contrast, shock exposure in air at ∼1989 K yields spherical oxidation products, such as TiO 2 and Al 2 TiO 5 . Additionally, a cubic TiC structure forms from Ti 3 AlC 2 after shock exposure in both argon and air. This study offers valuable insights into the structural stability and surface reactions of MAX phases at high temperatures, highlighting their potential for extreme-environment applications.

title: Exploring deformation localization via precipitate-free bands formed during low-cycle fatigue in a Cu–3.15 mass% Ti alloy
abstract: Precipitation-strengthened Cu alloys undergo channelized cyclic deformation, but its microstructural nature and orientation dependence remain unclear. In this study, a near-peak-aged Cu–3.15 mass% Ti alloy is subjected to low-cycle fatigue (ε p = 0.20%–1.00%) and interrupted at the stress-amplitude plateau. Correlative electron microscopy identifies the localizations as precipitate-free bands (PFBs), containing slip channels depleted of intact β′ precipitates without systematic band-scale Ti redistribution. High-resolution electron backscatter diffraction reveals that PFBs are zones of intense plastic localization, exhibiting high geometrically necessary dislocation densities (10 15 –10 16 m −2 ), continuous lattice rotations, and residual stress variations (∼10 2 MPa). Grain-scale probability maps reveal an amplitude-dependent orientation tendency: low Taylor-factor orientations are favored at ε p = 0.20%, whereas the product of directional Young’s modulus and maximum Schmid factor correlates more strongly at ε p = 0.50%. Orientation–based separation weakens near ε p ≈ 0.35%. Grain-level and population–averaged PFB coverage metrics describe localization intensity more robustly than highly scattered PFB widths. The study findings provide orientation- and coverage-based descriptors for assessing fatigue localization in precipitation–strengthened Cu alloys.

title: Cryogenic minimum quantity lubrication in GH4169 machining: meshfree chip formation simulation and microstructural evidence of improved surface integrity
abstract: Nickel-based superalloy GH4169 is widely used in aero-engine casings, but its high flow strength, strong work hardening, and low thermal conductivity make machining difficult and often lead to degraded surface integrity. The key question addressed here is how cryogenic minimum quantity lubrication (CMQL) can be utilized to control the processing-microstructure-surface integrity relationship during GH4169 machining. Controlled turning tests under dry, flood, MQL, and CMQL conditions were combined with SEM, TEM, EBSD, surface roughness, microhardness, residual stress, chip morphology, and tool-wear analyses. A GPU-parallelized smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) thermo-mechanical cutting model was further employed to interpret the cooling-induced changes in temperature field and chip formation. The novelty of the study lies in linking directed tool-side cooling to chip segmentation, near-surface microstructural evolution, and service-relevant surface integrity metrics for GH4169, including a production-oriented casing-machining case. Under CMQL, the machined surface showed improved topography (peak-to-valley, PV = 1.612 μm; Ra = 0.357 μm), a limited hardened layer of ∼110 μm, and a compressive residual stress of ∼55 MPa. Tool flank wear was reduced by ∼48% compared with dry cutting. TEM and EBSD confirmed a thin nanocrystalline surface layer and a reduced machining-affected layer, while SPH simulations reproduced the observed temperature and chip-morphology trends. These results demonstrate CMQL as a process-design strategy for improving the surface integrity and machinability of GH4169 components.

title: Prediction of segregation, short-range order, and plasticity in nickel based polycrystals: insights from an uncertainty aware machine learning potential
abstract: Trace phosphorus segregation at grain boundaries (GBs) offers a promising yet insufficiently quantified route to strengthen multicomponent nickel-based superalloy (NBS), where segregation, chemical short-range order (CSRO), and plasticity are intrinsically coupled. Here, we develop a quinary moment tensor potential for Ni-Cr-Fe-Al-P and validate its accuracy and transferability. Uncertainty quantification based on maximum‑volume and D‑optimality criteria is further employed to assess the reliability of the potential during polycrystalline segregation and tensile simulations. Hybrid MC/MD simulations reveal a temperature-driven transition in phosphorus segregation, from uniform GB segregation at 300 K to Cr 3 P-rich amorphous complexions localized at triple junctions at 1000 K. Uniaxial tension on the segregated models further identifies a CSRO-controlled strengthening baseline together with an additional morphology-dependent segregation strengthening associated with enhanced dislocation pinning, pile-ups, and sessile dislocation formation. These results highlight the potential for predictive segregation engineering in NBS.

title: Influence of ceramic retention on inter-splat bonding and mechanical behavior of cold-sprayed Cu-ZrC composite coatings
abstract: Cold-sprayed metal-ceramic composite coatings offer a promising route for high-performance surface engineering; however, the influence of ceramic retention on inter-splat bonding and mechanical performance remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Cu-ZrC composite coatings containing 30–85 wt% ZrC were deposited on Al-6061 substrates to investigate deposition behavior, interfacial integrity, and tribological response. Coating build-up was achieved for all compositions, although deposition efficiency decreased at higher ceramic loading due to increased particle rebound and reduced matrix continuity. Hardness increased continuously with ZrC content, while adhesion strength and scratch resistance showed non-linear behavior, with optimum cohesion observed at intermediate compositions (50–70 wt% ZrC). Scratch testing revealed reduced penetration depth and improved resistance to localized deformation with increasing ceramic content, indicating enhanced inter-splat bonding. Ball-on-disk wear testing demonstrated a progressive reduction in wear volume, reaching ∼ 93% lower wear for the 85 wt% ZrC coating compared to pure Cu, accompanied by a transition from ductile adhesive wear to brittle fragmentation-dominated mechanisms. Overall, intermediate ceramic contents provided the best balance between deposition efficiency, mechanical integrity, and tribological performance.

title: Biodistribution and transport of intratympanically administered drugs in the inner ear using a porcine ex-vivo chamber model
abstract: Effective pharmacotherapy for hearing loss remains a significant challenge because of the blood-labyrinth barrier, which limits systemic drug access and often necessitates local intratympanic (IT) administration. However, the distribution of drugs after IT injection between the vestibular system and cochlea is unclear. Although the round window membrane is the main recognized entry route, in this study, we explored alternative pathways, namely the oval window (OW) and the thin apical otic capsule, using an ex vivo porcine model to assess their permeability to different solvent vehicles. We demonstrated that the route of entry is critically on the solvent composition and additives; in particular, reconstituting dexamethasone-fluorescein in dimethyl sulfoxide enhanced permeability through the OW by 42-fold compared to that with methanol, establishing the OW as a pathway for this solvent type rather than the RWM. Furthermore, we identified the thin apical otic capsule as a third drug-entry route in young pigs. Surgical sealing of this pathway in vivo, which reduces perilymph drug levels, underscores its importance in human translational studies. In summary, we developed a robust ex vivo multi-barrier model integrated with FluidSim to predict the inner ear drug biodistribution.

title: Wear and fracture mechanisms of sputtered low-friction TiAlSiN:MoS2 thin films
abstract: Coating cutting tools with TiAlSiN thin films increases their lifespan; however, this still requires wet lubrication. Here, we demonstrate the viability of low-friction TiAlSiN thin films coupled with dry lubrication through molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) alloying (TiAlSiN:MoS 2 ) under varying alloying levels and exaggerated uniaxial loading to understand the fracture mechanisms. The films were fabricated through reactive magnetron sputtering, achieving 45% reduction in the coefficient of friction (CoF) upon introducing MoS 2 , compared to a reference film. The film with the lowest MoS 2 (3.6 at.%) exhibited the lowest CoF (∼ 0.0525) – owing to the formation of a MoO 3 /Mo x O y tribofilm, the highest S/Mo ratio (1.8), c -TiAlN crystal phases (in Si 3 N 4 matrix), and ordered 2H-MoS 2 . It also showed moderate hardness (∼5.6 GPa), elastic modulus (∼130 GPa), H/E (∼0.04), and H 3 /E 2 (∼0.01 GPa) ratios, excellent resistance to fracture, and minimal oxidative degradation. This film displayed a good balance between the desired structural and tribological properties for self-lubricating thin films. Lastly, an increase in MoS 2 transformed the fracture and wear mechanisms of the films: ductile – abrasive degradation to brittle – oxidative degradation, associated with the oxidation of MoS 2 . This study establishes a practical framework for the design, fabrication, and performance evaluation of self-lubricating TiAlSiN:MoS 2 coatings for advanced cutting tool applications.

title: Genetic optimization of partitioned architected lattices for broadband sound absorption
abstract: This study presents a computationally efficient optimization framework for designing architected lattice structures with broadband sound absorption. An equivalent material model was developed to replace the detailed lattice geometry with a homogeneous layer characterized by frequency-dependent complex impedance and propagation constant. This approach reduces the computational cost of acoustic simulations by more than three orders of magnitude compared with direct finite element modeling, enabling large-scale genetic-algorithm-based exploration of plate placement configurations. The optimized structures exhibit substantially enhanced broadband absorption relative to conventional octet lattices. The equivalent material method accurately reproduced the acoustic responses of both baseline and optimized geometries, showing strong agreement with full resolution simulations. To validate the numerical predictions, three optimized specimens were fabricated using a Stereolithography Apparatus (SLA) process. Impedance tube measurements confirmed the broadband absorption performance and demonstrated that the proposed designs remain effective even in the presence of geometric imperfections introduced during manufacturing. Overall, the results establish the proposed framework as a powerful and manufacturable strategy for engineering high-performance acoustic metamaterials.

title: Finite element investigation of topology-dependent functional behavior of interpenetrating phase composites with architected Nitinol cores
abstract: This work numerically investigates the functional behavior of three-dimensional dual-phase interpenetrating phase composites (IPCs). The architected phase comprises Nitinol (NiTi) shape memory alloy (SMA) cores embedded within an elastic–plastic AlSi10Mg matrix. Eight NiTi architected phases, including triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) and strut-based topologies, are analyzed, and unit-cell homogenization technique is adopted to evaluate the effective response of the periodic IPCs under uniaxial, shear, and hydrostatic loading. The results reveal a clear stiffness-strength trade-off: increasing NiTi content reduces effective stiffness but increases the yield strength of the IPCs. The preferred architecture depends strongly on loading mode, with strut-based IPCs providing higher resistance to uniaxial yielding and TPMS-based IPCs showing better shear resistance. The surrounding AlSi10Mg matrix amplifies local stresses in the embedded NiTi phase, producing more than 95% martensitic transformation during loading. However, the same constraint suppresses complete reverse transformation during unloading, resulting in residual martensite and incomplete superelastic recovery. Significant transformation-driven superelastic recovery appears only when the NiTi content exceeds approximately 35%. These findings establish a topology-property-transformation relationship for architected smart IPCs and provide quantitative design guidance for balancing stiffness, strength, phase transformation, and recoverable deformation.

title: Numerical and experimental analysis of thermal-flow-phase transformation in in-situ ceramic reinforced laser cladding Ti coatings
abstract: A coupled thermal-flow-phase transformation numerical model was developed and validated through experiments and multi-scale characterization to elucidate the formation and strengthening mechanisms of ceramic phases in laser-clad B 4 C/Ti-6Al-4 V coatings. Within the molten pool, Marangoni convection drives solute transport over a characteristic distance of ∼104.5 mm, significantly surpassing the characteristic solute diffusion length (∼40.6 μm), indicating that macroscopic convection, rather than diffusion, dominates solute redistribution of B, C, and N. Under such intense convection, a nitrogen atmosphere promotes in-situ formation of TiB 2 , TiC, and TiN reinforcements. This multi-phase structure increases the coating hardness to 648 HV 0 . 2 , a 224% enhancement over the substrate. This is primarily attributed to Orowan strengthening and grain refinement, while the wear rate decreases by 92.7%. These results establish quantitative relationships among process parameters, macroscopic morphology, microstructure, and mechanical properties, providing a basis for the digital design and performance optimization of titanium alloy coatings.

title: Octopus lenses: a flat 3D-printed contact lens architecture for geometry-driven ocular drug delivery
abstract: The development of drug-eluting contact lenses is constrained by fabrication complexity and limited design freedom, particularly for 3D-printed curved geometries. This study evaluates a flat-based 3D-printed contact lens architecture, termed the Octopus lens, as a simplified alternative that retains conformability to ocular curvature. Lenses were fabricated using a HEMA:PEGDA (97:3) hydrogel resin with 1 wt% TPO and compared with flat disks and directly printed curved lenses. Flat-based designs exhibited high optical transparency (∼90%), smoother surfaces (8.48 µm), and lower thickness (0.45 ± 0.02 mm) than curved lenses. All geometries showed comparable equilibrium water content (∼30%) and oxygen permeability (Dk ≈ 5.25–5.96 barrer), indicating similar bulk material properties. Methylene blue (MB) was used as a model compound to assess drug-delivery performance. All lenses exhibited similar MB uptake, normalized to dry weight (∼33%), while thicker, curved lenses showed higher absolute loading. Release kinetics were geometry-dependent and best described by diffusion-based models. Korsmeyer-Peppas analysis (n = 0.756–0.928) indicated anomalous transport dominated by diffusion. Octopus lenses demonstrated enhanced diffusion efficiency due to reduced diffusion path length and potentially increased exposed surface area.
