These findings establish geometry-driven diffusion control as a key design principle and highlight flat-based architectures as scalable platforms for ocular drug delivery.

title: Influence of process parameters on stability, surface roughness, and defect formation in wire laser additive manufacturing at high deposition rate
abstract: The wire-based laser additive manufacturing (WLAM) process enables the large-scale production of metallic components with complex geometries. To ensure the integrity of the produced parts, it is essential to assess the quality of the printed material. For this purpose, this study is divided into three parts. The first part focuses on the stability of single-wire deposition using an instrumented test bench. The second part investigates the overlap ratio between successive passes, aiming to minimize surface roughness and ensure optimal printing of the 3D structure. The third part aims at characterize the macroscopic defects observed in 3D structures under various parameter sets. The study on single beads deposition reveals the existence of a stable domain, based on geometric stability and observations of the laser-material interaction. The second study determines the minimum surface roughness and the optimal layer height for different printing conditions, while also highlighting the relationship between surface quality and the wetting angle. The analysis of macroscopic defects across various parameter sets shows a strong correlation between the type of defect and the manufacturing conditions. This study identifies a stable WLAM operating window enabling high deposition rates with good geometric repeatability, though internal defects may still occur.

title: Physics-inspired feature engineering and interpretable machine learning for thermoelectric properties of multicomponent materials
abstract: Machine learning can accelerate thermoelectric materials discovery, yet most models remain “black boxes” lacking physical insight. We present an interpretable framework coupling Extra Trees regression with SHAP analysis to predict electrical conductivity (EC), Seebeck coefficient (SC), and thermal conductivity (TC) across 3879 multicomponent compositions. Physics-inspired feature engineering expands descriptors to 73–84 per target via polynomial lattice-distortion terms, cross-interactions, and compositional disorder statistics. Random-split test-set values reach 0.961, 0.965, and 0.958 for EC, SC, and TC, respectively, surpassing a lightweight deep neural network. Composition-wise splitting reduces to 0.822, 0.871, and 0.876, indicating limited generalisation to unseen compositions. SHAP analysis reveals property-specific associations: elemental descriptors dominate all targets, lattice-distortion terms influence EC, and heavy-element features affect TC. As a consistency check, a ZT-proxy computed from the independently predicted transport properties agrees reasonably well with experimental values on the test set ( = 0.84); it is intended as a screening aid rather than a verified figure of merit. This interpretable framework supports screening and prioritisation backed by, not replacing, experimental validation.

title: Atomically precise Au24Cd1 clusterzyme suppresses ferroptotic secondary injury by remodeling iron-redox homeostasis after traumatic brain injury
abstract: Traumatic brain injury lacks effective therapies for delayed secondary injury, which is driven in part by hemorrhage-induced iron overload, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. We designed an atomically precise Au 24 Cd 1 clusterzyme through single-atom cadmium substitution in Au 25 and evaluated whether this material could remodel the post-traumatic iron-redox microenvironment. Au 24 Cd 1 showed stronger antioxidant, superoxide dismutase-like, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidase-like, and catalase-like activities than Au 25 . In mouse traumatic brain injury models, transcriptomics identified ferroptosis and iron-homeostasis dysregulation as dominant early responses. Longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging, histology, biochemical assays, and behavioral testing showed that Au 24 Cd 1 reduced lesion volume, accelerated hematoma resolution, improved survival and neurological recovery, preserved neurons, and suppressed oxidative stress, glial activation, and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, Au 24 Cd 1 lowered heme and Fe 2+ accumulation, promoted iron-homeostatic remodeling, preserved glutathione peroxidase activity, and enhanced nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) nuclear translocation with heme oxygenase-1(HO-1)-associated protection; these effects were weakened by Nrf2 inhibition. This work identifies iron-redox microenvironment remodeling by an atomically precise clusterzyme as a therapeutic strategy for ferroptotic secondary injury after traumatic brain injury.

title: Ultrasmall carbon nanotube-like network in ZSM-5 by optimized methane CVD
abstract: Achieving high filling of sub-nanometer carbon structures in zeolite channels remains challenging because premature carbon deposition can hinder precursor diffusion and internal growth. Here, we report an optimized methane chemical vapor deposition route for growing an ultrasmall carbon nanotube-like network in ZSM-5 zeolite with intersecting 5.1–5.6 Å channels. By introducing methane only after the reactor reaches the target temperature under high vacuum, carbon deposition during heating is suppressed and pore filling is markedly improved. The resulting carbon loading reaches 29.1 wt%, corresponding to a model-dependent estimated pore-filling factor of about 0.98. Raman spectra reveal characteristic features of strongly confined ultrasmall one-dimensional carbon structures, while thermogravimetric analysis indicates high thermal stability. Four-probe transport measurements show metallic-like behavior, further supported by density functional theory calculations. This work shows that process design governs precursor transport, pore filling, confined structure formation, and final properties, and thereby provides a practical route to densely filled ultrasmall carbon networks in zeolite hosts.

title: Precursor-engineered oxygen-self-sufficient carbon dots for remodeling the infectious microenvironment toward enhanced sonodynamic therapy of bacterial meningitis
abstract: Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) offers a promising non-antibiotic strategy for intracranial bacterial infections, but its efficacy is limited by the blood–brain barrier (BBB), lesion hypoxia, and potential systemic toxicity of conventional sonosensitizers. Here, we develop multifunctional manganese-doped carbon dots (Mn-CDs) through precursor engineering by hydrothermally carbonizing methylene blue (MB, a sonosensitive moiety), manganese gluconate (a coordinated catalytic source), and dragon fruit powder (a biocompatible carbon matrix). This design integrates MB-derived sonosensitive motifs and Mn-related catalase (CAT)-like catalytic sites into an ultrasmall carbon framework. Mn-CDs efficiently decompose pathological hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) into oxygen (O 2 ), thereby relieving hypoxia and fueling ultrasound-triggered SDT to generate singlet oxygen. The resulting oxidative stress disrupts bacterial membranes, impairs metabolic activity, and achieves 98% antibacterial efficiency against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in vitro . Owing to their ultrasmall size (around 4.84 nm) and good Mn retention, Mn-CDs cross the BBB and efficiently accumulate in infected brain tissue with favorable biosafety. In an MRSA-induced meningitis mouse model, Mn-CDs-mediated SDT markedly reduces cerebral bacterial burden, attenuates neuroinflammation by regulating TNF-α and IL-10, decreases neuronal apoptosis, and improves behavioral recovery. This microenvironment-adaptive Mn-CDs platform provides an intelligent strategy for treating drug-resistant central nervous system infections.

title: In situ atomic-resolution observation of the anisotropic decomposition in TaN
abstract: The service life of transition-metal nitride thin films is critically limited by their tendency to decompose under extreme conditions. Previous studies have generally suggested that decomposition proceeds through a gradual structural transformation between different phases, accompanied by nitrogen loss. Here, using in-situ high-resolution transmission electron microscopy and quantitative measurements combined with theoretical analyses, we carefully investigate the decomposition behavior of a rock-salt TaN film at the atomic scale under electron-beam irradiation. The results reveal that TaN decomposes directly into metallic Ta without forming the intermediate hexagonal TaN 2 phase. Furthermore, when irradiated along the [0 0 1] TaN direction, TaN exhibits a stronger tendency toward structural transformation, while most nitrogen remains within the irradiated Ta product. In contrast, irradiation along the [1 1 0] TaN direction promotes nitrogen loss from TaN but suppresses the structural transformation. The observed decoupling between structural transformation and nitrogen depletion is primarily attributed to the orientation-dependent decomposition of TaN crystals. These findings provide new insights into the anisotropic decomposition behavior of transition-metal nitrides and establish a framework for tailoring the stability and composition of non-stoichiometric nitride systems.

title: Near peak-aged strengthening of Al-Mg-Si-Cu alloys by extrusion-induced in-situ precipitation via short-process powder metallurgy
abstract: Conventional powder metallurgy (PM) processing of Al–Mg–Si–Cu alloys generally relies on solution–aging (T6) treatment to activate precipitation strengthening, resulting in long processing cycles and high cost. Here, a short-process PM strategy is developed by coupling rapid solidification with extrusion-induced in-situ precipitation to directly generate a near peak-aged microstructure. Gas-atomized Al–5.0Mg–0.5Si–(0.5/1.0)Cu powders exhibit fine cellular structures and high solute supersaturation. Hot extrusion at 300 °C simultaneously consolidates the powders, induces dynamic recrystallization, and activates in-situ precipitation, producing refined equiaxed grains and a high density of strengthening precipitates. The Al–5.0Mg–0.5Si–0.5Cu alloy achieves an ultimate tensile strength of 396.8 ± 1.7 MPa, a yield strength of 250.6 ± 1.7 MPa, and an elongation of 11.9 ± 1.1% directly in the as-extruded state, with only marginal softening after subsequent aging. TEM reveals that strengthening is dominated by coherent nanoscale β″/β′ precipitates, supplemented by coarser β (Mg₂Si) and Al₂CuMg phases. In contrast, solution treatment causes precipitate coarsening, density loss, and oxygen uptake, resulting in inferior properties. This work demonstrates a simplified and scalable route for producing high-strength, ductile Al–Mg–Si–Cu alloys without conventional T6 treatment.

title: Selaginella iepidophylla-Inspired cellulose nanofibers/graphene oxide biomimetic asymmetric film for multimodal simultaneous self-powered monitoring(BAMS) of respiration and sweat
abstract: Real-time and simultaneous monitoring of respiration and sweat status is of great significance for assessing human motion states. Inspired by Selaginella lepidophylla , this study designed a self-powered multimodal sensor based on a biomimetic asymmetric CNF/GO film. At the material level, an asymmetric film was fabricated using gradient drying and unilateral imprinting, achieving a maximum bending angle of 55° under humidity stimulation. At the device level, the TENG sensor integrated with PTFE achieved a maximum output voltage of 2.564 V. It exhibited distinct temporal characteristics and anti-interference capability in response to airflow and water vapor, while maintaining stable performance after 500 cyclic loadings. At the application level, the sensor effectively distinguished different breathing patterns and sweat variations across different body regions, and enabled physiological signal monitoring under resting, aerobic, and anaerobic conditions. Using professional athletes as subjects, wearable experiments were conducted for four types of sports: 400 m running, tennis, volleyball, and basketball. The sensor accurately captured changes in respiration and sweat signals before and after exercise. The observed signal differences corresponded well with the energy expenditure ratings of smartwatches, effectively distinguishing physiological response variations under different exercise intensities.

title: Hierarchical “Brick-and-Ball” silk fibroin microspheres for mechanically-reinforced cavity filling and photothermal–curcumin synergetic prevention of triple-negative breast cancer recurrence
abstract: Postoperative recurrence of triple-negative breast cancer often starts from residual cells left in an irregular lumpectomy cavity, where a short-lived drug depot is easily washed away and a weak filler gives little structural support. We designed injectable SFMA/MXene/curcumin-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticle (Cur@MSN) microspheres as a cavity-filling chemophotothermal depot rather than a membrane-like wound dressing. XPS confirmed silica-, curcumin- and MXene-associated signals, including Ti-O contributions in the composite. Mechanical tests showed that MXene/MSN reinforcement increased single-particle stiffness and improved hydrated packed-bed compression resistance, cyclic modulus retention and anti-flushing stability. Curcumin release continued for 14 days, and near-infrared irradiation increased the 32 h release from 68.97 ± 0.55% to 82.93 ± 0.45%. Normal 10A and NIH3T3 cells retained high viability, whereas 4 T1 cells showed concentration-dependent inhibition. In vivo thermal screening identified 2.0 mg/mL MXene with 0.50 W/cm 2 irradiation as a mild heating condition (∼43 °C). In a postoperative 4 T1 model, Cur/MXene microspheres with irradiation reduced bioluminescent tumor signals, supporting a locally retained, mechanically reinforced depot for recurrence-oriented therapy.

title: Magnesium-Chelating peptides from Miichthys miiuy scales enhance osteogenic and osteoprotective potential in vitro and in vivo
abstract: Magnesium deficiency is an underrecognized contributor to osteoporosis, yet conventional magnesium supplements often exhibit limited efficacy due to poor stability and bioavailability. Here, we developed magnesium-chelating peptides from Miichthys miiuy scale (MMSP-Mg) hydrolysates and systematically characterized its stability and osteoprotective activity. MMSP-Mg showed excellent physicochemical stability, retaining more than 80% of its magnesium content over a wide pH range (2–10), temperatures (0–60 °C), and after simulated gastrointestinal digestion. In MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts, MMSP-Mg significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation, increasing alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity by 2.05-fold, enhancing mineralized nodule formation by 2.14-fold, and upregulating the osteogenic markers COL1A1 (2.04-fold), Runx2 (1.64-fold), Osterix (1.96-fold), and Osteopontin (OPN; 2.12-fold). In osteoporotic mice, oral administration of MMSP-Mg improved bone metabolism, reducing serum tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) from 19.24 ± 8.63 to 13.71 ± 1.34 U/L and increasing serum phosphorus from 1.03 ± 0.43 to 1.42 ± 0.14 mmol/L, accompanied by marked restoration of femoral microarchitecture on micro-computed tomography. Further purification of MMSP identified two key bioactive peptides, QLGPMGPR and MAPGKDGLR, each exhibiting > 70% magnesium-binding capacity and significantly enhancing ALP activity, with these effects further strengthened upon Mg 2+ -chelation. Collectively, these results demonstrate that MMSP-Mg is a highly stable, peptide-based magnesium supplement with robust osteogenic and osteoprotective potential.

title: Enabling ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy through hybrid lightweight rotary anode design
abstract: Compact X-ray sources for spatially fractionated and ultra-high-dose-rate radiotherapy are limited by the extreme thermal and mechanical loads imposed on conventional rotary anodes. Here we investigate a hybrid rotary-anode architecture that separates X-ray generation from structural load bearing by bonding a tungsten–rhenium/titanium–zirconium–molybdenum (TZM) alloy target module to a lightweight titanium carrier. The diffusion-bonded interface was characterized by metallography and temperature-dependent tensile and shear testing up to 1000 . These experimentally determined strength limits were combined with three-dimensional thermomechanical finite-element simulations of a 600 mm high-speed anode exposed to transient absorbed heat loads up to 1 MW. The simulations show that the highest temperatures remain confined to the focal track and adjacent refractory target region, whereas the titanium–TZM interface remains below the experimentally identified temperature range of pronounced strength reduction. The segmented, lightweight architecture reduces centrifugal loading while providing a large transient thermal capacity. The revised analysis further discusses heat rejection, duty-cycle limitations, bearing concepts and the separated validation strategy required before full source integration.

title: Development of a new high-strength diffusion-assisted healable Al-Mg-Zr alloy produced by Powder Bed Fusion - Laser Beam/Metals
abstract: Additive manufacturing enables complex lightweight aluminium components but often generates microvoids or microcracks degrading the mechanical properties. Introducing healing ability into high-strength Al alloys could mitigate these defects and improve structural integrity. A new high-strength and healable Al-Mg-Zr alloy, Almazium®, was developed and processed by Powder Bed Fusion - Laser Beam/Metals (PBF-LB/M). High Mg content and Zr-induced grain refinement produce a fine bimodal microstructure and a yield strength of 317 MPa in the as-built condition. Synchrotron X-ray nano-holo-tomography revealed that a Healing Heat Treatment (HHT) at 540 ∘ C for 30 min fully closed 65 % of submicrometric voids, with complete healing up to 3.7 µm. At 400 ∘ C, 90 % of submicrometric voids were fully healed, with a maximum healed size of 1.5 µm. Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy and Atom Probe Tomography revealed a high Mg content in solid solution, supporting a Mg diffusion-based healing mechanism. The healing behaviour was maintained after a second thermal cycle, confirming the alloy’s re-healability. Under combined heat and pressure, the healing efficiency increased drastically, allowing full closure of voids up to at least 100 µm. These findings demonstrate that Almazium® combines high mechanical strength with intrinsic, replicable healing ability.

title: Additive manufacturing of patient–specific lattice prosthetic sockets via field–driven design and elastic–plastic homogenization
abstract: The development of patient-specific prosthetic sockets requires the integration of clinical data with advanced design methodologies to ensure both comfort and mechanical reliability. In this work, we propose a digital workflow combining 3D scanning of the residual limb, anatomical reconstruction, and computational design. The approach integrates elastic–plastic homogenization with a Field-Driven Design (FDD) strategy, where stress fields obtained from finite element analysis are mapped to spatially varying lattice properties and geometries. This approach enables a direct stress-to-structure transition for the design of lightweight, graded lattice sockets. The methodology is applied to a personalized socket manufactured via Multi Jet Fusion in PA12. Numerical simulations and experimental testing of a full-scale prototype demonstrate a weight reduction of up to 25% compared to a solid design, while maintaining a robust safety factor. Computed tomography analysis confirms good agreement between the as designed and as-built geometries. The proposed framework highlights the potential of integrating clinical data and Field-Driven lattice Design for next-generation and personalized prosthetic devices.

title: Engineering oxide-structured niobium composites via atomic layer deposition and spark plasma sintering
abstract: The precise control of nanoscale oxide dispersions offers a promising route to improve the mechanical performance of refractory metal systems. This study employs an atomic layer deposition (ALD)-based approach to deposit conformal TiO 2 nanocoatings on pure niobium powder surfaces using a rotary reactor, followed by densification via spark plasma sintering (SPS). During SPS consolidation, amorphous TiO 2 shells undergo phase transformation and redistribution, yielding crystalline rutile TiO 2 nanoparticles (10–20 nm) and interfacial Nb–Ti–O composite oxide phases localized along grain boundaries. Multiscale characterization confirms the spatial segregation and microstructural distribution of these phases. The ALD-derived oxide dispersoids suppress grain growth and impede dislocation motion, increasing hardness by up to 43 % in oxide-rich regions, as measured through nanoindentation. This strengthening arises from grain-boundary pinning, particle–dislocation interactions, and interfacial oxide stabilization, with the formation of Nb–Ti–O composite phases playing a notable role alongside discrete TiO 2 dispersoids. This study presents a scalable, contamination-free surface engineering strategy for fabricating nanostructured Nb-based composites with refined microstructures and enhanced room-temperature mechanical response. The approach offers a viable processing platform for refractory metal systems, with potential extension to high-temperature structural applications pending future thermal aging and mechanical evaluation at elevated temperatures .

title: Reinforcement learning for inverse silhouette design and rapid laser cutting of compact parallelogram quad kirigami prototypes
abstract: Kirigami is an increasingly useful fabrication method to produce shape-programmable metamaterial structures. However, inverse design remains difficult because deployment is nonlinear, and feasible cut layouts must satisfy discrete compatibility rules, avoid overlap, and map one target shape to valid designs. We present RL-Kirigami, an inverse design framework that combines optimal-transport conditional flow matching (OT-CFM) with reinforcement learning to generate compatible ratio fields for compact reconfigurable parallelogram quad kirigami. A marching decoder enforces global geometric compatibility, and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) aligns the generator with nondifferentiable rewards for silhouette matching, feasibility, and ratio-field regularity. Across procedurally generated target shape instances, a single sample from the pretrained OT-CFM prior reached and outperformed solver baselines while reducing forward simulator evaluations from hundreds to . GRPO improved accuracy to and, with regularity included, reduced from to while maintaining . Generated layouts were exported to DXF and laser cut in polymeric sheets to produce deployable prototypes in minutes per part. These results support a manufacturing-aware inverse design workflow for deployable kirigami metamaterials under geometric feasibility constraints.

title: A timescale-based framework for predicting filament stability in direct ink writing
abstract: Direct ink writing (DIW) often fails not because inks cannot be extruded, but because filaments lose continuity after nozzle exit due to insufficient resistance to extensional deformation. Although shear rheology governs extrusion, shape retention, and post-shear recovery, it does not fully capture this post-extrusion instability. Here, we isolate this extensional bottleneck using a rheology-decoupled model system in which shear properties are held nearly constant while filament extensibility is tuned by adding trace amounts of hydrolyzed polyacrylamide (HPAA) to a Pluronic F127 matrix. Despite nearly identical yield stress, shear-thinning behavior, viscoelastic moduli, and post-shear recovery, the formulations exhibit large differences in extensional response. By combining direct-writing experiments with capillary breakup extensional rheometry, we establish a predictive framework that links material response to processing conditions through two dimensionless parameters: the Deborah number, D e = λ / τ F , which characterizes the persistence of elastic stresses, and a process-imposed stretching parameter, Π = d v H / Q , which quantifies the kinematic deformation during deposition. The stability of the filament is organized within a stability map in the ( D e , Π ) space. For practical implementation, we show that die swell at the exit of the nozzle correlates with D e under fixed conditions, providing a simple proxy for locating a formulation within the stability map. Validation with independent formulations and benchmark printing tests demonstrates an accurate prediction of stable, transitional, and unstable regimes.

title: A polysaccharide-based composite wound dressing containing mafenide-loaded microparticles inspired by the ionic interaction: in vitro and in vivo study
abstract: Microbial infection is a major challenge in burn wounds, and mafenide is one of the best choices for its treatment. However, its clinical use is limited due to the rapid absorption from burn sites, poor preservation in avascular areas, and fast release. To address these issues, we prepared mafenide-loaded PCL/chitosan microparticles (MPM) by a double-emulsion method and incorporated them into an alginate-based wound dressing (AlgWD). In an innovative design, chitosan and alginate were added to the internal aqueous phase (W1) and the external aqueous phase (W2), respectively, to promote rapid ionic interactions between oppositely charged species during microparticle formation. The considered formulations were evaluated in vitro and in vivo. The microparticles were spherical with smooth surfaces. Both AlgWD films, especially AlgWD containing MPM, showed extended mafenide release and no cytotoxicity. The optimized AlgWD plus MPM containing 30% mafenide demonstrated strong antibacterial activity. In an infected burn wound model, this formulation produced the best epithelialization, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis, and its antibacterial effect was confirmed in vivo. Overall, the developed composite dressing appears to be a promising candidate for burn wound management through promoting drug delivery, antimicrobial efficacy, and tissue regeneration

title: Dissolving microneedles co-delivering indocyanine green and SR-717 for sonodynamic therapy combining STING activation in anti-tumor immunotherapy
abstract: STING agonists show great potential in cancer immunotherapy by stimulating both innate and adaptive immune pathways. However, targeted delivery of STING agonists to tumor tissues remains a critical challenge that limits their therapeutic performance. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT), a non-invasive treatment approach with strong tissue penetration, can not only directly destroy tumor cells but also induce immunogenic cell death (ICD), thereby enhancing anti-tumor immunity. To enable precise co-delivery of a sonosensitizer and a STING agonist, a dissolving microneedle (DMN) patch co-loaded with indocyanine green (ICG) and SR-717 (denoted as ICG&SR@DMNs) was developed. This biodegradable microneedle system, fabricated using a biodegradable polymer matrix, enables localized drug enrichment and controlled release through transdermal delivery. Under ultrasound irradiation, ICG-mediated SDT induces ICD in tumor cells, resulting in the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that facilitate dendritic cell (DC) maturation. At the same time, the released SR-717 activates the cGAS-STING pathway, further promoting DC function and enhancing T-cell infiltration. Experimental results confirm that this microneedle system effectively inhibits tumor growth and metastasis while initiating a strong systemic immune response. This study presents a novel delivery strategy for combining sonodynamic therapy with STING activation, offering strong potential for advancing cancer immunotherapy.

title: NIR-II fluorescence imaging of bone using synergistic targeting nanoprobes for precise diagnosis of skeletal disorders
abstract: Early diagnosis of bone-related diseases remains a critical clinical challenge, attributable to persistent limitations in imaging accuracy and safety. While near-infrared Region II (NIR-II) imaging confers substantial advantages for deep-tissue visualization, its clinical translation is hampered by the inadequate targeting specificity of conventional contrast agents. Here, we developed Au-Ag@Apo-Tf/3-Az (AA@TFN), a synergistic targeting gold–silver nanocluster probe engineered with glutathione and azide functionalities, which achieved bone-specific enrichment via a hierarchical three-level targeting mechanism. AA@TFN first anchored to hydroxyapatite in the bone matrix through glutathione carboxyl-mediated chelation, then targeted transferrin receptors highly expressed in bone marrow, and finally endured macrophage-mediated uptake facilitated by azide-enhanced bone affinity. A synergistic targeting strategy enabled real-time, high-resolution NIR-II imaging across the complete skeleton, with enhanced probe enrichment at lesion sites driven by microenvironmental changes. AA@TFN enabled visualization of synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis models and millimeter‑scale microlesions in multiple myeloma models. Furthermore, the probe exhibited excellent biocompatibility and favorable safety profiles, underscoring its strong translational potential. A versatile platform was established for the diagnosis of bone diseases and non-invasive monitoring of therapeutic efficacy.

title: Advancing laser powder bed fusion of metals via tailored laser beam shaping: A critical review
abstract: Laser beam shaping is increasingly explored to enhance Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Metals (PBF-LB/M) by controlling the spatial energy distribution within the laser spot. While conventional Gaussian beams remain widely used in commercial systems, their concentrated energy input can promote steep thermal gradients and localized overheating, which may restrict process stability, productivity, and part quality. This review critically synthesizes recent progress in laser beam shaping for PBF-LB/M, with emphasis on work from 2020 to early 2026. Compared with earlier reviews that mainly focused on optical implementation or broader laser–material processing concepts, this review integrates beam-shape generation with melt-pool dynamics, defect formation, surface quality, microstructural evolution, mechanical response, productivity, and emerging shape-aware process descriptors. The discussion shows how profiles such as core–ring, ring-dominant, top-hat, and elliptical beams can broaden stable process windows, suppress spatter and keyhole porosity, and promote more uniform thermal histories, with implications for surface quality, mechanical isotropy, and build efficiency. Modeling and simulation studies are also summarized to clarify the coupled heat-fluid–solid interactions controlling melt-pool behavior, thermal gradients, and solidification kinetics. Furthermore, major implementation challenges such as optical integration, energy-delivery stability, process reproducibility, and the lack of standardized beam descriptors are summarized. The review concludes by outlining emerging research directions aimed at enabling practical, reliable, and industrial-scale adoption of beam-shaping technologies in additive manufacturing.

title: Compositional tuning of structural, photothermal and optical properties of La-based high-entropy perovskite oxides
abstract: In this study, 14 lanthanum-based high-entropy perovskite oxides (HEPOs) with equimolar mixtures of transition metals (Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn) at the B-site were synthesized to investigate how multi-elemental interactions govern their structural and optical properties. Most compositions form single-phase perovskites after annealing at 1200 °C, as confirmed by XRD and Rietveld refinement. SEM and EDS reveal homogeneous elemental distributions with particle sizes tunable from < 250 nm to > 2 µm depending on composition. UV–Vis-NIR spectrometry shows broad absorption without a distinct measurable onset, while the electronic structure remains robust across the series. Ionisation potentials shift by up to 0.55 eV with cationic composition, demonstrating systematic compositional tuning of the occupied band (analogous to the valence band maximum). Photoluminescence measurements indicate thermally driven emission resembling broadband thermal radiation, consistent with a strong photothermal response in these materials. These results highlight high-entropy perovskite oxides as a versatile platform for engineering structural disorder, electronic energy-level alignment, and photothermal behavior, opening pathways toward oxide-based broadband infrared emission and high-temperature photothermal applications.

title: Phase-resolved plasticity and interfacial strength govern ductility in TiB2-reinforced steels
abstract: Ceramic-reinforced metal-matrix composites fail through complex interplay of matrix hardening ability, particle fracture, and interfacial debonding. We isolate how duplex-matrix fraction affects this coupling using a steelmaking-compatible model system: TiB 2 -reinforced high-modulus steels with comparable TiB 2 size/spacing statistics but varied austenite fractions. Quasi-in-situ tensile damage tracking, synchrotron X-ray diffraction, and redesigned wedge micromechanical tests were combined with a calibrated finite-element framework to quantify phase hardening, particle fracture, and phase-specific interfacial debonding. The model integrates phase-specific Kocks-Mecking hardening, cohesive-zone interfaces, and a Griffith-type size-dependent TiB 2 fracture criterion, reproducing both the macroscopic stress–strain response and the evolving damage-mode fractions. The results show that void nucleation consistently initiates by TiB 2 particle fracture, largely independent of matrix constitution. Crack propagation, however, depends on the competition between ductile-phase crack blunting and interfacial resistance. Increasing austenite improves plastic shielding and crack blunting, but also promotes TiB 2 /austenite debonding because this interface is weaker than the TiB 2 /ferrite interface. Consequently, strength–ductility performance varies non-monotonically with austenite fraction, with the best balance obtained at an intermediate duplex-matrix fraction. These findings highlight the need to jointly optimize matrix heterogeneity and interface in TiB 2 -reinforced steels.

title: A prediction approach for optimal interference-fit size of CFRP bolted joints under dynamic installation: Theory, numerical simulation, and experimental verification
abstract: This study employs a multi-scale experimental and theoretical approach to investigate the relationship between interference-fit size and structural response in CFRP bolted joints under dynamic installation driven by electromagnetic loading. A theoretical mechanical model for predicting the axial installation force under moderate interference-fit sizes is innovatively proposed, which captures the characteristic deformation of the “brush-like’’ hole-wall contact interface and enables accurate prediction of the joint’s mechanical behavior. A computational model capable of simulating the coupled intra-laminar and inter-laminar damage in CFRP laminates is further developed, providing insight into the initiation and progression of damage within the interference-fit region. Furthermore, dynamic installation experiments on CFRP bolted joints validate the theoretical and simulation models via axial installation force, with damage morphology in the interference-fit region further verifying the simulation model’s applicability. Results show that interference-fit sizes of 0.5% and 0.9% cause only slight localized damage to the CFRP hole wall, while larger sizes (1.3%, 1.7%, 2.1%) lead to severe damage of varying degrees. Compared with 0.5%, the 0.9% interference-fit size more effectively enhances joint performance. Thus, a 0.9% interference-fit size is optimal for Φ6.32 mm high-lock bolted CFRP joints under dynamic installation driven by electromagnetic loading.

title: Additive manufacturing of pure tungsten via electron beam powder bed fusion: Toward fusion-ready fabrication
abstract: Tungsten and its alloys are leading materials for plasma-facing components (PFCs) in thermonuclear fusion reactors, valued for their superior resistance to extreme conditions. The geometric complexity and extreme operating conditions of fusion PFCs, however, demand manufacturing capabilities beyond conventional powder metallurgy. Laser-based additive manufacturing, such as laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF), has been extensively explored but continues to face persistent challenges, including insufficient densification, multi-modal cracking driven by tungsten’s high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature, and impurity-induced grain boundary embrittlement. Electron beam powder bed fusion (E-PBF) has emerged as a transformative alternative. Its deep‑vacuum environment, near‑inertia‑free beam deflection, and layer‑by‑layer pre-heating capability maintain powder‑bed temperatures exceeding 1000 °C throughout the build while minimizing impurity contamination, thereby suppressing the predominant failure mechanisms. Recent studies have demonstrated ultra-dense ( ≥ 99.9%), crack-free tungsten with competitive mechanical properties, and resistance to extreme thermal and radiative conditions. This paper provides a timely review of advances in tungsten processing via E‑PBF in chronological order, covering processing fundamentals, resulting macro- and microstructures, non-irradiation and irradiation performance, and fusion‑grade component fabrication. Key challenges, including process reproducibility, microstructural anisotropy, post‑processing damage, and qualification pathways, are evaluated, and five pillars are outlined to support broader adoption and democratization of E‑PBF tungsten production.

title: Revealing the temperature-dependent cyclic plasticity and failure mechanisms in GH4169 nickel-based superalloy
abstract: s. The low-cycle fatigue behavior and associated microstructural evolution of GH4169 nickel-based superalloy were systematically investigated at elevated temperatures. The macroscopic cyclic results show a relatively stable cyclic response, with neither significant cyclic hardening/softening nor an obvious Bauschinger effect. However, the fatigue resistance degrades substantially at temperatures above approximately 650 °C. Microstructural characterization reveals that cyclic strain localization originates at high-angle grain boundaries and progressively penetrates into grain interiors. Concurrently, the frequency of low-angle grain boundaries increases continuously, while twin boundaries gradually deteriorate during cyclic deformation. Elevated temperature further promotes δ phase coarsening and the formation of precipitate-depleted zones. TEM analysis reveals that cyclic plasticity is dominated by dislocation rearrangement and dislocation-precipitate interactions. Fatigue cracks preferentially nucleate at free surfaces and grain-boundary regions, and then propagate mainly along high-angle grain boundaries. By contrast, twin boundaries effectively impede crack growth by inducing crack deflection.

title: Microwave-assisted two-step sintering of Gd2Ti2O7–TiO2 composites for enhanced thermal and mechanical stability
abstract: Burnable absorber (BA) pellet candidates for boron-free small modular reactors require high density, microstructural stability, and efficient heat dissipation, yet suitable oxide-based candidates remain limited. A two-phase oxide composite (20 mol% Gd 2 O 3 –80 mol% TiO 2 ) was sintered at 1300–1400 °C, yielding Gd 2 Ti 2 O 7 and rutile TiO 2 as equilibrium phases. Kinetic analysis yielded a densification activation energy of 95.3 kJ·mol −1 and grain-growth activation energies of 184.1 and 592.9 kJ·mol −1 for Gd 2 Ti 2 O 7 and TiO 2 , respectively. Two-step sintering (TSS) suppressed abnormal grain growth, yet densification remained insufficient. Microwave-assisted two-step sintering (MTSS) was subsequently introduced, achieving a relative density of 97.41%, a grain size of 1.49 µm, and a Vickers hardness of 9.2 GPa through accelerated densification and improved microstructural uniformity. Thermal conductivity was improved by 19.54% at 100 °C, primarily owing to reduced pore-induced thermal resistance. These findings demonstrate that MTSS offers a promising sintering route for oxide-based BA pellet candidates, with favorable microstructural stability and thermal performance.

title: AI-driven predictive and inverse design framework for defect engineering in hexagonal boron nitride monolayers
abstract: Nanostructured hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) exhibits exceptional mechanical properties; however, its performance is strongly influenced by the unavoidable presence of structural defects. Accurate prediction and targeted engineering of defect-induced properties remain challenging, particularly for complex mixed-defect configurations. In this study, an integrated AI-driven framework is developed for both predictive modeling and inverse design of defective h-BN monolayers. The framework combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for data generation, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for property prediction, and transfer learning to extend predictive capability to mixed-defect systems. Additionally, a data-driven inverse design module is introduced to generate optimal defect configurations with desired mechanical properties. The proposed models achieve mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 13.21 GPa and 3.81 GPa for Young’s modulus and ultimate tensile strength, respectively, with the best-performing transfer learning model demonstrating improved accuracy for mixed-defect configurations. Furthermore, the inverse design module is validated through statistical analysis, showing strong agreement with MD simulation results. Overall, the developed framework provides an efficient surrogate model for accelerated materials design, significantly reducing computational cost while enabling tunable property optimization, with potential applications beyond structural materials.

title: Atomistic insight into short-range order strengthening of TiZrVNb high-entropy alloys
abstract: Chemical short-range order (SRO) critically tailors the mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys (HEAs). However, experimentally characterizing the dynamic evolution of SRO remains challenging, while traditional computations struggle with high costs or limited accuracy. To overcome these barriers, we develop a high-fidelity machine learning potential for the lightweight refractory TiZrVNb HEA using the neuroevolution potential framework, achieving density functional theory (DFT)-level accuracy for large-scale simulations. Using hybrid molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations, we reveal that SRO formation is energetically favored and induces a unique pseudo-composite microstructure. This chemical heterogeneity divides the lattice into body-center-cubic-preferred (BCCP) clusters and hexagonal-close-packed-preferred (HCPP) clusters. Thermodynamically driven by HCPP clusters, localized HCP precursors form spontaneously prior to deformation. While both BCCP and HCPP clusters function as intrinsic hard fillers to enhance strength, the pre-existing HCP precursors maintain ductility by gradually growing during a continuous strain-induced phase transformation. Consequently, the SRO configuration achieves an average increase of approximately 55% in ultimate tensile strength relative to the random state, without compromising ductility. Beyond providing an efficient framework for large-scale simulations of refractory HEAs, this study elucidates the atomic origin of the strength-ductility synergy in TiZrVNb, offering a promising strategy for alloy design via precise SRO manipulation.

title: Exploratory mapping of processing-property relationships in mycelium biocomposites using interpretable machine learning
abstract: Mycelium biocomposites are promising low-carbon materials for insulation and lightweight building components, but their reported properties vary widely because fungal species, substrates, density, post-processing, and testing protocols differ across studies. This paper presents an exploratory meta-dataset analysis of processing-property relationships in mycelium biocomposites. A curated dataset of 331 quantitative observations from 47 empirical studies was analysed using Ashby material selection plots, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Random Forest Feature Importance (FI), and Partial Dependence Plots (PDP) analysis. This study presents a screening framework that combines Ashby plots with interpretable machine-learning summaries to compare literature-reported property envelopes, identify preliminary material applications and candidate property-improvement routes. Data heterogeneity is notable. Random forest validation showed stronger performance for thermal conductivity ( , Root Mean Square Error (RMSE)=0.014, Mean Absolute Error (MAE)=0.011) than for compressive strength ( , RMSE = 0.978, MAE = 0.446) and flexural strength ( , RMSE = 1.223, MAE = 0.628), reflecting limited cross-study predictability. The results suggest that density and pressing conditions are repeatedly associated with mechanical performance, while biological descriptors (e.g. fungal species) should be interpreted with substrate and processing choices. The framework is exploratory rather than prescriptive and supports future standardised testing.

title: Chitosan-coated zeolites as a promising platform for sodium risedronate adsorption
abstract: In this work, we report the synthesis and evaluation of chitosan-coated zeolites as adsorptive platforms for the delivery of sodium risedronate. Chitosan was selected due to its pH-responsive behaviour and inherent biocompatibility, serving both as a surface functional layer and as a regulator of drug–surface interactions. Comprehensive physicochemical characterisation (XRD, XRF, SEM/EDS, BET, zeta potential) confirmed successful surface functionalisation without significant loss of zeolite crystallinity. Cytotoxicity studies demonstrated that native zeolites significantly reduced cell viability, whereas chitosan-modified materials remained non-cytotoxic, confirming the beneficial role of polymer functionalisation. Adsorption studies revealed heterogeneous and multilayer adsorption behaviour, with calcium-exchanged chitosan-modified zeolites exhibiting the highest adsorption performance under optimised conditions. Mechanistic analysis indicated that adsorption was primarily governed by weak non-covalent interactions and was strongly influenced by pH-dependent electrostatic attraction between deprotonated phosphonate groups of risedronate and protonated amine groups of chitosan. Additional stability studies demonstrated partial framework-related ion release under acidic conditions while preserving the overall crystalline structure of the materials. Overall, the results highlight the potential of chitosan-functionalised zeolites as multifunctional platforms for pH-responsive bisphosphonate adsorption and future biomedical delivery applications.

title: PVD duplex treatment of AISI M2 high-speed steel additively manufactured by metal binder jetting
abstract: Among additive manufacturing techniques, metal binder jetting (MBJ) offers high build rates and cost-efficient manufacturing, making it attractive for large-scale production of tooling components. However, MBJ produced AISI M2 high-speed steel exhibits a distinct microstructure compared with conventionally manufactured material, and its influence on physical vapor deposion (PVD) duplex treatments has not yet been systematically investigated. Therefore, the effect of the manufacturing route on plasma nitriding and subsequent TiAlN deposition is evaluated by comparing MBJ produced and conventionally manufactured steel variants. Both steels are plasma nitrided at 420 °C for 4 h and subsequently coated with TiAlN using cathodic arc evaporation. Plasma nitriding results in nitrogen supersaturation of the martensitic matrix, producing a diffusion depth of 20 µm and pronounced surface hardening in both steels. TiAlN thin films exhibit comparable hardness (32–34 GPa) and dense morphologies independent of the substrate condition. While plasma nitriding slightly increases the coefficient of friction up to 6%, it significantly reduces the wear rate up to 29% of the TiAlN-coated MBJ produced steel variant. Overall, MBJ produced AISI M2 showed a plasma nitriding response comparable to conventional steel, demonstrating that established PVD duplex treatments can be successfully transferred to additively manufactured tool steels.

title: A synergistic Ce-Se nanozyme hydrogel activates the AMPK-Sirt3 axis establishing antioxidant defense for diabetic wound regeneration
abstract: The collapse of the endogenous antioxidant enzyme cascade constitutes the primary barrier preventing the healing of diabetic foot ulcers. Herein, we engineered a bio-instructive hydrogel, CSPC constructed from polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and carboxymethyl chitosan (CMS) crosslinked via dynamic borate ester bonds, allowing a dynamic hydrogel network for adaptive wound adhesion and pH-triggered therapeutic release. This intelligent matrix contained ultrasmall selenium within a mesoporous silica shell decorated with redox-switchable cerium species (Ce-Se@SiO 2 ). Ce-Se@SiO 2 not only mitigates selenium toxicity via controlled release but also drives a self-sustaining enzymatic cascade that mimics the SOD, CAT, and GPx activities. Additionally, we demonstrated that external ROS scavenging by CSPC was associated with the restoration of redox-sensitive mitochondrial antioxidant signaling. Specifically, CSPC reactivated the AMPK/PGC-1α/Sirt3 axis, promoted the deacetylation of mitochondrial SOD2, and thereby restored endogenous antioxidant defense. In a diabetic rat model, this strategy significantly accelerated wound closure, promoted angiogenesis, and facilitated tissue remodeling. This study establishes a new paradigm for chronic wound management by bridging synthetic catalytic chemistry with cellular metabolic regulation.

title: Dual-targeted iRGD-functionalized, DPP4-responsive micelles carrying an isoQC inhibitor remodel the tumor microenvironment in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is difficult to treat due to a dense stromal barrier and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), driven in part by overexpression of isoQC and DPP4. IsoQC promotes CD47-SIRPα-mediated immune evasion, while DPP4 contributes to stromal remodeling and limits T-cell infiltration. Targeting either factor alone is insufficient. Here, we developed a dual-targeting nanoplatform, iRGD@ 4 , composed of iRGD-functionalized polymeric micelles loaded with a DPP4-responsive prodrug of an isoQC inhibitor. The system enables tumor-specific activation, as elevated DPP4 in PDAC cleaves the prodrug to release the active inhibitor locally. Nanoparticles showed uniform size (158.2 nm), good stability (−29.5 mV), and high drug loading (10.6%). In vitro, the prodrug was efficiently activated by DPP4, releasing an inhibitor with IC 50 of 0.68 μM. iRGD@ 4 enhanced cellular uptake and achieved Golgi localization. In vivo, it showed ∼10-fold higher tumor accumulation than free drug and significantly inhibited tumor growth. Mechanistically, it reduced pE-CD47 expression by 62.3%, increased macrophage infiltration, and reshaped cytokine profiles. The system exhibited good biocompatibility with minimal toxicity. Overall, iRGD@ 4 effectively overcomes stromal and immune barriers in PDAC through enzyme-activated, tumor-targeted dual modulation.

title: A living Nanosilver-Probiotic therapeutic orchestrate Wnt-driven barrier repair and microbiota normalization in TNBS-induced murine colitis model
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) results from dysregulated interactions among gut microbiota, mucosal immunity, and host genetics factors, ultimately leading to chronic inflammation and compromise of the epithelial barrier. Existing therapies remain inadequate for many patients, emphasizing the need for strategies that simultaneously target pathogens, maintain barrier integrity, and modulate host responses. Here, we engineer a living nanomaterial therapeutic by coupling the probiotic Bacillus licheniformis with in situ-grown 7-nm nanosilver to creat a probiotic-nanosilver composite and evaluated its efficacy in TNBS-induced murine colitis. In vivo, Nano-Ag-probiotic enhanced survival in a dose-dependent manner, attenuated weight loss and disease activity, and restored both colon length and histology architecture. Mechanistically, the treatment reinforced epithelial integrity by restoring physiological Wnt/β-catenin signaling, inhibiting GSK3β activation, and re-establishing tight-junction scaffolds including ZO-1, occludin, and claudins. These effects were accompanied by attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokine signaling and downregulation of CCR2, indicating reduced recruitment of inflammatory monocytes. 16S rRNA sequence analysis revealed that Nano-Ag-probiotic treatment restored microbial diversity, improved Firmicutes/Proteobacteria ratio, reduced Bacteroides and enriched SCFA-associated Dorea in TNBS-induced colitis. Collectively, these data demonstrate that the nanosilver composite rebalances the microbiota-barrier-immunity axis in experimental colitis and represents a translationally promising platform for managing infection-exacerbated intestinal inflammation.

title: TRANSFORM: A modular variational framework for multifunctional and transforming materials—Metamaterials, electrically- and light-activated systems
abstract: We present TRANSFORM (Thermodynamically Rigorous and Adaptive Nonlinear Simulation Framework for Ordered Responsive Materials), a modular continuum framework that unifies variational modelling of multifunctional and transforming materials. The framework is demonstrated for four material classes: acoustic/elastic metamaterials, dielectric elastomers, photo-active liquid-crystal elastomers, and origami/morphing structures. Each class is formulated as a special case of one dissipative variational kernel, in which mechanical, electrical, photo-chemical, and metamaterial contributions share a common free-energy structure. Electromechanical and photo-mechanical coupling stresses are obtained by variational differentiation of the same energy density, avoiding double-counting of Maxwell stress. We do not claim to introduce finite-strain electroelasticity, Gent dielectric-elastomer models, azobenzene photo-kinetics, homogenisation, phase-field methods, or origami kinematics. Instead, the contribution is their integration in a thermodynamically consistent architecture with shared coupling, solver, and adjoint structure. Across eleven representative benchmarks, the calibrated framework reproduces published data with an average relative error of . These benchmarks demonstrate consistency after calibration rather than independent predictive validation. Illustrative applications to soft robotics, flexible energy devices, and biomechanics are also presented.

title: J-PINN: A domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network framework for kinematic field reconstruction in fracture mechanics
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) solve inverse problems, yet standard formulations fail to resolve the discontinuous fields inherent to fracture mechanics. This study introduces a novel, meshless Multi-Region PINN framework for 2D cracked elastic bodies. By decomposing the domain via strict kinematic constraints, the method restores the validity of the Navier–Cauchy equations within each partition. Validated against FEM, the framework accurately captures stress singularities using sparse boundary data, achieving relative errors below 1% for displacements and 2–4% for strain and stresses. Furthermore, a thermodynamic error-compensation strategy is proposed to correct systematic -integral drift, yielding path-independent strain energy release rate (SERR) estimates. Demonstrating utility for material characterization, the method is applied to experimental Digital Image Correlation (DIC) data from a Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) Double Cantilever Beam. Here, the PINN acts as a physics-informed reconstructor, recovering smooth singular fields from noisy inputs via a robust Huber loss and a physics-driven iterative outlier removal strategy. The calculated SERR ( ) shows strong agreement with analytical Modified Beam Theory (MBT), establishing a robust, assumption-free characterization methodology for interlaminar fracture toughness in fiber-reinforced composites and enabling data-driven extraction of cohesive zone parameters as faithful inputs for composite structural design.

title: Heterostructure design and strengthening of TC11 alloy based on interfacial β phase
abstract: Rational microstructure design is critical for achieving the excellent comprehensive properties in metallic materials. In this work, we optimized the strength-ductility balance of the quenched TC11 alloy by engineering a heterostructure through tailoring the β phase at the α p /β t interface. The formation of this phase was governed by the redistribution of β-stabilizing element Mo, which was strengthened by pre-deformation solution treatment. The high-density dislocations introduced by deformation significantly promoted Mo enrichment at the α p /β t interfaces. Therefore, the high-temperature β phase could be effectively stabilized and retained up to room temperature, becoming the interfacial β phase. During the aging treatment, this phase partially precipitated 10 nm-scaled α lamellae, which constitute a heterostructure together with submicron-scaled α lamellae formed from martensite decomposition and coarsening. Based on the fine-grain strengthening and heterogeneous deformation induced strengthening, this heterostructured alloy successfully achieved an ultrahigh strength of ∼1429 MPa, comparable to that of martensite alloys. Meanwhile, a superior ductility of ∼9.7 % was maintained and this significantly surpassed that of the latter.

title: MXene-integrated hydrogel with photothermal effects promotes diabetic wound healing via angiogenesis and infection control
abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds present a significant clinical challenge due to their complex pathophysiology, which includes impaired healing, persistent infections, and uncontrolled oxidative stress. To counter these challenges, we engineered a multifunctional hydrogel (denoted as PQM) composed of polyacrylamide (PAM), quaternary chitosan (QCS), and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene (abbreviated as MXene) nanosheets synthesized via radical polymerization. This resulting MXene-reinforced hydrogel features a porous architecture that confers superior swelling capacity, controlled degradation, robust mechanical strength, and injectable self-healing properties. The incorporation of MXenes provides notable antioxidant capabilities, a photothermal response to near-infrared light, and extensive antibacterial effects against E. coli , S. aureus , and methicillin-resistant S. aureus . In vitro analyses have demonstrated the hydrogel’s biocompatibility and capacity to enhance fibroblast migration, endothelial cell angiogenesis, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging. In diabetic murine models, the use of a PQM hydrogel with NIR irradiation sped up wound healing by 78.8% in six days, improved collagen deposition, and shifted macrophage polarization to an anti-inflammatory profile. Histological and immunohistochemical evaluations demonstrated enhanced re-epithelialization, neovascularization (CD31 + ), and proliferative activity (Ki67 + ). By facilitating rapid hemostasis, suppressing infection, and promoting tissue regeneration, the PQM hydrogel offers a comprehensive and clinically translatable strategy for managing the multifactorial impairments that hinder diabetic wound healing

title: Corrigendum to “Oxidation-controlled creep response of miniaturized Waspaloy specimens in a hydrogen-containing atmosphere” [Mater. Des. 265 (2026) 116020]
Coaxial electrospinning of continuous PVDF/Bi2O3/CeO2 nanofibre yarns with lead-equivalent X-ray attenuation for radiation-protective healthcare textiles
abstract: Lead-based protective garments weighing 2–7 kg impose a musculoskeletal burden on interventional radiology staff. Currently developed alternative shielding materials focus on enabling lightweight, textile-compatible protection; however, no lead-substitute material has yet been produced in a continuous yarn form. This study investigates electrospun yarn production via coaxial and conjugate-polarity configurations. Membrane casting was first used to establish the maximum filler loading at which PVDF and the bismuth/cerium oxides form a homogeneous, electrospinnable solution; loadings up to 90 wt% were achieved, substantially exceeding the practical limits of single-fluid electrospinning. A DMSO/acetone solvent system replaced toxic DMF while promoting a high β-phase content in the PVDF matrix. In the resulting core-sheath yarns, the core Bi 2 O 3 /CeO 2 provides shielding capacity while the PVDF sheath maintains mechanical strength. The composite membrane reached 48.7% X-ray attenuation at 80 kV. This nearly matches the commercial 0.2 mm lead film reference (47.8%). Transferred to the yarn format, the highest-loading yarn (90 wt%) reached an effective linear attenuation coefficient of 0.766 mm⁻ 1 , exceeding that of the membrane and demonstrating that shielding efficiency is retained in a continuous yarn.

title: Solute segregation and crack sensitivity in niobium-containing steel: mediated by atomic scale local structural transformation
abstract: As the core material of boiler tubes for supercritical units, the application of S30432 is subject to the problem of coarse niobium precipitation cracking caused by niobium segregation during continuous casting. This study provides an evaluation method for judging the segregation tendency of solute elements from the atomic scale. By establishing an atomic scale solidification model with the same proportion as the composition of niobium-containing steel, the stability of the atomic velocity autocorrelation function (VACF) curve is proposed as the main judgment basis for evaluating the segregation behavior of solute elements. It is found that rapid cooling promotes the formation of a highly coordinated structure, resulting in the blocking of Nb atom dynamics, triggering a non-gradient change in the VACF of the system, and achieving the solute trapping effect. In-situ solidification characterization and phase-field simulations confirm that higher cooling rates effectively suppress Nb grain boundary segregation. Rapid nucleation induces grid-like local lattice distortion, homogenizing strain at matrix-precipitate interfaces and lowering crack susceptibility. This work provides an atomic-scale insight into solute segregation during multicomponent alloy solidification and offers theoretical guidance for alloy composition design and process optimization in industrial production.

title: Multilayer jamming-reinforced inflatable systems for rapidly deployable lightweight construction
abstract: Variable stiffness concepts enable structural adaptation through smart materials with inherent stiffness variation or innovative configuration-based designs using conventional materials. Among these, multilayer jamming (MLJ) provides rapid, reversible, and controllable stiffness modulation via vacuum-induced interlayer friction. This study proposes an MLJ-reinforced inflatable system for adaptive stiffening and enhanced energy dissipation in rapidly deployable lightweight structures. First, the influence of layer stiffness on MLJ performance is examined, identifying a suitable stiffness range for efficient reinforcement and providing guidance for material selection. A meter-scale prototype combining MLJ plates and inflatable airbeam is then experimentally investigated under varying vacuum pressures, layer configurations, and loading conditions. The results show that vacuum activation significantly enhances stiffness and stabilizes the structure against collapse under reduced internal pressure. Quasi-static cyclic tests demonstrate that a 10 kPa vacuum condition achieves the best balance between stiffness enhancement, stable yielding, and energy dissipation, with dissipated energy increasing by 32–44% and ultimate load capacity by up to 38%. A simplified analytical model is developed to interpret stiffness evolution and the interaction between MLJ sliding and structural response. This work establishes MLJ as a scalable and designable material system for adaptive composite structures, with potential applications in construction, aerospace, and robotics.

title: High efficiency respiratory rate monitoring fiber optic sensing probe based on chitosan moisture sensitive film and temperature drift compensation method
abstract: Leveraging the advantages of Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) fiber sensors and chitosan humidity-sensitive materials, this study proposes and validates a high-performance humidity-sensitive fiber probe. Structural parameters of the chitosan-coated FPI fiber sensor were experimentally optimized, demonstrating that a hollow-core fiber (HCF) length of 104 μm and chitosan film thickness of 7 μm achieve a sensitivity of 0.6198 nm/%RH during 20%-70% RH. The maximum humidity sensitivity of 1.0132 nm/%RH was observed in the subrange of 45%-70% RH. The sensor exhibits rapid humidity response time of 547 ms and recovery time of 578 ms, enabling real-time environmental humidity monitoring. Its potential for human motion tracking was verified through respiratory experiments at varying frequencies. To address Internet of Things (IoT) requirements for simultaneous environmental monitoring, an integrated dual-parameter sensor was designed using cascaded temperature-humidity sensing units and a decoupling algorithm, achieving concurrent temperature-humidity detection.

title: Integrated CALPHAD and machine learning approach for the design of high-strength Sn-In-based low-temperature solders
abstract: The demand for reliable low-temperature solders is increasing with the development of flexible electronics. Eutectic Sn–In alloys are promising candidates due to their low melting temperature (118 °C); however, their relatively low mechanical strength limits broader applications. In this work, a data-driven framework with Gaussian kernel ridge regression (GKRR) integrating CALPHAD approach is developed for design of Sn–In–X alloys (X = Cu, Ag, Zn, Bi, Sb, Al, Ni). The GKRR model demonstrates good predictive capability, with a five-fold cross-validation R 2 of 0.78 and RMSE of 6.95 HV, and a testing R 2 of 0.91 with RMSE of 3.97 HV. Based on the integrated strategy, a new alloy, Sn–47In–1.59Ag–0.27Cu, was designed and experimentally validated. The designed alloy exhibits a Vickers hardness of 13.44 HV, approximately twice that of eutectic Sn–52In, and an ultimate tensile strength of 26.6 ± 0.8 MPa, representing an approximately threefold improvement while maintaining a reasonable elongation of 21.9 ± 1.4%. Microstructural characterization and thermodynamic analysis confirmed the formation of β-In 3 Sn, γ-InSn 4 , and (Ag, Cu)(In, Sn) 2 phases, with a melting point of 130.56 °C. These results demonstrate that the integration of machine learning and CALPHAD method provides an effective approach for accelerating the design of low-temperature Sn-In solders

title: Cost- and process-efficient conductive composites as electrodes for dielectric elastomer devices and their electromechanical analysis
abstract: High-performance dielectric elastomer (DE) devices necessitate synergistic optimization of electrode conductivity, mechanical compliance, and practical manufacturability. However, conventional studies often report material metrics in isolation without linking them to device-level requirements. This gap leaves electrode selection largely empirical and makes quantitative comparison of electrode materials across different actuator configurations difficult. To address this issue, we use a simplified electromechanical model as a screening tool that incorporates electrode stiffness and geometry, enabling quick assessment of electrode-induced performance variations in DEAs. In addition, we present a practically oriented conductive composite ink based on commercially available carbon nanotube (CNT) and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), designed to provide a cost- and process-efficient electrode solution for multilayer DEAs. Electrical resistivity, elastic properties, strain-dependent resistance, and printability-related viscosity of CNT–PDMS inks containing 0.5–3 wt% CNT are systematically characterized. The proposed model reveals that, once the target operating frequency is satisfied, minimizing CNT loading is critical for reducing electrode-induced stiffening and maximizing actuator performance. Multilayer dielectric elastomer actuators are then fabricated and evaluated through static voltage–stretch characterization and dynamic response tests. The measured actuator performance agrees well with model predictions derived from the experimentally determined electrode properties, validating the proposed framework.

title: Cyclic temperature-dependent response of unit cell auxetic structures in an additively manufactured shape memory alloy
abstract: This study investigates the mechanical response of additively manufactured NiTi sinusoidal hexagonal re-entrant auxetic structures, focusing on the combined influence of temperature and local geometry. The NiTi alloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) was thermomechanically characterised to identify conditions promoting enhanced superelastic response, while X-ray micro-computed tomography was used to assess internal porosity. Monotonic and strain-controlled cyclic tensile tests were performed on auxetic cells with three different fillet radii, using a dedicated setup combining digital image correlation and closed-loop temperature control. The results reveal a clear separation between material- and geometry-driven effects. Temperature primarily governs the load levels through the superelastic response of the alloy, whereas auxetic deformation behaviour and failure mechanisms are mainly controlled by the structural geometry, particularly the fillet radius. Increasing the fillet radius significantly affects the deformation and failure response of the auxetic structures, altering the relationship between failure strain and absolute displacement through the corresponding change in cell geometry. The experimentally measured Poisson's ratio was compared with predictions from analytical models. Although these overestimate the auxetic response, they provide a reasonable first-order estimate. These findings provide insight into the design of additively manufactured NiTi auxetic architectures.

title: High-throughput characterization of the effect of quenching rate and dispersoid type on precipitation kinetics in two Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloys
abstract: A high-throughput investigation has been conducted on two Al–Zn–Mg–Cu alloys with a different dispersoid population (Cr or Zr based) to study the influence of quenching rate on precipitation kinetics. We developed a modified Jominy specimen to vary the quench rate down to 1 K.s −1 . Across the obtained continuous range of quench rates, microstructure was evaluated using space and time-resolved small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), allowing to map the post-quench precipitation kinetics as a function of quench rate. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that Cr-containing dispersoids systematically trigger heterogeneous η-phase precipitation, while Zr-containing dispersoids remain inactive unless recrystallization induces loss of coherency. A critical cooling rate of 30 K.s −1 has been identified from the SAXS data, below which large precipitation-free zones develop and the volume fraction of strengthening precipitates decreases. These quench-induced precipitates modify the precipitation kinetics during natural and artificial ageing, both in terms of volume fraction, average size and precipitate size distribution. The resulting loss of hardness scales at first order with the square root of the precipitate volume fraction, indicating that the reduction in the fraction of homogeneous precipitates dominates over changes in size or spatial distribution.

title: Nanostructure-controlled thermal and acoustic performance in poly(lactic acid) (PLA) aerogels containing clay and graphene-based nanofillers
abstract: Different nanofillers: nanoclays (NC), halloysite nanotubes (HNT), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNP), were added into poly(lactic acid) (PLA) aerogels, and the relationship between the microstructure and mechanical, thermal, and acoustic properties were established. The addition of these fillers resulted in a density increase (25 %) in comparison to pure PLA aerogels, primarily due to higher shrinkage, while maintaining high crystallinity (>59 %). The microstructure was notably influenced by nanoparticle nature, size, and dispersion, leading to variations that significantly affected their final properties. Composites containing GNP exhibited the highest mechanical stiffness, with raw elastic moduli reaching 10.2 MPa (18 % absolute increase with respect to the reference), and also presented the lowest thermal conductivity, down to 26.5 mW/m∙K. The acoustic-absorption performance was investigated for the first time. Raw PLA aerogels showed Helmholtz resonator-like behavior, while the composites showed an improved efficiency in sound absorption over a wide frequency range (500–6500 Hz). Specifically, those doped with NC provided the greatest improvement in sound absorption, highlighting their strong potential for advanced acoustic insulation applications. Overall, this study presents an effective strategy for modifying the overall performance of PLA aerogels, providing a path to reach an optimized balance of properties that broadens their potential use.

title: Oxide-dispersion driven phase and microstructural evolution with an analytical framework for critical current density in synergistically yttria-titania doped Nb3Sn
abstract: This study presents a heat treatment–doping effect of individual and synergic nano-oxide Y 2 O 3 and TiO 2 dispersoids on Nb 3 Sn towards the interrelation among phase, microstructure and properties. Synergic doping of Y 2 O 3 and TiO 2 to Nb 3 Sn resulted in T c of 18 K after annealing at 400 °C for 9 h. A lower T c of 16 K was observed for as-sintered pristine Nb 3 Sn. Pristine samples were susceptible to heat treatment, indicated by the wide transition width of 2 K in T c . A high overall J c of 5.17 × 10 5 A/cm 2 (10 K, 2 T) was observed for Y 2 O 3 and TiO 2 co-doped Nb 3 Sn sample annealed at 400 °C for 9 h compared to the overall J c of 2.3 × 10 5 A/cm 2 for as-sintered. Solutionized and quenched samples showed poor overall J c performance, with the lowest J c of 9.1 × 10 4 A/cm 2 for the pristine. A higher NbO phase fraction led to a degraded overall J c performance in TiO 2 doped sample. A superior overall J c performance for co-doped sample was due to the synergic presence of Y 2 O 3 and TiO 2 at grain boundaries of Nb 3 Sn which acted as blanket to restrict the NbO formation. An analytical model to predict the microstructurally governed overall J c performance at different applied fields was developed.

title: Effects of fissure geometry on mechanical response and failure patterns of 3D-printed teeth under compression via DIC and DEM
abstract: To address the clinical vulnerability of cracked teeth to splitting failure and the unclear regulatory mechanisms of fissure geometry on damage evolution and mechanical response, this study fabricated single-fissure tooth models with varying lengths (5 mm-25 mm) and inclination angles (5°-75°) via stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing. Uniaxial compression tests integrated with Digital Image Correlation (DIC) were conducted to capture real-time full-field strain evolution, crack propagation and macroscopic failure morphologies. Using PFC DEM, we reconstructed crack evolution and force chains, showing that fissure geometry controls strain, crack type, stress concentration, failure morphology, and damage mechanisms in compressed 3D-printed teeth. Non-fissure tip induced cracks (NTCs) only occurred in short-fissure specimens, while all others were dominated by fissure tip induced cracks (FTCs). Peak load decreased monotonically with increasing fissure length, and showed a non-linear “decrease-then-increase” trend with inclination angle, with 30° being the critical angle for minimum strength. Long-fissure specimens exhibited multi-stage stepped plateaus in crack evolution curves, and low-inclination specimens showed blocked force chain transmission and higher failure brittleness. This study provides clinically actionable insights for the diagnosis, treatment planning, and restoration design of cracked teeth, particularly for patients with fissure-type defects, and offers a methodological reference for DEM-based biomechanical fracture simulations.

title: Ultra-high reduction of eddy current losses in additively manufactured soft magnetic material via a novel dense-stack lamination architecture
abstract: Eddy current losses in motors and transformers are undesirable because they degrade energy efficiency. Several methods have been proposed to reduce it in additively manufactured (AM) soft magnetic materials but suffer from low design efficiency and reduced stacking factors. In this study, a novel laser-powder bed fusion (LPBF) method (i.e., Line-and-Space (L&S) structure) was proposed and demonstrated to enable the fabrication of ultra-thin laminated structures with high stacking factors and high design efficiency. Dimensional control of L&S structure was realized by only controlling LPBF scanning parameters of laser power, scanning speed, and hatching space, where a minimum “Line” thickness of ∼0.06 mm and stacking factors as high as ∼87 % for ∼0.13 mm and ∼97 % for ∼0.26 mm were achieved. Compared to bulk samples, L&S laminated structure revealed a substantial reduction in eddy current losses, where eddy current loss of the bulk sample was ∼46 times higher than that in L&S sample at an AC frequency of 1 kHz. Overall, the proposed L&S method represents a significant advancement in loss optimization of AM electrical steels by simultaneously achieving ultra-thin lamination, high stacking factor, and high design efficiency. This approach offers a practical and scalable solution for reducing eddy current losses in LPBF-fabricated motors and transformers.

title: Fundamental investigation of melting and solidification behaviors of high modulus steel via electron beam single-bead remelting under PBF-EB-relevant thermal conditions
