abstract: High modulus steel (HMS), an Fe-based TiB 2 -reinforced composite, is promising for lightweight structural applications because of its high stiffness and wear resistance. However, conventional casting often causes TiB 2 coarsening and inhomogeneous distribution. This study investigated the fundamental melting and solidification behavior of nominal 15 vol% TiB 2 -reinforced Fe–17Cr alloy using single-bead electron-beam remelting of dense cast disks under PBF-EB-relevant thermal conditions, rather than full powder-bed PBF-EB fabrication. The alloy was irradiated without powder deposition at beam powers of 600–1800 W and preheating temperatures up to 1000 °C. Increasing beam power and preheating temperature promoted apparent TiB 2 dissolution/refinement, elemental homogenization, and local microstructural modification. The remelted regions contained Fe–Cr–Ti–B-rich complex boride-like candidate phases, spinodal-decomposition-like nanoscale modulation in α -Fe, and Al 2 O 3 –TiB 2 τ -particles that assisted α -Fe grain refinement through heterogeneous nucleation and pinning. High-temperature preheating suppressed major cracking, while local Vickers hardness increased in the remelted regions owing to combined grain-refinement, dispersion-strengthening, dislocation-strengthening, and nanoscale-modulation effects. These results provide mechanistic guidance for future PBF-EB processing of TiB 2 -reinforced HMS, while the findings should be interpreted as dense-substrate single-bead remelting behavior, not direct evidence for fully built PBF-EB components. This clarification helps define the next experimental steps for translating these mechanisms to powder-bed processing.

title: Geometric quantification for nonlinear deformation in knitted fabrics
abstract: Knitted fabrics exemplify a broad class of architected materials capable of large deformations, enabling shape morphing, mechanical biocompatibility, and embedded multifunctionality without material damage. Although geometric nonlinearity has been intuitively utilized in their design, a quantitative description of stitch-resolved deformation and its temporal evolution remains lacking. Here, we introduce a geometric quantification framework that reconstructs smooth yarn centerlines and fabric surfaces from sparse yarn-level representations and extracts interpretable descriptors across dimensions. Applied to representative knitted structures, this framework resolves how global deformation is distributed among stitch reorientation, loop bending, surface bending, and dilation. Moreover, it reveals how regions of large geometric variation emerge, persist, and redistribute over time. Rather than directly measuring stress, these geometric descriptors define a unified geometric state space for comparing knitted structures and identifying candidate regions of mechanical localization. The framework provides a quantitative language for nonlinear deformation in knits and establishes a geometry-based representation that can be coupled to constitutive models, experimental measurements, and graph-based inverse-design workflows.

title: Bioinspired sea cucumber-mimetic “shield-sword” hydrogel: smart drug release and NIR-augmented action for infected wound healing
abstract: Invasive Gram-positive bacteria secrete hyaluronidase to degrade wound extracellular matrix (ECM), and conventional topical antimicrobials often fail due to drug dilution, even inducing resistance and chronic infections. Current wound dressings only target pathogens but ignore protecting the endogenous hyaluronic acid (HA) network, a key for bacterial resistance and tissue repair, from bacterial hyaluronidase damage. Inspired by the defensive-offensive integration of sea cucumber cuvierian tubules, we engineered a hyaluronidase-triggered "shield-and-sword" hydrogel (APT-HA), with HA as the bacteria-specific trigger, loaded with aloeemodin (AE)-encapsulated PLGA microspheres and photothermal MXene nanosheets. APT-HA sacrifices exogenous HA to protect endogenous HA from degradation according to bacterial load, while hyaluronidase-induced hydrogel breakdown intelligently releases AE. MXene release combined with NIR irradiation boosts antibacterial efficacy and mild thermal stimulation for tissue repair, using bacteria’s virulence factor to eradicate them. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirm APT-HA effectively eliminates Staphylococcus infections and promotes skin/subcutaneous tissue regeneration, providing a novel strategy for intelligent dressings against complex infected wounds.

title: A growth-stability framework for microstructure selection in complex-component eutectics under rapid solidification
abstract: Complex-component eutectic alloys are promising for additive manufacturing because coupled growth can generate fine microstructures, but their complex solute partitioning and nonequilibrium solidification make microstructure selection difficult to predict. Here, we develop a generalized growth-stability framework for multicomponent dual-phase eutectics by solving the full two-dimensional solute field with exact multicomponent flux balance. Interfacial nonequilibrium is incorporated through an energy-dissipation-based partial-drag formulation, which enables quantitative evaluation of solute trapping, liquidus–solidus separation, local solute accumulation, and the Mg/Si redistribution responsible for constitutional undercooling. Coupled with CALPHAD thermodynamics and full diffusion matrices, the model identifies the partial-drag coefficient as a key parameter controlling eutectic interface stability. As a first experimental validation, the framework is applied to the α-Al/Mg 2 Si eutectic in Al-10 Mg-4.7Si and it predicts a planar-to-cellular transition velocity of ∼10 μm/s at a partial-drag coefficient of 0.3, in close agreement with directional-solidification experiments showing transition between 8 and 12 μm/s. A growth-stability map further reveals that tuning the Mg/Si ratio can exploit element-specific solute-trapping effects to suppress interfacial perturbations under technologically relevant thermal gradients, rather than solely reducing solute content. This framework provides a quantitative basis for composition design, microstructure selection, and process-window optimization in rapid-solidification-based manufacturing.

title: Corrigendum to “Cascade-activated mussel-mimetic hydrogel with aurantiamide acetate nanoparticles reprograms macrophages and modulates ROS for accelerated diabetic wound healing” [Mater. Des. 267 (2026) 116121]
A quasi-zero stiffness biasing mechanism for electrostatic bellow muscle zipping actuators
abstract: Electrostatic zipping actuators are electromechanical drives capable of large voltage-induced deformations, with promising applications in soft robotics and wearable mechatronics. To produce a stroke, certain zipping actuator topologies need to be pre-loaded by an external force, producing a deformation that is then counteracted by electrostatic forces. This study presents a concept for a quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) biasing mechanism for zipping actuators and demonstrates its integration in a family of contractile actuators known as electrostatic bellow muscles (EBMs). The mechanism uses pre-loaded buckling beams to provide a nearly constant force pre-load, which reopens the actuator after each actuation cycle without increasing stiffness in operation. Under large external tensile loads, the beams transition into a load-bearing state that limits additional extension, acting as mechanical constraints that protect the actuator from failure. In this work, a model and design guidelines for the QZS mechanism are developed, along with a prototype of a coupled mechanism-EBM system in which the biasing mechanism weighs less than 10% of the actuator. Tests demonstrated that the EBM-QZS system provides a nearly constant low-force stroke without compromising the EBM frequency response, while preserving structural integrity under external forces tens of times larger than the EBM’s weight.

title: Concentration-dependent tungsten effects on chemical short-range order and deformation behavior in Ni–W alloys
abstract: Ni–W based medium heavy alloys offer a promising pathway to bridge the density–strength gap between tungsten heavy alloys and ultrahigh-strength steels. In this study, the effects of W concentration on chemical short-range order (CSRO), deformation behavior, and grain boundary chemistry of Ni– x W in the range of x = 0 to 38 wt% alloys were systematically investigated using a suite of advanced characterization and modeling techniques, including synchrotron X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, atom probe tomography, and first-principles thermodynamic simulations. Our study reveals that strong CSRO emerges when W content exceeds ∼30 wt%, producing distinct diffuse scattering and significantly enhancing strain-hardening capacity. During deformation, the presence of CSRO promotes planar slip and twin formation, leading to strong dislocation interactions and elevated flow stress. Hall–Petch analysis demonstrates an exceptionally high grain boundary strengthening coefficient ( k y ≈ 1102 MPa·μm⁻ 1/2 ) in Ni–38 W, underscoring the intrinsic strengthening effect associated with CSRO. First-principles cluster expansion coupled with Monte Carlo simulations reveals that increasing W content enhances CSRO tendency through the stabilization of Ni 4 W type local configurations. These findings establish a mechanistic link between W concentration, CSRO evolution, and mechanical response, providing new insights for designing high-density, high-strength Ni–W based alloys with optimized performance.

title: Research on anti-welding performance and arc erosion resistance of TaB2/Cu-Te composites
abstract: Multi-component hybrid TaB 2 /Cu-Te composites were fabricated via the in-situ formation of anti-welding Cu 2 Te phases and arc-resistant TaB 2 particles within a copper matrix. The microstructure, mechanical properties, electrical conductivity, and electrical contact properties of the composites were systematically investigated. The results showed that the hybrid composites consisted of Cu 2 Te phases and TaB 2 particles, exhibiting excellent mechanical and electrical properties. During the electrical contact testing, the Cu 2 Te phases induced pores and cracks on the contact surface, significantly reducing the welding force. Meanwhile, the TaB 2 particles increased the viscosity of the molten pool and effectively dispersed arc, thereby reducing mass loss and arc energy. Through the combined incorporation of TaB 2 and Cu 2 Te, the anti-welding function of Cu 2 Te and the arc erosion resistance of TaB 2 were synergistically achieved. This enabled the composites to achieve reduced mass loss and arc energy while maintaining a low welding force, demonstrating excellent overall electrical contact properties.

title: Toward autonomous experimentation: Bayesian optimization over problem formulation space for accelerated alloy development
abstract: Accelerated discovery in materials science demands autonomous systems capable of dynamically formulating and solving design problems. In this work, we introduce a novel framework that uses Bayesian optimization over a problem formulation space to identify optimal design formulations in line with decision-maker preferences. By mapping various design scenarios to a multi-attribute utility function, our approach enables the system to balance conflicting objectives—such as ductility, yield strength, density, and solidification range—without requiring an exact problem definition at the outset. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through an in silico case study on a Mo–Nb–Ti–V–W alloy system targeted for gas turbine engine blade applications. The framework converges on a ‘sweet spot’ that satisfies critical performance thresholds, illustrating that integrating problem formulation discovery into the autonomous design loop can significantly streamline the experimental process. Future work will incorporate human feedback to further enhance the adaptability of the system in real-world experimental settings.

title: Deep learning for the optimal design of phononic crystals in acceleration sensing
abstract: Phononic crystals (PnCs) acceleration sensors have demonstrated strong potential for high-sensitivity sensing due to defect-mode resonance. The acoustic sensitivity of the device is closely related to the topology of the PnCs. However, the large topology design space makes conventional numerical optimization computationally expensive. In this work, we innovatively employ a deep-learning–based framework to identify PnCs structures with optimal acoustic sensitivity. Specifically, an improved convolutional neural network is developed as a surrogate model to predict the performance of PnCs topologies. Based on the surrogate model, a gradient-based optimization strategy is then applied to iteratively refine the PnCs configuration, ultimately yielding the optimal design. The results show that the deep-learning surrogate model achieves an accuracy of 99.12% and a prediction speed approximately times faster than finite-element simulations. Furthermore, the gradient-based optimization yields an acoustic sensitivity of 242.35 kHz/µm after 500 iterations, representing an improvement of about 21.2% compared with conventional cylindrical PnCs. The proposed method enables rapid and accurate identification of the optimal PnCs topology and shows strong potential for broad application across a wide range of metamaterials and microelectromechanical system (MEMS) devices.

title: Microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of Co-modified AlSi10Mg alloy fabricated via in-situ alloying in laser powder bed fusion
abstract: In this study, 3 wt% Co was introduced into AlSi10Mg via in-situ alloying using laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). The microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of samples fabricated by routine and remelting scanning strategies were investigated in the as-built and heat-treated states. Partially melted Co particles were found in the as-built microstructures. Remelting reduced, but did not eliminate, the residual Co particles, which in turn promoted more Al 9 Co 2 particles that contributed to an increase in tensile strength from 367–397 MPa with routine scanning to 380–423 MPa with remelting scanning. In contrast, elongation was only marginally affected, remaining at 3–3.6% for both scanning strategies. The Al 9 Co 2 phase existed as eutectic networks, as vortex-shaped particle distributions within the melt pool, and as discrete particles along the melt pool boundaries. After heat treatment, the microstructures from the two scanning strategies converged toward a largely homogeneous state, leading to similar tensile properties. Both the Si and Al 9 Co 2 phases transformed into a granular morphology. Compared with the as-built state, the tensile strength decreased to 245–249 MPa, while the elongation improved to 9–10%. This study demonstrates the feasibility of incorporating Co into LPBF Al alloys as a strengthening element.

title: Architected metamaterials for enhanced ductility and strength through bio-inspired twinning strategies and topology optimization
abstract: Architected materials offer promisingly high strength-to-weight and stiffness-to-weight ratios but are traditionally limited in ductility. This work proposes a bio-inspired design framework that combines twinning-inspired deformation control with topology optimization to overcome the conventional strength–ductility trade-off in architected metamaterials. Unlike previous approaches that improve either ductility or strength individually, the proposed methodology integrates stress-delocalizing twin boundaries (TBs) with connectivity-enhancing topology optimization to simultaneously improve both properties. Three configurations ( baseline , twinned , and optimised ) are fabricated with identical mass and tested under uniaxial compression. Full-field strain mapping is obtained via digital image correlation, and finite-element analysis is used to simulate stress distribution and failure mechanisms. Results show that TBs significantly increase ductility by ≈15–20 %, while the optimised lattice achieves a > 97 % increase in deformation capacity and ≈118 % increase in peak load relative to the base structure, in agreement with the numerical simulations. The optimised unit cell exhibits a bending-dominated response, facilitating larger plastic deformations and extended shear-band formation, in contrast to the stretching-dominated behavior of base and twinned cells. These promising findings will provide a foundation for damage-programmable metamaterials in applications requiring controlled deformation and high structural resilience.

title: A materials testing 2.0 framework for identifying creep parameters from full-field strain measurements of a notched specimen
abstract: The accurate identification of high-temperature creep constitutive parameters under complex stress states is a fundamental challenge in solid mechanics. The emerging Materials Testing 2.0 paradigm offers a promising alternative to conventional uniaxial testing by identifying parameters from a single heterogeneous test. However, its application to time-dependent deformation in notched structural alloys remains limited. This study proposes and validates a rapid identification framework for the Norton creep law parameters of Inconel 718 at 650 °C using a notched compact (C(T)) specimen. The framework couples high-temperature digital image correlation (HT-DIC) with a finite element model updating (FEMU) algorithm, employing a logarithmic objective function to effectively circumvent the numerical instability that can destabilize conventional linear formulations during nonlinear power-law inversion. The inverse analysis successfully identified creep parameters that reasonably reproduce the material response in the intermediate stress regime, which governs stress relaxation at crack tips. This regime was targeted by explicitly distinguishing it from the high-stress domain, where power-law breakdown (precipitate shearing) renders the simple power law inapplicable. In contrast, a discrepancy was observed in the low-stress regime, where the method overestimated the strain rate compared with that of the uniaxial baseline. This deviation was physically attributed to the prolonged duration of transient creep at low stresses, which persists beyond the short-term experimental window. These findings demonstrate that the proposed notched-specimen approach serves as a powerful and efficient tool for characterizing critical behaviors in the intermediate stress regime, provided that the physical boundaries imposed by transient kinetics and high-stress breakdown mechanisms are considered.

title: Acicular ferrite formation by interfacial spinel phase associated with titanium oxide inclusions in welded low-alloyed steel
abstract: Acicular ferrite is a key microstructural constituent in welded low-alloyed steel due to its beneficial effect on toughness, yet the exact nucleation mechanisms at non-metallic particles often remain incompletely understood. In this study, we present examples of acicular ferrite nucleation on rhombohedral Ti 2 O 3 phase-analogues within multiphase particles and provide direct experimental evidence for the formation of a spinel-type interfacial layer between (Ti,Mn) 2 O 3 and the ferrite (α-Fe) matrix. Using four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) diffraction mapping in combination with transmission electron microscopy–energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (TEM-EDS) analysis, the particle–matrix interface was reconstructed, and the thickness of the interfacial layer was estimated. Notably, manganese was found in abundance at the interfacial layer and the particle, suggesting a decisive role in nucleation, particularly around Ti 2 O 3 -containing inclusions. Taken together, these findings highlight that nucleation is not necessarily a direct Ti 2 O 3 –α-Fe process but can be facilitated by transitional phases, opening new perspectives for modeling acicular ferrite nucleation, assessing suitable particle chemistries for acicular ferrite formation, and tailoring inclusion chemistries to optimize steel toughness.

title: Reactive direct ink writing of binder-free MOF/COF monoliths with architecture-controlled transport
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer remarkable porosity and chemical tunability, yet their integration and shaping into binder-free, mechanically robust, and porosity-retaining architectures remains an issue. Here, we introduce reactive direct ink writing (RDIW), an additive-manufacturing strategy that utilizes the intrinsic thixotropy of high-aspect-ratio MOF nanorods to create printable inks without any polymeric binders. After extrusion of the ink into a bath of COF monomers, rapid imine condensation produces a continuous COF sheath around each filament, forming core-sheath MOF/COF aerogels that preserve the microporosity of both components. We demonstrate that this approach is general across multiple MOFs and four imine-linked COFs and produces wood-pile structured monoliths with tuneable composition and architecture. The 3D-printed aerogels exhibit over 4 times higher initial rate of adsorption h 0 than MOF, COF, or sol–gel-derived MOF/COF analogues, while maintaining structural integrity and recyclability. RDIW establishes a scalable framework for shaping porous crystalline materials into mechanically resilient, high-surface-area monoliths, opening new opportunities in water purification, separations, and catalytic flow systems.

title: CD44 receptor-blocking biomimetic nanoparticles attenuate extracellular matrix stiffness to enhance chemotherapeutic efficacy in pancreatic cancer
abstract: Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis, where chemoresistance is closely linked to fibrotic extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Hyaluronic acid (HA)-CD44 binding increases ECM stiffness and upregulates drug efflux protein ABCG2, exacerbating PDAC chemoresistance. Disrupting CD44-HA interaction is a promising strategy to overcome chemoresistance. Photothermal therapy (PTT) has high efficacy and low toxicity in cancer therapy, demonstrating notable synergy with chemotherapy. Methods MCuS@GEM@Antitumor agent-109@M (CGAM) nanoparticles were fabricated by coating mesoporous CuS (MCuS) loaded with AA109 and gemcitabine (GEM) using PDAC cell membranes. Physicochemical properties, photothermal conversion, and drug release were characterized via dynamic light scattering, UV–Vis spectroscopy, transmission/scanning electron microscopy, and thermal imaging. Hemocompatibility and anticancer efficacy were evaluated through hemolysis, cellular uptake, viability, live/dead staining, and apoptosis experiments. Flow cytometry and pancreatic patient-derived organoids fluorescence assays assessed CD44-HA blockade. A xenograft mouse model was established to examine biodistribution, antitumor efficacy, and biosafety. Results CGAM exhibited uniform size, stability, and efficient photothermal conversion. In vitro, CGAM combined with PTT effectively killed PANC-1 cells and disrupted CD44-HA binding. In vivo, CGAM selectively accumulated in tumors, significantly suppressing PDAC progression with favorable biosafety. Conclusion CGAM nanoplatform enables tumor-specific targeting, CD44-HA blockade, and enhanced GEM chemosensitivity.

title: Eco-conscious scalable interconnects and embedded capacitive sensors for non-contact microfluidic monitoring
abstract: A capacitive sensor detects solids or liquids without physical contact, using the same principle as touchscreens. In this study, screen-printed capacitive sensors (SPCSs) were developed for non-contact fluid sensing in microfluidic channels. SPCSs were fabricated by printing carbon–graphene ink onto hydrophilic polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polylactic acid (PLA) substrates via roll-to-roll rotary screen printing. Microfluidic channels were created by laser-cutting pressure-sensitive adhesive films and laminated onto SPCSs through pressure bonding, or hot embossed onto PLA or cellulose acetate (CA) and solvent-bonded to form integrated devices. Flexible carbon–graphene interconnects were incorporated to enable integration of additional components (e.g., bioenzymatic fuel cells, BFCs) and facilitate easier separation for recycling.Performance was demonstrated through timed multichannel fluid filling experiments with electrical readouts. Potential applications include monitoring air bubbles, reagent dissolution, dilution, and liquid movement without labels or optical analysis. Sustainability considerations guided material selection and fabrication, reducing environmental impact through PLA-based microfluidics and printing on the unused non-hydrophilic side of PET. Integration of metal-free paper-based BFCs provided a fully sustainable power source for low-power electronics. These BFCs, being recyclable and compostable, further minimize the device’s environmental footprint.

title: Dual mechanical and biochemical mimicry in 3D-printable hydrogels for spinal cord injury repair
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) results in irreversible neurological deficits due to a hostile microenvironment characterized by physical barriers (glial scars and cystic cavities) and biochemical inhibitors (inflammatory cytokines and extracellular matrix molecules). To address these challenges, we developed a dual-biomimetic, 3D-printable hydrogel scaffold (HDA) that integrates decellularized spinal cord extracellular matrix (dECM) with a dynamic dual-crosslinked network composed of reversible ionic bonds and stable covalent bonds. In a rat complete transection model, the HDA scaffold significantly reduced inflammation and glial scar formation, while promoting endogenous neural stem cell recruitment and neuronal differentiation. Multi-omics analyses further demonstrated activation of pathways associated with synaptic assembly, axonal guidance, and neurotransmission, indicating enhanced neural circuit reconstruction. Functionally, HDA treatment improved motor and urinary recovery compared with control groups. These findings suggest that simultaneously addressing biochemical and mechanical barriers provides an effective strategy for reconstructing a pro-regenerative microenvironment and promoting functional recovery after SCI.

title: Injectable decellularized endometrium extracellular matrix/chitosan hydrogels improved the endometrium regeneration and fertility restoration
abstract: Intrauterine adhesion (IUA) is an endometrial injury that leads to menstruation dysfunction and even infertility in women. Therefore, the therapy strategy to promote endometrial recovery and prevent adhesion formation could be beneficial for the clinical outcomes. In this study, we develop an in-situ formable hydrogel based on decellularized endometrium extracellular matrix (dECM) and chitosan. The hydrogel demonstrates biocompatibility, injectability and mechanical properties. And the dECM/chitosan hydrogel promotes the endometrial cell proliferation, cell invasion and exhibites pro-angiogenic effects. Finally, the effect of the dECM/chitosan hydrogel on endometrial damage and regeneration is validated in rat IUA model. It increases the endometrial thickness, gland and vessel numbers, alleviates fibrotic formation. Also, this hydrogel enhances the expression of estrogen and progesterone receptors, promotes endometrial receptivity, and contributes to the recovery of fertility. In summary, the dECM/chitosan hydrogel could be a potential therapeutic strategy for improving endometrial injury and fertility outcomes for women with IUA.

title: An efficient hemostatic hydrogel patch enabled by TXA-induced rapid wet adhesion and release
abstract: Non-compressible hemorrhage remains the leading cause of death in combat injuries and severe trauma. Herein, we developed a wet-adhesive drug-releasing hydrogel (WAR) based on tranexamic acid (TXA), which synergistically stops bleeding through TXA surface enrichment, rapid swelling, strong wet tissue adhesion, and antifibrinolytic effects. WAR enables rapid gelation, fast water absorption, strong wet-tissue adhesion, and simultaneous activation of coagulation and tissue repair pathways—promoting platelet activation, accelerating the coagulation cascade, and initiating early repair. In five rat models of non-compressible hemorrhage, WAR outperformed commercial GS® and CS® chitosan hemostatic gels. WAR can be detached on demand with low-concentration urea, without tissue damage. Additionally, WAR accelerates full-thickness skin healing, promotes M2 macrophage polarization, angiogenesis, and ordered collagen remodeling, and achieves near-scarless functional wound healing in 10 days. This work presents a TXA spatial rearrangement–driven strategy for designing hemostatic hydrogels against non-compressible hemorrhage.

title: Design and energy absorption performance of gradient-Orowan synergistically strengthened lattice structures
abstract: Lattice structures have attracted much attention in the engineering field due to their light weight, high specific strength, and excellent energy absorption characteristics. However, traditional homogeneous designs struggle to balance load-bearing and energy absorption performance. This paper couples Orowan strengthening with gradient strengthening, and designs and manufactures four new types of lattice structures using AlSi10Mg as the material: single-layer uniform lattice (SUL), Orowan-strengthened lattice (OSL), density-gradient strengthened lattice (GSL), and Grad-Oro-strengthened lattice (G-OSL). By combining the quasi-static compression test with finite element simulation. The results show that the G-OSL structure utilizes the density gradient-induced progressive crushing mode layer by layer. In addition, the effective deflection and bypassing effect of the shear bands brought about by the Orowan strengthening mechanism have demonstrated the most outstanding comprehensive impact resistance performance. Changing the interfacial spacing will cause different degrees of damage to the unit cell by the dislocations. Further analysis of the influence of the enhanced phase spacing (2 l, 4 l, 6 l) indicates that the spacing variation does not show a clear monotonic pattern for Energy absorption ( EA ). Gradient strengthening causes the lattice to undergo progressive collapse, while Orowan strengthening enables the shear band to bypass the strengthened phase. It provides an effective new idea for the design of high-impact-resistant lightweight lattice structures. It has great potential for application in fields such as rail transportation, aerospace, and protective equipment.

title: Growth of metal–organic frameworks on complex copper architectures fabricated by laser powder bed process
abstract: This study investigated the direct growth of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) on a copper substrate with complex architecture created via laser powder bed fusion process (PBF-LB/M). Specifically, a scalable route to functionalise gyroid primitive triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures with HKUST-1 (Cu 3 (BTC) 2 , also known as MOF-199) using a malachite-mediated two-step synthesis was analysed. The PBF-LB/M/Cu gyroid architecture provided a high surface-to-volume ratio and favourable curvature for nucleation, enabling uniform formation of Cu 2 (OH) 2 CO 3 nanoribbons across the entire TPMS network. Subsequent conversion into HKUST-1 yielded a continuous MOF coating composed of well-defined octahedral and cuboctahedral crystals. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) and computer tomography (CT) scan analysis confirmed homogeneous coverage even in highly curved regions, while X-ray diffraction (XRD) verified the presence of MOF-199 with minimal oxidation of the underlying copper. The lightweight coating (<3 wt%) preserved the openness and thermal conductivity of the metallic scaffold, establishing a robust hybrid platform that bridges metal additive manufacturing with MOF chemistry.

title: A multimodal machine learning approach for the integrated design of active magnetic regenerators with coordinated multilayer material layout and thermo-fluidic transfer characteristics
abstract: A multimodal machine learning (ML) framework is proposed for the holistic design of active magnetic regenerator (AMR). This approach comprehensively captures not only specialized assessments such as the suitability of magnetocaloric (MC) materials but also correlations among a multi-layer layout, operational parameters and the environmental temperature ( T rt ) and thermal load ( P n ). Dimensionally reduced MC feature vectors were successfully obtained from differential scanning calorimetry curves using a uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP). A multimodal dataset was constructed by classifying temperature span ( T span ) data across four-layer beds composed of La(Fe,Si) 13 variants under various operating parameters, treating the UMAP vectors as labels. The impact of T rt and P n was also incorporated as annotations for classification. The best predictive accuracy was achieved by a Gaussian process regression. A large no-load T span of 16.9 °C at 0.8 T, which was overlooked during the grid sampling, was found under conditions optimized for the trained four-layer layouts by the constructed ML model. Predictive optimization for untrained layouts utilizing virtual material selections constructed by combining the UMAP vectors was also effective, and the maximized no-load T span = 17.1 °C was demonstrated around the predicted conditions for a unique four-layer layout, that breaks heuristic approaches in material selection.

title: Bimetallic Al–Fe composites with tailored properties produced by cold spray additive manufacturing
abstract: Cold spray enables multi-material additive manufacturing through solid-state bonding, thereby reducing intermetallic formation and thermal residual stresses typical of fusion-based manufacturing routes. This study establishes a composition–structure–property framework for cold sprayed Al–Fe bimetallic composites produced by online powder mixing by varying Fe content from 0 to 100 vol% and relating retained composition to microstructure and mechanical response. The mixed deposits formed dense Al-rich matrices containing dispersed Fe splats, while retained composition deviated from the nominal feedstock composition at higher Fe contents. Porosity decreased from ∼0.8% in pure Al to ≤ 0.25% in the mixed deposits, and the flattening ratio of Al splats increased with Fe addition, indicating enhanced matrix deformation. Mechanical properties were governed by retained Fe content: elastic modulus increased from 32 to 61 GPa, while yield/tensile strengths rose from ∼40/55 to ∼77/94 MPa, approaching saturation beyond ∼23–28 vol% retained Fe. Ductility exhibited a non-monotonic trend, reaching a maximum in Al–25Fe (∼5% fracture elongation) and decreasing at higher Fe contents as clustering and interface-controlled fracture became more pronounced. Overall, retained composition and spatial distribution governed the balance between strengthening and damage mechanisms, defining an intermediate Fe regime that provides the most favorable mechanical performance.

title: Fluorine-programmed molecular chain engineering enables continuous and flexible apatite fibers with tunable surface topography
abstract: Continuous bioceramic fibers offer potential applications for flexible, damage-tolerant biomedical devices and bio-reinforcements. However, as a typical component of bioceramics, calcium phosphate is inherently brittle and prone to defect formation, which limits its ability to achieve true structural continuity, especially in apatite, where reports on continuous fibers remain scarce. Here, a fluorine-programmed molecular chain strategy was developed to direct organic–inorganic chain assembly, producing spinnable, structurally coherent precursors and enabling continuous, controllable dry-spun apatite fibers. Fluorine bridging enhances sol spinnability and lowers crystallization temperature, temporally aligning grain formation with pyrolytic shrinkage to suppress pore retention and improve densification. Using this approach, dense, flexible, and continuous apatite fibers with uniform diameters of 3–4 μm were successfully fabricated. These fibers exhibit tunable dual-phase microstructures and markedly improved nanomechanical properties, with elastic modulus approaching those of natural hard tissue. This work establishes a direct link between sol–gel chemistry and macroscopic fiber continuity, providing a general design route for continuous bioactive ceramic fibers and advancing wearable, implantable biomedical systems and high-performance bio-composites.

title: Safe and natural innovation in regenerative medicine: enhancing collagen scaffold stability with vitamin B2 (riboflavin)-mediated UV crosslinking
abstract: Collagen scaffolds are widely used in regenerative medicine but are limited by poor mechanical strength and rapid degradation. Traditional chemical crosslinkers, such as aldehydes or carbodiimides, can introduce cytotoxicity, necessitating safer alternatives. This study evaluates riboflavin-mediated UV crosslinking as a non-toxic method to enhance the stability of collagen scaffolds for wound healing, since riboflavin is naturally involved in tissue repair and regeneration. Collagen type I scaffolds were crosslinked using riboflavin (1–1000 µM) in water or ethanol while exposed to UV-A or UV-C light for varying durations. Structural integrity, swelling, enzymatic stability, and cytotoxicity were assessed and compared to carbodiimide-crosslinked controls. Results showed that water-based riboflavin solutions maintained scaffold porosity and the collagen’s triple-helix structure, while ethanol disrupted morphology. UV-A crosslinking with 1000 µM riboflavin achieved optimal stabilization, reducing water uptake and enzymatic degradation, while having minimal impact on collagen’s secondary structure. Although carbodiimides-crosslinked scaffolds exhibited slightly higher stability (>60% degradation vs. >70% for riboflavin-UV after 3 days), riboflavin-UV crosslinking eliminated cytotoxic risks and simplified processing. In conclusion, riboflavin-mediated UV crosslinking offers a safe, effective, and tunable alternative for stabilizing collagen scaffolds, thereby enabling their use in regenerative medicine and wound healing applications.

title: Z-parameter model based paradigm for fatigue life prediction and quality control
abstract: Manufacturing processes such as welding and additive manufacturing inevitably introduce defects, which pose a significant threat to structural safety. Establishing predictive frameworks that coherently link defect characteristics to fatigue life remains a fundamental challenge in manufacturing science and structural integrity. Existing fatigue models suffer from poor parameter robustness and lack of uncertainty quantification. Here, we establish fatigue life models of materials with different defect features using finite element analysis, and develop a novel hybrid physics-statistical method to achieve robust identification of material-dependent defect sensitivity parameters, improving the reliability of conventional Z -parameter model. Building on this, we propose an original Z -PIHREN framework integrating physics-informed neural networks with heteroscedastic regression and deep ensembles, to quantify fatigue uncertainty and assess structural reliability of defective structures. The model placed 84.2 % of samples within factor-of-three error bounds and achieved a validation-set coverage-calibration R 2 of 0.956 after temperature scaling. More importantly, by establishing quantitative correlations between defects and fatigue life, the proposed framework not only offers forward predictions for reliability assessment of long-term service structures, but also provides inverse guidance for manufacturing process optimization. This work demonstrates the prospect for establishing a physics-statistical framework that integrates fatigue life prediction with quality control in manufacturing.

title: 3D printing of continuous fiber self-reinforced thermoplastic composites
abstract: Self-reinforced composites (SRCs) offer a promising route toward lightweight and recyclable materials for additive manufacturing. In this study, continuous SRC filaments were fabricated via an overcoating process. High-performance polymer fibers, as monofilaments or twisted yarns, were coated with lower-melting thermoplastic sheaths from the same polymer families (polyamides and polyesters). Optical microscopy confirmed well-defined core–sheath structures with controlled fiber volume fractions (∼40 vol%) and a good interfacial consolidation. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed distinct melting transitions of core and sheath materials, defining a processing window that preserves fiber integrity during 3D printing. Among the investigated materials, overcoated polyamide 6 (PA6) filaments with copolyamide (CoPA) exhibited the best printability and mechanical performance. Printed parts achieved a tensile strength of 112 ± 4.5 MPa while maintaining ductility (elongation at break ∼25%). In contrast, overcoated twisted polyamide 66 (PA66) ply yarns with CoPA and overcoated polyethylene terephthalate (PET) monofilaments with copolyester (CoPES) showed limitations in mechanical performance related to processing and interfacial behavior. Polarization-dependent Raman spectroscopy confirmed that molecular orientation is retained in the PA6 fiber phase after printing, while the matrix remains isotropic. Mechanical reprocessing and re-extrusion of PA6/CoPA demonstrated the potential of SRC filaments for recyclable, high-strength 3D-printed parts.

title: Systematic study of the interplay between laser beam shape, energy input, and hatch spacing in PBF-LB/M of Ti-6Al-4V: experiments and numerical modeling
abstract: Programmable laser beam shaping tailors the spatial irradiance distribution in laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M), enabling control over melt-pool geometry and defect formation. However, the coupled effects of beam shape, hatch spacing (track overlap), and energy input on densification and microstructural development remain insufficiently understood. Accordingly, Ti-6Al-4 V is studied using single-track experiments, cube builds, and 3D transient multiphysics simulations across three ring-type beam profiles ranging from relatively core-weighted to strongly ring-dominated. Single tracks spanning a power–speed matrix (linear energy density, P / v ) quantified melt-pool width, depth, and molten area and mapped stability regimes (fragmentation, necking, stable) and transition thresholds with increasing energy input. Cube specimens mapped relative density versus beam mode, areal energy density A E D h = P / ( v h ) (J/mm 2 ), hatch spacing h , and geometric ratios h / d ( d : effective beam diameter) and W / h ( W : melt-pool width). Near-full density (∼99.9%) was achieved for all profiles at A E D h ≥ 2.8 –3.0 J/mm 2 ; relatively more core-weighted profiles reached this at lower A E D h , whereas ring-dominated profiles required higher input to suppress lack-of-fusion. Density dropped when h / d ≳ 1 , while W / h ≳ 1.2 preserved high density. Microstructure and Vickers microhardness (HV 0.2 ) were assessed across A E D h . All conditions exhibited martensitic α′ microstructures, and microhardness remained ≈360–395 HV 0.2 , converging once near-full density was reached. Simulations showed that ring-dominated density loss arises from insufficient inter-track remelting depth (cusp formation) despite lateral overlap, requiring higher overlap ratios for full fusion. Thermal gradients (G) and solidification rates (R) placed all cases in the columnar growth regime; higher G/R in more core-weighted profiles is consistent with stronger grain continuity than the more refined ring-dominated structures.

title: Designing functional metal–organic frameworks through synthesis–structure–interface coupling: toward structure–property relationships
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are versatile porous materials whose structure and functionality can be tuned through coordination chemistry. Their performance is governed not only by framework topology but also by the coupled effects of synthesis conditions, defect chemistry, and interfacial structure across multiple length scales. In this review, we introduce a unified synthesis–structure–interface–property framework that treats these factors as interdependent variables controlling adsorption, mass transport, and interfacial interactions in MOF systems. We examine how intrinsic modifications, including defect engineering, multimetallic node incorporation, and linker functionalization, regulate coordination environments, surface chemistry, and pore accessibility, and extend these concepts to confinement effects and interface-driven hybrid architectures such as MOF–MOF, metal oxide–MOF, MOF–carbon, MOF–COF, and MOF–MXene systems. By linking synthetic control to defect landscapes and interfacial organization, we establish general principles governing reactivity, transport, and stability, with particular emphasis on the interplay between surface chemistry and structural heterogeneity and the resulting trade-offs between activity, robustness, and reproducibility. Current limitations in predictive synthesis, interfacial characterization, and structure–property correlation are discussed, highlighting the need for operando and multiscale approaches to resolve dynamic behaviour under working conditions. This perspective provides a framework for advancing MOF-based materials in catalysis, separations, and energy-related applications.

title: Two-step simulating of conductivity for carbon black polymer nanocomposites by tunneling distance and interphase aspects
abstract: This study proposes a two-step modeling framework to predict the conductivity of composites filled with carbon black nanoparticles (PCB). In the first step, carbon black (CB) nanoparticles together with their surrounding interphase are conceptualized as a core–shell structure, and its effective conductivity is estimated. In the second step, this core–shell structure is treated as a dispersed phase within the polymer matrix, enabling the prediction of nanocomposite conductivity. The model explicitly incorporates interfacial tension, interphase conductivity ( σ i ), percolation threshold ( ϕ p ) and tunneling distance ( d ). Validation against experimental data and parametric studies confirm the predictive accuracy of the present approach. At a CB particle radius of 10 nm combined with an interphase thickness of 20 nm, the composite conductivity reaches 1.9 S/m, but when the CB radius exceeds 20 nm and the interphase depth is reduced below 5 nm, the sample is insulated. At CB volume portion ( ϕ f ) of 0.12 and σ i = 1000 S/m, the predicted conductivity is 0.12 S/m, while as ϕ f drops below 0.08, the nanocomposite exhibits insulating behavior. Also, at ϕ p = 0.001 and d = 1 nm, the estimated conductivity approaches 0.16 S/m, but when d surpasses 2 nm, the sample is insulated.

title: Immunomodulatory injectable AlgMA hydrogel incorporating WKYMVm-Encapsulated PLGA microspheres promotes articular cartilage repair
abstract: Articular cartilage injury is often accompanied by a hostile inflammatory microenvironment characterized by excessive ROS and pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, both of which impair endogenous chondrogenesis. To address this challenge, we developed an injectable immunomodulatory hydrogel composed of alginate methacrylate (AlgMA) and electrosprayed PLGA microspheres encapsulating the formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) agonist WKYMVm. This system was designed to enable sustained peptide release, scavenge ROS, promote M2 macrophage polarization, and support chondrogenic differentiation under inflammatory conditions. Uniform PLGA microspheres with an average diameter of 12.09 μm were fabricated by electrospraying and homogeneously incorporated into AlgMA hydrogel, allowing minimally invasive injection. In vitro, released WKYMVm significantly reduced intracellular ROS levels in H 2 O 2 -stimulated macrophages and upregulated M2 markers. Co-culture experiments further showed that the WKYMVm-loaded system enhanced the MSCs chondrogenic differentiation under inflammatory challenge, as indicated by 472% increases in collagen II expression. In vivo, the composite hydrogel promoted superior hyaline‑like cartilage regeneration in a rabbit cartilage defect model, with the compression modulus of the repair tissue increased to 3.22 MPa, compared with 1.18 MPa in the Blank group. Collectively, these findings indicate that the injectable Wm@μS/AlgMA hydrogel is a promising off‑the‑shelf candidate for the treatment of articular cartilage injuries.

title: Corrigendum to “Programmed polymeric integration of gold nanoparticles into multi-material 3D printed hydrogels” [Mater. Des. 250 (2025) 113650]
In situ ultrasound-activated hydrogen-releasing hydrogel alleviates ferroptosis and promotes functional recovery after spinal cord injury
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a disabling disease for which no effective treatment is currently available. Molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) has shown therapeutic promise in SCI owing to its antioxidant properties, but conventional delivery strategies struggle to achieve controllable and therapeutically effective local H 2 concentrations at the injury site. Here, we engineered an ultrasound-activated hydrogen −releasing hydrogel, termed CSVC, by integrating C 3 N 4 nanosheets, vitamin C (VC), and a methacrylated chitosan (CSMA) network to simultaneously optimize catalytic efficiency, local retention, controlled release, and stability. In this architecture, C 3 N 4 acts as a piezocatalyst for ultrasound-triggered H 2 generation, VC suppresses electron–hole recombination to enhance charge utilization and thereby improve H 2 generation efficiency, and the porous CSMA matrix stabilizes the components through noncovalent interactions and enables their localized retention. These structure-dependent properties endowed CSVC with efficient H 2 release under mild ultrasound stimulation and resulting in therapeutic efficacy in vitro and in vivo, including alleviation of oxidative stress, suppression of ferroptosis, and promotion of axonal regeneration and motor recovery. More broadly, this work establishes a modular design principle for stimuli-responsive biomaterials by integrating catalytic components, charge-regulating agents, and hydrogel matrices for localized gas therapy.

title: Spectral strong-contrast prediction of transverse elastic modulus in unidirectional fiber-reinforced composites
abstract: Accurate prediction of the transverse elastic modulus of unidirectional fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites is critical for virtual testing, as matrix-dominated response governs damage initiation. This study develops a microstructure-sensitive spectral strong-contrast framework for efficient estimation. To ensure geometric fidelity, an improved level-cut filtered Poisson field (LCPF) method is introduced, employing hard-core point sets and a supremum envelope to generate overlap-free representative volume elements (RVEs). Representing the microstructure via a primitive indicator basis, the framework facilitates efficient n-point statistics computation using discrete Fourier transforms (DFT) and approximates strong-contrast integral equations as algebraic series. Furthermore, an invariant embedding technique resolves numerical singularities in the Green’s function, ensuring stability for high-contrast media. Validated against analytical models, finite-element homogenization, and experimental data, the framework captures isotropic and anisotropic responses even at second-order truncation. Parametric analysis reveals that predictive accuracy relies on the reference medium’s proximity to the effective response. Theoretical derivation confirms this medium dictates the topological baseline, restricting predictions to Hashin-Shtrikman bounds. Optimizing the reference medium selection provides a pathway to high precision within low-order frameworks, avoiding complex higher-order statistics. Consequently, the proposed framework serves as a theoretically sound and numerically efficient foundation for the virtual design of FRP composites.

title: Faraday inductive breakdown: From spark plasma sintering to neuromorphic memristors
abstract: The field-induced transition of metallic granular media from an insulating to a conductive state, known as the Branly effect, presents a quantified energy deficit. A stress-dependent thermodynamic baseline, established from direct-current sweeps on oxidized copper, reveals that Ohmic heating cannot drive dielectric breakdown under pulsed regimes. An analytical electro-inductive model shows that this transition is governed by Faraday self-induction, originating from the network’s intrinsic percolative inductance. Validated in situ under Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) conditions, the model predicts the order of magnitude of the observed millisecond electrical transitions. The resulting localized currents trigger a magnetohydrodynamic Z-pinch instability. Macroscopic mechanical loading determines the microstructural outcome, converting droplet splashing into localized radial extrusion. By bridging macroscopic powder metallurgy and the sub-nanosecond electroforming of neuromorphic memristors, this electro-inductive framework yields a geometric and percolative scaling law that serves as a predictive design tool for interface engineering across 16 frequency decades.

title: Anti-fibronectin aptamer-functionalized zirconia promotes human gingival fibroblast adhesion and proliferation for enhanced peri-implant soft tissue sealing
abstract: The bioinert nature of zirconia implant abutments impedes robust soft tissue seal, a critical barrier against peri-implant diseases. To address this, we developed a novel surface functionalization strategy by covalently immobilizing an anti-fibronectin aptamer onto zirconia surfaces to selectively recruit fibronectin (FN) from the physiological fluids. The successful aptamer conjugation was verified by XPS and fluorescence imaging, significantly enhancing surface hydrophilicity and FN adsorption specificity. Human gingival fibroblasts (HGFs) cultured on modified surfaces exhibited superior adhesion, spreading, and proliferation in a dose-dependent manner. This enhanced cellular response was mediated by the significant upregulation of key adhesion-related molecules (integrin β1, FAK) and extracellular matrix components (FN, Col-I) at both the gene and protein levels. The aptamer coating remained stable in TE buffer for over two weeks. This facile biofunctionalization strategy transforms zirconia into a bioactive interface, offering promising clinical translation for peri-implant soft tissue integration.

title: Physical and microstructural properties of ultrasonically atomized Nickel-Tungsten (NiW) powders
abstract: Ultrasonic atomization was used to produce Ni–W alloy powders from arc-melted feedstocks with nominal compositions of 20, 40, 60, and 80 wt% W, and the influence of alloy composition on atomization behavior, powder characteristics, and spark plasma sintering response was systematically investigated. The cast feedstocks exhibited composition-dependent microstructures, ranging from a single-phase FCC Ni solid solution at low W contents to multiphase structures containing W-rich constituents at higher W contents. Ultrasonic atomization generated predominantly spherical powders with excellent flowability, negligible satellite formation, and no clear compositional trend in particle size distribution within the analyzed fraction; however, powder yield decreased markedly with increasing W content. Compositional analysis showed good chemistry retention and limited interparticle variability for Ni20W, whereas W-rich feedstocks produced broad, multimodal composition distributions and substantial deviation between feedstock and collected powder composition, indicating selective atomization under fixed processing conditions. SPS of Ni20W, Ni40W, and Ni60W powders achieved near-full densification. Microhardness increased systematically with W content in both cast and SPS conditions, where hardness in the W-rich alloys was governed primarily by phase constitution. These results demonstrate ultrasonic atomization as a viable route for producing spherical Ni–W powders while also revealing a composition-dependent limit in compositional fidelity for W-rich alloys.

title: 3D-printed polycaprolactone-bioactive glass composite scaffolds for bone tissue engineering: the effect of filler content on different surface modifications
abstract: Composite material technology and advanced surface modifications are the two most substantial components in designing an effective bone scaffold. In this study, the extrusion of polycaprolactone (PCL)-45S5 Bioglass® (BG) composite filaments using a dry-mix hot-melt extrusion method was investigated. PCL-45S5 BG (PCL-BG) composite filaments of three different filler contents, 1, 2, and 5 wt%, and their three-dimensional (3D)-printed constructs were studied and compared to an industrial-grade PCL filament and its 3D-printed constructs. Following the composite material study, the PCL and PCL-BG composite scaffolds were treated with three surface modifications: subtractive chemical etching, conventional biomimetic calcium phosphate (CaP) coating, and bioinspired polydopamine (PDA) modification. A collective, comparative, and comprehensive analysis package comprising microstructure and morphology observation, topography characterization, mechanical performance, and a series of in vitro studies were conducted. The results showed considerable changes in mechanical performance and osteogenic properties across different combinations of substrate materials and surface modification strategies. Adding to the current general understanding that surface-modified scaffolds follow the substrate’s properties, varying filler contents of composite substrates in interaction with surface modification strategies certainly influenced the essential properties of bone scaffolds. These findings emphasize the considerable details involved in designing and engineering patient-specific bone scaffolds.

title: Advanced laser technologies toward high-efficiency crystalline silicon solar cells: A review
abstract: Laser processing plays a crucial role in high-efficiency crystalline silicon solar cells by enabling precise, non-contact, and localized material modification. This review systematically examines the working principles, classifications, and parameter-dependent behaviors of advanced laser technologies, and surveys their representative applications in mainstream cell architectures, including passivated emitter and rear cells, tunnel-oxide passivated contact cells, silicon heterojunction cells, and back-contact cells. Key laser-enabled processes are discussed in terms of their governing mechanisms, technological evolution, and industrial relevance. Particular attention is given to how laser parameters control energy deposition, defect generation, and the resulting processing outcomes. The review further distinguishes laser processes with established manufacturing relevance from historical or limited-scale concepts, with particular attention to laser-induced damage, process uniformity, scalability, and architecture-specific compatibility. Finally, future research directions are outlined, emphasizing low-damage contact opening, laser-enhanced contact optimization, laser-assisted metallization, damage-controlled scribing, and laser-based module interconnection. Abbreviations: PV, photovoltaic; c-Si, crystalline silicon; Al-BSF, aluminum back-surface field; MWT, metal wrap-through; PERC, passivated emitter and rear cell; TOPCon, tunnel-oxide passivated contact; SHJ, silicon heterojunction; BC, back-contact; PCE , power conversion efficiency; FF , fill factor; V oc , open-circuit voltage; LCO, laser contact opening; LDSE, laser-doped selective emitter; LIFT, laser-induced forward transfer; PTP, pattern transfer printing; LECO, laser-enhanced contact optimization; LIA, laser-induced annealing; LFC, laser-fired contact; LEI, laser edge isolation; TLS, thermal laser separation; poly-Si, polycrystalline silicon; HAZ, heat-affected zone; a-Si:H, hydrogenated amorphous silicon.

title: Porous fiber sintered β-type Ti-Zr-Nb-Sn biomedical alloys with superelasticity: Application towards cancellous bone implant with low porosity case
abstract: Porous metal fiber sintered alloys are promising candidates for bone repair due to their readily tunable porosity with a wide range and fully interconnected open pore networks. In this work, the porous superelastic β-type Ti-Zr-Nb-Sn alloys with porosities of 50%, 55%, and 60% were fabricated via metal fiber sintering for the application towards cancellous bone implant with low porosity case. The interior structure in porous specimens shows a three-dimensional network of bonded fibers. All solution-treated porous specimens consist exclusively of a single β phase. An excellent combination of mechanical properties is achieved: a low elastic modulus (1.7–4.9 GPa) matching that of human cancellous bone with a low porosity case, a substantial recovery strain of 3.3–4.4%, and yield stresses ranging from 28 to 53 MPa. The stress-induced martensite transformation of β → α″ occurred during loading and was responsible for the superelastic recovery. The elastic modulus and yield stress are porosity-dependent and deviate from the theoretical values because of microstructural heterogeneities of the sintered fiber network. Importantly, the present Ti-Zr-Nb-Sn fiber sintering ensures an interstitial impurity-free β‑phase matrix in porous specimens. The present results underscore the potential of these porous Ti-Zr-Nb-Sn specimens for advanced applications in orthopaedic implants.

title: Metallic glass wire-based springs
abstract: In this work, we present the manufacturing, demonstration, and characterization of metallic glass (MG) springs. MG springs are manufactured by thermoplastically shaping MG wires, demonstrating exceptional performance in quality factor and elastic displacement. These springs are manufactured using two processes with differing resultant properties. The first is a single-step process that elastically and plastically deforms the MG wire at room temperature into a helical spring geometry, resulting in the formation of substantial shear band density where the remaining elastic stresses are then released upon heating. The second is a two-step process that incrementally deforms the MG wire entirely within the elastic regime at room temperature then applies heating and cooling cycles to realize a final shear-band-free geometry. The quality factor, spring constant, and maximum elastic force and displacement of these fabricated MG springs are compared to state-of-the-art spring steel and stainless-steel springs of the same geometry. We found that the elastically formed MG spring exhibits a higher quality factor (35%) and higher elastic displacement (2x) than state-of-the-art springs. The scalable, fast, and precise manufacturing processes presented in this work combined with the superior performance compared to state-of-the-art materials makes a strong case for the widespread use of MG springs.

title: Mesenchymal stem cell membrane coating of gelatin nanospheres with drug release ability for inflammatory tissue targeting
abstract: Abstract Improvements in drug delivery have been achieved using nanospheres to prolong drug efficacy, accelerate absorption, and target tissues with ongoing inflammation. Although nanospheres have numerous pharmacokinetic advantages their tissue-targeting ability is poor. In contrast, mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) accumulate in high numbers in inflammatory tissues via the interaction between CXC-chemokine receptor 4 (CXCR4) expressed on MSC and stromal cell-derived factor 1 (SDF-1) secreted during inflammation. Therefore, this study investigated coating gelatin nanospheres (GNS) with MSC membranes (MSC-GNS) by extrusion and ultrasonication methods to enhance their inflammatory tissue tropism. ζ-potential measurements, western blotting and single-particle analysis of MSC-GNS by flow cytometry demonstrated the GNS surface was successfully coated with MSC membranes. Dot blotting demonstrated the binding ability of CXCR4 for SDF-1 was retained by MSC-GNS but absent for MSC-membrane-free GNS. The blood clearance of MSC-GNS was examined by their intravenous injection into mice. Although MSC-GNS and GNS were retained during the early distribution phase, MSC-GNS had a higher retention than GNS during the later elimination phase. Finally, we investigated the tissue distribution of MSC-GNS by intravenous injection into a mouse model of liver fibrosis and their potential therapeutic effect on liver fibrosis. We found a higher accumulation of MSC-GNS in inflamed livers and higher blood retention compared with MSC-membrane-free GNS. Furthermore, MSC-GNS loaded with an anti-fibrotic agent (LSKL, a 4-amino acid peptide that inhibits fibrosis progression) had an enhanced therapeutic effect on liver fibrosis than uncoated nanoparticles. Therefore, MSC-GNS might be a drug carrier with inflammatory tissue targeting and controlled drug release abilities. Synopsis Table of Contents Graphic Mesenchymal stem cell membrane coated gelatin nanosphere as DDS nanocarrier

title: Growth-induced mechanical gradients and directional stiffness in ultrathin low-temperature ALD alumina coatings
abstract: Low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) produces hydroxyl-rich alumina films whose mechanical response at nanometer thickness remains poorly understood. Here, alumina coatings deposited at 50 °C on native-oxide Si(100) were studied over the 1–112 nm thickness range by combining spherical nanoindentation, laser-induced surface acoustic wave spectroscopy (LiSAWS), thickness metrology, and atomistic simulations. Spherical nanoindentation gave out-of-plane moduli of about 137–126 GPa from 7 to 112 nm, consistent with the intrinsic bulk-like response predicted for hydroxylated amorphous alumina. By contrast, LiSAWS yielded lower in-plane moduli and dropped to 60 ± 26 GPa in the ultrathin regime, revealing reduced lateral network connectivity during the earliest ALD stages. The divergence between both methods indicates a growth-induced mechanical gradient that is not directly resolved by TEM or ellipsometry alone. Thicker films remained mechanically compliant, with yield strength around 4.5–5.2 GPa. These findings explain why nanolaminate architectures can provide mechanical advantages over a single thicker monolithic alumina layer in barrier applications for flexible electronics, optoelectronics, and related devices.

title: Generative Bayesian machine learning framework for inverse alloy designing of lightweight high entropy alloy with target density and experimental validation
abstract: Lightweight high entropy alloys (LHEAs) are promising next-generation structural materials due to their excellent strength–ductility synergy and thermal stability. However, accurate control of alloy density remains challenging because severe lattice distortion in multicomponent systems often leads to deviations from conventional rule-of-mixture predictions. In this work, a generative Bayesian machine learning framework is developed for the inverse design of LHEAs with targeted density values. Physically informed descriptors based on elemental properties, including atomic weight, valence electron concentration, atomic size mismatch, melting temperature, mixing enthalpy, and electronegativity mismatch, are used to train supervised machine learning models. A Bayesian-optimised extra trees regression model predicts alloy density with high accuracy while providing uncertainty estimates through ensemble variance. A complementary phase classification model ensures physically plausible phase stability. The trained models are integrated into a generative inverse-design workflow to propose candidate LHEA compositions satisfying user-defined density constraints. Selected alloys are synthesised by vacuum arc melting, and experimentally measured densities validate the model predictions. The combined computational-experimental approach demonstrates a practical pathway for uncertainty-aware machine learning-guided discovery and experimental validation of lightweight high entropy alloys to accelerate alloy design.

title: A novel quadratic multilayer heterostructure framework with physics-informed learning for arbitrarily graded rotor disks in high-speed textile spinning
abstract: High-speed textile spinning rotors are subjected to severe centrifugal and thermo-mechanical loads that can induce stress concentrations and interfacial failure. To address these challenges, this study develops a novel multilayer heterostructure quadratic inhomogeneous (MHQI) framework for arbitrarily graded functionally graded material (FGM) rotors. The formulation employs a second-order layerwise representation to capture complex material gradation with minimal discretization. An axisymmetric rotating-disk model is formulated by incorporating material gradation, porosity, thermal effects, and centrifugal loading. The results are validated against finite element analysis, existing multilayer models, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The MHQI model achieves FEA-level accuracy using only two sublayers. Comparable accuracy in conventional multilayer formulations requires eight sublayers, representing a 75% reduction in layerwise discretization. The formulation also eliminates artificial stress discontinuities. For a Ti–ceramic rotor, centrifugal loading dominates the structural response, whereas thermal effects remain secondary. Controlled porosity reduces the effective density and centrifugal stress by up to 25%, while material gradation lowers the radial and hoop stresses by up to 25% and 20%, respectively. The PINN framework further identifies the optimal exponential grading configuration that minimizes the peak hoop stress and accurately recovers unknown gradation parameters from response data. The present framework is limited to steady-state operation at a constant angular velocity and does not consider transient thermo-mechanical effects or rotor dynamic imbalances.

title: Ginseng-derived exosome-like nanoparticles delivered miR-2118 suppresses ferroptosis by regulating zinc homeostasis via SLC39A7 targeting to alleviate osteoarthritis
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease marked by irreversible cartilage destruction, lacking effective disease-modifying therapies. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (PELNs) have emerged as promising natural nanocarriers. Here, we successfully isolated exosome-like nanoparticles from ginseng (GELNs) and evaluated their therapeutic potential for OA. GELNs were efficiently internalized by chondrocyte-derived SW1353 cells and mitigated IL-1β-induced apoptosis, inflammation, extracellular matrix degradation, and ferroptosis. Integrated transcriptomic and small RNA sequencing revealed significant enrichment of ferroptosis-related pathways and identified ginseng-specific miR-2118 as a key functional cargo within GELNs. Mechanistically, miR-2118 directly targeted the 3′-UTR of the zinc transporter SLC39A7. This targeting downregulated SLC39A7 expression, thereby restoring intracellular zinc homeostasis, improving mitochondrial dysfunction, and ultimately blocking the ferroptosis cascade. These cytoprotective effects were reversed by a miR-2118 inhibitor. In a mouse OA model induced by anterior cruciate ligament transection, intra-articular injection of GELNs markedly attenuated cartilage degradation and subchondral bone destruction. Our findings reveals that GELNs inhibit chondrocyte ferroptosis through the delivery of ginseng-specific miR-2118, which targets the SLC39A7/zinc homeostasis axis, underscoring the unique medicinal value of ginseng. Furthermore, these findings highlight the potential of PELNs as carriers for endogenous miRNAs capable of cross-species communication, providing an expandable nanotherapeutic platform for the treatment of OA.

title: Unexpected side Cu corrosion at Cu/MoO3 interface in Cu-based n-i-p type perovskite solar cells
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are regarded as a promising photovoltaic technology due to their low fabrication cost and simple processing; however, their commercialization is hindered by limited operational stability and unclear degradation pathways. In this work, we systematically investigate the degradation behavior of Cu electrodes in n-i-p structured PSCs under continuous light illumination. The results reveal pronounced side corrosion of the Cu electrode at the MoO 3 interface, while the Cu region overlapping with the bottom ITO electrode remains comparatively stable. To mitigate this issue, a thin Bi interfacial layer was introduced between MoO 3 and Cu, leading to significantly improved device stability and suppressed corrosion. TOF-SIMS 3D mapping and depth profiling confirm extensive iodine migration toward the Cu electrode in aged reference devices, whereas this diffusion is effectively blocked in Bi-modified structures. Based on these observations, a degradation mechanism is proposed in which light-induced perovskite decomposition generates iodide species that migrate to the Cu electrode, triggering Cu corrosion, while the underlying ITO layer partially protects the overlap region by facilitating charge extraction. This study elucidates the origin of Cu side corrosion and provides an effective interfacial engineering strategy for enhancing the durability of Cu-electrode PSCs

title: Acoustic energy dissipation mechanisms in Tesla valve-inspired acoustic metamaterials for tunable low-frequency sound absorption in high-strength cementitious composites
abstract: Low-frequency noise is difficult to mitigate with conventional porous absorbers because long-wavelength sound typically requires large material thicknesses, which limits the use of such absorbers. This study develops a Tesla valve-inspired asymmetric coiled-channel (ACC) metamaterial embedded in high-strength mortar for tunable low-frequency sound absorption. Thermoviscous acoustic simulations were combined with in-situ pressure–velocity probe measurements to clarify how coiling angle, leaf length, number of leaves, and Helmholtz opening geometry control the resonance frequency, absorption magnitude, and acoustic energy dissipation. Increasing the coiling angle shifted the experimental absorption peak from 835 Hz to 467.7 Hz, corresponding to a 44% decrease in resonance frequency. However, peak absorption increased only up to an intermediate configuration, but then decreased at higher geometric complexity, indicating that excessive tortuosity increases acoustic resistance and limits wave penetration. Leaf length provided secondary low-frequency tuning, whereas the number of leaves and Helmholtz opening controlled modal interaction, bandwidth evolution, and localized frequency-selective absorption. The results demonstrate that optimal absorption is governed not by maximizing geometric complexity but by balancing path elongation, thermoviscous dissipation, impedance matching, and acoustic accessibility. This work establishes a practical geometry–performance design framework for compact, tunable, structurally integrated cementitious acoustic metamaterials.

title: Interface-mediated precipitation-recrystallization synergy in ARB-fabricated Al-Ag-Sc/A1050 laminated composites governing strength-ductility-wear coupling
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive study on the synergistic microstructural and tribological optimization of an A1050/Al-Ag-Sc/A1050 multilayer laminated system processed by up to nine accumulative roll bonding (ARB) cycles. Through combined FE-SEM-EBSD analysis, tensile testing, microhardness evaluation, and sliding wear measurements, a direct correlation between deformation-induced microstructural refinement, texture evolution, and multifunctional property enhancement is established. Progressive grain subdivision governed by continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX), with limited localized continuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX), led to the formation of an ultrafine-grained (UFG) microstructure with a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) and a weakened rolling texture. These transformations increased hardness from ∼ 62 to ∼ 95 HV, yield strength (YS) from 166 to 412 MPa, and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) from 205 to 420 MPa, while elongation remained moderate at ∼6.3% even at the highest deformation level. Concurrently, wear rate decreased from 9 × 10 −6 to 1.56 × 10 −6 mm 3 ·m −1 and the coefficient of friction (COF) from 0.60 to 0.20, demonstrating an ∼83% improvement in wear resistance. Fractographic analyses confirmed a controlled transition from deep dimple rupture to fine dimple-shear mixed fracture without brittle cleavage, maintaining ductile failure mechanisms throughout processing. The novelty of this study lies in unveiling the cooperative role of nanoscale precipitation, texture weakening, and recrystallization-controlled grain boundary engineering in simultaneously promoting mechanical strength and tribological durability. These findings highlight ARB as an effective processing strategy for designing lightweight aluminum alloys with balanced structural integrity and surface wear resistance for demanding engineering applications.

title: LLM-driven automated literature review and taxonomy generation for powder metallurgy
abstract: The exponential growth of scientific literature in powder metallurgy presents significant challenges for comprehensive knowledge synthesis. Traditional manual review methods are insufficient for processing large-scale corpora, while existing automated approaches often lack semantic depth and contextual interpretation. This paper introduces a novel framework employing Large Language Model (LLM) agents to automate literature review and taxonomic organization of powder metallurgy research. We analyze 26,254 papers through a structured two-tier methodology. The first tier performs stochastic sampling and iterative classification, generating preliminary topic clusters subsequently refined into coherent categories through agent-based reasoning. The second tier implements contextual comparison and cross-document reasoning, where each paper is analyzed alongside semantically similar studies with iterative refinement until classification confidence reaches a predetermined threshold. This context-aware comparative reasoning distinguishes the proposed framework from conventional single-pass LLM classification approaches. The framework organizes the powder metallurgy literature into 15 coherent categories, revealing emerging research trajectories and knowledge gaps across the field. Expert validation confirms classification reliability, with a 90% unanimous agreement rate and Fleiss’ κ = 0.93.
