This work contributes methodological innovations in LLM-based scientific knowledge processing and domain-specific insights for powder metallurgy research, establishing a foundation for intelligent literature review systems across scientific disciplines.

title: Design-oriented multiscale shear behavior of sandstone-concrete interfaces via experiments and physics-informed learning
abstract: Sandstone-concrete interfaces are critical heterogeneous material interfaces in rock-concrete composite structures, where insufficient shear resistance can trigger interfacial instability under low confinement. The key design challenge is to establish a quantitative structure–property link between engineered interface morphology, damage evolution and shear response, while providing a physically consistent prediction tool for untested loading conditions. Here, serrated sandstone-concrete interfaces were examined under normal stress of 0.1–0.8 MPa through 8 direct shear tests combined with acoustic emission, digital image correlation, three-dimensional morphology characterization and ODE-constrained PINN modeling. Peak shear stress increased from 1.49 to 2.94 MPa with normal stress, accompanied by a transition from serration-interlocking brittle fracture to compaction-assisted frictional wear and root shearing. Acoustic-emission and digital-image-correlation results reveal that tensile opening is progressively suppressed and shear-dominated distributed damage develops. Three-dimensional surface metrics further show interface smoothing, with S a and S q decreasing by 20.8 % and 23.5 %, respectively. The proposed model, trained only on 0.1–0.6 MPa curves, predicted unseen 0.7–0.8 MPa responses with 9.17 % normalized root-mean-square error and peak errors below 2 %. This work provides design-relevant guidance for tailoring sandstone-concrete interface morphology and a physics-constrained framework for predicting shear resistance.

title: Destabilisation temperature effects on the microstructural evolution and dry-sliding wear response of a 15 wt% Cr high chromium cast iron
abstract: This study examines a hypoeutectic 15 wt% Cr cast iron in the as-cast state and after destabilisation treatments at 800, 900 and 980 °C (10 °C/min, water quenched). Secondary carbides (SC) nucleated, during the heating phase, mainly in the martensitic region adjacent to Cr-rich M 7 C 3 eutectic carbides and became progressively distributed within the matrix with increasing temperature and time. Mean SC size increased from 0.008 to 0.025 um 2 between 800 and 980 °C, while carbide volume fraction increased from 2.9% to 4.4% between 800 and 900 °C. Holding at 980 °C for 90 min intensified precipitation, increasing mean carbide size to 0.067 um 2 and volume fraction to 8.2%, and raising matrix microhardness by ∼ 90% relative to the as-cast state. Reciprocating dry sliding against Al 2 O 3 (20 N) produced progressively smaller wear tracks with increasing destabilisation temperature. Wear coefficient decreased by ∼ 50%, 71%, and 77% at 800, 900, and 980 °C, respectively. SEM analysis revealed a transition from severe abrasion with matrix grooving and carbide micro-cracking in the as-cast state to a milder wear regime after destabilisation. The wear response is governed primarily by the local carbide-matrix architecture generated during destabilisation rather than by bulk hardness alone.

title: Cold spray additive manufacturing of Inconel 718/Cu and Inconel 718/GRCop-42 multi-materials: effects of deposition sequence on interface and thermal conductivity
abstract: Fabricating high-performance Inconel 718 (IN718) multi-material structures with high-conductivity copper alloys is critical for advanced thermal management applications, yet controlling interfacial thermal transport remains a significant challenge. This study systematically investigates the role of deposition sequence and post-processing heat treatment on the interfacial microstructure, and thermal conductivity of IN718–Cu and IN718–GRCop-42 joints fabricated via Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing (CSAM). Directional heat transport was isolated by evaluating in-plane conductivity via the Transient Plane Source (TPS) method and through-plane conductivity via Laser Flash Analysis (LFA). The results show that deposition sequence strongly affects the dominant heat-transport mechanism: the Cu--IN718 material system yielded a superior in-plane thermal conductivity of ∼170 W/m·K by bypassing interfacial boundaries, whereas through-plane transport across all configurations was severely constrained by interfacial thermal resistance in the build direction. Furthermore, a standard two-step aging treatment induces a remarkable 131% increase in the in-plane thermal conductivity of GRCop-42/IN718 joints (from 48 to 111 W/m·K), driven by localized microstructural evolution within the copper-alloy regions, showing grain coarsening and reduction in Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM), indicating stress relief and defect recovery. Overall, this work clarifies how deposition sequence and post-deposition heat treatment govern interfacial quality and thermal performance in CSAM-fabricated Ni-based/Cu-based multi-materials.

title: Additively manufactured Weaire–Phelan Ti6Al4V scaffolds for bone repair: in vitro biomechanical evaluation and osseointegration insights using MG63 osteoblast-like cells
abstract: The repair of large bone defects resulting due to trauma, tumor resection, or degenerative diseases remains a critical challenge in orthopedics. This study investigates additively manufactured Ti6Al4V scaffolds designed using the Weaire-Phelan (WP) structure, a strut-based lattice scaffold that apes trabecular bone. Scaffolds with varying porosity (50–90%) were fabricated through direct metal printing (DMP) applying three different printing parameters – Robust , Good and Normal . The structural, mechanical, and biological performances of these scaffolds were assessed through various tests, including microstructural characterization (XRD, FESEM, micro-CT), axial compression testing, computational fatigue analysis, and cytocompatibility testing using MG63 bone cells. Obtained results showed that WPD scaffolds, with 70% porosity, provided the best balance of mechanical strength, cellular adhesion, and biomineralization for bone ingrowth. These scaffolds supported extended filopodia formation, high metabolic activity, and sustained apatite deposition over 28 days. The opposite effect was noticed for highly porous scaffolds (i.e. RC_WPD90), where lower cell spreading and mineral formation occurred highlighting the significance of optimized pore architecture. This study showcases the potential of WP-based Ti6Al4V scaffolds for bone tissue engineering, emphasizing the importance of optimized pore architecture in enhancing osseointegration and structural integrity of implants.

title: Complex structural evolution in BaTiO3 single crystals caused by the coexistence of competing anharmonic potentials
abstract: BaTiO 3 (BTO) was the first ferroelectric perovskite oxide discovered in the 1940′th.. It was also the first ferroelectric compound without hydrogen bonds. Its wide applicability, together with its simple cubic structure, directly intensified and inspired research on perovskite oxides, leading to the discovery of many additional oxides. Although known for more than 80 years, refined and newly developed high-resolution experimental techniques have uncovered novel results that have advanced physical insight into this material, which are challenging for theoreticians, and there is a need for novel ideas. Here we show that the complex phase diagram of BTO can be understood based on the coexistence of a double-well potential and a sixth-order one, where the former is related to the polarizable cluster mass TiO 6 , and the latter describes the local dynamics of the Ti ion in the octahedral cluster. In light of new results from birefringence experiments, the phase diagram of BTO is reinterpreted.

title: Morphological and crystallographic synergy in texture inheritance of cold-drawn pearlitic steels
abstract: Pearlitic steel wires are essential for applications demanding ultra-high strength in fine diameters, yet their performance depends on precise microstructural control during thermo-mechanical processing and cold drawing. This study clarifies that texture inheritance is governed by a dual preferred orientation formed during pre-drawing: morphological alignment of cementite lamellae along the drawing axis and the concurrent development of a ferritic <110>//drawing-axis fiber texture. When both features are continuous, the deformed pearlitic structure provides favorable sites for crystallographically constrained reverse transformation and subsequent pearlitic transformation, enabling partial preservation of the <110> fiber texture. In contrast, locally severe deformation in unfavorably oriented colonies produces fragmented cementite and nanoscale equiaxed ferrite structures, which disturb orientation continuity and reduce inheritance efficiency. By separating these favorable and detrimental microstructural paths, this work establishes a strain-dependent design framework for optimizing inherited texture and torsional ductility in high-strength pearlitic wires.

title: Interfacial hydrogen bonding and phase-inversion kinetics drive 3D pore networks in PLA–CNF membranes for dialysis-grade selectivity
abstract: Bio-based dialysis membranes could reduce polymer waste and additive leaching risks associated with conventional petroleum-derived dialyzers, but most bio-based systems have not been validated for dialysis permselectivity ( i.e., high passage of uremic toxins with protein retention) nor linked mechanistically to structure formation. Here, we report fully biobased poly(lactic acid)–cellulose nanofiber (PLA–CNF) composite membranes fabricated via scalable casting–phase inversion. CNF loading increased porosity from 58.5% to 75.7% and decreased water contact angle from 116° to 65°, enabling a ∼ 3 × higher water flux from 53.4 to 166.4 L m −2 h −1 at 0.5 ± 0.025 bar. In dialysis-mimicking separations, the membranes exhibited remarkably high solute passage, i.e., urea clearance ˃94% and creatinine clearance ˃ 85, with albumin rejection up to 78%. In addition, both pristine and composite membranes were cytocompatible (>85% viability for L929 and Vero cells). These results position PLA–CNF membranes as a sustainable platform for dialyzers and liquid purification modules, with future optimization targeting antifouling/charge-selective interfaces and long-term hemocompatibility under realistic flow regimes.

title: Engineering bi-directional microstructural heterogeneity through mechanical surface treatment
abstract: By integrating regions with distinct mechanical properties, heterogeneous materials can offer a wide range of mechanical properties and may even surpass the mechanical and functional properties observed in their homogeneous counterparts. Impact-based mechanical surface treatments have proven highly effective in generating microstructural heterogeneity by introducing severe plastic deformation at the surface and subsurface layers, resulting in gradient grain refinement and microstructural modifications while preserving the original properties of the core material. Herein, we employed a strategically modulated ultrasonic shot peening (USP) technique to engineer materials exhibiting bi-directional heterogeneity, i.e., both planar (across the specimen surface) and transversal (in-depth), specifically by creating gradients in both grain size and geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density. The innovative localized treatment uses masks of various geometric patterns to selectively shield or expose designated regions of the specimens during USP treatment. Tensile tests performed on the USPed specimens evidenced modulated material strengthening, supported by site-specific variations in microstructural features, microhardness, and residual stress distribution. The findings indicate that this novel USP strategy can be implemented to enable engineering materials with heterogeneous structures and tailored mechanical characteristics.

title: Emerging entropy-stabilized ceramics for high-temperature thermal-environmental barrier coatings
abstract: The gas-turbine sector is on the verge of a green revolution with the advent of carbon-free, hydrogen- and ammonia-based fuels. Meanwhile, metallic superalloys in the turbine hot-section are being replaced by lightweight but high-temperature resistant silicon carbide-based, ceramic matrix composites. Adoption of new fuels could be complicated as the water vapour produced by their combustion volatilizes the composites, causing rapid erosion and failure. Currently, is utilized as an environmental barrier coating on such composite components, however, the increased vapour content from the adoption of new fuels would require better safeguards. Consequently, coupled with the push for higher efficiency in gas turbines, the industry is hunting for the next generation of thermal-environmental barrier coatings. Catering to this need, academia has uncovered a new class of entropy-stabilized, rare-earth silicates with low thermal conductivity. This article addresses major research aspects of these candidate coating materials, from material engineering and synthesis to coating deposition and subsequent performance characterisation. A section is also devoted to computational methods to guide and aid experimental research, for keeping pace with rapid technological innovations. This review provides a foreword to entropy-stabilized, rare-earth silicate environmental barrier coatings, scrutinizes current research trends and recommends guidelines for future work.

title: Beyond viscosity curves: A critical rheological perspectives for converging material extrusion additive manufacturing and powder injection molding
abstract: Rheological behaviour of highly filled polymer feedstocks critically governs their processability in material extrusion (MEX) additive manufacturing and powder injection molding (PIM). These converging technologies require robust flow control to achieve defect-free, dimensionally accurate parts. Despite extensive rheology-related literature, clear and transferable links between measured properties and process optimization remain scarce. This review summarizes rheological strategies for improving processing of highly filled compounds, with emphasis on maximum packing, wall slip, yield stress, powder-binder segregation and pressure-dependent flow. It also highlights conceptually inconsistent practices, including the widespread use of simple shear-thinning models for structurally complex feedstocks or activation energy evaluated at a constant shear rate. By focusing on a limited set of physically meaningful rheological parameters and their relation to typical processing failures, the review outlines a framework for material selection and formulation optimization in converging MEX and PIM technologies.

title: Directional acoustic meta-sensor with gradient impedance matching meta-material
abstract: We propose a gradient-impedance directional sensing metamaterial achieving simultaneous high sound pressure gain and precision. Featuring a 5-stage concentric arc cascade channel with continuously varying cross-sections, it forms a 4-channel orthogonal array to calculate incident sound direction via the orthogonal difference method. This gradient cross-section acts as a broadband impedance transformer, enhancing the linear physical gain by 66.0% compared to conventional designs. It excites efficient localized Mie resonances within 300–1500 Hz, achieving a peak sound pressure gain of 13.7 times (22.7 dB) and an average gain of 4.7 times (13.4 dB).To decouple phase interference perturbations from third-order spatial harmonics, we introduce an analytical multipole expansion-based error compensation algorithm. This improves 360° omnidirectional tracking accuracy by 17.2%. Absolute positioning residuals are restricted within a ± 5.0° confidence interval, yielding a final prediction accuracy of 89.3%. This hardware-algorithm synergistic approach inspires compact, high-fidelity acoustic positioning terminals in complex soundscapes.

title: Evaluating the influence of surface texture design on the mechanical performance of interbody spinal cage devices
abstract: Intervertebral body fusion devices (IBFDs) are crucial medical devices that provide stability and promote bone fusion between vertebrae. This study investigated the effects of tailoring surface features and textures of Ti-6Al-4V IBFDs, on their mechanical performance, particularly the implant-to-bone interfacial bond. The textured surfaces were obtained using powder bed fusion – laser beam/ metal (PBF-LB/M) additive manufacturing (AM), along with electric-discharge machining (EDM). The influence of both the textured surface design and the manufacturing technique were assessed based on the mechanical performance of the textured surfaces. The EDM-generated surfaces exhibited greater geometric accuracy and more homogeneous surface textures but showed no significant performance difference compared with textures and features generated by PBF-LB/M (P < 0.05). The texture design was found to be the most influential variable tested. The texture with the most favourable biomechanical outputs was a parallel ridged texture. This was concluded based on the low damage on the sawbone in contact with the IBFD, combined with the mechanical performance of the texture design relative to several tested textures. The presence, type, and configuration of designed surface features along with texture have a significant (P < 0.05) impact on IBFD biomechanical performance at the IBFD-to-sawbone interface compared with a flat AM control surface.

title: Characterization of dynamic recrystallization phenomena in newly designed advanced austenitic stainless steels for developing liquid hydrogen storage technology
abstract: This paper presents the dynamic recrystallization (DRX) behaviour of three newly designed austenitic stainless steel (ASS) compositions (designated as SS, SS-Mn, and SS-Nb) to develop and produce advanced high-strength materials for liquid hydrogen (LH 2 ) storage systems through thermomechanical processing. While Alloy SS is essentially 304 L with 0.09 wt% N, SS-Nb is its microalloyed variant with 0.1 wt% Nb and reduced N content (0.035 wt%). Alloy SS-Mn is based on 201LN grade with reduced Ni (5.4 wt%) content and alloyed with high Mn (7 wt%) and N (0.2 wt%) contents. To establish the characteristics of dynamic softening, uniaxial single-hit hot compression experiments were conducted using Gleeble 3800 thermomechanical simulator at 950–1200 °C, 0.001–0.1 s −1 . Hot compression stress–strain analysis using the Poliak–Jonas criterion and EBSD reveals discontinuous DRX (DDRX) as the dominant mechanism in low SFE ASSs under varying temperatures and strain rates. Rising temperature and strain rate promote conversion of low- to high-angle grain boundaries, increasing twins and DRX, with SS and SS-Nb showing earlier DRX despite Nb drag, while SS-Mn exhibits higher stresses and slower DDRX due to solid-solution strengthening, sluggish boundary migration, and residual δ-ferrite in SS/SS-Nb aids recrystallization pathways, highlighting how composition and processing govern ASS microstructures.

title: Aging precipitation and corrosion resistance of peripheral coarse grained layer and matrix in Al-7.2Zn-1.9Mg-2Cu extruded profiles under multi-stage aging treatments
abstract: Peripheral coarse-grained (PCG) layers are frequently formed in solution-treated Al-Zn-Mg-Cu alloy profiles, but the distinct aging responses of PCGs and fine matrix grains (FGs) and their effects on corrosion resistance and mechanical properties remain unclear. In this study, the correlation between microstructure and properties was investigated under five aging regimes using TEM, quasi-in-situ tensile testing, quasi-in-situ EBSD, and intergranular corrosion (IGC) tests. The results reveal that IGC susceptibility is governed by precipitates, with grain morphology playing a secondary but non-negligible role. Under peak aging, coarse-grained specimens show lower corrosion resistance due to the greater continuity of grain-boundary precipitates, whereas in the over-aged state they exhibit improved resistance owing to enlarged precipitate spacing. The fine-grained specimen under natural aging exhibits the poorest corrosion resistance. Mechanical properties are mainly controlled by precipitate size and the corresponding dislocation-precipitate interaction. Fine η’ precipitates promote dislocation shearing and strain localization, causing early cleavage in coarse grains, whereas coarsened η precipitates after retrogression and re-aging treatment favor bypassing and multi-slip activation, improving deformation homogeneity and elongation. Among the investigated treatments, the triple-aging regime at 100 °C/6h + 130 °C/12 h + 170 °C/2h achieves the best strength-corrosion synergy by suppressing excessive precipitate coarsening.

title: High-throughput design of refractory multi principal element alloys for laser processing
abstract: Refractory multi principal element alloys are promising for high temperature structural applications, but their high melting temperatures and segregation during bulk processing restrict conventional manufacturing routes. Laser-based melting or remelting enables localized high energy input and rapid cooling for these chemistries, yet crack-free processing remains a primary bottleneck. A key gap is the absence of screening workflows that explicitly target laser melting and validate predictions under relevant thermal conditions. Here, we implement staged screening plus validation framework that down-selects refractory ternary compositions and tests whether predicted solidification behavior remains compatible with laser remelting. A total of 3420 ternary compositions in the Hf–Mo–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr system, covering all twenty ternary subsystems, were screened by equilibrium CALculation of PHAse Diagrams (CALPHAD) in TC-Python simulations for body-centered cubic (BCC) structure stability above 1000 °C, liquidus between 1680 °C and 2000 °C, and ΔT ≤ 50 °C to select six candidates, then ranked by Scheil Gulliver predictions and the Clyne crack susceptibility coefficient. Nb 25 Ti 20 Zr 55 and Hf 45 Nb 30 Ti 25 remained BCC dominated after arc melting and homogenization at 1350 °C for 1 h and successfully produced crack-free low porosity single track melt pools at 15.0 to 30.0 J mm −2 . This framework links thermodynamic down selection to an operational crack-free remelt criterion.

title: Construction and experimental validation of a machine learning-based design system for high-Mn steels aimed at strength-ductility synergy optimization
abstract: To address the low yield strength (YS) and empirical design limitations of traditional high-Mn austenitic steels, this study proposes a machine learning (ML)-based integrated design approach and establishes a Machine Learning Design System (MLDS). A database of 270 datasets coupling nine alloying elements and two heat treatment parameters was constructed. Following Pearson correlation analysis of the feature set, XGBoost and Random Forest (RF) were selected based on mean absolute error (MAE) results from systematic benchmarking for forward property prediction and inverse compositional design, respectively. A closed-loop strategy enabled high-throughput screening of one million candidates. Guided by target properties (UTS ≈ 1100 MPa, YS ≈ 500 MPa, EL ≈ 65 %), optimized alloys were experimentally validated. The 1000 °C solution-treated specimen achieved a UTS of 1137 MPa, YS of 490 MPa, and EL of 61 %, while the 1100 °C specimen exhibited 1053 MPa, 472 MPa, and 65 %, respectively, with prediction errors within 8 %. Microstructural analysis revealed that the synergy between grain refinement and dispersed precipitates at 1000 °C enhanced YS, while precipitate-induced stress concentration promoted deformation twinning during mid-to-high strain stages, sustaining high strain hardening rates. This work demonstrates a successful data-driven paradigm for the accelerated development of complex alloy systems.

title: Pulse regulation enables retained thickening of Mo2C films during molten-carbonate electroreduction
abstract: Retaining electrochemically generated carbide films on reactive metal substrates is limited by the coupling between carbon supply, substrate consumption, and product detachment. Here, Mo electrodes in LiCl-KCl-K 2 CO 3 melts were used to examine how pulse regulation controls retained Mo 2 C film growth during carbonate electroreduction. Although Ni and Mo showed similar cyclic voltammetric responses in the main carbonate-reduction region, phase and microstructural analyses revealed a substrate-dependent pathway on Mo. High current density produced dendritic carbonaceous deposits together with Mo 2 C, whereas low current density suppressed isolated carbon deposition and promoted interfacial Mo 2 C formation. However, prolonged galvanostatic electrolysis continuously consumed the near-surface Mo substrate, generated a porous support region, and caused Mo 2 C detachment. The collected detached products agreed with the calculated Mo2C-equivalent mass, showing that formation was not the limiting step; retention was. Pulse electrolysis resolved this formation-detachment behavior by temporally regulating carbon supply and interfacial reaction. A continuous Mo 2 C layer formed at the early stage and thickened to approximately 35 μm as a surface-retained layer. These results refine the post-carburization view of Mo 2 C growth and identify pulse regulation as a route for retained carbide-film growth during molten-carbonate electroreduction.

title: Processing–structure–property relationships in PS–SiO2 nanocomposite foams: a comparative study of batch and extrusion foaming for thermal insulation applications
abstract: Polystyrene (PS) foams are widely used as thermal insulators; however, further improvements in their performance require control of their cell size and scalable manufacturing strategies. Nanosilica (SiO 2 ) was proposed as an effective nucleating agent in laboratory-scale batch foaming. Yet, a knowledge gap remains regarding how nanosilica influences foam morphology in a continuous and industrially relevant technology as extrusion foaming. In this work, PS-SiO 2 nanocomposite foams were produced through two routes –batch and extrusion foaming– to establish process–structure–property relationships. Results show that nanosilica reduces cell size in both processes, with strong differences. Batch foaming induces a higher nucleation, resulting in microcellular structures (2–5 µm) with high open-cell content. Conversely, extrusion foaming yields foams with larger (100–200 µm) closed cells. These structures lead to contrasting mechanical responses, with the extruded nanocomposite foams showing enhanced performance over pure PS. Overall, both processes enable the fabrication of advanced thermally insulating materials, while highlighting the decisive role of the foaming process in the effectiveness of nanosilica. Open-cell microcellular foams produced via batch foaming are promising candidates for vacuum insulation panels (VIP), achieving thermal conductivities in the super-insulation range, while the extruded foams offer improved insulation due to reduced radiative heat transfer.

title: Ultrasound-responsive nanobubbles modulate tumor metabolism to enhance sonodynamic immunotherapy in triple negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a major therapeutic challenge due to its aggressive nature and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome these barriers, we developed a multifunctional ultrasound-responsive nanobubble formulation (RLC). The RLC consists of a sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas core encapsulated by a lipid shell, which is co-loaded with the glycolysis inhibitor lonidamine (LND) and the sonosensitizer chlorin e6 (Ce6), and functionalized with cRGD peptides for tumor targeting. Upon ultrasound irradiation, RLC provides acoustic contrast imaging and promotes ultrasound-responsive therapeutic activation. Mechanistically, ultrasound activated Ce6 generates reactive oxygen species (ROS), resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction and impaired oxidative phosphorylation in tumor cells. Concurrently, LND inhibits glycolysis and decreases extracellular lactate accumulation, thereby mitigating acidosis associated immunosuppression. These combined strategies induce immunogenic cell death (ICD) and enhance anti-tumor immunity by stimulating dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration. Our findings suggest that the RLC nanobubbles effectively remodel the immunosuppressive TME into a more immunologically responsive state, presenting a promising theranostic strategy for TNBC management.

title: Effects of initial density and pulse width on damage evolution and ignition response of PBX under multi-pulse loading
abstract: Ignition of polymer bonded explosives (PBXs) may occur under impact loading, while the ignition mechanism remains unclear because of the non-uniformity of PBXs and the complexity of loading conditions. In this study, the dynamic mechanical behavior and ignition response of PBXs with different initial densities under different pulse width conditions were systematically investigated using an improved split Hopkinson pressure bar device. The macroscopic deformation, mechanical response, damage evolution, ignition delay time and ignition threshold were quantitatively characterized. Under multi-pulse loading, the specimens sequentially underwent axial compression, radial expansion, crack initiation and propagation, local failure and ignition reaction. Impact ignition mainly occurred during the stage of rapid damage accumulation, where hotspots were generated by localized heat accumulation dominated by shear friction. A specific incident energy ignition criterion was proposed to replace the traditional strain rate criterion, and it provided an accurate description of the experimental results. The minimum measured specific incident energy required for ignition increased with increasing pulse width, whereas the critical ignition delay time decreased as the pulse width increased. The effects of initial density, loading strength and pulse width on the damage mechanism and ignition response of PBXs were clarified.

title: Mechanical–thermochemical removal mechanisms in high‑aspect‑ratio hole fabrication by mechanical-spark assisted chemical engraving (M−SACE) in silicon nitride
abstract: Silicon nitride (Si 3 N 4 ) is highly relevant in industry, yet its hardness and chemical resistance severely limit the machining of sub-millimeter, high-aspect-ratio features. This study introduces Mechanical-Spark Assisted Chemical Engraving (M−SACE), a hybrid process combining thermochemical degradation with mechanical drilling to micromachine Si 3 N 4 . Operating in a 20 wt% NaOH solution, a tool-electrode applies electrochemical discharges while simultaneously machining the substrate. In the tested operating conditions, the material removal mechanism is identified as heating from the discharges causing NaOH to preferentially attack silicon oxynitride-based grain boundaries, weakening the ceramic and allowing mechanical removal with minimal force. Voltage and feed rate were varied for machining 100 µm deep holes, demonstrating that this synergy yields higher material removal rates, lower machining forces, and reduced surface roughness (100–200 nm Sa) compared to isolated thermochemical or mechanical effects. Process capability and stability are validated by producing 500 µm depth holes. A deep hole (400 µm diameter, 1329 µm depth) is machined as a proof-of-concept for high-aspect ratio features, demonstrating the potential of M−SACE as a low-cost solution for ceramic micromachining. This work will serve as a basis for further research on precision hybrid thermochemical machining of hard and brittle ceramics.

title: Near-Infrared responsive Bi2S3-sensitized WO3 S-scheme heterojunction photoelectrochemical coating for effective solar-driven cathodic protection
abstract: Solar-driven photoelectrochemical cathodic protection offers a green and sustainable strategy for marine metal corrosion prevention, requiring no additional energy input and causing no environmental pollution. However, practical deployment is limited by narrow spectral utilization and the loss of protection in the dark. Herein, we design a near-infrared light responsive Bi 2 S 3 -sensitized WO 3 S-scheme heterojunction (TWB) photoelectrode coating that integrates efficient photoelectric conversion with electron storage capability. The TWB photoelectrode exhibits an absorption edge extending to approximately 1500 nm, enabling efficient utilization of visible and near-infrared light. Under simulated solar irradiation, the TWB photoelectrode achieves a photocurrent density nearly eight times higher than that of pure WO 3 . When coupled with metal, the composite photoelectrode provides sustained cathodic protection in the dark, deriving from the electron-storage characteristic of WO 3 . Combined DFT calculations, in-situ XPS, and ESR analyses confirm the S-scheme charge transfer mechanism, which achieves efficient charge separation and transport while preserving highly reductive electrons in Bi 2 S 3 for effective cathodic protection. This work provides a simple and operable strategy for designing wide-spectrum responsive and energy-storing photoelectrodes that advance green and sustainable corrosion protection for marine installations.

title: Benchmarking and assessing models of reactor pressure vessel steel embrittlement
abstract: Accurate prediction of ductile-to-brittle transition temperature shifts (TTS) of steel alloys used in reactor pressure vessels (RPVs) is critical for informing safe and reliable nuclear reactor operation. Recently, numerous physically-motivated semiempirical and data-driven machine learning (ML) models of TTS for RPVs have been developed. Here, we present detailed benchmarks of the most widely used models and discuss their pros and cons based on statistical metrics on key data subsets (e.g., predicting TTS of steels under reactor life extension conditions of low flux and high fluence) and their physical trends with key variables (e.g., irradiation flux and fluence). In addition, we develop an ensemble neural network ML model that includes a physics-informed loss function component which penalizes unphysical changes in TTS with flux and fluence. We show that this model overcomes shortcomings in a similar earlier model related to extrapolation to higher fluence over a range of flux values from low flux life extension conditions up to high flux test reactor conditions. We show detailed per-alloy and highest fluence data predictions, and provide life extension predictions for the US nuclear reactor alloys. Finally, we have developed a codebase to make the use and evaluation of all models readily accessible to the broader community. It is our hope this codebase can grow to encompass new models developed by the community and function as an informative benchmark for modeling of RPV steel embrittlement in the future.

title: Lithiation-driven nanotexturing of single-crystalline KTLO for selective NH3 chemoresistive sensing
abstract: K 0.8 Ti 1.73 Li 0.27 O 4 (KTLO), a lepidocrocite-type layered potassium lithium titanate, possesses a highly anisotropic crystal framework and rapid ion-exchange capability, making it an attractive platform for surface-reactive applications. However, its chemoresistive performance has remained limited because of insufficient control over surface reactivity and defect-mediated charge transport. Here, we report a lithiation-induced nanotexturing strategy that reconfigures the surface structure and electronic states of single-crystalline KTLO, thereby enabling selective NH 3 chemoresistive sensing. The lithiation/delithiation process generates a nanotextured surface with a ∼250% increase in specific surface area while preserving the (0 1 0)-oriented layered framework and exposing additional facets, including the (1 3 0) and (1 5 0) planes. This structural evolution induces abundant oxygen vacancies and increase surface electron density, as confirmed by XPS and optical analyses. As a result, KTLO-based chemiresistors exhibit a pronounced transition in gas selectivity, changing from CO-responsive behavior to a highly selective NH 3 response with an approximately twofold signal enhancement, while suppressing responses to CO and volatile organic compounds. This selectivity switching is attributed to a change in the dominant surface reaction pathway, from classical method of oxygen ion-mediated processes to vacancy-assisted electron exchange enabled by the defect-rich surface. These findings demonstrate that lithiation-induced nanotexturing is an effective route for engineering surface-electronic coupling in layered oxides and highlight KTLO as a tunable platform for selective gas sensing and related catalytic applications

title: Reentrant hexagonal zirconia bone scaffolds with negative Poisson’s ratio enhance osteo-angiogenic coupling via topology-activated FAK-MAPK signaling axis
abstract: Negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) structures, characterized by its unique compressive-contractive mechanical behavior, show great potential for bone implants, but their optimal configuration and osteogenic mechanisms in zirconia remain unclear. This study designs reentrant hexagonal zirconia scaffolds with internal angles of 60°, 45°, and 30°, and fabricates them using digital light processing (DLP) technology. In vitro experiments demonstrate that all NPR structures enhance the proliferation, adhesion, osteogenic differentiation, and paracrine angiogenic effects of rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (rBMSCs) compared to solid control, with the 60/1.5 group being most effective. Further RNA-sequencing and pathway validation reveal the FAK-MAPK axis crucially mediates osteogenic differentiation induced by the concave topography. In vivo , the 60/1.5 scaffold implanted in rat femurs promotes faster new bone formation and more mature vascularization than the solid control. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the internal angle is a critical geometric parameter governing the osteogenic performance of NPR structures. NPR zirconia scaffolds, specifically with the 60° internal angle, show great potential for enhancing early vascularized osseointegration, thereby providing a solid theoretical foundation and experimental support for the design of high-performance zirconia implants.

title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of AZ31B alloy/304 steel resistance spot welded joints using high-entropy alloy powders with different particle sizes
abstract: This study investigated the effect of FeCoCrNiAl high entropy alloy (HEA) powders with different particle sizes (0–20, 15–53, 53–105 μm) as an interlayer on resistance spot welding of AZ31B Mg alloy to 304 stainless steel under certain process parameters. Compared with the directly welded joint, the joint with 0–20 μm powder achieved a maximum tensile-shear load of 4243 N (75% increment) and a nugget diameter of 8.03 mm (38% increment). In the joint with 0–20 μm powder, partial HEA powder was uniformly dispersed within the Mg-side nugget and formed abundant honeycomb-like interlocking structures on the fracture surface during tensile testing, which transformed the fracture mode from full interfacial fracture into a mixed fracture consisting of interfacial and pull-out fracture. Owing to the finer particle size, the other powder was heated, compacted and sintered during the welding process. Moreover, the addition of the 0–20 μm powder triggered local recrystallization at the steel side, refining steel grains and alleviated residual stress, whereas columnar grains formed on the Mg-side under welding pressure. In summary, the honeycomb like interlocking structures played a decisive role in enhancing the strength of the AZ31B/304 RSW joint, broadening the application potential of HEAs in resistance spot welding.

title: Durable and efficient passive daytime radiative cooling enabled by hierarchically porous polymer composites
abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling offers an energy-free strategy for sustainable thermal management, yet maintaining long-term outdoor durability remains a major challenge for polymer-based emitters. Here, we report a durable hybrid cooling film based on a hierarchically porous poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) matrix incorporating a dual-functional ZrO 2 @potassium titanate (PT) hybrid filler. The high-refractive-index ZrO 2 enhances broadband solar reflection through strong dielectric scattering, while PT provides ultraviolet (UV) shielding via Ti–O coordination-mediated absorption and contributes to mid-infrared emission. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of hierarchical porosity and hybrid dielectric fillers, the optimized film achieves an ultrahigh solar reflectance of ∼97.2 % and a mid-infrared emissivity of ∼0.94, corresponding to a theoretical cooling power of ∼88.1 W/m 2 . Outdoor measurements demonstrate continuous subambient cooling, maintaining an average temperature ∼1.6 °C below ambient under realistic conditions. Building energy simulations across 18 representative cities predict substantial climate-dependent benefits, with annual cooling energy savings of up to ∼21.1 GJ per building and cooling-related carbon emission reductions of up to ∼6.3 t CO 2 -eq annually in high-cooling-demand regions. Combined with excellent UV resistance, hydrophobic self-cleaning capability, mechanical robustness, and chemical stability, this work provides a scalable and durable platform for long-term passive radiative cooling and sustainable thermal management.

title: Bio-inspired wave-impedance-matched PLA/TPU graded composite structure for low-velocity impact protection
abstract: Low-velocity impact protection requires polymer structures that reduce transmitted force while limiting internal stress. Inspired by Pachyrhynchus weevil elytra, we modeled a 2 mm PLA face sheet and layered TPU core using a simplified mechanical model, wave-impedance analysis and Abaqus/Explicit simulations. Under the fixed 1 kg, 1 m s −1 , 50 mm × 50 mm × 40 mm core and 3.18–25.00 MPa modulus range, the four-layer EXP design reduced the peak bottom reaction force by 56.6% relative to the uniform core. After thickness normalization, five-layer EXP gave the lowest force, with a 4.3% reduction relative to four-layer EXP under the adopted mesh; the same reduction direction was retained across all three matched mesh schemes. It also reduced the peak von Mises stress by 18.6% and 80.5% relative to the uniform and inversely graded cores. These results define a comparative wave-impedance-guided design framework; calibrated nonlinear TPU models and impact testing remain necessary for quantitative prediction

title: Application of cerium oxide nanoparticle for root canal disinfection
abstract: This study evaluated cerium oxide nanoparticles (CNPs) as adjunctive disinfectants for refractory Enterococcus faecalis ( E. faecalis ) root canal infections. CNPs were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Cytocompatibility with MC3T3-E1 cells and human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs) was assessed using fluorescence staining and flow cytometry. The antibacterial activity of CNPs against E. faecalis and its biofilms was evaluated using colony-forming unit (CFU) counting, SEM, confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), flow cytometry, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection. CNPs induced sustained ROS generation, oxidative stress, and bacterial membrane disruption. In an ex vivo refractory root canal infection model, CNPs combined with conventional irrigants (NaOCl/EDTA) and passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI) enhanced root canal disinfection and dentinal tubule cleaning. Moreover, when used as intracanal medicaments, CNPs promoted bacterial killing and deep intratubular penetration. A one-dimensional hindered diffusion model further simulated the spatiotemporal transport of CNPs within dentinal tubules. These findings suggest that biocompatible CNPs may serve as a promising adjunctive strategy for managing refractory root canal infections through ROS-mediated antibacterial activity and intratubular transport.

title: Investigations on the microstructural degradation and mechanical response of Ni–CGO anodes using phase-field method and stochastic modeling
abstract: The microstructural degradation of Ni–CGO anodes in solid oxide fuel cells affects both electrochemical and mechanical properties. This study presents an automated workflow to quantify the evolution of geometrical descriptors and their influence on effective mechanical properties. Three-dimensional anode microstructures were aged up to 35,000 h using phase-field and stochastic modeling, followed by mechanical loading simulations. Aging caused microstructural coarsening as the mean pore diameter increased, while pore specific surface area and triple-phase boundary density decreased. Effective elastic moduli also decreased with aging. While the average von Mises stress remained nearly constant, the critical volume fraction increased with aging. Within the studied microstructures, the effective Hill modulus was strongly related to pore volume fraction and pore specific surface area. The critical volume fraction related positively with pore diameter and inversely with pore specific surface area and triple-phase boundary density.

title: Exploring the potential extension of QSAR models for the toxicity of metal alloy biomaterials
abstract: Besides their use in different applications, metal alloys are extensively used as biomaterials, due to their stability, wear and corrosion resistance, as well as mechanical properties, among others. One of the first steps to determine the biocompatibility of materials is the assessment of their (cyto)toxicity. In this context, different in vivo and in vitro methods have been employed to assess the toxicity of different metal alloys. However, in silico toxicity assessment of such materials is still restricted, besides their establishment in chemo-informatics and their recent emergence in the field of nanomaterials. In this work, the potential extension of quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) approaches for the case of metal alloy biomaterials is explored. For this reason, two datasets are created, consisting of toxicity measurements for alloys in bulk and powder form, respectively. Combined classification and QSAR approaches are used to develop predictive models towards both datasets, allowing the identification of key material properties that lead to higher toxicity. These properties were similar across the two datasets, hinting towards similar mechanisms being responsible for toxic action. The results presented in this work could pave the way for such approaches to potentially be extended for the model-assisted safety assessment of alloys.

title: Photothermal phase-responsive nanocomposites boost cGAS/STING-Driven antitumor immunity via mitochondrial DNA damage
abstract: Activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase/stimulator of interferon gene (cGAS/STING) axis is a compelling route for enhancing cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional photothermal therapy (PTT) or photodynamic therapy (PDT) monotherapies seldom generate sufficient double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) damage to robustly engage in this pathway, allowing tumors to maintain immune tolerance and escape. In this study, we designed phase-change lauric acid nanocomposites (CCL NPs) consisting of photothermally active Cu2-XS nanoparticles and cisplatin (CDDP). Upon cellular uptake, synergistic PTT/PDT was triggered by near-infrared (NIR) irradiation. Subsequent NIR-II laser exposure converts Cu2-XS, generating heat for the precise melting of the lauric acid shell, unleashing CDDP directly inside the tumor microenvironment. Reactive oxygen species from PDT, together with released CDDP, inflict extensive mitochondrial DNA damage, liberating immunogenic dsDNA fragments into the cytosol. These danger signals potently activate the cGAS/STING pathway, boost antigen cross-presentation in dendritic cells, and recruit cytotoxic T lymphocytes in vivo. The resulting innate-to-adaptive immune cascade drives immunogenic cell death and sustains tumor suppression. Additionally, the copper component promotes cuproptosis, providing an additional chemotherapeutic mechanism. Collectively, CCL NPs integrate controllable chemotherapy/PTT/PDT with innate immune amplification, offering a versatile and powerful strategy for next-generation anticancer treatments.

title: Study on spheroidization annealing behavior of a medium carbon low-alloy steel with bainite as initial microstructure
abstract: This study adopts bainite as the initial microstructure and conducts a systematic investigation into how the bainitic phase influences the spheroidization behavior and carbide morphology evolution in 40CrMoSi steel. The results demonstrate that austenitization at 790 °C yields fine and uniformly distributed spheroidal carbides. Unlike the conventional “dissolution-coarsening” mechanism, spheroidization proceeds via a dual-pathway synergy involving carbide precipitation at migrating ferrite–austenite interfaces, while the undissolved carbides retained in austenite provide abundant nucleation sites that significantly promote divorced eutectoid transformation. More importantly, this optimized microstructure effectively refines the martensite block size during subsequent quenching and tempering, thereby enhancing hardness uniformity. This study elucidates the unique spheroidizing mechanism of bainite initial microstructures, providing new strategies for spheroidizing annealing techniques of medium carbon low-alloy steels.

title: Self-repairing performance of wear-reduction serpentine-reinforced iron composites based on orthogonal experiments
abstract: Self-repairing materials can effectively heal early-stage micro-damage; however, their performance is strongly governed by thermo-mechanical conditions during friction. The quantitative relationship between operational parameters and self-repairing efficacy remains insufficiently understood. In this study, a four-factor, three-level orthogonal experimental design was employed to systematically investigate the effects of serpentine content, applied load, sliding frequency, and test duration on the wear-induced self-repairing performance of a serpentine-reinforced iron-based composite (SP/Fe) fabricated via spark plasma sintering (SPS). This approach enabled the identification of optimal friction conditions for synergistic friction reduction and wear resistance. Multi-scale characterization of worn surfaces, combined with AIMD-based thermodynamic and kinetic analysis, was subsequently conducted to elucidate the mechanism by which friction conditions regulate self-repairing behavior. The results demonstrate that dispersed serpentine particles undergo phase transformation and structural reorganization during sliding, participating in complex tribochemical reactions at the friction interface and forming a protective tribofilm. The composition and microstructure of the tribofilm are highly dependent on the thermo-mechanical conditions. Under optimal conditions, the tribofilm consists of amorphous/nanocrystalline SiO 2 , Al 2 O 3 , Mg 2 SiO 4 , MgSiO 3 as hard ceramic phases; iron oxides and Fe 7 C 3 nanocrystals as reinforcing phases; and graphite together with residual serpentine as lubricating phases. This multiphase architecture endows the tribofilm with high nanohardness and elastic modulus, as well as favorable toughness and plasticity. Through the synergistic integration of lubrication, self-repair, and surface strengthening, the optimized tribofilm reduces the friction coefficient and wear volume of the SP/Fe composite by up to 45.7 % and 92.7 %, respectively, compared with the pristine iron. These findings clarify the intrinsic correlation between friction parameters and self-repairing performance and provide a mechanistic basis for the design of silicate-reinforced metal-matrix composites for demanding tribological applications.

title: Tailoring machinability and formability of an extruded Cu–Zn–Si alloy via heat treatment
abstract: This study investigates the optimal heat-treatment condition for improving straightness during cold drawing while maintaining the strength and machinability of an extruded Cu–Zn–Si alloy. Particular attention is given to the evolution of the metastable κ phase and its influence on residual stress and machining behavior. Heat treatment at 400 °C promotes the decomposition of the κ phase into Cu 3 Si intermetallic compounds, whereas treatment at 600 °C induces a κ-to-α phase transformation. The κ-to-α transformation generates severe lattice distortion and increases internal residual stress, leading to deterioration of dimensional stability during drawing. In contrast, heat treatment at 400 °C for 1 h retains a moderate fraction of the κ phase, facilitating chip segmentation, maintaining low cutting force, and suppressing residual stress development. As a result, this condition provides the optimal balance between machinability and dimensional stability, enabling improved straightness after drawing. These findings demonstrate that controlled κ-phase evolution can effectively tailor the microstructure of Cu–Zn–Si alloys, highlighting their potential as high-machinability Pb-free brasses for industrial applications

title: Neutrophil-hitchhiking luteolin-loaded nanozyme for vein graft restenosis
abstract: Vein graft restenosis (VG-RS) remains a critical challenge after vascular surgeries, driven by oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndoMT). Here, we engineered a neutrophil-hitchhiking nanoplatform (NeCPL) ---for targeted therapy of VG-RS. NeCPL comprises autologous neutrophils loaded with polydopamine-coated CeO 2 nanozymes (CeO 2 @PDA) and the natural flavonoid luteolin. Leveraging the innate inflammatory tropism of neutrophils, NeCPL actively homed to VG-RS lesions, where neutrophil extracellular traps triggered localized release of the payload. The CeO 2 @PDA nanozyme potently scavenged reactive oxygen species, while luteolin exerted anti‑inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects. In vitro , NeCPL suppressed EndoMT and shifted macrophage polarization toward an M2 phenotype. In vivo , NeCPL accumulated in remodeled grafted vein, attenuated vascular remodeling, reduced collagen deposition, and downregulated EndoMT‑related markers (α-SMA, Twist, Snail). Mechanistically, NeCPL inhibited the STING signaling pathway, which serves as a central molecular node where inflammatory signaling and EndoMT converge. Thus, STING pathway blockade by NeCPL simultaneously suppresses inflammation and prevents EndoMT through this unified mechanistic node rather than through independent parallel actions. Comparative studies revealed that NeCPL exhibited superior therapeutic efficacy compared to both free CPL and clinically used standard-of-care drugs (phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors), highlighting the necessity of the neutrophil “hitchhiking” strategy for enhanced vascular remodeling and treatment outcomes. This cell‑driven, multifunctional strategy demonstrates precise targeting, synergistic efficacy, and favorable biosafety, offering a promising nanotherapeutic approach for VG-RS

title: Engineering elastic bandgaps in TPMS-based metamaterials via geometric flattening and multi-morphology hybridization
abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architectures have become a prominent class of mechanical metamaterials, largely due to their excellent lightweight load-bearing capability and energy-absorption performance enabled by smooth, continuous, and highly connected geometries. In contrast, their dynamic characteristics remain far less systematically understood. In this work, we present a comprehensive study of 3D elastic-wave dispersion relations and bandgaps for fourteen TPMS-based metamaterials constructed from seven minimal surfaces using two thickening strategies (solid- and sheet-based). Building on these baselines, we further introduce two practical bandgap- engineering routes, geometric flattening and smooth multi-morphology hybridization, and quantify their effects on flexural bandgaps. Our results show that among the fourteen structures, only solid-primitive and solid-neovius support complete bandgaps, whereas sheet-diamond design exhibits no bandgap; the remaining structures predominantly feature directional bandgaps. Geometric flattening leads to a consistent downshift of flexural bandgap frequencies and a reduction in bandgap bandwidth, while multi-morphology hybridization further enables bandgap frequency downshift without requiring a lower volume fraction. The predicted bandgaps are validated through harmonic-response simulations and transmission experiments. Overall, our work offers a quantitative basis for selecting TPMS structures and corresponding volume fractions for vibration suppression panels, and provides engineering methods for future TPMS-based elastic/acoustic metamaterial design.

title: A dual-hijack strategy coordinating BBB transcytosis and intracellular ferritinophagy for glioblastoma gene therapy
abstract: Systemic gene therapy for glioblastoma is limited by poor brain-tumor delivery and resistance to apoptosis-based treatments. Here, we developed an ApoE-functionalized lipid nanoparticle (ApoE-LNP) for plasmid delivery of Ncoa4 , aiming to couple BBB transcytosis with ferritin/iron turnover–driven ferroptosis. ApoE-LNPs showed uniform size distribution, protected plasmid cargo from degradation, enhanced reporter-gene transfection in GL261 cells, improved transport across a bEnd.3 transwell BBB model and achieved deeper penetration in GL261 spheroids. Delivery of Ncoa4 increased NCOA4 expression, labile Fe 2 ⁺, ROS, lipid peroxidation, and MDA levels, while reducing GPX4 expression and cell viability. These effects were attenuated by ferrostatin-1 and partially rescued by bafilomycin A1, supporting a ferroptosis-associated phenotype linked to autophagy–lysosome/ferritin turnover. In orthotopic GL261 tumor-bearing mice, ApoE-LNPs prolonged plasmid circulation, enhanced cranial/tumor-associated fluorescence, suppressed tumor progression, and extended survival without overt abnormalities in preliminary safety assessments. These findings support ApoE-LNP@Ncoa4 as a promising proof-of-concept strategy for glioblastoma gene therapy.

title: Non-destructive three-dimensional orientation mapping of Nd–Fe–B permanent magnets
abstract: Three-dimensional observation of individual grains is essential for a comprehensive understanding of the magnetic properties of Nd–Fe–B permanent magnets. Local features such as grain size, shape, and crystallographic orientation must be resolved, as bulk-averaged measurements cannot adequately explain magnetic behavior. Although three-dimensional electron backscatter diffraction can provide such information, its application to Nd–Fe–B magnets is challenging due to surface damage during serial sectioning. Therefore, a nondestructive approach to three-dimensional orientation mapping is required. In this study, we apply the recently developed inclined scanning three-dimensional X-ray diffraction microscopy ( i -S3DXRD) to obtain a nondestructive three-dimensional orientation map of a neodymium magnet. The results reveal a pronounced three-dimensional fiber texture, in which the c -axis—the magnetic easy axis—is preferentially aligned parallel to the specimen x -axis, while the a -axis is randomly distributed. Surface orientation maps show good agreement with EBSD results. Orientation distribution function analysis revealed a fiber-type texture with a substantial mosaicity. Analysis of the volumetric orientation map further shows that the triple-junction network exhibits a complex three-dimensional distribution throughout the volume, with junction segment lengths comparable to the grain size. These results demonstrate that i -S3DXRD is a powerful nondestructive technique for comprehensive characterization of permanent magnets.

title: Backbone-encoded biofunction via covalent curcumin chain extension converts biodegradable polyurethane into a scaffold-as-drug with degradation-coupled liberation
abstract: Additive manufacturing enables geometric control of polymer scaffolds, yet durable molecular programming of biofunction remains a materials bottleneck. Here we develop a backbone-encoded scaffold-as-drug polyurethane (PU) by covalently integrating curcumin (Cur) as a reactive phenolic chain extender, transforming biodegradable PU from a passive carrier into an intrinsically therapeutic material. 1 H NMR, FTIR, GPC, TGA/DTG, XRD, and DSC verify Cur incorporation and Cur-dependent microphase modulation. Cur/PU is processed into extrusion-printed porous scaffolds while preserving print fidelity and elastomeric mechanics. Compared with physically blended Cur@PU, covalent encoding shifts Cur availability from diffusion-driven burst to degradation-coupled liberation, yielding sustained release that tracks scaffold mass loss for 12 weeks. Cur/PU scaffolds are cytocompatible with BMSCs and provide single-material pleiotropy: antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , suppression of LPS-induced inflammatory mediators (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, PTGS2) in macrophages, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation and mineralization. In a rat S. aureus -infected calvarial defect model, Cur/PU lowers early bacterial burden, attenuates pro-inflammatory cytokines, promotes M2-associated cues, and improves bone regeneration and collagen-rich matrix versus empty defects, PU, and Cur@PU. Overall, this work provides a conceptual framework for programming degradable PU scaffolds with degradation-coupled therapeutic availability via covalent small-molecule chain extension while avoiding multi-component loading or antibiotic incorporation strategies.

title: A multifunctional hydrogel co-encapsulating ROS-responsive quercetin nanoparticles and ADSCs to accelerate infected wound healing
abstract: Chronic infected wounds face healing challenges due to the interplay of persistent infection, excessive inflammation, and impaired angiogenesis. Conventional dressings often address only one pathological aspect, resulting in limited therapeutic effects. To overcome these barriers, we developed a multifunctional hydrogel Qu@NPs/ADSCs@CS-gel that integrates anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and immunomodulatory activities. The system was fabricated from genipin-crosslinked chitosan and silk sericin into a biocompatible hydrogel (CS-gel) that exhibits antibacterial activity and permits cellular matrix permeability. Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) were encapsulated within this hydrogel, while reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive quercetin-loaded nanoparticles (Qu@NPs), based on poly(propylene sulfide)-poly(ethylene glycol) (PPS-PEG), were attached to its surface. Upon wound contact, Qu@NPs are released from Qu@NPs/ADSCs@CS-gel, and PPS-PEG breaks down in response to ROS to release quercetin, effectively eliminating ROS and alleviating the inflammatory response, thereby establishing a regenerative microenvironment for ADSC-mediated repair. Qu@NPs/ADSCs@CS-gel exhibited potent antibacterial activity, reduced ROS accumulation in macrophages while preserving superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity. Furthermore, it inhibited M1 macrophage polarization and pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion, while promoting transition to the M2 phenotype. These effects collectively improved cell proliferation, re-epithelialization, angiogenesis, and collagen deposition, accelerating the three phases of wound repair. Our findings support Qu@NPs/ADSCs@CS-gel as an advanced dressing for infected wounds.

title: Conversion of hydrophilic glass to superhydrophobicity by CF4/Ar plasma etching
abstract: In the power generation and transmission, glass finds extensive use in high-voltage insulators and photovoltaic protection layers due to its exceptional insulating and light transmission properties. However, in wet or icy climates, glass insulators are susceptible to flashover (wet flashover and ice flashover) and photovoltaic output can be significantly diminished (droplet or ice adhesion affects light transmission), thereby posing a considerable threat to power security. Forming the glass into a superhydrophobic state can prevent droplet adhesion and icing. Plasma etching, a high-precision technique, can provide an effective solution to prepare superhydrophobic materials. Experimental studies reveal that factors such as gas pressure, gas ratio, discharge power, and etching duration significantly influence the plasma etching process, correlating with parameters like particle density, energy, and reactive species density. Following 60 min of plasma etching supplemented with low surface energy treatment, glass successfully transitioned from hydrophilic (water contact angle 55°) to superhydrophobic (water contact angle 157°). The findings of this study are expected to contribute to a more profound comprehension of the process of plasma etching glass microforms and to provide a theoretical foundation for the preparation of superhydrophobic glass for power facilities.

title: Physics-informed FEA–GPR–PSO optimization of perforated CARALL structures for simultaneous bending strength increase and lightweight design
abstract: Fiber metal laminates combine the advantages of metals and carbon fiber–reinforced polymers, among which carbon fiber–reinforced aluminum laminates (CARALLs) have attracted significant attention due to their excellent mechanical performance. However, insufficient bonding strength at the metal–adhesive interface often leads to interfacial delamination. Perforating the metal layer to form pin-like mechanical interlocking structures is an effective solution, while also enabling weight reduction. Nevertheless, perforation design involves multiple geometric parameters, including hole diameter, pitch-to-diameter ratio, hole type, and staggered arrangement, and improper combinations may induce stress concentration and stiffness degradation. Moreover, systematic optimization strategies suitable for high-end industrial applications remain limited. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-guided, data-driven optimization framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and particle swarm optimization (PSO) for perforated CFRP–aluminum–CFRP laminates. Experimental tests were conducted to calibrate and validate the FEA model. Based on an experimental design, surrogate models were established for tensile and bending strength, achieving normalized root mean squared errors of 4.14 % and 3.35 %, respectively. Global optimization results demonstrate a 5.47 % reduction in structural weight and a 9.52 % improvement in bending strength, with only a 1.82 % decrease in tensile strength, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed framework in balancing design.

title: A predictive framework for superhydrophobic aluminum alloys based on micro-geometric mapping and a two-state composite wetting mechanism
abstract: To precisely predict and control the micro-morphology and wettability of nanosecond laser-processed surfaces, a predictive framework is proposed in this work. It integrates Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and a two-state composite wetting mechanism. Superhydrophobic surfaces were fabricated on 6061 aluminum alloy by nanosecond laser point-matrix scanning and stearic acid modification. Laser parameters, including power, frequency and pulse width, were mapped to micro-geometric features by a second-order regression model. An aspect ratio ( H in / R in ) was chosen as a critical parameter to characterize the micro-geometric morphology. A composite contact angle model was established based on the synergy effect of composite wetting and Cassie-Impregnating states. Results show that laser power positively dominates geometric dimensions, while frequency exhibits a parabolic effect. A quantitative mapping between the aspect ratio and the composite wetting state area fraction ( λ 1 ) was discussed. It indicates that λ 1 is high and surface regularity is optimal in the range of H in / R in from 0.8 to 1.4. Finally, the high accuracy of the predictive framework is validated by experiments. During this ideal range of H in / R in , the basic point-matrix strategy can effectively overcome local pinning effect without complex biomimetic patterns. Furthermore, it enables the precise prediction and controllable fabrication of superhydrophobic surfaces with low sliding angles.

title: Phase-resolved characterization of hydride-induced hardening in Zircaloy-2 and Zr-2.5Nb using in situ nanoindentation and crystal plasticity modeling
abstract: Zirconium alloys used in nuclear reactors are prone to hydrogen embrittlement and hydride precipitation. In this study, the local deformation behavior of α-Zr, β-Zr, and δ-zirconium hydride phases in Zr-2.5Nb is investigated using in situ nanoindentation in a scanning electron microscope combined with pre- and post-indentation electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) experiments. Nanoindentation was performed within individual α and β grains as well as δ hydrides and results were compared with those obtained for α-Zr, and δ-hydride grains in Zircaloy-2. Crystal plasticity finite element simulations were used to support the experimental observations and to interpret the underlying deformation mechanisms. The results show that δ-hydrides exhibit a harder mechanical response than the surrounding matrix and act as strong barriers to slip transmission. Elevated geometrically necessary dislocation densities were observed in the α- and β-Zr regions adjacent to hydrides located at α/β interfaces in Zr–2.5Nb prior to indentation, indicating that the transformation strain associated with hydride formation induced local deformation before external loading. This pre-existing deformation state contributes to the measured indentation response, particularly in β grains located near hydrides. The results further show that the magnitude of local hardening depends on hydride size and loading rate during indentation.

title: Towards generalizable thermal profile prediction in additive manufacturing using constrained random walks and machine learning
abstract: Defect formation in additively manufactured materials is strongly governed by the thermal history experienced during printing, which depends on process parameters that interact in complex and often non-linear ways. A finite element method (FEM) model was developed to extract thermal profiles at representative locations in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) processes, iterating over a defined set of printing parameters under a single scanning strategy. Among the machine learning architectures evaluated, Neural Networks (NN) provided the most accurate and robust predictions. To generalise the approach beyond fixed scanning strategies, a constrained random walks (CRW) methodology has been introduced to generate training datasets with sufficient variability. The resulting model predicts thermal histories accurately and at a fraction of the computational cost of FEM, providing a practical basis for process optimisation and defect control in L-PBF.

title: Experimentally validated finite element model of the mechanical behavior of SS316L–IN718 bimetallic structures additively manufactured using laser directed energy deposition
abstract: Multi-material additive manufacturing (AM) enables the integration of dissimilar metals allowing tailored mechanical properties. The mechanical behavior of such structures remains insufficiently understood highlighting the need of accurate mechanical characterization and development of predictive models. The strong metallurgical compatibility of austenitic stainless steel (SS316L) and Inconel 718 (IN718) facilitates the employment of their direct bonding. This study investigates the mechanical properties of bimetallic structures of SS316L and IN718 manufactured using laser directed energy deposition (L-DED). The primary objective of the current work is developing an experimentally-validated finite element (FE) model, capable of capturing the elasto-plastic behavior of directly-bonded bimetallic structures with different volumetric fractions up to 10% strain. Monolithic specimens as well as different bimetallic configurations were printed in two build directions to account for anisotropy. A total of 30 printed specimens were extensively characterized. Experimental investigation included uniaxial tensile testing, surface topography analysis, microstructural characterization and full field strain measurements using digital image correlation (DIC). A FE model was developed to numerically predict the elasto-plastic behavior of the bimetallic structures up to 10% strain. The results indicated excellent agreement between the FE predictions and experimental results.

title: From processing text to counterfactual steel design: a knowledge-graph-organized and reliability-aware machine learning framework
abstract: Reliable steel design requires property models that transfer beyond random data splits to unseen grades, compositions and processing routes. Here, we develop a knowledge-graph-organized, mechanism-aware and risk-controlled framework for steel composition-processing-property prediction and counterfactual design. Semi-structured processing-condition text is parsed into process-step indicators, route families and inferred mechanism states, and integrated with alloy chemistry, section size, steel grade, process clusters and properties to construct a composition-processing-property knowledge graph. The dataset contains 3234 records, 228 grades and 939 unique processing texts; the graph contains 31,081 nodes and 74,494 edges. For yield strength, R2 decreases from 0.927 under random splitting to 0.447 under process-cluster holdout, revealing strong processing-route domain shift. Ablation shows that mechanism-aware representation improves cluster-holdout R2 from −5.864 for composition-only modeling to 0.447. A supervised risk gate reduces yield-strength MAE by 35.6 % under process-cluster holdout and 47.9 % under leave-one-cluster-out validation. Graph-conditioned DoWhy/EconML analyses and constrained counterfactual search provide assumption-dependent causal evidence and 60 feasible, evidence-ranked design hypotheses. The framework supports transferable, interpretable and reliability-aware steel design from heterogeneous observational data.

title: Oxidation mechanism of Ti2AlC-Ti5Si3/TiAl composite
abstract: A novel TiAl composite, where nano-Ti 2 AlC ceramic particles precipitate at the α 2 /γ lamellae interface and micro-Ti 5 Si 3 ceramic particles distribute at the lamellar colony boundaries, was successfully prepared by introducing graphene oxide (GO) and SiC into TiAl alloy via spark plasma sintering (SPS). The formation and growth behavior of oxide for TiAl composite was investigated at 950 °C in air, and the corresponding oxidation mechanisms were revealed. During the initial oxidation stages of the TiAl alloy, α 2 -Ti 3 Al was preferentially oxidized compared to γ-TiAl, accompanied by uneven growth of oxide particles. However, in the TiAl composite, the Ti 2 AlC and Ti 5 Si 3 ceramic particles retarded, forcing simultaneous oxidation of both the α 2 -Ti 3 Al and γ-TiAl phases. This positive effect inhibited the inhomogeneous growth of oxide particles, reduced void formation, and ultimately decelerated the overall oxidation rate of the TiAl composite.

title: Mechanical and electrochemical corrosion properties of stochastic open-cell Al-, Ni/Al- and Ni/PU foams
abstract: Aluminum (Al) alloys are the most commonly used materials for stochastic open-cell metal foams. However, alternative nickel (Ni)-based systems, such as stochastic open-cell Ni/polyurethane and Ni/Al foams, have achieved considerable technological advancement in recent years. The present study provides a direct comparison of these material systems with respect to their initial mechanical properties, their electrochemical corrosion behavior in a stagnant 3.5 wt% NaCl electrolyte and the resulting impact on the mechanical performance after six months of immersion. The results reveal a lower initial mechanical strength and energy absorption capacity for the Al foam system. Moreover, the stochastic open-cell Al foams exhibit microgalvanically induced dissolution, leading to a linear degradation of the mechanical properties under uniaxial compression. In contrast, the Ni-based systems show a significantly reduced effect of electrochemical corrosion on their mechanical behavior. Overall, the findings demonstrate a distinct advantage of the Ni-based material systems for energy absorption applications under realistic service conditions compared to stochastic open-cell Al foams.

title: Abnormal grain growth behavior and mechanism of longitudinal welds in 2196 Al-Cu-Li extrusions with different original microstructures
abstract: The longitudinal welds of 2196 Al–Li extrusions are prone to develop abnormal grain growth (AGG). The AGG behavior during solution treatment (ST) of profiles with different initial microstructures was analyzed and the AGG mechanism was clarified. High-temperature high-speed extrusion promoted sufficient dynamic recrystallization (DRX) in the welding areas and released most deformation storage energy, and formed stable Cube-textured coarse grains during extrusion and remained stable during ST. Low-temperature low-speed extrusion retained high dislocation density and dramatic shear textures in welds with high storage energy, which drives early recrystallization and produces fine-grained structures that constitute the core potential for subsequent AGG. The extrusion temperature of 450 °C and speed of 2 mm/s achieves a favorable balance between grain refinement and storage energy control, delivering a thermally stable microstructure throughout the profile service life. Based on sub-grain size, grain boundary misorientation and dislocation density, a storage energy model was established by incorporating the Read-Shockley relationship and was embedded into Q-Form software. This model enabled the quantitative characterization about the distribution of initial storage energy. The non-uniform distribution and thermal release of storage energy induced recrystallized grain size heterogeneity, which finally decided the curvature-driven boundary migration and AGG behavior.

title: Bias–induced energy engineering of Ta– and Y– doped TiAlN coatings: linking densification, residual stresses and tribological performance
abstract: Controlling the energetic conditions during PVD growth is critical for tailoring the structure–stress–property relationships of advanced TiAlN–based coatings intended for severe tribological and machining environments.
