The influence of substrate bias voltage (−60, −90 and –135 V) on the microstructural evolution, residual stress development and tribo–mechanical response of TiAlTaN and TiAlYN coatings deposited by reactive DC sputtering was investigated. Increasing negative bias enhanced ion bombardment and atomic peening, promoting grain refinement, coating densification and smoother morphologies. Simultaneously, compressive residual stress increased between 2.88 and 4.32 GPa for TiAlTaN and between 2.12 and 3.17 GPa for TiAlYN due to intensified energetic growth conditions. The results demonstrated that residual stress alone does not govern coating performance. TiAlTaN coatings developed higher compressive stresses but limited hardness improvement, whereas TiAlYN coatings showed superior structure–property synergy and resistance to plastic deformation. The TiAlYN coating deposited at –135 V showed the best overall mechanical and tribological performance. The Y-containing coating architecture promoted a more efficient conversion of ion-bombardment-induced energy into enhanced mechanical and tribological performance. The combined analysis of microstructure, residual stress and tribological behavior established a bias–driven structure–property framework, highlighting distinct strengthening and stress accommodation mechanisms in TiAlN–derived coatings for advanced wear–resistant applications.

title: Online monitoring method based on strain sensitivity analysis of composite materials
abstract: In the current research, through the integration of optical fiber sensing and finite element simulation technology, the detection efficiency of composite material manufacturing defects has been significantly improved. Through real-time monitoring of multiple measurement points, ply directions and strain indicators, full structural performance coverage is achieved to avoid missed detection; relying on the comparison between measured and theoretical values, combined with defect simulation and sensitive indicator screening, the existence of defects is accurately determined and their types and positions are located; based on defect parameter simulation and feature library mapping, it supports quantitative analysis from qualitative judgment to defect degree, adapting to high-precision engineering scenarios; the closed-loop of “simulation-virtual measurement-verification” is formed through finite element simulation and optical fiber virtual measurement, which enhances the reliability and efficiency of defect detection for complex structures and is suitable for full-life-cycle monitoring of composite materials

title: Thermo-mechanical grain structure and texture tailoring of Mo-9Si-8B by electron beam powder bed fusion
abstract: Refractory Mo-Si-B alloys offer superior mechanical strength and oxidation resistance at elevated temperatures, making them promising candidates for next-generation turbine engines. Electron beam powder bed fusion (PBF-EB) enables the direct fabrication of complex components from such high-temperature materials. While a 〈1 0 0〉 || BD fiber textures is commonly expected in PBF-processed cubic metals, the as-built Mo-9Si-8B developed a pronounced 〈1 1 1〉 || BD fiber or near-random textures, depending on the area energy. We elucidate the role of post-solidification plastic deformation in governing texture evolution and recrystallization in the Mo solid-solution phase. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and thermo-mechanical simulations were combined to relate the local plastic strain to recrystallization and texture evolution. The final 〈1 1 1〉 || BD texture arises from collective lattice reorientation of the initial weak 〈1 0 0〉 || BD solidification texture, driven by plastic deformation (pencil-glide) under a biaxial tensile stress state. The recrystallized fraction scales with the local magnitude of plastic strain, consistent with the thermo-mechanical simulation predictions, confirming plastic deformation as the unifying factor behind both texture evolution and recrystallization. This work establishes a quantitative area energy – plastic-strain – microstructure framework, providing a mechanistic basis for tailoring crystallographic texture and recrystallization, thereby supporting property-oriented process design in PBF-EB processed refractory alloys.

title: Micelle-confined self-assembly of gold nanoassemblies for near-infrared photothermal and photodynamic therapy
abstract: The construction of multifunctional phototherapeutic nanoplatforms typically relies on integrating multiple materials or exogenous components to achieve imaging, photothermal conversion, and ROS generation. However, such multi-material designs complicate preparation and raise biosafety concerns, while single-nanomaterial platforms that combine these functions remain limited. Herein, we report an in-situ micelle-confined self-assembly strategy for constructing F127/1-hexanethiol-confined gold nanoassemblies (FC-AuNAs). Within the confined micellar environment, 1-hexanethiol functions as both a reducing agent and a stabilizer, enabling ordered assembly of gold nanoparticles. FC-AuNAs exhibit characteristic NIR absorption and emission, a photothermal conversion efficiency of 31.7 %, and efficient 1 O 2 generation, as evidenced by an ABDA decay ratio of 66.9 % at 150 μg/mL. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, FC-AuNAs effectively induce tumor cell death in vitro and suppress tumor growth in a 4 T1 mouse model without causing obvious biotoxicity. This work presents a simplified, single-photoactive nanoplatform for 808 nm-triggered combined photothermal and ROS-associated antitumor therapy.

title: Pre-weakened anodization-assisted rapid thinning of silicon carbide wafers
abstract: Sub-100 µm silicon carbide (SiC) substrates are demanded for thermal management in sub-3 nm architectures, however, the extreme hardness of SiC hinders conventional thinning. Here, we present a hybrid electrochemical-mechanical thinning strategy utilizing a pre-weakened anodization. The anodization was achieved by a designed nonaqueous electrochemical process and then converted the rigid SiC into a carbon-rich porous, stress-dissipating sacrificial layer that absorbs impacts during subsequent conventional diamond wheel grinding. After fine diamond grinding, the bonded pair is separated, yielding ultra-thin (75 µm) SiC wafers that exhibited no visible cracking with reduced XRD peak broadening and a surface roughness of 1.63 nm. In contrast, directly grinding the SiC substrate was not only time-consuming but also consumed four diamond rough-grinding wheels through severe abrasive wear. Moreover, upon removing the protective backside adhesive film after grinding, the thinned wafer immediately warped and fractured. Pre-weakened anodization could effectively reduce fracture during ultrathin SiC wafer fabrication — opening a pathway toward large-diameter wafer processing for advanced packaging applications, including CoWoS and backside power delivery networks.

title: Impact of buffer layer creation method and annealing in air on efficiency of TiO2/CuxO solar cells obtained via magnetron sputtering
abstract: In this study the TiO 2 /Cu x O heterojunction solar cells deposited via direct current reactive magnetron sputtering were investigated. It was shown how different buffer layer creation methods and annealing at 150 °C in air impact on the device efficiency. By changing the interface/buffer layer deposition strategy and the heterostructure annealing, the changes in structural, optical, and electrical properties of the studied heterojunctions were analyzed. The results demonstrate that optimized buffer-layer configurations improve charge-carrier transport and suppress recombination losses, while controlled air annealing enhances crystallinity and interfacial quality. The present results offer deeper insight into processing–structure–property relationships that are crucial to the understanding and development of low-cost, high-efficiency thin-film solar cell technologies.

title: Fracture surface morphology–property relationships in Mo–Ti–C alloys revealed by quantitative descriptor analysis
abstract: Fracture surface morphology reflects essential information on fracture processes in high-temperature structural materials, yet its quantitative relationship with fracture properties remains unclear. In this work, the fracture behavior of heat-treated Mo–Ti–C alloys is investigated using four-point bending tests combined with detailed fracture surface characterization by scanning electron microscopy and confocal laser scanning microscopy. Quantitative morphology descriptors, including gray-level co-occurrence matrix texture features, surface roughness parameters, and fractal descriptors, are systematically extracted and analyzed within an explainable, machine-learning-assisted framework. The results reveal distinct morphology dependencies for fracture energy and fracture toughness. Fracture energy was dominated by a few key descriptors, with higher texture contrast and fractal dimension associated with lower fracture energy levels, whereas fracture toughness depended on multiple texture- and fractal-related descriptors. This study establishes an interpretable quantitative framework linking fracture surface morphology to fracture properties, providing new insights for morphology-informed fracture assessment and microstructure-guided materials design.

title: Effecting rate-dependent behavior with friction based geometrical design
abstract: This work investigates whether the architecture of a unit cell, rather than the properties of its base material, can govern strain rate sensitive behavior. We focus on additively manufactured Ti6Al4V, a lightweight titanium alloy with weak intrinsic rate sensitivity, and employ it to fabricate friction unit cells. The friction cell redirects compressive loads into frictional sliding between internal surfaces produced by the LPBF (Laser Powder Bed Fusion) process. Structural characterization from quasi-static (0.01 /s) to crash-relevant strain rates (500 /s) reveals a factor of 2.5 increase in peak stress, substantially exceeding the rate sensitivity of the base material. To identify the mechanism, the dynamic friction coefficient of the as-built Ti6Al4V tribo-pair is measured across sliding velocities from 0.01 to 8 m/s at 7.5 MPa and up to 6.5 m/s at 40 MPa. The kinetic friction coefficient more than doubles between the quasi-static plateau and the crash-relevant regime. Correlating the structural and tribological data establishes velocity-strengthening interfacial friction as the dominant mechanism behind the pronounced rate sensitivity of the friction cell. These results show that meso-scale friction, embedded through unit cell geometry and surface morphology, can dictate crash-relevant rate sensitivity that the base material alone does not possess.

title: Design of High-Performance Epoxy/Novolac adhesives using Zn-MOF-74 and amine-functionalized Zn-MOF-74 Composites in structural bonding
abstract: This study investigates the effect of Zn-MOF-74 and amino-functionalized Zn-MOF-74 (Zn-MOF-74 (–NH 2 )) on the mechanical and thermal properties of epoxy/novolac nanocomposite adhesives, synthesized via hydrothermal method. Characterization results confirmed the successful synthesis and functionalization of nanoparticles. The results of tensile and lap shear strength (LSS) tests revealed that the incorporation of 0.5 phr Zn-MOF-74 (–NH 2 ) nanoparticles into the epoxy adhesive increased the ultimate tensile strength (UTS), toughness and LSS by 85%, 120%, and 69%, respectively, compared with the neat epoxy/novolac adhesive. Contact angle measurements also showed a significant reduction in the contact angle from 84° to 42°, indicating enhanced wettability of the substrate surface. In addition, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and swelling test results demonstrated the positive and remarkable effect of amino groups on the curing behavior of the epoxy/novolac adhesive. Furthermore, thermogravimetric (TGA) results indicated increases of 66 and 26 °C in the initial degradation temperature (T i ) and the maximum degradation temperature (T max ), respectively. Microscopic observations also confirmed a more uniform distribution of the modified nanoparticles within the epoxy/novolac matrix. This study highlights the vital role of amino functionalization of nanoparticles in the design and development of a new generation of structural epoxy/novolac adhesives for engineering applications.

title: Effects of phase boundary orientation on slip transfer, slip localization, and damage in tension of Ti55511 titanium alloy
abstract: Heterogeneous strain distribution in dual-scale lamellar near-β titanium (Ti) alloys determines early damage sites and crack paths, yet the crystallographic and phase boundary (PB) factors governing this behavior remain unclear. To address this, in-situ electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) tensile experiments are combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on two ideal grain orientations to systematically elucidate how primary α (α p ) variant orientation, geometric compatibility and α p /β PB orientation control slip activation, transfer, and propagation in bi-lamellar Ti-5Al-5Mo-5 V-1Cr-1Fe (Ti55511) alloy. The MD simulations show that each α p variant accumulates dislocations or develops substructure according to its orientation and PB orientation, following an assumed uniaxial tension deformation boundary condition. In particular, α p /β PBs in 〈100〉 β grains have lower resistance to slip transfer than many in 〈110〉 β grains, which promotes earlier yielding, localized strain concentration, and preferential crack nucleation at 〈100〉 β grain boundaries (GBs). There is good correlation between the simulations and experimental observations. By linking local PB mechanics to macroscopic mechanical response, our work provides a fundamental basis and strategic direction for crystallographic and PB engineering to optimize strain distribution, thereby enhancing the strength-ductility balance in advanced aerospace Ti alloys.

title: Nonlinear increase in effective hydrogen diffusivity governed by three-dimensional pore connectivity in additively manufactured 17-4 PH stainless steel
abstract: Hydrogen diffusivity in additively manufactured (AM) 17-4 PH stainless steel was investigated over a wide porosity range to clarify the effect of pore structure on hydrogen transport. AM steels with porosities of 0.4 %, 4.4 %, and 13.8 % were fabricated, and effective hydrogen diffusivity was determined by fitting the analytical solution of the diffusion equation to desorption data. The steels with porosities of 4.4 % and 13.8 % showed comparable diffusivities, both approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that of the steel with 0.4 % porosity, revealing a strong nonlinear dependence on porosity. Finite element models constructed from X-ray computed tomography images suggestedthat three-dimensionally interconnected pores form preferential hydrogen transport pathways. These results highlight pore connectivity—rather than porosity alone—as the controlling factor for hydrogen transport in AM 17-4 PH steel.

title: Controlling local melt pool dimensions in laser powder bed fusion through multiscale physics-driven optimization
abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion is an additive manufacturing technique used to produce solid metal parts from metallic powder. It excels at producing complex geometries in small batches. However, processing conditions are still being optimized using time and labor intensive trial and error approaches. Even after optimization, the contrast between the complex geometry and the limited set of optimized processing conditions, yields a compromise between printability and melt pool homogeneity at best. We proppose a multiscale modeling approach to obtain a physics driven prediction of processing conditions tailored to a specific geometry. The workflow consist of two distinct modeling techniques utilized to capture the physics of the process, both, on the part scale, and on the melt pool scale. The optimization strategy aims to minimize melt pool variations in the vicinity of geometric features. The numerical methods and optimization algorithm are detailed, convergence studies are shown, and the effectiveness of the optimization is verified by high speed thermal imaging and X-ray tomography.

title: Kinetic regulation of PbI2–FAI conversion enables efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 perovskite solar cells
abstract: The development of low-cost and high-stability solution-processed perovskite technology provides a viable pathway for the mass production of efficient and durable solar cells, which is essential for reducing fossil fuel dependence and mitigating carbon emissions. However, the phase conversion of two-step processed FAPbI 3 is often hindered by sluggish reaction kinetics and competing formation of the non-perovskite δ-phase, which together limit device efficiency and operational stability. Here we report a coordination-mediated kinetic regulation strategy by incorporating sulfogaiacol (SG) into the PbI 2 precursor. SG modifies the local chemical environment of Pb species, reshaping the intermediate structure and directing the subsequent conversion towards phase-pure α-FAPbI 3 . In situ optical measurements show that SG accelerates the diffusion and reaction of formamidinium iodide, enabling faster α-phase formation while suppressing the parasitic δ-phase. Combined spectroscopic and structural analyses reveal that oxygen-containing groups in SG weaken the strong PbI 2 –DMSO coordination, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier for phase conversion and improving crystallization. The resulting films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grains, improved morphological uniformity and reduced defect densities. Devices based on SG-treated films deliver a power conversion efficiency of 26.1% , with an open-circuit voltage of 1.19 V and markedly suppressed current–voltage hysteresis. Encapsulated devices further retain around 80% of their initial efficiency after more than 3,200 h of continuous one-sun illumination at 75°C . These results identify coordination engineering of conversion kinetics as an environmentally friendly and effective route to efficient and durable FAPbI 3 photovoltaics, offering key technical support for sustainable energy governance.

title: Programmable crushing mechanism and dual mechanical protection of chiral metamaterials based on compression softening effect
abstract: While lightweight lattice structures are favored in aerospace engineering for their high specific strength and multifunctional tailorability, they are prone to shear band formation under compression, triggering strain localization and catastrophic global failure that drastically compromise energy absorption efficiency and load-bearing capacity. Chiral metamaterials, leveraging their unique compression–torsion coupling, offer a promising solution. Here, we propose a novel chiral architected material, FTCS‑12C‑A, which harnesses compression softening induced by this coupling to achieve intra-layer locking and sequential layer-by-layer collapse: post-buckling stiffness degradation confines deformation to the initiating layer until self-contact of adjacent layers restores stiffness and transfers load to the subsequent layer. This mechanism effectively suppresses stochastic shear band nucleation, enabling FTCS‑12C‑A to maintain a specific energy absorption (SEA) comparable to conventional benchmarks (BCC, FCC, and Octet‑truss) while significantly reducing effective stiffness and peak stress. Furthermore, programmable control over the collapse sequence via the geometric parameter θ generates a “cushioning–shielding” effect. This integrates high global energy dissipation with localized deformation isolation, presenting a dual-protection paradigm with substantial potential for aircraft structural health monitoring and impact-resistant transportation systems.

title: Irradiation tolerance of Co-free high entropy alloy: a quantitative microstructural evaluation of the effect of irradiation damage dose
abstract: High entropy alloys (HEAs) are potential structural materials for next-generation nuclear systems due to their excellent high-temperature strength and corrosion resistance. However, their viability in extreme environments remains uncertain, necessitating a rigorous understanding of microstructural stability under irradiation. This work provides a comprehensive quantitative evaluation of microstructure as a function of irradiation fluence at 300°C. Transmission electron microscopy revealed a dynamic disorder-order phase transformation (FCC-L12), resulting from the competition between irradiation-enhanced diffusion and ballistic dissolution. At low doses, pre-existing dislocations led to a heterogeneous distribution of dislocation loops. This effect became less pronounced at higher doses as the strength of competing defect sinks increased. Further irradiation facilitated the unfaulting of 1/3<111> Faulted/Frank loops into ½<110> Perfect loops, eventually evolving into a complex dislocation network. While void nucleation was suppressed at lower doses, discrete voids appeared at 10 dpa, due to vacancy supersaturation following enhanced interstitial absorption by the established dislocation network. Furthermore, Ni segregation at grain boundaries (initially driven by an interstitial drag mechanism) was less prominent at higher damage dose. This study offers mechanistic insight into irradiation induced microstructural evolution and the critical role of sink strength evolution in governing the long-term microstructural integrity of HEAs under irradiation.

title: Cover_268
Editorial Board
Effect of selected rotary-swaging routes on the microstructure, residual stresses, and compressive behavior of boron-modified AZ91
abstract: Rotary swaging (R-SWG) was used to tailor the microstructure and residual-stress state of magnesium alloys through combined radial compression and shear deformation. This work compares five thermomechanical R-SWG routes applied to permanent mold-cast AZ91 containing 0.03 wt% B in order to establish route-dependent relationships between microstructure, texture, residual stresses and compressive response. The investigated routes combined different second-pass temperatures, feeding rates, prior T4 treatment and total reductions. The route-dependent differences in grain refinement and radial microstructure heterogeneity have been revealed using electron microscopy. All processed conditions developed pronounced textures with distinct central-peripheral variations. Neutron diffraction resolved the residual-stress distributions across the full specimen cross-sections and showed that the finest microstructure did not necessarily coincide with the largest residual-stress gradients. Compared with the initial cast state, rotary swaging increased the compressive yield strength to approximately 240–290 MPa and substantially enhanced the strain to fracture, while Young’s modulus remained within 42–47 GPa. Finite element modeling (FEM) provided a physically consistent interpretation of route-dependent material flow, effective-strain penetration and temperature evolution. The study demonstrates that different thermomechanical R-SWG routes generate distinct process-structure-stress-property relationships in boron-modified AZ91 and highlights the value of full-cross-sectional neutron-diffraction residual-stress mapping as a complement to local microstructure characterization.

title: Additively manufactured mechanical metamaterial embedded design in robotics for passive vibration attenuation: a proof of concept study
abstract: Structural vibrations continue to limit the dynamic performance of industrial robotic arms, while conventional active vibration control techniques often increase complexity, energy consumption, and implementation cost. This study introduces a novel proof of concept approach that embeds additively manufactured mechanical metamaterials (MMs) in a robotic arm to passively attenuate its end-effector vibrations, while maintaining static structural integrity. Focusing on a simplified prototype design of a wire arc additive manufacturing robotic arm, vibration impact hammer testing is performed on individual links, and a validated finite element analysis (FEA) model is developed. FEA dynamic and static stress analyses are then carried out across various operational orientations: full stretch orientation (FSO), half stretch orientation, and least stretch orientation. The robotic arm models were designed with polymer material and analyzed using ANSYS. The impact of varying embedded MM lengths, i.e., 0, 50, 100, and 150 mm, within robotic arm links is analyzed. Based on the experimentally validated FEA model, the harmonic analysis results show that the embedded MM design in robotic arm links expectedly provides superior passive vibration damping, achieving up to a 93% reduction in resonant vibration amplitude in the most structurally vulnerable orientation, i.e., FSO, subjected to 159% higher von Mises stresses. This study highlights the ability of additively manufactured MMs to passively damp robotic arm vibrations without compromising static structural integrity.

title: Dual-function niobium-doped carbon dots for ferroptosis-driven anti-inflammatory therapy in pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia via GPX4 axis
abstract: Escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and the complex pathophysiology of severe hospital-acquired Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) pneumonia, driven by a vicious cycle of oxidation-inflammation and ferroptosis, require innovative therapeutic strategies beyond traditional antibiotics. Host-directed therapies that modulate immune responses and reduce tissue damage are promising. We developed niobium-doped Arctiin-derived carbon dots (Nb-Arctiin-CDs) via a one-step hydrothermal strategy. This nanoplatform integrates the intrinsic anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties of Arctiin with the redox activity of niobium within a biocompatible carbon-based framework, enabling enhanced therapeutic functionality. Nb-Arctiin-CDs demonstrate strong antibacterial and biofilm-eradication effects against PA, killing over 90% of bacteria by disrupting membranes and inhibiting bacterial growth. In infected MHS cells, Nb-Arctiin-CDs suppressed inflammatory cytokine and iNOS expression, reduced oxidative stress, and restored mitochondrial membrane potential. Critically, the nanomaterial also acts as a potent ferroptosis inhibitor by coordinately downregulating ferroptosis drivers and restoring the core defense axis, with GPX4 serving as a regulator linking ferroptosis suppression to anti-inflammatory effects. In a mouse model of PA pneumonia, Nb-Arctiin-CDs decrease lung injury, edema, and cytokine levels while improving bacterial clearance. Biosafety analysis shows excellent biocompatibility and no systemic toxicity. Nb-Arctiin-CDs offer a safe, effective host-directed therapy with potential for treating bacterial pneumonia and ferroptosis-related inflammatory diseases.

title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of Kovar and hypereutectic Al-Si alloy joints brazed with different processing parameters
abstract: Hypereutectic Al-Si alloys have emerged as promising next-generation electronic packaging materials because of their low density, high thermal conductivity, and tailorable coefficient of thermal expansion, whereas achieving reliable joining with Kovar alloy remains a key challenge for practical applications. Reliable vacuum brazing of Al-50Si alloy and 4J42 Kovar alloy at 540 ℃ was achieved using an Al-20Cu-12 Ga brazing filler foil prepared by rapid solidification. The effects of holding time on the microstructural evolution, mechanical properties, and hermeticity of the brazed joints were systematically investigated, revealing the intrinsic relationship among the brazing process, microstructure, and joint performance.The results show that the joint exhibits the best overall performance at a holding time of 40 min, with a shear strength of 67.99 MPa and a leakage rate of 1 × 10 −10 Pa·m 3 /s. Microstructural analysis indicates that the composite structure of a dense interfacial layer and dispersed strengthening phases formed at 40 min is responsible for the excellent joint performance. Fracture analysis reveals that the joint failure mode is a ductile–brittle mixed fracture dominated by brittle fracture. These results provide a reliable processing route and theoretical support for the low-temperature joining of dissimilar materials in electronic packaging.

title: Multiscale microstructural regulation and enhanced tensile and tribological performance of CNTs-reinforced IN718 fabricated by laser powder bed fusion
abstract: CNTs-reinforced IN718 composites were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) to clarify how CNT addition affects the microstructural evolution and service-related properties of the alloy. Compared with monolithic IN718, CNTs-IN718 exhibited clear grain refinement, an increased fraction of low-angle grain boundaries, and elevated local misorientation, indicating enhanced subgrain subdivision and a more defect-rich microstructure. Raman and TEM/EDS analyses further showed that part of the CNT-derived carbon framework was retained after LPBF, while carbon-containing nanoscale heterogeneities associated with Nb/Mo enrichment formed in the matrix. These multiscale structural changes led to a significant increase in hardness from 8.21 ± 0.02 GPa to 10.20 ± 0.02 GPa and in the H 3 /E 2 value from 0.00773 to 0.01972, indicating enhanced resistance to local plastic deformation. Correspondingly, the ultimate tensile strength increased from approximately 1.0 GPa to about 1.58 GPa, although accompanied by a moderate reduction in tensile ductility. In addition, CNTs-IN718 exhibited substantially improved tribological performance under dry sliding, with the wear volume and wear rate decreasing by about 54.3% and 53.4%, respectively. The improved mechanical and tribological properties are attributed primarily to multiscale microstructural regulation, including grain refinement, enhanced substructure evolution, local solute redistribution, and CNT-assisted interfacial constraint effects.

title: Bi-doped GeSeTe selector-only memory enabling enlarged threshold voltage window and stable array-level operation
abstract: Storage-class memory (SCM) bridges the performance gap between volatile main memory and nonvolatile storage in data-intensive and AI-driven computing systems. To achieve DRAM-comparable speed while maintaining nonvolatility, memory devices must provide high-speed operation, reliable switching characteristics, and compatibility with high-density integration. Selector-only memory (SOM) based on ovonic threshold switching (OTS) represents a promising candidate because it enables intrinsic cell selectivity without an additional selector device. Although the switching current is volatile, the threshold voltage can be nonvolatilely separated depending on the history of bipolar write pulses, allowing it to serve as a memory state. A quantitative comparison of GeSeTe (GST) and Bi-doped GeSeTe (GST:Bi) SOM devices fabricated under identical process conditions shows that Bi incorporation significantly enlarges the memory window, sharpens the switching onset, and improves endurance and drift stability. Stable threshold voltage separation is maintained at the array level. Electrical and material analyses suggest that Bi incorporation modifies the effective transport landscape and electronic structure, enabling enhanced threshold-voltage controllability and stable memory-window retention under the investigated device and array conditions.

title: NURBS-based explicit triply periodic minimal surfaces reconstruction for porous design and isogeometric analysis
abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface structures are increasingly used in high-performance engineering applications, but their complex topology and implicit representation hinder integration with conventional CAD/CAE systems. This work proposes a unified NURBS-based reconstruction framework for explicit modeling of triply periodic minimal surface porous structures, including four representative types: Primitive (P), I-Wrapped Package (I-WP), Gyroid (G), and Diamond (D). The framework first constructs -continuous spline patches using constrained fitting, then extracts smooth surfaces through a Bézier mapping strategy with enforced -continuity, and finally generates trivariate spline solids from offset surfaces for direct shell and solid extraction at prescribed offset distances. Quantitative reconstruction-error evaluation and continuity analysis confirm the accuracy and smoothness of the generated models. A quadratic relationship between offset distance and implicit level-set constant is established for thickness control, and an inverse design strategy is developed to obtain structures with target physical properties. The resulting explicit models are compatible with isogeometric analysis and standard boolean operations. An open-source software platform, Explicit TPMS Structure Generator, is developed to support modeling, inverse design, and geometry export.

title: Interfacial characteristics and mechanical properties of the WC/γ-Fe interface in WC/SS 316L composites fabricated by laser powder bed fusion
abstract: This study combines density functional theory (DFT) calculations with experimental analysis. The plane-averaged charge density difference at the interfaces was systematically evaluated, and the structural evolution and electronic property changes during different stages of tensile failure were thoroughly analyzed. The experimental characterization elucidated the strengthening mechanisms of WC particles on the matrix, elemental segregation behavior, and fracture micro-morphology. The calculation results indicate that a strong polar covalent bond exists between Fe and C, and the charge redistribution at the C-terminated interface has a more profound influence. For the three WC/γ-Fe interfaces, the theoretical critical strains are 1%, 13%, and 19%, corresponding to tensile strengths of 11.98 GPa, 34.66 GPa, and 37.53 GPa, respectively. Among these, the WC(0 0 0 1)/γ-Fe(1 1 1) interface with W-HCP configuration is the highest bonding strength. A higher interfacial tensile strength tends to shift the fracture location from the interface to the interior of the matrix. Experimentally, it was found that the introduction of WC provides heterogeneous nucleation sites for the melt pool, refining the matrix microstructure. The formed tungsten-rich carbides preferentially segregate along grain boundaries, effectively impeding dislocation motion, which constitutes the primary strengthening mechanism for the enhanced plasticity of the composite

title: pH/photothermal-responsive hydrogel with on-demand detachability for diabetic wound healing via macrophage reprogramming
abstract: Impaired wound healing in diabetic patients, driven by oxidative stress, bacterial infection, and inflammatory imbalance, poses a significant clinical challenge. Traditional dressings often cause secondary injury and pain during replacement, exacerbating patient distress. Herein, we developed an intelligent, on-demand detachable hydrogel dressing (CFTF) via dynamic crosslinking among carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS), 2-formylphenylboronic acid (2-FPBA), and tannic acid-Fe 3+ nanoparticles (TAFe NPs). Synergistic borate ester and metal-phenolic coordination bonds endowed the hydrogel with superior mechanical strength, self-healing capability, injectability, and tissue adhesiveness. Critically, the dressing enables citric acid-triggered on-demand dissolution for atraumatic removal without damaging fragile regenerating tissue. Its pH- and near-infrared (NIR)-responsive TA release enables efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging. Leveraging the photothermal effect of TAFe under NIR irradiation, the hydrogel effectively eradicated pathogenic bacteria and suppressed biofilm formation. Concurrently, the released TA induces macrophage polarization towards the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. It rectifies the inflammatory imbalance, downregulates pro-inflammatory cytokines, and thus remodels the wound microenvironment. In diabetic rat models, the CFTF hydrogel significantly accelerated wound closure by promoting granulation tissue formation, angiogenesis, and ordered collagen deposition. This multifunctional hydrogel, integrating on-demand removal with multi-modal therapeutic actions, presents a comprehensive and promising strategy for the management of diabetic wounds.

title: A defect-induced property degradation map for high-pressure die-cast aluminum structure based on 3D porosity and mechanical property heterogeneity
abstract: Large aluminum structures can be manufactured by HPDC with a large-tonnage clamping force. However, reliability cannot be ensured by geometric filling alone, because defects and properties vary along the flow path. In this study, a 3800 mm S-shaped thin-wall aluminum casting was used to reveal the link between process attenuation, porosity, and mechanical property degradation. Samples were taken at flow lengths of 1000, 2000, and 3000 mm. Computational fluid dynamics simulation, OM/SEM, micro-CT, pore classification, finite-element analysis, and tensile testing were combined. Progressive pressure loss and flow instability were predicted from the near-gate region to the flow end. A clear transition in pore population was identified. Sparse regular pores were replaced by gas-dominated irregular pores and mixed gas-shrinkage defects. Strength was only moderately reduced. Elongation was much more sensitive to pore volume fraction and volume-weighted sphericity. A defect-induced property degradation map was then constructed by using porosity fraction and volume-weighted sphericity as defect coordinates. Safe, transitional, and critical regimes were defined by property retention. The map was further validated using an integrated rear-floor casting. It provides a practical basis for property zoning and local quality assessment of long-flow HPDC aluminum structures. This framework supports local quality assessment in industrial castings.

title: Materials and design strategies for interposer-based packaging: A comparative review of silicon, glass, and organic platforms
abstract: In heterogeneous integration packaging, interposers are fundamental components that provide high bandwidth, low latency, and die-to-die connections by integrating multiple functional dies, such as logic and memory, within a single package. They have also gained significant attention for addressing challenges that are increasingly difficult to resolve through process scaling alone, such as rising power density, declining reliability, and memory walls. Packaging technologies are expected to become increasingly miniaturized and integrated as the demand for high-performance computing continues to increase in the fields of artificial intelligence, big data, and data center systems. Interposers provide high-density, die-to-die interconnects by combining fine-pitch wiring with through-via and through-via-less connections. In this review, we compare and summarize silicon, glass, and organic interposer technologies from material and structural perspectives, and discuss future research directions and applications, considering the advantages and limitations of each approach.

title: Experimental study of a refractory porous insulation structure used in a catastrophic flight data recorder
abstract: This article addresses the challenge of investigating the insulating composite structure of Promaform 1200 used in the thermal shields of catastrophic flight data recorders. Such a shield must ensure that the recorder can withstand a surface heat flux density of 158 kW/m 2 at 1100 °C for up to one hour. The motivation for conducting thermal tests on the insulating material is the need to investigate the coupled and complex heat transfer phenomena within a porous structure. The complexity and couplings of these phenomena require that the research program take into account a broader range of parameters that influence them. This article presents a comprehensive, multi-parameter methodology for investigating thermophysical properties, including measurements of thermal diffusivity, specific heat, thermal expansion, etc., with the determination of apparent thermal conductivity. The results illustrate the influence of the type of gas filling the porous structure, as well as its pressure, on the thermal transport properties. Additionally, the impact of a hot gas stream on the porous structure is demonstrated through the analysis of temperature rise on the rear surface of the tested sample. This analysis provides critical insights into heat and mass transfer phenomena, and the quantitative results offer valuable data for practical applications.

title: Effect of annealing on the microstructure, magnetic and corrosion properties of as-drawn Fe83Ga17 fiber
abstract: Fe-Ga alloys, capable of reversible deformation under external magnetic fields, hold considerable promise for biomedical applications. However, their practical use is limited by a reported minimum diameter of 500 μm. In this work, Fe-Ga fibers with a diameter of 200 μm were fabricated via multi-pass drawing process, followed by annealing at 850 ℃ under two different conditions: (i) without a magnetic field (annealed fiber), and (ii) with a 3000 Oe magnetic field applied along the fiber axis (MF-annealed fiber). The microstructure, magnetic properties, and corrosion behavior of the as-drawn, annealed, and MF-annealed fibers were investigated. In terms of phase composition, the three samples were similar. However, both the annealed and MF-annealed fibers exhibited a nearly perfect <101>//DD (drawing direction) texture. This differed from the as-drawn fiber, which showed a weak <001>// DD texture. Regarding magnetic properties, both annealed and MF-annealed fibers displayed reduced magnetostriction, and the MF-annealed fiber demonstrated the best soft magnetic performance, characterized by coercivity of 14.5 Oe, representing 66.7% reduction compared to the as-drawn fiber. Electrochemical tests revealed the annealed fiber possessed the highest corrosion resistance in simulated body fluid, indicated by lower corrosion current density (0.33 × 10 −4 A·cm −2 ) and higher low-frequency impedance modulus (8525.68 Ω·cm 2 ).

title: Long-term thermal stability of a novel B2-NiAl precipitate-hardened alumina forming martensitic steel
abstract: A new steel was designed for high-performance applications under extreme conditions by combining a martensitic microstructure and the co-precipitation of nano-sized MC and B2-NiAl precipitates, along with the ability to generate a protective Al-rich oxide scale. This study focuses solely on the long-term stability of this alloy during tempering at 550 and 650 °C for holding times exceeding 1000 h. At 550 °C, very fast precipitation of fine B2-NiAl particles occurred, providing remarkable strengthening even after annealing for 1100 h, while preventing the microstructural coarsening of the martensite blocks. In contrast, tempering at 650 °C induced the rapid coarsening of the B2-NiAl precipitates and the formation of precipitate-free zones. This accelerated microstructural evolution led to a more pronounced decrease in hardness compared to samples treated at 550 °C though the hierarchical martensitic microstructure was also retained. Nevertheless, it is observed that at 650 °C, (Cr, V) 23 C 6 carbides formed instead of the MC particles, in accordance with kinetic calculations carried out. The enhanced durability at temperatures below 650 °C suggests that this novel alumina-forming martensitic steel could be a suitable candidate for applications requiring long-term thermal stability under harsh environments.

title: Homologous Fe3+/Al3+-Baicalin nanoplatform remodel the tumor microenvironment for triple-negative breast cancer via synergistic ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is highly aggressive and lacks specific targeted therapeutic targets. Its immunosuppressive “cold” tumor microenvironment severely limits the efficacy of conventional chemotherapy and immunotherapy, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. To address the challenges, we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform (M@Ba-Fe/Al NPs) by coating Fe 3+ /Al 3+ -baicalin cores with homologous tumor cell membranes. Benefiting from the inherent homologous targeting capability, the nanoplatform efficiently accumulates in tumor tissues and penetrates the dense cancer-associated fibroblast barrier to achieve deep tumor infiltration. Mechanistically, M@Ba-Fe/Al NPs induce tumor ferroptosis by triggering Fenton-like reactions to deplete intracellular glutathione and accelerate lipid peroxidation, while simultaneously activating immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, Al 3+ acts as an immune adjuvant to promote dendritic cell maturation and increase intratumoral CD8 + T-cell infiltration, thereby comprehensively remodeling the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. By synergistically integrating ferroptosis and ICD dual antitumor pathways, the designed nanoplatform effectively suppresses tumor progression with favorable biosafety, providing a promising and translatable strategy for chemodynamic-immunotherapy of TNBC.

title: 3D bioprinted GelMA scaffolds loaded with Runx2 overexpressed BMSCs for bone regeneration
abstract: Large bone defects represent one of the most challenging problems orthopedic surgeons encounter in clinical practice. Conventional methods struggle to achieve effective filling and efficient repair of bone defects. Owing to the favourable biocompatibility, hydrogel scaffolds have become a staple material being widely used in bone regeneration. To enhance its osteogenic capacity, the transplantation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) is a frequently employed approach. However, the osteogenic differentiation capacity of unmodified BMSCs within hydrogels is often limited, which restricts their clinical applications. To address this limitation, lentiviral vectors were firstly employed to transfect the key osteogenic transcription factor Runx2 into BMSCs, in this work, to generate Runx2-overexpressing BMSCs ( Runx2 -OE-BMSCs). Subsequently, Runx2 -OE-BMSCs were encapsulated within methacrylated gelatin (GelMA) via 3D bioprinting to fabricate Runx2 -OE-BMSCs loaded hydrogel scaffolds ( Runx2 -OE-BMSCs@GelMA). The in vitro experiments confirmed that the Runx2 -OE-BMSCs@GelMA scaffold exhibits not only excellent biocompatibility but also significantly enhances osteogenic differentiation. Furthermore, the in vivo experiments demonstrated that the Runx2 -OE-BMSCs@GelMA scaffolds could significantly enhance the bone regeneration. In summary, This therapeutic strategy focused on enhancing osteoblast osteogenic activity offers new insights into the treatment of bone defect-related diseases.

title: Temperature dependent elastic constants of powder metallurgy processed Ti6242S-Ti4822 composites
abstract: The elastic stiffness coefficients of Ti6242S-Ti4822 metal–metal composites have been measured from room temperature up to 800 °C using the resonant ultrasound spectroscopy (RUS) technique. The Young’s and shear moduli of the composites increased with increasing content of the stiffer γ-TiAl based Ti4822 alloy. The elastic moduli of the composites were well predicted by the lower bound Reuss model using the properties of the terminal Ti6242S and Ti4822 alloys. All the composites exhibited a linear decrease in the elastic constants with temperature, consistent with the fundamental thermodynamic relationship between elastic moduli, thermal expansion (CTE), specific heat capacity, density, and the Grüneisen parameter of each of the two alloys. When thermal expansion is accounted for in the analysis of the RUS data, the estimates of the elastic moduli slightly decrease, with a maximum reduction of only 1% at 800 °C for Ti4822. A simple, easily differentiable, analytical expression for the combined linear temperature and quadratic composition dependence is proposed for use during multi-material design with this composite system.

title: Atomistic deformation mechanism of CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with the grain-size gradient microstructure induced by shaped charge acceleration
abstract: The microstructural evolution of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) during the collapse process is crucial for evaluating their suitability as shaped charge liners. Here, an experimental apparatus was developed to recover liner material at collapse stage for microstructural characterization. Result reveals a pronounced gradient grain-size in the CoCrFeNi HEA liner during collapse deformation, and this feature is expected to participate in the subsequent collapse and jet formation process. Molecular dynamics (MD) planar impact simulations were further conducted to clarify the mechanical response and microstructural evolution under different gradient configurations. Simulation results under ideal nanocrystalline conditions indicate that the gradient grain-size structure exhibits a certain tendency toward shear-stress localization. Grain refinement weakens dislocation-mediated plastic deformation in this high-entropy alloy. For the gradient nanograin-size structure, increasing the proportion of the fine-grained region and introducing pre-existing twins suppress the formation of dislocation-related defect structures to some extent, thereby weakening dislocation activity. In contrast, strengthening the grain-size gradient feature significantly enhances grain-boundary activity. Grain refinement helps promote deformation homogenization in this high-entropy alloy. For the gradient nanograin-size structure, increasing the proportion of the fine-grained region and introducing pre-existing twins reduce shear-strain fluctuations in the coarse-grained region, thereby enhancing the deformation homogenization

title: Light-induced photothermal processing of hybrid GPTMS-APTES sol-gel coatings on 316L stainless steel
abstract: Coatings are a key aspect in industry, from catalytic and gas-specific barrier coatings to anti-corrosion and stealth coatings. The ability to create a coating depends on adhesion to the substrate, governed by complex mechanochemical properties, while preparation and stabilization methods facilitate their application. Robotized coating preparation enables quick application and repair on large-scale installations such as gas pipes. Hybrid GPTMS-APTES sol–gel coatings are an established option for protective surface treatment of stainless steel, but their industrial deployment is limited by energy-intensive thermal stabilization (TS) and difficulties in treating large or fixed components in situ. This work introduces a photothermal stabilization (PHTS) procedure in which a 405 nm light-emitting diode (LED) array delivers surface-localized heating, driving solvent evaporation and siloxane condensation in a conventional, photoinitiator-free GPTMS-APTES formulation. Coatings were deposited by ultrasonic atomization spraying and stabilized using three procedures: ambient (AMS), TS and PHTS. Coating thickness, surface topography, FT-IR-derived network structure, scratch-test cohesive/adhesive response and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) were used to assess whether PHTS can reproduce the coating structure, mechanical integrity and barrier performance of TS. Overall, PHTS is demonstrated as a low-energy (energy efficient), substrate-friendly alternative to standard TS, delivering equivalent protection for hybrid sol–gel coatings.

title: Experimentally informed physics-based multi-scale simulation for microstructure tailoring and cracking behavior modification in Inconel 718 during PBF-LB/M
abstract: Powder bed fusion of metals using a laser beam (PBF-LB/M) allows for the manufacturing of geometrically complex parts with tailored mechanical properties. However, residual stress-induced cracking remains a major limitation for widespread industrial adoptions. In this study, a physics-based multi-scale simulation approach to predict the microstructure evolution and its influence on cracking in Inconel 718 during PBF-LB/M is introduced. Experiments were conducted using crack samples manufactured with varying laser powers and scan strategies. Microstructures, plastic zones, crack lengths, and crack orientations were evaluated in as-built and heat-treated states. A 3D cellular automaton microstructure simulation model was set up and integrated into an extended Johnson-Cook failure model to predict local cracking susceptibilities as a function of the microstructure. The results demonstrated that grain size, grain aspect ratio, and crystallographic texture strongly affect the crack formation. Increased laser power and bidirectional scan strategies without hatch rotation promoted favorable microstructures that enhance transgranular crack resistance. The mean crack length was reduced by 16 %. The tailored microstructures contributed to an intergranular crack deflection. The proposed multi-scale modeling approach effectively predicted the cracking susceptibility after local process parameter adaptations. Consequently, the potential of microstructure tailoring to improve the component reliability was highlighted.

title: Development of pH-responsive and antibacterial semi-IPN hydrogel films based on carboxymethylcellulose and tetraethyl orthosilicate
abstract: Multifunctional hydrogel films which could combine pH responsiveness, antibacterial activity, and cytocompatibility are attractive for advanced biomedical and functional applications. In this study, semi-interpenetrating polymer network (semi-IPN) hydrogel films were fabricated from sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), followed by the incorporation of silver chloride (AgCl) to introduce antibacterial functionality. The structure, morphology, and thermal properties of the films were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The developed hydrogels exhibited reversible pH-dependent swelling, reaching approximately 850 ± 34 % in alkaline media while shrinking under acidic conditions. Ag-containing films inhibited the growth of both Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis , producing inhibition zones of 9.5 mm for each strain. Cytocompatibility evaluation using the MTT assay demonstrated excellent fibroblast viability after 7 days, with cell viabilities of 97.49 ± 0.85 % for CMC films and 93.68 ± 2.40 % for Ag-containing films, satisfying ISO 10993–5 requirements. The combination of simple processing, inexpensive raw materials, pH-responsive behavior, antibacterial performance, and cytocompatibility highlights the potential of these semi-IPN hydrogel films for applications including wound dressing, controlled drug delivery, active food packaging, biosensing, and agricultural technologies.

title: The relationship between microstructures and anisotropic constitutive behaviors in wire-arc directed energy deposition
abstract: To reveal the internal relationship between microstructures and anisotropic mechanical properties in wire-arc directed energy deposition (DED), a new integrated model for process-microstructure-property relationship is proposed with experimental design for validation. It reveals that the grain boundary effect leads to the higher mechanical strength along scanning direction in comparison with building direction due to the smaller mean free path. The mechanical strength is decreased along the building direction. The yield strength in the scanning direction is decreased from 1036.54 MPa in 5th layer to 949.57 MPa in 25th layer. The change in mechanical properties under thermal accumulation is attributed to the reduced contributions from dislocation interactions and grain boundaries. The yield strength is decreased with the increase of temperature. The flow softening can be found in stress–strain curve after the initial hardening at 600 °C-800 °C due to the formed grain globularization at high temperatures.

title: Quenching-partitioning-tempering (Q-P-T) steels: Microstructural design, interface-mediated deformation, and mechanical-property synergy
abstract: Advanced high-strength steels require a balanced combination of strength, ductility, toughness, fatigue resistance, and cost efficiency, but these properties are often limited by competing deformation and damage mechanisms. Quenching-partitioning-tempering steels address this challenge by coupling martensitic transformation, carbon partitioning, carbide precipitation, retained-austenite stabilization, and martensite/austenite interface regulation. This review summarizes recent progress in quenching-partitioning-tempering steels from three connected perspectives: microstructural design, interface-mediated deformation, and model-guided property optimization. Particular attention is given to retained-austenite stability, interfacial dislocation transfer, static/dynamic mechanical-property synergy, and predictive modelling. Current challenges are also discussed, including process-window robustness, carbide-precipitation competition, service reliability, industrial scale-up, and model transferability. Future opportunities involving additive manufacturing, interface engineering, and data-driven design are highlighted. This review provides a concise framework for understanding and designing quenching-partitioning-tempering steels for high-performance engineering applications.

title: Bio-inspired design of a 3D-printed flexible polishing tool: Structural compliance and material removal mechanisms for K9 glass
abstract: To mitigate interface closure, pressure concentration, and slurry starvation in the precision finishing of hard-brittle optics, a novel flexible polishing tool featuring a plant-root topology was designed and fabricated via stereolithography 3D printing. Incorporating hierarchical branching and continuous curvature turning, a 3D labyrinthine micro-circulation network comprising mixing, transport, and textured polishing zones was integrated into the tool. A cross-scale theoretical model coupling a modified Preston equation with elastoplastic matrix deformation and multiphase dynamics was developed to clarify the material removal mechanisms. FEA and CFD simulations demonstrated that the internal channels proactively modulate localized structural compliance—transforming the quasi-Gaussian peak stress into a flattened multi-modal profile—while alleviating core zone slurry starvation via a deformation driven pumping mechanism. Fixed point polishing experiments on K9 glass validated that the bio-inspired tool improved contact pressure homogeneity by 40.22 %, yielding a rapid surface roughness convergence from Ra 2.60 μm to 0.241 μm within 10 min, and ultimately achieved a precision finish of Ra 0.090 μm. This study provides a scientifically viable structural paradigm for high efficiency, green processing of hard-brittle materials.

title: Biomechanical effects of anatomical morphology and soft tissue stiffness on customized compression stocking design: optimized 3D finite element modelling and 3D-printed leg manikins
abstract: Graduated compression stockings (GCSs) are widely used to aid venous therapy and post-exercise recovery, yet the delivered pressure often diverges from design targets due to variations in limb morphology, tissue stiffness, and fabric mechanics. This study proposed a novel framework that integrates a morphological irregularity (IR) factor, rigid-to-soft pressure correction (CR) factor, subject-specific 3D finite element (FE) modelling, and anatomical 3D-printed manikins to systematically analyze how anatomical morphology and tissue stiffness affect GCS performance. Using 3D body scanning, shear wave elastography, and customized material characterization, 36 subject-specific FE body–garment models were developed across diverse body types and three compression classes (I, II, III). The findings revealed that limb irregular geometry, fabric material properties, and soft tissue stiffness are key determinants of pressure distribution and tissue deformation. Optimized 3D bio-leg FE models showed high predictive accuracy (4.1% average deviation; 2.8 mmHg mean absolute error) relative to measured pressures. IR factor quantified anatomically geometry-driven pressure variation for region-specific design optimization, and the 3–6 mmHg pressure offset between rigid manikins and soft bio-legs defined the critical CR factor to translate lab manikin data to real-user applications, enhancing ergonomic design and user-centered virtual fit evaluation of wearable compression textiles and garments.

title: Acid-responsive manganese carbonate-based nanotherapeutics for combined chemo- and biomineralization block therapy of hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Spontaneous calcification of the treated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has been proven to be a good prognosis predictor in the clinic. In line with this concept, artificially induced biomineralization in the tumor tissue is considered to be an unconventional yet promising therapeutic modality for HCC. However, the limited mineral ions concentration in/around tumor tissue and the modest ion-chelating capabilities of conventional biomineralization initiators often resulted slow biomineralization process and compromised antitumor efficacy. Herein, an in situ biomineralization inducing nanotherapeutic was developed for achieving precise and speedy HCC mineralization block therapy. Specifically, cytomembrane-insertion moiety DSPE-PEG was first conjugated with ion-chelating motif alendronate (ALN) to obtain the chelator DPA. And then, DPA was modified on sorafenib (SF)-loaded acidic tumor microenvironment (TME)-sensitive mesoporous MnCO 3 nanoparticles. After intravenous injection into HCC-bearing mice, the SF@MnC@DPA could accumulate in tumor site medicated by EPR effect. Subsequently, SF@MnC@DPA responds to the acidic TME to releases DPA, Mn 2+ and SF. Benefiting from the similar chemical structure of DSPE and phospholipid layer, DPA can be easily inserted into the cell membrane, and the bisphosphonic acid group of ALN could bind with the Mn 2+ to in situ construct a mineralized barrier around the tumor, thereby achieving synergistic chemotherapy and mineralization block therapy. In vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that SF@MnC@DPA successfully induced the tumor mineralization and sharply inhibited tumor growth for subcutaneous and orthotopic HCC without evidence of systemic side effects. Altogether, the proposed selective biomineralization provides an outlook for a new avenue in HCC therapy and anticancer drug development.

title: Lithium metaborate as a lightweight ultra low temperature cofired ceramic substrate for high speed communication systems
abstract: The research is aimed at fabrication, and structural, microstructural, thermal and dielectric characterization of new, inexpensive, lightweight, low permittivity substrates based on metaborate LiBO 2 , with a special focus on their applicability in the terahertz frequency range suitable for high-speed 6G communication systems and feasibility in ULTCC (ultra-low temperature cofired ceramics) technology beneficial for miniaturization, integration and cost reduction. Conventional solid state reaction methods are used for LiBO 2 synthesis and sintering of pure LiBO 2 ceramics and LiBO 2 ceramics containing two dopants − AlF 3 -CaB 4 O 7 and AlF 3 -CaB 4 O 7 -Li 2 TiO 3 . The structure, composition, microstructure and sintering behavior are investigated using XRD analysis, EDS analysis, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, thermal analysis, dilatometric measurements and heating microscope studies. Inexpensive starting materials, compatibility with cheap commercial Ag conductors and ultra low sintering temperature (650-710 °C) determines low fabrication costs of the developed substrates. LiBO 2 ceramics show very good dielectric properties in the terahertz range: a very small relative permittivity (4.5–5.2 at 1 THz), stable in a broad frequency range and a relatively small dielectric loss. The applied dopants facilitate processing due to restriction of the reactivity with water and mitigation of excessive shrinkage and warpage during sintering.

title: Plasma plume emission-driven closed-loop control in directed energy deposition
abstract: Laser-based directed energy deposition (DED) enables fabrication of large-scale metallic components; however, maintaining thermal stability and geometric consistency during multilayer deposition remains challenging. Under open-loop deposition with constant laser energy input, increasing build height promotes heat accumulation, destabilizing melt-pool dynamics and resulting in geometric inconsistency, surface irregularities, and process variability. Existing thermal and image-based closed-loop strategies remain constrained by emissivity dependence, plasma-plume shielding, spatter interference, and high computational requirements. In this study, an optical emission spectroscopy (OES)-based closed-loop framework is developed for real-time regulation of melt-pool behavior during SS 316L thin-wall DED. Plasma-plume emission at the Fe I 520.79 nm line serves as physics-linked feedback signal for hybrid rule-based and PID laser-power control. The proposed framework is evaluated against open-loop deposition. Open-loop operation exhibits increasing plume intensity, melt-pool dimensions, clad width, and geometric deviation, indicating heat-accumulation dominated behavior. In contrast, closed-loop deposition stabilizes plume intensity within a prescribed operating window, reducing melt-pool width and length variations by ∼95% and ∼80%, respectively. Surface-flatness deviation and build-height error decrease by ∼75% and ∼78%, while uniform clad width (∼1.55–1.58 mm) and fusion-band spacing (∼0.38–0.40 mm) are maintained. This work establishes plasma-plume emission as a reliable real-time feedback signal for DED process.

title: Gallium based metal–organic frameworks reverse chemoresistance in oral squamous cell carcinoma via ferroptosis induction and redox modulation
abstract: Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle in the treatment of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), especially in advanced cases where surgery is not viable. Conventional chemotherapeutics such as doxorubicin (Dox) and paclitaxel (PTX) function primarily through reactive oxygen species (ROS)-induced cytotoxicity. However, the upregulation of antioxidant defenses—particularly glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4)—enables cancer cells to neutralize ROS and resist treatment. In this study, we developed gallium-based metal–organic framework (GaMOF) as a multifunctional nanoplatform to overcome OSCC chemoresistance by modulating intracellular redox homeostasis. GaMOF disrupt antioxidant systems and promote ROS accumulation, thereby triggering ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death associated with lipid peroxidation. When loaded with Dox or PTX, GaMOF not only enhances drug efficacy in resistant OSCC cell lines but also significantly reduce tumor burden in vivo. Mechanistically, GaMOF inhibits GPX4, elevate Fe2 + and ROS levels, deplete glutathione (GSH), and reduce mitochondrial membrane potential, confirming ferroptosis induction. Notably, Chemoresistance cells were more sensitive to GaMOF than parental cells, highlighting GaMOF’s therapeutic specificity. Our findings underscore the potential of GaMOF as redox-responsive carriers capable of reversing chemoresistance via ferroptosis, offering a promising strategy for improving treatment outcomes in OSCC and other drug-resistant cancers.

title: Zwitterionic supramolecular nanoprodrug for hypoxia-responsive chemo-photodynamic therapy
abstract: Hypoxia in solid tumors poses a major obstacle to chemotherapy, often limiting the therapeutic efficacy of hypoxia-responsive prodrugs. Here, we report a zwitterionic supramolecular nanoprodrug (ZSN-DOX/Ce6) to co-delivery doxorubicin (DOX) and chlorin e6 (Ce6) for synergistic chemo-photodynamic therapy (PDT-CT). ZSN-DOX/Ce6 was constructed by 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine-pendant poly( D,L -cysteine) (PMPC), doxorubicin (DOX)-grafted pillar[5]arene-terminal-modified poly( L -lysine) (P5-PTL-DOX 2 ), and encapsulated chlorin e6 (Ce6) based on host–guest recognition. The zwitterionic corona of PMPC can effectively reduce the nonspecific protein adsorption and prolonged blood circulation. Under intracellular hypoxia, the hypoxia-responsive ternary cross-linkers (TL) in P5-PTL-DOX 2 degraded, causing the disassembly of ZSN-DOX/Ce6 to release Ce6 and activated DOX. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, photosensitizer Ce6 converted oxygen to generate single oxygen ( 1 O 2 ), further aggravating hypoxia and enhancing DOX activation. In vivo , the nanoprodrug showed prolonged circulation, enhanced tumor accumulation, and achieved an effective tumor suppression effect without systemic toxicity. Overall, ZSN-DOX/Ce6 offers a promising avenue for advanced combinatory cancer therapy.

title: A synergistically freeze-enzymatically crosslinked silk fibroin hydrogel for sustained kartogenin delivery and enhanced cartilage regeneration
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains challenging because of limited intrinsic regeneration and the need for sustained mechanical and biological support. We developed a silk fibroin (SF) scaffold combining directional freezing with HRP/H2O2-mediated enzymatic crosslinking. The resulting EF-SF hydrogel exhibited high compressive strength, limited swelling, aligned porosity, and delayed degradation. Kartogenin (KGN)-loaded PLGA nanoparticles were incorporated to form EF-SF/PK. Compared with direct KGN loading, PLGA encapsulation markedly reduced early release and prolonged KGN delivery. EF-SF/PK supported BMSC viability, proliferation, and chondrogenic gene expression, while LDH and residual peroxide measurements showed no progressive in vitro cytotoxicity. In a rabbit femoral cartilage-defect model, EF-SF/PK improved macroscopic, imaging, and histological repair over 12 weeks. These findings support a hierarchical SF scaffold that integrates mechanical stability with controlled local delivery for cartilage regeneration.

title: Multimodal fNIRS-sEMG assessment reveals enhanced cortical engagement during robot-assisted hand rehabilitation in stroke survivors
abstract: Stroke-related hand motor dysfunction severely compromises activities of daily living and remains a major target of neurorehabilitation. This study evaluates a self-developed flexible cable-driven hand rehabilitation robot in terms of its effects on cortical activation and hand muscle activity in stroke survivors and healthy controls. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) monitored sensorimotor cortical hemodynamics, while eight-channel surface electromyography (sEMG) captured muscle activation during three grasping conditions: voluntary grasping, robot-assisted passive grasping, and bimanual grasping with unilateral robotic assistance. Robot-assisted and bimanual tasks elicited stronger contralateral motor-cortex activation than voluntary grasping alone, particularly in stroke participants. Within the study cohort, machine-learning analysis of the sEMG signals distinguished affected from unaffected hand movements and robot-assisted from non-assisted states with 97.33 % and 94.67 % accuracy, respectively. These findings quantify the synergistic roles of motor intention, sensory feedback, and robotic assistance in modulating cortical activity and muscle recruitment, and provide evidence to guide the design of intelligent, data-driven hand rehabilitation strategies after stroke.

title: Smart response food-derived polysaccharide hydrogels: reprogramming the microenvironment for skin rejuvenation
abstract: Skin aging is a multifaceted biological process marked by the disruption of the ROS-MMP-collagen axis, resulting in the degradation of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and compromised barrier function. Traditional synthetic interventions often face challenges related to biocompatibility and limited efficacy in targeted delivery. In contrast, food-derived polysaccharide hydrogels (FDPH) have emerged as a novel class of bio-instructive materials. These hydrogels extend beyond the conventional role of passive scaffolds by leveraging their intrinsic bioactivity and tunable three-dimensional architectures, which may contribute to the modulation of aging-associated microenvironmental factors. This review offers a comprehensive critical analysis of the evolution of FDPH from their initial role as structural fillers to their current status as sophisticated therapeutic platforms. These platforms are capable of detecting pathological signals, including pH, ROS, and enzymes, thus facilitating more precise and localized therapeutic interventions.We explore the molecular mechanisms that underpin their dual functionality in mitigating oxidative stress and influencing fibroblast-associated regenerative processes that may support collagen remodeling. Additionally, it identifies challenges such as structural variability, transdermal efficiency, and long-term safety. The review also predicts future trends in precision design and personalized applications, fueled by AI and multi-omics, guiding the advancement of FDPH for skin health and anti-aging.

title: Machine-learning-guided critical thickness design of gradient-nanostructured layers for fretting-resistant 304 stainless steel
abstract: Fretting damage severely limits the service reliability of stainless-steel components operating under cyclic micro-slip conditions. Although surface mechanical attrition treatment (SMAT) can introduce gradient nanostructures (GNS) and improve damage resistance, optimizing the GNS layer thickness remains computationally expensive because it typically requires repeated simulations or experiments. In this work, we develop a simulation-driven machine-learning framework for predicting the fretting damage response of GNS materials. A multi-parameter two-dimensional finite-element model was first established, from which the key parameters controlling fretting damage response were identified through linear and nonlinear analysis. A material-specific database for SMATed 304SS was then constructed by stochastic sampling within the reduced feature space. TabPFN was selected as the surrogate model after benchmarking against conventional regressors. SHAP analysis further revealed the physically interpretable roles of key variables, especially the dominant effect of GNS layer thickness on suppressing plastic-zone expansion. Based on the predicted response curves, a critical effective GNS layer thickness was identified and a secondary surrogate model was established for rapid finite-element-consistent thickness screening. Controlled sliding tests qualitatively supported the predicted saturation-type trend in contact-induced plastic deformation. The proposed framework provides an efficient route for response prediction and gradient-structure design of fretting-resistant GNS materials.

title: Material-Driven Design of Friction-Minimized Coned Disc Springs Using Anisotropic Magnetic Elastomers
abstract: The structural design of conventional coned disc spring (CDS) isolators is inherently constrained by asymmetric hysteresis and excessive frictional damping. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a material-driven design strategy utilizing anisotropic magnetic rubber (MR) interlayers to develop a novel, high-performance vertical isolation device. Leveraging the double-sided adhesion of the MR sheets, the interfacial contact mechanics are fundamentally altered. This functional material integration effectively suppresses inter-disc slippage, minimizes parasitic friction, and enhances structural alignment under cyclic dynamic loading. This hybrid material-structural design was evaluated through material characterization, cyclic component testing, three-dimensional finite element (FE) contact analysis, and modified Bouc-Wen phenomenological modeling. Planar tensile characterization of the MR material revealed a three-stage elastomeric response, optimally captured for predictive numerical design by a second-order Ogden hyperelastic formulation. Cyclic testing validated the proposed architecture, demonstrating that the MR-enhanced configuration reduces unloading stiffness and frictional energy dissipation, thereby yielding symmetric hysteresis and superior self-centering capacity compared to traditional CDS designs. Both the FE framework and the analytical model reproduced the nonlinear kinematics and energy dissipation characteristics across varying operational parameters. Thus, the integration of MR interlayers provides a mechanically stable, repeatable design solution for advanced vertical vibration isolation and seismic mitigation systems.

title: Bulk acoustic wave-assisted preparation of the hydrogel with directionally arranged particles
abstract: The directional arrangement of particles in the hydrogel is a pivotal factor influencing their performance and applicability. However, how to achieve precise particle arrangement during the preparation of the hydrogel is a key challenge. Herein, by integrating a photo mask, a novel preparation method of hydrogel with particle directional arrangement induced by bulk acoustic waves (BAWs) is presented. Different directional arrangement modes of the PS microspheres can be controlled by applying a sinusoidal voltage to different piezoelectric transducers. By adjusting the driving frequency and the peak-to-peak value of the applied sinusoidal voltage frequency driving voltage of BAWs, the spacing and arrangement time of the particle arrangement in the hydrogel can be flexibly adjusted. Hydrogels with different three-dimensional morphologies can be prepared through the integrated use of a photo mask. This method has been successfully applied in the application of the magnetic actuator, indicating significant potential for use in fabricating functional hydrogels.

title: Design strategy, properties and application of high-strength and tough hydrogel: A review
abstract: Hydrogels have garnered significant attention in diverse fields, including flexible electronics, biomedicine, and water treatment, owing to their unique physicochemical properties and biocompatibility. However, the inherent trade-off between mechanical strength and toughness in traditional hydrogels has severely limited their practical applications, particularly in load-bearing scenarios and harsh environments. To address this issue, extensive efforts have been devoted to developing high-strength and tough hydrogels through structural design and functional modification. This review systematically summarizes the core design strategies for enhancing the mechanical performance of hydrogels, including molecular network engineering, morphological structure optimization, filler-filled modification, and other innovative approaches.
