Furthermore, the applications of these high-performance hydrogels in various fields, such as flexible sensors, tissue engineering, and antifouling materials, are comprehensively discussed.

title: Fiber printing: Functional 3D printing of structural hinges for deformable structures
abstract: Deformable structures comprising rigid components and connecting hinges may be fabricated in a single fused filament fabrication 3D-printing process. The hinges must be highly flexible and sufficiently strong. In the present study, a concept of fiber printing was proposed. A flexible yet high-strength fiber filament comprising Kevlar fibers partially coated with a thermoplastic polymer was developed. Compared with conventional composite filaments, the impregnation level was intentionally kept low to maintain fiber mobility. The polymer coating was utilized to increase the printability of fibers. The fiber-printed hinge had higher tensile strength than a 3D-printed compliant hinge made of thermoplastic polyurethane, even after 10 5 bending cycles. For comparison, printing with two other types of composites made of Kevlar fibers fully impregnated with Nylon or polyurethane, rather than a surface coating, was adopted to produce hinges. However, the hinges made of the composites failed during cyclic bending, or their tensile strength was significantly reduced. These results demonstrated the advantages of fiber printing as a means of producing high-strength and flexible hinges. Gripper structures were 3D-printed to demonstrate the technique. Gripping tests showed that the fiber-printed deformable structure had a higher output force than a compliant gripper, demonstrating that the fiber-printing ensures enhanced functionality.

title: Study on the formation and suppression mechanism of defects corresponding to typical morphologies in electron beam powder bed fusion
abstract: Electron beam powder bed fusion (PBF-EB) offers high energy utilization and forming efficiency, making it attractive for aerospace, biomedical, and other applications. However, large-scale forming faces challenges due to defects such as incomplete fusion, porosity, and cracks. This study investigates the correlation between typical morphologies and defect formation. Forming experiments under varying beam conditions were conducted, and defects in parts with different morphologies were analyzed. Balling surfaces in PBF-EB tend to cause porosity, while over-melted surfaces lead to geometric defects. Images show a linear correlation with CT results, though prediction errors remain large. Flow3D simulations reveal that low energy input yields insufficient melting and spherical surfaces, whereas moderate input remelts them, eliminating incomplete fusion. Forming experiments with varying beam current confirmed that energy input adjustment effectively suppresses defects, guiding feedback regulation in PBF-EB.

title: The influence of alloying on properties of additively manufactured in-situ particle reinforced Fe-Ti alloys using reactive process atmospheres
abstract: In powder bed fusion – laser beam (PBF–LB), the process gas has been used to fabricate in-situ oxide dispersion strengthened (ODS) steels. Processing in reactive atmospheres, e.g. CO 2 and N 2 , causes process gas dissociation and absorption into the melt pool, thereby promoting nanoparticle formation. The intensity of the interaction depends on the atmosphere’s reactivity and the alloy composition. A strong interaction with the atmosphere is favorable to enhance nanoparticle formation. In this work, Fe-Ti model alloys with varying Ti content are processed via PBF–LB. The influence of the Ti alloying content on process gas uptake, nanoparticle, and slag layer formation is studied using Ar, CO 2, and N 2 atmospheres. Based on thermodynamic simulations, the resulting oxides are, depending on the Ti concentration, TiO or Ti 2 O 3 . The fraction and number density of nanoparticles are mainly determined by the processing gas and resulting O supersaturation in the melt pool. In-situ alloying and Ti-oxide nanoparticles additionally affect the grain structure of the processed materials and hence the hardness and creep performance of the materials. This work provides the fundament for targeted alloy design for advanced in-situ particle reinforced materials using reactive atmospheres in AM

title: Graphene nanosheets for enhancing the corrosion resistance of stainless steel in marine environments
abstract: This study presents a sustainable and cost-effective approach for enhancing the corrosion resistance of stainless-steel (SS) using graphene nanosheet (GNSs) coatings. GNSs were produced via liquid-phase shear exfoliation in water and deposited onto SS through an interfacial self-assembly process to form uniform and well-adhered films. Structural and morphological characterization confirmed the formation of highly crystalline few-layer graphene (3 to 5 layers) with lateral sizes of 50–80 nm. Continuous coatings with thicknesses ranging from 30 to 120 nm were obtained by varying the number of deposition cycles. Electrochemical measurements demonstrated that the self-assembled graphene coating significantly improved corrosion protection. Compared with bare SS, coated samples exhibited a more noble E corr (− 30 mV), a fivefold reduction in Jcorr (12 nA.cm −2 ), nearly double the polarization resistance (Rp = 253 kΩ), and an almost fourfold decrease in corrosion rate. EIS measurements further confirmed the long-term protective performance of the coating. Post-immersion SEM, Raman, and XRD analyses revealed excellent structural stability in a marine environment, with no detectable corrosion products. These findings demonstrate that self-assembled graphene nanosheet films act as effective barriers against chloride-induced corrosion, highlighting their potential as durable, ultrathin and environmentally friendly protective coatings for metallic substrates.

title: An integrated experimental and modeling approach to mitigate defects in multi-layer bronze HSLC
abstract: The application of high-speed laser cladding (HSLC) to multi-layer deposition is hindered by interlayer defects, as the powder stream attenuates a significant fraction of the laser power reaching the previous layer. This study investigates the origin of these defects, explores mitigation strategies, and proposes an integrated experimental and analytical methodology to support physically informed multi-layer HSLC process development. Three bilayer deposition strategies were evaluated: surface preparation via laser remelting, laser power adaptation, and a combined approach. At low deposition power on rough surfaces, partial filling of surface asperities keeps layers attached through mechanical interlocking but leaves seam lines and lack-of-fusion defects. Increasing deposition power on rough surfaces improves interlayer continuity, but promotes spherical pore formation. Surface pre-smoothing removes the interlocking potential, causing sharp delamination at insufficient second-layer power. Combining pre-smoothing with moderately increased deposition power suppresses visible lack-of-fusion and delamination. This strategy was applied to produce a four-layer proof-of-concept demonstrator. An adapted 1D heat conduction model was fitted to experimental remelting depth data. By correlating remelting thresholds from the fitted model with experimental bilayer results, an effective attenuation of ∼ 63% was estimated. This study supports multi-layer HSLC process development by shifting from trial-and-error toward a more physically informed approach.

title: Plane-stress fracture toughness of hygrothermally degraded PC/ABS blends evaluated by the essential work of fracture: characterization and degradation-index-informed prediction
abstract: PC/ABS blends are widely used in thin-walled components for electronics and automotive applications, where resistance to hygrothermal embrittlement is important for long-term durability. In this study, the degradation of fracture resistance under plane-stress conditions was investigated for two PC/ABS blends (50:50 and 75:25) using double-edge-notched tensile (DDENT) specimens and the essential work of fracture (EWF) methodology. The specimens were subjected to accelerated hygrothermal aging at 85 °C/85% RH for up to 1344 h. The specific essential work of fracture, w e , and the slope term, βw p , were used to quantify intrinsic fracture resistance and crack-growth-related plastic dissipation, respectively. Both parameters decreased with increasing exposure time for both blends. The 50:50 blend exhibited marked deterioration and a transition to brittle behavior after 1008 h, whereas the 75:25 blend showed a similar transition after 672 h, indicating earlier embrittlement. In addition, statistical analyses were performed to further assess the degradation-related property reductions, and a data-informed property prediction model was developed by training an artificial neural network using FT-IR-derived chemical indices and data augmentation. The predicted EWF parameters showed close agreement with the measured values, supporting the proposed data-informed framework for durability assessment of thin-walled PC/ABS structures under hygrothermal environments.

title: Active-learning-guided discovery of alumina-forming refractory complex concentrated alloys
abstract: Refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs) are of significant interest for advanced high-temperature applications due to their wide compositional range and potential for attractive mechanical properties and oxidation resistance. However, their compositional complexity challenges conventional alloy discovery approaches. Here, an active learning framework integrating Gaussian process regression with Bayesian global optimization is introduced to accelerate the identification of oxidation-resistant RCCAs. Focusing on aluminum-containing quaternary systems, alloy and oxide descriptors were used to predict oxidation performance at 1000°C. Beginning with a dataset of 81 experimentally validated alloys, the framework iteratively selected batches of five alloys, balancing exploration and exploitation to minimize experimental costs. After six iterations, two alloys—nominal Al₃₀Mo₅Ti₁₅Cr₅₀ and Al₄₀Mo₅Ti₃₀Cr₂₅—exhibited specific mass gains below 1 mg/cm² after 24 h at 1000°C in air, forming adherent external α-Al₂O₃ scales with parabolic oxidation kinetics consistent with diffusion-limited scale growth. Multiobjective analysis further demonstrates that these alloys achieve high specific hardness (>0.12 HV·m³/kg) and thermal expansion compatibility with thermal barrier coating systems, suggesting their potential as candidate bond coat materials, warranting further investigation. This work underscores the efficacy of active learning in traversing complex compositional landscapes and offers a scalable strategy for developing advanced materials for extreme environments.

title: Dual-functional daytime radiative cooling and anti-mosquito fabrics via the single-step coating strategy for tropical outdoor personal protection
abstract: In tropical environments, outdoor tent fabric (OTF) is challenged by the dual threats of thermal strain and vector-borne diseases. Conventional multifunctional finishing processes typically involve repetitive coating cycles, which not only compromise fabric flexibility but also lead to inefficient and complex manufacturing workflows. This study aims to develop a dual-functional radiative cooling and anti-mosquito fabrics by one-step coating of mosquito repellent-loaded SiO 2 microcapsules (SiO 2 -M). SiO 2 -M with a branch-like porous structure was prepared via a template agent-induced pore formation method, which was further stabilized by TPU. The as-prepared coating agent was applied to polyester fabric using a simple blade-coating process. The coated fabric exhibited a uniform micro/nano rough surface structure, achieving a solar reflectance of 92% in the visible light range, a thermal emissivity of 92.5% in the mid-infrared atmospheric window, and a radiative cooling power of 108 W/m 2 under the optimal coating conditions. The coated polyester fabric achieved a maximum temperature drop of up to 11.4 °C under sunlight exposure, compared to that of pure fabric. Furthermore, coated fabric achieved a repellency rate over 70% against Aedes albopictus and good abrasion resistance. In addition, the fabric exhibited satisfactory hydrophobic and anti-ultraviolet characteristics, exhibiting a water contact angle of 139° and an ultraviolet protection factor (UPF) of UPF50+. In summary, the prepared coated fabric showed satisfactory radiative cooling and mosquito prevention effects, indicating its potential for applications in outdoor tents and equipment.

title: Endogenous near-infrared chemiluminescent heteronuclear transition-metal hydrogel platform: imaging-guided multimodal therapy for bacteria-infected wounds
abstract: Current treatments for bacteria-infected wounds face significant challenges, including increasing bacterial resistance, inadequate regulation of the wound microenvironment, and lack of real-time monitoring, severely compromising deep-tissue healing. To address these challenges, we designed a quad-modal smart hydrogel platform ( CS-PPA-Cu/PF@Arg ) responsive to the infected microenvironment. Constructed via dynamic Schiff-base crosslinking between chitosan-grafted copper porphyrin derivatives ( CS-PPA-Cu ) and a protocatechualdehyde-ferric tricomplex ( PF ), this platform integrates near-infrared chemiluminescence (NIR CL) imaging-guided therapy, photothermal/photodynamic therapy (PTT/PDT), and nitric oxide (NO) gas therapy. It introduces peroxynitrite (ONOO − )-activated NIR CL imaging into wound healing research and leverages copper/iron bimetallic synergy to enable visual monitoring of deep-tissue inflammation, dynamic reactive oxygen species (ROS) regulation, and combined PTT/PDT. The copper porphyrin enhances the NIR emission intensity by approximately 11-fold and increases penetration to 8 mm, enabling real-time ROS sensing and scavenging, while the iron complex ensures efficient PTT conversion and anti-inflammatory/antioxidant activities via ligand-to-metal charge transfer. In vitro and in vivo , CS-PPA-Cu/PF@Arg significantly accelerates wound healing through synergistic PTT/PDT, NO release, and metal ion effects, promoting epithelial migration, suppressing excessive inflammation, exerting antibacterial/antioxidant actions, and stimulating angiogenesis. This integrated strategy pairs NIR CL diagnostics with multimodal therapy, offering a promising approach for intelligent wound biomaterials

title: Effect of synthesis pathway on HER performance of tungsten carbide compared to commercial WC
abstract: The relationship between synthesis strategy and electrocatalytic performance plays an important role in the rational design of non-noble metal catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, tungsten carbide (S-WC) was synthesized via a facile ammonia-assisted route, and its electrocatalytic activity was systematically benchmarked against commercially available tungsten carbide (C-WC). Electrochemical measurements revealed that S-WC achieved a current density of 0.5 mA cm −2 at overpotentials of 297 mV in 1 M KOH and 340 mV in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 , demonstrating superior HER activity compared with C-WC under identical operating conditions. The corresponding Tafel slopes of 128 and 140 mV dec –1 suggest that the HER kinetics in both alkaline and acidic media are governed predominantly by a Volmer step-limited pathway. Furthermore, the higher exchange current density obtained for S-WC indicates more favourable interfacial charge-transfer kinetics than those of C-WC. The improved performance is attributed to the ammonia-assisted synthesis route, which modifies the surface characteristics of tungsten carbide and increases the density of electrochemically accessible active sites, thereby facilitating faster interfacial charge transfer. Overall, this work demonstrates how synthesis strategy governs the structure–property relationship in tungsten carbide catalysts and provides insight into the rational design of efficient, pH-universal HER electrocatalysts.

title: Interfacial design of a dual-channel Au–CC nanoplatform for orthogonal decoding of complementary MMP-12/uPA proteolytic axes in NSCLC
abstract: Proteolytic remodeling is a key feature of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progression, yet most activity-based probes focus on single enzymes and provide limited information on coordinated invasive behavior. Here, we report a dual-channel Au–C C nanoplatform for orthogonal decoding of matrix metalloproteinase-12 (MMP-12) and urokinase-type plasminogen activator (uPA), two complementary proteolytic axes associated with extracellular matrix remodeling and pericellular proteolysis in NSCLC. The platform was fabricated by co-anchoring a 5-TAMRA-labeled MMP-12-responsive peptide and a FITC-labeled uPA-responsive peptide onto gold nanoparticles, enabling dual fluorescence activation after enzyme-triggered cleavage. The resulting nanoplatform showed uniform morphology, good colloidal stability, clear spectral orthogonality, and stable interfacial performance under thermal, glutathione-rich, and pH-variable conditions. Quantitative fluorescence responses were obtained for MMP-12 and uPA, with detection limits of 3.26 ng/mL and 1.62 ng/mL, respectively. In living cells, the platform displayed good cytocompatibility, distinguished A549 from Beas-2b cells, and supported activity-level profiling of an NSCLC-associated proteolytic state. This work highlights the value of Au–C C interfacial design in constructing dual-channel nanoplatforms for coordinated protease decoding in cancer-related remodeling.

title: A 3D-printed GTP@PTH composite scaffold with synergistic immunomodulatory and osteogenic capabilities for osteoporotic bone regeneration
abstract: The treatment of osseous deficiencies in osteoporotic patients continues to pose significant clinical difficulties, requiring scaffolds that can simultaneously modulate the regenerative immune microenvironment and restore bone homeostasis. Here, we fabricated porous microspheres capable of the sustained release of the immunomodulator proanthocyanidin (PC) and the bone‑anabolic regulator PTH(1‑34). These microspheres were then integrated into a 3D‑printed organic–inorganic composite scaffold that exhibited high compressive strength and modulus. The scaffold’s interconnected porosity supported tissue in‑growth, while its high modulus and inorganic salt composition promoted osteogenic differentiation of stem cells. In parallel, surface‑grafted alendronate (ALN) regulated osteoblast/osteoclast activity and chelated calcium ions on the bone surface to form stable interfacial structures. Both in vitro and in vivo studies indicate that the GTP@PTH scaffold, leveraging the combined actions of PC and PTH (1–34), modulates the immune microenvironment and skeletal homeostasis to support bone regeneration. This system restrains M1 macrophage polarization, promotes an M2 phenotype, and limits osteoclast over-differentiation, thus enhancing osteogenic activity. Such a multifunctional platform shows considerable promise for repairing bone defects under osteoporotic conditions, offering a viable approach for developing clinically applicable biomaterial solutions

title: On the compressive and flexural properties of additively manufactured 316 L stainless steel sheet-based spinodal, stochastic and periodic TPMS cellular metamaterials
abstract: The mechanical properties of cellular structures derived from spinodal decomposition and triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMSs) are gaining interest for lightweight metamaterials, particularly with advances in additive manufacturing. While the compressive and flexural performance of periodic cellular structures has been widely studied, the influence of stochasticity in microstructural orientation remains insufficiently investigated. This study investigates the mechanical response of sheet-based cellular structures, including TPMS-based periodic, TPMS-based stochastic, and spinodal-based structures. TPMS-based stochastic structures are generated using Gyroid and Diamond topologies through random rotation of unit cells within dispersed control volumes, whereas spinodal-based structures are formed using the Gaussian random field method. Experimental and numerical analyses are performed to evaluate the stress–strain responses under uniaxial compression and three-point bending loadings. Numerical results indicate that periodic TPMS structures exhibit up to 58% and 61% higher compressive yield and plateau strengths, respectively, and up to 51% higher flexural strength than their stochastic counterparts. The numerical predictions for stochastic structures are validated experimentally, demonstrating good agreement. All analyzed stochastic cellular structures display similar compressive and flexural responses, with Gyroid-based stochastic structure showing slightly better properties. Overall, TPMS-based stochastic design approach produces stochastic structures with enhanced compressive and flexural properties compared with spinodal-based structures.

title: Molecular process modeling and validation of a bismaleimide resin for multiscale composites design
abstract: Bismaleimide (BMI) resins are widely used as a matrix in high-performance polymer matrix composites used for aerospace structural applications. Despite the growing use of integrated computational materials engineering (ICME) frameworks in modern structural design to model residual stress evolution and damage during composite material processing, the cure-dependent properties of BMI remain poorly characterized, limiting their effective use as critical ICME inputs. This work is the first to produce an experimentally-validated molecular dynamics (MD) cure model of a BMI resin as a function of processing progression, thus successfully incorporating the complex and process-sensitive chemistry of the resin into a virtual cure model. MD simulations are used to simulate a virtual processing cycle which is experimentally validated using FTIR data as a function of processing time. The volumetric shrinkage, Young’s modulus, shear modulus, yield strength, and Poisson’s ratio are additionally predicted in MD and presented as a function of cure progression, providing reliable data for higher length-scale modeling and ICME-driven composites design.

title: Influence of inoculants on microstructure evolution during fast solidification of aluminium: A computational approach under laser powder bed fusion conditions
abstract: A combined computational strategy is proposed to investigate the influence of inoculants on microstructure evolution during the solidification of aluminium alloys under conditions representative of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). The approach integrates multiphase-field modelling, thermal simulations, and thermodynamic calculations to capture the key physical mechanisms governing inoculation-driven solidification. The study considers typical inoculants including Al 3 Hf, Al 3 Sc, Al 3 Zr, and TiB 2 . Results show that inoculants promote microstructure refinement primarily through heterogeneous nucleation at the particle–matrix interface, with nucleation effects dominating over kinetic contributions. Among the investigated systems, TiB 2 exhibits the strongest refinement capability due to its higher nucleation driving force. Parametric analysis reveals that increasing inoculant particle radius enhances solidification velocity and promotes dendrite refinement, while higher particle number density increases grain refinement by providing more nucleation sites. The influence of LPBF process parameters is examined to identify a processing window for defect-free solidification. A grain-size-dependent constitutive model is incorporated to estimate final grain size, showing good agreement with experimental data and confirming model predictability. Overall, the methodology provides quantitative insight into inoculant-driven solidification and supports the design of high-strength aluminium alloys for additive manufacturing.

title: Cell-free adipose extracellular vesicle glue ameliorates hypertrophic scars by suppressing engrailed-1 expression
abstract: Hypertrophic scars remain a major clinical challenge because of excessive fibroblast activation and aberrant extracellular matrix deposition. Although adipose-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have shown therapeutic promise, their clinical translation is limited by complex cell expansion and purification procedures. Here, we report an injectable, viscoelastic, cell-free adipose-derived extracellular vesicle-rich glue (cfAEG) fabricated through mechanical emulsification and low-speed centrifugation, enabling rapid preparation without in vitro cell culture or ultracentrifugation. Rheological analyses demonstrated that cfAEG possesses favorable injectability and gel-like mechanical properties suitable for local administration. In vitro, cfAEG markedly inhibited the proliferation and myofibroblastic differentiation of human dermal fibroblasts, accompanied by reduced expression of fibrotic markers. In vivo, local injection of cfAEG significantly attenuated hypertrophic scar formation in both the rabbit ear and minipig skin models, outperforming saline controls and showing efficacy comparable to that of triamcinolone acetonide. Mechanistically, cfAEG consistently suppressed the expression of Engrailed-1 (EN1), a key transcriptional regulator of profibrotic fibroblast activation, thereby reducing collagen deposition and α–SMA expression. Collectively, this study presents cfAEG as a clinically feasible, injectable, EV-rich biomaterial that modulates fibroblast fate and scar remodeling by suppressing EN1 expression, highlighting its potential as a cell-free therapeutic strategy for hypertrophic scar management.

title: Hierarchical high-throughput parametric optimization of laser powder bed fusion 316H stainless steel
abstract: As power-generating technologies attempt to increase design temperatures and boost economic efficiency, advanced manufacturing technologies have the potential to modularize component production and decrease capital costs. In this work, a multi-objective, parametric optimization of grade 316H stainless steel (SS-316H) produced via laser powder bed fusion was performed to assess the printability of the higher-carbon system. For a geometrically complex part comprising 11 unique regions, a hierarchical optimization framework using in situ process monitoring and high-throughput X-ray computed tomography (XCT) was applied to assess spatially resolved porosity distributions for 54 unique sets of processing parameters. Within the processing window that produced minimized porosity, destructive characterization of low-porosity samples revealed a grain morphological transformation from refined chevron-shaped grains to epitaxial columnar grains. This transition in grain texture and size resulted in significant mechanical anisotropy, warranting a final parametric filtering threshold linked to the grain structure within the minimized porosity region observed via XCT analysis. The final processing window that minimized low porosity and anisotropy used input parameters in a range of 52–71 J/mm 3 equivalent volumetric energy density. The multi-objective parameter optimization process outlined here is critical for designing materials with simultaneously low defect density and minimized microstructural anisotropy.

title: Redefining grip: Quantitative evaluation of soft grippers
abstract: Soft robotic grippers have attracted increasing attention in recent years owing to their delicate grasping and shape-morphing capabilities. As their designs become more diverse and application-specific, the need for rigorous, comparable performance evaluation grows. Yet, the mechanical performance of soft grippers, including shape-morphing, compliance and load-bearing capabilities, are often assessed through qualitative demonstrations, design-specific tests or isolated metrics, complicating the comparison between different designs and hindering design optimization. Here, we present a quantitative, reproducible and experimentally supported performance assessment framework for soft grippers that combines three complementary groups of metrics: contact interaction, bending stiffness and payload capacity. Contact interaction is characterized through the contact area, mean contact pressure and pressure uniformity, while structural response and load-bearing capability are assessed through directional bending stiffness and pull-off measurements. The framework is applied to a family of metamaterial-based grippers and benchmarked against reference and commercial designs. Numerical and experimental results show that the integrated metamaterial architecture significantly enhances contact behaviour, structural stiffness and payload capacity. More broadly, the proposed framework provides a general basis for benchmarking and architecture-driven optimization of soft robotic grippers.

title: Impurity concentration prediction of Czochralski silicon based on domain-adversarial transfer learning: Physical consistency and cross-furnace adaptability study
abstract: This study presents a domain-adversarial transfer learning (DATL) framework for the precise prediction and control of impurity concentrations in Czochralski silicon, directly addressing the persistent challenges of data scarcity, poor model transferability, and limited robustness in industrial deployment. By integrating simulation and industrial data through adversarial learning, DATL distills domain-invariant physical laws, thereby suppressing negative transfer and ensuring physical consistency. In oxygen content prediction, DATL demonstrates high accuracy (RMSE = 1.099 ppma) with 1147 samples and robust resistance to process noise and drift. Its key advantage is data-efficient commissioning of a new furnace, achieving high accuracy (RMSE = 1.307 ppma) with only 302 samples. Ablation studies identify the domain-adversarial mechanism as the direct source of this adaptability and robustness. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis not only identifies and ranks the governing physical parameters, but also, by analyzing parameter-specific contributions across six industrial scenarios, directly yields a hierarchical control strategy. This effectively bridges interpretable prediction with actionable process control. This work delivers a practical solution for rapid furnace qualification and stabilized yield. More broadly, it establishes a paradigm of distilling domain-invariant physics via adversarial learning, paving the way for managing diverse impurities and advancing adaptive intelligent manufacturing in crystal growth.

title: Composition-engineered copper-doped ZIF-8 nanoplatform for oxidative stress regulation and ferroptosis suppression in osteoarthritis
abstract: Engineering metal–organic framework (MOF)-based materials with tunable composition and biological function offers a promising strategy for regulating pathological oxidative microenvironments. Herein, a composition-engineered copper-doped zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 nanoplatform, Cu@ZIF-8, was designed to modulate oxidative stress-associated lipid peroxidation and chondrocyte ferroptosis for osteoarthritis (OA) therapy. The incorporation of copper into the ZIF-8 framework enabled homogeneous elemental distribution while preserving the crystalline structure and high specific surface area of the MOF platform. In H 2 O 2 - and RSL3-induced chondrocyte injury models, Cu@ZIF-8 reduced intracellular ROS accumulation, alleviated lipid peroxidation, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, restored GPX4/SLC7A11 expression, and maintained extracellular matrix homeostasis. Mechanistic studies suggested that Cu@ZIF-8-mediated ferroptosis suppression was associated, at least in part, with modulation of p38 MAPK/AKT signaling. In a surgically induced rat OA model, intra-articular administration of Cu@ZIF-8 attenuated cartilage degeneration, reduced oxidative and ferroptosis-related damage, and showed no apparent systemic toxicity under the tested conditions. This study establishes a composition-engineered MOF nanoplatform that links copper-doped ZIF-8 design with oxidative stress regulation, ferroptosis suppression, and cartilage protection, providing a materials-design strategy for OA microenvironment modulation.

title: Effect of component ratios on dynamic properties and mesoscale mechanical response of PTFE-Al-W composites
abstract: This study investigates the influence of component ratios on the dynamic properties and mesoscale mechanical response of polytetrafluoroethylene-aluminum-tungsten (PTFE-Al-W) composites through dynamic tests and numerical simulation. Five types of PTFE-Al-W composite specimens with different component ratios (61.5:22.2:16.3,32.7:11.8:55.5,19.4:7.0:73.6, 14.4:5.2:80.4 and 11.3:4.1:84.6.) were prepared. Their dynamic properties were characterized by using split Hopkinson pressure bar tests, and the microstructures of deformed specimens and recovered fragments were examined with a VHX-7000 digital microscope system. Influences of the component ratios on dynamic properties such as the yield stress, the ultimate stress, the ultimate strain, were analyzed. Based on the ANSYS/LS-DYNA platform, the two-dimensional mesoscale simulation models of the PTFE-Al-W composite were established to explore effect of the component ratios and the initial porosity on the mesoscale dynamic behavior. The results show that the component ratios have significant influence on particle distribution, shear bands initiation and growth, failure response of PTFE and force chain effects within the specimens. Consequently, macroscopic dynamic properties such as fracture toughness and stress–strain relationships vary with changes in the component ratios.

title: FluxGAN: Physics-aware generative modeling of coupled microstructure and heat transport in heterogeneous coatings
abstract: Physical response in heterogeneous materials is governed by complex microstructures, yet connecting local morphology to spatially resolved response fields remains challenging. Existing generative approaches typically synthesize structural or physical quantities independently, limiting their ability to support physics-consistent inference and design-space exploration across complex microstructural spaces. Here we introduce FluxGAN, a physics-aware generative framework that learns the joint distribution of microstructure and heat-transport response directly from a multi-channel representation of the data. By embedding structure–field correspondence into the generative process, FluxGAN enables joint synthesis of microstructure and transport fields, conditional generation under localized thermal constraints, and scalable inference without iterative simulation. Using thermal-sprayed niobium coatings as a validation testbed, we demonstrate the generation of coupled microstructures and heat flux fields, conditional inference from partial heat flux inputs, favorable computational scaling relative to finite element solvers, and a proof-of-concept extension to three-dimensional synthesis. The generated structures reproduce key morphological statistics and yield heat flux fields that remain consistent with independent finite element recomputation, showing that the model captures morphology-dependent transport beyond global descriptors such as porosity. More broadly, FluxGAN provides a scalable data-driven workflow for learning coupled microstructure–transport representations and exploring thermally constrained design spaces in heterogeneous materials.

title: Mechanical and electrical behaviour of reactive magnetron sputtered low-Al content epitaxial single-crystalline Ti1-xAlxNy thin films
abstract: High quality epilayers with a minimum of microstructural features can act as test beds to elucidate intrinsic materials properties and improve the understanding of more complex materials. We report on the growth of epitaxial Ti1-xAlxNy thin films with low aluminium content (x = 0-0.4) on MgO (001) substrates using reactive magnetron co-sputtering from a pure Ti and a compound Ti0.75Al0.25 target. The films are fully strained and display a pronounced (001) orientation with low mosaicity and high lateral coherence. The hardness increases up to 29 GPa because of solid-solution hardening and coherency strains associated with early-stage spinodal decomposition, despite an increase in tensile residual stress with Al content. Electrical resistivity increases as the charge carrier concentration decreases with Al content, because enhanced solute scattering and progressive depletion of the metallic Ti-3d-N-2p hybridized conduction band. Al substitution for Ti introduces lattice distortions that increase disorder, reflected by a decreasing Ioffe-Regel parameter (kFl) with Al content. Mobility shows a non-monotonic trend, first decreasing and then increasing with Al content. The changes in electrical resistivity, carrier density, mobility and Ioffe-Regel parameter imply a shift from metallic to increasingly localized electronic transport with increasing Al incorporation.

title: Piezoelectric materials for reconstruction of osteogenic microenvironment coupling: new advances and insights
abstract: Bone tissue relies on the intricate interplay between blood vessels, nerve fibers and immune system, which are all essential for physiological and pathological processes of the skeletal system. When the integrity of the bone is destroyed, various physiological responses are initiated, among which the electric signal is a promising intervention since it has been proved effectively modulate the vascular, neural and immune coupled osteogenesis. Among several electricity supplementary strategies, piezoelectric materials have gained significant traction in recent years. This review first elucidates the biological interplay among the vascular, neural, and immune systems, with a focus on their synergy with electrical signaling in osteogenesis. It then delineates the fundamental properties and design principles of piezoelectric biomaterials. Furthermore, the specific mechanisms by which these systems mediate bone regeneration are comprehensively discussed. By synthesizing recent advances, this review highlights key structure–function relationships to guide the rational design of next-generation piezoelectric platforms for enhanced bone repair.

title: Machine learning-mediated composition-process optimization and high strength-toughness performance achievement of ductile iron
abstract: To overcome the high cost and inefficiency associated with traditional trial-and-error methods in optimizing the strength and toughness of ductile cast iron, this study proposes an intelligent design framework that combines physical metallurgy features with machine learning. By combining composition-process data with atomic-scale elemental attributes, a high-dimensional feature space was constructed. Multi-level feature screening was employed to extract key interactive features influencing ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elongation (EL). High-precision performance prediction models were developed based on a multilayer perceptron, and inverse design of three composition-process schemes for ductile cast iron with balanced high strength and high toughness was achieved by integrating the NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm. Experimental validation confirmed their excellent mechanical properties, the UTS reaches 940 MPa, and the EL reaches 6.3%. SHAP analysis further elucidated the regulatory mechanisms of the key features. As a preliminary exploratory extension, the proposed feature engineering method was preliminarily applied to a 7xxx series aluminum alloy in the T6 temper. The model achieved promising predictive performance, with an R 2 of 0.90 for UTS and 0.87 for EL. These results preliminarily suggest that this feature construction strategy may have the potential to be transferred to other precipitation-hardened alloy systems.

title: Effects and mechanisms of hBN/PEI composite sizing agent on the interfacial properties of carbon fiber reinforced polyetheretherketone composites
abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced poly (ether ether ketone) (CF/PEEK) composites exhibit excellent comprehensive properties, but their performance is often restricted by weak interfacial bonding between chemically inert carbon fibers and the PEEK matrix, which limits efficient load transfer. To overcome this limitation, a hexagonal boron nitride/polyetherimide (hBN/PEI) composite sizing agent was developed to modify the carbon fiber surface and regulate the CF/PEEK interface. The uniformly decorated hBN/PEI sizing layer increased the surface roughness of carbon fibers and improved interfacial adhesion with the PEEK matrix. As a result, the interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) of the sized CF/PEEK composites increased by up to 45.07%. To elucidate the underlying reinforcement mechanism, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to investigate molecular-scale interfacial interactions. The simulation results showed that the hBN/PEI sizing interlayer strengthened the interactions between carbon fibers and PEEK. This enhancement was mainly attributed to intensified mechanical interlocking, which changed the interfacial failure mode and enabled more effective load transfer. This study provides an effective interfacial regulation strategy for CF/PEEK composites and offers theoretical guidance for designing high-performance thermoplastic composites.

title: Characterization and regulation of hygroscopicity and dimensional stability for C/C honeycomb sandwich structures
abstract: The carbon/carbon (C/C) honeycomb sandwich structure is promising for precision optics due to its light weight, high stiffness, and dimensional stability. However, systematic research on its hygroscopic expansion behavior and internal regulation mechanisms is still limited. Here, we precisely characterize the hygroscopic deformation of C/C composites using a self-developed testing system, and investigate water vapor adsorption via dynamic vapor sorption (DVS). The results reveal that the linear hygroscopic strain of C/C composites is lower than 0.733 ppm, and its relative mass change is less than 3.2 × 10 −4 . Water adsorption follows a reversible physical process governed by van der Waals forces. For the honeycomb sandwich structure, the face sheet thickness modulates constraint reactions by altering structural stiffness. The adhesive film thickness is positively correlated with hygroscopic deformation, while the adhesive type plays a decisive role: organic adhesive films, rich in polar functional groups, induce ∼ 3 μm expansion; conversely, a self-developed SiBCN-based inorganic adhesive film with a rigid covalent network achieves near-zero deformation.

title: Multiscale design and uncertainty analysis of assembly interface oriented to uniform stress assembly
abstract: Assembly serves as the final safeguard in manufacturing, determining the performance of complex precision electromechanical equipment. Uniform stress assembly represents a key frontier, with assembly interface design emerging as a promising technique for achieving it. However, current interface designs ignore the multiscale features and uncertainties inherent to interface shape. This study attempts to perform multiscale interface shape design oriented to uniform stress assembly, along with analysis of shape uncertainty effects. The general similarity law between the interface shape and stress distribution is revealed, based on which a heuristic method for multiscale interface shape design is proposed. Its effectiveness is verified through elastic-to-elastic assembled structure and pipe flange bolted structure. Influence of roughness on stress distribution is investigated and interface shape design is performed under varying rough conditions. The effect of uncertainty in multiscale interface shape on stress distribution uniformity are further quantitatively analyzed.

title: Photocrosslinked konjac glucomannan/silk fibroin/glycyrrhizic acid hydrogel microneedles with antimicrobial peptides for diabetic wound healing
abstract: Diabetic wound healing is a challenging clinical problem. Factors such as poor blood supply, repeated inflammatory stimulation, and susceptibility to infection can slow down or even prevent wound healing. A hydrogel microneedle (KKSG) for wound healing of diabetic skin in mice was prepared by compounding methacrylic anhydride (MA) modified konjac glucomannan (KGMMA), cationic antimicrobial polypeptide (KLR), glycidyl methacrylate (GMA) modified silk fibroin (SFGMA) and oxidized glycyrrhizic acid (AGA). Importantly, KKSG hydrogel microneedles exhibit excellent macrophage M2 polarization and angiogenesis both in vivo and in vitro . In addition, KKSG hydrogel microneedles exhibit excellent biosafety and favorable antibacterial ability. In animal experiments, KKSG hydrogel microneedles exhibit excellent wound healing effects. In conclusion, KKSG hydrogel microneedles are a good wound dressing for diabetes and are expected to provide a new method for wound repair in diabetes.

title: Processing of SA508 Grade 3 steel powders by laser direct energy deposition and hot isostatic pressing
abstract: This study investigated the influence of powder atomization atmosphere on the microstructure and mechanical properties of SA508 Grade 3 steel processed by Laser-Directed Energy Deposition (L-DED) and subsequent Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP). Powders atomized in argon and nitrogen atmospheres were deposited using laser powers of 1000 W and 1250 W and subjected to a two-step HIP cycle consisting of austenitization and tempering. Mechanical properties were evaluated by instrumented Charpy impact testing, three-point bending, and microhardness measurements, while microstructural characterization was performed using optical microscopy, SEM, EBSD, and EDS. HIP significantly reduced porosity in all specimens; however, the residual pore content strongly depended on the atomization atmosphere. Nitrogen-atomized powder produced approximately one order of magnitude lower residual porosity and a finer pore-size distribution than argon-atomized powder. Consequently, the highest impact toughness (191 ± 7 J), flexural strength, and microhardness (241–249 HV0.1) were achieved in nitrogen-based specimens. EBSD analysis revealed a homogeneous bainitic microstructure after HIP treatment. The results demonstrate that nitrogen atomization improves densification and mechanical performance of L-DED + HIP processed SA508 steel, making it a promising feedstock route for safety–critical nuclear applications.

title: Lightweight magnesium-based vapor–liquid two-phase heat transfer device with phytic acid decoration
abstract: Aluminum-based phase-change heat transfer devices offer lightweight thermal management, but further weight reduction requires alternatives. Magnesium has been proposed, yet its chemical reactivity has hindered practical implementation. Here, we propose a surface modification strategy utilizing phytic acid to generate a chelating protective coating on magnesium surfaces. This coating suppresses adverse reactions between the packaging material and working medium while introducing hydrophilic groups and a micro-crack structure, with Mg-O-P coordination bonding confirmed by FTIR. Under boiling conditions, the 3 wt% PA coating thickness stabilizes at ∼3.65 μm after 48 h. A comparable trend under static immersion indicates that dissolution of excess physisorbed PA, rather than hydrodynamic stress, drives the thinning. Capillary rise height in ethanol increases from 57 mm to 75 mm after 3 wt% PA modification. The 3.04 g device achieves a maximum effective thermal conductivity of 1367 ± 65 W/(m·K) and thermal resistance of 3.18 ± 0.15 K/W, with no degradation over 100 cycles. Performance-per-mass comparison against literature devices confirms that the Mg device occupies a unique lightweight position among two-phase heat transfer systems. These results establish PA-modified magnesium as a promising lightweight packaging material for phase-change thermal management, particularly in aerospace applications.

title: Linking novel processing, thermo-mechanical response and high-temperature oxidation in refractory high-entropy alloy via a multiscale computational-experimental approach
abstract: A novel synthesis route was studied to prepare aluminium-containing refractory high-entropy alloys. The approach involves co-reduction of constituent refractory metal oxides using aluminium in predetermined proportions. For demonstration, a Ta 19.3 Mo 23.4 Nb 20.1 Cr 16.7 Al 20.4 alloy (molar percentages) was designed using FactSage thermochemical databases based on heat and mass balance calculations. The as-reduced material was sequentially processed by arc-melting, annealing and deformation at 1250 °C and 1400 °C. The alloy comprised of two body-centred cubic phases: a Mo-rich phase and a Cr(Al,Nb)-based solid solution with metastable C14-Laves phase. The elastic moduli of these two phases were predicted using density functional theory simulations coupled with finite element modelling and experimentally correlated to nanoindentation results. Hot deformation produced synchronous grain refinement in both derived ordered B2 phases. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that these phases accommodated deformation through dislocation cells and antiphase boundaries, promoting dynamic recrystallisation, whereas the C14-Laves grains exhibited dense parallel stacking faults transitioning to the C15-Laves phase. Oxidation at 850 °C for 50 h showed marginal weight-gain vis-à-vis a similar composition produced by the arc-melting route, forming protective Al 2 O 3 and NbCrO 4 oxide layers. This work establishes a cost-effective and scalable process for this class of materials offering microstructures and properties comparable to conventionally adopted techniques.

title: Internal oxidation as a pathway to fabrication of ODS-like 316LY stainless steel by laser powder directed energy deposition
abstract: Oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) stainless steels offer high-temperature strength but typically require costly mechanical alloying. However, direct additive manufacturing routes for forming Y-containing oxide particles without ex situ oxide addition remain insufficiently established. This study evaluates internal oxidation of pre-alloyed Y during laser powder directed energy deposition of 316L as a route to ODS-like 316LY. Gas-atomized 316L + 0.14 wt% Y powder was deposited to >99% relative density at 600–700 W and 600 mm min −1 and aged at 1000 °C for 100 h. Electron backscatter diffraction, scanning transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, hardness testing, and room-temperature tensile testing compared the as-printed and aged conditions. The as-printed alloy contained a cellular austenitic matrix and amorphous Y–Si–Mn–O-rich oxide particles averaging 118 ± 25 nm. Aging produced recovery-dominated microstructural evolution with negligible recrystallization and promoted oxide coarsening and nanocrystallization toward Y 2 O 3 -rich particles averaging 152 ± 15 nm. Ultimate tensile strength decreased from 760–774 to 592–623 MPa, while elongation increased from 22–36% to 42–67%. First-order calculations estimated dispersion-hardening contributions of only 14.7 and 11.9 MPa before and after aging, respectively. These results demonstrate a proof-of-concept route for ODS-like 316LY while highlighting oxide refinement and quantitative oxygen-potential control as priorities.

title: Design guidelines for multi-layer additively manufactured electronics via in-situ embedding of isotropic conductive adhesive in FFF printed parts
abstract: The in-situ embedding of isotropic conductive adhesive (ICA) in fused filament fabrication (FFF) represents a novel single-step approach to additively manufactured electronics (AME), utilizing the heat of the molten thermoplastic to cure the ICA and develop its electrical conductivity. This study presents the first systematic derivation of design guidelines through a series of experiments on the effect of the distance between the conductor path and heated bed, external and vertical interconnection via press-fitting pin headers, and the printability of curves and corners. A minimum distance of 10 mm to a 90 °C heated bed is recommended to ensure homogeneous conductor path cross-sections and high electrical conductivity. Electrical contacts can be reliably achieved by pre-drilling 0.5 mm diameter holes in the conductor path and press-fitting a pin header, yielding a contact resistance of 68.2 mΩ (± 17.7 mΩ). Corner angles up to 90° and curve radii as small as 1 mm can be reliably printed without measurable effects on the conductor path geometry and electrical conductivity. To validate the design guidelines, two multi-layer planar inductor coils were fabricated, demonstrating contactless energy transfer and compatibility for near-field communication (NFC) applications.

title: Generative inverse design of cold metals for low-power electronics
abstract: Cold metals possess an intrinsic energy gap located close to the Fermi level, which enables cold-carrier injection for steep-slope transistors and is therefore promising for low-power electronics. High-throughput screening has revealed 252 three-dimensional (3D) cold metals in the Materials Project database, but database searches are inherently limited to known compounds. Here we present an inverse-design workflow that generates 3D cold metals using MatterGPT, a conditional autoregressive Transformer trained on SLICES, an invertible and symmetry-invariant crystal representation. We curate a training set of 26,309 metallic structures labeled with energy above hull and a unified band-edge distance descriptor that merges p-type and n-type features to address severe label imbalance. Property-conditioned generation targeting thermodynamic stability and 50–500 meV band-edge distances produces 148,506 unique candidates; 92.1 % are reconstructed into 3D structures and down-selected by symmetry, uniqueness and novelty filters, followed by high-throughput DFT validation. We identify 257 cold metals absent from the Materials Project database, all within the targeted 50–500 meV window. First-principles phonon, electronic-structure, and work-function calculations for representative candidates confirm dynamical stability and contact-relevant work functions. Our results demonstrate that SLICES-enabled generative transformers can expand the chemical space of cold metals beyond high-throughput screening, providing a route to low-power electronic materials discovery.

title: Interdiffusion-suppressing glassy medium-entropy alloy for stable skutterudite thermoelectric single legs
abstract: Phase diagram engineering, coupled with the medium-entropy alloy (MEA) concept, identifies a β-Ti single-phase region in the quaternary Ti–Al–Ni–Cr system, enabling rational diffusion-barrier design for CoSb3 thermoelectric single legs. Compared with conventional crystalline Ni films, a glassy single-phase MEA film (Ti70Al15N10Cr5) exhibits suppressed interdiffusion with CoSb3, owing to restricted diffusion pathways associated with its quasi-amorphous structure. This effectively prevents the formation of detrimental intermetallic compounds commonly observed at Ni/CoSb3 interfaces. Device-level measurements over ΔT = 50–350 K show comparable peak conversion efficiency but markedly improved cycle-to-cycle stability for MEA-coated single legs, consistent with reduced interfacial resistance and minimized parasitic losses. Interfacial characterization by characterized by Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and synchrotron-based X-ray Fluorescence (XRF), and compositional line profiling confirms a chemically abrupt and well-preserved Cu/solder/MEA/CoSb3 architecture, with no detectable intermetallic formation even after exposure to a hot-side temperature of 623 K. These results demonstrate that the glassy MEA thin film simultaneously meets the requirements for both contact compatibility and diffusion-barrier functionality by maintaining a single-phase structure while suppressing fast grain-boundary diffusion, thereby stabilizing thermoelectric interfaces under operating conditions.

title: Pore architecture as a design parameter to tune mechanical compatibility and bone repair in LPBF-fabricated porous tantalum scaffolds
abstract: Reconstruction of critical-sized defects in load-bearing metaphyseal bone requires implants that combine mechanical compatibility with durable bone repair. Although additive manufacturing enables programmable porous architectures, the role of pore architecture as an independent design variable, beyond porosity and pore size, remains insufficiently defined for porous tantalum (Ta). Here, three LPBF-fabricated porous Ta scaffolds with distinct pore architectures (cubic, Ta C; rhombic dodecahedral, Ta R; and stochastic trabecular, Ta T) were compared with a trabecular Ti-6Al-4V scaffold (Ti). With porosity and strut diameter matched, we systematically evaluated compressive mechanics, in vitro cell responses and in vivo bone repair. Porous Ta exhibited higher ductility and more reliable post-yield deformation than Ti, while Ta T and Ta R achieved elastic moduli closer to the cancellous bone range. In vitro, Ta T and Ta C promoted cell adhesion and proliferation, whereas Ta T and Ta R enhanced early osteogenic differentiation. In vivo, Ta T and Ta R promoted bone ingrowth, with Ta T showing the highest osseointegration while maintaining a cancellous-bone-like modulus (∼2.6 GPa). These findings indicate that pore architecture can be used to tune the trade-off between stiffness matching and bone integration in LPBF porous Ta scaffolds for load-bearing applications.

title: Additive manufacturing of chaos-generated cellular architectures with XCT-based validation
abstract: This study presents a deterministic framework for generating cellular architectures with non-periodic intra-domain morphology derived from chaotic dynamical systems for additive manufacturing. Chaotic trajectories were used as geometric templates to design intricate, lightweight, and reproducible cellular structures. Four chaotic attractors, Lorenz, Thomas, Aizawa, and Sprott A, were modeled, fabricated by vat photopolymerization using a liquid–crystal-display (VPP-LCD)-based system, and validated via X-ray computed tomography (XCT). The geometric comparison between the CAD models and the fabricated specimens indicated overall agreement between the nominal and reconstructed geometries. Median surface deviations ranged from 0.05 mm to 0.20 mm, with RMSE values between 0.10 mm and 0.30 mm. The 95th percentile Hausdorff distance remained below 0.60 mm, indicating limited local deviations for most of the reconstructed surface. A systematic positive bias was observed, with volume increases of 8% to 19% relative to the nominal designs. Boundary fidelity was high (PIB ≈ 0.99), while volume fidelity (PIV ≈ 0.75–0.93) reflected internal material variations. The directional compression FEA comparison indicated that the chaos-generated architectures can produce competitive stiffness under comparable solid fraction conditions; the Lorenz geometry attained a mean normalized stiffness of 0.1479, almost equivalent to the simple-cubic lattice of 0.1613. Overall, the study demonstrates that chaos trajectories can be converted into manufacturable cellular architectures with quantifiable and repeatable local complexity and competitive directional stiffness.

title: A volume-conservation‑based approximate method for determining densification strain of high‑porosity electrodeposited copper foam
abstract: Densification strain is critical for high-porosity copper foam used as a three-dimensional current collector in lithium metal batteries, as it governs volume expansion buffering. However, the applicability of evaluation methods to electrodeposited copper foam with 98% porosity and 20 PPI remains unclear. Here, we perform quasi-static compression tests at different loading rates (1–16 mm/min) and compare four evaluation methods: the empirical method, tangent method, energy method and ISO 13314 standard method. The results show that the copper foam exhibits weak positive strain-rate sensitivity, but the densification strain varies significantly among methods: 97.2% (empirical), 82.9%–83.6% (tangent), 58.6%–60.1% (energy) and 49.2%–52.7% (standard). Based on the principle of volume conservation, we propose an approximate method that takes the initial porosity (98%) as the densification strain. SEM and X-CT observations confirm that at 98% strain the struts exhibit multiple cracks and local fractures without overall failure, validating the proposed method. Using this approximate method, the densification strength and energy absorption capacity were measured as 49.30 ± 4.20 MPa and 1.86 ± 0.03 MJ/m 3 , values that are higher than previous values. This study reveals the underestimated plasticity and energy absorption potential of high-porosity copper foam and provides a physically grounded approximate method for evaluating densification strain in metal foams.

title: Ultrastructure, crystallography and growth of biomineral structures in the goose barnacle Pollicipes pollicipes (Pollicipedidae, Pollicipedomorpha)
abstract: Barnacles (Cirripedia) are crustaceans that secrete calcitic skeletal elements that grow by accretion and are not molted, yet their biomineral structures remain poorly known, especially in pedunculate forms. This study examines the ultrastructure, crystallography, and growth of capitular plates and peduncular scales in the Atlantic goose barnacle Pollicipes pollicipes. Using a combination of optical, electron, and atomic force microscopy, together with electron backscatter diffraction, we reveal clear differences between these two calcified elements. Capitular plates consist of microgranular calcite arranged in dendritic crystallographic domains and show weak fiber textures, with the c-axis oriented at a high angle to the growth surface, as in balanomorph barnacles. In contrast, peduncular scales are oligo- to polycrystalline, with bimodal grain sizes and large domains that accommodate significant intragranular lattice rotation during growth. In both structures, crystallographic axes progressively rotate to maintain a high angle between the calcite c-axis and the growth surface. This process is enabled by thin organic interfaces acting as low-angle boundaries that permit gradual lattice reorientation. These findings indicate that P. pollicipes forms two distinct biomineral architectures largely governed by physicochemical processes, with biological control mainly exerted through organic matrices that influence crystal orientation during growth.

title: Microstructural evolution and mechanical behavior of cold-drawn high-carbon bainitic steel wire
abstract: This study systematically investigates the effects of microstructure on the mechanical properties of cold-drawn high-carbon steel wire, focusing on the comparison between pearlite and bainite. Results indicate that bainitic wire quenched at 335–375 °C exhibits higher initial strength compared to traditional pearlitic wire. As the salt-bath austempering temperature decreases, the microstructure transforms from upper bainite to lower bainite, accompanied by brittle martensite formation, increasing tensile strength but reducing plasticity. During multipass cold drawing, the strengthening coefficient of bainitic wire is lower than that of pearlitic wire, with upper bainite showing the weakest coefficient. The repeated bending performance of bainitic wire depends on the austempering temperature; fine lower bainite formed at 360 °C demonstrates the optimal bending performance, surpassing pearlitic wire by approximately 15 % . However, the presence of brittle martensite and the weak < 110 > fiber texture formed during cold drawing result in inferior torsion performance compared with pearlitic wire. Furthermore, high-speed wear-test results show that bainitic wire exhibits better resistance to wear than pearlitic wire. This is attributed to the finer lath substructure of bainite and its tendency to form a tough transformed layer during high-speed wear. This study provides new insights into the microstructural design of bending-resistant and wear-resistant steel wires.

title: Microstructure and creep behavior of antimony containing high silver solder alloy Sn-3.9Ag-0.6Cu-3.0Sb
abstract: Antimony containing Sn-3.9Ag-0.6Cu-3.0Sb (SAC 396 + ) is a high reliability solder alloy but its microstructure and creep behavior is not sufficiently investigated yet. In this paper the correlation between microstructure, using SEM, TEM, and XRD, and compression creep properties was investigated. Furthermore, a comparison in creep performance between SAC 396 + and Sn-3.8Ag-0.7Cu (SAC 387) was drawn, and the long-term microstructure evolution until 1500 h at 125 °C was compared. For SAC 396+, microstructure investigations of pre-aged (24 h at 125 °C) bulk samples revealed that Sb is mainly dissolved in β-Sn (Sb 2 Sn 23 , tetragonal, I41/amd), whereas some fine SbSn precipitates (Sb 0.49 Sn 0.51 , rhombohedral, R-3 m) were found in β-Sn. Compression creep tests were performed at temperatures between 35 °C and 125 °C with stresses between 7.5 MPa and 32.5 MPa. Stress exponents were in the range of 7.4 to 7.5 at 100 °C or below, and 4.8 at 125 °C and activation energies were in the range between 84.7 kJ/mol and 99.6 kJ/mol, indicating dislocation creep, controlled by pipe diffusion or by lattice diffusion. Overall, Sb hardened SAC 396 + showed better creep performance at all tested temperatures, as well as after isothermal ageing at 125 °C for 24 h, 500 h, or 1500 h.

title: Feasibility-guided inverse design of pressure-tunable interlocking structures using random forest
abstract: Structures with tunable mechanical properties enable adaptive load bearing and energy absorption, yet their inverse design remains challenging because structural parameters, confinement conditions, and mechanical responses are coupled through nonlinear and many-to-one relationships. These difficulties are amplified in small-data settings, where deep generative models are hard to train and often lack physical interpretability. Here, we propose a random-forest-guided inverse-design framework for tunable-stiffness interlocking structures under prescribed confinement conditions. A calibrated RF forward model identifies feasible design regions for a target stiffness band and generates diverse candidate structures through likelihood-guided sampling, avoiding direct learning of a nonunique response-to-design mapping. Using fewer than 250 finite-element-generated geometry–pressure samples, the framework demonstrates improved sample efficiency, feasible-design ranking, and design-space coverage compared with genetic algorithms and covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategies. PDP, SHAP, and interaction analyses reveal how pressure and geometry jointly control stiffness accessibility and regime transitions. Additional finite element analyses show that increasing confinement activates inter-particle contacts, promotes particle rearrangement, enhances frictional dissipation, and forms connected force-transmission pathways, thereby increasing stiffness, peak force, and energy absorption. The calcaneal off-loading example further demonstrates the framework’s potential for application-oriented design of adaptive load-bearing and energy-absorbing systems.

title: Regenerative repair of intervertebral disc degeneration: a synergistic strategy of cells and biomaterials
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is the main pathological basis of chronic low back pain (LBP). Its complex pathological mechanisms make it difficult for single therapies to simultaneously restore the structure and function of the intervertebral disc (IVD). Simple cell injection therapy faces problems such as low cell survival rate and poor tissue integration. Therefore, synergistic therapies combining cells and biomaterials provide a new cell therapy strategy for the regeneration and repair of IVDD. This article aims to review synergistic regeneration and repair strategies based on cells and biomaterials, and reviews and analyzes the biomaterials for cell delivery. Next-generation functionalized biomaterials possess multifunctional biocomposite properties such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and responsive properties. This article also introduces the types and applications of different cell sources and strategies to enhance therapeutic effects, such as gene modification, nanozymes, and the construction of three-dimensional (3D) cell spheres and organoids. Finally, the theoretical basis and possibilities for realizing personalized medicine are discussed in conjunction with 3D printing technology. Through deep synergy and integration of cells, tissue engineering, and the microenvironment, the regenerative microenvironment of IVD can be reshaped, providing a solution with potential for clinical translational applications in the treatment of IVDD.

title: Scaling relationships governing the thermomechanical response of rotating detonation engine combustor liners
abstract: The recent maturation of rotating detonation engine combustion science and engineering has positioned this technology to disrupt the space economy, among other industries. Rotating detonation engines offer enhanced performance and cost reductions through their more compact and higher-efficiency designs compared to traditional deflagration-based engines. While it is known that sustaining detonation waves within the annular combustor of a rotating detonation engine imparts extreme cyclic thermal and pressure loadings, the severity of these loadings and their couplings for the combustor wall has not previously been established. Here, scaling relationships are provided for the thermal and pressure stresses when the annular combustor is modeled as a semi-infinite solid (sub-structural scale) and 2D ring in plane strain (structural scale) subjected to simultaneous harmonic gas temperature and pressure oscillations. Dimensionless groups are identified that govern contributions from inertial and steady-periodic solutions. Key conclusions are that thermal expansion induced inertial effects from passing detonations are always negligible and significant stress amplifications due to resonance are found over a large range of detonation velocities and liner thicknesses for all metallic materials. The scaling relations developed may be used to guide material selection, combustor sizing, material damping, and detonation frequency targets in order to promote liner durability.

title: Reprogrammable ori-kirigami metamaterial with self-locking stacked polyhedral units
abstract: Origami metamaterials typically suffer from an inherent trade-off between load-bearing capacity and shape reconfigurability. To address this issue, we propose a synthesis approach for constructing stacked ori-kirigami metamaterials incorporating self-locking polyhedral units with independent concave-convex transformation capabilities. The 2 × 2 prototypes composed of oblique polyhedral units (O4-4) demonstrate reprogrammable behavior, with compressive strength tunable from 6 kPa to 10.8 kPa. Quasi-static compressive tests of stacked metamaterials reveal that 4–4 models exhibit the maximum SEA, while 4–2 models achieve superior load-to-weight ratios. Compared with conventional O4-4 models, oblique polyhedral units with holes (OH4-4) achieve an 11.63 % increase in SEA and a 16.57 % enhancement in load-to-weight ratio. Geometric gradient designs with tunable oblique angles and unit sizes further tailor the compressive response, enabling SEA to vary from 0.36 to 0.58 J/g and load-to-weight ratios from 11,600 to 20,500. Additionally, modifying lateral connections through geometric defects strengthens the structural load-carrying capability, increasing the load-to-weight ratio by 24.63 % and crush force efficiency (CFE) by 26.86 % . The proposed design methodology is extendable to N × N arrays with diverse polyhedral units, showing potential applications in reusable protective packaging, lightweight impact attenuators, deployable buffering components, and temporary protective structures.

title: Defect dependent dynamic nanoindentation hardness of copper up to 25000s−1
abstract: Metals exhibit an upturn in strength at strain rates of approximately 1 000 s −1 – 3 000 s −1 , governed by rapid dislocation multiplication, interactions and storage. This phenomenon is strongly influenced by the initial dislocation density before testing. However, the role of immobile dislocations arranged in low-angle grain boundaries (LAGBs) on deformation under such extreme conditions remains unexplored, despite their ubiquity in engineering materials. Here, we employ high strain rate nanoindentation targeted at an LAGB with tilt and twist components in copper crystals with different dislocation densities. We demonstrate that Taylor hardening remains valid over a wide range of strain rates. It was found that the influence of LAGBs on mechanical properties is within the scatter of the measurements. However, slip traces of indents close to the LAGB suggest that the LAGB acts as a barrier to dislocations. Molecular dynamics simulations further confirm these findings. The measured activation volume and low strain rate re-indentation onto indents performed at different higher strain rates give insights into the deformation mechanism. This work provides new insight into the interplay between microstructure and high strain rate deformation.

title: The role and mechanism of magnetic hydrogels in bone diseases
abstract: Magnetic hydrogels are emerging as intelligent biomaterials that integrate superparamagnetic nanoparticles into hydrogel networks. Under external magnetic fields, they enable remotely controlled targeted delivery, mechanical stimulation, and thermal regulation, offering a strategy for treating bone diseases. This review outlines the construction of magnetic hydrogels and their regulatory mechanisms. At the cellular level, magnetic hydrogels have been associated with several study–specific signaling responses that regulate osteogenic differentiation, macrophage polarization, stem–cell fate, and chondrocyte metabolism. The strength of evidence supporting these mechanisms varies: some pathways are supported by pathway specific molecular assays or pharmacological perturbation, whereas others remain mechanistic hypotheses inferred from established biological knowledge. Simultaneously, these hydrogels guide the differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells and chondrocytes by adjusting the physicochemical microenvironment. In disease models, magnetic hydrogels show integrated therapeutic potential across osteoarthritis, osteosarcoma, fractures, and bone defects, including inflammation modulation, combination tumor therapy, sequential drug release, and defect repair. We further discuss the remaining challenges for clinical translation, including long–term biosafety, magnetic field standardization, manufacturing reproducibility, and structure–property–performance relationships.

title: Intrinsic crystallographic tuning: origin of superior plasticity in an oxygen-doped near-α titanium alloy
abstract: This study investigates an as-cast oxygen-doped near-α titanium alloy, developed via a kinetics-driven materials design strategy, that successfully overcomes the long-standing strength-ductility trade-off. Compared with the base alloy, the doped variant achieves a simultaneous enhancement in ultimate tensile strength (1178 MPa) and elongation (6.4%). Microstructurally, Oxygen doping induced the formation of a basketweave structure with significant hard-oriented microgeometry, where preferentially grown α-variants align their c-axes parallel to the tensile direction. The superior ductility is attributed to a dual-mechanism synergy. Intrinsically, inferred oxygen occupancy in tetrahedral sites triggers anomalous a-axis expansion and a significantly reduced c/a ratio , as macroscopically corroborated by systematic peak shifts and lattice parameter calculations in X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. This lattice distortion fundamentally lowers the Peierls barrier, activating pyramidal <c+a> wavy slip. Extrinsically, The dislocation slip propagation behavior observed in adjacent α phases indicates that the addition of oxygen provides the interface with extremely high geometric compatibility(m'>0.7). This favorable interface matching can effectively alleviate local stress concentration and delay premature fracture, offering a novel pathway for designing high-performance titanium alloys.

title: Bioinspired hierarchical-gradient designs for tendon-to-bone interfaces: Continuous and discontinuous fatigue behavior
abstract: Mimicking the natural tendon-to-bone interface poses a significant challenge due to its complex hierarchical and transitional properties. In this study, novel bioinspired hierarchical-gradient mechanical metastructures were designed and fabricated using 3D printing to address these challenges. By rationally integrating intermediate hybrid unit cells, the designs successfully reproduce a transition in Poisson’s ratio, spanning from negative values in tendon to positive values in bone. Experimental and computational analyses demonstrate that the optimal architecture significantly enhances static mechanical properties. Specifically, it exhibited a 106.1 % increase in Young’s modulus and a 28.4 % improvement in ultimate stress compared to the conventional design. These enhancements are primarily driven by the mitigation of localized stress concentrations, yielding a strain-distribution that more closely resembles the mechanical transition of the native tendon-to-bone interface. Under continuous fatigue loading, the bioinspired regulation of local auxeticity extended the fatigue life by 132.9 %. Furthermore, discontinuous fatigue assessments revealed critical insights into the failure mechanisms of viscoelastic metastructures. While short resting intervals had minimal impact on the number of cycles to failure, prolonged intervals significantly accelerated mechanical degradation. Ultimately, this study establishes a bioinspired mechanical design framework for developing mechanically resilient tendon-to-bone metastructures, providing a basis for future scaffold development and orthopedic applications.

title: Crack-guided self-assembly of polydopamine nanoparticles into macroscopic fibrous structures
abstract: Polydopamine is a bioinspired polymer with broad applicability. However, its ability to form ordered macroscopic structures through interfacial processes remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate a crack-guided interfacial self-assembly mechanism that enables the formation of centimeter-scale fibrous structures from polydopamine nanoparticles doped with chiral 1,2-diaminocyclohexane (DACH), without the use of external templates.
