We show that the dopamine-to-DACH ratio governs nanoparticle size and dispersity, which in turn controls evaporation-driven assembly and macroscopic fiber formation on polymeric surfaces. The process is driven by interfacial interactions and crack propagation, resulting in highly ordered fibrous architectures composed of densely packed nanoparticles. The resulting fibers exhibit mechanical properties comparable to natural hair, as revealed by micro-Brillouin spectroscopy, and display pronounced humidity-responsive swelling behavior. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for interfacial assembly in catechol-based colloidal systems and provide a route toward the design of bioinspired fibrous materials with tunable structural and functional properties.

title: Pilot-scale production of monodisperse helical silica nanorods: As-synthesized structure and application to rubber compounds
abstract: This work discloses a pilot-scale synthesis process allowing the growth of monodispersed silica (SiO 2 ) nanorods, using cost effective and nontoxic reactants only. Water is here the only solvent used, with cetyltrimethylammonium chloride (CTACl) micelles acting as soft templates to control the anisotropic growth of SiO 2 . The abundant, inexpensive, and non-toxic sodium metasilicate precursor is used as a silicon source, allowing the consideration of this synthesis process for the industrial preparation of monodisperse SiO 2 nanorods. We demonstrate the process’ versatility in a pre-industrial 50 L large-scale reactor and display its robustness to repeatedly synthesise anisotropic SiO 2 nanorods with controlled lengths and widths. The added value of those anisotropic SiO 2 structures has been studied in model rubber compounds. We show that SiO 2 nanorods led to a reduction of filler agglomeration, resulting in an increase of the tan δ magnitude, a longer elongation at break and a decrease of the elastic modulus.

title: Spatiotemporal fusion sub-aperture polishing paradigm enables collaborative manufacturing of optical element in spatial-frequency domain errors
abstract: Sub-aperture polishing is widely used to control spatial-domain errors in optical components. However, the spatial invariance of the tool influence function (TIF) restricts process flexibility, while the conventional convolution-based material removal mechanism tends to introduce mid-spatial-frequency (MSF) errors, resulting in a trade-off between figure correction and frequency-domain error suppression. To achieve coordinated control of spatial- and frequency-domain errors, this study proposes a spatiotemporal fusion sub-aperture polishing method. By simultaneously optimizing dwell time and the spatial distribution of the TIF, the proposed method enables collaborative error control across domains. Theoretical analysis reveals the mechanism by which spatiotemporal fusion polishing improves spatial-frequency errors. Based on linear formulations and an adaptive genetic algorithm, solution algorithms are developed to determine the spatiotemporal distribution of the TIF. B-spline curves are introduced to reduce the optimization dimensionality of TIF spatial distribution, and a multi-objective Pareto strategy is adopted to balance spatial- and frequency-domain objectives. A complete framework integrating the polishing system, TIF spatiotemporal distribution model, and collaborative optimization strategy is established. Experiments on a controllable spiral magnetorheological finishing system verify that the proposed method significantly improves coordinated error control and manufacturing accuracy compared with conventional sub-aperture polishing.

title: Metal-Phenolic Nanoplatform Tailored to the Metabolic Dependence of Prostate Cancer to Amplify Cuproptosis and Apoptosis
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) cells, characterized by sustained high mitochondrial respiratory activity following malignant transformation, possess intrinsic sensitivity to cuproptosis, rendering them suitable candidates for cuproptosis-induced therapies. By exploiting this metabolic vulnerability, tumor microenvironment-responsive copper-based metal-phenolic networks (Cu-Phl MPNs) were developed via self-assembly of Cu2+ and phloretin to synergistically induce of apoptosis and cuproptosis in respiration-active PCa cells. Following cellular internalization, Cu-Phl MPNs underwent glutathione (GSH) responsive degradation, co-releasing Cu+ and Phl. The liberated Phl specifically interrupted GLUT1-mediated intracellular glucose supply, suppressing ATP and NADPH synthesis. ATP depletion downregulated the copper exporter ATP7A and curbed copper efflux, while impaired NADPH production compromised GSH regeneration and diminished copper chelation, collectively facilitating intracellular Cu+ accumulation. The accumulated Cu+ drove a Fenton-like reaction to generate reactive oxygen species, which disrupted redox homeostasis and triggered mitochondrial apoptosis. Meanwhile, cuproptosis could be efficiently activated under the combination of excess Cu+ and inherent sensitivity. Both in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that Cu-Phl MPNs exerted potent and selective antitumor efficacy against respiration-active LNCaP cells while exhibiting minimal toxicity toward glycolysis-dependent PC3 cells, with favorable biosafety profiles. This work presents a metabolism-directed nanoplatform that aligns therapeutic mechanisms with tumor intrinsic features for precision PCa therapy.

title: L-glutamine-enabled injectable hydrogel for rapid vaginal wound repair
abstract: Vaginoplasty serves as a primary therapeutic intervention for restoring anatomical and functional integrity of the lower female reproductive tract. However, its clinical application is often compromised by protracted postoperative recovery requiring prolonged mold placement, leading to obvious patient discomfort and inconvenience. Herein, we report a drug-free injectable hydrogel for vaginal wound repair using L-glutamine (L-Gln) as a central functional component. In this system, L-Gln facilitates the free-radical polymerization of hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA), participates in hydrogen-bond-mediated network formation, and provides bioactivity relevant to tissue repair. Furthermore, sodium alginate (SA) is incorporated to optimize rheological properties, while bioactive magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) are introduced to construct a hybrid-crosslinked network integrating coordinative and hydrogen bonds, yielding the hydrogel PHSG-Mg 2+ . Through this design, the hydrogel achieves injectability, mechanical robustness, anti-swelling capacity, and favorable biocompatibility in both in vitro and in vivo settings. Biological studies further indicate that the sustained release of L-Gln, together with Mg 2+ , is associated with oxidative-stress alleviation and improved tissue regeneration. Benefiting from these integrated structural and biological advantages, the PHSG-Mg 2+ hydrogel significantly accelerates wound closure, enhances re-epithelialization, promotes collagen deposition, and stimulates angiogenesis in a standardized rat vaginal defect model. Overall, this work establishes an L-Gln-centered strategy for constructing multifunctional injectable hydrogels for vaginal wound healing after reconstruction.

title: Origami-inspired metamaterial absorber using 3D-printed shape memory hinges for thermo-mechanical frequency switching
abstract: Mechanical tuning offers a promising route for modulating electromagnetic responses without reliance on active electronic components. Specifically, this approach facilitates the reconfiguration of metamaterial absorbers (MMAs), in which the absorption frequency is tuned by controlling individual unit cells. However, mechanically reconfigurable MMAs are difficult to realise without the integration of additional actuators or metallic plates. This work proposes a frequency-switchable MMA that achieves reconfiguration through an origami-inspired structure enabled by a 3D-printed shape memory hinge (SMH). The non-hinge regions consist of multiple materials to support shape retention during thermal actuation. This design simplifies fabrication, maintains a compact structure during deformation, and improves structural stability. The proposed MMA enables discrete frequency switching, with the absorption peak shifting from 10.6 GHz in the unfolded state to 10.95 GHz in the folded state. Programming the folded state requires an externally applied force, whereas reheating triggers self-recovery to the original unfolded state. Experimental results demonstrate that this frequency tunability is directly induced by origami kinematics mediated through the SMH, without the need for an external biasing network. This work establishes a design strategy for reconfigurable MMAs, exploiting mechanically driven deformation to achieve thermally triggered discrete frequency switching.

title: Endoplasmic reticulum-targeted Cepharanthine-loaded metal–organic framework nanoreactor potentiates immunotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Our previous work revealed that cepharanthine (Cep) could elicit endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress for blocking hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of Cep in the ER of HCC restricts its application. In this study, metal organic framework (MOF) modified with N-acetylgalactosamine-rhodamine B and glibenclamide, which was abbreviated as GR-Gli-MOF, were prepared for loading Cep to boost ER stress and anti-HCC immunotherapy. The morphology, particle size, zeta potential, elemental composition, characteristic Ultraviolet–Visible absorption, and infrared vibration peaks were identified, verifying the successful preparation of Cep@GR-Gli-MOF. Further fluorescence imaging and sections results showed the prominent distribution of Cep@GR-Gli-MOF in tumor tissues. Cep@GR-Gli-MOF exhibited potent targeting in HCC cells and the ER, which released Cep and iron ions under acid conditions and triggered robust ER stress for facilitating Calreticulin (CRT) membrane translocation and immunogenic cell death. Significant efficacy was observed in subcutaneous and in situ HCC-bearing mice treated with Cep@GR-Gli-MOF, superior to free Cep and other agents. To summarize, the prepared Cep-loaded MOF possesses characterization of cascade targeting to the ER of HCC. Cep@GR-Gli-MOF induce vigorous ER stress and boost immunotherapy against HCC. The present work provides novel insight for how natural phytomedicine synergize with chemical vectors to mediate cancer immunotherapy.

title: Crystalline tubular origami with non-coincident stacking enabled by isomorphic symmetry breaking for enhanced crashworthiness
abstract: The developable double-corrugation (DDC) surface, also known as the Miura-ori, is a classic origami pattern widely used across length scales, from deployable space structures to shape-shifting biomedical devices. Although the original DDC pattern is flat-foldable and globally planar, it can be easily transformed into flat-foldable and globally curved surfaces through alternating changes in the acute fold angles of the facets. However, the broader design space of globally curved DDC surfaces remains largely unexplored. Here, using a crystallography-based design framework, we construct three families of such tubular structures and establish their geometric closure conditions. Their crashworthiness is then evaluated under quasi-static axial compression via finite element simulations, with selected designs experimentally validated using laser-scored, folded, and thermally welded polypropylene sheets. The results show that isomorphic symmetry breaking does not simply increase absorbed energy in all cases; rather, it provides a mechanism for regulating the crushing process. In particular, reduced-symmetry patterns promote non-coincident stacking pathways, distribute contact and compaction events over a larger displacement range, suppress densification-induced force peaks, and thereby improve crush force efficiency. This study demonstrates, for the first time, that isomorphic symmetry breaking can be used as a design principle for more effective tubular energy absorbers, providing new guidelines for origami-inspired metastructures for impact mitigation and protection applications.

title: Upcycling recycled carbon fibres into hybrid limestone calcined clay cement (LC3) composites for strengthening applications
abstract: A large share of structures worldwide cannot meet current design requirements due to updated anti-seismic guidelines, traffic growth, ageing, and severe climate change. High-Performance Fibre-Reinforced Cementitious Composites (HP-FRCC) represent an effective solution for structural strengthening; however, their widespread adoption is made less attractive by their high clinker content and reliance on virgin reinforcing fibres. This study investigates the development of sustainable HP-FRCCs based on limestone calcined clay cement (LC 3 ) incorporating recycled carbon fibres (rCFs) recovered from end-of-life sources and brass-coated steel fibres (BSFs). Two commercially available rCFs were first characterised to identify the most suitable reinforcement before developing hybrid LC 3 -based composites. The incorporation of rCFs increased compressive strength by up to 25% and flexural strength by more than 30% through microstructural refinement, while BSFs governed post-cracking behaviour and energy absorption. Hybridisation enabled the replacement of one third of the steel fibre content while maintaining confinement performance comparable to that of reference steel-fibre systems. Concrete cylinders strengthened with LC 3 -HP-FRCC jackets exhibited compressive strength increases of up to 107% compared with unconfined specimens, together with significantly improved damage tolerance. The results demonstrate that combining rCFs with BSFs and LC 3 binders provides sustainable high-performance cementitious composites for structural retrofitting.

title: Dual-scale analysis of mechanical behavior of laser powder bed fusion manufactured 316 L stainless steel
abstract: Additively manufactured (AM) 316 L stainless steel produced by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) exhibits heterogeneous microstructures that strongly affect its macroscopic mechanical behavior. To capture these complex microscopic features and address size effects, a dual-scale simulation system linking electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) characterization to mechanical analysis has been developed. Statistical analysis was performed on EBSD data decomposing grains into two groups according to their morphology. To overcome the 2D nature of EBSD measurements, a method for extending crystallographic information was introduced to reconstruct 3D grain information for the generation of 3D representative volume elements (RVE). RVE generation was optimized using a microstructure representativeness assessment diagram (MRAD). Crystal plasticity (CP) simulations, with parameters calibrated from nano-indentation, were performed to predict the homogenized mechanical behavior. The Bai-Wierzbicki (BW) yield surface was upscaled from the CP simulations to represent the microstructure-informed mechanical behavior. To address the non-uniqueness of CP parameters identified from nano-indentation, an inverse calibration framework was established. The simulation framework achieves agreement in the early yielding range with experiments and enables predictions of size effects on mechanical behavior. The results highlight the significant effects of crystallographic features on macroscopic yielding behavior and introduce a trustworthy framework for microstructure-informed mechanical property prediction.

title: Influence and regulation strategy of crystal orientation on residual stress and displacement field in single-crystal turbine blades
abstract: The fabrication of single-crystal turbine blades necessitates simultaneous and stringent control of dimensional accuracy and metallurgical quality. However, studies about influence of crystal orientations on the residual stress and dimensional accuracy of entire blades are limited. This paper systematically addressed the influence of primary and secondary orientation on the residual stress and displacement field. In this work, stress and displacement field were simulated based on ProCAST software, the crystal orientations were controlled by single-crystal substrate stimulating technique. The deviation angles selected for primary orientation [0 0 1] (α) were 0°, 6°, and 12°, respectively. The deviation angles for secondary orientation [1 0 0] (β) were nine discrete orientations designated at 10° intervals relative to longitudinal axis of the platform. The blade with primary orientation deviation of 6° demonstrates the smallest residual stress and smallest maximum deformation, whereas the case with deviation of 0° exhibits the largest. And the blade with secondary orientation deviation of 30° exhibited satisfactory results. Then, a regulation strategy employing α = 6°, β = 30° yielded significant improvements, of which residual stress decreased by 450 MPa, and maximum deformation decreased by 50%. This strategy demonstrated a certain extent effectiveness across another blade. Finally, exploratory analysis was conducted on the influence of crystal orientation on residual stress and displacement fields

title: Physical twins for structural safety evaluation: An experimental approach
abstract: This study presents an experimental approach for evaluating flaw-containing components using additively manufactured Physical Twins. The Physical Twin concept combines qualification by testing and similarity, enabling the replication of real internal flaws for structural safety assessment. A miniaturized reactor pressure vessel made of 22NiMoCr3-7 steel was employed as a case study. Additive manufacturing via laser powder bed fusion, followed by post-process heat treatment, produced a ferritic–bainitic microstructure comparable to the forged reference material, with tensile strength and elongation differing by less than 13%. Specific crack configurations were successfully reproduced. The design for a Physical Twin of a reactor pressure vessel which is used for component testing is explained. Burst tests on reference and crack-containing vessels reached pressures up to 1630 bar. The observed failure modes corresponded closely to numerical predictions based on an extended damage-mechanics Rousselier model, demonstrating strong agreement between experimental and simulated results. Crack interaction and initiation behavior were accurately reproduced, confirming mechanical and failure similarity between the Physical Twin and its reference component. The findings verify that sufficient material and mechanical similarity can be achieved between additively manufactured and conventionally produced components. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of using additively manufactured Physical Twins for experimental safety qualification of flaw-containing structures, particularly in safety-critical applications such as nuclear pressure vessels. This approach offers a novel and practical pathway for assessing the influence of real internal flaws on component integrity.

title: From dry powder to multi-functional hydrogel: a self-healing and shape-adaptive dressing for improving diabetic wound healing
abstract: Diabetic wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to the dysregulation of inflammatory phase and impaired cellular activity. Although hydrogel sheet dressings have demonstrated a great potential, their application to irregular wounds and the ability to improve wound healing are often limited. In this study, a practical hydrogel powder dressing (O3C-H30LP) was developed from the OGCB precursor suspension which contained oxidized sodium alginate, gelatin, calcium carbonate microspheres and borax. The suspension exhibited an excellent injectability. After gelation and crosslinking, the hydrogel was freeze-dried and mechanical ground to obtain O3C-H30LP. The swelling ratio was 517.02 ± 11.02% and showed a good dimensional stability. The particle size was 109.8 ± 8.9 μm; after rehydration, they were integrated together to demonstrated a high self-healing ability. In addition to favorable biodegradability, in vitro studies showed that the sample possessed good hemocompatibility and promoted adhesion and proliferation of murine fibroblasts. Furthermore, in vivo tests based on diabetic rat model revealed that O3C-H30LP significantly accelerated wound closure during the critical stages of healing, enriched matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), modulated the wound microenvironment, and effectively promoted tissue remodeling. This multifunctional dressing provides a simple yet efficient strategy for the management of diabetic wounds.

title: Process-field evaluation of residual-stress-uniformity risk in hot-rolled Q355B strip by coupling transformation timing, dilatometric strain and microstructural constraint
abstract: Widthwise residual-stress non-uniformity generated during post-rolling cooling remains difficult to screen because adjacent regions follow different thermal, transformation and dimensional histories while remaining mechanically continuous. Under a fixed upstream rolling schedule, this work evaluates widthwise cooling-rate fields for Q355B using 150 full-factorial Gleeble paths, corrected dilatometry, central-zone electron backscatter diffraction and hardness, and a five-zone process-field model. The model separates mismatch formation ( J mis ) from cooling-intensity-associated retention ( J cool ), with microstructural descriptors treated only as relative path-state indices. The nominal 60 °C/s condition was verified from specimen-thermocouple records (59.15 ± 0.84 °C/s), and industrial hole-drilling measurements showed section-wise widthwise longitudinal-stress ranges of 67.3–121.1 MPa. Across 4182 admissible fields and 5000 sensitivity runs, moderate centre cooling with equal or slightly slower edge cooling remained the stable low-risk family. The formal minima were CT650-IH at 27.5/23.0 °C/s (centre/edge) and CT650-DC at 25.0/24.5 °C/s when holding was excluded. The dimensionless ranking provides a post-rolling process-screening framework rather than an absolute three-dimensional stress prediction.

title: Microstructural evolution of SIMP steel during martensitic transformation
abstract: SIMP steel, a reduced activation ferritic/martensitic heat–resistant steel, is a promising candidate for structural applications in future nuclear fusion reactors. Understanding the evolution of microstructure in SIMP steel is of practical importance for improving the structural integrity of components made from this material. In this work, we study the effects of cooling rate on the evolution of microstructures in the SIMP steel, including martensitic transformation and indentation deformation. At low cooling rates, the martensitic transformation exhibits characteristics of multi–step transformation, while these characteristics disappear at high cooling rates. A modified Koistinen-Marburger model was introduced to analyze the temporal evolution of martensite in the SIMP steel at stage IV under three different cooling rates (0.5, 1, and 5 K/s). The characteristic undercooling temperature at stage IV follows a power-law dependence of the cooling rate with a power index of 0.17. The dependence of indentation hardness on the characteristic block width exhibits two distinct regimes: a Hall-Petch-like relationship for block widths less than or equal to 4.1 μm, and a possible inverse Hall-Petch-like relationship for block widths larger than or equal to 4.1 μm.

title: Laser shock peening in hydrogen environments: coupled stress–transport–trapping mechanisms and application gaps
abstract: Hydrogen embrittlement limits the deployment of high-strength steels and advanced alloys in hydrogen infrastructure. Laser shock peening (LSP) is increasingly considered as a mitigation route because it combines deep compressive residual stresses with near-surface microstructural modification. This review critically assesses LSP not as an isolated strengthening treatment, but as a surface layer design strategy governed by coupled stress, hydrogen transport and trapping mechanisms. Evidence from steels, nickel based alloys and additively manufactured materials shows that compressive residual stresses may suppress stress assisted hydrogen transport and delay crack initiation, while LSP-induced nanostructuring, dislocations, twins and interfaces can either redistribute hydrogen beneficially or promote localized plasticity and damage. Reported trends are frequently confounded by hydrogen charging mode, surface roughness, contamination, residual stress depth profiling and limited structure performance correlations. Two design critical gaps are identified: the lack of quantitative links between post-LSP stress/defect architectures and hydrogen assisted fatigue crack growth, and the near absence of impact toughness data after LSP under hydrogen exposure. The review proposes mechanism informed qualification routes combining residual stress mapping, hydrogen characterization, service representative mechanical testing and modelling

title: Lost cells, retained structure: proteomic mapping of decellularized lung matrisome across species
abstract: Decellularized lung scaffolds represent a promising platform for respiratory tissue engineering, yet it remains unclear how decellularization remodels the proteome, which extracellular matrix (ECM) components are depleted or retained, and whether residual non-matrisome proteins persist despite DNA-based clearance benchmarks. Moreover, systematic cross-species comparison remains unaddressed. We applied a single detergent-based protocol to mouse, pig, and human lung tissue and characterized the resulting scaffolds using histology, ultrastructural imaging, immunofluorescence, mass spectrometry-based proteomics with matrisome annotation, and STRING-based protein–protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Decellularization achieved consistent cellular clearance while preserving alveolar ECM architecture. Proteomic profiling identified a 96-protein matrisome core shared across all three species, dominated by structural collagens, basement membrane glycoproteins, and elastic fibre components, whereas matrisome-associated proteins showed substantially lower cross-species conservation. PPI network analysis mapped this core onto three modules of known and predicted associations. Beyond the matrisome, species-specific residual cellular protein signatures persisted despite scaffolds meeting DNA-based clearance criteria. As an initial demonstration of cytocompatibility, human expandable lung epithelium progenitor cells on pig scaffolds remained attached and proliferative over 28 days. These findings reframe scaffold assessment beyond cellular clearance toward molecular evaluation of ECM composition and network architecture, arguing for proteomic criteria alongside anatomical considerations in lung bioengineering.

title: Semi-empirical and computational modelling of the laser structuring effect on wettability performance of polypropylene
abstract: Developing laser-textured surfaces to achieve a target wettability remains a time-consuming process, as texture selection often relies on trial-and-error approaches. To contribute to a more systematic design strategy, this study proposes a methodology to support and accelerate the selection of feature dimensions to achieve a target wettability. The approach combines a 3-factor, 3-level Design of Experiments with computational phase field modelling to evaluate the wettability of laser textured polypropylene surfaces. Square pillar textures were developed, and the effects of pillar width, cavity width and pillar height on the measured Contact Angle (CA) was quantified. The experimental results showed that pillar height was the most influential parameter, and a simplified regression model was proposed to describe its effect on contact angle variation. In parallel, a 2D computational Phase Field model implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics 5.4, was developed to support the rapid selection of texture dimensions for targeted wettability. Model parameters were calibrated and validated using experimental contact angle measurements, showing good agreement within the investigated texture range. Overall, the combined DoE–simulation framework provides additional information on how surface topography affects contact angle variations and helps guide texture design, reducing experimental trial-and-error steps for the considered scenario.

title: Characterisation of the crystallinity and fracture behaviour of additively manufactured polylactic acid (PLA) through the material extrusion method
abstract: This study investigates the influence of AM parameters and annealing on the microstructure, crystallinity, and mechanical properties of material extruded polylactic acid (PLA) specimens. Specimens were 3D-printed with layer heights of 0.1 mm and 0.3 mm, infill densities of 25 % and 100 %, and nozzle temperatures of 190 °C and 220 °C. Tensile tests showed that as-printed specimens exhibited similar behaviour across the parameters, whereas annealed specimens showed notable differences. The low-density (25 % infill density) annealed specimen showed higher Young’s modulus (434.9 MPa) and yield strength (35.5 MPa) compared to the high-density annealed specimen (with Young’s modulus of 398.4 MPa and yield strength of 31.6 MPa). Flexural tests indicated improved strength and stiffness with higher layer height, infill density, and nozzle temperature. FE-SEM micrographs revealed smaller spherulites (4.8 µm) at the lower limit of layer height, infill density, and nozzle temperature, while larger spherulites (7.0 µm) were observed at higher values of process parameters. Annealing increased crystallinity (∼33 %) and shifted fracture behaviour from ductile to brittle, especially in low-density parts. Results demonstrated that printing parameters combined with annealing significantly affected microstructure and mechanical performance, highlighting that smaller, more numerous spherulites and lower infill density could enhance tensile properties in annealed PLA parts.

title: Taking advantage of miniemulsion polymerization for developing super-wettable membranes for emulsified oil/water separation
abstract: Polymerization has been used in various applications, including the development of promising, efficient membranes for water treatment and desalination. In such a scenario, various polymerization methods have been explored to develop polyamide and mixed-matrix membranes. However, the potential of miniemulsion polymerization has not been well explored, particularly for developing polymeric membranes for water treatment. This study has focused on developing different variants of the polypyrrole (Ppy) by gradually increasing the concentration of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) during polymerization. The SDS concentration was maintained at three levels: below the water-based critical micelle concentration (CMC), at CMC, and above CMC to achieve miniemulsion polymerization of Ppy on an alumina (Al 2 O 3 ) ceramic disc. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) measurements showed enhanced stabilization of monomer (pyrrole) particles/droplets in the emulsion with increasing SDS concentration. The DLS also showed an increase in the size of Ppy particles along with changes in zeta-potential with increasing SDS. As a result, the three membranes showed variations not only in their physical features but also in their performance. For instance, among the three membranes prepared in the current study, Above-CMC-Ppy@Al 2 O 3 showed relatively better characteristics, features, and performance for oil/water emulsion separation. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed that the polymer particles were larger and more numerous when the SDS concentration exceeded the CMC during pyrrole polymerization. Therefore, the Above-CMC-Ppy@Al 2 O 3 membrane exhibited enhanced separation efficiency for the emulsified oil-in-water feed. The permeate flux of the Above-CMC-Ppy@Al 2 O 3 membrane was 2619 L m −2 h −1 (LMH) at 4 bar transmembrane pressure using distilled water as feed, whereas with the 100 ppm crude oil emulsion, the flux was 929.6 LMH and the separation efficiency was > 97.8 % at 4 bar. In contrast, the Below-CMC-Ppy@Al 2 O 3 membranes showed a permeate flux of 295.8 LMH and a separation efficiency of > 99 % at 4 bar. Moreover, stability studies revealed consistent performance of the membranes in terms of separation efficiency over an extended period of membrane testing. The membranes also retained their surface wettability features essential for separation even after exposure of the membranes to corrosive environments.

title: Phase evolution and functional properties of electro spark deposited CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy coatings on steel
abstract: Carbon steels are widely used industrially but suffer from insufficient wear and corrosion resistance, necessitating protection. High–entropy alloy (HEA) coatings are attractive due to their ability to promote solid-solution phases over intermetallics. In plasma-based coating techniques, heat input critically influences phase evolution. The current study investigates the microstructural evolution, mechanical responses, tribological behavior, and corrosion resistance of CoCrFeMnNi HEA nanocrystalline-coatings deposited on steel using electro-spark deposition (ESD) under different heat inputs. Low-energy coatings exhibit a single-phase FCC structure, negligible Fe dilution, and nanocrystalline grains (19–24 nm). High-energy coatings show significant dilution (29.1 %), coarser grains (25–29 nm), and secondary, harder BCC (A2/B2) phases due to Fe-Cr segregation and Fe-Co ordering reaction. The moderate-energy coating (56 mJ) delivers the best performance: lowest wear loss (0.0016 g), stable friction coefficient (0.4), highest deformation resistance (H 3 /E 2 = 1740 Pa), lowest current density (2.8 × 10 −7 A.cm −2 ), and highest polarization resistance (13 kΩ). These optimum results arise from coating’s dense and nanocrystalline structure. The highest-energy coating, despite greatest hardness (384 HV), suffers from poor tribology and corrosion resistance due to a non-uniform surface profile and defective structure. In brief, strict control over ESD parameters is imperative to preserving the as-designed HEA structure after deposition.

title: Construction of epigallocatechin gallate/exosomes co-loaded dual-layer sustained‑release microneedles for alleviating skin photoaging and pigmentation
abstract: Skin photoaging (SP) is a condition caused by prolonged exposure to solar ultraviolet radiation, leading to skin laxity, wrinkles, pigmentation, and accelerated aging, which significantly impacts appearance, health, and lifestyle. Current therapeutic approaches, including topical creams, gels, and intradermal injections, suffer from limitations in efficacy and safety. Herein, we developed a dual-layer sustained-release microneedle platform: epigallocatechin gallate/exosomes@chitosan/β-glycerophosphate-hyaluronic acid microneedles (E/Ex@CS-HA MNs). The MN consists of a fast-dissolving hyaluronic acid (HA) base and a sustained-release tip composed of CS/β-GP crosslinked thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with exosomes (Exos) and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Upon application, the HA base rapidly dissolves, leaving the hydrogel tips embedded in the dermis for prolonged drug release. In vitro , the E/Ex@CS‑HA MNs scavenged 88% of free radicals, protected UVB-damaged HDFs cells, and inhibited melanin synthesis by 58%. In a guinea pig photoaging model, the MNs reduced epidermal melanin deposition by 80%, and downregulated senescence/inflammation markers (e.g., MMP‑1, AGEs). The platform provided sustained release of EGCG and exosomes over 7 days (cumulative release ∼78%). These results demonstrate that the E/Ex@CS‑HA MNs achieve simultaneous anti‑photoaging and whitening effects through dual‑drug delivery, supporting its potential as a comprehensive transdermal intervention for skin photoaging.

title: Pore-structure regulation and coal dust capture mechanisms of solid-waste-based foamed concrete modified with SDS/CTAB
abstract: To address the challenge of integrating lightweight thermal insulation, structural support, and coal dust capture in sprayed materials for underground mine roadways, this study developed a solid-waste-based foamed concrete using coal gangue, fly ash, basalt fibres, and ceramsite. An anionic–cationic SDS/CTAB system was introduced to regulate interfacial behaviour, foam stability, and surface-pore characteristics and to evaluate dynamic coal dust capture. SDS effectively reduced surface tension but showed limited foaming ability in the highly alkaline and ion-rich system, whereas CTAB regulated the apparent electrical state of the liquid phase but provided insufficient foam stability. At SDS and CTAB dosages of 0.15% and 0.19%, respectively, the combined system achieved low surface tension, a slightly positive zeta potential, and improved foam stability, while the resulting specimens reached a coal dust capture efficiency of 65.03%. Microscopic analyses showed that SDS/CTAB did not markedly inhibit the formation of major hydration products, while optimised surface-pore characteristics, rough pore walls, and intra-pore spaces promoted coal dust deposition and retention. The optimal group achieved a 28-day compressive strength of 13.52 MPa and a thermal diffusivity of 2.53 × 10 −8 m 2 /s, indicating balanced dust capture, thermal insulation, and mechanical performance.

title: Virus-mimetic Gd-Fe nanocarriers co-delivering cisplatin and a TGF-βRI inhibitor induce ferroptosis and sensitize ovarian carcinoma to PD-1 blockade
abstract: Ovarian carcinoma remains poorly responsive to immune checkpoint blockade, partly because of a TGF-β-enriched and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. We developed a virus-mimetic hollow Gd-Fe nanocarrier for the co-delivery of cisplatin (DDP) and the TGF-β receptor I inhibitor TGFβRI-IN-3 (IN-3), aiming to integrate chemotherapy, ferroptosis induction, and TGF-β pathway blockade into a single therapeutic platform. DDP/IN-3@Gd-Fe nanoparticles (NPs) were prepared using a hard-template strategy. Cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, apoptosis, and ferroptosis-associated biochemical changes were evaluated in SKOV3 cells. In tumor-bearing mice, biodistribution, T1-weighted MRI contrast, biosafety, and antitumor efficacy were further investigated. The prepared NPs exhibited uniform size, good stability, and high drug loading with sustained release. In vitro, DDP/IN-3@Gd-Fe NPs were effectively internalized by SKOV3 cells and demonstrated superior cytotoxicity, apoptosis induction, and ferroptosis promotion compared to free drugs. In vivo, DDP/IN-3@Gd-Fe NPs exhibited the strongest tumor growth inhibition, involving synergistic induction of apoptosis and ferroptosis and effective suppression of the TGF-β signaling pathway. Finally, DDP/IN-3@Gd-Fe NPs were found to remodel the immunosuppressive TME by increasing inflammatory mediators and promoting tumor infiltration of cytotoxic T cells and dendritic cells. In conclusion, DDP/IN-3@Gd-Fe NPs provide an MRI-traceable chemo-ferroptosis platform that may attenuate TGF-β-associated immunosuppression and improve checkpoint blockade responses in ovarian carcinoma

title: Wave propagation control in a 2D dual–rotor metamaterial: zero–frequency bandgap, waveguiding, and negative refraction
abstract: Two-dimensional elastic wave metamaterials have attracted considerable interest due to their ability to manipulate in-plane elastic waves with high efficiency and versatility. In this work, the propagation behavior of elastic waves in a two-dimensional dual-rotor metamaterial is investigated. This metamaterial introduces two different connection methods between adjacent unit cells. It can induce the emergence of a zero-frequency bandgap, a bandgap whose lower edge starts at zero frequency. The dispersion relation is derived using Bloch’s theorem, and parametric analyses are performed to reveal how structural parameters affect the bandgap and passband characteristics. Group velocity distributions are computed from frequency contours to quantify the direction and magnitude of wave energy transport. Then, numerical simulations using finite elements are performed to verify the predicted wave propagation behaviors, including isotropic, anisotropic, and hybrid modes. By introducing defect states, waveguiding along straight and folded paths is achieved, and pattern design is demonstrated. Furthermore, total reflection and negative refraction are investigated when waves propagate across the interface between two different regions. These findings provide theoretical foundations for ultra-low-frequency vibration isolation, directional waveguiding, and subwavelength focusing applications.

title: Additive manufacturing of TiN/Ti6Al4V composites in reactive atmospheres: A universal strategy for fabricating metal matrix composites with synergistic property enhancement
abstract: • TiN/Ti6Al4V composites are additively manufactured by gas–metal reaction in nitrogen. • Clean interface and good dispersion between the TiN and Ti matrix are achieved. • In-situ formed TiN precipitates refine the composite grains via their pinning effect. • The composite formed in 2 vol% N 2 achieves both high strength and high plasticity. As additive manufacturing (AM) advances, the use of gas as a reaction medium to optimize material properties becomes more and more important. In this study, we manufactured titanium matrix composites (TMCs) with uniformly dispersed reinforcement TiN by gas–liquid in-situ reaction using an integrated strategy combining AM and laser gas nitriding (LGN) in low nitrogen (N 2 ) concentrations (2 vol% and 8 vol%). Meanwhile, both good mechanical and electrochemical properties were achieved. As the N 2 concentration was raised from 2 vol% to 16 vol%, the content of N in the samples gradually increased, accompanied by enhanced TiN generation, and the compositional variation triggered significant microstructural evolution, which affected the overall properties of the material. Notably, the strength and plasticity of the samples prepared in 2 vol% N 2 concentration reached the maximum value simultaneously. In addition, the samples prepared in low N 2 concentrations (2 vol%, 8 vol%) possessed superior wear resistance and corrosion resistance. The mechanisms behind the strengthening and toughening as well as the tribological and corrosion mechanisms were studied. These findings provide a new possibility for fabricating tailorable high-performance TMCs.

title: Magneto-elastic coupling and non-reciprocal acoustic phonons at the antiferromagnetic phase transition in MnPS3 revealed by Brillouin light scattering
abstract: We investigate magneto-elastic coupling at the antiferromagnetic phase transition of the van der Waals compound MnPS 3 using temperature-dependent Brillouin light scattering. In backscattering geometry we observe the longitudinal acoustic phonon propagating along the layer normal at about , corresponding to an out-of-plane elastic stiffness . The phonon frequency exhibits a distinct anomaly at the Néel temperature K, located through the logarithmic coefficient introduced here as sensitive transition indicator. Separating the magnetic contribution from the anharmonic background yields an effective critical exponent , consistent with the quasi-two-dimensional character of the compound; the phonon linewidth steps at the transition, reflecting suppressed spin-phonon scattering. Below , a splitting of GHz emerges between the Stokes and anti-Stokes frequencies, evidencing non-reciprocal propagation of long-wavelength acoustic phonons enabled by simultaneous time-reversal and inversion symmetry breaking. The splitting scales with the order parameter rather than with , as predicted for intrinsic phonon non-reciprocity in -symmetric antiferromagnets. Brillouin spectroscopy thus provides direct access to magneto-elastic structure–property relationships in van der Waals magnets.

title: A cell membrane inspired multifunctional hydrogel loaded with ginsenoside Rh1 for S. aureus infected wound healing
abstract: During the healing process of skin wounds, there are challenges such as slow tissue regeneration and bacterial infections. This paper has developed a drug-loaded composite hydrogel dressing that can promote angiogenesis, inhibit bacteria, and reduce inflammation. The hydrogel is composed of gelatin (Gel) and acrylamide (AM), and is formed into a biomimetic cell membrane structure through cross-linking. By adding different concentrations of graphene oxide (GO), the tensile strength of the hydrogel dressing can be significantly increased (from 57.54 KPa to 95 KPa), and the adhesion strength (shear strength) can be effectively enhanced (16.44 KPa). Additionally, Panax ginsenoside Rh1 has been successfully encapsulated in the hydrogel, achieving local controlled release. In vivo evaluation shows that the enhanced matrix by graphene oxide and the sustained release of Panax ginsenoside Rh1 have an antibacterial rate of up to 98.69% against S. aureus . It also stimulates the proliferation, migration, and tube formation of endothelial cells, thereby achieving strong vascularization at the wound site. Moreover, it can enhance the secretion capacity of anti-inflammatory factors (IL-4 from 19.54 to 105.61 pg/mL, IL-10 from 151.94 to 339.98 pg/mL), thereby accelerating the wound healing process. This hydrogel dressing provides a promising strategy for achieving high-quality wound repair.

title: Effect of pre-deformation and multi-step ageing on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Al-Cu-Li alloys
abstract: Achieving high strength while retaining adequate ductility remains challenging in precipitation-strengthened Al–Cu–Li alloys. Herein, a multi-step T9I6 treatment comprising two-step solution treatment, pre-ageing, pre-deformation, and interrupted ageing was employed to regulate dislocations and T1 precipitation. Increasing pre-deformation from 0% to 7% raised the ultimate tensile strength and yield strength from 518.6 and 409.1 MPa to 632.6 and 576.1 MPa, respectively, while retaining an elongation of 8.3%. At 4% pre-deformation, the T9I6 specimen exceeded the conventional T84 specimen in ultimate tensile strength, yield strength, and elongation by 6.57%, 4.78%, and 27.94%, respectively. Increasing pre-deformation raised the dislocation density from 9.19 × 10 13 to 6.23 × 10 14 m −2 , reduced the average in-plane length of T1 precipitates from 100.9 to 72.1 nm, and increased their areal density from 68.4 to 169.8 μm −2 . Deformation-induced dislocations provided direct strengthening and heterogeneous nucleation sites. Together with T1 precursors retained after pre-ageing, they promoted finer and denser intragranular T1 precipitation, increasing the precipitation-strengthening contribution from 174.3 to 242.8 MPa. Thus, the superior strength of the T9I6-7% specimen originated from the synergistic enhancement of dislocation and T1 precipitation strengthening.

title: Exploring the potential of Ta-Nb-Ti-based multi-component alloys for biomedical applications: Microstructural evolution and key mechanical observations
abstract: The present study investigates multi-component alloys based on the biocompatible elements Ta, Nb, and Ti, designed via thermodynamic calculations, synthesized by arc-melting, and subjected to homogenization heat treatments. Microstructures were characterized using SEM and XRD, whilst mechanical properties were evaluated through hardness testing, room-temperature compression, and 3-point bending on microsamples. Results show a strong correlation between mechanical performance and Ti content, homogenization time, and temperature. Overall hardness increased after homogenization, which is attributed to solid solution strengthening. However, grain-orientation specific hardness indentation did not yield clear correlations, attributed to the high number of active slip systems in bcc lattices and the large grain sizes present. Compression tests revealed high plastic deformability (> 25 %) and composition-dependent yield strength for all alloys, with deviations noted at higher Ti contents post-homogenization. All alloys demonstrated enhanced elastic deformability and reduced flexural moduli compared to the reference, aligning more closely with bone and suggesting improved suitability for orthopedic applications. Notably, the equimolar Ta-Nb-Ti alloy exhibited the most balanced mechanical properties in terms of hardness, flexural strength, and compressive behavior, making it a promising candidate for further evaluation as an orthopedic implant material.

title: Regression-based explainable deep learning for estimating Hamiltonian parameters from magnetic nanodot images
abstract: Magnetic nanodots host topological spin textures whose stability is dictated by an extended Heisenberg Hamiltonian combining symmetric exchange, the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, magnetocrystalline anisotropy, and the Zeeman field. Inferring these atomistic parameters from two-dimensional magnetization images underpins the design of functional magnetic materials, yet it remains an ill-posed inverse problem: under certain external conditions and transient states, configurations relax into noisy, weakly discriminative textures that render the dataset ill-conditioned. Deep-learning estimators act as opaque black boxes and rely on slow atomistic simulations. We propose an explainable regression methodology whose novelty lies in data generation and interpretability: a matrix decomposition of the extended Hamiltonian enables GPU-accelerated Metropolis–Hastings Monte Carlo with simulated annealing, accelerating computation without altering the underlying physics, while Regression Activation Maps (RAMs), a novel error-based attribution metric, turn the network into a traceable gray-box model. Trained on several configurations, convolutional and Vision Transformer regressors reliably recover the physical parameters from simulated nanodot images, while the higher-order exchange constants remain bounded by the intrinsic identifiability limits of the s z projection. Comparing both families through their attention maps and accuracy-versus-size trade-off, RAMs isolate the chiral domain walls and skyrmion cores driving predictions.

title: Processing strategies to avoid abnormal grain growth during T4 heat treatment of AA2024 friction surfacing depositions
abstract: Friction surfacing (FS) is a friction stir-based solid-state layer deposition process, leading to deposits characterized by fine-grained microstructures. Precipitation-hardenable alloys typically present hardness gradients. To increase and homogenize the mechanical properties, a post-process heat treatment is required, resulting in unfavorable abnormal grain growth (AGG). This work explores processing strategies to avoid AGG during the post-process heat treatment: room temperature (RT), preheating FS, and FS combined with post-processing via hybrid friction diffusion bonding (HFDB) of AA2024. Preheating FS and HFDB post-processed conditions successfully preserve the refined grains during heat treatment. Grain stability has proven to be affected by the Zener pinning effect, thus by grain size and particle dispersion. The AGG of the RT FS condition has been correlated with the smallest grain size, the lowest secondary particle volume fraction, and secondary particle equivalent diameter. Secondary particle shapes and locations, and microstructure strain energy add additional stability to preheating FS and HFDB post-processed conditions. The combination of RT FS with HFDB has demonstrated the highest material efficiency of the processes, joining efficiency of the deposits, and grain stability during heat treatment. This understanding allows to suppress and/or tailor AGG for FS deposits.

title: Automated high-throughput data collection and analysis of composition-process-structure relations by utilizing casting segregation in a Ni-base superalloy
abstract: We attempt to address the problem of generating large, reliable experimental datasets that interrelate composition, processing and microstructure in a short timeframe by combining a heterogeneous sample with a gradient heat treatment. Composition-Process-Structure datasets are essential for both physical and purely statistical models aiming to predict material behavior. Using the segregated microstructure of a cast single-crystal sample of Ni-base superalloy MGA1400 in combination with a temperature gradient furnace, we cover a whole range of heat treatment temperatures and compositions according to elemental partitioning. Data collection uses automatic, correlative FE-SEM and EPMA analysis for microstructure images with corresponding local concentration. Image analysis combined with precipitate shape fitting using superellipses allows evaluation of phase fractions, precipitate size/shape/aspect distributions as well as inter-precipitate distances and relative angles for investigating clustering and alignment phenomena. As a result, we were able to generate a pseudobinary phase diagram indicating the γ′ solvus. The activation energy for coarsening of γ′ was found to be mostly independent of as-segregated composition. Further, results showed lattice misfit between the γ and γ′ phase to cause precipitate shape to vary with treatment temperature, and precipitate aspect ratio to vary between the dendrite core and interdendrite regions, indicating dendritic stresses from solidification.

title: A Forsythiaside A-loaded, oxygen-releasing thermosensitive hydrogel accelerates diabetic wound healing by remodeling the microenvironment
abstract: The healing of diabetic wounds is severely compromised by an adverse microenvironment characterized by persistent hypoxia, infection, and inflammation, necessitating the development of innovative and integrated therapeutic strategies. To address these challenges, we have engineered a multifunctional hydrogel (OTH-FTA) by incorporating an oxygen-generating matrix within a thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with forsythiaside A (FTA). In vitro studies revealed that OTH-FTA exhibited sustained oxygen release, excellent biocompatibility, and potent synergistic effects, including antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-apoptotic activities. In a diabetic mouse model, OTH-FTA significantly accelerated wound closure, as evidenced by enhanced granulation tissue formation, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis. Mechanistically, OTH-FTA suppressed the IL-17/TNF-α/NF-κB pathway and reduce inflammation and promote M2 macrophage polarization, thereby remodeling the immune microenvironment. This immunomodulation subsequently improved skin cell functionality through paracrine signaling. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that OTH-FTA represents a coordinated therapeutic strategy that simultaneously targets multiple pathological barriers, offering a promising integrated treatment for refractory diabetic wounds.

title: Microstructure-dependent thermocyclic fatigue and damage evolution in pre-cracked tungsten-rhenium X-ray anode conversion layers
abstract: This study elucidates structure–property relationships governing the thermal fatigue performance of X-ray anodes for medical imaging through an integrated experimental and computational approach. Controlled surface modifications in the form of pre-induced thermal-shock crack networks were introduced into two advanced conversion layer materials with distinct microstructures and subjected to thermal loading via pulsed electron beam exposure. Characterization of surface damage evolution, the associated X-ray photon starvation, and fracture modes revealed that anodes with grains elongated normal to the surface exhibit enhanced thermal fatigue resistance. In these materials, the crack networks promote compliant deformation, accommodate cyclic thermal strains, and reduce thermally induced stress concentrations, resulting in mitigated surface damage and improved functional stability. In contrast, materials with a globular grain structure display non-uniform damage evolution, where crack deflection along grain boundaries parallel to the surface leads to delamination and accelerated surface degradation under continued thermal cycling. Computational analyses correlated the observed damage mechanisms with stress distribution–microstructure interactions. The results demonstrate that tailoring microstructural architecture and crack network morphology is critical for optimizing thermal fatigue resistance of X-ray anodes under extreme thermal loading conditions.

title: Interaction response of ballistic impact with different material in-filled projectiles against layered composite target
abstract: Ballistic impact involves the high-velocity interaction response of a projectile with a protective target, resulting in projectile deformation, target damage, and mass loss. The Finite Element Method (FEM) implemented in ANSYS/Autodyn was used to investigate the ballistic response of a Kevlar Fiber Reinforced Polymer (KFRP) and epoxy layered target subjected to a 5.45 × 18 mm Malokalibernyj Pistolentyj Tsentralnogo boya (MPTs) projectile at 350 m/s. Four projectile material infill configurations were considered namely full lead (Pb), copper-plated steel (Cu), copper-plated steel encapsulated lead (Cu + Pb), and copper-plated steel encapsulated lead with a hard-steel core (Cu + Pb + HS). All configurations perforated the target within 60 μs, indicating insufficient target resistance. Projectile deformation included erosion, shear-off, and mushrooming. The Cu projectile retained the greatest structural integrity, whereas Pb showed the highest mass and length reductions. Cu + Pb + HS produced pronounced front-face deformation and interlayer failure, while Cu generated maximum back-face displacement and projectile fragmentation. Epoxy layers exhibited greater plastic strain than KFRP layers, propagating through the thickness while remaining concentrated near the impact region. These results demonstrate the influence of projectile configuration on projectile deformation, target damage, and ballistic response

title: Natural nanovesicles as a promising therapeutic strategy for radiation-induced organ injury
abstract: A serious and frequent complication of cancer radiotherapy is injury to vital organs, including the skin, lungs, heart, bone marrow, and intestines. Radiation injury involves complex mechanisms including oxidative stress, inflammatory cascades, tissue fibrosis, and cellular senescence. Current clinical approaches, such as advanced radiation techniques and pharmacological agents, often suffer from significant limitations, including inadequate protective effects, systemic side effects, and a general inability to effectively promote the regeneration of damaged tissues. In this context, natural nanovesicles have arisen as a novel and promising class of bio-derived therapeutics. These vesicles are derived from diverse sources such as mammalian cells, plants, and mammalian body fluids. They offer unique advantages for clinical translation, primarily due to their high biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, and innate ability to cross biological barriers and target sites of injury. More importantly, they are natural carriers of bioactive molecules and have been shown in preclinical studies to modulate immune responses, reduce oxidative damage, inhibit fibrotic pathways, and actively stimulate tissue repair and regeneration. This article provides a comprehensive review of the application and potential of natural nanovesicles in the treatment of radiation-induced organ injury, and unveils the targeted molecular mechanisms.

title: Thermomechanical stress distribution and fracture behavior of cracked Cu/Al2O3 bimaterials with functionally graded interlayers
abstract: Metal–ceramic bimaterials are widely used in high-temperature and structural applications because they combine the toughness of metals with the thermal resistance of ceramics. However, differences in elastic modulus and coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) create significant residual stresses at the interface, which can lead to cracking and failure. This study investigates the thermomechanical behavior of a cracked copper/alumina (Cu/Al 2 O 3 ) system using a three-dimensional finite element model. Functionally graded material (FGM) interlayers with linear, logarithmic, and exponential property variations are analyzed. Results show that thermal loading plays a dominant role in stress development, significantly increasing stress concentrations near the interface due to material mismatch. As temperature rises, both residual stresses and the mode-I stress intensity factor (K I ) increase, indicating a higher risk of crack propagation. Cracks located close to the interface experience the greatest amplification in K I , highlighting strong interaction effects. The inclusion of an FGM interlayer effectively reduces stress concentration and smooths stress distribution across the interface. Among the investigated gradation profiles, the logarithmic variation provides the most favorable overall redistribution of von Mises stress, whereas the gradation law producing the lowest mode-I stress intensity factor depends on crack length and crack–interface distance.

title: Data-driven inverse design of a dual-stiffness TPMS fusion cage with experimental validation
abstract: Data-driven design of architected biomedical structures requires controllable geometry-property relationships and experimental validation of manufacturable designs. This study proposed an inverse design framework for a dual-stiffness triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) fusion cage by integrating parametric finite element analysis (FEA), deep learning, laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), and mechanical testing. A TPMS-Gyroid cage was parameterized by wall thickness, internal gap, pillar dimension, and unit-cell size to regulate contact-induced stiffness transition. FEA identified parameter effects on staged stiffness, transition load, and porosity. Based on 800 simulated designs, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) was trained to establish the nonlinear geometry-property mapping, achieving high predictive accuracy ( ) for force, elastic modulus, cage height, and porosity, and enabling inverse generation of geometric parameters from target mechanical performance. Optimized Ti6Al4 V cages were fabricated by LPBF and evaluated under uniaxial compression, three-point bending, and eccentric loading, representing flexion, extension, and bending, respectively. The experimental results agreed well with the numerical predictions and confirmed a robust bilinear, contact-induced dual-stiffness response. The cages showed a compliant first stage, second stage modulus of to , and porosity of to . This work provides a complete, transferable data-driven design route for additively manufactured TPMS fusion cages.

title: Catechol-mediated anchoring of PEG/Ag nanocomposite coatings on silicone catheters for synergistic antifouling and antibacterial applications
abstract: The clinical utility of medical catheters is frequently compromised by biofouling and bacterial infections. To circumvent these challenges, we herein propose an “interface-initiated in-situ growth” strategy for catheter surface modification. Using polydopamine as the adhesive interlayer, a dense antifouling network was constructed via free dopamine crosslinking, followed by mild in-situ reduction to grow and immobilize silver nanoparticles (PDMS-PPA). The engineered coating demonstrates superior dual functionality: it achieves 99.99% antibacterial efficacy against S. aureus ( S. aureus ) and Escherichia coli ( E. coli ), retains a bacteriostatic rate above 94.0% after eight consecutive challenge cycles, and supports sustained Ag + release over 28 days. Furthermore, the modified surface exhibits remarkably enhanced hydrophilicity. Compared with the pristine catheter, the coating reduces protein adsorption by 85.7% and platelet adhesion by more than 70.0%, while preserving favorable cytocompatibility with cell viability above 95.0%. In vivo results further verify that the coating effectively inhibits bacterial colonization and alleviates local inflammatory responses, with no obvious systemic toxicity. This work achieves long-term synergism between antifouling and antibacterial performances, offering a robust and reliable strategy for surface modification of medical catheters.

title: Site-dependent Ga substitution in FeAl: Elastic and thermal transport properties
abstract: FeAl intermetallics have very high potential in structural and thermal applications at high temperatures due to their light-weight and oxidation resistance. However, they have low mechanical strength and poorly understood thermal behavior when alloyed with other elements. Gallium substitution has not been studied in detail, particularly with respect to its influence on structure, elasticity, and thermal transport in FeAl. In this study, we used density functional theory to study the properties of alloyed FeAl when gallium substitutes for either aluminum or iron. We performed structural, elastic, and thermal property calculations. It was found out that gallium substitution onto aluminum sites causes only a small lattice expansion and preserves the stability of the structure, but reduces both its stiffness thermal conductivity. Gallium on the iron sites, on the other hand, caused a significant jump in the lattice parameter, which led to mechanical instability and lower thermal conductivity. Most of the thermal transport was found to be dominated by electrons. This shows that gallium doesn’t just tweak FeAl’s properties, but it provides a way to tune them, depending on the site where the substitution is done. However, it is necessary to check intermediate substitution levels that yield ideal materials for structural applications.

title: Ti3C2-induced phase and interfacial effects in PVDF composites on the triboelectric behavior
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have emerged as promising candidates for sustainable energy harvesting and self-powered sensing due to their structural simplicity, scalability, and adaptability. In this work, multi-layer Ti 3 C 2 T x was incorporated into poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) at different concentrations via drop-casting to investigate the influence of MXene incorporation on the structural, dielectric, tribological, and triboelectric properties of the resulting composite films. Structural characterization by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) revealed that MXenes promote the transformation of PVDF towards the electroactive β-phase through interfacial interactions between PVDF dipoles and MXenes’ surface terminations. Dielectric measurements demonstrated a progressive increase in dielectric constant with increasing MXene content, which was attributed to the combined effects of enhanced β-phase formation and interfacial polarization. Tribological experiments showed that low MXene loadings (2 wt%) had only a marginal influence on friction compared with neat PVDF, whereas higher contents led to a pronounced increase in coefficient of friction due to increased surface heterogeneity and roughness. The triboelectric characterization confirmed an improved electrical output for MXene-containing composites in both contact-separation and sliding modes. The highest open-circuit voltages reached approximately 17.5 V for the composite containing 20 wt% in contact-separation mode, while 20.5 V were achieved for 8 wt% in sliding mode. The enhanced triboelectric response is attributed to MXene-induced modulation of the interfacial electronic structure, including an increased density of electronic states and trap-state formation, facilitating charge transfer and suppressing charge recombination. Based on the experimental observations, a mechanism is proposed linking interfacial electronic states, charge trapping, and triboelectric charge transport in MXene-PVDF composites. Our findings provide further insights into structure–property-performance relationships in MXene-based triboelectric materials and contribute to the design of advanced polymer-based triboelectric systems for sustainable energy harvesting applications.

title: Trace H2O-dependent oxidation behavior and oxide scale evolution of a Mo-Re-Ti-Zr-Nb alloy in ultra-high-temperature helium
abstract: In this work, the oxidation behavior of a Mo-7 wt% Re-0.3 wt% Ti-0.3 wt% Zr-0.3 wt% Nb alloy was investigated in He containing 10 or 50 ppm H 2 O at 1120 °C. Online impurity monitoring during heating was combined with mass-gain measurements, XRD, SEM, EDS, TEM and TOF-SIMS analyses to evaluate how trace H 2 O affects oxidation kinetics and near-surface microstructural evolution. A transient H 2 O release was detected during heating, indicating that the initial oxidation stage occurred under non-ideal impurity conditions. During isothermal exposure, however, the alloy exhibited consistently lower net mass gain under 50 ppm H 2 O than under 10 ppm H 2 O. Under 10 ppm H 2 O, a continuous Mo-based external oxide scale formed, together with Ti/Zr internal oxidation beneath the surface. The retained external scale was mainly composed of Mo oxides and contained locally distributed Mo-Re-rich particles and Ti-rich oxide regions. In contrast, under 50 ppm H 2 O, a continuous Mo-based external scale was not established. The surface was characterized by localized TiO 2 - and ZrO 2 -rich oxide nodules, while fine internal oxides were dispersed beneath the surface. These results indicate that increasing the trace H 2 O content did not simply increase the oxidation rate, but altered the partitioning between external oxide accumulation and internal oxidation.

title: Clinically-sized biohybrid ossicular scaffolds: toward restoring native mechano-acoustic function of middle ear
abstract: Conductive hearing loss affects millions of individuals worldwide and frequently arises from degeneration or disruption of the ossicular chain (OC). Current reconstructive strategies rely on autologous grafts or alloplastic prostheses, yet complications such as graft resorption, prosthesis extrusion and limited long-term hearing restoration remain unresolved. Here, we propose a tissue-engineered approach to regenerate bone-like ossicular replacements by combining in vitro produced osseous extracellular matrix with mechanically and acoustically optimized polymer scaffolds. Using fused deposition modeling, we fabricated porous, anatomically relevant OC scaffolds (“nail-shaped”; stem: 2.2-mm diameter, 4-mm length; head: 3.5-mm diameter, 0.8-mm height) capable of supporting human mesenchymal stem cell attachment and osteogenic differentiation under clinically compliant conditions. The OC constructs exhibited consistent bone matrix deposition in vitro and achieved native mechano-acoustic transmission in human cadaveric ears, with no average loss below about 4 kHz and approximately 10 dB loss at 10 kHz. This work demonstrates the feasibility of acoustically-functional replacements and may establish a translational framework for next-generation biomimetic implants in middle ear reconstruction.

title: Enhanced high-temperature fatigue resistance of LPBF hastelloy X via LSPwC: Synergy of surface integrity and hierarchical gradient substructures
abstract: Insufficient fatigue performance remains a critical barrier to the application of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) alloys in high-reliability components, particularly under elevated-temperature service conditions. In this study, a mJ-level laser shock peening without coating is proposed to synergistically optimize the surface integrity and high-temperature fatigue resistance of LPBFed Hastelloy X alloy. The results demonstrate that this method uniformly improves surface quality, achieving a reduction in roughness of 54.25%, while simultaneously inducing a hierarchical, multi-scale gradient substructures consisting of ultrafine grains, deformation twins, and high-density dislocations in the subsurface region. Moreover, the introduced compressive residual stress (CRS) exhibits excellent thermal stability at elevated temperature, with a relaxation rate of only 26.03%. High-cycle fatigue testing reveals that the fatigue strength at 650 °C is enhanced by approximately 12%. Detailed fractographic analysis indicates that the multi-scale gradient substructures, together with the thermally stable CRS, synergistically delays fatigue crack initiation and suppresses crack propagation. This study provides a novel regulation strategy and an engineering implementation pathway for achieving high-reliability service performance in additively manufactured components.

title: Influence of Mo-for-W substitution and Hf/C ratio control on carbide evolution and high-temperature strength in low-density Nb-based alloys
abstract: Low-density, high-strength Nb-based alloys require coordinated control of matrix strengthening, carbide strengthening, and high-temperature microstructural stability. Here, a CALPHAD-guided two-step design strategy is developed for Nb-W-Mo-Hf-C alloys by Mo/W matrix alloying and Hf/C-controlled MC carbides. Mo is used to partially substitute W to reduce density while maintaining matrix strengthening, whereas the Hf/C atomic ratio is adjusted to regulate the chemistry, morphology, and distribution of MC carbides. The optimized alloy achieves a density of 9.19 g·cm −3 with specific yield strengths of 99.2 MPa·cm 3 ·g −1 at room temperature and 44.8 MPa·cm 3 ·g −1 at 1300 °C. The Hf/C tuning transforms elongated NbC-rich needles and network-like carbides into refined (Nb, Hf)C rods and near-equiaxed particles. The strengthening mechanism is interpreted as the combined contribution of Mo/W-regulated solid-solution strengthening and Hf/C-regulated carbide dispersion strengthening. This work establishes a composition-thermodynamics-microstructure-property framework for designing Nb-based ultra-high-temperature alloys with improved density-strength balance.

title: Structural characterization of Lysimachia christinae acidic polysaccharides and investigation of its adjuvant efficacy for mRNA vaccines
abstract: The limited availability of effective adjuvants for mRNA vaccines necessitates the exploration of novel immunostimulatory agents. Here, we isolated and structurally characterized an acidic polysaccharide (LCAP) from the traditional Chinese herb Lysimachia christinae, and evaluated its adjuvant efficacy in an mRNA vaccine platform. LCAP, a 27.4 kDa heteropolysaccharide with a branched backbone enriched in galacturonic acid, was co-encapsulated with rabies virus glycoprotein (G) mRNA into lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). The resulting G mRNA + LCAP LNP formulation exhibited uniform size (∼100 nm), high encapsulation efficiency (>90%), and favorable colloidal stability. In DC2.4 cells, LCAP-LNP significantly upregulated CD86 and MHC-I/II expression, indicating enhanced dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation. In a mouse model, the co-encapsulated formulation elicited significantly higher antigen-specific IgG and neutralizing antibody titers compared to mRNA-LNP alone or a physical mixture of the two components. Moreover, it promoted robust Th1-biased cellular responses, as evidenced by increased frequencies of IFN-γ + TNF-α + polyfunctional T cells, germinal center B cells, and follicular helper T cells. These findings establish LCAP as a safe and effective natural polysaccharide adjuvant for mRNA vaccines, with its branched structure and uronic acid content likely underpinning its immunomodulatory activity.

title: Liquiritigenin-glycyrrhiza polysaccharide self-assembled nanomicelles ameliorate doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by inhibiting Nrf2-mediated ferroptosis
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is widely applied in cancer chemotherapy, yet it induces severe side effects. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death, plays an important role in the pathogenesis of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC). Liquiritigenin (LQ) has potent antioxidant activity, and its active components have shown considerable potential for alleviating DIC. In this study, we developed LQ-glycyrrhiza polysaccharide (GP) self-assembled nanomicelles (AngA-LQ-GP@Ms) for the targeted delivery of LQ to cardiomyocytes to suppress oxidative stress and ferroptosis. We found that AngA-LQ-GP@Ms exhibited perfect myocardial-targeting capability both in vitro and in vivo , significantly improved cardiac function in DIC mice, restored mitochondrial structure, alleviated oxidative stress and apoptosis, and effectively inhibited ferroptosis. Furthermore, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and Cellular Thermal Shift Assay suggested (CETSA) that nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) could be a direct target of AngA-LQ-GP@Ms. We further confirmed that blocking Nrf2 expression in cardiomyocytes partially abolished the cardioprotective and antiferroptotic effects of AngA-LQ-GP@Ms in vitro . Therefore, the protective effects of AngA-LQ-GP@Ms against DIC may be partially mediated through the Nrf2 pathway via the inhibition of ferroptosis, thereby providing valuable insights and experimental evidence for the development of targeted therapeutic strategies to alleviate DIC by suppressing ferroptosis in cardiomyocytes.

title: Development and evaluation of personalized testicular prostheses fabricated using 3D-printed molds and functionalized with antibacterial and anti-inflammatory coatings
abstract: Testicular prostheses currently face critical clinical limitations, including mechanical mismatch with native tissues, postoperative infection, and excessive fibrotic capsule formation. To solve these problems, we fabricated a multifunctional composite prosthesis via regulating the blending ratio of two-component silicone elastomer and constructing a bioactive coating based on propolis ethanol extract (EEP). Specifically, reducing the crosslinking density of the silicone network effectively lowers its elastic modulus, endowing the composite with soft tissue-matched mechanical compliance while preserving excellent structural stability under large deformation (elongation at break > 400%). In vitro experiments revealed that EEP coatings at moderate to high concentrations (50–75 mg/mL) exert concentration-dependent antibacterial properties and desirable cytocompatibility, whereas the maximum concentration (100 mg/mL) triggers significant cytotoxicity. In a 30-day rat subcutaneous implantation model, the optimized prosthesis (A1B2 silicone modified with 75 mg/mL EEP coating) exhibited superior in vivo performance. Compared with the uncoated control group (618.33 ± 59.89 μm), the optimized group showed mitigated macrophage infiltration, downregulated α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression, reduced collagen deposition, and a markedly thinner fibrous capsule (213.17 ± 44.58 μm). Additionally, no systemic inflammatory response or visceral organ toxicity was observed in vivo. Collectively, these results validate that the synergistic strategy of mechanical property regulation and biofunctional surface modification can effectively modulate peri -implant biological responses.
