This work provides a feasible and promising foundation for the development of personalized, biofunctionalized testicular prostheses with improved clinical adaptability.

title: Bionic horsetail-honeycomb tube: design, crashworthiness analysis and data-driven optimization
abstract: Thin-walled tubular energy absorbers require balance between load-bearing capacity, energy absorption efficiency and lightweighting. This study proposes a bionic horsetail-honeycomb thin-walled tube (BHHT) merging the multi-chamber configuration of horsetail stems with the energy-absorbing topology of hexagonal honeycombs. Specimens were fabricated via selective laser melting and tested under quasi-static compression. The validated finite element model achieved simulation errors below 8% for EA, SEA, and IPCF. Coupling analysis revealed that the overall EA of BHHT reached 142% of the algebraic sum of its substructures. Parametric studies identified complex nonlinear interactions among geometric parameters. A three-stage machine learning optimization framework was developed: a dataset was constructed using Latin hypercube sampling and finite element simulations; a high-precision surrogate model (R 2 > 0.97, MAPE < 4.5%) was trained and interpreted to quantify parameter contributions; NSGA-II with combined-weighting TOPSIS was then employed to maximize EA and SEA while minimizing IPCF. The optimal design (n = 10, t = 0.61 mm, d = 26.52 mm, l = 2.51 mm) yielded EA = 4123 J, IPCF = 108.67 kN, and SEA = 51.81 kJ·kg⁻ 1 . Compared with the original design, IPCF decreased by 32.84% and SEA increased by 8.32%, achieving synergistic optimization of loading smoothness, energy absorption efficiency, and lightweight performance. This study provides a methodology for the design and data-driven optimization of bionic energy-absorbing structures.

title: Loading-mode-dependent deformation mechanisms of sintered porous Cu
abstract: Sintered porous Cu contains a heterogeneous particle-neck-pore architecture whose deformation depends strongly on loading mode. In this study, porous Cu structures prepared from small particles (184 nm) and large particles (1451 nm) were examined using micropillar compression, micro-cantilever bending, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Under compression, the large-particle structure exhibited a higher apparent elastic modulus (14.5 0.9 GPa) than the small-particle structure (12.7 0.5 GPa), whereas the small-particle structure showed an approximately 80% higher yield strength (364 58 versus 202 71 MPa). In contrast, the large-particle structure exhibited an approximately 245% higher conditional fracture toughness (5.56 0.14 versus 1.61 0.16 ) and 1270% higher total bending work (8823 1245 versus 644 164 pJ). Microstructural analyses revealed that the refined particle-neck network accommodated compression through distributed pore compaction, neck deformation, and dislocation accumulation, suppressing strain localization. The coarser network promoted intraparticle slip and interfacial sliding under compression, while enhancing remaining-ligament continuity and neck bridging during crack propagation. MD simulations reproduced these distinct compressive responses and defect-evolution characteristics. These findings provide guidance for optimizing particle-neck-pore architectures in reliable sintered Cu interconnects.

title: Autophagy-dependent ferroptosis triggered by photodynamic therapy: A metabolic regulation nanoplatform for enhancing anti-tumor immunity
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most challenging subtype in breast cancer treatment because of its high metastatic potential and therapeutic resistance, which are associated with its unique metabolic reprogramming. To overcome these limitations, we developed a tumor metabolism-regulated photosensitizing nanoplatform (3CP) in this study. By loading glycolysis inhibitor 3-bromopyruvate (3BP) and photosensitizer chlorin e6 (Ce6) into biocompatible poly (lactic acid-glycolic acid)-poly(ethylene glycol) nanoparticles, the hypoxic tumor microenvironment was alleviated, and non-apoptotic cell death was induced. Photoacoustic imaging demonstrated effective accumulation of 3CP at tumor sites. Sustained release of 3BP inhibited tumor energy metabolism, reduced oxygen consumption, improved hypoxic microenvironment, and induced metabolic starvation in tumor cells. Under Ce6-mediated photodynamic therapy (PDT), excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production synergized with metabolic stress to induce excessive autophagy and ferritin degradation, thereby triggering ferroptosis and redirecting tumor cells from an apoptotic-resistant state to a non-apoptotic pathway. Concurrently, release of damage-associated molecular patterns stimulated anti-tumor immune response and modulated the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This strategy effectively enhanced the antitumor efficacy of PDT in vitro and in vivo experiments. Overall, this study provides a simple and effective strategy for addressing the treatment challenges associated with TNBC.

title: Decoding the hydrogen storage signature of LaMgHn (n = 1–24) clusters: Atomic-scale insights for rare-earth modified magnesium hydrides
abstract: The rational design of high-capacity hydrogen storage materials demands a fundamental understanding of hydride formation at bimetallic active sites. We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of LaMgH n (n = 1–24) clusters (where n denotes the number of hydrogen atoms), the simplest rare-earth–magnesium diatomic model. Unbiased global structure search combined with density functional theory reveals that the rigid La-Mg dimer forces homogeneous hydrogen distribution on both metal centers, a behavior that contrasts sharply with the site-specific adsorption in Sc-Mg systems. Energetic analysis identifies pronounced odd–even stability oscillations and several magic clusters (LaMgH 5 , LaMgH 7 , LaMgH 17 ) whose exceptional stability is electronically encoded by optimal La charge and even-electron closed-shell configurations favored by odd-n electron counting. Leveraging Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules, we establish a three-level hydrogen storage classification: (1) anchored isolated H, (2) anchored H 2 , and (3) unanchored physisorbed H 2 . This physically grounded framework shows that all hydrogen up to n = 16 belongs to Levels I and II, giving LaMgH 16 a theoretical gravimetric density of 8.99 wt% at 0 K. However, finite-temperature RRHO thermodynamic analysis reveals that only n = 8 among the Level 2-containing clusters (n = 6–16) retains its anchored H 2 at room temperature (ΔG(300 K) > 0), while all others, including LaMgH 16 , spontaneously desorb their Level 2H 2 above their respective T des (ranging from < 50 K to 329 K). This framework effectively separates usable hydrogen from weakly bound species. For n ≥ 17, unanchored H 2 emerges, defining a practical capacity ceiling. By integrating energetic, electronic, and topological descriptors, this work delivers an atomic-scale characterization for the La-Mg core, offering useful insights for guiding the development of rare-earth-modified magnesium hydrides. It is important to emphasize that this study is based on isolated gas-phase clusters (0D model) and the reported gravimetric densities are theoretical limits for individual molecules, not directly achievable capacities for bulk solid-state materials. The results provide fundamental insights into metal–hydrogen interactions at the atomic level, which may inform the design of nanostructured or amorphous hydrides where such diatomic motifs could be stabilized, but direct extrapolation to bulk crystalline hydrides would be inappropriate.

title: Dynamic failure and energy dissipation in graphene–carbon nanotube laminates under high-velocity impact
abstract: Designing lightweight protective materials that simultaneously achieve high stiffness, efficient energy dissipation, and damage tolerance under high-velocity impact remains a grand challenge. This study designs a functionally graded, sandwich-like graphene/CNT networks/graphene (Gr/CNTNs/Gr) continuous laminate and utilizes coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to resolve its impact response. The laminate dissipates energy through a coordinated sequence involving rapid fragmentation of the top graphene, bending and inter-tube sliding within the CNT networks, and shear-controlled deformation of the bottom graphene that suppresses fragment ejection. Impact velocity governs a transition from global dissipative deformation to localized covalent bond rupture. With the interlayer CNT networks serving as a tunable damping medium, a strict geometric and mass normalization analysis isolates the coupled thickness effects, revealing that both the energy absorption per unit thickness and the specific energy absorption (SEA, 10.4 MJ/kg) simultaneously converge at a unified optimal density of . At , the laminate doubles the SEA of graphene and reduces hazardous fragment kinetic energy by 67% compared to CNT films. Crucially, the laminate retains a load-bearing framework post-impact, enabling effective repair via simple graphene patching to withstand secondary strikes. This balanced performance surpasses steel, Kevlar, and graphene/polymer composites, offering architecture-level guidelines for hierarchical carbon laminates.

title: Wide-range predictions of hydrogen-dependent vacancy diffusion in nickel from a near-DFT-accurate machine-learning potential
abstract: Vacancy-mediated atomic transport plays a central role in high-temperature creep and microstructural evolution. Pure Ni provides a representative model system because Ni is the principal matrix element of many Ni-based heat-resistant alloys, while its prototypical FCC structure enables the intrinsic effects of hydrogen to be isolated. However, quantitative understanding of how hydrogen modifies vacancy formation, migration, and the resulting self-diffusion in Ni over wide temperature and pressure ranges remains limited. We therefore develop a near-DFT-accurate machine-learning moment tensor potential for the Ni–vacancy–hydrogen system and map the vacancy diffusion coefficient over 300 – 1500 K and hydrogen gas pressures – . The equilibrium vacancy concentration is obtained from the vacancy formation free-energy, while the hydrogen-dependent jump frequency is evaluated from the activation free-energy using the excess hydrogen thermodynamic integration method. The maps show that hydrogen suppresses vacancy diffusion at low temperatures over the entire investigated range of , whereas it enhances vacancy diffusion at high temperatures. Incorporating the hydrogen-enhanced equilibrium vacancy concentration, the vacancy-mediated Ni self-diffusivity increases under hydrogen charging for all conditions, with the strongest acceleration at low temperature and high H 2 pressure.

title: Corrigendum to “Displacement modeling for liquid cast forming process development considering microstructure evolution“ [Mater. Des. 268 (2026) 116455]
Role of structural heterogeneity size in shear band formation and mechanical response of rapidly solidified metallic glasses
abstract: The compositional heterogeneity may enhance plastic deformation at the clustering stage by facilitating shear-band formation, whereas, when phase separation occurs, it may increase brittleness by promoting shear-band propagation. However, the influence of pre-phase-separation compositional heterogeneity on different deformation behavior remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Y-induced structural heterogeneity was modulated by varying the Y content in Cu–Zr–Al–Y metallic glasses. Small-angle X-ray scattering and atom probe tomography showed that increasing Y content led to larger and more extensive structural heterogeneity. The mechanical response was evaluated through micro- and nano-indentation analyses, bending-induced kink angle measurements and bending fatigue tests. Interestingly, with increasing Y content, the critical shear stress decreased, while the tendency for shear-band formation increased. This was evidenced by lower Vickers and nano-hardness, elastic modulus, reduced maximum shear stress at the first pop-in, higher shear-band density in the kink region, and decreased fatigue resistance. These findings indicate that structural heterogeneity promotes shear-band initiation by providing preferential nucleation sites, but excessive heterogeneity deteriorates certain mechanical properties. These results establish correlations between progressively developing structural heterogeneity and mechanical response in the pre-phase-separation regime and highlight the need to optimize, rather than simply maximize, nanometer-scale structural heterogeneity to improve mechanical performance.

title: Spiral bionic design enhances the compression performance and deformation mode of thin-walled structures
abstract: Some traditional thin-walled structures have problems such as low energy absorption efficiency and disordered crushing patterns, which limit their application in high-performance lightweight component engineering scenarios. This study proposes a spiral biomimetic design strategy, using the elytra of beetles, natural honeycomb structures, and the shells of turtles as the basic thin-walled units. By introducing the spiral gradient arrangement mechanism of the Bouligand structure, three biomimetic spiral thin-walled structures are constructed: the spiral double-convex (BRHS), the spiral hexagonal (BHHS), and the spiral negative Poisson’s ratio (BNHS) forms. Quasi-static compression tests and finite element simulation analysis show that the mechanical response of the designed spiral bionic structure is significantly better than that of the corresponding original structure, among which BHHS-30° has the best performance with a specific energy absorption as high as 25.7 kJ/kg. Under the optimal configuration, further explore the influence laws of interlayer spiral angles (15°, 30°, 45°, 90°) and layup configurations (single/double spiral configurations) on structural performance. The research results show that, under the condition of equal relative density, by jointly regulating the helix angle and the layup configuration, the energy absorption performance and deformation mode can be simultaneously optimized, providing a new design concept for high-performance lightweight energy-absorbing structures.

title: VAP peptide-modified Forsythiaside A-pretreated exosomes promote the repair of the blood-spinal cord barrier by regulating endothelial cell autophagy
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts the blood-spinal cord barrier (BSCB), triggering secondary damage and permanent neurological deficits. Forsythiaside A is a natural bioactive compound isolated from Forsythia suspensa. It boasts robust anti-inflammatory and tissue-repairing capacities and can precondition stem cells to enhance the therapeutic potency of their secreted exosomes. To equip FSA-primed exosomes with precise targeting, we utilized SNTRVAP (VAP), a GRP78-specific peptide with the sequence SNTRVAP. Here, we constructed VAP-Exos by conjugating VAP onto FSA-preconditioned human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell exosomes, which effectively restore BSCB integrity. Binding GRP78 to target endothelial cells, VAP-Exos upregulates tight junction proteins (ZO-1, Occludin, Claudin5) and lowers BSCB permeability. Single-nucleus sequencing proves they stimulate endothelial proliferation, elevate Itga5, and activate autophagy pathways; elevated autophagic flux is validated by increased LC3-II/I ratio and P62 degradation. Meanwhile, VAP-Exos alleviate oxidative stress, shift microglia toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, and rebalance the spinal immune microenvironment. In vivo assays on SCI mice show smaller lesions, attenuated glial scarring and recovered motor function. Collectively, VAP-Exos safeguard BSCB integrity through endothelial autophagy modulation, representing a promising engineered exosome candidate for SCI therapy.

title: Design implications of matrix composition and micro-galvanic interactions governing corrosion behavior in Al–Zn–Mg–(Cu) alloys
abstract: The effects of aging treatment and Cu addition on the corrosion behavior of Al–Zn–Mg alloys were systematically investigated via mechanical, electrochemical, and microstructural analyses. Aging enhanced strength through η-phase precipitation and reduced Zn and Mg in the matrix, thus causing a noble shift in corrosion potential and a decrease in corrosion current density. By contrast, Cu addition increased the corrosion potential but significantly increased the corrosion current density, thereby indicating deteriorated corrosion resistance. The Base alloy exhibited passivation followed by pitting, whereas the High-Cu alloy showed active dissolution with virtually no passive regions. With increasing Cu content, the corrosion morphology evolved from pitting to grain boundaries and intragranular corrosion owing to a transition from anodic Zn–Mg precipitates to cathodic Cu-rich sites. These results reveal that corrosion behavior is governed by the relationship between matrix composition and micro galvanic interactions. Additionally, the findings provide design guidelines for optimizing the tradeoff between strength and corrosion resistance in high-strength Al alloys.

title: Multi-parameter acoustic emission analysis for damage evolution and mode identification in woven lattice sandwich-ply laminated panels
abstract: This study presents an acoustic emission (AE)-based approach for analyzing damage mechanisms in woven lattice sandwich-ply laminated panels (SLPs). Six types of SLPs, varying in sandwich-ply number and core orientation, were prepared and tested under edgewise compression. The digital image correlation revealed distinct deformation patterns of SLPs, including compression-bending coupling, global buckling. AE characteristic parameters were extracted and reduced to three principal components via factor analysis. Fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering was then applied to classify AE events, enabling identification of distinct damage modes. Three dominant damage mechanisms were revealed, including core shear failure, core fracture, and face fracture. The AE-based classifications were consistent with deformation patterns observed via digital image correlation method, including compression-bending coupling and global buckling, confirming the reliability of the approach. The proposed AE-FCM framework provides a technique for real-time monitoring and qualitative characterization of progressive damage in SLPs with multi-layered configuration.

title: Engineering strength-ductility balance in Ti-15Zr alloy with corrosion resistance
abstract: Titanium alloys are attractive materials, but achieving a balance between high strength and adequate ductility remains challenging. In this study, a two-pass cold drawing process with intermediate annealing was applied to a Ti-15Zr alloy. The microstructural evolution, characterized by EBSD and TEM, reveals a transition from a high-density dislocation substructure to a recrystallized coarse-grained state. As the annealing temperature increased from 350 to 450 °C, the tensile strength decreased from 1129 to 1049 MPa, while the elongation substantially increased from 7.7 % to 15.1 %. Notably, the 450 °C treatment provided an optimal recovery substructure, facilitating the formation of nanotwins during the subsequent cold drawing, which effectively impeded dislocation motion and preserved high strength while enhancing plasticity. When the annealing temperature reached 550 °C, significant grain growth occurred, leading to a sharp decrease in tensile strength. Electrochemical tests showed that fine grains enabled a denser passive film, CD-350 exhibited the highest corrosion resistance, followed by CD-450. All samples confirmed excellent cytocompatibility in vitro. Therefore, intermediate annealing at 450 °C enables the production of Ti-15Zr alloy with a superior strength-ductility balance, acceptable corrosion resistance, and satisfactory biocompatibility, making it a preferred material for dental implant applications.

title: TNF-α-pretreated GMSC-derived apoptotic vesicles promote diabetic skin wound healing by modulating macrophage polarization via the miR-146a-5p/TRAF6 axis
abstract: Diabetic skin wound healing is severely impeded by persistent inflammation dominated by M1 macrophages and an imbalance in macrophage polarization, making the modulation of inflammation and restoration of polarization balance a key therapeutic strategy. Apoptotic vesicles (apoVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) show promise in tissue repair, yet the influence of donor cell inflammatory preconditioning on their biological functions remains unclear. This study compared apoVs from TNF‑α‑pretreated (i‑apoVs) and normal (n‑apoVs) gingival MSCs, which were isolated, characterized, and loaded into GelMA hydrogels for sustained release. In a diabetic rat skin defect model, i‑apoVs significantly accelerated wound closure, promoted re‑epithelialization, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis, and induced a shift from pro‑inflammatory M1 to reparative M2 macrophages. In vitro, i‑apoVs were more potent than n‑apoVs in driving LPS‑stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages toward M2 polarization, as evidenced by decreased iNOS and CD86 and increased Arg‑1 and CD206. miRNA sequencing identified miR‑146a‑5p enrichment in i‑apoVs, which directly targets TRAF6 to inhibited NF‑κB activation and promoted M2 polarization. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that i‑apoVs enhance diabetic wound healing by delivering miR‑146a‑5p to macrophages, regulating the TRAF6/NF‑κB axis and rebalancing macrophage phenotypes, providing a novel cell‑free strategy for diabetic wound therapy.

title: A novel immersion chemical–mechanical synergistic polishing method for precision GCr15 gear finishing
abstract: Traditional planar chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) cannot achieve uniform finishing on complex curved gear surfaces. This paper develops an immersion chemical–mechanical synergistic polishing (ICMSP) method for GCr15 gear. A force-coupled material removal model is established to predict material removal rate. Optimized experiments reduce surface roughness Ra from 0.867 μm to 0.416 μm within 0.5 h. Combined with MD simulation, XPS and FTIR characterizations, the chemical–mechanical polishing mechanism is clarified: H 2 O 2 generates Fe/Cr oxide films, acid dissolves the brittle oxide layer, and SiC abrasives strip softened products. XPS results verify the formation of iron and chromium oxides/hydroxides on the tooth surface. Compared with conventional gear grinding, ICMSP delivers better surface quality and higher efficiency, offering a new route for precision gear finishing.

title: Effect of rolling direction pre-deformation on microstructure and mechanical properties of aluminum-lithium alloys
abstract: Third-generation Al-Li alloys are highly valued in aerospace for their excellent specific strength, with the T 1 (Al 2 CuLi) as the key strengthening precipitate. This study integrates first-principles calculations with systematic experiments to investigate rolling-direction pre-deformation in an Al-Li-Cu-Mg-X alloy. DFT calculations reveal a negative T 1 /Al interfacial energy of −0.81 eV/Å 2 , indicating thermodynamic stability, and a stronger segregation tendency of Cu atoms at dislocations of −0.32 eV compared to −0.18 eV for Li, which promotes T 1 formation. Composition screening identifies Al-0.1Sc-0.2Zr as optimal, achieving a tensile strength of 408.96 MPa after aging. Pre-deformation tests from 1 % to 8 % show that 3 % pre-deformation yields the best properties, with a tensile strength of 508.14 MPa and Vickers hardness of 151 Hv. Excessive deformation above 4 % leads to property degradation due to dislocation tangles, precipitate coarsening, and micro-void formation. This work elucidates the non-linear impact of pre-deformation and identifies 3 % as the optimal processing window for high-performance Al-Li alloys.

title: Corrigendum to “Development of pH-responsive and antibacterial semi-IPN hydrogel films based on carboxymethylcellulose and tetraethyl orthosilicate” [Mater. Des. 269 (2026) 116717]
Microstructural and phase evolution of BaTiO3–BaO–B2O3–Bi2O3 glass composites during pressureless and spark plasma sintering
abstract: BaTiO 3 –BaO–B 2 O 3 –Bi 2 O 3 (BBB) glass composites were investigated to clarify how BBB content and sintering route control low-temperature densification, pore evolution, glass-derived phase redistribution, and crystalline phase development. Densification was assessed using 15 and 30 wt% BBB glass with pressureless sintering (PS) at 600–800 °C and spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 500–800 °C. Monolithic BaTiO 3 exhibited limited densification at 800 °C, suggesting that solid-state diffusion was inadequate for consolidation. The addition of BBB facilitated the formation of a transient liquid phase, enhancing glass softening and pore filling. Densification improved with temperature and BBB content under PS, although residual porosity remained, particularly for 15 wt% BBB. SPS significantly modified microstructural evolution, achieving a relative density of 98.28% for 30 wt% BBB at 800 °C due to SPS-assisted liquid redistribution. SEM analysis revealed a shift from interconnected pores to isolated pinholes, with Bi-rich BBB regions redistributing in the BaTiO 3 framework. Tetragonal BaTiO 3 was the primary crystalline phase, while 30 wt% BBB, after SPS, formed secondary borate phases. These results establish a processing–microstructure–phase relationship for BaTiO 3 –BBB glass composites and show that BBB-assisted SPS enables low-temperature densification.

title: A novel magnesium alloy-based drug delivery system loaded with marine-derived CHNQD-00603 for synergistic corrosion resistance and autophagy-driven bone regeneration
abstract: The reconstruction of critical-sized bone defects, particularly in craniomaxillofacial and orthopedic surgery, remains a formidable clinical challenge. While biodegradable magnesium alloys hold great promise as barrier materials for such applications, their clinical utility is severely limited by a mismatch between their rapid degradation rate and the natural bone healing cycle. To address this challenge, we designed a multifunctional drug delivery system on AZ31 alloy comprising a micro-arc oxidation (MAO) base and a silane-sealed intermediate layer (PAPTMS) loaded with etidronate (ETN) and a novel marine-derived compound named CHNQD-00603. This hierarchical MAO/PAPTMS-ETN-603 coating exhibits a dense structure that significantly mitigates degradation rates while ensuring sustained drug release. In vitro evaluations confirmed that the coating not only supports the adhesion and proliferation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells but also enhances osteogenic differentiation by activating autophagy. Furthermore, in vivo assessment in a rabbit calvarial defect model demonstrated that the composite coating significantly accelerates new bone formation. This study establishes a promising strategy for developing novel bioactive barrier membranes that synergistically manage corrosion and drive tissue repair via autophagy-mediated osteogenesis.

title: Mechanism of abnormal microstructural degradation in TP347HFG steel induced by service/peak-shaving operation
abstract: The abnormal σ-phase precipitation (occurring considerably ahead of schedule) results in microstructural degradation and deterioration of mechanical properties in TP347HFG austenitic heat-resistant steel during service or peak-shaving operation of USC units leads to microstructural aging and degradation of mechanical properties. In this study, TP347HFG steel tubes that had served in a power plant for six years were investigated. Using SEM, TEM, EBSD, in situ tensile testing, and finite element simulation, the precipitation behavior, distribution, and influence on mechanical properties of the σ-phase were systematically studied. The results show that the σ-phase preferentially nucleates at triple grain boundaries. The majority of the σ-phase exists as dispersed particles, which are incoherent with the austenite matrix. However, it is also noted that a portion of the σ-phase may develop a semi-coherent interface with the austenite matrix on one side of the grain boundary. The precipitation of the σ-phase is temperature-sensitive, with a significantly higher content in the outer wall region (where the temperature is higher) than in the inner wall region. Moreover, with increasing σ-phase content, the elongation of the specimens decreases markedly. Texture evolution indicates that < 111>//RD and < 001>//RD are stable orientations, and grains preferentially rotate toward these directions during deformation to coordinate plastic deformation. During in situ tensile testing, a high density of GNDs generated at the interfaces between the σ-phase and the matrix, serving as preferential sites for microcrack initiation. Meanwhile, slip bands blocked at grain boundaries also induce microcracks. When the stress exceeds the ultimate strength, pre-existing cracks rapidly connect with microcracks along slip bands and around the σ-phase, leading to fracture. This study reveals the embrittlement behavior of the σ-phase, providing a theoretical basis for life assessment and material optimization of heat-resistant materials in USC units.

title: Electroresponsive hyaluronic acid click hydrogels for combined antibacterial delivery and wound healing applications
abstract: The versatility of electroresponsive hyaluronic acid (HA)-based hydrogels, a promising platforms for wound healing, can be further extended to controlled drug delivery, enabling on-demand release of therapeutic agents. This work reports the development of advanced HA-based electroresponsive hydrogels incorporating electrospun poly(lactic acid) (PLA) fiber mats functionalized with conducting polymers (CPs), such as poly(hydroxymethyl-3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) and polypyrrole, and loaded with chloramphenicol (CAM). The systems were fabricated through a multi-step approach involving plasma treatment, in situ polymerization of CPs on the fiber mats, and then semi-interpenetration with CP within a click-chemistry crosslinked HA network. The resulting hybrid hydrogels exhibited suitable mechanical properties, swelling behavior, and electrochemical activity, enabling CAM release under both passive and controlled electrically stimulated conditions while maintaining biocompatibility. Electrical stimulation significantly enhanced the initial burst release, while the subsequent release phase showed a sustained profile over an extended period (11 days). The antibacterial activity of the released CAM was confirmed against E. coli and S. aureus using an agar diffusion assay. Although both CPs exhibited comparable CAM release behavior, the polypyrrole-based hydrogel demonstrated superior wound healing performance. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of electroresponsive HA-based composite hydrogels as smart wound dressings capable of controlled and sustained antibiotic delivery

title: Distinct origins of electric-field-axis and polarization-axis asymmetries in ferroelectric hysteresis
abstract: Ferroelectric hysteresis asymmetry critically influences switching stability, imprint, and preferential polarization states in nonvolatile electronic devices. However, hysteresis asymmetry is generally characterized only by horizontal loop shifts, partly because conventional polarization–electric-field measurements contain an integration-constant ambiguity that prevents independent evaluation of polarization-axis asymmetry. Here, we reveal that ferroelectric hysteresis asymmetry contains two physically distinct components by using pyroelectric hysteresis measurements that avoid this offset ambiguity. Congruent LiTaO 3 exhibits a pronounced electric-field-axis shift associated with defect-related internal bias, whereas near-stoichiometric LiTaO 3 exhibits pronounced polarization-axis asymmetry despite a small internal bias. Combined cycling experiments, sweep-field dependence, Rayleigh analysis, and piezoresponse force microscopy imaging identify domain-wall pinning and an unswitched polarization component as the origin of the polarization-axis asymmetry. In contrast, the electric-field-axis shift is governed primarily by a reconfigurable defect-related internal-bias state. These results demonstrate that ferroelectric hysteresis asymmetry should not be characterized solely by a horizontal loop-shift parameter and establish a framework for decoupling internal-bias and pinned-domain effects in ferroelectrics. The findings provide materials-design principles for improving switching reliability, imprint control, and polarization-state engineering in defect-engineered ferroelectrics.

title: Effects of outer coating thickness on the failure strength of a SiC-based nuclear-fuel cladding up to 1200°C
abstract: Continuous SiC fibre reinforced SiC matrix composites (SiC f -SiC m CMC) with monolithic SiC coatings are promising candidate accident-tolerant fuel cladding materials for light-water-reactors. Thick monolithic SiC coatings can increase failure strength and improve hermeticity, but may also suppress toughening mechanisms in the cladding system. Here, 2D fibre braided SiC f -SiC m cladding with thick inner and outer SiC coatings were examined, with outer-coating-thickness ranging from ∼240 to ∼440 μm. C-ring compression tests were performed up to 1200°C in Ar, combined with in-situ synchrotron X-ray micro-computed tomography and digital-volume-correlation (DVC) to quantify 3D strain distributions. All specimens exhibited brittle fracture initiated in the outer coating, consistent with localized tensile hoop strain measured by DVC. No obvious crack-deflection toughening at the coating/CMC interfaces was observed before failure. Within the limited six-specimen dataset, apparent nominal hoop strength and DVC-derived localized hoop strain showed a positive association with outer-coating-thickness. Because coating-thickness and testing temperature were not varied independently, this association is an indicative trend rather than a design allowable or general thickness–strength law. Newman–Raju calculations semi-quantitatively rationalized the thickness-associated trend in terms of surface-flaw stress intensity. These results highlight the designing need to balance coating thickness, CMC-layer fraction and interfacial strength.

title: Hot extrusion of Ni-based superalloy pipe: Constitutive model evaluation, process simulation, experimental study and recrystallization analysis
abstract: For the desired microstructure, the preparation of Ni-based superalloy pipe with unique properties via hot extrusion has always been a focus of attention. In this work, a more applicable unified model for describing the dynamic recrystallization behavior involving flow behavior and microstructure evolution was applied to the finite element (FE) simulation of the superalloy pipe during hot extrusion. Based on FE simulation, the innovative process window with grain size variation was established to facilitate the controllable microstructure of the Ni-based superalloy extruded pipe. Moreover, a commercial extruded pipe was prepared to verify the applicability of the window through considering the on-site condition. Moreover, through microstructural characterization of the extruded pipe, both discontinuous and continuous dynamic recrystallization mechanisms were identified during the extrusion process. The metadynamic recrystallization and static recrystallization mechanisms played a crucial role in the subsequent transport stage. Meanwhile, the identification of sub-grain formation within twins demonstrated that twinning facilitated the microstructural evolution. Furthermore, the Cube {100} < 001 > component was determined as the dominant texture in the Ni-based superalloy extruded pipe. The methods and findings proposed in this work provide a theoretical basis for the formability improvement and microstructural regulation of the extruded pipe of the Ni-based superalloy.

title: Auxetic behavior and viscoelasticity of GO membrane: Influence of Al3+ modification
abstract: Mechanical reinforcement of graphene oxide (GO) membranes via metal cation modification enhances strength and stiffness, yet its coupling with emergent 3D-auxeticity and viscoelastic damping remains unexplored. This study investigates the fundamental mechanical response of GO membranes through tailoring Al 3+ coordination. Using an integrated in-situ framework of 3D-digital image correlation and X-ray diffraction, we identify a unique 3D-auxetic response characterized by a macroscopic negative Poisson’s ratio as low as −0.625. We demonstrate that this behavior originates from a lattice-scale “interlayer puffing” mechanism, where uniaxial tension drives out-of-plane expansion. While Al 3+ intercalation reinforces the membrane—enhancing both Young’s modulus and tensile strength—it simultaneously “pins” the wrinkled architecture, yielding a stabilized, albeit heterogeneous, auxetic framework. Furthermore, Al 3+ modification triggers a dramatic 188 % increase in damping capacity. This enhanced energy dissipation is captured by a “hard-filler/soft-segment” viscoelastic model, wherein ionic cross-links function as dynamic, energy-dissipating bridges. These insights establish a constitutive link between coordination chemistry and multiscale mechanics, providing a blueprint for designing GO-based systems that combine structural rigidity with extreme energy dissipation and tunable 3D-auxeticity.

title: PCL-HAMA-Sema3A scaffold promotes bone regeneration
abstract: Abstract A 3D-printed polycaprolactone (PCL) scaffold was combined with hyaluronic acid methacrylate (HAMA) hydrogel carrying Semaphorin-3A (Sema 3A) to create an implantable PCL-HAMA-Sema 3A construct for critical-size bone defects. PCL provided robust mechanical support and interconnected macropores, while HAMA overcame PCL’s hydrophobicity and enabled sustained Sema 3A release. Sema3A orchestrates bone homeostasis via the neuropilin-1/plexin-A holoreceptor. It simultaneously drives osteoblast differentiation through Wnt/β-catenin activation and suppresses osteoclastogenesis by disrupting RANKL/RANK signaling. Sema3A scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) and shifts macrophages from the M1 to the M2 phenotype, thereby mitigating inflammation and preventing oxidative and inflammatory bone loss. Additionally, it enhances angiogenesis by up-regulating VEGF. Collectively, Sema3A couples osteogenesis, anti-resorption, anti-oxidation and vascularization, offering a multi-target therapeutic strategy for critical bone defects.

title: Effect of surface topography induced by cavitation Jet, laser cladding and hammer peening on epoxy adhesion of 7075 aluminum alloy
abstract: This study addresses the insufficient coating adhesion of 7075 aluminum alloy in eco-friendly marine anti-corrosion coatings, and investigates the influences of cavitation jet, laser cladding and machine hammer peening on substrate micromorphology and bonding strength of epoxy primer. Within the investigated processing conditions, the coating bonding strength did not increase monotonically with surface roughness, indicating that roughness magnitude alone was insufficient to explain the observed adhesion behavior. Under optimal parameters, cavitation jet treatment produces uniform micro-pits on the substrate, achieving a maximum bonding strength of 8.9 MPa with excellent stability, whereas laser cladding readily causes local stress concentration. A dimensionless morphological factor Rt/Ra is proposed to define the optimal surface topography. In the present dataset, specimens with Ra values of approximately 50–60 μm and Rt/Ra values of approximately 5.0–6.5 exhibited relatively high adhesion strength. These empirical ranges may be associated with differences in surface-feature scale and uniformity; however, resin wettability and interfacial stress distribution were not directly measured in this study. This work establishes a model correlating microscopic morphology with macroscopic failure mechanisms, providing theoretical basis and technical guidance for the optimization of coating pretreatment processes.

title: Microstructure-property relationships in recycled polyethylene terephthalate particle-modified glass/epoxy composites
abstract: Waste polyester textiles require higher-value recycling routes that retain material functionality without energy-intensive chemical processing. Mechanically decomposed waste-PET fragments with a larger S1 particle (median ≈ 209 μm) and a smaller S2 fraction (<100 μm) were incorporated into glass-fabric/epoxy laminates (GF/EP-PET) and particle-filled epoxy composites (EP-PET). Surface coverage, cross-sectional apparent porosity, SEM/EDS morphology, tensile behavior, non-failure bending up to 60°, and Charpy impact strength were evaluated. S2 at 2.5 wt% provided the best overall GF/EP-PET response, increasing tensile strength by 20.0% and 25.5% and elongation at break by 43.1% and 48.9% in the warp and weft directions, respectively; the weft bending stiffness increased by 27.8%. By contrast, S2 at 3.75 wt% increased porosity to 5.799% and reduced tensile strength by approximately 53%. For EP-PET, S1 at 1.25 wt% achieved the highest impact strength of 10.249 mJ/mm 2 , corresponding to a 172.4% increase over particle-free epoxy. The results demonstrate an application-dependent optimum governed by competition between particle-mediated energy dissipation and defect-assisted crack propagation. This method provides a novel, convenient, and environmentally friendly approach for using recycled PET particles as sustainable secondary fillers in customized epoxy based composite materials.

title: Nanoconjugated caffeic acid-gold nanoparticles for passive diffusion of simulated blood-brain barrier and neuroprotective activity
abstract: Efficient transport of antioxidant therapeutics across brain-associated barriers remains a major challenge for neuroprotective strategies. Here, we report caffeic acid–functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs–CA) engineered to enhance passive diffusion and provide intrinsic redox activity. Monodisperse ∼ 12 nm AuNPs were synthesized and covalently conjugated with caffeic acid, yielding stable nanoconjugated systems that retained the catechol–quinone redox interconversion essential for antioxidant function. Transport properties were evaluated using a non-cellular, electrospun PMMA–gelatin scaffold designed as a simplified passive-diffusion model that mimics selected structural features of the blood–brain barrier. AuNPs–CA exhibited controlled release of caffeic acid under enzymatic degradation and demonstrated significantly improved diffusion compared to free CA. SH-SY5Y neuronal-like cells showed high viability upon exposure to the nanoconjugated systems and also preserved their normal morphology. Antioxidant assays confirmed strong radical-scavenging activity, indicating that the conjugation strategy maintains the redox functionality of caffeic acid. These findings establish AuNPs–CA as a dual-function nanoplatform that couples enhanced passive diffusion through a simulated barrier with robust neuroprotective properties, supporting their potential utility in future therapeutic approaches targeting oxidative stress–related neurodegenerative conditions.

title: A systematic review on interlocking structures to enhance dissimilar materials joining by additive manufacturing
abstract: Multi-material systems are increasingly pursued to meet industrial demands for lightweight, high-performance structures. However, reliable joining remains critical. In recent years, mechanical interlocking has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome limitations of conventional joining methods such as adhesive bonding, mechanical fastening, and welding. By exploiting the geometric freedom of Additive Manufacturing (AM), interlocking structures can be directly integrated into the interface, enabling new opportunities for multi-material integration. Yet, the literature remains fragmented and lacks transferable design principles. This study reframes AM-enabled interlocking as a design-driven interface strategy and, through a PRISMA-guided literature review, introduces a unified design-material-process-performance mapping of the field. Interlocking structures are classified across scales as micro-features, macro-pins, and macro-lattices, and further interpreted through a common set of mechanism-based descriptors. These design categories are then examined alongside dominant material combinations, AM and joining processes, reported mechanical response and failure modes. Sector-specific requirements in aerospace, mobility, biomedical, robotics, and electronics applications are mapped onto the proposed framework, and the main barriers to industrial uptake – lack of standardization, limited non-destructive inspection, scalability, and sustainability – are translated into concrete research directions.

title: Bioinspired wrinkled wCNT@PS/PDMS composites for electromagnetic absorption and dynamic buffering
abstract: Inspired by dehydration-induced wrinkling in fruits, a bioinspired wCNT@PS/PDMS composite was fabricated by embedding wrinkled CNT-coated PS spheres into a PDMS matrix. Thermally induced shrinkage generates hierarchical wrinkles on sphere surfaces, which may increase effective surface roughness, facilitate CNT network reconstruction, and provide heterogeneous interfaces for electromagnetic attenuation. The electromagnetic loss characteristics of wCNT@PS sphere assemblies were evaluated by coaxial ring measurements, while the bulk composite was evaluated by free-space measurements, achieving a minimum reflection loss of –22.10 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 7.10 GHz. The composite exhibits typical three-stage compression behavior under quasi-static loading and pronounced strain-rate sensitivity under dynamic compression (2000–3500 s −1 ), with an energy absorption density approximately twice that of pure PDMS. The wrinkled CNT framework and PDMS matrix contribute to impact-energy dissipation through sphere deformation, interfacial interaction, and viscoelastic deformation, while retaining overall structural continuity after dynamic loading. Compared with reported lightweight electromagnetic absorbers, the wCNT@PS/PDMS composite achieves a balanced combination of broadband electromagnetic absorption, dynamic buffering, and structural stability. This work provides a bioinspired design strategy for lightweight integrated absorption-protection materials through coupling hierarchical electromagnetic structures with mechanically adaptive polymer matrices.

title: CO2 carbonation in cementitious systems: a multiscale review based on atomistic simulations
abstract: Carbon mineralization in calcium-rich cementitious materials is a promising route to permanent CO 2 sequestration that can simultaneously enhance material performance, yet a unified mechanistic picture spanning length scales is still lacking. This review develops one by integrating density functional theory, classical molecular dynamics, and reactive force-field simulations with experimental observations. Carbonation is analysed sequentially—from CO 2 adsorption and activation at mineral surfaces, through Ca 2+ release and transport in nanoscale pores, to the nucleation, growth, and polymorphic transformation of CaCO 3 —for the principal precursor phases: portlandite, calcium silicate hydrate, and unhydrated clinker minerals. Across these phases, the atomistic evidence converges on a single organising principle: carbonation is governed by the coupling of CO 2 transport, calcium availability, and interfacial reaction kinetics, whose local balance, rather than any single rate, determines the outcome. Carbonation is therefore better regarded as window-controlled than rate-controlled, with the competition between densification and decalcification governing CO 2 -utilization efficiency and long-term performance. This structure–transport–reaction framework links atomistic structure to macroscopic behaviour and provides a mechanistic basis for the rational design of CO 2 -efficient, high-performance cement-based materials.

title: Adaptive horizons in 4D printing: stimuli-responsive materials, computational intelligence, biomedical translation, and sustainable futures
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) printing has emerged as a transformative paradigm in additive manufacturing that uniquely incorporates time as the fourth dimension, extending static three-dimensional constructs into dynamic, stimuli-responsive architectures capable of programmed evolution over time. Unlike conventional 3D printing, which produces static geometries, 4D printing creates adaptive structures with programmability, temporal functionality, and reconfigurability that enable active interaction with their environment.This review critically synthesizes advances across seven interconnected domains: theoretical foundations, material innovations, fabrication modalities, biomedical translation, computational intelligence, reproducibility and ethical accountability, and sustainability with future directions. Stimuli-responsive materials, including shape memory polymers, liquid crystal elastomers, hydrogels, ceramics, metals, and cell-laden biomaterials, provide diverse actuation pathways, while fabrication strategies such as digital light processing, two-photon polymerization, direct ink writing, extrusion-based printing, and bioprinting translate these capabilities into functional constructs. Biomedical applications demonstrate translational potential, achieving > 90% cell viability and vascularization within seven days across tissue engineering, implantable devices, and drug delivery platforms. Recent advances in 4D-printed cardiac occluders, vascular stents, intestinal stents, and patient-specific surgical guides further underscore the clinical relevance of this technology. Computational intelligence accelerates design cycles via machine learning, topology optimization, and multi-physics simulations, achieving prediction accuracies above 90% and design cycle reductions exceeding 50%. Reliability and reproducibility frameworks safeguard scientific integrity, while ethical considerations, including informed consent, data privacy, and equitable access, ensure responsible biomedical translation. Sustainability is advanced through recyclable resins, eco-friendly energy devices, and bioinspired composites, while emerging cell contractile force-mediated actuation opens new frontiers in biologically driven morphogenesis. Despite these achievements, critical challenges persist in scalability, high-throughput biofabrication, and standardized evaluation frameworks-gaps that this review systematically addresses. By integrating adaptive materials, computational design, and ethical accountability, 4D printing redefines the boundaries of manufacturing and sets the stage for next-generation technological innovation in personalized medicine, sustainable infrastructure, and intelligent functional devices.

title: Cracking mechanisms of teeth models with pre-existing V-shaped fissures: A combined 3D printing and discrete element study
abstract: Tooth fracture is a prevalent clinical disease in dental hard tissues. Understanding crack propagation and fracture mechanisms under occlusal loads is crucial for early warning and restoration. This study systematically investigates the effects of V-shaped fissure geometry on the failure behavior of standardized dental models using 3D printing tests with digital image correlation (DIC) monitoring and discrete element simulations using the particle flow code (PFC2D). Results indicate that geometric parameters significantly regulate bearing capacity and failure characteristics. For fixed fissure length, peak load decays nonlinearly with increasing inclination angle α, with a critical drop of 29.5% when α increases from 45° to 60°, accompanied by a 29.3% reduction in maximum displacement over the same interval. For fixed fissure angle, bearing capacity exhibits a non-monotonic trend, first increasing then decreasing with fissure length l . Both experiments and simulations reveal a tensile-shear composite mechanism, where wing tensile cracks initiate at fissure tips, followed by secondary shear cracks from the flanks. High inclination angles ( α = 75°) or large lengths ( l = 20 mm) shorten the stable propagation stage and prematurely trigger anti-wing cracks, leading to networked coalescence and instantaneous brittle instability. Meso-mechanically, exceeding thresholds ( α = 60° or l = 20 mm) transforms uniformly distributed strong force chains and principal stresses into localized convergence at fissure tips, forming oriented load-bearing channels that dominate post-peak failure. Under asymmetric long fissures ( l = 25 mm), preferential cracking at the longer left side exhibits a unique pre-peak strengthening stage and prolonged load maintenance. These findings elucidate biomechanical weakening mechanisms and provide micro-meso foundations for clinical prevention and restoration.

title: Effect of cell wall architecture on stiffness and microstresses in softwoods: microstructure generation and finite element modeling
abstract: The geometrical features of softwood's cellular microstructure determine its mechanical clearwood properties, particularly the transversal properties perpendicular to the grain. These structure-property links are usually modeled using analytical mean-field homogenization schemes or unit cell models, which, however, cannot capture the stochastic geometric variations inherent to naturally grown softwood.To address this gap, we first developed a fully parameterizable softwood microstructure generator for the transveral plane. Distortion maps with Gaussian smoothing are used to transform an initially regular grid into stochastically varying grids, from which realistic wood cell architectures are reconstructed using Bézier curves. Next, hundreds of these cellular geometries were translated to finite element meshes and modeled using generalized periodic boundary conditions, applicable to the generated non-periodic clearwood structures. Systematic sensitivity studies revealed that irregularities in cell geometry moderately reduce the effective stiffness but strongly increase microstress concentrations in both the middle lamella and the secondary cell wall, compared to a structure with perfect geometry. Moreover, different stochastic realizations of the same microstructural parameter set lead to noticeable variations in mechanical behavior, highlighting the importance of stochastic geometry for microstructure-based modeling of softwood.

title: Substrate geometry and edge effect on microstructure in axial SPPS YSZ coatings: experimental and modeling insights
abstract: Axial-solution precursor plasma spraying (SPPS) has recently emerged as a promising route for producing columnar yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) thermal barrier coatings (TBCs). This study systematically investigates the effects of substrate size and geometry on the microstructure of axial SPPS-derived 8 wt% YSZ coatings. Systematic experimental characterization across flat (button and plate), concave, and convex geometries revealed a pronounced, size-independent “edge effect”. On flat substrates, a ∼ 5 mm transition zone occurs near sample edges where the columnar microstructure transforms into a denser, vertically cracked microstructure, characterised by lower porosity and higher microhardness. On concave substrates, this transition zone expands to ∼ 10 mm, whereas convex surfaces exhibit widespread vertically cracked microstructure. Three-dimensional Euler-Lagrangian CFD simulations demonstrate that local gas flow deflection near boundaries modifies particle axial velocity distributions. High-inertia particles (St ≫ 1) retain normal impact momentum near substrate edges to promoting dense, cracked-dominant regions, whereas fine particles (St ∼ 1) follow deflected gas streamlines to sustain columnar growth via shadowing. The simulated variations in particle deflection and normal-impact behavior were consistent with the experimentally observed transition. These results provide key insights for industrial implementation of SPPS technology on complex-shaped components.

title: Grain boundary segregation of tramp elements and embrittlement of scrap-based green steels
abstract: Growing reliance on scrap recycling in green steel production can increase concentrations of tramp elements like Sn, Sb, Cu, and Ni, which can degrade the mechanical performance of steels. This study examines tramp element effects in a 51CrV4 steel under simulated industrial processing conditions. Alloys with varying tramp element contents were quenched and tempered at 450°C and 650°C. Atom probe tomography and high-energy X-ray diffraction, supported by density functional theory calculations, were used to establish processing-structure-property relationships.Sn, Sb, and Cu were found to segregate to grain boundaries and to be primarily responsible for impact-toughness reductions of up to 60%. No measurable difference in segregation behavior was established between random high-angle and prior austenitic grain boundaries. Density functional theory supports these findings, showing that the combined effects of Cu, Sn, and Sb on grain-boundary cohesion are more detrimental than their individual contributions. Comparison of experimentally measured segregation enrichment with first-principles segregation energies demonstrates that ab initio calculations can reliably capture low-concentration segregation trends, except for elements involving interstitial grain-boundary positions. This study provides insights into the role of tramp elements in the embrittlement of modern steels and offers guidance for mitigating their effects in future scrap-based steel production.

title: A forming anisotropy CPFEM model of superalloys electroplasticity based on conductivity tensor
abstract: Electro-assisted forming (EAF) was widely applied for forming thin-walled superalloy components. However, temperature, stress, dislocation, and Taylor factor are affected under different current loading directions and amplitudes, which remains insufficiently explained. This study conducted electrically assisted uniaxial tensile tests of superalloy GH4169 sheets. Based on EBSD observations, the current direction significantly influences the transition of grain boundaries from low angles to high angles, forming a unique deformation polarity. Then, a multi-grain RVE model considering the property difference of grain boundaries and interiors was established. Besides, an anisotropic electrical conductivity tensor and current direction factor were established. Based on this, a CPFEM (crystal plasticity finite element method) model was developed to describe the forming anisotropy. Furthermore, under various current directions and amplitudes, the evolution of temperature and dislocation density, as well as the variation of stress–strain curves and Taylor factor, were analyzed. This study provides a novel perspective for expanding the theoretical framework and an insightful interpretation of EAF applications.

title: Romosozumab-engineered 3D-BMSC Apoptotic Extracellular Vesicles to synergistically alleviate inflammation and enhance osteoporosis treatment by activating Wnt/β‑catenin pathway
abstract: The pathogenesis of osteoporosis (OP) is complex and multifactorial, and current treatment options are largely limited to single-target agents with modest efficacy. Romosozumab (Rom) is a monoclonal antibody for sclerostin (SOST), and exerts dual regulatory effects on bone remodeling. However, its clinical application remains significantly restricted due to potential cardiovascular safety risks and suboptimal therapeutic efficacy compromised by inflammatory microenvironment. To enhance the efficacy and bone-targeting capacity of Rom, we developed Rom-engineered 3D apoptotic extracellular vesicles (Rom@3D-AEV). In the osteoporotic inflammatory microenvironment, Rom@3D-AEV were cleaved by overexpressed MMP-9, releasing Rom and miR-10b-5p-enriched 3D-AEV, which synergistically restored bone homeostasis and suppressed inflammation through the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. In addition, Rom@3D-AEV may accumulate within BMSCs in inflamed osteoporotic bone, potentially involving integrin αvβ3, thereby alleviating bone loss and delaying the progression of OP. Notably, compared with free Rom, Rom@3D-AEV reduced serum cTnI levels and no obvious vascular calcification was observed in OVX mice. Beyond providing a superior therapeutic option for OP, this work establishes a versatile bone-targeted delivery platform for precision treatment of skeletal disorders.

title: Hydrogel particles under uniaxial compression: Tetrapod-based DEM approach and experimental validation
abstract: Hydrogels are soft, water-rich polymer networks whose mechanical behavior governs applications from biomedicine to packed bed processes. In aerogel manufacturing, hydrogel particles represent an intermediate state in which mechanical stability determines scalability and process reliability. However, predictive particle-scale models for deformable matrix-fluid systems remain limited. Biopolymer-based hydrogel particles are investigated under uniaxial compression through monotonic, cyclic, and stress-relaxation experiments at compression rates of 0.1-3.0 mm/s. Apparent stiffness increased strongly with rate, followed by saturation above 0.5 mm/s, where the apparent Young’s modulus became rate independent. Within the elastic regime, the response is reproducible and hysteretic, whereas higher strains induced plastic deformation. Aging over one year led to additional stiffening, indicating ongoing structural evolution. To complement the experiments, a novel discrete-element-method framework based on tetrapod-shaped parcels is introduced. Tetrapods qualitatively represent the 3D polymer network and predominantly carry mechanical loads, while embedded spheres mimic the aqueous phase. Parameters are calibrated using a full-factorial design and Bayesian optimization. Simulations reproduce the force–strain response, apparent elastic properties, and particle deformation. Random packings produce comparable scatter, while stress relaxation and cyclic loading are reproduced qualitatively. The approach advances predictive modeling of deformable particles and provides a basis for solvent exchange and process-scale simulations.

title: Evaluation of high-temperature properties of binary, eutectic Ni-X alloys (X = B, Ca, Ce, La, Y, Zr)
abstract: We investigated the high-temperature behavior of binary eutectic nickel-base alloys with low-solubility elements, towards developing alloys with new combinations of structural and functional (e.g. thermal or corrosion) properties. Based on thermodynamic screening, we cast binary near-eutectic Ni-B, Ni-Ca, Ni-Ce, Ni-La, Ni-Y, and Ni-Zr alloys and characterized their microstructure and high-temperature properties. All alloys (except Ni-Ca) contain a fine eutectic microstructure, containing submicron alternating lamellae of γ-Ni and continuous intermetallic phases. The eutectic microstructure did not significantly coarsen at 700°C (except for Ni-B), but measurably coarsened in all alloys at 900°C, most quickly in Ni-B, followed by Ni-Ce, Ni-La, Ni-Y, and Ni-Zr. Coarsening in these alloys occurs by fault migration; diffusion within the intermetallic, and its interfacial energy, likely influence coarsening kinetics. At room-temperature, all alloys possess negligible ductility due to the continuous, brittle intermetallic. At 700 and 900°C, the Ni-Zr alloy showed the best combination of strength and ductility. Oxidation experiments at 900°C on Ni-Zr and Ni-Ce revealed heavy internal oxidation of the continuous intermetallic phase. Overall, the Ni-Zr alloy showed good high-temperature coarsening resistance and strength, though ductility and oxidation resistance require improvement for use in structural applications. Possible routes for improving alloy properties via additive manufacturing are discussed

title: An Esculetin Nanoparticle-Loaded hydrogel system for treating atopic dermatitis
abstract: To address the need for topical therapies with enhanced skin penetration and retention for infantile atopic dermatitis (AD), we screened esculetin (Esc), an active monomer from traditional Chinese medicine, in a cellular AD model. Esc demonstrated pronounced anti-inflammatory activity. Subsequently, a self-assembled nanogel delivery system, Esc@(HAP/PSI)-gel, was engineered using hydroxyapatite (HAP) and polysuccinimide (PSI) for sustained release. The optimized nanoparticles were spherical (Average diameter: 156 nm, zeta potential: −15.7 mV) with pH-responsive drug release. Compared with Esc-gel, Esc@(HAP/PSI)-gel significantly enhanced skin permeation and drug retention without inducing irritation. In AD mice, Esc@(HAP/PSI)-gel alleviated skin lesions, reduced ear swelling, lowered the spleen index, attenuated epidermal/dermal thickening, suppressed inflammatory cell infiltration, and modulated key cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IgE) more effectively than Esc-gel. Hence, the HAP/PSI-based nanogel delivery system enables the efficient and sustained delivery of Esc, enhances transdermal absorption, and demonstrates considerable therapeutic potential for AD.

title: First-order computational homogenization of arterial media with solid-embedded fibers: Homogenized and micromechanical responses
abstract: Arterial response emerges from interactions among collagen, elastin, smooth muscle cells, and ground matrix, but macroscopic models resolve these mechanisms only indirectly. We propose a first-order computational homogenization framework based on a solid-embedded-fiber representative volume element (RVE) coupled to a macroscopic finite element problem. Four configurations combine two fiber-tracing strategies with linear boundary displacement or periodic microscale constraints. All four produce comparable homogenized responses and reveal phase-specific behavior unavailable from effective curves alone. Collagen dominates homogenized stress, while local fields show heterogeneous and asymmetric load transfer between fibers and matrix. Periodic constraints slightly reduce peak stresses, broaden local stress and strain distributions, and increase solution times. Recruitment-window parameters most strongly influence nonlinear stiffening, followed by collagen stiffness and volume fraction. Similar homogenized responses can hide local-field differences caused by fiber topology and boundary conditions. The nested FE 2 framework links each macroscopic point to an embedded-fiber RVE during equilibrium. This coupling supports complex problems and constituent viscoelasticity, damage, fiber failure, or rupture because the local deformation path need not be known beforehand. Microscale boundary conditions must be selected in advance to produce a representative RVE response. Constituent-specific data remain necessary for validation.

title: Refining immiscible microstructure and enhancing tribological performance of HCWRS/Cu composite coatings via laser oscillation
abstract: A novel strategy utilizing laser oscillation technology was used to fabricate Cu composite coatings reinforced by high carbides wear-resistant steel (HCWRS). The influences of laser oscillation frequency from 0 to 150 Hz on the microstructure evolution, interface characteristics, and tribological properties under electrical contact conditions were systematically investigated. The results indicate that laser oscillation significantly refined the immiscible microstructure. At an optimal frequency of 100 Hz, the HCWRS/Cu composite coating exhibits a bimodal microstructure with nanoscale HCWRS particles dispersed within Cu-rich region and a metallurgical bonding interface, attributed to the enhanced Marangoni convection and element diffusion. Consequently, the coating fabricated at 100 Hz demonstrated superior properties of the highest microhardness of 125.8 HV 0.2 , nanohardness of 2.42 GPa and the lowest wear rate of 1.32 × 10 −7 mm 3 ⋅N −1 ⋅mm −1 at 2 A current. This work highlights that laser oscillation is an effective method to refine the microstructure and enhance the performance of the immiscible Cu-Fe based composite coatings

title: Effect of ultra-high-frequency induction aging on the hardness and dry sliding wear behaviour of graphene-SiC reinforced Al 7xxx hybrid composites
abstract: In this study, Al 7xxx matrix hybrid composites reinforced with 10, 15, and 20 wt% SiC and 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 wt% graphene were fabricated by powder metallurgy and subjected to conventional and ultra-high-frequency induction system (UHFIS) processing routes. The hybrid composites were evaluated in terms of densification, hardness, microstructure, strengthening mechanisms, and dry sliding wear behaviour. Among the investigated compositions, the 7.1.10 hybrid composite reinforced with 10 wt% SiC and 0.1 wt% graphene provided the most favourable overall combination of relative density and hardness. The relative density of this composition reached 97.22% after conventional aging and 98.30% after induction-assisted aging, while its hardness increased from 100.1 ± 3.50 to 157.2 ± 2.95 HBW. The 7.1.10 hybrid composite exhibited the lowest wear loss under both aging routes, and the specific wear rate decreased by approximately 56%, from 1.304 × 10 −6 to 5.731 × 10 −7 cm 3 /N·m after UHFIS aging. The lowest friction coefficient was obtained in the 7.3.10 hybrid composite, with values of 0.36 after conventional aging and 0.34 after UHFIS aging, which is consistent with a solid-lubricating contribution of graphene during dry sliding. UHFIS reduced the total thermal-processing duration from 900 to 13 min while simultaneously improving hardness, densification, and wear resistance.

title: Piezoelectric-powered osseointegration and photothermal-driven infection defense: a dual-functional BCG nanocomposite coating for dental implants
abstract: Titanium (Ti) implants, though clinically prevalent for dentition restoration, suffer from insufficient osteogenic activity and lack of antibacterial properties. The role of bioelectricity in bone homeostasis suggests that piezoelectric materials which generate micro-electric fields via mechanical stimuli (e.g., mastication) may be able to promote osseointegration. Herein, thiolated barium titanate-chitosan-graphene oxide nanoparticles (BCG-NPs) were fabricated, as well as grafted onto Ti through polydopamine (PDA). BCG-Ti exhibited good piezoelectric properties which allow it to convert mechanical force into electrical signals, inducing osteogenic differentiation of Human Umbilical Cord Wharton’s Jelly-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells (hWJ-MSCs) and M2 macrophage polarization, and thus improving bone regeneration. Moreover, BCG-Ti possessed excellent photothermal effect, and it demonstrated near-infrared (NIR) irradiation triggered localized hyperthermia for broad-spectrum bacterial eradication. By integrating bioelectric and photothermal modalities, this strategy establishes a pro-healing microenvironment, addressing key limitations of traditional implants to extend their functional lifespan.

title: Cover_269
Editorial Board
Piezoelectric materials: a new dawn in neural injury repair
abstract: Neural injuries affecting the peripheral and central nervous systems remain major clinical challenges because primary tissue disruption is followed by injury-specific secondary cascades, inhibitory extracellular environments, and limited circuit reconstruction. Piezoelectric biomaterials can convert physiological micromotion or externally applied ultrasound into localized electrical cues and therefore offer a self-powered route to combine structural repair with neuromodulation. This review critically compares natural, inorganic, organic, and composite piezoelectric systems in terms of piezoelectric coefficients, representative device-level outputs, mechanical compatibility, degradation, and biosafety. We first establish the physiological basis for bioelectric regulation in peripheral nerve injury (PNI), spinal cord injury (SCI), traumatic brain injury (TBI), and ischemic stroke, emphasizing the distinct cellular and electrophysiological requirements of each lesion. We then discuss rational engineering strategies, including structural alignment, compositional modification, interface engineering, and multifunctional integration, and relate these strategies to site-specific scaffold and activation requirements. Particular attention is given to controlling the catalytic activity of multiferroic materials, standardizing electromechanical characterization, and defining translational benchmarks for manufacturing, sterilization, long-term safety, and regulatory evaluation. Overall, piezoelectric materials are promising for neural injury repair, but clinically meaningful progress will require pathology-matched design and quantitative comparison rather than optimization of piezoelectric output alone.

title: Non-monotonic evolution of magnetization driven by grain boundary Cr-depletion and self-healing in austenitic stainless steel during long-term high-temperature service
abstract: This study investigates the microstructural and magnetic evolution of Super304H stainless steel subjected to high temperature at 605 ℃ service up to 100,000 h. Room-temperature saturation magnetization exhibits a non-monotonic trend, peaking at 53,000 h before significantly attenuating. This fluctuation is driven by Cr-rich M 23 C 6 carbide precipitation at grain boundaries, causing localized Cr-depletion and elevating the martensite start temperature (Ms). Consequently, cooling to room temperature induces ferromagnetic martensite formation. After 72,000 h, magnetization decreases as matrix Cr diffusion homogenizes boundary gradients, representing a “healing” mechanism that restores austenite stability. The subsequent precipitation of σ phase at the expense of M 23 C 6 has a negligible effect on magnetization due to sluggish kinetics. This research establishes a direct correlation between magnetic signatures and microstructural degradation, offering a novel framework for the non-destructive evaluation of austenitic stainless steels during long-term service.

title: Single-crystal β-Ti–42Nb fabricated via flat-top laser powder bed fusion: melt-pool stability–controlled cellular-dendritic growth
abstract: Single-crystal formation in a β-Ti–42wt.%Nb alloy fabricated via flat-top laser powder bed fusion was governed primarily by melt-pool stability, which was considerably influenced by laser scanning speed, without using single-crystal seeds. Under stable melt-pool conditions at low scanning speeds, multilayer single-crystal structures with 〈001〉//build direction (BD) and 〈100〉//scan direction/hatch direction (SD/HD) were obtained using a bidirectional scanning strategy with alternating HDs of 0° and 90°, accompanied by the suppression of both high- and low-angle grain boundaries. Within a single melt pool in the single-crystal region, [001]-oriented cellular-dendritic structures grew epitaxially from the underlying layer in the bottom region. Although 〈010〉- and 〈100〉-oriented structures formed near the melt-pool surface, repeated remelting during multilayer deposition removed these layers. As a result, a lower solidified region dominated by BD-oriented cellular-dendritic structures with short secondary arms extending along the HD remained. Due to the weak lateral thermal gradient along the HD, crystallographic alignment along the HD gradually converged with increasing build height, enabling single-crystal formation. In contrast, at high scanning speeds, unstable melt pools with asymmetric and laterally wandering morphologies disrupted epitaxial cellular-dendritic growth primarily along the HD. This resulted in weak 〈010〉 texture intensities along the SD/HD, thereby inhibiting single-crystal formation.

title: Apoptotic cell membrane-inspired particles for inflammation regulation
abstract: Chronic inflammatory disorders, particularly diabetic wounds, are characterized by persistent macrophage-mediated inflammation that delays tissue repair. Herein, we developed pH-responsive apoptotic cell membrane-inspired polymeric particles in which phosphatidylserine (PS) was temporarily shielded by polyethylene glycol (PEG) through an acid-labile Schiff base linkage to achieve inflammation-responsive activation. The PEG-PS particles were synthesized and characterized by NMR, GPC, DLS, and zeta potential measurements. Their pH-responsive behavior, macrophage uptake, and anti-inflammatory activity were evaluated in vitro, while therapeutic efficacy was assessed in a streptozotocin-induced diabetic wound model. Under acidic conditions, PEG shedding promoted PS exposure, resulting in enhanced macrophage uptake, significant inhibition of NF-κB activation and IL-6 production, together with reduced TNF-α and increased TGF-β1 expression. In vivo, PEG-PS particles significantly accelerated wound closure, reduced granulation tissue formation, enhanced collagen deposition, and improved histological healing compared with PS particles and untreated diabetic wounds. These findings demonstrate that pH-responsive PEG shielding provides controlled activation of PS-mediated immunomodulation and represents a promising strategy for inflammation regulation and diabetic wound healing.

title: Interfacial charge transfer driven enhancement of thermal properties and molecular dynamics insights into mechanical behavior of novel polyaniline/vanadium nitride nanocomposites
abstract: Understanding interfacial interactions in nanocomposite materials is essential for various technological applications. Here, we synthesize polyaniline (PANI)-vanadium nitride (VN) nanocomposites. Experimentally, we observe a 25 K increase in thermal degradation temperature ( T d ) and a 103 K increase in glass transition temperature ( T g ), corroborated by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) reveal strong interfacial attraction between PANI and VN. This attraction originates from type-II band alignment, which enables spontaneous electron transfer from VN to PANI. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) confirms complete nanoparticle encapsulation by the polymer matrix. Polymer diffusion decreases with increasing nanoparticle loading, consistent with the observed T d and T g trends. MD simulations further show that the nanoparticles alter the radius of gyration of polymer chains, leading to more compact packing and non-monotonic mechanical reinforcement. The nanocomposites exhibit improved thermal and mechanical stability, demonstrating an interfacial electronic structure engineering strategy validated by experiments, MD, and DFT.

title: ECM-inspired GHTA@CuS nanocomposite hydrogel for early skin-to-muscle tissue repair under 1064 nm photothermal stimulation
