abstract: Full-thickness skin-to-muscle injuries remain difficult to repair because restoration of multiple tissue layers requires coordinated control of inflammation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. In the current study, an ECM-inspired nanocomposite hydrogel (GHTA@CuS) was developed as a localized 1064 nm photothermal interface for early skin-to-muscle tissue repair. The hydrogel consisted of a gelatin–hyaluronic acid matrix containing tannic acid-stabilized Ag nanoparticles and CuS nanoparticles. In vitro testing demonstrated low hemolytic activity and short-term cytocompatibility, and ex vivo photothermal assessment supported the selection of 0.5 W/cm 2 for 1 min for in vivo treatment. In a rat skin-to-muscle wound model, the combined treatment with GHTA@CuS hydrogel and 1064 nm laser irradiation reduced the day-7 wound area to 0.02 ± 0.01 cm 2 compared with the untreated and laser-only groups and decreased neutrophil infiltration. Histological analysis revealed improved early organization and a greater area of muscle-like tissue. At day 7, the combined treatment was associated with increased ERK and AKT phosphorylation and changes in the expression of Ki67, COL1, and COL3. These findings support GHTA@CuS as a localized photothermal biomaterial interface for enhancing early repair of skin-to-muscle injuries.

title: Novel additive manufacturing method of ultra-high temperature ceramics: electron beam melt assisted in-situ synthesis of TiB2 – ZrB2 – TiC
abstract: Ultra-high temperature ceramics have gained increased interest in recent years due to their exceptional thermal and mechanical properties for applications in extreme environments such as advanced rocket propulsion, hypersonic aircraft, and materials for the nuclear sector. Additive manufacturing could allow for the fabrication of geometrically complex components reducing the cost and improving the design flexibility. This paper reports a novel technique for near net shape manufacturing of ultra-high temperature ceramics utilising a self-propagating high temperature synthesis in an electron beam melt system. The self-propagating high temperature synthesis reaction of Ti-B 4 C was modified by adding ZrB 2 dilutant to suppress the self-propagating behaviour, enabling near net shape manufacturing using a 3D printing method. A complex mix of zirconium and titanium borides and carbides was obtained as a result. Moderate beam currents (5–7.5 mA) yielded the most promising results, guiding future compositional and process optimisation.

title: Metastable five-fold twinning mediates chemical-order inheritance in high-entropy alloys
abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are multicomponent alloys with complex local chemical environments, in which phase-transformation pathways and their hidden structural consequences remain insufficiently understood. Here, we perform molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the crystallization behavior of a prototypical CoCrCuFeNi HEA. We identify a metastable five-fold twinning superstructure (MFTS) that competes with glass formation and the stable face-centered cubic (FCC) phase during solidification. The formation of MFTS is closely associated with local chemical segregation arising from the underlying many-body interatomic interactions, and its appearance leads to a non-classical crystallization pathway from the undercooled liquid to the stable crystal phase. We further show that MFTS exhibits spatially heterogeneous chemical ordering, part of which can be inherited by the final FCC phase during the subsequent transformation. Tensile simulations suggest that, under the present simulation conditions, the MFTS-containing structure may display a stronger mechanical response than a conventional polycrystal. These results provide atomistic insight into a previously underexplored metastable structural motif in HEAs and suggest a physically motivated, experimentally testable pathway linking metastable phase formation, chemical-order reorganization, and mechanical response.

title: Designing HA–PVA composite microneedles with synergistic mechanical reinforcement for deep skin MRSA biofilms: unveiling a new antimicrobial target
abstract: Deep skin MRSA biofilm infections are difficult to treat because the effective delivery of antimicrobial concentrations at deep skin is challenging. HcCATH-KL30 (CATH) – a novel Cathelicidin peptide isolated from sea snake have shown potential antimicrobial activity. However, hydrophilicity and high molecular weight (∼3.4 kDa) limit its permeation across skin making it unsuitable for conventional topical delivery. To overcome these problems, bilayer CATH dissolving microneedles (CATH-DMNs) were prepared from a mechanically reinforced composite matrix system of hyaluronic acid–polyvinyl alcohol (HA–PVA). The prepared microneedle system was characterized for morphology, mechanical properties, insertion studies, skin distribution, in-vitro, ex-vivo, in-vivo, mechanism and safety studies. The optimized architecture showed strong mechanical strength (28.6 ± 0.7 N/patch), high CATH loading (113 ± 10 μg/patch), and deep skin penetration (∼530 μm). DMNs dissolved in 45 min, while cytotoxicity at 200 μg/mL remained <20%. In vitro and ex vivo findings showed ∼99% reduction in MRSA burden, while in vivo efficacy was interesting and significantly eradicated the bacterial burden within 4 days. Faster effect than conventional antibiotics highlighting the potent nature of CATH. Mechanistic insights showed membrane disruption by CATH followed by AgrA suppression directly, unveiling a new antimicrobial target by Cathelicidin family of peptides

title: Synergistic dual photothermal-photodynamic nanoplatforms via BSA-stabilized gold nanospheres for selective melanoma phototherapy
abstract: Gold nanospheres (AuNSs) are promising agents for light-triggered cancer therapy, yet their biomedical performance strongly depends on surface chemistry and colloidal stability. Here, we report a multifunctional nanoplatform based on Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA)-coated AuNSs designed to synergistically combine photothermal and photodynamic effects under low-power LED irradiation. Systematic optimization of the BSA coating revealed that a dense protein corona at 225 µM yields highly stable, monodisperse nanosystems with preserved plasmonic features and excellent thermal reproducibility over multiple irradiation cycles. These optimized AuNSs-BSA were further functionalized with Rose Bengal (RB) to obtain hybrid RB-AuNSs-BSA nanoplatforms integrating plasmonic heating with efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Under 530 nm irradiation, the hybrid nanoplatforms induced a enhanced oxidative response in melanoma A375 cells, accompanied by significant viability loss and ultrastructural features indicative of mitochondrial and endoplasmic reticulum stress. In contrast, normal HaCaT keratinocytes displayed minimal ROS increases and maintained high viability, demonstrating a clear therapeutic selectivity. Control experiments confirmed that neither BSA coating nor RB loading compromised optical stability or colloidal integrity. Overall, this work establishes RB-AuNSs-BSA as a biocompatible, and LED-activatable nanoplatform capable of dual photothermal-photodynamic action, highlighting its potential for safe and selective melanoma treatment and for broader multimodal theranostic applications.

title: Closed-loop active-inverse learning for constrained discovery of high-resistivity Fe-based amorphous alloys
abstract: High-resistivity Fe-based amorphous alloys are difficult to design because electrical transport and glass-forming ability must be optimized simultaneously in a sparse composition space. Here, we develop a closed-loop active-inverse learning framework for accelerated discovery of high-resistivity Fe-Si-B-Ni-Cr amorphous alloys. Using a literature-derived dataset, the framework combines resistivity regression, amorphous-feasibility classification, constrained inverse search, and iterative experimental feedback. After three closed-loop cycles, GMM-based local enrichment was used to densify experimentally supported high-potential regions and improve subsequent model refinement. This stage yielded additional amorphous alloys with resistivities up to 202.85 μΩ·cm. A final experimental validation round identified Fe 65.11 Si 14.96 B 10.04 Ni 6.9 Cr 2.99 (D3), which exhibited a resistivity of 215.27 μΩ·cm. Structural and electronic analyses suggest that the resistivity increase is associated with chemical disorder ( σ ) and hopping-related transport descriptors( t ¯ ). The framework provides a practical strategy for constrained inverse design of amorphous alloys under sparse-data conditions.

title: Tailoring grain and second-phase particles in 6061 aluminum alloy via cryogenic forging to improve surface quality in single-point diamond turning
abstract: The enhancement of surface quality in ultra-precision machining of aluminum alloys is frequently impeded by coarse grains and second-phase particles. This study investigated microstructural refinement of 6061 aluminum alloy through cryogenic multi-directional forging combined with heat treatment to enhance surface quality in single point diamond turning (SPDT). Samples underwent initial annealing (AT) or solution treatment (ST), followed by 1–9 passes of cryogenic forging, solution treatment, and artificial aging. Microstructural characterization revealed that, compared to AT pretreatment, ST pretreatment suppressed dynamic recovery under cryogenic deformation, yielding higher dislocation density and substructure formation. These provided additional nucleation sites for static recrystallization in subsequent solution treatment, resulting in finer, equiaxed grains. Cryogenic forging fragmented coarse second-phase particles, while solution treatment enhanced their dissolution, reducing particle size and volume fraction. Increased dissolution into the aluminum matrix promoted a more uniform precipitation state, which contributed to improved hardness uniformity. SPDT experiments demonstrated that the refined microstructure reduced grain-boundary steps and defects associated with second-phase particles. Compared with the AT1 sample, the ST9 sample exhibited a decrease in the arithmetic average surface roughness, Ra, from 12.54 nm to 6.81 nm, corresponding to a reduction of 45.7%.

title: Critical review: bridging mycelium-based biocomposites, lignin-hybrid systems, and engineered wood toward dynamic lightweight applications
abstract: This review examines engineered wood products (EWP), lignin-hybrid composites, and mycelium-based biocomposites (MBB) as a converging engineering platform to identify what characterisation investments are needed before any of them can enter regulated dynamic structural applications. Despite differences in maturity, processing, and density, all three families share the same challenges: binder-matrix interface quality, moisture response, batch variability, and end-of-life design. For each family, available experimental data on quasi-static mechanical, hygrothermal, and dynamic properties are compiled and the missing measurements identified. For EWP, fatigue data exist but are confined to constant-amplitude bending at low moisture content, insufficient for structural design under combined hygrothermal and dynamic loading. For lignin-hybrid composites, substitution ratios of 20–50% of phenol by kraft lignin are established in particleboard adhesives, but creep, fatigue, and vibration characterisation under automotive service conditions are absent. For MBBs, fatigue, impact, and creep data are non-existent. Hygrothermal characterisation of recycled-wood MBBs is reported, including steady-state thermal conductivity and the first EN-compliant water vapour diffusion resistance dataset revealing a threefold anisotropy between core and skin layers, alongside the first dynamic mechanical analysis dataset for any MBB. Closing the fatigue and creep data gap is identified as the field-level priority linking all three families.

title: Mismatch between fracture and impact toughness in local brittle zone (LBZ) of FH420 offshore jacket pipe steel
abstract: This study challenges the common premise of a linear correlation between impact and fracture toughness in LBZ of High-strength low-alloy steels, revealing a fundamental mismatch between them. In this study, fracture/impact toughness tests were conducted on simulated LBZ specimens with different heat inputs, and their fracture mechanisms under quasi-static loading and impact loading were investigated respectively. The results showed the crack tip opening displacement (CTOD) value of coarse-grained HAZ (CGHAZ) exhibited a three-fold increase with increased t 8/5 (cooling time from 800℃ to 500℃), while the impact absorbed energy remained stable at about 200 J without significant fluctuations. Under low heat input ( t 8/5 = 4 s and 7 s), a lath bainite (LB)/lath martensite (LM) mixed microstructure in the CGHAZ provided high impact toughness via martensite plasticity deformation, but quasi‑static cracks propagated along brittle bainite, lowering fracture toughness. At higher heat inputs ( t 8/5 = 11 s and 17 s), a “softened” acicular ferrite (AF)/granular bainite (GB) mixed microstructure effectively resisted crack propagation under both loading conditions, ensuring excellent comprehensive toughness. In the intercritically-reheated CGHAZ (ICCGHAZ), numerous martensite–austenite (M−A) constituents induced microcracks and embrittled all microstructures, causing a drastic toughness deterioration. This work provides a mechanistic framework for designing welding processes to ensure structural integrity under complex loading scenarios.

title: Optimization of wear and corrosion resistance in high-entropy alloy coatings: Synergistic enhancement mechanism of Al–Mo alloying
abstract: Strengthening phases generally improve alloy wear resistance but often degrade corrosion resistance, limiting long-term service in marine engineering environments. In this study, an Al–Mo coupled regulation strategy is proposed to optimize both the wear and corrosion resistance of laser-cladded high-entropy alloy coatings. CoCrFeNiSiAl x Mo 1−x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1) coatings were fabricated by laser cladding, and first-principles calculations were employed to elucidate the intrinsic differences between Al and Mo in wear and corrosion behaviors from an electronic-structure perspective. The results demonstrate that the phase constitution of the coatings gradually evolves from an FCC + σ to the BCC/B2 structure. At x = 0, the wear resistance is optimized, yielding a minimum wear rate of 1.73 × 10 −5 mm 3 ·N −1 ·m −1 . Meanwhile, the combined Al–Mo alloying stabilizes the passive film, and the corrosion resistance reaches its optimum at x = 0.25, with an I corr of 1.31 × 10 −7 A·cm −2 . The present study provides a pathway for the compositional optimization of laser-cladded high-entropy alloy coatings and for the balanced enhancement of wear and corrosion resistance in marine engineering applications.

title: Interface-Engineered ZnO/PTFE@SiC coatings via Decoupling–Coupling strategy for multifunctional transparency
abstract: Transparent multifunctional coatings integrating UV shielding, hydrophobic self-cleaning and mechanical robustness are urgently needed for photovoltaic cover glass, yet conflicting material demands cause inherent functional trade-offs. Herein, a layered ZnO/PTFE@SiC coating with engineered Zn–O–Si interfacial bonds is fabricated via magnetron sputtering based on a decoupling–coupling strategy. Quantitative comparison reveals direct ZnO/SiC co-sputtering produces amorphous films with only 71.5% visible transmittance and weakened UV resistance, while the spatially separated layered architecture well preserves ZnO crystallinity. Optimized ZnO/PTFE@SiC coating achieves 83.16% visible transmittance, 75.90% UV shielding efficiency and a 104.7° water contact angle; after 60 abrasion cycles, its water contact angle only drops by 4.1°, whereas pure PTFE film loses 41.3° hydrophobicity under identical friction. XPS depth profiling verifies Zn–O–Si interfacial bonding, which realizes stress redistribution and suppresses interfacial delamination. This decoupling–coupling design effectively eliminates the performance compromise of co-deposited coatings, offering a scalable principle for robust multifunctional transparent films with potential for outdoor applications, though further environmental validation is required.

title: In situ fabrication and thermo-mechanical performance of alternating layer TPU–PLA multi-material structures by dual-nozzle fused deposition modelling
abstract: Currently, material extrusion-based Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) filaments with wire diameters of 1.75 mm or 2.85 mm are produced using extrusion techniques. However, this existing extrusion method is expensive, complex, and time-consuming. A novel in situ multi-material alternative TPU-PLA layer-printing method is proposed using a dual-nozzle FDM approach. In-situ TPU-PLA samples were printed using FDM, subjected to Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), surface roughness measurements, Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Micro tensile testing, and Shore-D hardness testing. The micro tensile samples were printed under different process parameters. It was found that TPU-PLA samples have an intermediate thermal degradation temperature range of 312–483 °C. The TPU-PLA sample exhibits an intermediate average surface roughness of 66 µm. The highest UTS of 6.24 MPa was achieved with a 3D Honeycomb pattern at 100% infill density. It’s significantly reduced in TPU-PLA samples due to the poor interfacial bonding compared to monolithic TPU and PLA samples. The highest Shore D hardness values, 47.67 and 47.39, were achieved with Rectilinear and Tri-Hexagon patterns, respectively. Hence, this work warrants further investigation, as there is limited work reported in the literature

title: Self-Optimization strategy for accelerating new alloy discovery: A Mini-Review
abstract: Currently, in alloy design, trial-and-error-based experimental screening is inefficient given the extremely vast multi-principal element composition space, and efficient, universal theoretical prediction tools are lacking. The self-optimization strategy offers a novel pathway for the rapid composition design of high-performance alloys by harnessing the natural solute partitioning and diffusion processes in existing dual-phase or multiphase materials. This mini-review traces the historical development and key advancements of this approach, highlighting its successful application in discovering new alloys, including single-phase high entropy alloys (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi, Ti 38 V 15 Nb 23 Hf 24 ), intermetallics (e.g., B2, L1 2 ), and traditional alloys (e.g., eutectic Al, Ti alloy). These materials exhibit exceptional mechanical properties, such as ultrahigh strength, high ductility, and thermal stability, stemming from their supersaturated solid-solution matrix, homogeneous microstructures, and high aging response. Beyond accelerating the exploration of vast compositional spaces, the self-optimization strategy reduces reliance on trial-and-error experiments, providing accurate and the most promising compositions, delivering significant economic and environmental benefits. This paper systematically formalizes a method for selecting the self-guiding components of an alloy system as a “self-optimization strategy”, offering guidance for transforming this strategy from isolated cases into a general design methodology.

title: Graph attention networks based multimodal feature fusion model for semi-cutting formability prediction
abstract: Accurate formability prediction is essential for industrial forming applications, but remains challenging due to cross-scale fracture mechanisms and local microscopic heterogeneity. In this study, a graph attention network based multimodal feature fusion model is proposed to predict the critical semi-cutting ratio of low-carbon steel by integrating local carbide particle topology, macroscopic mechanical features and microstructural statistical descriptors. Cross-validation results show that the proposed model outperforms GCN, CNN, MLP, and RF baseline models, highlighting the importance of topology-aware carbide graph representation for nonlinear formability prediction. Model interpretation and quantitative topology analysis indicate that carbide coarsening, high-aspect-ratio carbides, and directional chain-like carbide topology are associated with reduced formability. The out-of-fold attention analysis further shows that the GAT branch emphasizes locally aligned carbide connections, supporting the role of carbide spatial topology in CSCR prediction. This work provides a topology-aware framework for cross-scale formability evaluation and suggests that carbide size, aspect ratio, and directional spatial topology should be jointly considered in low-carbon steel microstructure design.

title: Uncertainty-aware structure–property mapping of spinodoid metamaterials via heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression
abstract: Spinodoid metamaterials provide a tunable design space for anisotropic mechanical properties, but their structure–property relationships are commonly represented as deterministic mappings from cone-angle descriptors to single stiffness values. This view overlooks the stochastic nature of Gaussian random field (GRF)-based topology generation, in which identical descriptors produce different morphologies and property scatter. We present an uncertainty-aware framework that interprets cone-angle descriptors as defining input-dependent stiffness distributions. Using heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression (GPR), the framework infers a low-dimensional, globally shared noise function from residual patterns across sparse observations. The results show that morphology-induced scatter varies across the design space and among stiffness components according to their mechanically active directions. Designs with similar mean stiffness can therefore exhibit different aleatoric uncertainty. In reliability-based design optimization (RBDO), direct repeated-realization validation confirms that only the heteroscedastic RBDO design satisfies the prescribed reliability target, whereas deterministic optimization and homoscedastic RBDO remain vulnerable to constraint violations. Accounting for heteroscedasticity therefore improves design reliability by incorporating spatial variation in morphology-induced scatter. These findings establish an uncertainty-aware framework for spinodoid modeling and design, while nonlinear responses and correlation-aware multi-output surrogates remain for future work.

title: Structurally architected perforated dielectric substrate via stereolithography 3D printing for low-loss angle-selective surfaces
abstract: For microwave components, 3D printing offers a rapid prototyping and cost-effective fabrication route; however, the inherently high dielectric loss of many 3D-printable materials often generates significant insertion loss in radio-frequency devices. This study addresses this limitation via a structural approach, uniquely enabled by additive manufacturing. A structurally architected perforated dielectric substrate is proposed to effectively reduce dielectric loss and applied as the supporting platform to fabricate an angle-selective surface (ASS). Numerical simulations revealed that the designed ASS exhibits a transmission coefficient of −0.6 dB under normal incidence, representing an improvement of over 2.6 dB relative to a counterpart employing a non-perforated substrate. The perforated substrate was fabricated using stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing, and the conductive patterns were realised using silver paste. Subsequently, an 11 × 11 array prototype was manufactured and experimentally characterised. The measured normal-incidence transmission coefficient was −1.3 dB, 1.9 dB higher than that of the non-perforated substrate-based ASS. These results demonstrate that structurally architected perforated dielectric substrates fabricated via SLA 3D printing offer a promising low-loss, lightweight, and cost-effective platform for angle-selective surfaces and related microwave components.

title: Structure–function insights from bamboo shark denticles applied to protective composite design
abstract: The white-spotted bamboo shark ( Chiloscyllium plagiosum ) exhibits unique functional adaptations to benthic habitats. However, the morphology, mechanical properties, and functional roles of its dermal denticles remain insufficiently elucidated. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was employed to investigate the microstructural features and squamation patterns of denticles across different body regions. Electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) served as a key technique for mapping elemental distributions within the outermost and inner layers. Nanoindentation measurements revealed a graded reduction in modulus and hardness from crown to root, with regional variation, indicating localised protective adaptations. Based on these findings, we proposed that bamboo shark denticles function as natural protective armour. Inspired by this structure, a biomimetic denticle design was developed using distinct materials with graded layers of decreasing elastic moduli across crown, neck, and root regions, consistent with nanoindentation results. The design was fabricated using multi-material 3D printing, and its mechanical performance was evaluated through quasi-static compression and creep-relaxation tests to assess energy dissipation behaviour. Furthermore, dynamic testing at a velocity of approximately 2 m/s was performed on various 3D‑printed samples, including drop‑weight impact tests and split Hopkinson pressure bar experiments, to evaluate the behaviour of 3D‑printed denticles under dynamic loading. This bioinspired strategy provides a viable pathway for designing impact-resistant, energy-dissipative composite systems for underwater and marine applications.

title: An intelligent inflammation-responsive hydrogel for localized and sustained co-delivery of hydrogen and magnesium ions to regenerate degenerative intervertebral discs
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of lower back pain, is characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, and cellular senescence. Hydrogen therapy shows promise in mitigating these pathological processes, however, its clinical translation is hindered by poor bioavailability and rapid clearance. Here, we developed an innovative, inflammation-responsive magnesium hydride (MgH 2 )-loaded GelMA-PLGA-MMP hydrogel system (MgH 2 @GPMgel) for the sustained and localized delivery of hydrogen and magnesium ions to treat IVDD. This photocrosslinkable hydrogel enables minimally invasive injection and in situ gelation, forming a stable implant that undergoes matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-triggered degradation within the degenerative disc microenvironment, thereby enabling on-demand release of therapeutic agents. In vitro studies demonstrated that MgH 2 @GPMgel effectively scavenged reactive oxygen species, promoted M2 macrophage polarization, and rejuvenated senescent nucleus pulposus cells. In a rat IVDD model, the stimulus-responsive hydrogel system significantly attenuated disc degeneration, restored extracellular matrix homeostasis, and promoted tissue repair. Overall, this study presents the first evidence that a microenvironment-responsive MgH 2 -based hydrogel through the synergistic effects of hydrogen and magnesium ions, offers a promising strategy for IVDD treatment, with potential for clinical translation.

title: NIR-responsive dissolving microneedles for 5-fluorouracil delivery in the treatment of hypertrophic scars
abstract: Hypertrophic scars (HS) are fibrotic skin disorders characterized by excessive fibroblast activity and collagen accumulation, frequently leading to aesthetic distortion and physical discomfort. While 5-fluorouracil (5-Fu) injection has been used clinically to suppress HS progression, its efficacy is often limited by rapid clearance and systemic side effects. To address the limitations of conventional 5-Fu therapy, we developed a near-infrared (NIR)-responsive dissolving microneedle (5FIPP MNs) system for localized and sustained drug delivery. The microneedle tips, composed of polyvinylpyrrolidone co-loaded with 5-Fu and indocyanine green (ICG), enable mechanical penetration into scar tissue and undergo photothermal-triggered separation upon NIR irradiation, leaving drug-loaded tips embedded intradermally for prolonged release. In vitro studies revealed that 5FIPP MNs effectively induce apoptosis and arrest cell cycle progression, thereby significantly inhibiting fibroblast proliferation, migration, and collagen synthesis. In vivo , the 5FIPP MNs enabled sustained 5-Fu release directly within scar tissue, leading to significantly greater scar regression than free 5-Fu, along with optimized Collagen I/III ratio, attenuated local inflammation, and minimal systemic exposure. This design reconciles the trade-off between insertion robustness and prolonged drug release observed in traditional microneedles. Our findings highlight the potential of this platform for efficient HS therapy and for treating other fibrotic skin conditions.

title: Trimetallic AuPt@CeO2 nanozyme-integrated multifunctional nanoplatform for targeted synergistic thrombolysis and vascular microenvironment modulation in venous thromboembolism
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress is a pivotal driver of thrombosis progression and subsequent vascular dysfunction. Consequently, mitigating oxidative stress is imperative for enhancing thrombolytic efficacy and restoring vascular homeostasis. Addressing the critical need for integrated therapeutic strategies, a comprehensive nanoplatform (AuPt@CeO 2 @mSiO 2 @cRGD-urokinase, APCMC-UK) was engineered to concurrently manage thrombolysis and vascular microenvironment. This platform comprises a trimetallic AuPt@CeO 2 nanozyme core encapsulated within a mesoporous silica shell, functionalized with cRGD peptides for targeted delivery of urokinase. Under near-infrared (NIR) laser irradiation, APCMC-UK exerts potent targeted thrombolysis through a synergistic mechanism combining urokinase and photothermal therapy. The vascular microenvironment is regulated by AuPt@CeO 2 via robust antioxidant activity to scavenge excess ROS and suppress local inflammatory responses. In a rat model of lower limb deep vein thrombosis, APCMC-UK combined with NIR irradiation achieves efficient thrombolysis while alleviating oxidative stress. In a rat pulmonary embolism model, APCMC-UK + NIR further exhibits significant therapeutic efficacy against this life-threatening thrombotic complication. In vivo biosafety evaluations confirm the favorable biocompatibility of the nanoplatform. This study demonstrates that the integration of targeted thrombolysis and vascular microenvironment modulation provides a comprehensive, safe, and effective strategy for venous thromboembolism treatment.

title: Carbon fiber-reinforced PEEK surpasses subtractive manufacturing reproducibility: systematic comparison of PAEK variants in high-temperature material extrusion for patient-specific implants
abstract: Material extrusion (MEX) of high-performance polymers typically yields lower dimensional performance than subtractive manufacturing, thereby limiting clinical applications. This study systematically compared MEX across polyaryletherketone (PAEK) variants, including polyetheretherketone (PEEK), polyetherketoneketone (PEKK), and CFR-PEEK, with subtractive milling and manual casting, using identical patient-specific cranial geometries. CFR-PEEK MEX achieved manufacturing reproducibility of 0.09 ± 0.05 mm root-mean-square error (RMSE), outperforming milled PEEK at 0.16 ± 0.05 mm ( p < 0.01), with fiber reinforcement suppressing edge-localized thermal distortion and achieving ± 0.3 mm spatial uniformity across 95 % of complex surfaces. PEKK MEX demonstrated 57 % higher manufacturing reproducibility than PEEK MEX (0.21 ± 0.05 mm versus 0.49 ± 0.02 mm RMSE), attributable to narrower thermal processing windows and higher glass transition temperature. Quasi-static biomechanical testing revealed controlled linear fractures at layer interfaces in MEX materials, with PEKK MEX maintaining structural integrity beyond 10 mm displacement (>1500 N), in contrast to the brittle stellate fragmentation observed in cast PMMA. All manufacturing methods met clinically acceptable dimensional thresholds for cranial reconstruction, demonstrating that point-of-care composite CFR-PEEK MEX can achieve dimensional performance comparable to established subtractive manufacturing workflows.

title: A 3D-printed hydrogel scaffold promotes infected diabetic wound repair via anti-inflammation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix remodeling
abstract: Infected diabetic wounds are difficult to heal due to bacterial colonization, persistent inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and defective extracellular matrix remodeling. Conventional dressings and non-printed hydrogels often provide limited structural support, insufficient antibacterial protection, and inadequate wound microenvironment regulation. Here, we developed a multifunctional 3D-printed SilMA/HAMA dual-crosslinked hydrogel scaffold loaded with PDA-EGCG nanoparticles, termed SH-EGCG, for infected diabetic wound repair. The optimized bioink showed favorable printability, porous architecture, suitable mechanical properties, swelling behavior, and degradability. PDA-EGCG enabled sustained EGCG release and enhanced scaffold bioactivity. In vitro, SH-EGCG exhibited good hemocompatibility and cytocompatibility and showed antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus ( MRSA ) and Escherichia coli ( E. coli ). It also promoted L929 fibroblast proliferation and migration, enhanced HUVEC tube formation, and favored reparative M2 macrophage polarization. In vivo , SH-EGCG accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammatory infiltration and TNF-α expression, increased TGF-β and VEGF, and promoted granulation tissue formation, hair follicle regeneration, collagen deposition, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Transcriptomic analysis associated SH-EGCG treatment with re-epithelialization and extracellular matrix organization, including partial normalization of KRT17, KRT19, CDH1, COL1A1, and COL3A1 expression. These findings highlight SH-EGCG as a promising multifunctional scaffold for infected diabetic wound repair through antibacterial, immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, and extracellular matrix-remodeling effects.

title: Probing the damage constitutive modeling of low-heat cement concrete subjected to acid deposition
abstract: The performance of low-heat cement concrete (LHCC) in high arch dams under sulfuric-nitric acid deposition remains insufficiently understood. This study conducted laboratory simulation tests involving coupled acid deposition immersion and temperature-humidity cycles. By integrating macro-performance testing, multi-scale micro-characterization, and statistical damage mechanics theory, the mechanical degradation patterns and micro-deterioration mechanisms of LHCC under acid deposition were systematically investigated, and a statistical damage constitutive model was developed. The results indicate that acid deposition induces distinct evolutionary patterns in the macro-performance of LHCC; notably, splitting tensile strength is highly sensitive to erosion, effectively characterizing latent damage within the interfacial transition zone. At the micro-scale, acid erosion triggers calcium leaching and structural cross-linking transformations within the calcium silicate hydrate. Furthermore, a uniaxial compression statistical damage constitutive model for LHCC, constructed using a Weibull–Lognormal composite distribution, demonstrates high fidelity to experimental data (R 2 > 0.94). This model accurately characterizes the three stages of damage evolution and quantifies the influence of erosion severity on damage progression. This research elucidates the internal deterioration mechanisms of LHCC under acid deposition, providing a theoretical framework and technical basis for the long-term service safety assessment and material optimization of high arch dams subject to composite acid deposition.

title: Deciphering the effect of microstructural heterogeneities on the macro- and micro-mechanical behaviour of additively manufactured high-strength aluminium alloys
abstract: Additively manufactured high-strength aluminum (Al) alloys exhibit exceptional strength and reasonable ductility, since they benefit from the heterogeneous as-built grain structure with alternating fine and coarse grains at the melt-pool boundaries and melt-pool interiors, respectively. Although the formation of such microstructures has been studied extensively, the nature of deformation at low length scales, specifically the complex interplay and individual contribution of microstructural heterogeneities, remains largely unexplored. The high-strength Al alloy Scalmalloy® was processed by PBF-LB/M. Its deformation behavior was investigated by macroscopic tensile tests performed at different temperatures and strain rates as well as by microscopic tensile tests in conjunction with high-resolution digital image correlation (µDIC). Specifically, the strain localization patterns as well as strain partitioning between the alternating fine and coarse grains were quantitatively analyzed. Inhomogeneous deformation behavior was observed in macroscopic tests in the form of temperature and strain rate-dependent serrated flow. µDIC and interrupted tensile EBSD results revealed severe strain and geometrically necessary dislocation density localizations near the interface between fine and coarse grains. Multiple microstructural heterogeneities like grain clusters, local L1 2 precipitate fraction and dislocation distribution were identified as decisive factors contributing to inhomogeneous micro- and macro-scale plasticity.

title: Multifunctional superhydrophobic swimming goggles with efficient drag reduction and self-cleaning-driven optical recovery: toward high-performance aquatic sports equipment
abstract: Superhydrophobic surfaces are widely employed for waterproofing, drag reduction, and self-cleaning, yet their integration into sports equipment remains substantially underexplored. Swimming goggles, in particular, continue to suffer from pronounced hydrodynamic drag, lens fouling by oils and other contaminants, and the limited service life of conventional anti-fogging coatings. Herein, a transparent superhydrophobic coating was fabricated on polycarbonate (PC) goggle lenses via a sol–gel approach. The resulting surface exhibits a water contact angle of 162.16° and a sliding angle of 2.11°, while retaining superhydrophobicity under a battery of demanding conditions: 2000 g sand abrasion, 1.5 MPa water-jet impingement, 48 h ultraviolet irradiation, NaClO immersion, and accelerated thermal ageing. Hydrodynamic measurements reveal a drag reduction of approximately 31% under both partially and fully submerged regimes. Moreover, the coating effectively repels and self-cleans at least ten categories of contaminants commonly encountered during swimming, including perspiration, rainwater, and cola. Collectively, these advances endow swimming goggles with markedly enhanced superhydrophobicity, drag-reduction efficiency, durability, and self-cleaning capability, and further indicate the broad applicability of the strategy across a wide spectrum of underwater equipment.

title: Potential of Chitosan hydrogel with Canarium ovatum pulp extract for diabetic wound healing application
abstract: • Diabetes treatments are inaccessible and costly in the Philippines • Local medicinal plants show antimicrobial, antioxidant, and wound healing properties. • Canarium ovatum contains polyphenolic compounds and strong antioxidant potential. • Chitosan biopolymers enhance herbal extracts but have stability limitations. • Chitosan hydrogels with Canarium ovatum show potential for diabetic wound healing. Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a rapidly growing global health concern, particularly dominant and disproportionately affecting low and middle-income countries (LMIC). The Philippines is an LMIC that faces persistent challenges in the treatment of DM due to socioeconomic and healthcare constraints in the country. Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are among the most severe complications that are characterized by impaired wound healing, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and high susceptibility to infection. DFUs are a leading cause of prolonged hospitalization, lower-limb amputation, and reduced quality of life, placing a substantial burden on both patients and the national healthcare system. The limited accessibility to safe, effective, and affordable wound treatments underscores the vital need for natural therapeutic alternatives. The integration of medicinal plants into diabetic wound care has attracted interest due to their antioxidant, antidiabetic, and anti-inflammatory properties. Canarium ovatum Engl. is a native and underutilized Philippine species that has demonstrated anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties relevant to wound healing. Chitosan is a biopolymer that provides moisture retention and enhanced wound healing properties when combined with medicinal plant extracts. The paper examines the potential of a CS-based hydrogel enriched with C. ovatum pulp extract as a sustainable and cost-effective therapeutic option for diabetic wound healing.

title: Multifunctional ZnO nanoflower-integrated supramolecular dual-network hydrogel to remodel regeneration microenvironment for infected wound healing
abstract: Infected wounds present a formidable clinical challenge, in which persistent bacterial colonization, excessive oxidative stress, and dysregulated inflammation converge to impair tissue regeneration. Here, we developed ZNFs@GA/GelMA, a multifunctional supramolecular dual-network hydrogel for infected wound therapy. The ZNFs@GA/GelMA hydrogel dressing system was constructed by integrating glycyrrhizic acid (GA), zinc oxide nanoflowers (ZNFs), and gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA). In this design, GA-driven supramolecular self-assembly first forms an injectable and defect-adaptive physical network, followed by photoinitiated GelMA polymerization to generate a structurally stable dual-network for conformal wound coverage. The incorporated ZNFs endowed the hydrogel with efficient antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) and E. coli . In vitro , ZNFs@GA/GelMA decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, shifting macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory state. In vivo studies demonstrated that ZNFs@GA/GelMA effectively reduced bacterial burden and inflammatory responses, promoted angiogenesis and extracellular matrix remodeling, and accelerated infected wound closure. Overall, ZNFs@GA/GelMA provides a promising multifunctional dressing strategy for the management of infected wounds.

title: Influence of deposition-induced directional stochasticity on strengthening mechanisms and anisotropy in LW-DED printed IN718
abstract: Mechanical and microstructural anisotropy is a pressing issue in Additive Manufacturing (AM), especially in processes with high deposition rates, such as Laser Wire Directed Energy Deposition (LW-DED). While deposition strategies can control anisotropy, the influence of directional stochasticity on microstructural and mechanical homogeneity remains largely unexplored. Therefore, this study investigates the effect of deposition-induced directional stochasticity on the microstructural and mechanical homogeneity of LW-DED IN718 alloy. IN718 is widely used in aerospace, making it suitable for studying LW-DED stochasticity. Four deposition paths (raster, triangle, wiggle, honeycomb) were designed to systematically introduce increasing levels of directional stochasticity. Cuboidal samples were fabricated and systematically analysed across three principal planes: top, build, and diagonal. The grain morphology, phase distribution, crystallographic texture, and mechanical properties of the samples were evaluated. Increasing deposition-induced directional stochasticity progressively reduced microstructural and mechanical anisotropy by disrupting columnar growth and redistributing crystallographic orientations. Low directional stochasticity (raster) produced strongly aligned columnar grains, leading to anisotropy. In contrast, high directional stochasticity (honeycomb) disrupted epitaxial growth, leading to weaker texture and more uniform microstructural distribution. Strengthening mechanism analysis further revealed that directional stochasticity modifies the relative contributions of grain boundary and dislocation strengthening by altering grain morphology and stored dislocation density.

title: In-situ investigations of tensile and fracture behavior of 316 L stainless steel lattice struts fabricated by laser powder bed fusion
abstract: Lattice materials, fabricated using additive manufacturing, offer a lightweight alternative to traditional bulk structural components while meeting mechanical performance requirements. Despite these advantages, the complex geometry of lattice structures and additive manufacturing processes introduce defects that can significantly impact the mechanical properties of individual struts of lattices. This study investigates the mechanisms through which fabrication-induced defects influence the tensile response and fracture behavior of 316 L stainless steel lattice struts manufactured by laser powder bed fusion in horizontal and vertical orientations. In-situ tensile testing within an X-ray computed tomography instrument was conducted to visualize and analyze the evolution of the three-dimensional structure during the test. Horizontally built struts exhibited geometric irregularities, such as irregular cross-sections, dripping effects, and strut warping, primarily due to limited support of loose powder during fabrication. These irregularities created regions with reduced cross-sections that served as sites for fracture initiation, resulting in less ductility. Meanwhile, vertically built struts exhibited uniform cross-sections, but displayed a higher fraction of porosity, characterized by spherical pores near the surface. These pores acted as sites for strain localization, with cracks initiating and propagating near them. However, the absence of reduced cross-sections in vertically built struts delayed fracture and provided higher ductility.

title: Integrated metal MEX manufacturing of bimetallic TPMS-core sandwich panels for lightweight structural applications
abstract: Multi-material metal additive manufacturing (AM) enables the integration of dissimilar alloys within a single component; however, fully integrated bimetallic sandwich panels remain largely unexplored. This work presents a one-step AM strategy for fabricating bimetallic sandwich panels with bio-inspired cellular cores, combined with a full-geometry finite element (FE) model for predicting flexural behavior. The panels were manufactured without secondary joining, achieving continuous material transitions and effective interfacial bonding. Three-point bending tests were performed to evaluate stiffness, strength, and failure mechanisms, validating the FE model and capturing the effects of material heterogeneity and architectural features beyond homogenized approaches. The manufactured panels exhibited flexural modulus values of 29.98–150.45 GPa and flexural strength values of 200.44–769.12 MPa, with densities ranging from 1740 to 6384 kg/m 3 . Flexural performance reached up to approximately twice that of single- and hybrid-manufactured reference structures. These results demonstrate the feasibility of fully additive fabrication of structurally functional bimetallic sandwich panels and provide a validated framework linking process, architecture, and mechanical response.

title: Additive manufacturing of graphene-reinforced copper matrix composites produced via cold spray
abstract: Graphene (Gr)-reinforced composites offer significant potential for enhanced thermal, mechanical, and functional performances, yet their fabrication via energy beam-based additive manufacturing (AM) is challenging due to the thermal sensitivity of Gr, the risk of agglomeration, and limitations of high-temperature processes. As a solution, Cu-1 wt% Gr deposits were successfully produced using cold spray additive manufacturing (CSAM), providing a solid-state route to fabricate dense 2D metal matrix composites (2DMMCs). The effects of Gr incorporation and gas temperature were systematically investigated on microstructural evolution, dynamic recrystallization, and functional properties. 2DMMCs properties were compared with pure Cu to isolate the effects of Gr reinforcement. The effect of microstructural homogenization induced by post-deposition heat-treatment was analysed on thermal, electrical and mechanical performances. Findings indicate that the presence of Gr alters how strain and thermal energy are distributed within the deposits, promoting heterogeneous microstructures and increasing microhardness. Higher gas temperature led to higher density and thermal conductivity. However, mechanical and electrical properties were moderately reduced due to Gr-induced stress concentrations and interparticle bonding limitations. Subsequent post-deposition annealing partially reduced bulk defects and led to enhanced thermal and electrical performance. Our findings demonstrate that CSAM enables the efficient production of Cu–Gr 2DMMCs. The structure–property relationships established in this work identify interfacial bonding and Gr distribution as the key factors governing composite performance, providing a foundation for future optimization of solid-state AM strategies for large scale 2DMMCs.

title: Cross-route comparison of additive manufacturing of a low-carbon steel: Microstructure and mechanical properties for high-strength structural applications
abstract: This study investigates how additive manufacturing routes influence the microstructure and mechanical properties of a low-carbon steel for high-strength structural applications. A direct comparison was performed for laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB), laser directed energy deposition with wire and powder feedstocks (DED-LB/w and DED-LB/p), and arc directed energy deposition (DED-Arc), using multiscale characterization by optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, electron backscatter diffraction, and transmission electron microscopy. Distinct thermal histories produced markedly different microstructures. PBF-LB resulted in lath martensite, whereas the DED routes produced bainitic microstructures due to their lower cooling rates. No retained austenite was detected, and prior austenite grains were elongated along the build direction in all conditions. These microstructural differences strongly affected mechanical properties. Vickers hardness ranged from 271 ± 6 HV0.5 for DED-Arc to 366.3 ± 11 HV0.5 for PBF-LB, with similar trends in yield and ultimate tensile strengths. Among the bainitic conditions, DED-LB/w showed the highest mean tensile strength, while DED-Arc exhibited the greatest ductility, demonstrating clear route-dependent differences in the strength–ductility balance. Overall, additive manufacturing route selection enables substantial tailoring of microstructure and mechanical performance within a single low-carbon steel composition, providing access to a broad property range relevant to high-strength structural applications.

title: Stress-relaxation-informed thermo-metallurgical-mechanical modeling of residual stress and distortion for LDED of TA15 alloy
abstract: Residual stress and distortion in laser-directed energy deposition (LDED) are critical issues affecting dimensional accuracy and component reliability. Currently, thermo-mechanical-based (TMB) models are widely used for residual stress and distortion prediction in LDED. Nevertheless, TMB models generally neglect the coupled effects of solid-state phase transformation (SSPT) and stress relaxation. In particular, stress relaxation induced by repeated thermal cycling remains insufficiently captured, limiting the fidelity and accuracy of residual stress prediction. To address this issue, a stress-relaxation-informed thermo-metallurgical-mechanical (TMM-SR) model was developed for LDED of TA15 alloy based on a previously validated thermal and SSPT framework. A calibrated hyperbolic-sine constitutive model was introduced to incorporate high-temperature stress relaxation into the SSPT-based mechanical framework, enabling simultaneous consideration of SSPT and stress relaxation. A two-stage deposition experiment combining DIC-based in situ monitoring and ex situ residual stress measurements was conducted for validation. The results demonstrate that the proposed TMM-SR model significantly improves the prediction accuracy of residual stress and distortion compared with conventional TMB models, providing deeper insights into their evolution mechanisms during LDED.

title: Micromechanical response and pore-skeleton characteristics of oil shale waste-modified asphalt mixtures
abstract: Oil shale waste (OSW) has the potential to serve as an aggregate in asphalt pavements due to its unique porous structure and oil storage characteristics. However, in practical applications, these intrinsic properties and their reinforcing effects on asphalt pavement performance are often overlooked. To address this issue, the mechanisms underlying OSW’s performance enhancement as a fine aggregate in asphalt mixtures were investigated using X-ray computed tomography (CT) scanning and Particle Flow Code (PFC) numerical simulations, combined with laboratory mechanical tests. The CT results showed that the number of contact points between coarse aggregate and asphalt mortar in the OSW asphalt mixture (OSW-AM) was 26.44% higher than that in the basalt asphalt mixture (BS-AM), indicating a more uniform spatial distribution. In addition, the asphalt film thickness in the OSW-AM was 33.60% greater than that in the BS-AM, demonstrating the superior oil absorption capacity of OSW. Force chain analysis further revealed that the maximum contact force in the OSW-AM increased by 18.3% compared with that in the BS-AM, suggesting that the incorporation of OSW enhances the stability of the aggregate skeleton structure. These findings provide theoretical support for the application of OSW in road engineering.

title: Impact energy release and damage effect of fluoropolymer-based reactive projectile against low–slow–small drone
abstract: To enhance the destructive effect of PTFE-based reactive materials on the low–slow–small (LSS) drone with lightweight protective capability, six types of reactive projectiles with different compactness and fillers were assembled. Mechanical properties across a wide range of strain rates were systematically characterized by combining micromorphology analysis with quasi-static compression and split-Hopkinson pressure bar experiments. Reaction heat, reaction overpressure and reaction efficiency were systematically investigated. The damage effect of the impact energy release of reactive projectile on LSS drone was evaluated finally. The results indicate that the addition of Ni enhanced both the static and dynamic compressive strength of the material. The inclusion of MnO 2 reduced the static and dynamic compressive strength. Both ZrH 2 and MnO 2 increased the reaction energy and reaction overpressure of the material, whereas Ni decreased the reaction energy, reaction overpressure, and reaction efficiency. While a reduction in material compactness lowered the initial impact pressure, the resulting adiabatic compression of pores significantly improved the reaction efficiency of the material. Considering the chemical and mechanical properties comprehensively, the selection of PTFE/Al/MnO 2 reactive projectile substantially enhanced the damage effect of LSS drone.

title: A biopolymer-reinforced collagen hydrogel mimicking the 3D mechanical microenvironment promotes osteogenic differentiation via mechanotransduction
abstract: Mechanical forces play a critical role in the oral and maxillofacial region. Understanding cellular responses to mechanical forces is essential. However, current mechanobiological studies are largely confined to 2D cultures, which poorly represent native 3D contexts. Although hydrogels offer promise for 3D studies, integrating high-magnitude mechanical stretch with biocompatibility remains challenging. This study developed a novel collagen-based gelatin/cellulose nanocrystal/alginate (C-GCA) hydrogel. The elongation at break of the hydrogel reaches 95.4%, demonstrating excellent tensile properties, which is attributed to the reinforcing effect of CNCs and SA. Concurrently, the presence of collagen and gelatin confers favorable biocompatibility to the hydrogel (cell viability exceeding 95%). Crucially, the biological responses of Periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs) laden in the C-GCA hydrogel-based 3D microenvironment were strain-dependent. Under 20% tensile strain, the expression of osteogenesis-related genes, namely RUNX-2 , OSX , COL1A1 , and OPN , was 3.1, 4.1, 1.7 and 2.8 times that of the control group, respectively. Meanwhile, the cell projection area increased by 1.38 folds, and the apoptosis rate reduced by 45.5%. Overall, the C-GCA hydrogel not only provides a solid foundation for a deeper understanding of the mechanisms of mechanostimulation in the oral and maxillofacial regions but also offers new strategies for the biomedical material design.

title: 4D printing of photocurable shape memory resins activated via indirect heating
abstract: This work introduces a DLP-based 4D printing strategy that enables the fabrication of monolithic, electrically triggered shape-memory structures through indirect Joule heating. Two polyurethane–methacrylate-based resin blends were prepared from commercially available photopolymer resins and processed by Digital Light Processing (DLP) printing. NMR and rheological analyses confirmed the compatibility of the resin components and their suitability for vat photopolymerization processes, while FT-IR analysis demonstrated the effective crosslinking induced by UV curing. Post-curing significantly improved the mechanical properties of the printed parts, leading to elastic modulus values up to 2.9 GPa and high thermal stability. Both formulations exhibited stable shape memory behavior, with shape fixity ratio values above 93% and rapid recovery of the permanent shape upon thermal activation allowing also to lift external loads. NiCr wires have been successfully embedded during the printing process, enabling indirect activation through the Joule effect with recovery time of 20 s

title: Multiscale XFEM–CZM simulation of crack propagation in silica/epoxy nanocomposites with interfacial contact effects
abstract: Understanding the fracture behavior of nanoparticle–reinforced polymer composites requires an accurate description of damage mechanisms operating across multiple length scales. In this study, a unified multiscale numerical framework is established to investigate crack initiation and propagation in silica/epoxy nanocomposites from the nano– to macroscale. The approach integrates representative volume element (RVE) modeling with the extended finite element method (XFEM) coupled to a cohesive zone model (CZM), enabling simultaneous simulation of matrix cracking, particle–matrix debonding, and interfacial damage. At the nano and microscale, unit–cell and clustered RVEs are employed to quantify the effective elastic modulus, tensile strength, and fracture energy under three interfacial bonding conditions: perfect bonding, frictional sliding, and cohesive interaction. Microscale responses are subsequently transferred to meso– and macroscale models to predict heterogeneous and homogenized fracture behavior. The modified Halpin–Tsai–Lewis–Nielsen model accurately captures interphase effects and demonstrates good agreement with RVE–based finite element predictions. Across all scales, interfacial bonding quality emerges as the dominant factor governing stiffness, strength, and fracture resistance. The CZM provides the most realistic representation of particle–matrix interactions and is therefore recommended for predictive fracture analysis and design optimization of particulate polymer nanocomposites.

title: Achieving high strength of laser welded Al/steel joint by optimized energy distribution with adjustable mode beam heat source
abstract: This study investigates the role of ring–beam power (Pr) in adjustable mode beam (AMB) laser welding of dissimilar 6061 Al alloy to DP590 steel, with a focus on the critical balance between porosity suppression and intermetallic compound (IMC) control. Unlike conventional lasers, AMB enables independent modulation of the center and ring beams, providing precise energy distribution essential for dissimilar joining. By integrating high–speed imaging and CFD simulations, we reveal that Pr governs keyhole stability and melt–pool convection. The results show that Pr = 600 W yields the highest mean shear force of 1067 N, with a recommended processing window of 500–700 W, within which mechanical performance is significantly improved over both lower and higher power conditions,the enlarged and stabilised keyhole effectively reduces porosity, while the formation of a ductile Fe 3 Al–rich layer enhances joint ductility and strength. However, when Pr exceeds 800 W, excessive turbulent mixing can lead to an excess of brittle Fe 2 Al 5 and FeAl 3 phases, triggering IMC-induced brittle cracking, severely degrading mechanical performance. This combined experimental–numerical approach provides a quantitative mechanistic framework for optimising Al/steel laser welding and clearly defines the allowable Pr window for achieving sound joints.

title: High-performance cobalt-based model superalloy with aging-stable <101> texture and uniform γ′ precipitates by laser powder bed fusion
abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of strong crystallographic textures, but post-process heat treatments often trigger recrystallization that degrades the as-built microstructure. We demonstrate that a LPBF‑fabricated Co‑5Al‑14V (at.%) alloy exhibits a pronounced <101>//BD (Building Direction) texture that remains stable after aging near the γ′ solvus, resulting in a unique microstructure combining strong texture with uniformly distributed γ′ precipitates. This study systematically investigates microstructural evolution, texture stability, and γ′ precipitation under different heat treatment conditions (as‑printed, directly aged, and solution‑treated plus aged). We perform a qualitative assessment of the combined microstructural contributions from dislocation substructures, precipitate distribution, and recrystallization to the mechanical properties. The alloy achieves an exceptional strength‑ductility synergy with an ultimate tensile strength of ∼1 GPa and uniform elongation of 20%. These findings provide fundamental insights into microstructure–mechanical interactions in LPBF‑manufactured cobalt‑based superalloys and guide the design of next‑generation superalloys.

title: Optical manipulation and applications of quasi-one-dimensional nanomaterials
abstract: Quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) nanomaterials serve as essential building blocks for next-generation nanodevices, owing to their high specific surface area, strong quantum confinement, and highly tunable properties. The precise manipulation of individual nanostructures is therefore critical for assembling high-performance nanoscale devices. Among various micro- and nanoscale manipulation methods, optical tweezers stand out for their non-contact operation, high spatial precision, and programmable controllability, thus enabling stable trapping and precise manipulation of single quasi-1D nanomaterials in diverse environments. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in optical manipulation using different optical tweezer platforms, including conventional optical tweezers, scanning optical tweezers, holographic optical tweezers, optical fiber tweezers, plasmonic optical tweezers, and optoelectronic systems. We compare their underlying principles, trapping performance, and application scenarios, and identify key challenges in trapping stability, orientation control, and device integration. To address these challenges, potential approaches have been proposed, including advanced optical field engineering, hybrid field coupling, customized trap architectures with coordinated multi-trap operation, and in situ assembly approaches such as thermally induced bonding and localized electrochemical deposition. By consolidating recent progress and outlining future directions, this review provides a structured perspective on optical manipulation of quasi-1D nanomaterials and supports their integration into novel nanodevice fabrication and multifunctional systems.

title: Thickness-dependent deformation and fracture characteristics of AL6XN super-austenitic stainless steel subjected to tensile and fatigue loads
abstract: The thickness-dependent tensile and fatigue behavior of AL6XN super-austenitic stainless steel was investigated over 0.1–––2.0 mm. With the increase in specimen thickness, the ultimate tensile strength increases from 585 MPa to 728 MPa, the tensile fracture strain rises from 22% to 52%, and the fatigue life under the cyclic stress amplitude of 275 MPa extends from approximately 5.7 × 10 3 cycles to 1.1 × 10 5 cycles. The fracture surface roughness, quantified by the fractal dimension D f increases, reflecting progressively more tortuous crack paths in thicker specimens. The improved mechanical performance under both monotonic and cyclic loading is attributed to the increased grain boundary area, which provides more sites for dislocation storage and twin nucleation, promoting a progressive transition from planar slip to deformation twinning as thickness increases. Furthermore, the elevated stress triaxiality in thicker specimens suppresses localized necking and retards crack propagation. In fatigue, the increased twin density induces crack deflection and creates more tortuous crack paths, which further enhances crack propagation resistance. These findings establish a mechanistic link between specimen thickness and deformation mode transition in austenitic stainless steels, and provide a critical reference for the design of thin-walled components in nuclear, chemical, and marine engineering applications.

title: Guiding encapsulant choice in perovskite solar cells with LCA: climate change footprints, break-even lifetimes and recycling perspective
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have demonstrated the potential for reducing environmental impacts of photovoltaic-generated electricity. However, like other solar cells, PSCs require encapsulation to withstand outdoor conditions. Environmental impact of encapsulation is insufficiently discussed during the design stages, while encapsulants may significantly contribute to the overall impact. Present study fills this gap by providing comparative life cycle assessment (LCA) of cells encapsulated with various polymers. Using end-of-life perspective during discussion, present LCA guides the final material choice. According to the LCA cells encapsulated with polyolefin elastomer exhibited lowest environmental impact related to manufacturing (24.7 kg CO 2 eq./m 2 ). Thermoplastic polyurethane had the highest impact (27.4 kg CO 2 eq./m 2 ), contributing significantly to the overall footprint of the PSC. This high contribution undermines the viability of sacrificing TPU to recycle PSCs. Furthermore, lifetime and performance of the modelled PSCs were found to be the crucial parameters for the final choice of the encapsulant. Scenario modelling revealed that if the encapsulated cells could operate for six years, the total life-cycle Climate Change impacts would break even with those of traditional solar panels. Accordingly, combination of present LCA results with future rigorous comparison of lifetime performance of encapsulated PSCs should guide the final material choice

title: Binder Jetting of hardmetals: a literature review and patent landscape analysis on commercial and in-house developed granules and liquid binders
abstract: In recent years , Binder Jetting (BJT) has attracted significant interest within the Hardmetals industry. BJT relies on a layer-by-layer powder deposition, followed by the selective jetting of a binder. Literature on BJT of Hardmetals shows considerable effort towards optimising printing parameters. However, one cannot dissociate the ability to fabricate accurate and dense parts from the properties of the granules and binders, which are often overlooked. Specifically, for Hardmetals, the limited variety of available grades and the challenges to densify the granules are two urgent issues. Regarding the binders, the challenges are extended across the whole BJT ecosystem. Binders are still largely seen as simple sacrificial glues to bond powders. However, the chemistry behind them and how they can influence or promote the formation of deleterious phases cannot be disregarded, particularly for Hardmetals. In this context, this review provides an overview of BJT for Hardmetals, from academia to industry. It particularly addresses strategies for densifying Hardmetal granules and for efficient bonding provided by the liquid binders, specifically developed for Hardmetals. From research studies and communications to a dedicated patent analysis, this review analyses the different and most relevant approaches towards the development of Hardmetal granules and binders for BJT.

title: Effect of hot pressing holding time on microstructure evolution, mechanical properties and impact energy characteristics of Al/Ni reactive materials
abstract: To examine how holding time influences mechanical response, impact energy release, microstructural evolution, and chemical reaction behavior of Al/Ni reactive materials, three specimens were prepared at holding times of 30, 45, and 60 min within the 30–60 min range. Dynamic/static compression and quasi-sealed container impact tests were conducted, and microstructure was characterized by SEM, EDS, and XRD. Results indicate that with increasing holding time, atomic interdiffusion intensifies, intermetallic compounds increase and evolve from isolated islands to a network. Yield strength first increases then decreases, while ultimate fracture strain shows the opposite trend. At 30 min, effective Al-Ni bonding with few scattered brittle phases results in optimal plasticity; the ultimate fracture strain reaches 0.262, 118.33% and 54.12% higher than at 45 and 60 min. At 45 min, interconnected brittle phases cause embrittlement; the quasi-static yield strength peaks at 394.25 MPa, 48.34% and 70.97% higher than at 30 and 60 min. Under high-velocity impact, specific chemical energy first increases then decreases, peaking at 45 min, 1.64 kJ/g, 64% and 59.07% higher than at 30 and 60 min. This study clarifies the influence mechanism of heat treatment on Al/Ni reactive materials, offering a theoretical basis for performance optimization and energetic structural applications.

title: A physics-regulated neural framework for learning 3D grain growth dynamics
abstract: Grain growth is governed by the reduction in grain boundary energy and exhibits well-established statistical scaling laws. Developing data-driven surrogates that preserve these physical invariants while remaining computationally scalable remains challenging, especially in 3D. We present 3D-PRIMME (Physics-Regulated Interpretable Machine Learning for Microstructure Evolution) for learning three-dimensional grain growth dynamics. The model is trained using only two consecutive time steps yet accurately reproduces the linear coarsening law and preserves topological statistics over extended time scales. Despite being trained on a grid points with 512 grains, the learned evolution operator is applied to domains up to grid points with 550,000 grains without retraining, maintaining consistent kinetics and grain topology across orders-of-magnitude increases in system size. These results demonstrate that 3D-PRIMME learns a scale-independent and temporally stable local evolution rule, enabling efficient and robust large-scale surrogate prediction of 3D microstructure evolution.

title: Rotating nozzle fused filament fabrication (FFF) 3D printer for short-fiber polymer composite manufacturing
abstract: This research highlights a recently patented rotating nozzle Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) 3D printing technology that accelerates print speeds and facilitates an isotropic-like fiber-orientation distribution in 3D printed polymer composites. The printer incorporates a 1.1-kilowatt indirect drive system, equipped with sensors for real-time data acquisition of temperature, filament feed rate, nozzle rotational speed, and extrusion force to describe the interrelation between processing parameters and final part performance. Experiments using short glass-fiber-reinforced nylon filament reveal fiber orientation distribution evolution, providing a path to material isotropy. Introducing a rotational nozzle shows improvements in ultimate tensile strength perpendicular to the printing direction by approximately 40 % and accelerates the extrusion processes by reducing the required force for extrusion as viscosity is reduced through shear-thinning. These improvements have the potential to broaden the scope of fused filament fabrication applications, particularly in high-performance engineering sectors such as aerospace and automotive industries which demand custom performance metrics.

title: Yb oxide particles collaboratively enhancing fracture toughness and oxidation resistance in Nb-Si based alloys
abstract: Rare earth elements exhibit significant advantages in synergistically improving the overall performance of alloys. This study systematically reveals, for the first time, the mechanisms by which the rare earth element Yb affects the microstructural evolution, room temperature fracture toughness and high temperature oxidation resistance of Nb-Si based alloys. The results show that the introduction of Yb can significantly refine its microstructure. When 0.8 at.% Yb is added, the room temperature fracture toughness increases to 16.06 MPa·m1/ [2] , representing a 53.7 % improvement over that of the base alloy; meanwhile, the high temperature oxidation rate decreases by 62.7 %, demonstrating superior overall service performance compared with previously reported Nb-Si based alloys. The simultaneous enhancement of fracture toughness and oxidation resistance is mainly attributed to the strengthening and regulating effects of Yb oxide particles in the alloy. On the one hand, Yb forms finely dispersed Yb oxide particles through in situ oxidation, thereby reducing oxygen contamination in the matrix and promoting the occurrence of secondary cracking, crack deflection and crack bridging during crack propagation. On the other hand, Yb 3 Al 5 O 12 formed during oxidation effectively improves the protective performance of the oxidation scale, driving the oxidation kinetics of the alloy toward a parabolic law.

title: Comparative synthesis and electrochemical performance of Ti3C2 MXene via LiF/HCl and HF etching routes
abstract: Two-dimensional Ti 3 C 2 MXenes are promising electrode materials for energy storage, but their structural and electrochemical properties depend strongly on the etching route used for synthesis. In this work, Ti 3 C 2 MXene was synthesized from Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase via two routes, direct HF etching and LiF/HCl-assisted etching and directly compared under identical conditions. XRD peak-fitting showed only a marginal (002) shift (9.57°→9.53° for both etched samples; d-spacing 9.23 → 9.27–9.28 Å), while Scherrer analysis of the (104) reflection showed increased crystallite size after etching (15.5 nm MAX vs. ≈21 nm for both MXenes), with no significant difference between routes. Raman and FTIR analyses showed that HF-etched MXene showed defect-rich, fluorine-dominated surfaces, while LiF/HCl MXene retained richer –OH, C=O, and C-F functionalization. EDS confirmed higher oxygen and fluorine incorporation for LiF/HCl samples. Electrochemically, HF-etched MXene delivered a higher specific capacitance (1.905F g –1 ) than LiF/HCl MXene (0.934F g –1 ), but with higher charge-transfer resistance, whereas LiF/HCl MXene showed good charge-transfer kinetics. These structure–property correlations show that etching chemistry, rather than interlayer spacing, governs the capacitance-versus-charge-transfer trade-off, providing design guidance for next-generation energy storage devices. HF etching favours maximum capacitance, whereas LiF/HCl etching favours rate and durability-critical, the optimal choice is therefore application-dependent.

title: A brief review on optimizing biogenic selenium nanoparticle synthesis: parameters, mechanisms, and reporting standards (2020–2025)
abstract: Biogenic selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) are attractive for biomedical and agricultural–environmental uses, but their properties depend sensitively on process parameters. This method involves several parameters that can significantly influence the size, shape, and other properties of the biogenically synthesized SeNPs. These features directly affect the biological potential of the SeNPs. Therefore, creating efficient and suitable SeNPs with desired traits for effective biological applications requires a thorough understanding of these parameters. This mini–review critically synthesizes how pH, temperature, incubation time, precursor identity/molarity, extract: precursor ratio, and mixing influence nucleation, growth, and stability of SeNPs across plant– and microbe-mediated routes. Intracellular and extracellular synthesis mechanisms, reductase actions, and biomacromolecule encapsulation that govern nanoparticle formation and stabilization of the biogenic SeNPs are further explored. We compile typical operating windows reported from 2020 to 2025 and highlight mechanistic levers (reductant strength, caps, and mass transfer). This framework supports rational optimization and more reliable translation of SeNPs. Improved control over the SeNPs’ physicochemical properties is demonstrated via synthesis condition optimization and in-depth mechanistic insight. However, standardized reporting, reproducibility, and scalable manufacturing remain major challenges, and filling these gaps will facilitate the development of reliable, reproducible, and clinically translatable biogenic SeNPs for biomedical and industrial applications

title: The critical co-dependence of Nb and Mo on γ′/γ phase stability and creep resistance of Nimonic 80A superalloys
abstract: This study investigates the combined effects of minor Nb and Mo additions on the high-load creep behaviour of modified Nimonic 80A superalloys at 750 °C under 356 MPa.
