Finally, important challenges related to stability of defects, reproducible synthesis, techno-economic feasibility and commercialization are identified providing a roadmap for the development of scalable, intelligent and high-performance photocatalysts for hydrogen evolution, CO 2 reduction and nitrogen fixation.

title: Microstructure-informed creep residual-life assessment of Ni-based single-crystal superalloys using γ/γ′ degradation features
abstract: Residual-life assessment of Ni-based single-crystal superalloys is challenging because local temperature and stress histories in turbine blades are difficult to measure, while the creep-degraded γ/γ′ microstructure records prior thermo-mechanical exposure. Here, γ/γ′ degradation descriptors are used as experimentally accessible morphological state descriptors to develop a microstructure-informed two-stage physics-regularized model for the DD6 Ni-based single-crystal superalloy. In the first stage, γ-matrix channel width, rafting degree, γ′ volume fraction and creep exposure time are used to reconstruct the equivalent service state in terms of temperature and stress consistent with the current microstructural state. In the second stage, the reconstructed service state and microstructural descriptors are combined to predict creep residual life, with a condition-dependent channel-width relation and a channel-width-dependent Orowan–Garofalo formulation introduced as low-order physics regularization. Stage-wise validation, hold-out full-pipeline tests, and strict leave-one-condition-out validation show that introducing γ/γ′ degradation features and physics regularization improves the accuracy and consistency of service-state reconstruction and residual-life prediction within the investigated temperature–stress window. The proposed framework links microstructural degradation, equivalent service-state information, and creep life response, providing an interpretable route for creep residual-life assessment within the investigated DD6 experimental domain.

title: Novel approaches and physical Criteria for the scalable construction of metal single crystals
abstract: This study investigates the bonding behavior of bulk Cu single crystals under varying surface roughness and proposes a scalable construction strategy for single crystal integration based on atomic level bonding principles. Surfaces with distinct roughness from 6 nm to 185 nm were prepared using diamond turning and acid pickling. Results revealed that 20 ∼ 30 nm roughness allows three interface types—recrystallized, incomplete, and atomic level bonding—through parameter tuning. In contrast, 60 ∼ 80 nm roughness yields only recrystallized and incomplete interfaces, with atomic level bonding unattainable regardless of parameter adjustments. Based on these findings, a physical criterion is established, defining a critical surface roughness threshold of approximately 35 nm for atomic level bonding in Cu single crystals. The bonding process evolves through three stages: elastic contact expansion, creep-driven void elimination, and interfacial reconstruction for atomic continuity. This criterion can predict critical roughness for other metallic and alloy single crystal systems, including Ni-based superalloys and PST TiAl. Thus, this provides a reliable basis for producing large-sized, high-performance components from engineering alloy single crystals.

title: Composition-programmed PVA/Silk fibroin/chondroitin sulfate aligned electrospun nanofiber scaffold for annulus fibrosus repair
abstract: The annulus fibrosus (AF) is a hierarchically organized, anisotropic load-bearing tissue whose structural disruption contributes to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) and recurrent disc herniation. Effective AF repair requires a scaffold that not only fills the defect but also provides directional structural guidance, mechanical support, and regulation of the inflammatory-catabolic microenvironment. Here, we developed a composition-programmed polyvinyl alcohol/silk fibroin/chondroitin sulfate (PVA/SF/Cs) aligned electrospun nanofiber scaffold based on structure–property-biofunction relationships. By tuning the PVA/SF ratio and Cs loading, P5S5C10 was identified as the optimized formulation, producing uniform, highly aligned nanofibers and the best overall tensile, shear, and cyclic mechanical performance among the tested compositions. The aligned architecture provided native-like topographical cues that directed AF cell elongation and orientation while maintaining cell viability and proliferation. Under IL-1β-induced degenerative stimulation, Cs-containing scaffolds, particularly P5S5C10, attenuated inflammatory and catabolic responses and promoted extracellular matrix-related anabolic activity. In a rat AF defect model combined with local IL-1β challenge, P5S5C10 preserved disc height and hydration, maintained AF lamellar organization, promoted collagen I and aggrecan deposition, and reduced local IL-1β expression. These findings demonstrate a rational materials-design strategy in which compositional tuning integrates anisotropic structure, mechanical reinforcement, and immunoregulatory biofunction within a single scaffold for AF regeneration.

title: Intratracheal instillation of Janus biomimetic nanomotors for lung adenocarcinoma therapy
abstract: This study addresses the challenges associated with docetaxel (DTX) treatment in lung adenocarcinoma, including its poor solubility, limited tumor targeting, and significant side effects, by developing an active-targeting and self-propelling nanomotor delivered system. We constructed a Janus biomimetic nanomotor (Janus GOx@NM-DTX-NPs) coated with neutrophils membrane (NM) and glucose oxidase (GOx). This system leverages the innate tumor-targeting ability of neutrophils and utilizes GOx-catalyzed propulsion for deep tumor penetration. Its acid-sensitive core enables release DTX and gadolinium in the tumor tissues, while GOx-mediated glucose depletion synergistically enhances therapeutic and diagnostic efficacy. In an orthotopic lung cancer mouse model, the nanomotor demonstrated superior tumor targeting and penetration, significantly inhibited tumor growth, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and exhibited excellent biocompatibility. This study provides a promising platform for targeted, combination therapy and MRI diagnosis in lung cancer.

title: Pathogen-specific and non-leaching antibacterial coatings for textiles
abstract: Hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) are responsible for over 100,000 deaths annually in the US alone. Health care materials for wound dressings, hernia meshes, as well as hygiene products, are especially important to avoid HAIs. The methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) strain is a major contributor to HAIs. This study focuses on developing an efficient MRSA-specific antimicrobial coating for cellulose-based (Lyocell) and synthetic (polyurethane) textiles to efficiently kill MRSA. MRSA-specific targeting is achieved through the endolysin ClyF, which is as fusion protein immobilized on textiles using the material-binding peptide macaque histatin (MacHis). MacHis binding is very strong preventing leaching and proteolytic digest was not observed. ClyF targets various pathogenic bacterial species and interestingly, beneficial skin bacteria, like Corynebacterium and Cutibacterium that aid in wound healing, remain unaffected. ClyF-17x-MacHis-coated textiles reduce MRSA within a ≥ 4.6-log scale with minimal impact on skin microbiome. Notably, a combined application of the antibiotic levofloxacin fully eradicates mixed cultures of MRSA and P. aeruginosa; the latter effect cannot be achieved with either antimicrobial agent alone. The developed scalable antimicrobial coating offers high efficacy, low resistance, non-leaching properties, and pathogen-specificity, providing a promising coating platform with new treatment options to accelerate wound recovery from bacterial infections and address mixed infections that are hard to treat with individual therapeutic approaches.

title: Hybrid cell membrane-functionalized biomimetic nanozymes: Triple-modal CDT/PTT/PDT therapy activates apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and cuproptosis to eliminate breast cancer
abstract: Breast cancer is a highly prevalent malignant tumor among women. Traditional therapies suffer from inherent toxicity and drug resistance issues, while novel monomodal treatments have also failed to deliver satisfactory outcomes. To address these limitations, we developed a biomimetic nanoparticle system by preparing polydopamine (PDA)-modified Cu 2 [Fe(CN) 6 ] bimetallic nanozymes loaded with IR783 (a near-infrared photosensitizer) and encapsulated in hybrid cell membranes (TRCM), aiming to achieve highly efficient and precise breast cancer treatment. TRCM endowed the nanoparticles with immune evasion and breast cancer targeting capabilities, enhancing their accumulation at the tumor site. Simultaneously, TRCM@IPCu nanoparticles could deplete glutathione (GSH) to enhance reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, alleviate tumor hypoxia, and generate heat to initiate chemodynamic therapy (CDT), photodynamic therapy (PDT), and photothermal therapy (PTT), achieving synergistic CDT/PTT/PDT treatment. Mechanistic studies confirmed that TRCM@IPCu induced tumor cell death through multiple pathways including apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and cuproptosis, and significantly inhibited tumor growth in vivo. This approach offered novel insights for developing multifunctional nanozyme-based anti-breast cancer therapeutics.

title: Hierarchical crack-path regulation in Yb2SiO5/(Yb2SiO5–Yb2Si2O7)/Si environmental barrier coatings: mechanisms and design principles
abstract: The Yb 2 SiO 5 /(Yb 2 SiO 5 –Yb 2 Si 2 O 7 )/Si trilayer environmental barrier coating (EBC) has garnered significant attention in recent years for its excellent corrosion resistance and thermal compatibility with SiC f /SiC. Under thermal cycling, surface vertical cracks initiate and propagate downward, branch and coalesce within the interlayer, ultimately leading to coating delamination and failure. This study employs the finite element method to quantitatively elucidate the influence of interlayer composition and surface crack density on integrated crack propagation behavior. Three critical crack propagation mechanisms are systematically analyzed, including effect of inter-crack elastic shielding within Yb 2 SiO 5 top coat on suppressing the downward propagation, the competition between deflection and penetration at the Yb 2 SiO 5 /(Yb 2 SiO 5 –Yb 2 Si 2 O 7 ) interface, and composition-driving crack bifurcation geometry within the (Yb 2 SiO 5 –Yb 2 Si 2 O 7 ) interlayer. Based on these insights, an optimal surface crack geometry and interlayer compositions are proposed enables stable crack arrest, controlled interfacial deflection, and moderate-energy-dissipative branching, thereby maximizing structural toughness and extending service lifetime.

title: Replication of fusion tokamak plasma disruptions on Eurofer 97 steel using Magnum-PSI
abstract: Plasma disruptions will impose high magnitude, short duration radiative loads on the plasma-facing first wall of a commercial-scale tokamak, constituting a transient thermal ageing mechanism that affects the performance and lifetime of underlying structural and heatsink materials. In this work, the Magnum-PSI linear plasma device and an ancillary Nd:YAG laser were used to expose 9 samples of the structural steel Eurofer 97 to 1, 100, and 1000 reactor-representative thermal transients of 0.5, 1 and 3 ms duration. The resultant microstructural evolution was characterised via scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and microhardness mapping. A duration-dependent evolution of grain diameters, precipitate populations, and hardness were observed. Notably, after 1000 transients of 3 ms, evidence of dynamic recrystallisation, followed by grain coarsening was observed, accompanied by the dissolution of MX and M 23 C 6 precipitates. For the 1000 transient set, hardness reductions of 13%, 6.3%, and 11.2% for the 0.5, 1, and 3 ms respectively suggest a reduction of Hall-Petch strengthening and precipitate hardening contributions. A damage depth of 110–120 µm is estimated from analysis of precipitate depletion. This is supported by carbon diffusion length calculations and hardness mapping.

title: Numerical and experimental study of in-flight MgAl2O4 particles in atmospheric plasma spraying: Effect of arc current variation
abstract: A coupled numerical–experimental framework was developed to quantify the effects of arc-current variation on the plasma jet, in-flight MgAl 2 O 4 particles, and atmospheric plasma-sprayed coatings. The arc discharge and plasma flow inside the torch were simulated using OpenFOAM, while particle transport, heating, and two-way momentum–energy coupling were resolved in ANSYS FLUENT. Model predictions were evaluated against DPV measurements at a stand-off distance of 100 mm. Increasing the arc current from 400 to 600 A expanded the high-temperature and high-velocity plasma regions, enhanced particle heating and acceleration, increased the mass fraction of particles classified as molten from their calculated temperatures, and reduced particle escape. The calculated particle temperatures and velocities differed from measurements by 11.49–15.57% and 0.90–5.08%, respectively, demonstrating good predictive capability for particle velocity and reproduction of current-dependent trends. Coating thickness increased from 135 to 175 μm and Vickers hardness from 769 to 900, while porosity varied non-monotonically and reached 4.02% at 600 A. XRD detected no additional crystalline phase, whereas EDS revealed a slight decrease in the Mg/(Mg + Al) ratio with increasing current. Higher arc current therefore promoted particle deposition and coating densification, but process selection should balance these benefits against possible compositional deviation.

title: Reactive atmosphere fabrication of nanostructured alumina-forming austenitic alloys for nuclear applications
abstract: Although advanced austenitic alloys are advantageous in non-nuclear applications due to their high creep strength, designing irradiation-resistant austenitic alloys is challenging due to the difficulty of dispersing irradiation defect-capturing sinks uniformly throughout the material. In this work, nanostructured alumina-forming austenitic (NAFA) alloys were successfully produced with fine multi-precipitate dispersions of oxides and carbonitrides using a reactive atmosphere melting and solidification technique. Following processing, chemical composition analysis confirmed the successful uptake of oxygen within the BM variant and N 2 within the reactive atmosphere build; other compositions remained unchanged based on the processing methodology. It was found that due to the extended high temperature hold times associated with consolidation, that the HIP and BM variants exhibited low fracture toughness and lower strength at high temperature due to the nucleation of grain boundary intermetallic phases. Conversely, the LPBF-produced Ar and N 2 prints exhibited high tensile strength (900 MPa) and ductility (10%-30%) at 600 °C and fracture toughness values of approximately 100 MPa⋅m 1/2 . Printing in a nitrogen reactive atmosphere produces Y-rich oxides (10–20 nm diameter) and Zr/Nb-rich carbonitrides (20–30 nm diameter). These spatially anticorrelated precipitate distributions demonstrate the feasibility of multi-dispersion reactive element alloys that can be optimized for strength and irradiation resistance.

title: Laser surface alloying of titanium with WC-Co deposition: a super-hard facing layer
abstract: The focus of this research is on laser surface alloying and hardening of a commercial pure titanium (CP-Ti) substrate using a fiber laser beam as the energy source, with simultaneous variation of laser processing parameters (laser power and scanning speed) and the introduction of WC-Co micro-sized particles. Three different laser surface alloying strategies of localized heating, multi-pass overlapping, and surface composite fabrication by in situ alloying were implemented, and the extent of alloyed regions alongside the melt pool formation and heat-affected zone (HAZ) was investigated. For each processing state, different sets of laser parameters, in combination with power and scanning speed, were evaluated to determine the optimal working windows for surface hardening or alloying scenarios, yielding the best surface and cross-sectional appearances. Subsequently, microstructural evolution and possible phase transformations in the modified surface layers were studied using advanced microscopy techniques. Phase identification by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and chemical analysis by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) indicate a martensitic phase transformation of the titanium surface during laser melting, alloying, and solidification. The corresponding in situ formed nanoscale phases within the fusion zone (FZ) were further characterized by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). As the leading mechanical property for a “super hard-faced layer,” microhardness results showed increasing hardness in all remelted and alloyed specimens. Meanwhile, the FZ of the surface-alloyed CP-Ti/WC-Co material under the optimized processing parameters exhibited the highest indentation hardness of ∼2200 HV, corresponding to an increase of approximately 1500% compared to the primary state of the pure Ti substrate (∼150 HV), which is controlled by the martensitic transformation of pure titanium and by the strengthening effect of other in situ formed nanoscale secondary phases.

title: Low-cost soft robotic gripper – combining textile sensors and a lightweight hybrid CNN–LSTM model
abstract: Soft robotic grippers are compliant systems for object manipulation and interaction. However, most existing studies focus on individual components, such as materials or structural design, with limited system-level integration. This work presents a soft gripper system that integrates textile-based sensing, compliant actuation, and embedded machine learning within a unified architecture. The CNT-textile stretch sensor exhibits a gauge factor of 5.7 and stable operation over 5000 repeated loading cycles. The pressure sensor, with a thickness of 0.77 mm, achieves a sensitivity of 0.47 kPa −1 , a response/recovery time of 60/55 ms, and durability exceeding 5000 cycles. The soft fingers are fabricated from 3D-printed TPU with a fin-ray structure, enabling adaptive and conformal grasping. A lightweight convolutional neural network–long short-term memory (CNN–LSTM) model (1.09 MB) is deployed on edge hardware for object classification, achieving an overall accuracy of 95.68%. All sensing, preprocessing, and inference processes are executed locally on the embedded platform. A label-only transmission strategy is adopted, reducing payload size by approximately 99.6% compared with raw data streaming. The proposed system features a simple architecture, low fabrication cost, and high reproducibility. It provides a scalable and efficient framework for intelligent soft robotic manipulation with strong potential for practical deployment.

title: Coating of graphene oxide and alendronate sodium on poly-ether-ether-ketone to improve its antibacterial effect, surface bioactivity and osteogenic property
abstract: The bio-inertness and lacking of antimicrobial property limit further application of poly-ether-ether-ketone (PEEK) used in orthopaedics field. To solve the above problem, this study firstly prepared a layer of microporous structure on PEEK by sulfonation treatment, then polydopamine (PDA) was coated on the microporous surface to further fix graphene oxide (GO) and alendronate sodium (ALN) to acquired the SPD-GO/ALN sample. By the aid of the surface topology and chemistry, the SPD-GO/ALN sample exhibited superior hydrophilic property and revealed the long-term ALN release behavior, fitting well to the Korsmeyer-Peppas model. In-vitro biological experiments showed that the SPD-GO/ALN sample not only high-efficiently killed Escherichia coli and S. aureus by the GO-triggered reactive oxygen species generation, but also accelerated hydroxyapatite (HA) deposition, as well as promoted the osteoblastic adhesion, osteo-differentiation and extracellular matrix (ECM) mineralization of MC3T3-E1 cells. In addition, the mechanical properties of PEEK were maintained after surface modification, and the initial in-vivo results also confirmed the strong osteogenic activity of the prepared SPD-GO/ALN sample. These results show that composite-grafting of GO and ALN can confer PEEK surface dual functions of antimicrobial and osteogenic properties without compromising the mechanical properties, providing new insight to develop high-performance bone implants used in clinic.

title: Numerical investigation of an SNG metamaterial-based multiband THz biosensor for early non-melanoma skin cancer detection
abstract: This article presents a high-sensitivity terahertz (THz) metamaterial absorber–based biosensor for the early detection of non-melanoma skin cancer through refractive index sensing. The proposed sensor consists of a pair of concentric gear-shaped resonators (GSRs) fabricated from gold and integrated on a polyimide dielectric substrate, forming a compact unit cell with a periodicity of 75 µm. The designed metasurface exhibits multi-band resonance characteristics, with the highest absorption reaching 99.99 % at a resonance frequency of 1.4485 THz, demonstrating near-perfect absorption behavior. The structure also achieves a high-quality factor (Q-factor) of 1116.8, indicating strong electromagnetic confinement and excellent spectral selectivity. Comprehensive parametric analyses are performed to optimize the geometrical parameters and evaluate the stability of the absorption response under different polarization angles. The sensing performance is investigated by varying the refractive index of the surrounding medium within the biologically relevant range of 1.35–1.39, corresponding to normal and cancerous skin tissues. The proposed biosensor exhibits a clear and consistent resonance shift with refractive index variation, achieving a maximum sensitivity of 190 GHz/RIU and a figure of merit (FoM) of 146.49, confirming its capability to detect subtle dielectric variations in biological samples. Furthermore, the absorption response remains stable under polarization variations, highlighting the robustness of the design for practical sensing environments. These results demonstrate that the proposed THz metamaterial absorber provides a compact, highly sensitive, and reliable platform for label-free biomedical refractive index sensing, offering promising potential for early-stage skin cancer detection in terahertz diagnostic systems.

title: Design lattice metamaterials with pre-strain-enabled soft mode switching via topology optimization
abstract: Soft deformation modes govern the compliant response and elastic-wave characteristics of lattice metamaterials, but these modes are usually determined by the as-fabricated geometry. This study presents a topology-optimization framework that jointly designs lattice connectivity and prescribed pre-strain to tailor the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the tangent effective elasticity matrix. Prestress-dependent numerical homogenization accounts for changes in member geometry and the geometric stiffness generated by internal axial forces. The framework produces unimode lattices with prescribed soft-mode directions and bimode lattices with prescribed hard-mode directions. For two fixed topologies, independently selected pre-strain states give different nullmode, unimode, and bimode classifications; these results demonstrate state-dependent soft-mode reclassification but do not establish a continuous or reversible switching path. An additional screening procedure identifies lattices with limited changes in selected low-frequency dispersion branches under vertical compressive pre-strain. At compression, the maximum frequency shifts, normalized by the prescribed frequency upper bound, are approximately for the selected unimode lattice and for the selected bimode lattice over the evaluated branch–wave-vector pairs. A separate ANSYS Bloch-wave implementation provides consistent numerical results. The framework provides a computational approach for designing pre-strain-dependent soft-mode classifications and screening their low-frequency dispersion sensitivity.

title: Multifunctional conducting oxide metasurface for electrothermal heating and high optical and electromagnetic transparency
abstract: Ice accumulation on critical surfaces threatens the reliability of aviation, transportation, and infrastructure systems. Existing electrothermal anti-icing layers often rely on continuous conductive films, which can limit optical and microwave transmission. To address this challenge, this study presents a multifunctional conducting oxide metasurface that combines electrothermal heating capability with broadband electromagnetic transmission for transparent electrothermal components with potential anti-icing applications. The metasurface is fabricated by infrared laser patterning of an indium tin oxide (ITO) film on a flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate. The patterned structure improves microwave transmission over the 2–18 GHz band while maintaining high optical transparency and uniform electrothermal heating. The fabricated metasurface achieves a visible-light transmissivity of 88.6 % at 530 nm and a microwave transmissivity exceeding 77 % across the operating band, together with a uniform temperature distribution and a peak temperature of 64.6 °C at 75 V. The results indicate that the proposed ITO metasurface can increase microwave transmissivity while retaining continuous current paths for Joule heating, offering a promising route for transparent electrothermal anti-icing components.

title: Post-annealing-free heteroepitaxial growth of (2¯01)-oriented β-Ga2O3 thin films on c-plane sapphire by low-temperature laser-assisted RF sputtering
abstract: β-Ga 2 O 3 is a promising ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor for next-generation power electronics and deep-ultraviolet optoelectronics, but its epitaxial growth generally requires substrate temperatures above 600 ℃ or post-annealing. Here, we report post-annealing-free heteroepitaxial growth of ( 2 ¯ 01) -oriented β-Ga 2 O 3 thin films on c-plane sapphire using a 1064 nm ytterbium pulsed laser-assisted radio frequency magnetron sputtering process. Preferentially oriented β-Ga 2 O 3 films were formed at 100–400 ℃, and a well-defined ( 2 ¯ 01) -oriented heteroepitaxial film was obtained at 400 ℃. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the lowest substrate temperatures reported for sputtering-based β-Ga 2 O 3 heteroepitaxy without post-annealing. RF power control experiments confirmed that increasing RF power alone did not reproduce the orientation selective growth achieved under laser irradiation. X-ray diffraction (XRD), reciprocal space mapping, φ-scan, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM), and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) confirmed the epitaxial relationship of β-Ga 2 O 3 ( 2 ¯ 01) ||Al 2 O 3 (0001), with six in-plane rotational domains. The 400 ℃ film exhibited a sharp interface, a density of 6.34 g/cm 3 , and an optical bandgap of 4.95 eV. XPS showed enhanced Ga–O bonding and reduced oxygen-vacancy-related components at higher substrate temperatures. These results demonstrate laser-assisted RF sputtering as an effective low-thermal-budget route for β-Ga 2 O 3 heteroepitaxy on sapphire without post-annealing.

title: pH-responsive bromophenol blue/NH2-mPEGylated BSA@MnO2 nanoplatform for rectal cancer marking after neoadjuvant therapy
abstract: After neoadjuvant therapy (NT), precise localization of original tumor margins remains challenging. Here, we developed a pH-responsive BPB/NH2-mPEG-BSA@MnO2 (BBNPBMs) nanoplatform. BSA coating, NH 2 -mPEG modification, and BPB loading generated a (198.7 ± 5.43) nm composite structure, enabling long-term local retention, tumor microenvironment (TME) responsiveness, and synergistic naked-eye and MR visualization. BBNPBMs exhibited excellent dispersibility, stability, facile preparation and storage. Toxicological evaluation was favorable. Mn 2+ was primarily metabolized via liver, kidneys, and lymph nodes, and excreted in feces or urine. Under weakly acidic (pH 6.0–6.5) and oxidative conditions, MnO2 gradually degraded, continuously releasing paramagnetic Mn 2+ and enhancing T1-weighted MR signals. At 3.0 T, r1 and r2 reached 14.1 and 23.3 mM -1 s −1 , 3.34- and 4.41-fold higher than Magnevist® respectively, with imaging maintained > 30 days and visual marking > 90 days. Compared with carbon nanoparticle suspension injection (CNSI), BBNPBMs (200 μg/mL) showed a smaller diffusion area (1.38 ± 0.15 cm vs. 2.49 ± 0.40 cm, *P = 0.023). In summary, through the functional relationship of ‘pH response-gradual Mn 2+ release-visualization and long-term MR enhancement’, BBNPBMs meet localization requirements for 2–4 cycles of NT and demonstrate high translational potential.

title: Surface-Functionalized ZnO nanopads enhance angiogenesis and collagen remodeling for dermal regeneration
abstract: Cutaneous wound healing requires coordinated control of microbial burden, cellular responses, vascularization, and extracellular matrix organization. Here, we developed a surface-engineered wound dressing by post-fabrication decoration of electrospun poly(ε-caprolactone)–collagen (PCL–Coll) nanofibrous scaffolds with biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). The ZnO-decorated scaffolds were characterized physicochemically and evaluated for Zn 2 ⁺ release, antibacterial activity, and human dermal fibroblast responses in vitro, followed by assessment in a full-thickness excisional wound model in rats. The surface-engineered scaffolds exhibited sustained biphasic Zn 2 ⁺ release over the 10-day observation period, together with antibacterial activity and favorable fibroblast compatibility. In vivo , PCL–Coll/ZnO treatment accelerated wound closure compared with the control groups and was associated with improved histological tissue repair and collagen organization. Histomorphometric and immunohistochemical findings were consistent with a vascularization-associated regenerative response, while increased Col1a1 and Col3a1 expression indicated a collagen-related transcriptional response during healing. The surface-engineered nanopads facilitate the transition of the wound microenvironment toward a more organized and physiologically regenerative state. Finally, these findings demonstrate that post-fabrication ZnO surface decoration of PCL–Coll nanofibrous scaffolds provides a promising multifunctional platform for antibacterial and regenerative wound-dressing applications.

title: Structure–function insights into magnesium distribution and release in co-axial pellet-printed biomaterials via nano-CT and high-throughput image analysis
abstract: Magnesium-releasing scaffolds can enhance bone regeneration, but their performance depends on the controlled spatial distribution of magnesium sources and the resulting release behaviour. Here, we present an integrated analytical framework that combines nano-computed tomography (nano-CT), high-throughput automated image analysis using CellProfiler, and magnesium-ion release quantification to evaluate co-axial pellet-printed biomaterials with a core–shell architecture. This approach extends nano-CT analysis beyond qualitative structural imaging by enabling objective, large-scale quantification of internal scaffold features, including magnesium-particle morphometrics and core–shell proportions. By linking these structural parameters with experimentally measured release profiles and biocompatibility outcomes, we establish a direct structure–function relationship showing how scaffold architecture governs magnesium transport and cellular response. This imaging–analysis–performance workflow provides a reproducible and scalable strategy for designing and optimising complex multimaterial scaffolds for bone tissue engineering.

title: Energy absorption of additively manufactured PLA/PCTG plate vs. Truss lattices under normal and oblique impact: Topology- and carbon-fibre-reinforcement effects
abstract: This study establishes an architecture–material framework for additively manufactured polymer lattices by comparing plate and truss analogues at 30% nominal relative density under normal and oblique low-velocity impact. Simple cubic (SC), face-centred cubic (FCC), and body-centred cubic (BCC) lattices were fabricated by fused filament fabrication from polylactic acid (PLA), polycyclohexylene dimethylene terephthalate glycol-modified (PCTG), and their short-carbon-fibre (CF)-reinforced counterparts. Performance was assessed using peak contact force, specific energy absorption, mean crushing force, crushing force efficiency, micro-CT porosity, and high-speed imaging. Under normal impact, PLA plates absorbed 34–50 J versus 3.5–13 J for matched trusses because continuous walls preserved load paths after damage initiation. Carbon-fibre effects were matrix dependent: CF/PLA increased bulk absorbed energy from 170 to 184 J, whereas CF/PCTG decreased it from 180 to 126 J and exhibited 6% porosity versus 2% for CF/PLA. The plate–truss contrast persisted under oblique impact, although topology, printing- and fibre-induced anisotropy, and contact kinematics modified the response. Across 0°, 25°, and 45°, the CF/PLA FCC plate maintained 43–48 J absorbed energy and 11.8–14.4 kN peak contact force, providing a balanced multi-metric response. Crashworthy lattice design requires coordinated control of architecture, material, print quality, and loading direction.

title: Chemical durability and surface modifications of PGM doped UO2 pellets under long-term wet interim repository conditions
abstract: The corrosion behavior of dense UO 2 pellets, either undoped or doped with Platinum Group Metals (PGMs: Ru, Rh and Pd), was investigated under conditions representative of wet interim storage in spent fuel cooling pools. For this study, sintered pellets of UO 2 containing PGMs as metallic inclusions were prepared by hydroxide precipitation, followed by high-temperature sintering at 1500°C and 1600°C, then characterized. Long-term leaching experiments were conducted in boric acid solution (2,500 ppm H 3 BO 3 , pH = 5) at 50°C for up to 1,385 days. Uranium release, surface alteration products, and solution chemistry were characterized to understand the mechanisms controlling corrosion. Under mildly oxidizing conditions, uranium normalized leaching rates remained low, confirming that corrosion was primarily controlled by the slow oxidation of U(IV) by dissolved dioxygen. Prior to uranium saturation, normalized leaching rates were (1.3 ± 0.2) × 10 −3 g.m −2 .d −1 for PGM-doped pellets and (6.0 ± 2.0) × 10 −4 g.m −2 .d −1 for undoped UO 2 . The presence of PGMs induced only a slight increase in uranium release, indicating a limited catalytic effect in the absence of strong oxidants. However, PGMs significantly altered the corrosion pathway. Undoped UO 2 followed a classical oxidative mechanism involving the formation of hyperstoichiometric UO 2+x and U 3 O 7 surface phases, whereas PGM-doped materials exhibited a dissolution–reprecipitation process leading to the formation of secondary U(VI) phases, including metaschoepite and uranium hydroxides. After approximately 250 days, precipitation of these secondary phases reduced the reactive surface area and controlled long-term corrosion kinetics. These results demonstrate that PGMs slightly accelerate UO 2 corrosion and modify the alteration mechanism through microstructural effects and the formation of secondary phase.

title: Nanoscale gradient grain structure formation on selective laser melted (SLM) FeCoCrNiMn alloy surface by single point diamond cutting
abstract: In this study, single-point diamond cutting was employed to successfully generate a nanoscale gradient grain structure on the surface of a selective laser-melted FeCoCrNiMn high-entropy alloy, leading to significant enhancement of its mechanical properties. Cutting depth critically influences gradient-structure evolution, with 4 μm yielding finer layering and better surface quality than 16 μm. The evolution mechanism of the nanoscale gradient structure is revealed to be governed by the coupled effects of geometrically necessary dislocation accumulation, grain refinement, grain boundary evolution, deformation twinning, and face-centred cubic to hexagonally closed packed phase transformation. Smaller cutting depths promote localized shear deformation, increasing the fractions of high-angle grain boundaries and the hexagonally closed packed phase, whereas larger cutting depths favor the formation of twin-related low-angle grain boundaries through expansion of the shear-affected layer. These structural changes enhance resistance to plastic deformation and improve the strain accommodation capability of the machined surface. These findings demonstrate that single-point diamond cutting is an effective post-processing strategy for generating nanoscale gradient grain structures and enhancing the mechanical performance of additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.

title: Microstructure and solidification morphology of Stellite 6 superalloy during laser-based directed energy deposition
abstract: This study presented a quantitative approach for understanding the process-microstructure-properties relationship during laser-based directed energy deposition of Stellite 6. Laser power, scan speed, powder feed rate, and number of layers were systematically changed. Dilution decreased from 19% to 9% as the scanning speed increased from 8 to 18 mm/s, and was further reduced by increasing the powder feed rate. Coating microhardness increased as specific energy density decreased. Specimens fabricated with specific energy densities of 46.2 and 90 J·s/g·mm exhibited hardness values above 800 HV. Solidification morphology and secondary dendrite arm spacing were characterized, revealing dendrite refinement and a columnar-to-equiaxed transition at lower energy input. X-ray diffraction revealed FCC and HCP cobalt phases, while carbides such as Cr 7 C 3 and Cr 23 C 6 were observed mainly in the interdendritic regions. Nanoindentation of dendritic and interdendritic regions showed that interdendritic nanohardness was about 1.8–1.9 times higher than in dendrite cores, consistent with the higher carbide fraction in these regions. Calculation of elastic–plastic parameters showed that the continuous carbide network acted as a strong barrier to dislocation motion and reduced the work-hardening capacity. Wear tests demonstrated that the specimen with the lowest energy input (E = 46 J·s/g·mm) combined higher hardness with improved wear resistance.

title: Flexible tabletop modular milligram extrusion line for polymer processing in high-throughput
abstract: We present a flexible, tabletop, milligram-throughput extrusion line (µX) for rapid, low-material polymer processing and data-rich experimentation. The platform combines a custom 8 mm single screw (L/D = 8) with a modular downstream temperature-control block, three additional thermal zones, and in-line pressure sensing. Long-chain-branched polypropylene (PP) was used as a model material to define the operating window as a function of screw speed, die diameter (0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 mm), and temperature. Under steady operation at 220 °C, mass flow increased with screw speed before reaching a pressure- and torque-limited plateau. An optional oscillatory downstream-conditioning mode produced reproducible coupled temperature–pressure oscillations (approximately 10–40 bar), demonstrating thermo-rheological process sensitivity without establishing changes in crystallinity, morphology, or final properties. Copper particles provided an initial assessment of distributive mixing: particle counts were reasonably uniform at the filament scale, while residual local clusters showed incomplete dispersive mixing. Steady-state generalized-Newtonian CFD reproduced the onset and die-diameter dependence of torque-limited operation at an engineering level, but is not considered quantitatively validated for local viscoelastic stresses or mixing. The µX therefore provides a modular, continuous, low-inventory platform for controlled studies with scarce formulations; extension beyond the PP grade studied here requires material-specific validation.

title: Microstructure, interfacial characteristics and dry sliding tribology of surface-localised SiO2/304SS transition layer reinforced maraging steel composite
abstract: A surface-localised SiO 2 -reinforced maraging steel (MAS) composite with a 304 stainless steel transition interlayer was fabricated by layered powder stacking and spark plasma sintering. The Fe-18Ni-4.5Mo-0.5Ti-8.5Co matrix supported a mixed SiO 2 /304SS (1:1) surface layer. Post-sintering, SiO 2 particles were uniformly embedded in the metallic layer with continuous, pore- and crack-free interfaces. EDS/EBSD revealed narrow elemental interdiffusion and refined grain orientation, with elevated KAM near the particles (median 0.2955° and 0.2323° in the two particle regions) attributable to local plastic constraint and thermal mismatch. Compared with monolithic steel, the composite reduced the average coefficient of friction by 21%–42% and the pin wear rate by 45%–96% under all tested loads (25–100 N), with the largest advantage at low loads. At higher loads (75–100 N), particle fracture and pull-out generated hard SiO 2 -containing debris that promoted three-body abrasive wear, weakening the performance advantage and increasing the wear of the GCr15 counterpart. The improved tribological performance is attributed to the surface-localised architecture, the crack-free reinforcement/matrix interface and the constrained deformation of the metallic matrix. The 304SS constituent is inferred to act as a ductile bridging medium that facilitates interfacial bonding, although its individual contribution could not be isolated without dedicated reference samples. These findings establish interface-structure-wear correlations for surface-localised composites and provide a potential design concept for lightweight, wear-resistant maraging-steel components for precision mould applications.

title: In situ synchrotron investigation of the microstructural heterogeneity induced on alloy 718 by laser melting
abstract: Laser processing of high-temperature Ni-base alloys offers high precision, reliability, and design flexibility, but can significantly affect microstructural stability and thus the overall reliability of components. In this context, this study evaluates the microstructural evolution of Inconel Alloy 718 during laser melting, focusing on the formation of microstructural gradients and the effects of laser reheating and remelting. An experimental synchrotron setup enabling parallel laser melting and in situ high-energy X-ray diffraction was developed. Combined with ex situ analyses, this setup allowed the evolution of the main phases to be tracked during processing, together with oxidation mechanisms and lattice distortion. Laser incidence caused the dissolution of γ′, γ″, and δ phases, while reheating promoted reprecipitation of γ′ and γ″. Reheating also increased the fraction of MC carbides and the Laves phase. Oxidation in air was dominated by Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, and NiCr₂O₄, with a shell-like morphology observed for the former two oxides. Significant γ lattice distortion was detected, showing a transition from expansion to contraction when a given region experienced reheating and/or partial remelting.

title: Ultrasound-assisted synthesis of porous cerium based metal–organic frameworks for microenvironment regulation and neural function repair in traumatic brain injury
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a significant cause of death and disability. After TBI, a large amount of reactive oxygen species (ROS) is generated, which triggers oxidative stress, destroys blood–brain barrier, induces inflammation, neuronal apoptosis and neurological damage. Therefore, regulating ROS balance is crucial for improving the prognosis of TBI. Nano antioxidant materials provide ideas for coping with ROS, among which metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have attracted attention due to their diverse structures, high porosity and excellent catalytic performance. Cerium MOFs exhibit CAT-like and SOD-like activities through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ cycling. However, the traditional hydrothermal method for synthesizing Ce-MOF suffers from problems such as time-consuming, energy consuming and uneven morphology, therefore urgently requires green and efficient preparation strategies. This paper employed an ultrasound assisted method to rapidly prepare spherical porous Ce based MOF (SP-Ce-MOF), using self-assembled micelles as soft templates. The introduction of ultrasound promoted the rapid occurrence of coordination reactions. The SP-Ce-MOF exhibited excellent antioxidant activity and effectively alleviated neuronal oxidative damage. Besides, neuroprotective drug curcumin (Cur) was loaded to construct Cur@SP-Ce-MOF, which effectively restored neural function and reduced neuronal apoptosis, providing a promising novel strategy for TBI therapy.

title: Process optimization of LIG preparation by CO2 and UV laser based on data-driven learning
abstract: Laser-induced graphene (LIG), produced via chemical-free laser ablation of polyimide, holds great promise for applications in heating elements and temperature sensors. However, the strong sensitivity of the fabrication process to laser parameters necessitates extensive experimental trials. In this study, a data-driven optimization strategy is proposed for achieving high-quality LIG using a glass-tube CO 2 laser under ambient conditions. Through a comprehensive set of experiments, a quantitative relationship was established between key laser parameters (e.g., laser power) and sheet resistance. After screening the machine learning models, the GBR model was identified as the optimal model for CO 2 laser-fabricated LIG. To assess generalizability, the workflow was extended to a UV picosecond laser system, where the decision tree regressor (DTR) was identified as the optimal model. Following optimization, the glass-tube CO 2 laser yielded a minimum sheet resistance of 4.28 Ω/sq with a prediction deviation rate of only 1.86 %, while the CO 2 laser also produced even lower resistance. Measurement reliability was ensured by repeated random sampling under identical conditions. The optimized LIG was integrated into heating and sensing devices, demonstrating efficient Joule heating, temperature sensing, and stable flexible response. This data-driven paradigm offers a new route for high-quality, scalable fabrication of LIG in flexible electronics.

title: Platinum-Enhanced MXene Nanocomposites Attenuate Liver Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Dual Targeting of Oxidative Stress and Inflammation
abstract: Hepatic ischemia–reperfusion injury (HIRI), a critical factor in postoperative complications and early liver dysfunction following hepatic surgery or transplantation, remains a formidable challenge in clinical management. Capitalizing on the liver’s unique hepatic first-pass effect and mononuclear phagocyte system, which facilitate nanoparticle-liver interactions and enhance nanomedicine uptake, we design and engineer a multifunctional two-dimensional (2D) soybean phospholipid (SP)-modified platinum-loaded niobium carbide MXene heterojunction (Nb 2 C-Pt@SP). This heterojunction achieves the dual targeting of oxidative stress and inflammation for effective HIRI management. The Nb 2 C matrix not only enables stable dispersion of Pt clusters and efficiently suppresses their aggregation but also promotes interfacial electron transfer, collectively endowing the nano-heterojunction with excellent antioxidant capacity for the management of HIRI. In vivo experiments demonstrated that intravenous administration of Nb 2 C-Pt@SP significantly decreased serum levels of liver enzymes by 60%-80% and decreased the necrotic area by over 50%, effectively alleviating HIRI. The therapeutic mechanism involves the capability of Nb 2 C-Pt@SP nanosystem to inhibit Kupffer cell and monocyte/macrophage activation while suppressing ROS-related parthanatos through its potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. These findings collectively position Nb 2 C-Pt@SP as a highly promising nanotherapeutic platform for the prevention and treatment of HIRI, thereby expanding the biomedical application scope of MXene-based nanomaterials.

title: Effect of titanium surface roughness on macrophage-bacteria interactions
abstract: Surface roughness of titanium implants enhances osseointegration but increases susceptibility of bacterial infection. At the same time, macrophages play a key role in bacterial clearance in infected implants. Here, we investigated the impact of titanium surface characteristics in three clinically approved implants on macrophage–bacteria interactions. We observed that increased surface roughness alters the balance of M1 and M2 macrophage phenotypes. Specifically, during the early phase of infection (within 12 h), the proportion of M1 macrophages increases with higher surface roughness, favoring a pro-inflammatory, bactericidal response. In contrast, at later stages (12–24 h), M2 macrophages become more prevalent, accompanied by a reduction in reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and a transition towards tissue repair and immune resolution. In addition, proteomic profiling reveals that these phenotypic transitions are mediated through key pathways, including chemokine signaling, sphingolipid signaling, estrogen response, necrotic and endocytic processes, and HIF-1 signaling. These findings provide insights into how surface topography modulates immune dynamics during implant-associated infection.

title: Simultaneously enhancing impact toughness and fracture toughness of TB18 high-strength titanium alloy through heterogeneous α precipitation
abstract: Architecting heterostructured titanium (Ti) alloys to harness mechanical potential is gaining significant traction. However, recent research has predominantly mitigated the strength-ductility trade-off, with limited attention devoted to impact toughness and fracture toughness, which are two critical mechanical attributes for structural reliability under dynamic and overload conditions. Here, we employ a counterintuitive approach that utilizes sub‑saturated precipitation to generate a heterogeneous α-phase morphology that simultaneously enhances the impact and fracture toughness in industrial high-strength TB18 titanium alloy bars via a simple reduction of the aging duration within the conventional heat treatment, with Charpy impact energy (∼18.3 J) and fracture toughness (93.9 MPa·m 1/2 ) increasing by ∼48 % and ∼29 % over homogeneous samples. In impact tests, precipitation free zones (PFZs) enable sufficient plastic deformation before crack propagation, cooperating with surrounding precipitation zones (PZs) to enlarge plastic affected zones (PAZs) and delay crack initiation, improving impact toughness. In three-point bending, PFZs adjacent to the main crack undergo pronounced plastic flow during crack propagation, triggering cooperative deformation in PZs and expanding PAZs, markedly raising fracture toughness. Hence, PFZs plastic activation governs overall toughness enhancement. These findings offer an industrially feasible route for achieving high combined toughness in age hardening structural materials under dynamic and overloaded conditions.

title: Zinc oxide nanoparticle-based nanosystem elicits anti-cancer activity against lymphoma cell lines by inducing ROS-dependent apoptosis without promoting necroptosis or ferroptosis
abstract: Nanotechnology-based agents have emerged as potential drug candidates for hematological malignancies. Particularly, functionalized or polymer-coated nanomaterials demonstrate superior effectiveness and safety compared to monocomponent nanoparticles (NPs). We evaluated the anti-lymphoma effect of a two-component nanosystem composed of a star-like dextran-graft-polyacrylamide (D-PAA) polymer and ZnO NPs, referred to as D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc), focusing on the ability of this nanosystem to induce different cell death pathways in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cell lines. IC 50 values were in 1 mM range, suggesting good anti-lymphoma activity. Analysis of regulated cell death pathways revealed that D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc) induced apoptosis, as evidenced by caspase-3/7 activation and phosphatidylserine externalization, with no noticeable involvement of necroptosis or ferroptosis. Oxidative stress appears to play a key role in D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc)-induced death of DLBCL cells. Analysis of potential apoptosis-regulating signaling pathways demonstrated that D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc) promoted reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, lipid peroxidation, and a compensatory increase of intracellular levels of reduced glutathione. Additionally, increased intracellular Fe 2+ levels could contribute to D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc)-induced oxidative stress. As a compensatory mechanism, D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc)-induced toxicity against DLBCL cell lines was associated with AKT (protein kinase B) activation. The D-PAA/ZnONPs(−OAc) nanosystem is a promising apoptosis-inducing agent that can be further investigated as a potential anti-lymphoma nanodrug.

title: Metal scaffolds for bone tissue engineering: materials, challenges, and clinical prospects
abstract: Bone scaffolds remain essential in bone tissue engineering, with the material choice dictating both mechanical and regenerative success. Compared to polymers and ceramics, metallic scaffolds are highly valued for their superior strength and stability in load-bearing applications. Non-degradable metals, including titanium, tantalum, and stainless steel, provide excellent support but face significant challenges like stress shielding, wear debris, and the need for secondary removal surgeries. Conversely, degradable metals like magnesium, zinc, and iron offer temporary support while resorbing. However, their clinical use is currently hindered by uncontrolled corrosion kinetics, premature loss of mechanical integrity, and excessive ion release. Furthermore, cobalt-based alloys and nitinol are studied for their wear resistance and shape-memory traits, yet mismatched mechanics and poor biological integration restrict broader application. To overcome these critical hurdles, contemporary research emphasizes innovative alloy design, topology and porosity optimization, hybridization with polymers or ceramics, and advanced surface engineering through coating and functionalization. This review systematically categorizes these metallic biomaterials into non-degradable and degradable classes, thoroughly evaluating their inherent properties and clinical limitations. Finally, we highlight emerging alternative approaches and discuss future directions toward developing multifunctional metallic scaffolds that seamlessly combine mechanical reliability, bioactivity, and long-term safety for effective bone regeneration.

title: Tailoring microstructure and hardness of modified PH 13-8 Mo manufactured using DED-LB through interlayer temperature control and post-processing heat treatments
abstract: This study investigates the effect of interlayer temperature control and post-processing heat treatments on the microstructure and hardness of modified pH 13-8 Mo manufactured using directed energy deposition with a laser beam and powder (DED-LB/p). Modified pH 13-8 Mo blocks were deposited at controlled interlayer temperatures. By controlling the interlayer temperature (180 ± 5 °C) above the M s temperature, a relatively homogeneous microstructure and hardness (344 ± 7 HV 0.2 ) were achieved in the as-deposited material. The average hardness of the depositions increased to 366 ± 15 HV 0.2 and 397 ± 32 HV 0.2 as interlayer temperatures (100 ± 5 °C and 30 ± 5 °C) decreased below the M s temperature, accompanied by a transition from a more homogeneous to a heterogeneous microstructure, driven by the intrinsic heat treatment during deposition. Additionally, the blocks were subjected to post-processing solution heat treatment, which reduced microstructural variations, leading to comparable hardness values regardless of interlayer temperature. The highest average hardness (528 HV 0.2 ) across all interlayer temperatures was achieved after solution heat treatment followed by aging. These findings highlight the potential and effectiveness of interlayer temperature control and post-processing heat treatments to tailor the microstructure and hardness of modified pH 13-8 Mo manufactured by DED-LB/p.

title: Corrigendum to “Stress-relaxation-informed thermo-metallurgical-mechanical modeling of residual stress and distortion for LDED of TA15 alloy” [Mater. Design 270 (2026) 116882]
Photothermal responsive pine pollen-derived hemostatic agent accelerates infected wound healing through rapid hemostasis and antibacterial action
abstract: Designing multifunctional bio-derived hemostatic materials that simultaneously achieve rapid hemostasis, antibacterial activity, and inflammatory microenvironment regulation remains challenging for infected wound treatment. Herein, a pollen-derived multifunctional hemostatic agent (PP@TFe) was rationally engineered by integrating the hierarchical porous architecture of carbonized pine pollen with a tannic acid-Fe 3 ⁺ metal-phenolic network. The porous multi-chamber structure promotes rapid blood absorption and blood component enrichment, while the TA-Fe 3 ⁺ coating provides NIR-responsive photothermal conversion, and antioxidant activity. PP@TFe reduced the whole-blood clotting time to 69.7 ± 4.0 s and achieved over 90% antibacterial efficiency against three representative bacterial strains under NIR irradiation. In rat hemorrhage and infected full-thickness wound models, PP@TFe reduced blood loss, decreased bacterial burden, improved the wound immune microenvironment, and accelerated tissue repair. These findings demonstrate how natural porous architecture and surface coordination chemistry can be integrated to couple hemostasis, infection control, and wound-microenvironment regulation.

title: Climate-responsive durability of 3D-printed concrete: a critical review from materials design to field performance
abstract: Three-dimensional concrete printing enables automated, formwork-free, and resource-efficient fabrication of cementitious components. However, its layered architecture creates climate-dependent durability risks that conventional concrete tests and homogeneous transport assumptions cannot adequately capture. This critical review develops a climate-process-microstructure-transport-degradation-durability framework for 3D-printed concrete and evaluates evidence across five performance-based exposure regimes: cold, marine, hot-arid, hot-humid, and temperate. The evidence identifies connected interfaces, filament boundaries, cold joints, surface defects, and non-uniform curing as pathway amplifiers that govern directional transport and localized damage. These effects remain strongly dependent on material, printer, geometry, orientation, and protocol. Moreover, the importance of test orientation, interlayer interval, curing, and component-scale and geometry variability are highlighted. Accordingly, reported data are translated into evidence-informed mixture-process-curing design ranges with climate-specific validation criteria rather than universal limits. Furthermore, transport reporting in three directions, interface-sensitive durability metrics, and an evidence-maturity hierarchy from printed coupons to monitored field structures are proposed. Service-life calculations remain system-specific and model-assisted until anisotropy, interfaces, curing, component scale, and field exposure are incorporated and validated.

title: Correlation of deformation mechanisms and crystallization kinetics in bulk metallic glasses
abstract: The correlation between deformation behavior and crystallization kinetics was systematically investigated for three Zr-based bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) with all metallic constituents, namely Zr 35.0 Ti 30.0 Cu 7.5 Be 27.5, Zr 46.8 Ti 8.2 Cu 7.5 Ni 10.0 Be 27.5 , and Zr 52.5 Cu 17.9 Ni 14.6 Al 10.0 Ti 5.0 . The compressive plasticity of the alloys was 10.5%, 3.5%, and 2% for Zr 35.0 Ti 30.0 Cu 7.5 Be 27.5, Zr 46.8 Ti 8.2 Cu 7.5 Ni 10.0 Be 27.5 , and Zr 52.5 Cu 17.9 Ni 14.6 Al 10.0 Ti 5.0 , respectively. The shear transformation zone (STZ) volume of the alloys was determined to be ∼ 8.0, 6.0, and 5.0 nm 3 for Zr 35.0 Ti 30.0 Cu 7.5 Be 27.5 , Zr 46.8 Ti 8.2 Cu 7.5 Ni 10.0 Be 27.5 , and Zr 52.5 Cu 17.9 Ni 14.6 Al 10.0 Ti 5.0 , respectively, with relatively larger STZ volume for the alloy that showed greater plasticity. The activation energy of crystallization was found to correlate inversely with plasticity, where alloys with lower activation energy exhibited superior plastic deformation behavior. This was attributed to lower structural stability of the alloys with lower crystallization activation energy, which may promote greater degree of local atomic rearrangements and distributed shear-band activity during deformation.

title: Topology guided evaluation of additively manufactured lattice separators: flow resistance characteristics and separation efficiency
abstract: Additively manufactured lattice media provide deterministic pore structures for compact gas liquid separation, but the topology rules that simultaneously govern flow resistance, droplet capture and mechanical reliability remain unclear. In this paper, a topology guided multi performance evaluation framework is established for laser powder bed fused Ti-6Al-4 V lattice separator media. Twelve TPMS and strut-based lattices with comparable relative density were constructed and screened by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of airflow and oil droplet transport. Four representative topologies were fabricated and evaluated by quasi-static compression and in situ micro computed tomography (CT) digital volume correlation (DVC). The results show that separation performance is governed by the spatial arrangement of pore channels rather than relative density or specific surface area alone. STR-B provides the lowest pressure drop due to open straight-through channels but poor droplet capture. STR-I gives nearly complete separation and the highest energy absorption at the cost of a large pressure penalty. STR-D achieves the most favorable transport balance by introducing inclined channels and repeated non-parallel impingement surfaces. In situ CT DVC further reveals topology dependent damage modes. These findings demonstrate how topology can balance pressure drop, separation efficiency and compression tolerance in multifunctional porous metallic media.

title: Sequence-responsive biomimetic double-network hydrogel coordinating physical isolation, inflammation modulation, and physiological regeneration to prevent postoperative peritoneal adhesions
abstract: Postoperative intra-abdominal adhesions present a significant clinical challenge following abdominal and pelvic surgeriesTraditional physical barriers offer only passive isolation, failing to address the dynamic inflammatory microenvironment and abnormal fibrotic remodeling at the injured site. Grounded in the physiological sequence of tissue healing, we developed a genipin-crosslinked hyaluronic acid/chitosan (CS/HA) double-network hydrogel dual-loaded with emodin and mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (CS/HA-Exo-Emo). The genipin-mediated dynamic Schiff base crosslinking endows the hydrogel with an interconnected porous structure, superior wet-tissue adhesiveness (102.3 kPa), and exceptional anti-swelling performance, ensuring robust physical isolation in liquid environments. In a mouse model of cecal-abdominal wall injury, the CS/HA-Exo-Emo hydrogel significantly minimized adhesion formation (scoring 1.33 ± 0.58 compared to 4.67 ± 0.58 in controls). Histological and immunofluorescence analyses revealed that the joint incorporation of bioactive agents orchestrates a sequence-responsive therapeutic effect: the early action of emodin markedly suppresses inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α) and inhibits aberrant collagen deposition, while the sustained biological effect of exosomes upregulated VEGFA expression, thereby transitioning the microenvironment from inflammation to physiological angiogenesis and functional tissue regeneration. This multifunctional hydrogel system marks a critical shift from passive barrier isolation to active, sequence-responsive microenvironment orchestration, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for advanced postoperative anti-adhesion management.

title: Influence of nitrogen flow on the mechanical properties of multilayers for the design of metal nitride coatings
abstract: This work proposes two distinct methods to characterise mechanically and structurally Ti 0.54 Al 0.46 N/Ti 0.67 Al 0.33 multilayer coatings, referred to as TiAlN/TiAl respectively deposited by reactive gas pulsing process. In the first method, the properties of the coating are supposed to be driven by the volume fraction of TiAlN ( V f ). To directly quantify this volume fraction from mechanical response, an analytical model and a finite element model representing an equivalent homogenized multilayered coating were calibrated. Similar results are found for both models: an imbalance between TiAl and TiAlN lead to an increase of V f with the decrease of the period Λ . The second method consists of evaluating the mechanical properties of the interface between adjacent layers through density functional theory and molecular dynamics calculations. The results indicate that the interfaces exhibit a higher hardness and elastic modulus than predicted by a rule of mixtures. This enhancement is attributed to the presence of nitrogen within the transition layer. A very good correlation is observed between V f and 1 / Λ suggesting that the mechanical properties of any multilayer with a particular period value can be extrapolated.

title: Advanced bioprinting for cell-based bone engineering
abstract: The precise repair of bone injuries and large-area bone defects is a major challenge in the field of regenerative medicine. Traditional bone grafting strategies are limited by donor scarcity and insufficient bioactivity, while the emergence of 3D bioprinting technology offers the possibility of constructing personalized, highly porous biomimetic scaffolds. To overcome the limitation of insufficient bioactivity in synthetic scaffolds alone, this paper focuses on multicellular bioprinting strategies combining stem cells (such as mesenchymal stem cells, MSCs) with non-stem cells (such as vascular endothelial cells, osteoblasts, etc.). This system, by co-loading multipotent stem/progenitor cells and functionally defined non-stem cells into advanced bioink systems, can mimic the complex cellular composition and spatial microenvironment of natural bone tissue. Stem cells provide long-term regenerative potential and immunomodulation, while non-stem cells, through direct bone matrix secretion or rapid initiation of vascularization, form significant synergistic effects with stem cells. Research indicates that this multicellular integrated printing solution can not only precisely regulate the anatomical structure of bone tissue but also has shown the potential to enhance blood supply reconstruction and functional bone regeneration. This bio-driven approach, combining the multipotency of stem cells with the functional advantages of non-stem cells, provides a preclinical rationale for future translation for the efficient repair of complex bone defects.

title: Energy-harvesting conductive materials: a material-structure synergy framework for self-powered chronic wound healing
abstract: Chronic wounds, especially diabetic ulcers, are sustained by persistent inflammation, infection, impaired angiogenesis, delayed re-epithelialization, extracellular matrix dysregulation, and metabolic imbalance. Bioelectrical signaling is not the sole driver of repair but provides a biophysical regulatory layer affecting immune responses, cell migration, vascularization, and tissue remodeling. Conventional electrical stimulation is hampered by reliance on external power sources and by inconsistent delivery across moist, mechanically compliant wound beds. Energy-harvesting conductive biomaterials offer a path toward self-powered intervention; however, therapeutic efficacy depends on far more than maximal electrical output. This Review proposes a material–structure synergy framework that connects intrinsic attributes—energy conversion, charge transport, catalytic function, and biological properties—with structure-governed behaviors including tissue contact, mechanical compliance, mass transport, and signal distribution. We examine triboelectric, piezoelectric, biofuel-cell-based, magnetoelectric, moisture-driven, thermoelectric, and photovoltaic systems through the lens of interface-specific bottlenecks that determine whether harvested energy translates into stable, physiologically relevant stimulation. Cross-platform comparison further highlights the need for wound-mimetic output characterization, quantitative electrical dose–response correlations, rigorous discrimination between electrical and material-intrinsic effects, and comprehensive biointerface safety assessment. This framework provides design criteria for clinically translatable self-powered wound bioelectronics.

title: GelMA–HIF-1α composite hydrogels drive osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling for bone defect repair
abstract: Bone defects remain a major clinical challenge due to limited intrinsic bone regeneration and insufficient vascularization. This study asked whether sustained presentation of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) within a biomaterial scaffold could simultaneously couple osteogenesis and angiogenesis to improve bone repair. A GelMA-based hydrogel was engineered by covalently immobilizing HIF-1α via EDC/NHS chemistry to achieve prolonged bioactivity. In vitro effects were evaluated using bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs) and endothelial cells, and in vivo efficacy was assessed in a rat calvarial defect model. Multi-omics analyses and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) assays were used to explore underlying mechanisms. The novelty of this work lies in the stable covalent conjugation strategy enabling sustained HIF-1α signaling within a degradable hydrogel, integrated with systems-level mechanistic analysis linking cellular responses to metabolic regulation. Results showed enhanced osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs, increased endothelial migration and tube formation, and significantly improved new bone formation with greater mineral deposition and vascular ingrowth in vivo. Mechanistically, HIF-1α promoted intercellular communication, extracellular matrix remodeling, hypoxia adaptation, and metabolic reprogramming, accompanied by elevated glycolytic activity. Overall, this study demonstrates a biomaterial platform that coordinates vascularized bone regeneration through sustained HIF-1α signaling and metabolic coupling.

title: Upcycled cellulose pulp from local agricultural waste as a crosslinker in one-pot DLP-printable formulations for ionic wearable sensors
abstract: Strain-responsive materials are attracting growing attention due to their pivotal role in technologies such as wearable sensors and flexible electronics, rapidly expanding fields that are shaping the future of smart devices. As the demand for these functional materials grows, so does the need to produce them in more sustainable ways. Herein, cellulose pulp (CP) was extracted from local waste and dispersed in a photopolymerizable deep eutectic solvent (DES) composed of a hydrated salt and acrylic acid. The treatment with this solvent enables the dispersion of CP with its simultaneous functionalization with acrylic moieties, making it an added-value crosslinker for the DES photopolymerization. The resulting dispersion is suitable for VAT 3D printing, thanks to the cellulose's crosslinking role. The printed eutectogel boasts excellent ionic conductivity, and mechanical performance tailored for sensing applications. The eutectogel exhibits exceptional sensitivity to both small (0.02%) and large (above 200%) deformations, a performance that can be tuned through the interplay between the material intrinsic properties and 3D design and allows the device implementation in wearable sensors. Moreover sensing performances are maintained for over twenty weeks, far beyond than the other reported works in cellulose based eutectogels. This work paves the way for the next generation of sustainable, high-performance, and customizable soft electronic materials, able to exploit and valorise local waste, entering the mindset of the circular economy.

title: Novel biochar‒incorporated stearic acid composite phase change materials with multimodal‒triggered charging capacities for wearable thermotherapy
abstract: This work fabricated composite phase change materials (CPCMs) based on Fe 3 O 4 ‒modified carbonized water hyacinth (CWH@Fe 3 O 4 ), stearic acid (SA), and a small amount of expanded graphite (EG), which exhibited multimodal electro‒, photo‒, and magneto‒triggered thermal energy conversion and storage. The resulting CPCMs showed high crystallization fractions (91.1‒96.5%) and high heat storage capacities (102.3‒162.2 J/g), with varying SA contents. They also exhibited a high SA confinement of 80% without leakage, negligible degradation after 500 heat storage/release cycles, and enhanced thermal conductivity (9.0‒11.3 times that of pure SA). The magnetism of Fe 3 O 4 enabled the CPCMs to undergo accelerated magnetothermal conversion. The combination of EG’s sp 2 hybridization, CWH’s black, and Fe 3 O 4 ′s surface plasmon resonance endowed the CPCMs with enhanced VIS‒NIR absorption, resulting in effective photothermal conversion efficiencies (83.4‒90.2%). The high electrical conductivity of EG also enabled CPCMs to achieve effective electrothermal conversion. Indeed, the fabricated CPCM80 (a composite with 80% SA) could be thermally charged at a low applied voltage of 1.5 V. In a thermotherapy test, a CPCM80 thermal pad maintained a heat release within 50‒53 °C for 35 min, meeting and even surpassing therapeutic requirements. The high thermal performance and multiple charging options made the CPCMs promising for practical thermotherapy applications.

title: Design of stepwise gradient intermediate compositions in Ti2AlNb-GH4099 bimetallic structure manufactured via laser melting deposition
abstract: The metallurgical bonding at the Ti-Ni interface remains a critical challenge in functionally graded materials research. A compositional pathway design method for laser melting deposition was proposed based on the Scheil-Gulliver solidification theory and thermodynamic calculations. The stepwise gradient Ti 2 AlNb-GH4099 alloy was fabricated, and its microstructural evolution, phase composition, interfacial characteristics, solidification behavior and mechanical properties across interfaces were systematically investigated. The results demonstrate that the designed deposition pathway effectively suppresses the formation of Ti-Ni intermetallic compounds, particularly Ti 2 Ni and Ti 3 Ni 4 , thereby improving interfacial compatibility and mitigating local brittleness. The graded alloy exhibits Young’s modulus values of 80–157 GPa, nano-hardness values of 6–14 GPa, and an average microhardness of 744.68 HV 0.1 , indicating stable local deformation resistance across the compositional transition. The microstructural evolution is governed by the coupled effects of compositional gradients, non-equilibrium solidification and phase transformation, leading to the formation of a continuous B2/β-O-γ multiphase architecture together with locally precipitated γ′ phases. The resulting multiphase microstructure promotes strain accommodation and reduces the tendency for continuous brittle intermetallic formation. Thermodynamic calculations reveal the relationships among composition pathway, solidification sequence and phase evolution, providing a mechanistic basis for the design of graded dissimilar alloy systems, offering transferable guidance for bimetallic materials.

title: Mechanical metamaterials & metastructures for vibration suppression: From physical mechanisms to quantitative performance maps
abstract: Mechanical metamaterials offer new opportunities for vibration suppression through architecture-driven control of dynamic response, overcoming limitations of conventional isolation techniques. This review presents a mechanism-based framework for the design and analysis of vibration-suppressing metastructures, classifying existing approaches into four physical attenuation mechanisms –geometry-induced attenuation, local resonance, dynamic stiffness tuning, and energy dissipation–, together with hybridization as a cross-cutting design strategy. For each category, the governing physical principles are linked to representative structural realizations, with emphasis on design strategies and manufacturable architectures. Wave-based bandgap concepts and transmissibility-based metrics are integrated, enabling consistent evaluation of finite, experimentally realizable systems. A curated database of reported designs is formed and analyzed using Ashby-type performance maps to compare attenuation frequency ranges, bandwidth, stiffness, and structural efficiency across mechanisms. Particular attention is given to design-for-manufacture considerations, including additive manufacturing-enabled geometries, multi-material integration, and scalability. Key challenges—such as broadband low-frequency attenuation, tunability, and load-bearing integration—are analyzed alongside emerging solutions based on nonlinear stiffness, multi-resonator systems, and hybrid material–structural concepts. The work provides a unifying framework for the design and physical realization of vibration-suppressing, advanced materials and structures, identifying applicability limits and trade-offs across attenuation mechanisms and open benchmarking needs.

title: Bio-based photocurable binder design for vat photopolymerisation 3D printing of advanced ceramics
abstract: Reducing reliance on petroleum-derived resins in ceramic vat photopolymerisation (VP) requires developing bio-based photocurable binder systems that retain both printability and final ceramic performance. This study evaluated how binder-phase bio-based carbon content (BCC) affects rheology, cure response, green-body integrity, and post-sintering properties in alumina VP. A staged strategy screened oligomer chemistry before refining monomer substitution and solids loading for practical processability. At 52 vol% solids, selected G4293-based formulations with 72.8% and 55.0% BCC produced sintered alumina with ∼ 97% relative density, flexural strengths of 313–320 MPa, and hardness of ∼ 18 GPa.
