Partial substitution of IBOA with MPDDA reduced BCC to 55.0% and decreased apparent viscosity at 30 s −1 from ∼ 2600 to ∼ 890 mPa·s. Across the controlled BCC-reduction series, lower BCC also reduced critical exposure energy and increased green tensile strength. Between 72.8% and 55.0% BCC, green tensile strength increased from ∼ 10 to ∼ 15 MPa. These results identify binder-phase BCC as a practical formulation descriptor for balancing renewable carbon content and processability. High BCC remained compatible with successful ceramic VP, while partial BCC reduction provided a wider processing window without compromising post-sintering performance.

title: Effect of sintering temperature on microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of (NiCoCr)p/6061Al composites
abstract: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) was employed to fabricate (NiCoCr)p/6061Al composites at sintering temperatures ranging from 560 to 590 °C. The effects of sintering temperature on microstructural evolution, interfacial characteristics, and mechanical properties were systematically investigated. A multi-level heterogeneous structure was identified at the interface, wherein the central nanocrystalline zone comprised alternating Cr-rich and Co-rich nano-grains domains whose SAED patterns were provisionally consistent with B2-type and Al 9 Co 2 -type structures, respectively, while an amorphous structure is present at the interfacial periphery.The overall interface adopts a core–shell structure that fully encapsulates the NiCoCr reinforcing particles. This heterogeneous interfacial structure is inferred to act as a rigid load-bearing skeleton bridging the soft Al matrix and the moderately hard NiCoCr core, which may contribute to constraining matrix deformation and facilitating stress redistribution through the interfacial region. With increasing sintering temperature, the thickness of the core–shell structure progressively increases; however, at 590°C, excessive interfacial growth and partial consumption of the NiCoCr reinforcement are inferred to cause the proposed rigid skeleton to fragment into discretely dispersed isolated islands, thereby reducing the compressive strength of the composite to 359 MPa. The optimal sintering temperature is 580 °C, and the compressive strength is 547 MPa

title: Grain boundary-specific effects of Mn concentration on hydrogen trapping and embrittlement in bcc Fe: A spin-polarised DFT study
abstract: Hydrogen embrittlement limits the performance of ferritic steels in liquid-hydrogen environments, where hydrogen-enhanced decohesion (HEDE) dominates due to reduced hydrogen mobility. Using spin-polarised density functional theory, we quantify how manganese (Mn) modifies hydrogen solution, segregation, and cohesion at two representative bcc Fe grain boundaries: the high-angle Σ5(013)[100] (Σ5) and the coherent-twin Σ3(1-12)[110] (Σ3). At Σ5, Mn induces a coverage-dependent reversal in hydrogen energetics: low coverage weakens intrinsic trapping, intermediate coverage deepens traps beyond those of pure Fe, and full coverage eliminates deep traps and renders hydrogen (H) insertion thermodynamically unfavourable. Charge-density-difference maps reveal corresponding transitions from diffuse to strongly localised Mn–H–Fe interactions, followed by electronic passivation at full Mn coverage. At Σ3, Mn monotonically suppresses H trapping without producing intermediate stabilisation regimes. Magnetic effects are restricted to Mn located at the GB plane. In all cases, Mn increases intrinsic cohesion, and at Σ5 high Mn coverage partially restores cohesion in the presence of H. These results reconcile conflicting literature reports and show that Mn is neither universally embrittling nor beneficial; its effect depends on boundary structure, concentration, and site occupancy. High Mn coverage suppresses H trapping and improves GB resistance, while intermediate coverage deepens traps and reduces cohesion at boundaries.

title: Scan strategy as a microstructure design variable in electron beam powder bed fusion of Inconel 718
abstract: Electron beam powder bed fusion (E-PBF) of Inconel 718 (IN718) provides a rare degree of control over as built microstructure. The vacuum chamber, the pre-heated powder bed, and the inertia-free beam together make the surface melted a usable process variable. This review examines whether that control can be turned into a design tool, treating scan strategy as a distinctive and underexploited lever through which grain morphology, crystallographic texture, defects, segregation, and mechanical anisotropy can be influenced by beam path, geometry, and post-processing. The thermophysical behavior that makes IN718 sensitive to thermal history is developed first. The taxonomy of raster and spot melting strategies is then set out, followed by measured effects, including the inversion of grain structure from columnar to equiaxed at constant nominal energy input. The forward modeling pipeline and the inverse framework are assessed by the same standard as experiments. Scan strategy demonstrably controls grain structure, and raster models reproduce the columnar morphology and qualitative texture trends, although quantitative texture strength remains sensitive to nucleation density and scan-rotation treatment. In contrast, spot melt prediction, model validation, the segregation and phase response, and closed loop control remain open. Nine gaps are consolidated, and three near term programs are identified.

title: Ultra-precision cutting force prediction in SiCp/Al composites assisted by elliptical ultrasonic vibration
abstract: SiCp/Al composite, a high-performance metal matrix material, is prized for its remarkable specific strength, low coefficient of thermal expansion, and superior resistance against wear. However, the pronounced discrepancy in physical properties between the matrix and reinforcement phase results in processing defects, rendering it a notoriously difficult-to-machine material. To address these challenges, elliptical ultrasonic vibration-assisted cutting (EUVC) was adopted to improve machinability and surface integrity. A predictive model for cutting force was established, which meticulously accounts for material heterogeneity by decomposing the total cutting force into four distinct components: chip formation force, tool-chip friction force, plowing force, and particle fracture force. In particular, a characteristic state function was introduced to describe the periodic contact–separation behavior induced by elliptical ultrasonic vibration, thereby enabling the extension of the conventional force model to ultrasonic vibration-assisted cutting conditions. Experimental validation confirmed that the deviation between the predicted results and the measured data is within 10%. This model provides valuable process guidance for the high-precision machining of SiCp/Al material.

title: Inverse design of lightweight manufacturable TPMS structures based on a constitutive-aware neural operator
abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures have conventionally relied on inefficient trial-and-error forward design. Existing data-driven inverse approaches, dominated by generative adversarial networks (GANs) and more recently diffusion models, suffer from core drawbacks: training instability, poor physical consistency, neglect of additive manufacturing constraints, and a fixed relative density. Here, we propose a fabrication-aware deterministic inverse design framework driven by a Constitutive-Aware Neural Operator (CANO). This framework achieves end-to-end integration of the neural operator with differentiable manufacturing constraints, unlocks the joint optimization of topology and density, and realizes the efficient inversion from target mechanical properties to manufacturable geometric parameters of lightweight TPMS structures. Our framework encodes all smooth TPMS topological variants through a four-parameter continuous implicit function, treats relative density ρ ∈ [0.05, 0.20] as an independent design variable, and constructs a four-dimensional continuously differentiable design space. We train a manufacturability proxy network (MPN) and embed its logarithmic barrier term into the optimization objective, thereby realizing fully differentiable integration of additive manufacturing geometric constraints and eliminating post-hoc geometric screening. The forward prediction model attains coefficients of determination (R 2 ) of 0.940 for compressive strength and 0.982 for elastic modulus. At identical relative density and unit cell size, the inversely designed customized topologies deliver 14.9 % higher strength and 34.7 % higher modulus than the classic Gyroid, and 34.9 % and 81.1 % improvements over the Primitive, respectively. Measured mechanical responses closely match the design targets. The mean experimental relative errors are 4.1 % for compressive strength and 9.9 % for elastic modulus, with corresponding 95 % t-confidence intervals of −2.6 % to 10.8 % and 7.8 % to 12.1 %. This work provides a verifiable engineering framework for performance-driven customization of carbon-fiber-reinforced composite TPMS structures.

title: Molecular dynamics simulation of physical behaviors in silver-based bimetallic nanosystems
abstract: In this study we applied molecular dynamics simulations (MD) to investigate the stability, structural refinement and dynamical behavior of bimetallic nanoparticles with different compositions. The nanoparticles include different configurations of Ag/X and X/Ag in which X represents metals like gold (Au), copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), palladium (Pd) and platinum (Pt).The position of silver atoms, either in the core or in the shell, disturbs the stability, structural alteration and dynamical behavior of these nanoparticles. The results show that the stability of these particles both depends on the metallic composition and structural arrangement of these molecules. Moreover, the structural modifications and dynamics of nanoparticles in different conditions undergo impressive changes which could impact the industrial applications of these particles.We observed structural modifications in these nanoparticles towards the surface segregation of silver atoms and the enrichment of the core by x metals. These modifications have been analyzed with radial distribution functions (RDFs), mean square displacement (MSD) and strain analysis. The results of RDF analysis reveal strong interactions of Ag-X and X-X in systems with stronger bindings and higher lattice consistency. The data of MSD analysis show that the items with higher mobility like platinum and gold result in the increase of robustness of the structure while less mobile atoms like copper favors more structural rearrangement.The dynamical behavior is also conducted by strain distribution which shows that tensile or compressive stress depends on the difference in atomic sizes and modulus inconsistency which ends up in segregation or the restructuring of the nanoparticles. Overall, these findings show that the atomic interactions and mechanical distortions both control the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the nanoparticles.

title: Photothermal conversion and enhanced solar water treatment by plasmonic MoOx nanosheets immobilized on fabrics
abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable freshwater production; however, its efficiency is critically governed by the photothermal layer and its integration with supporting substrates. Herein, plasmonic oxygen-deficient molybdenum oxide (MoOx) nanosheets were synthesized via a simple anodizing-exfoliation route and immobilized onto commercial textile substrates using two distinct approaches: conventional dip coating and microwave-assisted deposition. A systematic comparison reveals that microwave-assisted immobilization induces enhanced nanosheet aggregation, increased surface roughness, and stronger interfacial adhesion, resulting in superior broadband optical absorption and more effective heat localization. Under simulated solar irradiation (1.3 sun), the optimized MoOx-coated felt reaches surface temperatures up to ~155 °C, significantly exceeding those obtained via dip coating (~80 °C). Consequently, an evaporation rate of 2.12±0.11 kg m−2 h−1 is achieved when treating highly saline and dye-contaminated water, corresponding to a photothermal conversion efficiency of 95±5%. This study demonstrates that the immobilization strategy plays a decisive role in governing photothermal performance and highlights microwave-assisted deposition as a scalable and cost-effective route for engineering high-efficiency textile-based photothermal evaporators.

title: Self-foaming PMMA bone cement for osteomyelitis: Enhanced antibiotic delivery with translational potential
abstract: The treatment of osteomyelitis remains a challenge in orthopedics. The burst antibiotic release and low total elution of conventional antibiotic loaded PMMA bone cement limited its therapeutic efficacy in clinical application. Herein, a self-foaming PMMA cement was developed with citric acid and sodium hydrogen carbonate as foaming agents (FA) to create an interconnected microporous structure which facilitated antibiotic release. The PMMA + 10 %FA formulation satisfied the ISO 5833-2002 compressive strength requirement (>70 MPa) and sustained an effective bactericidal concentration of Van (>15 mg/L) for over 28 days, yielding a 4.6-fold higher cumulative drug release when compared with the conventional PMMA. Micro-CT and mercury intrusion porosimetry demonstrated that FA incorporation elevated open porosity and refined the pore-size distribution which enabled sustained drug diffusion. The cytocompatibility was verified using MC3T3-E1 cells and HUVECs. In addition, PMMA + FA demonstrated potent in vitro anti-MRSA activity, and effective in-vivo infection control and osteogenic capacity in a rat femoral osteomyelitis model. This self-foaming cement, prepared with FDA-approved agents and a simple protocol, offers a clinically adaptable strategy for enhancing local antibiotic delivery and pro-osteogenic activity.

title: Al2O3 and mixed oxide formation in MCrAlY(M=Ni, Co) alloy powders: Effects of diffusion pathways, Al availability, and oxygen partial pressure
abstract: This study investigates the oxidation behavior and mixed oxide (MO) formation of commercial MCrAlY (M = Ni, Co) alloy powders used as bond-coat materials in thermal barrier coating systems. NiCrAlY and NiCoCrAlY powders were oxidized under different temperatures and oxygen partial pressures to examine the effects of grain-boundary-related diffusion pathways, Al availability, oxygen partial pressure, temperature, and time. Al availability and effective Al reservoir capability strongly influenced the onset of MO formation. The higher Al content and β-NiAl phase in the NiCoCrAlY powder sustained protective Al 2 O 3 growth for a longer period and delayed MO formation, although a larger Al concentration gradient enhanced the initial TGO growth rate. Grain-boundary-related diffusion pathways contributed to relatively uniform Al 2 O 3 formation during early oxidation. Oxygen partial pressure strongly affected the oxidation rate and the apparent formation location of oxide phases other than Al 2 O 3 . Cr-rich oxides formed beneath the Al 2 O 3 layer under higher oxygen partial pressures, whereas NiO/Cr 2 O 3 or Y–Al-rich oxides formed above the Al 2 O 3 layer under low oxygen partial pressure after extended oxidation. These findings provide a useful reference for understanding intrinsic MCrAlY powder oxidation while excluding thermal-spray-induced effects.

title: Metamorphic green nanomaterials: bio-responsive architectures for adaptive theranostics
abstract: Adaptive nanomaterials are emerging as a cornerstone of sustainable theranostics, offering intelligent, responsive, and environmentally responsible solutions to complex biomedical challenges. This perspective introduces metamorphic green nanomaterials as a paradigm shift from static constructs to dynamic bio-responsive systems. Traditionally, green nanomaterials have been valued for eco-friendly synthesis and passive biocompatibility. In this work, we explore how they can be re-engineered to undergo pre-programmed architectural and functional transformations in situ upon encountering specific biological cues. Such metamorphosis, through controlled disassembly, reassembly, or shape-shifting, unlocks emergent functionalities at target sites, enabling adaptive theranostic capabilities. We discuss how converging innovations in the biosynthesis of complex precursors, dynamic DNA/RNA nanotechnology, biocatalytic triggers, and AI-driven computational co-design are pivotal to realizing these multi-state systems. Potential applications include sequential drug delivery cascades that overcome biological barriers and resistance, sense-and-remediate platforms for pathogenic niches or environmental pollutants, and dynamic scaffolds for regenerative medicine that adapt to evolving tissue needs. While challenges remain in fidelity and scalable manufacturing, the inherent biocompatibility and sustainability of green components provide unique advantages. Metamorphic green nanomaterials may represent a step toward autonomous living nanomachines and may advance theranostic technologies through enhanced intelligence, adaptability, and ecological responsibility, paving the way for personalized nanomedicine.

title: Biomimetic magneto-responsive nanoparticles delivering yakuchinone A attenuate traumatic brain injury via TREM2/NRF2/GPX4 modulation
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a cascade of secondary pathological events, including blood–brain barrier (BBB) disruption, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress, leading to neuronal loss. Effective pharmacological intervention remains challenging because most therapeutic agents fail to efficiently cross the BBB and lack the ability to selectively target activated microglia, which are central regulators of secondary injury. To overcome these delivery barriers, we designed a hierarchical biomimetic magneto-responsive nanoplatform (NFZY) by integrating a magnetic Fe 3 O 4 core, pH-responsive ZIF-8 framework, and neutrophil-membrane (NM) biointerface, then loading yakuchinone A (YA). This architecture enables magnetic field–assisted accumulation, pH-triggered release, inflammation-guided homing, and enhanced BBB translocation. NFZY exhibited superior uptake by activated microglia in vitro and improved brain targeting in TBI mice under magnetic guidance. It attenuated microglial inflammatory activation, suppressed reactive oxygen species (ROS), and inhibited ferroptosis. In vivo, NFZY reduced lesion volume, restored BBB integrity, mitigated neuronal degeneration, and improved neurological outcomes. Mechanistic studies revealed that NFZY upregulated TREM2 (Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-2) and subsequently activated the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 signaling pathway, which enhanced antioxidant defenses and inhibited ferroptosis. Overall, this work demonstrates that the hierarchical integration of magnetic responsiveness, stimuli-responsive release, and biomimetic surface engineering in NFZY markedly improves YA delivery efficiency and alleviates secondary injury after TBI.

title: Strength–ductility synergy in heterogeneous layered WE43/AZ31 composites fabricated by alternating layered extrusion
abstract: Hetero-structure is regarded as promising for overcoming the strength–ductility trade-off in magnesium alloys. In this work, a novel alternating layered extrusion process is proposed to fabricate a well-bonded laminated WE43/AZ31 magnesium alloy hetero-structure composite with strength-ductility synergy. The ultimate tensile strength of the fabricated composite reaches 275.7 MPa, representing increases of 8.0% and 24.5% compared with monolithic WE43 and AZ31, respectively, and the elongation increases from 9.1% (for monolithic WE43) and 11.2% (for monolithic AZ31) to 18.2% in this laminated composite. Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms responsible for the strength–ductility synergy were investigated using TEM, in situ EBSD, and high-resolution digital image correlation (HR-DIC). The results reveal that the laminated composite exhibits coarse grains in AZ31 layers and fine grains in WE43 layers. Furthermore, the dispersed interfacial compounds enriched in Al, Gd, and Y induce Orowan strengthening and facilitate the activation of non-basal slip by reducing the stacking fault energy, thereby enhancing the interfacial strength and overall plastic deformability. During deformation, strain first concentrates in the AZ31 layer, whereas the WE43 layer exhibits a more uniform strain distribution at a later stage, mitigating strain localization. This strain redistribution, along with interfacial coordination, enables the laminated composite to achieve superior strength-ductility synergy.

title: Bio-inspired edible self-spinning flyers
abstract: Air dropping can quickly deliver supplies to the ground. However, the ground impact of free-falling objects could be high, inflicting risks to humans and goods alike. To address this problem, we propose edible self-spinning flyers inspired by the slow, autorotating descent of maple seeds. The edible flyers are fabricated by assembling multiple edible components produced through hot-compression moulding, 3D food printing, and drying. A range of edible materials was investigated for a composition that balances manufacturability with mechanical performance. The nutritional profile of the edible flyers can be tailored by adjusting the material composition of the edible wing and payload mass. The aerodynamic properties were evaluated using vertical wind tunnel experiments, while indoor drop tests confirmed their ability to reduce descent speed through self-spinning motion. Aerial distribution of edible flyers could offer a rapid means of emergency response in future by enabling the quick distribution of life-saving nutrition to humans and animals.

title: Go-wrapped copper nanoparticle-decorated graphite/epoxy composites: interfacial stabilization and enhanced thermal transport
abstract: This study presents an APTES-mediated GO-coated Cu nanoparticle-decorated graphite hybrid filler for high-loading epoxy-based thermal management composites. Cu nanoparticles were deposited onto graphite surfaces by electroless deposition to provide nanoscale bridging sites between adjacent graphite platelets, followed by APTES-mediated GO modification to improve interfacial stability. The sequential surface modification was characterized by SEM, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, XPS, EDS, and TGA. XPS revealed Si- and N-containing APTES-derived species and increased oxygenated carbon components, while weaker Cu 2+ -related satellite features were observed after APTES/GO modification. At a fixed filler loading of 60 vol%, GCG60 exhibited in-plane and through-plane thermal conductivities of 20.828 and 3.518 W m −1 K −1 , corresponding to increases of 28.6% and 75.7%, respectively, relative to G60. The thermal anisotropy ratio decreased from 8.09 to 5.92, while the flexural modulus increased by approximately 41.6%. These results demonstrate that the combined Cu nanoparticle bridging and APTES/GO-mediated interfacial stabilization provide an effective approach for improving cross-plane thermal transport and stiffness in graphite-rich epoxy composites.

title: Oxygen-regulating strategies in scaffolds for vascularized bone tissue engineering
abstract: Bone tissue engineering (BTE) is promising for reconstructing critical-sized bone defects. However, inadequate early vascularization and limited oxygen diffusion (<200 μm) lead to central hypoxia, waste accumulation, and cell necrosis in large scaffolds, processes which hinder clinical translation of BTE. Oxygen critically regulates the bone regenerative microenvironment with context-dependent effects. Moderate hypoxia activates HIF-1α to initiate angiogenesis and osteoclast remodeling, whereas controlled oxygenation (e.g., hyperbaric oxygen therapy) enhances redox homeostasis and promotes osteoblast proliferation, matrix mineralization, and angiogenesis–osteogenesis coupling. To mitigate scaffold-associated hypoxia, we summarize four strategies: (i) biomimetic structural optimization via three-dimensional (3D)-printed gradient porosity, vascular-like channels, triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) architectures, and surface topographies for passive oxygen transport; (ii) active in situ oxygenation using inorganic oxygen-generating materials, oxygen carriers, and photosynthetic microalgae; (iii) bioactive signaling via the controlled release of angiogenic factors or hypoxia-mimetic agents to accelerate vascularization; and (iv) scaffold prevascularization using in vivo AV-loop models or in vitro 3D-bioprinted microvascular networks. Finally, we discuss the limitations of single-modality approaches and emphasize the necessity for dynamically adaptive biomimetic scaffolds with intelligent microenvironment responsiveness to achieve spatiotemporally coordinated vascularized osteogenesis. This review offers a systematic framework for designing advanced biomaterials for large bone defect repair

title: Tensile behavior of lead-free SAC305 solder: constitutive modeling and fracture mechanisms
abstract: Reliable constitutive descriptions of SAC305 (Sn-3Ag-0.5Cu) are needed for solder joint assessment in electric vehicle battery packs, but the small dimensions of solder balls impede direct mechanical characterization. The surface of a continuous cast SAC305 billet was considered because its microstructure and microhardness most closely matched those of a laboratory-prepared solder-ball reference. ASTM-standard cylindrical dog-bone specimens were machined from this region, and tensile tests were conducted at −40, 25, 75, and 125 °C and strain rates of 0.005, 0.01, and 0.1 s −1 . Fracture evolved from mixed faceted and shallow dimple morphology at −40 °C to ductile dimple rupture at higher temperatures. EBSD identified candidate twin boundaries at −40 °C, while site-specific TEM confirmed a planar β-Sn twin boundary with an approximately 62° misorientation about 〈100〉. A modified Anand model incorporating temperature dependence in S 0 and temperature-strain rate dependence in h 0 was calibrated and improved the predictive accuracy of the conventional Anand formulation. UTS-normalized Fréchet-distance analysis showed a 59 % reduction in mean curve-shape discrepancy relative to the original formulation. The calibrated parameters describe bulk cast SAC305 under monotonic tension and provide candidate inputs for simulations requiring joint-specific validation in the relevant reflowed configuration.

title: Uncertainty-guided multi-stage adaptive active learning framework for pareto optimization of blast-resistant fiber-metal laminates
abstract: Optimizing the thickness configuration of fiber-metal laminates subjected to blasts in confined spaces is critical for balancing protective performance and lightweight requirements. However, traditional surrogate-based multi-objective optimization approaches suffer from high local predictive uncertainty and insufficient exploration of the pareto frontier. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel active learning-based adaptive iterative framework incorporating a multi-stage strategy. This decoupled optimization strategy initially generates learning candidates within high-uncertainty regions to refine the Gaussian process regression surrogate model. Subsequently, the learning focus shifts toward exploring the boundaries of the pareto optimal frontier by prioritizing candidates with the highest pareto contribution, facilitated by the NSGA-II algorithm. Results demonstrate that compared to a standard non-iterative baseline comprising 250 samples, the proposed multi-stage strategy enhances optimization outcomes while utilizing merely 54% of the sample data. Specifically, the active learning framework successfully reduced the maximum predictive uncertainty by 44.2% and the mean uncertainty by 20.8%. Furthermore, it significantly expanded the boundaries of the optimal solution set, achieving a 7.3% increase in the hypervolume metric and a 52% increase in the number of non-dominated solutions. Ultimately, this multi-stage strategy provides a highly reliable, data-efficient multi-objective optimization method for the advanced design of blast-resistant protective structures.

title: Self-powered functional materials for immune modulation by electrical stimulation
abstract: Electrical stimulation (ES) can promote the proliferation, migration and differentiation of a wide range of cell types, including immune cells. Recent advances demonstrate that ES can effectively modulate both innate and adaptive immune cells, thereby reshaping immune responses. It thus finds extensive applications in tissue repair, neurological functional recovery, tumor therapy and many other fields. Novel self-powered functional materials, such as piezoelectric, triboelectric, photovoltaic and pyroelectric materials, are capable of converting renewable energy sources into ES. This enables the miniaturization of electronic devices and minimizes tissue damage. Furthermore, when integrated with drug delivery, tissue engineering and immunotherapy, such materials can amplify immunomodulatory effects and address the limitations inherent to monotherapy strategies. This review summarizes the latest research advances in self-powered materials, and systematically analyzes the energy conversion mechanisms of various self-powered effects, material properties, and design principles of relevant self-powered electronic devices. The mechanisms by which ES regulates immune cell behavior and signaling pathways are also discussed, alongside representative applications in tissue repair, arthritis, and cancer immunotherapy. Refined self-powered system design and deeper mechanistic understanding of ES-mediated immune modulation will enable precise, controllable immune microenvironment modulation across diverse clinical applications.

title: Impact response of W0.75NbTiZr energetic structural material: microstructural evolution and energy-release behavior
abstract: The mechanical properties and energy-release behavior of the W 0.75 NbTiZr energetic structural material (ESM) were investigated using Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) and ballistic gun experiments. The impact response of the material was further analyzed, combined with microstructural evolution. The results demonstrate that biphase microstructure endows it with excellent strength and plasticity, as well as energy-release characteristics. Under dynamic loading, the material exhibits a significant impact-ignition phenomenon, and multiple delayed micro-explosion reactions occur at high strain rates. Fracture morphology and microstructural observations indicate that high-strain-rate loading promotes the aggregation, growth, and precipitation of the W-rich phase, improves the material’s strength, and alters the internal stress concentration state, providing a structural basis for the delayed reaction behavior. The ballistic gun experiment verified the favorable energy-release characteristics of the W 0.75 NbTiZr energetic metallic material. A reaction energy calculation method was proposed based on energy conservation and pressure measurement data, which can capture the delayed reaction behavior of ESMs and quantitatively evaluate the energy-release rate and energy-release amount. The research results provide a theoretical basis and experimental support for the regulation of microstructure and the synergistic design of mechanical energy in high-performance energetic structural materials.

title: Failure-mode transition in resistance spot-welded Zn-coated martensitic steels containing residual Sn and Sb
abstract: The accumulation of residual Sn and Sb during scrap-based steelmaking raises concerns regarding their influence on Zn-induced liquid metal embrittlement (LME) during resistance spot welding. Zn-coated martensitic steels containing different Sn or Sb additions were investigated using mechanical testing, crack characterization, elemental mapping, EBSD and first-principles calculations. Compared with steel 0Sn, the Sn- and Sb-containing steels exhibited greater LME crack populations and a transition from pull-out to partial interfacial failure. The latter involved fracture along or near the fusion-zone boundary on one side and a Zn-associated HAZ path on the other. EPMA revealed microscale Sn/Sb enrichment near selected fusion-line fractures, but could not resolve atomic-scale grain-boundary segregation. EBSD analysis showed finer reconstructed prior-austenite grains and higher high-angle grain-boundary fractions in the Sn- and Sb-containing steels. At equivalent occupancy in an idealized BCC Fe Σ5(310) boundary, DFT predicted segregation tendencies and local bonding perturbations for isolated Sn and Sb solutes. The observations support an interpretation based on competition between possible HAZ and fusion-line/nugget failure paths. However, solidification partitioning, local weld geometry, baseline weld strength and pre-existing LME crack geometry may also contribute. The proposed mechanism is therefore an evidence-supported interpretation rather than an independently established causal sequence.

title: Low-cost and performance-balanced Cu-Ni-Cr-Si copper strips designed with machine learning and fabricated with short processing route
abstract: Advanced copper alloys are widely used in core electronic components. However, their excellent performance severely depends on the addition of expensive elements. To achieve the synergistic target of low cost and high performance, a graph neural network (GNN) model and an artificial neural network (ANN) model were constructed to screen key elements and optimize precise composition, respectively. A novel Cu-1Ni-1Cr-0.5Si-0.2 Mg-0.2Zn (wt.%) alloy was designed and fabricated via a short processing route comprising triple-stage cold rolling and aging treatment. The studied alloy exhibited excellent comprehensive performance, with an electrical conductivity of 41.8 ± 0.1% IACS, a hardness of 234.7 ± 1.2 HV, an ultimate tensile strength of 715 ± 7.4 MPa, a failure elongation of 15.6 ± 0.8%, and a strength-ductility product of 11.15 GPa·%. Compared to conventional Cu-Ni-Si and Cu-Ti alloys, the designed alloy achieved a competitive strength-ductility product with a 21.3% reduction in processing cost and approximately 1.5% lower material cost. Additionally, the experimental results agreed well with the predictions, indicating that the machine learning method was effective and provided a general, scalable approach for developing high-performance, cost-effective copper alloys

title: Tailored heat source-sink approach with a proposed modulus amplification factor for investment casting
abstract: To address the limitations of empirical insulation design in investment casting, this study establishes a quantitative framework centered on a novel modulus amplification factor, K . A physically-based model was derived to correlate insulation thickness with K by regulating thermal sources and sinks. The methodology was validated using complex Ni-based superalloy fairing spoke castings. Numerical results demonstrate that the theory-guided approach suppresses shrinkage porosity by 97.7% (from 12.16 cm 3 to 0.03 cm 3 ) by optimizing the solidification sequence, with a predictive deviation for K within 3.4%. Experimental validation confirmed that the K guided design effectively prolonged solidification from 1470 s to 6069 s, transforming macroscopic defects into discrete, healable micro-porosity (∼ 0.5 cm 3 ) suitable for hot isostatic pressing. This K factor-based approach provides a precise, actionable methodology for the high-integrity manufacturing of complex superalloy castings.

title: Precipitate–dislocation interactions governing the high-temperature creep behavior of a Mg–Gd alloy
abstract: The high-temperature creep behavior of Mg-10Gd-0.4Zr alloys with different initial precipitation states was systematically investigated at 225–300 °C. Four microstructural conditions, namely the as-cast, solution-treated (T4), peak-aged (T6), and over-aged states, were examined. Dislocation pile-up and tangling around the α-Mg + Mg 5 Gd eutectic phases caused local stress concentration, whereas coarse incoherent β precipitates were bypassed through the Orowan mechanism, resulting in weak creep strengthening. In contrast, coherent β′ precipitates effectively impeded dislocation motion and provided the strongest creep-strengthening effect. Consequently, the T6 state alloy containing a high density of intragranular β′ precipitates exhibited the best creep resistance below 260 °C. At 275 and 300 °C, however, the T4 alloy exhibited better creep resistance than the T6 alloy. TEM analysis revealed distinct precipitation evolution behaviors in the T4 and T6 state alloys during creep at 275 °C. Dynamic precipitation produced a relatively high fraction of β′ precipitates in the T4 alloy, whereas pre-existing β′ precipitates in the T6 alloy progressively transformed into semi-coherent β 1 precipitates. The β 1 precipitates impeded dislocation motion but exhibited lower creep-strengthening capability than β′. These results demonstrated that creep resistance was governed by both the initial precipitation state and its temperature-dependent evolution during creep.

title: Bridging data gaps in polymer additive manufacturing via knowledge-informed, LLM intelligence guided prompt engineering for 3D-printed PLA tensile-strength prediction
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has shown potential to transform additive manufacturing (AM). However, the lack of sufficient training data is a challenge. This paper presents a knowledge-informed prompt-engineering approach that utilizes large language models (LLMs) to generate physically meaningful synthetic data related to 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA). The objective is to answer two important questions: (a) whether LLMs can generate synthetic data to improve AM machine learning models? If yes, (b) what type of prompting approaches can be most beneficial? Using a mixed experimental dataset collected across two laboratories, we design seven structured prompting strategies to generate synthetic datasets, integrate them with experimental data, followed by evaluation across five conventional classification ML models and a multilayer perceptron (MLP). Our studies reveal that small injections of synthetic data, such as 10%−20% (or 5–10 points) of the number of real data, generally lead to stable ML model performance, whereas large injections such as 200% or more generally degrade the accuracy. Among the models, XGBoost and CatBoost demonstrate the strongest performance. The numeric, few-shot prompts result in the highest average macro-F1 score of ∼0.92. Our results indicate that LLM-driven, prompt-engineered synthetic data generation can serve as effective approach for overcoming AM data scarcity.

title: Superior strength-ductility synergy in TiAl-based composites via a multi-dimensional heterogeneous structure constructed by nano-TiB2 particles and micro-TaB rods
abstract: Limited plasticity restricts the engineering applications of TiAl alloys. Herein, a novel multi-dimensional heterogeneous structure, characterized by heterogeneity in size scale, morphology, and spatial distribution of reinforcements, was constructed within the TiAl matrix to simultaneously improve strength and ductility. In this case, the nanoscale TiB 2 phases were granular and located at grain boundaries, while the microscale TaB rods exhibited a large aspect ratio and traversed the lamellae. Such a multi-dimensional heterogeneous structure enabled grain refinement strengthening and dislocation strengthening, while promoting the formation of stacking faults and the development of hetero-deformation-induced hardening, which enhanced deformation compatibility and stability. Consequently, the TiB 2 -TaB/TiAl composite exhibited superior compressive properties to the TiAl alloy over the strain-rate range of 10 −4 –10 −2 s −1 , indicating a stable compressive response. The optimal compressive performance was achieved at 10 −2 s −1 , with a yield strength of 1090 MPa, an ultimate compressive strength of 2116 MPa, and a fracture strain of 23.1%, corresponding to improvements of 52.4%, 9.8%, and 22.9%, respectively, over the TiAl alloy. This demonstrates that the construction of a multi-dimensional heterogeneous structure provides a promising strategy for designing high-performance TiAl-based alloys.

title: Design strategies for low-voltage dielectric elastomer actuators from materials to systems
abstract: Dielectric elastomer actuators enable large strain and fast response, but their adoption is limited by the driving voltage at the kV level, which hinders safety, miniaturization, and system integration. This review summarizes recent strategies for achieving sub-kV operation across the material, structure, and system levels. At the material level, we review approaches to increase dielectric permittivity and reduce the modulus of elasticity, including filler incorporation, polar group engineering, plasticization, and molecular architecture design. Structural paths such as thinning and multilayer stacking of dielectric films and compliant electrode techniques that maintain low electrical resistance even under large deformation are discussed. We also review power supply and control strategies including resonance-based operation, integrated switching, and compact high-voltage conversion. The key trade-offs associated with low-voltage operation, such as dielectric breakdown, leakage losses, electrode-induced stiffening, and defect sensitivity in thin films, are compared, and an outlook is provided for applications in untethered soft robots, micro aerial vehicles, and portable microfluidic systems.

title: Laser induced self-propagating reaction of cobalt silicide formation from reactive multilayers
abstract: Reactive multilayer foils of Co-Si were fabricated by magnetron co-sputtering and locally ignited using an 808 nm near-infrared laser to initiate self-propagating reactions. The variations in bilayer thickness and atomic ratio significantly influence the resulting phase compositions. Combined with velocity analysis, the results indicate that bilayer thickness and premixed layer thickness regulate the flame temperature. When the bilayer thickness exceeds a critical value, the flame temperature may surpass the liquidus minimum indicated in the Co-Si phase diagram. It enables liquid-phase mixing and partial melting of CoSi 2 , thereby altering the final reaction products. These results support the development of a proposed reaction pathway model for self-propagating reactions in Co-Si reactive multilayers. The physical model developed in this study extends beyond the specific system investigated, providing a generalized understanding that facilitates controlled reactions in a broad range of related material systems in power devices and thermoelectronics.

title: Effect of cooling rate on phase transformation and microstructure evolution in a heat-resistant medium-carbon bainitic steel
abstract: This study investigates the effect of cooling rate on phase transformation behaviour, microstructural evolution and hardness of a heat-resistant 1CrMoV medium-carbon low-alloy bainitic steel for turbine rotor applications. To establish a predictive framework for evolved microstructures and corresponding hardness values, dilatometry tests simulating constant cooling rates from 0.03 to 50 °C/s were performed using a Gleeble 3800 thermomechanical simulator. Microstructures were characterized by CLSM, FE-SEM/EBSD, TEM and XRD, while hardness measurements supported the model assessment. Depending on cooling rate, different phase mixtures, including quasi-polygonal ferrite, degenerated pearlite, granular bainite, lath-like bainite and lath/blocky martensite, were observed and quantified. Ferrite formation was suppressed above ~ 0.5 °C/s, while cooling at intermediate rates of 1–1.5 °C/s rendered the finest effective grain and lath sizes due to bainite-assisted subdivision of prior austenite grains. A previously developed phase transformation model was calibrated using the dilatometry data, including the incomplete bainite transformation phenomenon, and coupled with a hardness prediction model. Dilatometer data supported by detailed microstructural analyses resulted not only in the development of a continuous cooling transformation diagram but also enabled utilization of this framework to outline and simulate complex, non-linear industrial cooling paths in corroboration with the predictions of phase transformation model.

title: Failure resistance and vibration isolation in natural rubber composites: role of matrix- and filler-dominated viscoelastic loss
abstract: Viscoelastic dissipation governs both vibration attenuation and fatigue durability in rubber components; however, the role of its physical origin in determining engineering performance remains unclear. This study establishes a unified mechanistic framework to distinguish matrix-dominated and filler-network-dominated dissipation pathways using four natural-rubber-based compounds: unfilled NR, an NR–ENR blend, and NR reinforced with N220 and N772 carbon blacks. Mechanical properties, dynamic mechanical behavior, Payne effect, heat build-up, tear resistance, fatigue crack growth, and vibration transmissibility were systematically evaluated. The results reveal that NR–ENR achieves enhanced damping through molecular relaxation and intermolecular interactions, increasing the loss factor by 112.5% and reducing resonance transmissibility from 6.3 to 3.1, while maintaining excellent fatigue resistance with no complete crack growth after 8 × 10 5 cycles. In contrast, filler-network dissipation, governed by network breakdown/reformation and interfacial friction, improves static reinforcement but induces higher hysteresis and heat accumulation, accelerating fatigue failure. These findings demonstrate that damping magnitude alone cannot define rubber component performance; instead, vibration isolation, thermal stability, and durability are controlled by the underlying energy dissipation mechanism and its associated energy redistribution pathway.

title: CFD-FEM simulation-guided regulation of interfacial intermetallic layer uniformity in Al/steel circular oscillating laser-welded joints
abstract: Robust Al/steel dissimilar joints are essential for lightweight structural applications, yet their mechanical reliability is often limited by the heterogeneous growth of brittle Fe-Al intermetallic compounds(IMCs) at the joining interface. In this study, a coupled CFD-FEM framework was established to resolve the interfacial thermal cycles and molten-pool flow behavior during circular oscillating laser welding(COLW), and the simulation results were used to guide process regulation. Compared with conventional laser welding (CLW), COLW redistributed the laser heat input across the direct irradiation, middle, and weld toe regions, reducing the maximum interfacial temperature difference from 251°C to 102°C. The shortened high-temperature residence time and modified melt-flow trajectory suppressed localized elemental diffusion and promoted the formation of a thinner and more uniform interfacial reaction layer. Finally, a continuous dual-phase IMCs layer composed mainly of η-Fe 2 Al 5 and θ-Fe 4 Al 13 was obtained, with the thickness variation decreasing from 31.13 μm under CLW to 4.83 μm under COLW. The optimized joint reached a tensile-shear load of 273 N/mm, representing a 12.4% improvement over the CLW joint, and the fracture path changed from predominantly brittle interfacial failure to mixed ductile–brittle fracture propagating through the weld seam. These results demonstrate that simulation-guided control provides an effective strategy for tailoring IMCs evolution

title: Recent advances in perovskite oxide-based materials for electromagnetic interference shielding and microwave absorption
abstract: With the rapidly evolving telecommunications sector, including 5G/6G and the Internet of Things (IoT), there has been a growing push towards developing advanced materials for Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding. Traditionally, highly conductive metallic shields have dominated the field. However, their susceptibility to high-temperature oxidation, structural degradation, and high-reflection-induced secondary EMI pollution limits their use in next-generation applications. Recently, perovskite oxide-based materials, characterized by their exceptional structural robustness, thermal stability, and tunable electromagnetic properties, have emerged as promising alternatives. This review provides an overview of recent advancements in perovskite oxide-based shielding materials, focusing on the intrinsic structure-property relationships governing their EM-wave attenuation performance. The fundamental mechanisms of electromagnetic attenuation – including conduction pathways, interfacial polarization, and natural resonance – have been covered, along with a detailed discussion of the effects of advanced synthesis routes on the material’s microstructural evolution. The effects of aliovalent doping, defect engineering, and the formation of synergistic composites with conductive fillers (carbon nanomaterials, MXenes, and polymers) on modulating the dielectric and magnetic losses to achieve absorption-dominated shielding have been thoroughly discussed. A few critical gaps have been identified, particularly in sustainability and rapid material identification, and probable pathways have been proposed for designing multifunctional shields.

title: A hybrid data-driven J2-based plasticity model for plastic anisotropy evolution in metals
abstract: This study proposes a plasticity framework for describing anisotropic hardening and flow direction evolution, which employs data-driven concepts to enhance the traditional von Mises plasticity framework. The approach is an alternative to advanced anisotropic phenomenological plasticity models. On one hand, it incorporates all available data within the experimentally investigated loading path domain into the constitutive plastic response, unlike the traditional models which only use a limited part of the data. On the other hand, it defaults to standard isotropic J2 plastic flow outside of the investigated domain, without making unbased extrapolations of the plastic flow direction far into the untested loading paths. The hardening response is represented using an artificial neural network trained on stress–strain data obtained from different loading directions. Simultaneously, a plastic flow corrector reproduces the experimentally measured r-value evolution. The performance of proposed framework was assessed through finite element simulations of tensile specimens and compared against a conventional Voce hardening model calibrated using a single material orientation. The best agreement with experiments is achieved before the onset of necking, while larger deviations occur under the complex stress states that develop during post-necking deformation. The study demonstrates a thermodynamically admissible framework for modeling highly anisotropic plastic deformation.

title: Laves phase morphology governing strength-plasticity in additively manufactured IN718 alloy
abstract: In additively manufactured IN718, Nb-rich Laves phases often act as crack-sensitive constituents and degrade tensile performance. However, the role of Laves phase geometry in crack initiation and propagation remains insufficiently understood. Here, directed energy deposition was used to regulate melt-pool solidification by varying laser scanning speed, producing IN718 samples with long-chain Laves phases, mixed morphologies, and fine near-spherical Laves phases. In-situ SEM tensile testing shows that long-chain Laves phases promote early Laves/Ni interfacial decohesion, followed by intra-Laves cracking and crack linkage along quasi-continuous Laves-rich paths. In contrast, fine near-spherical Laves phases interrupt these weak paths. Although Laves particles can still crack at higher strain, they no longer dominate the primary crack path; final failure proceeds mainly through microcrack nucleation and coalescence within the Ni matrix. The improved tensile response results from two related effects: strength enhancement mainly from grain refinement and increased Nb/Mo/Ti retention in the Ni matrix, and ductility improvement mainly from reduced Laves connectivity and delayed crack linkage. This work clarifies the morphology-dependent crack-path transition in AM-IN718 and provides guidance for tailoring Laves phase geometry in process design.

title: Breaking the strength and densification trade-off in low-temperature co-fired ceramic substrates via glass network depolymerization
abstract: Advanced electronic packaging requires low-temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC) with exceptional mechanical strength and good dielectric properties. However, increasing filler content to improve strength typically hinders the liquid-phase mass transport required for densification. Here, this trade-off is resolved by strategically incorporating Ca 2+ modifiers to partially depolymerize the highly cross-linked borosilicate framework. This maintains a low-viscosity liquid phase of CaO-Al 2 O 3 -B 2 O 3 -SiO 2 glass at elevated temperatures, thereby facilitating the densification for composites containing ≥65 wt% Al 2 O 3 filler. Concurrently, localized Al diffusion from the Al 2 O 3 filler enriches the adjacent liquid phase. This specific elemental migration promotes the in-situ formation of a chemically bonded Ca(Al 2 Si 2 O 8 ) interfacial layer, which effectively eliminates the stress concentrations typically associated with weak physical bonding. Consequently, LTCC substrates achieve an exceptional bending strength of 437 MPa. Crucially, this is achieved while maintaining excellent high-frequency dielectric properties (ε r = 7.4, tanδ = 4.6 × 10 -3 @15 GHz) and co-firing compatibility. This work provides a general approach for the fabrication of high-performance LTCC substrates for large-scale applications.

title: Continuum-consistent Lagrange-Hermite contact framework with direct validation of rough surface parameters
abstract: • Lagrange-Hermite model ensures C1 continuity, removing stiffness jumps. • Rough joint stiffness/damping errors cut from 62% to 16%. • Applicable to MEMS, biological joints, granular media, and additive manufacturing. Rough surface contact is a fundamental challenge in fields ranging from mechanical engineering and biomechanics to MEMS and granular materials. A long standing inconsistency plagues existing contact models: the elastic plastic transition of asperities lacks C 1 continuity—a natural requirement for a physically smooth transition in contact stiffness. We establish a continuum-consistent framework via Lagrange–Hermite (LH) interpolation that enforces C 1 continuity of values and derivatives at critical transition points, eliminating the discontinuity of the Kogut–Etsion (KE) model without additional free parameters. For validation, we develop a direct verification methodology that combines high precision modal testing with joint simulation based optimisation and fractal parameter extraction via structural function analysis. Experiments on marble joint surfaces under 20–80 N·m preloads show that the LH framework reduces prediction errors for normal stiffness and damping from 62% for the KE model to ≈16%. Residual errors are attributed to intrinsic limitations of classical continuum theory when applied at the microscale. The framework is material agnostic and scale agnostic, and is readily transferable to biological joints, MEMS switches, granular contacts, and other rough surface systems.

title: Tailoring the microstructure and properties of low-carbon martensitic steel via cooling rate control during temperature-controlled quenching and deformation
abstract: To address severe quenching distortion and inefficient leveling of ultra-thin ultra-high-strength steel (UHSS) plates, a temperature-controlled quenching and deformation (TCQD) process was investigated. This study examined the effect of cooling rate during the deformation-controlled cooling (DCC) stage on the final microstructure and mechanical properties. Compared with conventional quenched and tempered (Q&T) steel, the specimen cooled at 11 °C/s exhibited 2.3% lower tensile strength but 1.3% higher hardness, 7.5% higher elongation, and 5.0% higher product of strength and elongation. Without subsequent tempering, this specimen also showed 7.8% lower dislocation density and 0.9% lower residual stress. The favorable mechanical performance was mainly associated with finer and more densely distributed cementite and the retention of a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries, whereas the reductions in dislocation density and residual stress were primarily related to slower cooling within the martensitic transformation range. Among the cooling rates investigated, 11 °C/s provided the most favorable overall balance of microstructure, mechanical performance, and residual stress. These results demonstrate the feasibility of tempering-free TCQD processing and provide a promising processing route for ultra-thin UHSS plates.

title: Oxygen uptake, reuse stability, and recycling of copper powder in powder bed fusion
abstract: Oxidation behavior and reuse stability of copper (Cu) powder were systematically investigated for laser- and electron-beam-based powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M and PBF-EB/M) as a function of process atmosphere and reuse cycles. Repeated powder reuse altered key powder properties, including infrared reflectivity and flowability. Build plate preheating increased densification in PBF-LB/M-process but simultaneously promoted oxygen uptake in Cu powder processed in inert Ar atmospheres. In contrast, an Ar–2 vol% H 2 process gas suppressed powder oxidation by scavenging residual oxygen from the process atmosphere. When combined with build plate preheating, the reducing atmosphere additionally promoted the reduction of pre-existing oxide phases, reducing the powder oxygen content to below that of the virgin feedstock. However, the lower oxide content also decreased infrared laser energy absorption, resulting in lower relative densities in PBF-LB/M samples than in specimens produced from virgin powder or from powder processed in Ar atmosphere with build plate preheating. Within the investigated process and density range, electrical conductivity correlated primarily with relative density, while grain size, dislocation density, and oxide fraction had secondary effects. PBF-EB/M samples reached nearly full density and electrical conductivities of 101–102% IACS, whereas PBF-LB/M samples exhibited 80–90% IACS depending on sample density.

title: Melt-based 3D printing of PPC/PBS biodegradable membranes featuring a controlled bilayer periosteum-mimetic architecture for guided bone regeneration
abstract: Guided bone regeneration (GBR) requires barrier membranes that combine effective soft-tissue exclusion, sufficient space-maintaining stability, biodegradability, and favorable bone-regenerative performance. In this study, an asymmetric PPC/PBS membrane featuring a precisely controlled bilayer periosteum-mimetic architecture was fabricated by melt-based 3D printing. The membrane consisted of a dense barrier layer and a well-defined porous layer, enabling controlled structural organization on the soft-tissue- and bone-facing surfaces. The printed PPC/PBS membrane exhibited stable tensile properties after hydration, effective inhibition of fibroblast penetration, favorable cytocompatibility, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation and matrix mineralization of MC3T3-E1 cells in vitro. In vivo degradation analysis showed prolonged structural persistence with progressive mechanical deterioration, while rabbit calvarial defect experiments demonstrated progressive bone formation over 12 weeks. Micro-CT and histological analyses showed that the bone-regeneration performance of the PPC/PBS membrane was generally comparable to that of commercial PTFE and Bio-Gide membranes and superior to the untreated control. No evident systemic adverse effects were detected within the evaluated parameters. These findings suggest that melt-printed PPC/PBS bilayer membranes provide a structurally controllable and biodegradable platform with promising potential for GBR applications.

title: Recent advances in ultrasound-responsive bone tissue engineering: mechanisms, designs, and applications
abstract: Bone tissue engineering (BTE) has emerged as a promising strategy for the treatment of diverse skeletal disorders. However, conventional BTE scaffolds often suffer from insufficient functional diversity, limited biological responsiveness, and inadequate spatiotemporal control over therapeutic factors and cellular responses. Ultrasound, particularly low-intensity pulsed ultrasound, has attracted increasing attention as a non-invasive and remotely controllable stimulus in regenerative medicine. By inducing mechanical, electrical, and chemical effects, ultrasound enables the regulation of stimuli-responsive biomaterials and transforms conventional scaffolds from passive structures into dynamically regulated therapeutic platforms. In this review, we summarize the fundamental mechanisms underlying ultrasound-responsive BTE and discuss the design strategies of representative scaffold biomaterials, including hydrogels, ceramics, polymers, and metals. We further highlight their applications in complex bone-related pathological conditions, such as infected bone defects, diabetic bone defects, osteoporosis, and osteosarcoma. In addition, we discuss current challenges associated with ultrasound parameter standardization, material optimization, clinical validation, and future development toward intelligent therapeutic systems. Collectively, ultrasound-responsive BTE provides a promising strategy for integrating remotely controlled acoustic stimulation with biomaterial design, advancing precise and clinically translatable bone regeneration.

title: Corrigendum to “Replication of fusion tokamak plasma disruptions on Eurofer 97 steel using Magnum-PSI” [Mater. Design. 270 (2026)]
From copper Ion flood to lipoylation Collapse: An NIR-II-Responsive CD44-directed nanoplatform for Two-Pronged Strike on Triple-Negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) lacks targetable receptors and rapidly expels cytotoxic copper via ATPase copper–transporting alpha/beta (ATP7A/B) pumps, rendering conventional cuproptosis inducers ineffective. We report an acid-activatable, CD44-directed nanoplatform (CuS@ZIF-8/HA NPs) that converts NIR-II irradiation into a synchronized mitochondrial “copper flood–heat shock” event. In the acidic tumor microenvironment, ZIF-8 decomposes and releases Cu 2+ , which is reduced to cytotoxic Cu + , triggering oligomerization of lipoylated dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase (DLAT), the core driver of cuproptosis. Concomitant ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) protein degradation serves as a downstream biochemical marker of cuproptotic injury. The photothermal effect (55.6 °C at 1 W cm −2 ) simultaneously accelerates copper release, amplifies oxidative damage, and ablates cells by hyperthermia. In 4 T1 tumor mice model, eight i.v. doses (10 mg kg −1 ) plus NIR-II light achieved profound tumor suppression without relapse or systemic toxicity, outperforming either monotherapy. Thus, CuS@ZIF-8/HA NPs turns NIR-II light into a spatially confined cuproptotic-photothermal double hit, offering a safe, precise, and translatable strategy against therapy-refractory TNBC.

title: First-principles screening of PbI2 adsorption on functionalized biochar-inspired carbon
abstract: Lead leakage from degraded and end-of-life perovskite photovoltaic modules motivates the development of sorbents capable of immobilizing neutral PbI₂, a representative Pb-containing degradation product. Here, first-principles calculations were used to screen graphene-like carbon motifs bearing carboxyl, amine, thiol, phosphate-like, and pyridinic-N sites under dry conditions and in relaxed-interface implicit-water environments. In the dry baseline, G–NH₂ binds PbI₂ most strongly (Eₐdₛ = −1.576 eV, Pb–N = 2.239 Å), followed by pyridinic-N graphene (−1.442 eV) and G–PO₃H₂ (−1.423 eV). All functionalized motifs outperform pristine graphene (−0.671 eV). Pb-directed sampling is essential for thiol and phosphate-like groups, which otherwise relax into shallow, non-coordinated minima. Relaxed-interface implicit water preserves the functionalization advantage but alters motif robustness: G–NH₂ remains the strongest binder (−1.803 eV), whereas O-, S-, and P-containing motifs are more strongly screened. Charge-density-difference, projected-density-of-states, and COHP analyses indicate Pb-centered coordination, orbital coupling, and interfacial polarization rather than substantial net charge transfer. Short molecular dynamics simulations at 300 K show no spontaneous dissociation of representative N- and O-bound contacts within 5 ps. These results identify N-rich and selected phosphate-like carbon motifs as experimentally testable candidates for PbI₂ retention from perovskite waste streams.

title: Mangiferin-loaded biomimetic coaxial scaffolds promote bone repair by reprogramming the osteoimmune microenvironment via NF-κB/CXCL2 pathway inhibition
abstract: The initial inflammatory response and osteogenic microenvironment dysregulation critically hinder oral and maxillofacial bone defect repair. Fabricating scaffolds integrating early immune remodeling with mid-to-late osteoinduction is essential to address current repair bottlenecks. This study designs a novel core–shell coaxial electrospun scaffold. Its polylactic acid/nano-mineralized collagen core provides mechanical support and osteoinductivity, while the gelatin shell loads natural anti-inflammatory mangiferin (MAG) to ameliorate early acute inflammation. Physicochemical tests confirm the scaffold possesses good biocompatibility and enables sustained in vitro MAG release. Biological evaluations identify 0.8 % as the optimal MAG concentration, which induces RAW264.7 macrophage polarization toward the reparative M2 phenotype and further promotes BMSC osteogenic differentiation. Proteomic analysis and rescue experiments validate that the scaffold inhibits macrophage NF-κB signaling activation, downregulates CXCL2 secretion, and relieves inflammation-induced suppression of BMSCs osteogenesis. Rat mandibular critical-sized bone defect models verify that the scaffold alleviates local inflammation and enhances in vivo bone regeneration. This MAG-loaded mineralized collagen coaxial scaffold exhibits superior biocompatibility and osteoimmunomodulatory capacity, serving as a promising candidate for clinical oral and maxillofacial bone defect therapy.

title: Coupled evolution of gas pores and hydrogen in spray-formed 2195 Al alloy during solution treatment and quenching
abstract: This study investigates the coupled evolution of gas pores and hydrogen in a spray-formed 2195 (SF-2195) aluminum alloy during solution treatment and quenching. The water-quenched (WQ) sample exhibited the highest gas porosity and the largest average pore size, followed by the air-cooled (AC) sample and then the hot-rolled (HR) sample. The quenching-induced stress gradient promoted pore expansion and coalescence, while the elevated internal pressure generated by the hydrogen trapped in pores further drove pore growth. The total hydrogen content was highest in the WQ sample (8.00 wt ppm), exceeding that of the HR (4.87 wt ppm) and AC (4.45 wt ppm) samples. The significant hydrogen uptake during water quenching stemmed from the vigorous reaction between water vapor and the fresh alloy surface. The content of hydrogen trapped in pores was also the highest in the WQ sample because water quenching uniquely provides an additional hydrogen supply and induced increased density of pores acting as trapping sites. These findings provide new insights into the coupled evolution of pores and hydrogen behavior during quenching and offer practical guidance for designing quenching protocols for spray-formed Al-Cu-Li alloys.

title: Lignin-based polyurethane elastomers combining excellent mechanical properties and self-healing behavior for flexible sensing and biomedicine applications
abstract: Conventional polyurethane elastomers face challenges in balancing mechanical properties, self-healing ability, and biosafety, along with heavy reliance on petrochemical resources. Here, we propose a strategy combining dynamic covalent crosslinking with nano-interfacial toughening to construct a lignin-based self-healing polyurethane (TPU-LNP). A dithiol-bis(boronic ester) chain extender (BDB) was synthesized to introduce reversible crosslinks into the polyurethane backbone, while nanoscale lignin particles serve as a green reinforcing phase, forming multiple hydrogen bonds and enabling stress transfer. The dynamic network and physical interfacial interactions synergistically overcome the typical trade-off between strength and self-healing efficiency. Compared with single dynamic network polyurethane (P-TPU), TPU-LNP shows > 500% increase in tensile strength while retaining 1000% elongation at break. Efficient self-healing of TPU-LNP is achieved under ambient conditions, and the tensile strength of the healed specimen is still 3.9 times that of P-TPU. Sensors fabricated with this elastomer as the flexible substrate exhibit sensitive strain-sensing capacity and can capture diverse human movements, demonstrating great application potential in wearable monitoring. In vitro and in vivo biocompatibility evaluations verify that the material possesses extremely low cytotoxicity and triggers negligible tissue inflammatory responses, indicating its adequate biosafety. This work offers a route to high-performance self-healing elastomers for biomedical and smart flexible applications.

title: Design of hybrid anapole metal–dielectric cavities for giant magnetic Purcell enhancement
abstract: Magnetic resonances enable subwavelength localization of optical magnetic fields, yet their enhancement is fundamentally limited by the weak magnetic response at optical frequencies. Here, we report a periodic gold–silicon–gold symmetric reflective disk supporting a magnetic anapole (MA) resonance via hybridization of a gold gap mode and a silicon electric anapole mode. The resulting mode exhibits spatial and spectral overlap of electric and magnetic responses. Experiments confirm its excitation, yielding electric and magnetic field enhancements of 17 and 35, respectively, with a magnetic Purcell factor up to ~512. By incorporating lattice resonances, radiation loss is further suppressed, increasing the Q factor from 24 to 148 and enhancing the electric and magnetic fields to 50 and 120, respectively, and boosting the magnetic Purcell factor to ~1200—representing a 3–5 times improvement over conventional designs. These results establish a compact platform for magnetic-field–driven nonlinear optics and single-photon emission.

title: Sono-responsive self-assembled coppery nanodrugs amplify cuproptosis for high-efficiency cancer chemo-immunotherapy
abstract: Cuproptosis-based therapy holds great promise in boosting systemic anti-tumor efficacy, especially when synergistically combined with sonodynamic therapy, which amplifies oxidative stress and offers superior tissue-penetration capabilities. In this study, a cuproptosis amplifier (DTX/TPPS-Cu) was developed through copper ion-mediated coordinative self-assembly of the sonosensitizer porphyrin (TPPS) and the chemotherapeutic agent docetaxel (DTX), aiming to boost cancer chemo-immunotherapy. DTX/TPPS-Cu nanoparticles internalized by tumor cells can be activated by intracellular glutathione (GSH) to release Cu⁺, which induces the oligomerization of lipoylated proteins, thereby triggering proteotoxic stress and irreversible cuproptosis. Upon ultrasound irradiation, the released TPPS generates a sonodynamic effect that further depletes excessive GSH, thereby preventing Cu⁺ chelation and amplifying cuproptosis in tumor cells, ultimately sensitizing DTX-mediated chemotherapy. More importantly, the significantly elevated reactive oxygen species levels and highly efficient cuproptosis contribute to the reversal of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, thereby promoting immunogenic cell death and eliciting robust systemic anti-tumor immune responses for the tumor eradication. Thus, we propose a precisely regulated sonodynamic cuproptosis strategy to amplify chemo-immunotherapeutic efficacy, potentially heralding a new paradigm in cancer therapy.

title: Nuclear-targeted CeO2 nanozymes drive cuproptosis and immunotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Nucleus-targeted nanocatalysis potentiates mild photothermal therapy (mPTT), establishing a coherent therapeutic axis that couples chemosensitization with systemic antitumor immune activation. Herein, we designed a multifunctional nanozyme, HCuS@Cu 2 S@Au/PEI@CeO 2 @DOX/ICG@9R-P201 (HAPCDI9P). The platform orchestrates triple enzyme-mimetic functionalities—catalase (CAT), peroxidase (POD), and phosphatase—wherein the phosphatase-like activity is functionally corroborated by ATP-depletion-mediated suppression of heat shock proteins (HSP70/HSP90). These actions collectively enhance the efficacy of mPTT. The 9R-P201 peptide confers active nuclear targeting, enabling efficient therapeutic delivery to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells. Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) excitation, the nanozymatic construct elicited dose-saturating orthotopic tumor growth arrest (96.3 % suppression) through convergent multimodal engagement. Mechanistically, the therapeutic endpoint was gated by copper-dependent mitochondrial proteotoxic collapse along the canonical cuproptosis-like cell death pathway, alongside robust antitumor immune responses that effectively inhibit tumor recurrence. This work establishes nuclear-targeted nanozyme-mPTT as a potent strategy and expands the biomedical applicability of nanozymes.

title: Synergistic interaction of 3D printing high-speed and nozzle temperature on energy absorption and manufacturing efficiency
abstract: FFF (fused filament fabrication) is among the most popular additive manufacturing techniques; nevertheless, enhancing production efficiency without any degradation in mechanical properties is still a major issue. While numerous studies have investigated the influence of print speed and print temperature, the relationship between them, especially at higher print speeds, has not been researched extensively. Thus, the current research seeks to investigate the impact of high printing speed and temperature on the energy absorption capacity of FFF-printed structures in three repetitions. There was no deterioration of the energy absorption capability when printing speed was increased from 50 mm/s to 450 mm/s. At 230 °C, the specimen with a printing speed of 450 mm/s gave the highest total energy absorption (TEA) and specific energy absorption (SEA) of 31.4 J and 5.17 J/g, respectively, which were about 4.6% and 4.3% higher than those at a speed of 50 mm/s. In light of manufacturing time, normalized TEA and normalized SEA have risen by about 22.0% and 21.7%, respectively. The results confirm a pronounced interaction between printing speed and nozzle temperature, suggesting that high-speed FFF has the potential to increase manufacturing efficiency while maintaining and potentially improving the energy absorbing properties of PLA structures.

title: Injectable ophthalmic hydrogels: design principles, therapeutic mechanisms, clinical applications, and translational perspectives
abstract: Injectable ophthalmic hydrogels are increasingly investigated as local delivery and tissue-support platforms for ocular therapy, particularly where eye drops are cleared rapidly and repeated intraocular injections increase clinical burden. After administration, these materials form hydrated polymer networks that can retain therapeutic agents, tune their diffusion, protect fragile cargos, and provide temporary biomechanical cues to damaged tissues. Their clinical use, however, is constrained by the unique intolerance of ocular tissues to material mismatch. A translational hydrogel must preserve vision, avoid pressure- or swelling-induced damage, adapt mechanically to the target compartment, degrade in a predictable manner, and be manufactured and sterilized without compromising performance. This review presents a structure–function-translation framework for injectable ophthalmic hydrogels. We relate ocular barriers, delivery routes, and payload properties to the choice of polymer chemistry and gelation mechanism, and compare natural, synthetic, hybrid, and composite systems through the way their networks form and evolve in vivo. We further discuss how network architecture controls drug release, tissue integration, optical behavior, and therapeutic duration. Finally, we outline design principles for clinically viable systems, arguing that while future hydrogels should evolve from passive depots toward responsive and multifunctional platforms, translational success will depend on maintaining sufficient robustness and simplicity to meet well-defined therapeutic needs without compromising ocular safety or reproducibility

title: Achieving strength-ductility synergy in Au-Pt alloys through systematic screening of alloying elements: First-principles insights
abstract: The intrinsically low strength of Au-Pt alloys remains a key obstacle to their wider use in advanced applications requiring high mechanical reliability and service durability. To address this issue, we employ first-principles calculations to systematically evaluate the effects of diverse alloying elements on their mechanical properties, aiming to identify promising candidates for alloy design. A combined analysis of solid-solution strengthening and slip barrier reveals that Re and Os, located near the boundary between the high-melting transition and platinum-group metals, together with rare-earth element Ce, exhibit an outstanding strength-ductility synergy. Notably, the strengthening induced by high-melting transition additions is primarily governed by chemical interactions, whereas lattice distortion arising from volume misfit dominates for most other solutes. Ce delivers the strongest solid-solution strengthening due to its largest size mismatch. Electronic structure analyses further reveal that solid-solution strengthening originates from the injection of additional valence electrons. Meanwhile, Ce uniquely reduces the slip barrier by weakening the local bonding character in the vicinity of the Fermi level, thereby effectively preserving the intrinsic slip capability of the Au-Pt base alloy while markedly enhancing strength. Overall, this work provides a quantitative basis and mechanistic guidance for performance optimization and ternary-alloy design of Au-Pt alloys
