title: Research on the characterization and multiscale constitutive model of 2A10 aluminum alloy under transverse ultrasonic vibration-assisted compression
abstract: The prediction of microstructural characteristics during the deformation of metals has consistently been a key area of research. Previous studies have shown that ultrasonic vibration-assisted riveting experimentally produces quantitative changes in grain size (GS) and geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density of rivets. However, existing microscale theoretical models predominantly focus on the prediction of total dislocation density. Moreover, most established models are developed for longitudinal ultrasonic vibration, while few studies have addressed the quantitative prediction of GS and GND density of microstructural characteristics during transverse ultrasonic vibration-assisted forming. Therefore, this study focused on 2A10 aluminum alloy specimens, which are widely used in aviation. Transverse ultrasonic vibration-assisted compression (TUVAC) tests were performed under different ultrasonic amplitudes. Based on the experimental investigation, a multiscale ultrasonic constitutive model incorporating GND density and GS was established, and a VUMAT subroutine was developed to predict the microstructural characteristics of the 2A10 aluminum alloy in TUVAC simulations. The results indicated that the maximum flow stress decreased from 509.7 MPa to 477.4 MPa as the ultrasonic amplitude increased from 0 μm to 21.2 μm. Compared to the original specimen, the intensity of the < 111>||ND fiber texture decreased significantly after simple compression. When transverse ultrasonic vibration was applied during compression, the Copper texture continuously weakened and the Brass texture gradually strengthened with increasing ultrasonic amplitude. In contrast, both the S texture and the < 111>||ND fiber texture initially increased and then decreased. GND density increased nonlinearly while the GS gradually decreased, indicating significant grain refinement. The predicted results of the ultrasonic constitutive model were compared with experimental data. This comparison showed that the average absolute relative error (AARE) for stress remained below 2.2 % under different amplitudes. A comparative analysis of experimental and simulation results revealed that the maximum AARE was approximately 15 % for GND density, approximately 12 % for GS, and below 5 % for microhardness. Thus, the proposed constitutive model can accurately predict both macroscopic mechanical behavior and microstructural characteristics and thereby provides a solid theoretical foundation for further investigation into the micro-mechanisms and performance of ultrasonic-assisted riveting.

title: Scalable fabrication and mechanical behaviour of hierarchical porous nickel networks
abstract: As the demand for light-weight structural and functional materials grows, the fabrication of hierarchical, high-performance micro- and nano-architectures becomes increasingly important. Here, we present a scalable alloying–dealloying strategy to fabricate porous metal with two- and three-level hierarchical networks (2 L-/3 L-HN). By exploiting the vapour pressure difference between Ni and Zn, vapour phase alloying of Ni foam with Zn, followed by vapour phase dealloying of the resulting -Zn 84 Ni 16 foam, generates a second hierarchical level, producing 2 L-HN Ni or 2 L-HN -Zn 50 Ni 50 . Re-alloying 2 L-HN -Zn 50 Ni 50 to 2 L-HN -Zn 84 Ni 16 via vapour phase alloying while preserving its hierarchical architecture enables chemical dealloying to create a third level of hierarchy at the nanoscale, producing 3 L-HN Ni with significantly increased specific surface area. A novel scaling law is proposed to predict the mechanical properties of these hierarchical porous metallic networks as a function of solid fraction, and its validity is supported through compression tests on 2 L-HN Ni with varying densities. This work establishes a scalable and versatile route for fabricating multiscale porous metallic networks with light-weight, tunable mechanical performance and high surface area.

title: Effect of long-term ageing and associated precipitation on creep deformation behaviour of a Ni based superalloy
abstract: Creep behaviour of solution-treated and isothermally aged Ni-based superalloy Haynes 282 was investigated in the temperature and stress range of 750–800 °C and 300–420 MPa, respectively. Ageing was carried out at 750 °C for 46, 470, and 6000 h, resulting in progressive γʹ precipitate coarsening with negligible grain growth. Creep deformation occurred predominantly in the steady-state and tertiary regimes. The minimum creep rate, ε̇ min , initially decreased with ageing and reached its lowest value for the 470 h aged alloy, followed by a marked increase after 6000 h ageing, while rupture life exhibited the opposite trend. The threshold stress corrected-stress exponent, n eff , of all alloys is between 4–7, indicating that the steady-state creep rate is governed by dislocation glide mediated climb. Post-creep microstructural analysis revealed precipitate shearing and stacking faults within γʹ precipitates in all samples except the 6000 h aged condition, where γʹ precipitates exhibited nanotwins and were surrounded by dense dislocation networks. Variations in creep response are explained by changes in stress required for precipitate shearing or bypass and increasing contribution of dislocation climb in coarser precipitates. Tertiary creep mechanisms leading to intergranular fracture are discussed in brief, and a critical appraisal of service life extrapolation methods is provided.

title: Dirac tuning and boundary-induced topological robust transmission in symmetric honeycomb optical waveguide networks
abstract: Topological valley Hall photonic structures enable low-loss, robust light propagation without external excitation, emerging as a critical frontier for integrated photonic chips. Here we propose multi-connected honeycomb optical waveguide networks (OWNs), and analytically derive its dispersion relation. We systematically demonstrate that the degeneracy of -point Dirac cones is governed by the parity of waveguide length ratios. Odd length ratios enable robust formation of frequency-locked -point Dirac cones, which exhibit outstanding frequency stability and defect immunity and further give rise to a distinctive pseudo-diffusive transport response. In contrast, K-point Dirac cones exhibit unprecedented tunability, where their quantity and frequency positions can be flexibly regulated by varying the length ratios. These tailored Dirac modes efficiently excite boundary-induced topological edge states, realizing unidirectional boundary transmission. Defect simulations confirm that the excited edge states maintain robust propagation against local defects at both structure boundaries and interior domains. Different from conventional symmetry-breaking schemes relying on sublattice parameter modulation, our strategy constructs topological domain interfaces purely via finite-lattice boundary configuration differences, fundamentally eliminating fabrication errors and extra optical losses introduced by traditional designs. This work deepens the physical understanding of Dirac dispersion engineering, offering a novel paradigm for low-loss integrated topological photonic devices.

title: Architecture-property-performance relationships in pressure-relieving support structures: A finite element and multi-indicator design framework
abstract: Pressure-relieving cushions and mattresses increasingly use porous or lattice architectures, yet their performance is often evaluated using limited pressure metrics, obscuring the relationships among structural compliance, pressure redistribution, and stress concentration. Here, we aimed to determine whether greater structural compliance necessarily leads to a more favorable pressure-relieving mechanical response by comparing five support-interface configurations: solid, orthogonal lattice, honeycomb, auxetic, and cylindrical-array models. All models shared the same external dimensions, material properties, contact definitions, and boundary conditions. The primary comparison used a common prescribed-indentation protocol, while supplementary force-controlled simulations examined loading-mode sensitivity. Contact pressure, effective contact area, pressure uniformity, deformation, apparent stiffness, and von Mises stress were evaluated. At maximum indentation, porous configurations reduced the apparent stiffness index by 53.8–72.9% relative to the solid model. However, the most compliant honeycomb configuration did not show the lowest peak pressure and exhibited relatively high stress measures. The orthogonal lattice configuration produced the lowest peak contact pressure (5.837 kPa; 26.9% lower) and 95th-percentile contact pressure (4.225 kPa; 44.3% lower), while maintaining a comparable effective contact area. It ranked first under all tested weighting schemes. These results indicate that pressure reduction depends on structural arrangement, contact response, and stress transfer rather than stiffness alone.

title: Metallurgy-inspired multi-modal design and interfacial strengthening of heterogeneous lattice structures for superior compressive performance
abstract: Inspired by the synergistic strengthening mechanisms of heterogeneous grain structures in metallurgy, this study proposes a novel multi-modal design strategy that integrates global architectural layout design with local interfacial strengthening. Rather than relying solely on conventional density-based topology optimization, we introduce scaling resolution together with relative density to construct a stiffness-efficient lattice architecture and evaluate the impact on deformation behaviors and collapse stability. Meanwhile, a genetic algorithm (GA)-based interfacial optimization method is developed to emulate grain boundary strengthening, effectively bridging dissimilar lattice blocks and alleviating localized stress concentrations without changing the original lattice configuration or volume. Fabricated via fused deposition modeling (FDM), the designed lattice structures exhibit a transition from shear slipping to stable progressive buckling and collapse. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multi-modal design with GA-optimized transitions achieves increases of 18.61 % in stiffness, 42.57 % in strength, and 78.90 % in energy absorption relative to the average properties of the three benchmark uniform reference lattices. Compared with the linearly-tapered transition design, the GA-optimized design further achieves average enhancements of 1.03 % in stiffness, 10.18 % in strength, and 12.05 % in energy absorption. This metallurgy-inspired paradigm provides an effective pathway for unlocking the load-bearing and energy-dissipating potential of advanced heterogeneous lattices.

title: Debris cloud redirection in origami-inspired foldcore structures under hypervelocity impact: a review
abstract: The increasing population of micrometeoroids and orbital debris (MMOD) has intensified the need for lightweight and efficient shielding systems capable of withstanding hypervelocity impacts (HVI). Conventional shielding concepts, such as Whipple shields and honeycomb or foam-core sandwich panels, primarily rely on projectile fragmentation and energy absorption but provide limited control over the resulting debris cloud. Origami inspired foldcore structures have recently attracted attention because their open-channel geometry offers the potential to influence fragment trajectories through geometric design. This review summarizes the current state of research on foldcore sandwich structures subjected to HVI, covering both experimental investigations and numerical simulations. The influence of fold geometry, material system, impact location, and loading conditions on debris cloud formation, redirection, and dispersion is discussed and compared with conventional shielding concepts. Based on the available literature, the governing mechanisms of debris-cloud control are identified, and a conceptual Redirection Efficiency Index (REI) together with quantitative descriptors for debris trajectory characterization are proposed to support future performance assessment. The review also discusses current limitations in experimental validation and numerical modelling, and highlights research needs including standardized testing procedures, cumulative damage under repeated impacts, and integrated experimental-computational approaches for the development of future spacecraft shielding systems.

title: Engineering a multifunctional Fe–Mn–Al–Cr–C–Ti alloy combining superior mechanical properties with temperature-stable high electrical resistivity
abstract: We designed and investigated a high-performance multifunctional steel with high strength, low density, high electrical resistivity, low temperature coefficient of resistivity (TCR), and good hot/cold workability. The designed alloy, with a nominal composition of Fe-19.3Mn-22.7Al-1.8Cr-4.7C (at.%) showed a γ phase containing κ-ordered precipitates and an ordered BCC (D03) phase. Furthermore, the addition of 0.1 at.% Ti into the designed alloy was found to induce the formation of NaCl-type TiC carbides, leading to microstructural refinement and improved hot workability. The 0.1 at.% Ti-added alloy (0.1Ti alloy) heat-treated at 1100 ℃ for 120 min had a high yield strength (>1000 MPa), high ultimate tensile strength (>1200 MPa), and moderate tensile elongation of 10% due to the combination of shearable ordered phases, grain refinement, κ-ordered precipitate refinement, and Ti carbide precipitation. The 0.1Ti alloy had a density of 6.47 g/cm3, resulting in a specific strength of 196 MPa·cm3/g in the air-cooled alloy. In addition, when heat-treated at 1100 ℃ for 40 min followed by air cooling, the 0.1Ti alloy contained a moderate amount of ordered BCC (D03) phase, achieving a high resistivity (>190 μΩ∙cm) and low TCR (15 ppm/℃) within the temperature range of 25–100 ℃.

title: Research on Cr-Ni-Mn metastable austenitic steel with tunable magnetism via martensitic transformation
abstract: By exploiting the reversible transformation between non-magnetic austenite and ferromagnetic martensite in steel, magnetic properties can be controlled without altering the chemical composition. However, existing austenitic steels are not designed with a focus on magnetic transformation. This work analyzed the effects of major alloying elements in metastable austenitic steels and key parameters related to martensite transformation to propose a composition design that maintains non-magnetic austenite at room temperature while enabling efficient and reversible magnetic control. The target composition range is Cr: 16.3 ± 0.3 wt%, Ni: 8.5 ± 0.3 wt%, and Mn: 1.0 ± 0.2 wt%. Steel samples within this target range were prepared via melting. Microstructural characterization reveals that the as-prepared matrix consists predominantly of austenite. After mechanical impact, partial austenite transforms into martensite, converting the material from a non-magnetic to a ferromagnetic state. The unit magnetic weight ratio of the target sample increases by 613.07 %, significantly exceeding that of commercial AISI 301 austenitic steel (22.28 %). Moreover, deviations from the target composition result in diminished magnetic transformation efficiency. After heat treatment, the martensite phase in the sample reverts to austenite, and the saturation magnetization recovers to 83.34 % of its initial value. This work provides a reference for further tuning magnetism via martensitic transformation.

title: Tuning texture, grain size, and [111] grain boundary type in aluminum films on (0001) α-Al2O3
abstract: Thin films have increasing industrial applications and are also in great demand scientifically as they allow to experimentally investigate the atomic structures of grain boundaries (GBs). Frequently, fcc thin films are strongly (111) textured and contain columnar grains separated by tilt GBs. It is widely acknowledged that the deposition parameters affect evolution of the microstructure and, in turn, the properties of fcc thin films. However, the influence of deposition parameters on [111] tilt GB distributions remain largely unexplored. This study examines Al thin films, grown on (0001) oriented sapphire substrates by using e-beam evaporation at varying temperatures (room temperature-300 °C). An experimentally established processing parameter window is developed based on the observed dependence of film density, surface morphology, texture, grain size, and GB morphology on the deposition conditions. The aim is to obtain Al films with smooth and dense surfaces, uniform thickness, large grain size (>10 μm), and a wide distribution of [111] columnar tilt GBs. Systematic characterization of the resulting microstructures by scanning/transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM) therefore identifies a processing window near or above 300 °C at 3 Å/s for obtaining columnar grains with a common surface normal required for atomic-resolution investigations. Atomic-resolution STEM imaging with atomistic simulations elucidate the structures of [111] low-angle tilt GBs for varying misorientation angles. The atomic-scale dislocation configurations at the GBs are characterized to understand the relationship between dislocation structures and boundary geometry.

title: Tailoring magnetic Fe3O4 nanocarriers with chitosan and β-cyclodextrin for optimized ciprofloxacin release: a comparative study
abstract: Natural polysaccharide-derived materials such as chitosan (CS) and β–cyclodextrin (β–CD) have emerged as versatile platforms for designing next–generation drug delivery systems owing to their adjustable physicochemical behavior and excellent biocompatibility. In this work, magnetic nanocarriers based on Fe 3 O 4 were engineered in two forms, CS–coated nanoparticles (Fe 3 O 4 @CS) and β–CD–functionalized chitosan nanoparticles (Fe 3 O 4 @CS–g–β–CD), to investigate their performance in transporting ciprofloxacin (CIP). Structural, morphological, and magnetic analyses using 1 H NMR, FT–IR, FESEM, TEM, XRD, EDX, VSM, TGA, and zeta potential measurements verified the successful fabrication and stability of the hybrids. Drug loading parameters and release behavior were quantified via UV–Vis spectroscopy, and kinetic modeling was applied to clarify the release mechanisms. The β–CD–grafted system exhibited markedly enhanced CIP release, attributed to the combined effects of β–CD inclusion capability and the mucoadhesive nature of CS. Cytotoxicity assessments further demonstrated that Fe 3 O 4 @CS–g–β–CD/CIP achieved superior selective anticancer activity (SI = 2.42 at 48 h) compared with Fe 3 O 4 @CS/CIP (SI = 1.52), underscoring the beneficial role of β–CD incorporation in improving therapeutic efficacy

title: 3D-printed Soft Optical sensor with a Lens (SOLen) for light guidance in mechanosensing
abstract: Additive manufacturing is enabling soft robots with increasingly complex geometries, creating a demand for sensing solutions compatible with single-material, one-step fabrication. Optical soft sensors are attractive for monolithic printing, but their performance is often degraded by uncontrolled light propagation (ambient coupling, leakage, scattering), while common mitigation strategies require multimaterial interfaces. Here, we present a 3D-printed soft optical sensor with a lens (SOLen), in which a printed lens is placed in front of an emitter within a Y-shaped waveguide. The sensing mechanism relies on deformation-induced lens rotation and focal-spot translation, redistributing optical power between two branches to generate a differential output that encodes motion direction and amplitude. An acrylate polyurethane resin was modified to improve compliance, and single-layer characterization was used to derive wavelength-dependent optical properties while minimizing printed layer-related artifacts. The refractive index was used in simulations to design a lens for a target focal distance, which was then printed with sub-millimeter fidelity. Rotational tests demonstrated reproducible branch-selective signal switching over multiple cycles, increasing sensitivity by over 65-fold compared with a configuration without a lens. These results establish a transferable material-to-optics workflow applicable to any printable transparent material, opening new perspectives for monolithic soft robots with direction-sensitive optical sensing.

title: Influence of pad grooves and retaining rings on slurry renewal in chemical mechanical polishing: a local mean age approach
abstract: Slurry renewal in chemical mechanical polishing (CMP) controls fresh-slurry delivery and aged-slurry removal at the confined pad–wafer interface. This study develops a three-dimensional transient computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model with local mean-age transport to quantify effects of pad grooves and retaining-ring confinement on slurry residence. The age-of-fluid scalar and solver settings were verified using analytical pipe-flow and plane Couette-flow benchmarks, with age errors below 1.5% and velocity-slope deviation below 0.01%. Three geometries were compared under identical conditions: non-grooved, concentric-grooved, and grooved pads with a retaining ring. The normalized age of fluid, , and high-age area fraction diagnose delayed renewal. Pad grooves reduced pad-side high-age area from 73.5% to 45.7% and wafer-side area from 11.4% to 4.7%. Because mean in-plane velocity changed by less than 1%, the improvement is attributed to transport-topology modification and surface-normal exchange, not bulk acceleration. Retaining-ring confinement lowered pad-side high-age area from 45.7% to 32.2%, but slightly increased wafer-side area from 4.7% to 5.6% while reducing wafer-side age variation. This framework supports mechanism-based evaluation of CMP geometries.

title: 3D-printed glass–ceramic composite scaffolds based on borosilicate bioactive glasses and Ag/Sr-substituted hydroxyapatite for bone regeneration and infection control
abstract: The incidence of bone defects and implant-associated infections is increasing due to population aging, rising injury rates, and antimicrobial resistance. To address these challenges, multifunctional glass–ceramic composite scaffolds based on borosilicate bioactive glass (BG) and silver/strontium-substituted hydroxyapatite (Ag/Sr-HAp) were fabricated by robocasting (direct ink writing). Scaffolds with varying BG/HAp ratios exhibited a biphasic composition, interconnected macroporosity (200–600 μm), compressive strengths of 0.12–17.22 MPa, and Young’s moduli of 5.65–382.06 MPa. All scaffolds showed a negative zeta potential, with less negative surface charge correlating with increased protein adsorption. Human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells displayed good viability, proliferation, and osteogenic markers expression on scaffolds containing no or low Ag + content, whereas higher Ag + concentrations induced cytotoxicity. Antibacterial activity against S. aureus and Escherichia coli was achieved with scaffolds containing higher Ag + concentrations, producing complete bacterial growth reduction. Minimum bactericidal concentration analysis revealed that the 20.0 mol% Ag/Sr-HAp scaffold required approximately 50% lower concentrations to eliminate bacteria than the 10.0 mol% counterpart. The results demonstrate that optimizing Ag + incorporation is critical for balancing antibacterial efficacy and biological performance in bioactive scaffolds for bone regeneration.

title: Interfacial characteristics and microstructure morphology evolution of W/Cu heterogeneous structures fabricated by multi-material laser powder bed fusion
abstract: W/Cu heterogeneous structures hold an irreplaceable position in extreme-service environments due to their high-temperature damage resistance and excellent plasma radiation resistance. However, the fabrication of W/Cu heterogeneous interfaces remains challenging due to negligible mutual solubility and severe thermophysical mismatch. In this study, W/Cu heterogeneous interfaces without obvious macroscopic or continuous interfacial cracking were fabricated via multi-material laser powder bed fusion (MM-LPBF) without an interlayer. A dual-region interfacial structure was identified within the interfacial transition region, consisting of a Cu-rich discrete region and a W-dominated skeleton region, which strongly influenced the interfacial characteristics and microstructural evolution. Specifically, the interpenetrating W/Cu morphology promoted mechanical interlocking, whereas the ∼58.8 nm interfacial transition layer enabled metallurgical interactions. Cu appeared to facilitate thermal-strain accommodation and reduce the tendency for W cracking, while W became irregular and fragmented under shear associated with the velocity mismatch between the dissimilar phases. Meanwhile, Cu grains exhibited systematic variations in grain size, texture, and stress accumulation. These findings offer valuable insights for the fabrication of high-quality W/Cu heterogeneous interfaces via MM-LPBF

title: High-entropy stabilized A-site cation occupancy in filled tungsten bronzes with great piezoelectric performance
abstract: The high-entropy design concept has been widely applied to perovskite ferroelectrics, leading to new compositions and promising functional properties. However, the structure–property relationships in filled tungsten bronze ferroelectrics designed via the high-entropy concept remain largely unexplored. In this work, a high-entropy tungsten bronze ceramic with nominal composition Ca 0.5 Sr 0.5 Ba 0.5 Pb 0.5 NaNb 5 O 15 (CSBPN) was synthesized by introducing Ca2 + and Pb2 + into the A-site of the structure. Structural analysis shows that CSBPN adopts an orthorhombic structure (space group Bbm2). This symmetry indicates the absence of non-180° domain walls, which is further supported by electron microscopy observations and electro-strain measurements. Dielectric measurements reveal a diffused phase transition associated with A-site compositional disorder, rather than relaxor characteristics. The XRD and dielectric results indicates structural stability under variations in temperature and applied electric field, which is attributed to the high-entropy effects of sluggish diffusion and severe lattice distortion. Hysteresis-free strain–electric field (S–E) loops were observed, suggesting that the field-induced strain is dominated by piezoelectric and electrostrictive contributions. The CSBPN ceramic exhibits d 33 = 72 pC/N, low Q m = 5, and strong anisotropy in electromechanical coupling ( k t = 0.46, k p = 0.15). These characteristics make CSBPN a promising candidate for piezoelectric ultrasonic detection.

title: Mechanical interlocking as a design-driven approach to strengthen multi-material laser powder bed fusion interface
abstract: Multi-material laser powder bed fusion (MM-LPBF) enables spatial control of material composition, offering a pathway to fabricate complex designs with localized properties. However, the performance of MM-LPBF components is limited by weak metallurgical bonding and defect formation, where differences in thermal conductivity, melting point, and solubility lead to lack of fusion, cracking, or intermetallic formation. This study investigates mechanically interlocked interfacial geometries as a strategy to improve tensile bonding strength and ductility. Tensile specimens were fabricated using 316L stainless steel and CuCrZr with three interface designs: flat interface, dovetail joint, and dual interlocked solid gyroid. Mechanical testing showed that the interlocked geometries achieved approximately 9% higher yield load and exhibiting ductile failure modes rather than brittle separation. Finite element analysis (FEA) revealed that with greater interfacial interlocking mechanism (e.g., 3D interlocked features), the predicted stress–strain response aligned more closely with experimental behavior. Microstructural analysis using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and micro-computed topography (micro-CT) confirmed interface defect patterns influenced by build orientation. Results demonstrate that geometric interlocking can effectively mitigate the influence of interfacial defects, providing a practical design-based approach to enhance the mechanical integrity of MM-LPBF parts.

title: Microstructure-based design criteria for crack-free self-pierce riveting of hypoeutectic AlSi casting alloys
abstract: Mechanical joining of large aluminium-silicon (AlSi) castings produced via megacasting poses a significant challenge in multi-material vehicle chassis design, as the inherent brittleness of hypoeutectic AlSi alloys leads to crack formation during self-pierce riveting (SPR). To establish evidence-based design criteria for crack-free joining, this study characterises the microstructure, mechanical properties, and SPR joinability of three hypoeutectic AlSi casting alloys (AlSi9, AlSi10Mg, and AlSi12) across solidification rates from 2.89 K/s to 65.54 K/s in as-cast and heat-treated conditions. Increasing solidification rate modifies the DAS and silicon morphology, improving ductility and reducing crack susceptibility during joining. Joinability thresholds are identified: 23.5 K/s for AlSi9, 5.4 K/s for AlSi12, and 59.63 K/s combined with precipitation hardening at 120 °C for AlSi10Mg. Solution annealing spheroidises Si particles, compensating for insufficient solidification rates, enabling crack-free joints down to 2.89 K/s. Based on these findings, microstructure–property–joinability correlations, a joinability prognosis model, and a logistic crack-susceptibility model are established for Si contents between 9.75 wt% and 11.75 wt%. Both models utilise solidification rate and DAS as input parameters, enabling quantitative predictions of joining suitability and crack formation, and providing an evidence-based foundation for the process and material design of AlSi castings in mechanical joining processes.

title: Alginate scaffolds functionalized with calcium-stabilized cubic zirconia nanoparticles for periodontal tissue engineering
abstract: Alveolar bone regeneration is challenging due to the adverse microenvironment, characterized by irregular bone defects, bacteria infiltration and masticatory forces. Biomaterials-based tissue engineering (TE) strategies arise as alternatives to the current reconstructive treatments, which include bone grafts with limited efficacy and predictability. Zirconia (ZrO2) has been frequently used in dentistry due to its mechanical strength, biocompatibility and antibacterial properties. In this work, alginate scaffolds, capable of adapting to irregularly shaped defects, were functionalized with calcium-stabilized cubic ZrO2 (c-ZrO2) nanoparticles (NPs). Alginate + c-ZrO2 and alginate scaffolds were characterized in terms of swelling behavior, degradation, compressive Young’s modulus, and biological performance using human periodontal ligament stem/stromal cells (PDLSC). Alginate + c-ZrO2 scaffolds showed controlled swelling behavior and augmented mechanical properties while enhancing PDLSC proliferation and osteogenic differentiation. The incorporation of c-ZrO2 NPs within the alginate matrix led to a more elongated PDLSC morphology, increased phalloidin (≈ 2-fold) and bone extracellular matrix proteins expression, and significantly upregulated periostin gene expression (≈ 7-fold). Overall, this work reports the first development of an alginate porous scaffold incorporating calcium-stabilized c-ZrO2 NPs, which significantly enhanced both mechanical properties and biological performance, highlighting the scaffold’s potential for innovative periodontal TE strategies aimed at alveolar bone regeneration.

title: Star-shaped phononic crystals with wide elastic wave band gaps: Design, numerical analysis, and experimental validation
abstract: Phononic metamaterials enable elastic wave manipulation beyond the limits of conventional solids; however, the realization of wide band gaps in the audible low-frequency (0–20 kHz) regime remains challenging due to the inherent trade-off between structural compactness and dynamic inertia. In this work, two star-structured metamaterial configurations are proposed, derived from a baseline star topology and manufactured using Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) polymer. Through targeted geometric modifications of the unit cell, substantially widened low-frequency elastic wave band gaps are achieved. The dispersion characteristics are analyzed numerically using the finite element method (FEM) in conjunction with Bloch periodic boundary conditions. A systematic parametric study is performed to quantify the influence of rib length on band gap formation and coverage. Guided by the numerical predictions, selected designs exhibiting the widest band gaps are fabricated using additive manufacturing, and their elastic wave transmission responses are characterized experimentally. The measured transmission spectra show good agreement with the predicted band gap regions, thereby validating the numerical results and the proposed designs. Compared with previously reported phononic metamaterial structures, the present star-structured configurations exhibit enhanced low-frequency wave attenuation, highlighting their potential for vibration isolation and wave filtering applications.

title: A robust indentation framework for accurate Young’s modulus determination and uncertainty quantification in soft materials
abstract: Mechanical characterisation of soft materials is challenging, with significant measurement variability observed across techniques and laboratories. This study introduced a robust indentation methodology to achieve traceable capabilities and high operational reproducibility by standardising the experimental setup and mathematical analysis. The methodology hierarchically integrates four key contributions: (i) custom, precision-controlled indentation apparatus featuring high-resolution force-depth sensing and enhanced sensitivity for initial contact detection; (ii) finite element (FE)-derived finite-size correction factors eliminating half-space boundary assumptions; (iii) traceable uncertainty propagation workflow based on metrological standards; and (iv) multi-platform benchmarking pipeline against ultrasound shear wave elastography (SWE). The Young’s modulus was determined by processing preconditioned load–displacement data through a contact model modified with the geometric correction factors. Combined uncertainty was determined by quantifying statistical and systematic error chains, ensuring direct traceability. The framework is valid across a broad parametric window, including Young’s moduli from 3 to 85 kPa, Poisson’s ratios from 0.4 to 0.5, and indentation depth ratios from 0.05 to 0.3. Comparisons demonstrated that the linear elastic approximation introduces a maximum deviation of 3.4 % (mean absolute error of 1.4 %) relative to a second-order hyperelastic reference model. Identified Young’s moduli showed strong consistency against SWE across all phantoms, yielding an expanded uncertainty of ∼ 5 %.

title: Influence of microstructural metastability on enhancing radiation tolerance in multi‑phase high‑entropy alloys
authors: Mohan Sai Kiran Kumar Yadav Nartu
abstract: Metastable multi‑phase microstructures offer a unique opportunity to manipulate defect evolution under irradiation, providing pathways for enhanced radiation tolerance that are not accessible in equilibrium alloys. Here we show that metastability in an additively manufactured Al 0 . 3 Ti 0 . 2 Co 0 . 7 CrFeNi 1 . 7 high‑entropy alloy can be harnessed to suppress damage. A single 800 °C heat treatment generates a heterogeneous FCC + L1 2 microstructure: recrystallized grains with discontinuous L1 2 nanorods and non‑recrystallized grains containing fine spherical-L1 2 precipitates. Under 4 MeV Ni 2+ irradiation at 500 °C to 100 dpa, the alloy shows no observable voids across the irradiated region. Transmission electron microscopy reveals a depth‑dependent sequence, from near‑surface partial loops, to ultra‑fine (13–19 nm) interstitial loops at the damage peak, to elongated dislocation tangles deeper, consistent with efficient point‑defect recombination. Nanoindentation indicates modest irradiation‑induced hardening, with hardness increasing from 5.983 ± 0.298 GPa to 6.393 ± 0.296 GPa (∼6 %). Atom probe tomography shows that the metastable FCC matrix undergoes compositional modulation into Ni–Al–Ti‑rich and Cr–Fe–Co‑rich nanodomains, whose amplitudes and wavelengths increase under irradiation. These nanodomains potentially impede long‑range vacancy migration and suppress void nucleation. The combined effects of hierarchical precipitation, matrix metastability, and irradiation‑enhanced chemical modulation create a multi‑length‑scale defect‑sink network. Together, these results establish metastability as a tunable design principle for developing radiation‑tolerant high‑entropy alloys.

title: Strain-tunable room-temperature magnetocaloric response in two-dimensional GdB2N2
abstract: Two-dimensional ferromagnets combining a near room-temperature Curie temperature with a sizeable magnetocaloric effect remain rare. We investigate monolayer GdB 2 N 2 , in which a Gd plane is sandwiched between two h-BN sheets, using density functional theory with a Hubbard correction (U = 7 eV) and classical Heisenberg Monte Carlo simulations. Energy mapping on collinear magnetic configurations gives an effective nearest-neighbour exchange that falls by a factor 2.3 between 0 and + 3 % biaxial tensile strain, consistent with an RKKY-like carrier-mediated coupling. The magnetic anisotropy is the small residual of a near cancellation between the dipolar interaction and a spin–orbit contribution of comparable magnitude arising from 5d hybridisation. Strain halves the exchange and lowers the characteristic transition scale from 280 to 140 K, moving the peak of |ΔS m |(T) at 7 T from 300 K, where the unstrained monolayer operates at room temperature, down to 160 K. In return, the peak entropy change rises from 5.07 to 7.89 J kg −1 K −1 and the relative cooling power from 861 to 1026 J kg −1 . Phonon dispersions and ab initio molecular dynamics confirm the stability of both monolayers. Biaxial strain therefore tunes operating temperature and magnetocaloric performance in opposite directions.

title: pH-responsive quercetin-loaded MOF nanoplatform for targeted intervertebral disc delivery to disrupt inflammation-matrix catabolism crosstalk in disc degeneration
abstract: Current clinical treatments fail to reverse intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), hindered by the avascular intervertebral disc barrier and unsatisfactory pharmacokinetics of bioactive compounds. We fabricated a quercetin-loaded ZIF-8 nanodelivery system (MOF@QP) modified with type II collagen-targeting peptide for precise IDD intervention. ZIF-8 features abundant mesopores and ultrahigh specific surface area to efficiently encapsulate quercetin, and degrades in a pH-responsive manner matching the acidic degenerative nucleus pulposus (NP) microenvironment to realize on-demand local drug release. The surface peptide enables specific binding to NP collagen II fibers and improves targeted nanocarrier enrichment. In vitro assays prove MOF@QP increases intracellular quercetin accumulation, suppresses oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory factors, and upregulates the synthesis of collagen II and proteoglycans. In vivo rat models confirm the platform relieves NP dehydration and matrix degradation to ameliorate IDD. This study proposes a novel nanomaterial strategy for IDD disease-modifying therapy and extends the application of ZIF-8 MOFs in degenerative joint disorders.

title: Bismuth-coordinated nanocomplex drives M2 macrophage polarization via mitochondrial reprogramming against invasive aspergillosis
abstract: Invasive aspergillosis has a high mortality rate, and existing antifungal drugs face the dual challenges of drug resistance and immune evasion. In this study, we designed a bismuth-coordinated self-assembled nanocomplex (Bi@CBD-DFO) constructed by fusing a chitin-binding domain, the STING-activating peptide mN18, and the siderophore mimetic deferoxamine, which formed regular spherical particles driven by bismuth ions, possessing triple functions of fungal targeting, iron competition, and STING pathway activation. After being taken up by macrophages, this nanocomplex repaired the Aspergillus fumigatus -damaged mitochondrial network in an OXPHOS-dependent manner, restored electron transport chain complex I/II activity and TCA cycle flux, activated the pentose phosphate pathway, reversed infection-induced M1 polarization, and promoted M2-like phenotype transformation. In vitro experiments showed that Bi@CBD-DFO concentration-dependently protected lung epithelial cells (recovery to 74.2% at 0.4 mg/mL) with no obvious cytotoxicity; transcriptomics and metabolomics confirmed its systemic regulation of mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming at multiple levels. Mouse aerosol administration results indicated that this nanocomplex did not affect major peripheral blood routine parameters but significantly increased monocyte counts, suggesting in vivo immune activation. This study proposes a synergistic therapeutic strategy of “targeting iron metabolism − restoring host mitochondrial function − remodeling antifungal immunity,” providing experimental evidence for immunometabolic intervention in invasive aspergillosis.

title: Exosomes derived from IL4-treated microglia alleviate retinal ganglion cell loss and alleviate retinal damage in diabetic retinal neuropathy
abstract: In the progression of diabetic retinal neuropathy, the loss of the retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) is an important event, which involves multiple pathological changes especially the inflammation. IL4-treated microglia are activated during the repair of CNS injury. We hypothesize that their role in diabetic retinopathy may also be significant.However, their effect and the mechanism behind diabetic retinal neuropathy are unknown. Here, we investigated the protective role of IL4-treated microglia derived exosome (IL4-Exos) in diabetic retinal neuropathy. Firstly, we provided evidence that IL4-treated microglia participated in the process of both human and rodent diabetic retinal neurodegeneration. In the Streptozotocin (STZ) induced diabetes mice model, intravitreal injection of IL4-Exos prevented RGC loss by changing inflammatory factors, thus preserving the ganglion cell complex thickness and visual capabilities. In the in vivo optic nerve crush (ONC) model, IL4-Exos preserved RGC axons and central retinal projections following optic nerve injury. Our exosomal miRNA sequencing indicated that IL4-Exos contained high levels of miR-26a-5p, which may target the PTEN mRNA and activate the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway. These findings indicate that IL4-Exos exert neuroprotective effects and axonal integrity effects of RGCs through the miR-26a-5p/PTEN/PI3K/AKT axis.

title: Edge cracking mechanisms in extruded AZ31 alloy thin-walled components considering friction effects
abstract: High-performance magnesium alloy thin-walled components are highly desirable for the lightweighting of next-generation advanced weaponry and equipment. During the hot forming of these components, interfacial friction induces the evolutionary reconstruction of surface micro-morphology and microstructural gradients, which subsequently triggers surface crack initiation. In this study, the edge cracking behavior of Mg alloy thin-walled components under varying friction conditions and deformation amount is systematically investigated through backward extrusion experiments coupled with finite element method (FEM) simulations. The results indicate that with increasing deformation, the stress state of the components transitions from pure compression to tension or a complex tension–compression state. By combining electron backscatter diffraction, in-grain misorientation axis analysis and two-beam diffraction, the synergistic mechanisms between grain size and dislocation slip during crack propagation are elucidated. Under lubricated conditions, plastic deformation is primarily accommodated by deformation twinning. Conversely, under unlubricated conditions, crack initiation is intimately associated with incompatible grain boundary sliding. At low deformation amount, crack propagation is predominantly twin-induced, whereas multiple slip systems are synergistically activated at higher deformation amount. Ultimately, this work establishes a fundamental framework for understanding the cracking mechanisms in Mg alloy thin-walled components.

title: Corrigendum to “A mussel-inspired wet-adhesion hydrogel with hemostasis and local anti-inflammation for managing the development of acute wounds” [Mater. Design 213 (2022) 110347]
Shock and vibration tests of space lightweighted hollow cube corners manufactured with fused silica direct bonding process
abstract: The interferometer of the Meteosat third generation satellite is composed by two cube corners. The specifications, in terms of optical performances, mechanical and thermal environments are very stringent compared to the actual knowledge. To answer to the mass, optical and mechanical specifications, a lightweighted hollow cube corner is designed. An integration process based on enhanced direct bonding is developed and tested. This process required a fine polishing of the three mirrors of the cube corner before adhesion in order to obtain a very low flatness, roughness and angle precision. The mechanical strength of the enhanced direct bonding process is measured with static and impact tests on elementary direct bonded samples. Then the solution is validated on three mockups submitted to vibrations and shock.

title: Assessment of carburization and hardness profile in steel rods using low-frequency magnetic incremental permeability and advanced numerical modeling
abstract: This study presents a hybrid experimental-numerical approach for the nondestructive evaluation of carburization profiles in steels. The method is based on low-frequency magnetic incremental permeability (LF-MIP) measurements and establishes a quantitative relationship between the electromagnetic signature and the hardness gradient induced by carburization. Finite element simulations are used to compute the LF-MIP response of layered media representative of various carbon and hardness distributions, using experimentally calibrated magnetic and electrical properties. These simulated responses are organized into a reference impedance chart that enables the inverse reconstruction of hardness profiles from LF-MIP measurements. The approach is validated on 18NiCr5-4 steel specimens with distinct case depths, for which the predicted hardness profiles are compared with microhardness measurements. The results show excellent agreement, with an average relative Euclidean distance of approximately 4%, demonstrating the robustness and accuracy of the proposed method.

title: PEG-stabilized albumin nanoparticles co-loaded with MnO2 and paclitaxel reverse hypoxia-driven multidrug resistance in ovarian cancer
abstract: Paclitaxel (PTX) is the primary chemotherapeutic agent used to treat ovarian cancer. Clinically approved nanoparticle albumin-bound PTX (nab-paclitaxel; Aiyue®) offers therapeutic advantages. However, their extensive application is limited by their intricate manufacturing processes. Additionally, its effectiveness is significantly diminished due to hypoxia-induced multidrug resistance (MDR) within the tumor microenvironment (TME). To circumvent these limitations, we rationally designed polyethylene glycol (PEG)-stabilized human serum albumin (HSA) nanoparticles co-encapsulating manganese dioxide (MnO 2 ) and PTX (PTX-HSA@MnO 2 NPs) to enhance therapeutic efficacy against ovarian cancer. In vitro characterization revealed that PTX-HSA@MnO 2 NPs exhibited enhanced colloidal stability compared with Aiyue®, exceptional biocompatibility, a pH-responsive drug release profile under simulated TME conditions, and sustained oxygen-generating capacity. In vivo experiments demonstrated that MnO 2 -mediated oxygen generation effectively mitigated tumor hypoxia, consequently downregulating the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α and P-glycoprotein, two key factors responsible for chemotherapy resistance. Consequently, PTX-HSA@MnO 2 NPs effectively reversed PTX resistance and potentiated the antitumor efficacy against drug-resistant ovarian cancer. These findings provide a viable approach to combat MDR in ovarian cancer, while simultaneously promoting the innovation of safer, more manufacturable albumin-based nanotherapeutics. Moreover, Mn 2+ released from MnO 2 degradation provides this nanoplatform with prospective magnetic resonance imaging –monitoring capacity for potential theranostic applications in future studies.

title: Mg-Fe nanocomposites overcome the strength-corrosion dilemma of Mg-based materials
abstract: The low density and excellent biocompatibility makes magnesium (Mg) a promising candidate for lightweight structures in the mobility sector and for biodegradable implants. Nevertheless, a widespread use is hindered because of Mg's low strength and poor corrosion resistance. Strengthening through alloying often compromises corrosion resistance as the low solubility of most elements leads to precipitation and hence, formation of micro-galvanic couples. Mg-based metal–metal composites face similar issues. Here, we show that Mg-Fe nanocomposites synthesized via severe plastic deformation, dismantle the strength-corrosion trade-off through nanoscale composite architecture design. Micropillar compression and immersion tests in NaCl and phosphate buffered saline confirmed that a reduction of the phase spacings to the nanoscale (<100 nm) enable 1 GPa strength combined with degradation rates similarly low as that of ultra-high purity Mg. Scanning Kelvin probe force microscopy confirms the distribution of sub-micrometer sized anodes and cathodes and points on a resulting more uniform surface potential distribution for the finer Mg-Fe nanocomposite structure, correlating with the low degradation rate obtained. Combining 1 GPa strength with very slow degradation for a Mg-based composite opens new avenues for structural materials and load-bearing biodegradable implants, considering that the composite architecture provides an exceptional lever to further tune properties.

title: The role of degradation rate in microchannel scaffold-mediated spinal cord injury repair
abstract: Axonal regeneration impairment following spinal cord injury (SCI) frequently results in irreversible neurological deficits. Biomimetic microchannel scaffolds—engineered to recapitulate the structural anisotropy and fascicular organization of native white matter—offer critical topographical cues and mechanical support to guide directional axonal regrowth. Nevertheless, the influence of microchannel scaffold degradation kinetics on functional neural repair remains poorly understood. Therefore, the study engineered biomimetic microchannel scaffolds with precisely tunable degradation kinetics by integrating decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) into Pluronic F127 diacrylate (F127DA) and methodically varying the F127DA content (5FE, 10FE, and 15FE). In vitro experiments confirmed that these microchannel scaffolds exhibited distinct differences in mechanical properties, swelling behavior, microstructure, and cell compatibility. Subsequent long-term in vivo evaluation of in situ degradation revealed that the 5FE group was completely degraded after 3 weeks post-implantation, while partial degradation occurred in the 10FE group at 12 weeks, and no significant degradation was observed in the 15FE group at the same time point. Furthermore, animal experiments demonstrated that the 10FE group promoted linear axonal regeneration, myelination, and angiogenesis, while suppressing fibrotic scarring to a certain degree. This study reveals the complex relationship between scaffold degradation rate and SCI repair outcomes, providing critical theoretical insights for optimizing scaffold design.

title: Transition metal dichalcogenides-based flexible transistors: from material and interface engineering to intelligent system integration
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as a promising platform for flexible electronics owing to their atomic-scale thickness, tunable electronic structures, and mechanical flexibility. Compared with conventional silicon-based devices, TMDs offer unique advantages in extreme scaling, and low-power operation, and electromechanical adaptability. This review provides a comprehensive overview of TMD-based flexible transistors, focusing on cross-scale optimization from atomic-level materials engineering to system integration. We first summarize structural modulation strategies, including polymorphic phases, alloying, Janus architectures, defect regulation, and doping engineering, for tailoring electronic properties and device functionalities. Interfacial engineering strategies involving Schottky barrier modulation, dielectric passivation, and contact resistance reduction are further discussed to improve carrier injection and reliability. The role of mechanical strain in regulating transport behavior and enhancing device stability is systematically evaluated. Finally, emerging system-level applications, including wearable sensing nodes, edge-Artificial intelligence of Things (AIoT) platforms, and neuromorphic computing systems, are highlighted, followed by perspectives on scalable manufacturing, reliability assessment, and material–device–system co-optimization toward next-generation intelligent flexible electronics.

title: Tannic acid‑functionalized poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanoparticles with surface‑conjugated zoledronic acid for bone‑targeted therapy
abstract: Effective accumulation of drugs in bone tissue and side effects of high-dose administration are the main clinical issues in treating osteoporosis. Tetrandrine (TET) can relieve bone loss by interfering with osteoclasts, although its effective accumulation is low. Zoledronic acid (ZA) is a clinical front-line drug for osteoporosis, has side effects at high doses but offers bone-targeting capabilities through nanoparticles (NPs). Exploring a nano-drug delivery system that enhances bone-associated accumulation presents a promising therapeutic approach. We successfully developed a system using poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) NPs as a carrier, encapsulated with TET, ZA for active targeting modification, and tannic acid (TA) as a bridge connecting PLGA and ZA. The construction of NPs was confirmed by particle size, zeta potential, transmission electron microscopy and spectral analyses. The system exhibited good stability, high drug-loading capacity, slow drug release, and enhanced bone-associated accumulation. PLGA@TET NPs-TA-ZA facilitated the shift of macrophage-associated marker expression toward an M2-like profile, which was associated with suppression of TNF-α and IL-1β expression and inhibition of p38 MAPK pathway activation. The system inhibited osteoclasts activity and overabsorption, increases BMD and bone strength, thus promoting bone regeneration and achieving osteoporosis treatment effects. The nanocarrier provided an effective strategy for osteoporosis treatment.

Regrowing mycelium acoustic and insulation panels: The biofabrication, performance, and environmental impact
abstract: Low-density mycelium-bound composites (LD-MBCs) have emerged as promising bio-based alternatives to petroleum-based thermal and acoustic insulation foams, such as expanded polystyrene (EPS). Often described as circular materials, their potential to be recycled into new MBC material has not yet been studied. In this paper, circular LD-MBC (88–143 kg/m3) is investigated over three consecutive life cycles, one initial and two recycled, using Trametes versicolor cultivated on rapeseed straw. The influence of recycled MBC (60–100 %), nutrients (bran), and moisture content (40–55 %) was assessed. Compressive strength, flexural strength, acoustic absorption, and thermal conductivity ( λ ) were measured for each life cycle. The thermal performance was found to remain relatively stable across life cycles (±0.002 W/mK), while mechanical performance fluctuated and acoustic absorption often peaked in the second life cycle. A performance-based life cycle assessment (LCA) compared the multi-life cycle production of LD-MBC against partially recycled EPS. The LCA showed a cumulative reduction of 55–62 % in global warming potential (GWP100) when using LD-MBC while identifying trade-offs in ecological categories such as land use and water consumption potential. These findings provide the first evaluation of multi-life cycle mycelium-based insulation materials and establish recycling through regrowing as a viable strategy for reducing material-related environmental impacts in construction.

title: Evolution of herbal phase structures across the entire process: structural regulation from molecular co-assembly to functional realization
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is characterized by multicomponent synergy and network-level regulation. However, its material basis has long been interpreted within a reductionist paradigm centered on single active compounds, which fails to explain the structure-dependent effects and processing-related functional variations commonly observed in complex herbal formulations. This review aims to systematically elucidate the formation and evolutionary trajectories of herbal phase structures across the entire TCM lifecycle, encompassing fresh herbs, processing, decoction, and in vivo transformation, and to clarify their role as a key structural intermediate linking molecular co-assembly to overall therapeutic outcomes. Growing evidence suggests that phase-structured assemblies driven by noncovalent interactions constitute an important mesoscale organizational level bridging molecular cooperation and pharmacological efficacy. These structures can significantly regulate solubility, stability, interfacial behavior, trans -barrier transport, and release kinetics, thereby contributing to overall therapeutic modulation. Compared with exogenous carrier-based systems, endogenous self-assembly and coordination-driven architectures offer a potential “carrier-minimized” strategy for drug delivery; however, their formation mechanisms and dynamic in vivo evolution remain insufficiently understood. Herbal phase structures emerge throughout the TCM lifecycle, from native tissue organization and processing-induced reconstruction to decoction co-assembly and physiological transformation, forming micelles, vesicles, hydrogels, coordination networks, and hybrid nanostructures. Nevertheless, quantitative structure–efficacy relationships and unified dynamic models are still lacking. Addressing these gaps, this review systematically delineates the phase evolution rules across the full TCM lifecycle, elucidates the intrinsic links between phase architecture and pharmacological effects, and discusses key scientific challenges and future directions from a multiscale and process-oriented perspective, with the aim of providing a theoretical foundation and methodological reference for herbal phase engineering and formulation design.

title: Towards plastic property extraction from shallow indentation data
abstract: High-throughput synthesis techniques, such as combinatorial thin film libraries, enable rapid exploration of materials for extreme environments. These libraries often consist of micrometer-scale films, making mechanical property evaluation challenging. While nanoindentation is a scalable technique at this length scale, it typically provides only hardness and modulus. This work, the second in a three-part study, focuses on extracting plasticity parameters from shallow spherical indentation depths using machine learning. Finite element simulations are conducted using true tip geometry and Voce-type plasticity models with parameters drawn from a uniform distribution. A sensitivity analysis reveals that indentation depth is a more robust input than stiffness in the presence of substrate compliance. Load-depth curves are truncated at various depths (100-1800 nm) and encoded using polynomial coefficients, power-law fits, and dimensionality-reduced descriptors. These are input to neural networks, Gaussian processes, deep kernel learning, and genetic algorithms to predict elastic and plastic parameters. The models are validated on simulated and experimental data from copper, molybdenum, and tungsten wires. The method achieves <10% error in yield and ultimate tensile strength beyond 400 nm, <20% error in modulus, and ~40% error in failure strain; demonstrating its potential for thin film plasticity characterization.

title: Electric field-fabricated ultra-sensitive mechanoluminescent composites for self-powered force sensing
abstract: Flexible force sensors for wearable health monitoring and soft robotics increasingly demand high mechanical compliance and low-power operation. This study reports a stretchable, ultra-sensitive, and mechanically powered mechanoluminescent (ML) force-sensing composite fabricated with an electric field generated by a high voltage discharge. The resulting composite, namely ultra-sensitive ML composite (USMLC), possesses a dense, shallowly embedded ML particle sensing layer approximately 300 µm thick. The ultra-sensitivity is compared to conventional homogeneous ML composites of the same ML concentration, where the USMLCs exhibit a nearly 4000% enhancement in the measured ML intensity. In addition, the USMLCs maintain high stretchability ( > 85% ultimate strain) and demonstrate repeatable mechano-optical sensing response over 1000 cycles of loading with a high signal-to-noise ratio. Furthermore, USMLCs are integrated with miniaturized photodiodes for compact optical readout, enabling relative spatiotemporal ML intensity mapping in localized indentation tests and a proof-of-concept transtibial prosthetic socket phantom test. Collectively, electric field-fabricated ML composites provide a scalable route to highly sensitive, self-powered optical force sensors for wearable and robotic tactile sensing.

title: Resource efficient nano noble metals catalysts supported on porous metal alloys for acetalization reactions: Toward sustainable chemical production
abstract: The acetalization of carbonyl compounds with polyols is a key reaction in organic synthesis and sustainable chemical manufacturing particularly for producing bioderived fuel additives and intermediates. In this work, novel heterogeneous catalysts consisting of ruthenium (Ru) or rhenium (Re) nanoparticles (NPs) supported on porous multicomponent metallic alloy granules were developed. The catalytic supports, based on Cu, Fe, Ti, Co, and Mo alloys were fabricated using powder metallurgy including high energy ball milling cold pressing, and sintering. This approach enabled the formation of porous alloys with controlled composition and tailored surface morphology. The proposed strategy integrates materials engineering with catalyst design by combining mechanically robust porous metallic granules with catalytically active noble metal nanoparticles. The multimetallic porous supports, facilitating efficient nanoparticle dispersion and strong metal − support interactions. Such integration promotes synergistic effects that are unattainable in monometallic systems. Catalytic evaluation demonstrated that coupling alloy based supports with Ru and Re nanoparticles enhances both conversion and selectivity in acetalization reactions. The developed materials exhibit significant potential for application in energy efficient and sustainable chemical processes, supporting the advancement of green catalytic technologies.

title: Investigating the influence of oscillation strategies in Ti-6Al-4V arc-based directed energy deposition: layer geometry, power-source signal stability, and robot dynamics
abstract: In arc-based directed energy deposition (DED-Arc) of Ti-6Al-4 V, torch oscillation is commonly applied to tailor bead profiles. Although comparative studies of selected oscillation patterns exist, systematic comparisons of a broader range of strategies under identical nominal deposition conditions remain limited, leaving their specific effects on process stability poorly understood. To address this gap, this study systematically compares five common oscillation strategies—meander, sinusoidal, circular, figure-8, and zigzag—by manufacturing wall structures at identical deposition energy to isolate the influence of path design. Geometric stability, logged power-signal stability, and robot-dynamic loads are evaluated. The results show that the oscillation strategy significantly affects all three response variables and leads to distinct trade-offs. Sinusoidal and meander trajectories provide the highest power-source signal stability and approximately 50% lower robot-dynamic loads, associated with lower accelerations, but cause up to 6.6-fold larger layer-height fluctuations. Circular and figure-8 trajectories show the opposite trend, with improved geometric stability but less favorable power-source signal stability and dynamic behavior. Among the strategies investigated, zigzag oscillation provides the most balanced overall performance. These findings demonstrate that oscillation strategy is a key process variable in DED-Arc of Ti-6Al-4 V and its selection should consider the specific process and part requirements.

title: Semi-interpenetrating, breathable conductive hydrogel grids via low-temperature direct ink writing for high-fidelity physiological signal monitoring
abstract: Non-invasive epidermal electrodes necessitate conformal contact, low impedance, breathability, and customizable geometries, yet integrating these properties into printable hydrogels remains challenging. Here, a semi-interpenetrating conductive hydrogel grid electrode (PLS-Ca) was fabricated by low-temperature direct ink writing using a poly(vinyl alcohol)/sodium alginate matrix, Ca 2+ -mediated ionic crosslinking, and eutectic gallium–indium liquid metal. The cooled printing platform improved shape retention, while the printed grid architecture enhanced water vapor transport, and the incorporation of liquid metal lowered impedance. The PLS-Ca grid exhibited a higher water vapor transmission rate than a non-grid PLS-Ca film, cloth tape, and PVC tape under the tested conditions. It achieved a fracture elongation of approximately 1011%, with a response time of 130 ms and a recovery time of 120 ms. As an epidermal electrode, PLS-Ca recorded representative electrocardiogram (ECG) and electromyogram (EMG) signals, while frontal biopotential recordings were additionally obtained using an EEG acquisition setup. Its electrocardiogram signal-to-noise ratio was higher than that of commercial silver/silver chloride electrodes, and signal acquisition capability was retained after 10 days of storage. This work provides an integrated material–structure strategy for printable, breathable hydrogel electrodes for wearable physiological monitoring.

title: Fe3O4-Containing plasmonic hybrid nanomaterials in photocatalytic environmental remediation of phenolic compounds
abstract: Phenol and its derivatives are highly toxic, poorly biodegradable organic contaminants commonly found in industrial effluents. Photocatalytic degradation has emerged as a promising, eco-friendly, and energy-efficient method for removing phenol and its derivatives from industrial effluents. The use of Fe 3 O 4 -based photocatalysts for phenol degradation has attracted great interest due to their attractive properties: visible-light activity, chemical stability, low cost, magnetic recoverability, and the possibility of catalyst reuse. Several limitations in their practical applications, however, restrict their use, including incomplete understanding of reactive oxygen species (ROS), degradation intermediates, and the relative contributions of photocatalytic and photo-Fenton mechanisms. Most studies are performed in ideal lab conditions, and little attention is paid to long-term stability, iron leaching, ecotoxicity, real wastewater performance, scale-up, and techno-economic feasibility. In this review, these aspects of knowledge gaps are critically analyzed, and the design of Fe 3 O 4 -based hybrid nanocomposites with metal oxides, noble metals, and carbonaceous materials is correlated to their photocatalytic performance. Special attention is given to the synthesis of Fe 3 O 4 nanostructures and the use of carbonaceous substrates to increase photocatalytic efficiency through localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) and improved electron transport. Lastly, the review suggests future research priorities, including standardization of tests, extensive mechanistic and stability investigations, ecotoxicity testing, and pilot-scale validation of Fe 3 O 4 -based photocatalytic systems for the production of scalable, efficient, and environmentally friendly systems for wastewater treatment in industry.

title: Cracking the code: surface cracking, microstructure evolution, and forgeability of high-γ′ cast-and-wrought superalloys
abstract: Hot-die forging of high-γ′ cast-and-wrought Ni-based superalloys is often hindered by surface cracking, which is a key factor limiting their processability. Despite its practical importance, the mechanisms leading to this cracking and to the low ’forgeability’ of high-γ′ alloys remain poorly understood. This work studies the microstructural dynamics behind surface cracking in Udimet 720 by analysing small samples thermomechanically tested under conditions mimicking forging and ’die chilling’. The results indicate that γ′ dissolution and reprecipitation are the primary factors controlling crack formation: at higher initial forging temperatures, secondary γ′ dissolves leading to extensive cracking due to reprecipitation upon cooling of very fine tertiary γ′. Lower initial temperatures preserve larger fractions of secondary γ′ and produce fewer tertiary particles, facilitating dislocation motion and reducing crack severity. Cooling rate exerts a similar effect: higher rates promote fine tertiary γ′, while lower rates favour coarser growth and reduced cracking susceptibility. The study challenges the idea that optimal forging temperatures for these alloys lie close to the γ′ solvus, given the extensive cracking promoted by γ′ reprecipitation and refinement. The findings can be used to define new routes for processing difficult-to-forge superalloys based on their γ′ dynamics, helping to reduce material and energy waste.

title: Interfacial engineering of rubber/steel cord composites through optimization of the RF/HMMM adhesive system: Experimental and molecular dynamics studies
abstract: The interfacial adhesion between rubber and brass-plated steel cord plays a crucial role in the durability and mechanical reliability of tire composites. This study systematically investigated the effects of the RF/HMMM adhesive system, including the ratio and dosage, on the interfacial properties of rubber/steel cord composites through experimental characterization and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Experimental results showed that the optimal RF:HMMM ratio was 1:1.495, with RF resin and HMMM dosages of 2.3 wt% and 3.44 wt%, respectively. Under these conditions, the composite exhibited the higher pull-out force, excellent heat aging resistance, and balanced vulcanization and mechanical properties. Samples loaded with excess HMMM exhibit degraded interfacial properties, which may show a potential correlation with the intensified self-condensation propensity of rigid HMMM. MD simulations further show that an appropriate HMMM adhesive ratio maximizes cohesive energy density while suppressing polymer chain movement and molecular diffusion, consistent with the formation of a dense and uniform crosslinked network. Furthermore, rubber-adhesive-Cu 2 S interface simulations indicate that an appropriate adhesive dosage can provide a balance between interfacial adhesion, structural compactness, and mechanical stability. This study provides experimental and theoretical guidance for designing environmentally friendly, mechanically durable rubber/steel cord composite adhesives for high-performance tires.

title: Atomistic mechanism of Ni strengthening and friction reduction in (AlCoCrFe)1-x(Ni)x HEAs: Dislocation locking and stacking fault synergy
abstract: The properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are governed by composition, yet the atomic-scale role of Ni in tribological behavior remains unclear. Molecular dynamics simulations of (AlCoCrFe) 1–x Ni x show that increasing Ni content (x ≥ 0.1) reduces the friction coefficient while enhancing wear resistance, hardness, and yield strength. This behavior is associated with the preferential formation of Lomer-Cottrell (LC) locks and stacking faults (SFs) that impede dislocation slip. Nanoindentation further reveals increased Hirth and Stair-rod dislocations, while tensile simulations indicate enhanced dislocation pinning. Ni enrichment lowers the stacking-fault energy and promotes the formation of extended stacking-fault ribbons bounded by Shockley partial dislocations in Ni-rich alloys.

title: Thickness-engineered cascaded (FA)2BiCuI6/Cs2SnBr6 perovskite solar cells with ∼ 30% efficiency in Pb-Free photovoltaics
abstract: We propose and numerically investigate a cascaded dual-absorber architecture that combines the formamidinium-stabilized double perovskite (FA) 2 BiCuI 6 and the vacancy-ordered perovskite Cs 2 SnBr 6 to achieve broad, complementary light harvesting while preserving lead-free chemistry. Device structures were modelled in SCAPS-1D under AM1.5G (1000 W·m −2 ) and 300 K, using P3HT as the hole transport layer, TiO 2 as the electron transport layer, and FTO/Ag contacts. The baseline single-absorber device FTO/TiO 2 /(FA) 2 BiCuI 6 /P3HT/Ag reproduces the simulated performance (V OC = 0.95 V, J SC = 11.37 mA·cm −2 , FF = 87.62%, PCE = 9.49%). Inserting Cs 2 SnBr 6 , which acts as both a complementary absorber and a band-alignment interlayer, between TiO 2 and (FA) 2 BiCuI 6 produces a cascaded (FTO/TiO 2 /Cs 2 SnBr 6 /(FA) 2 BiCuI 6 /P3HT/Ag) with markedly improved photon collection and reduced recombination, raising simulated PCE to 25.97% (V OC = 1.05 V, J SC = 28.20 mA·cm −2 , FF = 87.13%). Systematic thickness optimization reveals strong sensitivity of device metrics to absorber geometries: a global optimum is predicted at (FA) 2 BiCuI 6 = 200 nm and Cs 2 SnBr 6 = 2500 nm, where PCE reaches 29.43% alongside V OC = 1.07 V, J SC = 31.12 mA·cm −2, and FF = 87.74%. The optimized device incorporates a 200 nm (FA) 2 BiCuI 6 absorber with a donor density of 1 × 10 13 cm −3 and a 2500 nm Cs 2 SnBr 6 absorber with an acceptor density of 1 × 10 18 cm −3 , while maintaining low interface defect densities at both the TiO 2 /Cs 2 SnBr 6 and Cs 2 SnBr 6 /(FA) 2 BiCuI 6 interfaces. Mechanistically, the performance gain arises from spectral complementarity between the two absorbers, improved internal quantum efficiency, and mitigation of interfacial recombination through energetic and physical buffering by Cs 2 SnBr 6 . These findings establish cascaded, lead-free double-perovskite stacks as a promising route toward high-efficiency, environmentally friendly photovoltaics and provide specific guidance for experimental realization via thickness engineering and interface control.

title: Hydroxyapatite nanoparticle assembly in biodegradable scaffolds modulates osteoregeneration and immunity in a dose-dependent manner during fracture repair
abstract: Synthetic degradable composite scaffolds have emerged as a promising solution for bone defect repair. Particularly, hydroxyapatite (HA) nanoparticles are incorporated into the formulations due to their osteoinductive properties. However, the comprehensive, dose-dependent effects of HA content on scaffold properties, osteogenesis, and inflammatory reactions remain poorly understood. In this work, Hydroxyapatite (HA) nanoparticles are loaded in copolymer of poly (lactic acid) (PLA) and poly (ethylene glycol) (PEG) in a concentration gradient design, and the resulting composites are electrospun into fibrous meshes. Increasing HA content not only leads to a smoother, finer fiber structure with reduced diameter but also lowers the mechanical strength of the electrospun meshes. High HA content enhances osteogenic differentiation by upregulating the expression of osteogenic genes Sp7 , Col1a1, and Ocn in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and osteoblasts. In vivo, high-HA electrospun meshes increase M2 macrophage polarization upon implantation, thereby promoting bone repair and regeneration. Most importantly, HA electrospun meshes dose-dependently improve bone repair in the mouse tibial monocortical defect model. Our results show that 30 % HA electrospun meshes remarkably accelerate new bone formation, increase M2 polarization, and enhance defect healing without additional exogenous agents, indicating their potential as an effective clinical scaffold for bone regeneration.

title: Optimization of acoustic, thermal, and flame retardant properties in hybrid polyurethane foams reinforced with natural fibers and metal hydroxide nanoparticles
abstract: Modern architectural insulation demands a rigorous balance of acoustic, thermal, fire, and structural performance. This study developed hybrid flexible polyurethane foams utilizing alkali-treated flax/rice husk fibers and co-precipitated Al(OH) 3 /Mg(OH) 2 nanoparticles. Using response surface methodology, the predicted optimal baseline (46.5 mm thickness, 8.7 wt% fiber) targeted a 45 kg/m 3 density. The experimentally realized fiber-only foam (47 kg/m 3 ) achieved a sound absorption average (SAA) of 0.764 and thermal conductivity of 0.0315 W/m·K. Integrating 9 wt% endothermic nanoparticles physically densified the matrix to 65 kg/m 3 . This final hybrid maintained excellent acoustic damping (SAA = 0.767) with an effective thermal conductivity of 0.0360 W/m·K. Furthermore, the combined effect of stiff inorganic fillers and overall densification increased compressive stress (at 50 % strain) from 14.4 kPa (neat PU) to 22.3 kPa. While the natural fibers initially increased matrix hydrophilicity (284.4 %), the nanoparticles partially offset this uptake, reducing it to 259.7 %, which appropriately remains above the 236.8 % neat PU baseline. Finally, the multiphase synergistic shield improved the limiting oxygen index to 24.45 % and secured a UL-94 HB rating, demonstrating a scalable pathway for multi-hazard resistant insulation.

title: Corrigendum to “Camphorquinone, a popularly-used photoinitiator, induced ER responses in dental pulp cells: association with MAPK signaling, cytotoxicity, 8-isoprostane and PGE2 production” [Mater. Design 267 (2026) 116322]
