abstract: The authors regret that an inadvertent error was identified in the published version of this article.The corrected version of the error is presented in this corrigendum.This correction does not affect the conclusions of the study.Figure 7A: The radiographic images were inadvertently selected and included during the preparation of the figure.The images in Figure 7A have been corrected and replaced below, with corresponding changes made to the figure legend.

title: Ultrafast intense pulsed light bonding process for multi-die stacked packages
abstract: In this study, we report the first demonstration of the intense pulsed light (IPL) flip-chip bonding process for multi-die stacked package assemblies (2-, 3-, and 4-die configurations). While conventional methods struggle with thermal management in 3D stacks, this work demonstrates that the IPL process inherently produces a top-down temperature and time above liquidus (TAL) gradient, optimized at 50, 70, and 110 pulses for each respective configuration via FEM simulation. The resulting intermetallic compound (IMC) thickness (0.7–2.0 μm) exhibited a precise layer-by-layer gradient consistent with the predicted thermal distribution. The IPL process completed bonding within 0.5–1.1 s, achieving 29–78 % thinner IMC layers and fewer interfacial defects compared to conventional mass reflow. Thermal cycling tests revealed that IPL-bonded packages sustained 1.9–4.7 times more cycles to failure than their reflow counterparts. Notably, the transition from interface failure to solder crack failure in the 2-die package underscores that reduced thermal exposure preserves interfacial integrity. These results demonstrate that the IPL bonding process is a viable high-speed alternative for 3D multi-die packaging, offering improved microstructural control and enhanced thermomechanical reliability compared to mass reflow.

title: Mechanistic insights into supercritical CO2 corrosion via interpretable Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
abstract: Predicting steel corrosion in supercritical CO₂ (ScCO₂) pipelines is important for carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) systems but challenging, because many coupled variables are involved. Machine learning can reach reasonable accuracy, yet most models are black boxes offering little mechanistic insight. This study applies the Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN), whose learnable edge functions can be read directly as curves, to predict corrosion rate and pitting of steels in ScCO₂. Using 386 samples from 32 published studies under a leak-free cross-validation protocol, the regression model reached a mean test R² of 0.81, comparable to tuned tree ensembles and higher than a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron, so the KAN is competitive rather than more accurate; the classifier reached 88.3% accuracy and 0.947 AUC. Because prediction and interpretation share one model, its partial-dependence curves were read directly: chromium showed saturating protection, temperature an Arrhenius-type increase, immersion time a power-law decay, and pressure a non-monotonic trend, all broadly consistent with corrosion chemistry, while the increasing oxygen effect reflects enhanced mass transport under dynamic conditions. Unlike post-hoc SHAP attributions, which shifted with method and background, the KAN curves are smooth and reproducible, making it a practical tool for studying ScCO₂ corrosion mechanisms.

title: Deformation induced α′-martensite transformation during cyclic bending under tension and its effect on springback
abstract: This study investigated the effects of deformation-induced α ′ -martensite transformation on springback behavior and residual stress evolution during cyclic bending under tension (CBT). Two austenitic stainless steels, SS304 (transformation-prone) and SS316L (transformation-stable), were subjected to CBT processing at 10°C and 20°C with varying number of cycles. The experimental results showed opposite springback trends, i.e., SS316L exhibits decreasing springback attributed to progressive stretching-dominated deformation, while SS304 experienced increasing springback driven by transformation-induced strengthening that maintains higher bending energy. X-ray diffraction measurements showed that SS304 developed substantially larger through-thickness stress gradients and higher surface residual stresses compared to SS316L. Cyclic effects in the CBT process reduced transformation kinetics, compared to uniaxial tension at the same strain levels, with temperature effects more pronounced in SS304. Finite element (FE) simulations incorporating stress state-dependent transformation kinetics and composite hardening were validated against experimental force–displacement curves and transformation evolution, then employed for energy decomposition analysis to quantify stretching, bending, and shearing contributions. The findings establish that transformation-controlled deformation mode evolution determines springback behavior, providing a framework for material-specific CBT optimization based on austenite stability

title: Hydrogel-guided benzoylpaeoniflorin delivery rebalances Nrf2/NF-κB signaling for osteoarthritis therapy
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease driven by intertwined chondrocyte apoptosis, inflammatory activation, and extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Disease-modifying pharmacological options remain limited, and intra-articular small-molecule therapy is often constrained by rapid clearance from the joint cavity. Here, we investigated benzoylpaeoniflorin (BPF), a bioactive monoterpenoid glycoside from Paeonia lactiflora, and developed a BPF-loaded injectable HDPB hydrogel for local OA treatment. In IL-1β-stimulated primary chondrocytes, BPF reduced apoptosis-related proteins, inflammatory mediators, and matrix-degrading enzymes while restoring ECM anabolic markers. Mechanistically, BPF promoted Nrf2 activation and suppressed NF-κB signaling, whereas Nrf2 knockdown weakened these chondroprotective effects. In destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM)-induced OA mice, free BPF alleviated cartilage degeneration and inflammatory activation. The HDPB hydrogel displayed a porous architecture, tissue adhesion, shear-thinning injectability, and self-healing behavior, enabling sustained local delivery of BPF. Compared with free BPF, intra-articular HDPB treatment further preserved cartilage structure, reduced iNOS and cleaved caspase-3 expression, and restored collagen II. These findings identify BPF as an Nrf2/NF-κB-modulating chondroprotective agent and support HDPB (HA-HAD-HAP-BPF) hydrogel-mediated delivery as a promising local therapeutic strategy for OA.

title: Data-augmented crystal graph convolutional neural network for uncertainty-aware thermodynamic stability prediction of two-dimensional MXene/MoS2 materials
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) MXenes and molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) are promising functional materials, but density functional theory (DFT) evaluation of thermodynamic stability is computationally expensive. This study develops a crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) framework to predict formation energy ( E f ) and energy above the convex hull ( E hull ) from a limited dataset of 414 Materials Project structures. The limited dataset represents epistemic uncertainty, while controlled atom-wise perturbations represent local structural variability, whereas rigid translation is used as an invariance control. CGCNN hyperparameters were selected using an L 9 (3 4 ) orthogonal array with analysis of means and range analysis. Among the evaluated augmentation strategies, the combined shift case achieved the lowest mean absolute errors of 0.0052 and 0.0058 eV atom −1 for E f and E hull , respectively. Separately, the three repeated baseline models were used to construct validation-calibrated 95% prediction intervals for uncertainty-aware screening of held-out structures, with 97.6% empirical coverage for both targets. The results demonstrate a practical small-data workflow for thermodynamic stability prediction while highlighting reduced reliability in sparsely represented unstable regions.

title: Targeting the interplay between pathological hallmarks via a lipid hybrid nanozyme to activate synergy therapy of Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is locked in a self-amplifying loop of amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) and chronic neuroinflammation that has defied every single-target drug to date. We therefore engineered Asi-PtL, a rabies-virus-glycoprotein (RVG)-decorated lipid-hybrid nanozyme that co-loads the pleiotropic natural small-molecule asiaticoside (Asi) and a platinum (Pt) nanozyme, converting two independent bioactivities into one synchronized therapeutic pulse. After intravenous injection, RVG-decorated lipid directs Asi-PtL across the blood–brain barrier and enriches it 3.68-fold higher in brain parenchyma than its non-targeted counterpart. The resulting pharmacological-catalytic synergy erodes the AD triad in vivo: Aβ plaque load plummets by 83.60% and NFT density by 69.11%, while neuroinflammation is extinguished more effectively than with either Asi or nanozyme alone. Proteomic analyses attribute the anti–inflammatory efficacy to the restoration of microglial mitochondrial fitness, encompassing mitigation of oxidative damage, reprogramming of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, and re–establishment of bioenergetic homeostasis. Asi–PtL represents a multi–target nanomedicine that consolidates diverse therapeutic requirements within a single administrable agent, offering a promising strategy for Alzheimer’s disease intervention.

title: Stress-dependent creep behavior and deformation mechanisms in a Ni3Al single-crystal alloy under 1200℃ ultra-high temperature
abstract: A novel Ni 3 Al-based single crystal superalloy was subjected to creep testing at 1200 °C under applied stresses ranging from 60 to 100 MPa. The stress-related deformation mechanism was elucidated through creep performance testing and examination of microstructure evolution. The creep life decreased from 360.5 h to 22.6 h as the stress increased from 60 to 100 MPa. while the minimum creep rate increased from 5.02 × 10 -9 s - 1 to 2.77 × 10 - 7 s - 1. A single Norton-law fit over the entire stress range yielded an overall apparent stress exponent of n = 7.43.Increasing applied stress accelerated γ′ rafting and topological inversion, while also increasing the spatial heterogeneity of the γ/γ′ interfacial dislocation network, as evidenced by the emergence of bimodal dislocation-spacing distributions at 90 and 100 MPa. Meanwhile, dislocation climb remained a readily activated deformation mode throughout the nominal stress range. At 100 MPa, particularly during tertiary creep, local true-stress amplification and interfacial dislocation accumulation further enhanced dislocation activity within the γ′ phase, thereby increasing the relative contribution of γ′ shearing. In summary, this study reveals stress-dependent deformation behavior and microstructural evolution under varying stress conditions at 1200℃, providing foundational data for the material selection of turbine blades in advanced aeroengines.

title: Tensile behavior and high-temperature oxidation resistance of directed energy deposition-processed rare-earth oxide-reinforced commercially pure Ti
abstract: The effect of adding Sm 2 O 3 , Tm 2 O 3 , and Lu 2 O 3 rare-earth oxides (REOs) to directed energy deposition (DED)-processed commercially pure Ti (CP-Ti) on its mechanical properties and oxidation resistance at 800 °C is studied. Builds are fabricated from CP-Ti with 1 wt% Tm 2 O 3 or Lu 2 O 3 and up to 2wt.%Sm 2 O 3 . Except for Lu 2 O 3 , the REO additions do not significantly refine the α-Ti microstructure. While Lu 2 O 3 and Tm 2 O 3 are distributed homogeneously in the matrix and retain a near-random texture, Sm 2 O 3 segregates to the α-lamellae boundaries and sharpens the (101̅1) crystallographic texture. The yield and tensile strengths of all composites exceed those of CP-Ti, reaching a maximum yield strength of 581 MPa for 2wt.%Sm 2 O 3 , while ductility remains ≥ 28%. Deformation is predominantly governed by dislocation slip with some twinning. All composites exhibit superior oxidation resistance to CP-Ti. The enhanced strength is attributed to dispersion strengthening by retained RE-containing particles and oxygen solid-solution strengthening after partial REO dissociation. The latter remains semi-quantitative because matrix oxygen was not measured. Improved oxidation resistance is associated with REO dispersions impeding oxygen percolation. Overall, the DED-fabricated REO-reinforced Ti composites achieve a better strength–ductility combination than conventionally manufactured counterparts, making them potential candidate materials for applications requiring high strength and oxidation resistance.

title: Enhanced strength‑ductility synergy in Al‑rich AlTiVCr lightweight multi‑principal‑element alloys via simultaneous V and Cr adjustment
abstract: Lightweight multi‑principal‑element alloys (MPEAs) show great potential for aerospace high‑temperature components, yet their practical application is limited by density and poor plasticity. In this work, Al‑rich AlTiVCr lightweight MPEAs with different V and Cr contents were designed, and their performance was optimized by annealing. The optimized Al 4 Ti 3 VCr alloy (4.06 g/cm 3 ) achieves comprehensive strength‑ductility performance and excellent high‑temperature stability, with annealed room‑temperature compressive yield strength of 800.0 MPa and fracture strain of 23.2%, and high‑temperature specific strengths of 186.3 N·m/g at 600 °C and 185.7 N·m/g at 800 °C. Increasing V‑Cr content raises the BCC phase fraction to improve mechanical properties, whereas excessive V‑Cr triggers brittle D0 22 precipitation and degrades plasticity. Annealing transforms incoherent BCC/L1 0 interfaces into coherent ones, which is regarded as the dominant factor for ductility enhancement. Meanwhile, annealing reduces the BCC fraction and generates D0 22 precipitates with detrimental effects on plasticity. This work offers guidance for developing low‑density heat‑resistant lightweight MPEAs.

title: Engineering tunable Elastin-Like Polypeptide/PEGDA composite hydrogels as injectable soft tissue fillers
abstract: Soft tissue augmentation is widely used for cosmetic and reconstructive indications, requiring void filler materials that can be delivered minimally invasively while maintaining structural stability and tissue-like mechanics. Here, we engineered a biocompatible, injectable composite hydrogel based on elastin-like polypeptides (ELPs) and poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) with tunable viscoelasticity, favorable mechanical properties, and high structural integrity for soft tissue reconstruction. Hydrogels were formed via photoinitiated crosslinking through a combination of thiol–ene coupling between cysteine thiols on ELP and acrylate groups of PEGDA, along with acrylate radical polymerization, resulting in rapid in situ gelation and formation of an interconnected polymer network. The ELP component provided elastin-like extensibility, while PEGDA contributed resilient elastic recovery with low energy dissipation under cyclic loading. By modulating the PEGDA/ELP ratio, the composite viscoelastic response could be tuned, enabling mechanical performance that exceeded either polymer network alone and producing elastic moduli comparable to soft tissue. Notably, the ELP/PEGDA (50/50) formulation achieved > 300% elongation, minimal permanent deformation (∼3.5%), and low energy loss (∼15%), comparable to native elastin, supporting its potential as an injectable void filler for soft tissue reconstruction.

title: Biocompatibility and osteogenic capability of an injectable nHA/calcium silicate composite for bone regeneration: In vitro and in vivo studies
abstract: This study investigated the biocompatibility and osteogenic potential of an injectable nano-hydroxyapatite calcium silicate (nHA/CS) composite as a bone-grafting material for maxillofacial bone defects. The 20% nHA formulation showed favorable injectability and cohesiveness. After hydration for 3, 5 and 7 days, its compressive strength increased, and porosity decreased. The degradation rate and solution pH increased over time but remained with biocompatible ranges. n vitro, The material exhibited no significant cytotoxicity to bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMMSCs), and cell proliferation was comparable to controls (ChronOS tricalcium phosphate or regular medium). BMMSCs pretreated with nHA/CS-conditioned medium displayed significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation. In a rat critical-size maxillofacial defect model, nHA/CS implants were compared to a commercial tricalcium phosphate control (ChronOS). Micro-CT and histological analysis at 6 and 12 weeks revealed significantly greater new bone density, enhanced mineralization, and accelerated bone maturation in the nHA/CS group. These results indicated that Injectable nHA/CS composite possesses excellent biocompatibility, favorable osteogenic potential, and significantly enhanced bone regeneration, showing promise as a bone graft substitute and advancing clinical maxillofacial reconstruction.

title: Conventional and emerging polymer nanomaterial systems: a unified review of applications and translational challenges
abstract: Polymer-based nanomaterials have emerged as a versatile class of engineered materials, distinguished from conventional inorganic nanomaterials by inherent biocompatibility, biodegradability, tunable degradation kinetics, and low toxicity. Despite substantial sector-specific literature, no prior review has organized progress across both conventional and emerging polymer nanomaterial systems while tracking two defining translational barriers, the manufacturing scale-up gap and the toxicity and environmental fate gap, through every application domain. This narrative, expert-guided synthesis, drawing on targeted searches of Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (January 2020 − June 2026), surveys four conventional system types (natural polymers, synthetic polymers, nanocomposites, electrospun fibers) and four emerging directions (stimuli-responsive systems, polymer-nanoparticle hybrids, 4D-printable shape-memory composites, green or biodegradable formulations). For each system, processing route is linked explicitly to resulting structure and quantifiable property outcome rather than reporting application results in isolation. Applications spanning biomedical, agricultural, environmental, and energy and electronics sectors are reviewed, with representative studies tabulated per sector. A state-gap-direction research agenda is proposed for each emerging direction, and technical, biological, environmental, regulatory, and economic challenges are critically examined. Translational progress is found to be constrained less by laboratory innovation shortage and more by absent standardized manufacturing protocols, ecotoxicological data, and regulatory harmonization, requiring coordinated cross-disciplinary effort to achieve real-world deployment.

title: Machine learning-driven multi-objective optimisation of shape-memory programming parameters in 4D-printed PLA
abstract: 4D printing extends additive manufacturing by introducing time-dependent functionality through stimuli-responsive feedstocks such as shape-memory polymers (SMPs). In 4D-printed PLA, performance is governed by programming temperature, holding time, and recovery temperature, whose effects are reflected in recovery time, shape fixity ratio, and shape recovery ratio. This study combines a replicated 49-condition Latin-square design, machine-learning surrogate models, NSGA-II multi-objective optimisation, and experimental validation to identify a Pareto-optimal process window. Eight regression models were evaluated using leave-one-condition-out (LOCO) cross-validation with nested hyperparameter selection. The surrogates achieved LOCO R 2 values of 0.973 (RMSE 7.29 s) for recovery time, 0.874 (1.17 percentage points, pp) for the shape fixity ratio, and 0.975 (4.31 pp) for the shape recovery ratio. The shape fixity ratio increased from 90.2% to 98.8% between 50 and 55 °C before plateauing, with no significant additional effect of holding time. NSGA-II identified a knee point at 67.5 °C programming temperature, 2.0 min holding time, and 80.0 °C recovery temperature, predicting a recovery time of 3.14 s, shape fixity ratio of 99.72%, and shape recovery ratio of 91.70%. Across five validation points, maximum absolute deviations were 0.36 s, 0.75 pp, and 3.82 pp for recovery time, shape fixity ratio, and shape recovery ratio

title: Strengthening anisotropy of stress-oriented Guinier–Preston zones in Al-Cu polycrystals: a multiscale investigation
abstract: Precipitation hardening is a key strategy for enhancing the mechanical properties of materials and has been extensively studied through both experimental and simulation methods. The phenomenon of stress-oriented precipitation motivates further exploration of orientation-dependent hardening. While previous studies have primarily classified the {100} plate-shaped precipitates in Al-Cu alloys into two types, 0° and 60°, there has been limited reporting on the anisotropic strengthening behavior within the 60° category. This study employs multiscale mechanical tests to investigate the interactions between dislocations and Guinier-Preston (GP) zones of three variants, namely, (60 + ), (60 − ), and (0), characterized by the interaction energies. Vickers hardness, compression testing, nanoindentation, micropillar compression, TEM observations, and EBSD characterization were combined to evaluate strengthening behavior across multiple length scales. The results reveal significant strengthening anisotropy between the (60 + ) and (60 − ) variants at 300 K. Nanoindentation results further indicate a transitional strengthening regime associated with the evolution of GP(II) precipitate size and spacing, where local pinning effects become important in addition to average interaction-energy effects. The results suggest that internal stress modifies effective dislocation pinning and activation processes, providing a physical origin for variant-dependent strengthening.

title: Morphology-dependent indentation response of pressure-assisted sintered Cu for power electronic packaging
abstract: Sintered copper (Cu) particles are widely used in catalysis, biomedical devices, energy systems and electronic packaging, yet the role of particle morphology in governing their mechanical response remains insufficiently resolved. Here, we investigate porous sintered Cu produced from monomodal spherical, bimodal spherical and flake-shaped particles by combining nanoindentation, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Both spherical and Berkovich indenters were used to interrogate morphology-dependent deformation mechanisms. The bimodal spherical network exhibited the highest elastic modulus, whereas the monomodal spherical network showed the highest indentation yield strength. In contrast, the flake-derived network displayed substantially reduced elastic modulus and strength due to weak through-thickness connectivity. Correlative SEM images and MD simulations reveal morphology-dependent deformation mechanisms: distributed neck plasticity in the monomodal network, hierarchical load sharing between coarse and fine particles in the bimodal network, and anisotropic strain localization along interlamellar interfaces in the flake-derived network. Indenter geometry further modulates the response, with spherical indentation promoting distributed compaction and Berkovich indentation promoting stress concentration at weak interfaces. These findings highlight particle morphology as a critical factor governing the topology-dependent mechanical performance of porous sintered Cu.

title: Effect of the pressure drop rate on the cell formation in a high pressure foaming process
abstract: High-pressure foam injection molding (HP-FIM) with core-back technology is known for its ability to produce a uniform foam morphology with a high cell density that exceeds that of conventional foam injection molding. The advantage of HP-FIM is that it is possible to control the formation and expansion of cells by controlling the pressure drop through the expansion of the cavity volume. This study examines the influence of pressure drop as a fundamental parameter in cavity expansion, leveraging pressure control as a tool for foam morphology optimization. In order to comprehend the behavior of polycarbonate foam formation when saturated with nitrogen, a mini-batch foaming process is used to replicate the pressure history of the injection molding process. Various process configurations are set up to achieve the variation in pressure drop history. As a result, the effect of the pressure drop rate on the expansion is studied in situ, and the resulting density reduction and cell morphology are investigated. Batch foaming results are compared with HP-FIM, showing a good agreement and proving the utility of a purposefully designed, lab-scale experimental campaign to instruct process design in industrially-relevant technologies.

title: Topological evolution of Multi–Vortex spin textures in amorphous magnetic architectures
abstract: Advances in understanding exotic magnetic configurations and their complex behavior are paving the way for future technologies based on magnetic nano- and microstructures. In this study, we investigate the evolution of magnetic flux closure configurations in amorphous magnetic architectures using a combination of experimental techniques and advanced micromagnetic simulations. To realize the architectures, an amorphous paramagnetic Fe 89 Zr 11 film is first created by sputtering. Next, boron ion implantation through a mask locally transforms the paramagnetic matrix into embedded ultra-soft ferromagnetic Fe 80 Zr 10 B 10 disks. With a size of a few micrometers, these disks enable the observation of large-scale flux closure structures by Kerr microscopy. By relating Kerr images and FORC diagrams, we resolve the subtle differences in the nucleation and annihilation fields of the magnetic structures yielding unique signatures for single, double, and multiple vortex configurations. A deeper understanding is provided by a large-scale micromagnetic model, which accurately reproduces the complexity of multi-vortex magnetic textures and enables a comprehensive analysis of their underlying topological properties. Hence, ion-implanted amorphous magnetic architectures can serve as a tunable platform for designing magnetic hardware that leverages topological protection to realize robust, reconfigurable, multi-state magnetic embedded elements for enhanced computational functionality.

title: Directed growth of bacterial nanocellulose in constructal scaffolds
abstract: Bacterial nanocellulose is a strong, highly crystalline and biodegradable biopolymer, but its use has stayed largely confined to flat sheets. Its potential as a three-dimensional design material remains untested. This research investigates how the geometry of a solid scaffold directs where the material forms. Within a material-driven design framework, we combined hands-on exploration with parametrically defined channels, bio-inspired flow architectures and porous gyroid lattices. We followed growth in situ by time-lapse imaging under static batch feeding. Scaffold geometry influenced deposition through capillary transport at the air-liquid interface. Below a critical channel width of about 1 to 1.3 mm, capillary rise lifted and destabilised the interface, producing uneven, vertically inclined pellicles and trapped fluid pockets. Highly permeable architectures suppressed capillary rise, held the interface flat and gave uniform colonisation. Scaffolds of 10% solidity reached a mean cellulose area fraction of 65 ± 3.7%, compared with 7.0 ± 1.6% at 40% solidity. Geometry is therefore an active design parameter that determines where cellulose grows, and it offers a route to programming grown composites through physical boundary conditions rather than through post-growth assembly.

title: Mechanical property–forming defect relationship in flax fiber composite reinforcements: A multivariate analysis
abstract: Understanding the relationship between the mechanical properties of natural fiber fabric reinforcements and their forming-induced defects is key to advancing their emerging adoption in structural and non-structural composite applications. This study investigates wrinkles, folds, and bridging defects in select natural fiber flax reinforcement architectures (2 × 2 twill woven and biaxial non-crimp fabrics), together with a 2 × 2 twill glass fabric used as a synthetic reference. Mechanical characterization (tensile, shear, bending, and friction) and vacuum-assisted forming trials were conducted, and defect severity was quantified through visual inspection via 3D scanning, followed by expert user scoring. These multivariate data, together with forming parameters, were analyzed using t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) to visualize clustering patterns associated with defect severity. Results show that the fabric architecture and the resource type (natural versus synthetic) are the primary parameters influencing the defect intensity. Namely, the fabric alternatives with lower tensile modulus and shear stiffness, and higher bending stiffness and ply–ply friction coefficients are associated with a fewer and reduced defect severity. Manufacturing process parameters, such as the fabric orientation and the number of plies, also subtly influence the forming-induced defects.

title: Organic acids in cementitious systems: Surface and solution phase interactions
abstract: Organic acids, encompassing carboxylic and phosphonic acids, are widely used as cement admixtures, yet the same compound can act very differently from one binder to the next. As the binder landscape diversifies toward lower-carbon construction, that variability increasingly decides whether an admixture works at all. This review examines how such acids interact with Portland cement, alkali-activated materials, calcium sulfoaluminate cements, and magnesia-based systems through surface adsorption, ion complexation, and phase modification. Research has tended to address one binder at a time, leaving a fragmented picture compounded by inconsistent terminology. By comparing these mechanisms across systems, we build a more coherent account of organic acid behavior and identify where the evidence is inconsistent or missing. The central finding is that behavior cannot be generalized: mechanisms established for Portland cement often fail in alternative binders, because each system differs in surface chemistry, pore solution composition, and hydration products. Current knowledge supports empirical optimization for specific applications, but mechanistic understanding remains incomplete; a notable gap is the absence of direct evidence for metal–ligand complexation under the high pH and ionic strength of real pore solutions. The comparison provides candidate admixtures for each binder family and the measurements needed to close these gaps.

title: Effects of high-volume fly ash on the rheological and mechanical properties and crack propagation behavior of aeolian sand cemented backfill
abstract: Using coal fly ash (FA) in aeolian sand cemented backfill diverts industrial waste and reduces Portland cement demand, but high contents may impair fresh-state behavior and early-age structural integrity. This study investigated aeolian sand cemented backfill containing 50–80% fly ash by total binder mass using rheological testing, uniaxial compression, acoustic emission (AE) monitoring, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Yield stress first increased and then decreased with fly ash content, whereas plastic viscosity showed the opposite trend. At 60% fly ash, yield stress peaked at 31.115 Pa and plastic viscosity reached a minimum of 0.299 Pa·s. At 7 d, increasing fly ash from 50% to 80% reduced uniaxial compressive strength from 2.70 to 1.24 MPa and elastic modulus from 0.287 to 0.141 GPa. The stress–strain response shifted from Type IV to Type VI, accompanied by a tensile-to-shear failure transition. The maximum AE ringing count decreased by 55.0%, while crack-initiation and damage stresses decayed exponentially. SEM revealed less abundant calcium silicate hydrate gel and a progressively looser and more porous matrix at higher fly ash contents, consistent with weakened cementation and cracking resistance. These findings quantify trade-offs among solid-waste utilization, slurry rheology, and early-age structural performance, supporting resource-efficient mixture design.

title: High-throughput nanomechanical evaluation of Fe–Ni–Cr ternary alloys relevant to lunar stainless steels
abstract: Stainless steels are attractive candidates for lunar infrastructure due to their robust properties and native availability of iron, nickel, and chromium resources. Here, correlated high-throughput characterization methods are used to study effects of varying Ni and Cr concentrations on microstructural and mechanical properties of Fe–Ni–Cr ternary alloys relevant to lunar applications. A diffusion multiple representing the Fe-rich portion of the Fe–Ni–Cr ternary was synthesized using a novel laser powder-bed fusion based fabrication process, yielding a compositional library spanning 57 – 99 wt% Fe, 0 – 43 wt% Ni, and 0 – 23 wt% Cr. Correlated high-speed nanoindentation mapping, scanning electron microscopy, energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and electron backscatter diffraction were used to establish relationships between compositional, microstructural, and mechanical characteristics for 5,625 constituent alloys, providing insight into the effects of Ni and Cr variation. Simultaneous additions of 5–25 wt% Ni and 5–15 wt% Cr strongly increase hardness, with grain refinement a key contributor. Additionally, micro-pillar compression of select compositions supports mechanical trends identified via nanoindentation. Ultimately, alloys containing 5–10 wt% Ni and 12–16 wt% Cr maximize both hardness and plasticity index, indicating a promising regime for developing high-strength, wear-resistant in situ resource utilization-based stainless steels.

title: Structure-property relationship in material extrusion-fabricated polymeric scaffolds
abstract: Additive manufacturing has emerged as a promising approach for fabricating bone tissue engineering scaffolds. However, achieving desirable mechanical performance while maintaining sufficient porosity, transport capacity, and biological functionality remains a key challenge. In this work, a hybrid machine learning–particle swarm optimization (ML–PSO) framework was developed to establish structure–property relationships in material extrusion (MEX)-fabricated poly(lactic acid) (PLA). Four boosting-based machine learning algorithms were trained using a literature-derived dataset. Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and ensemble learning achieved an R 2 of 0.71 for the complete database and a conditional R 2 of 0.92 following residual-based screening and model retuning. The ML–PSO framework identified optimal processing parameters corresponding to a predicted compressive strength of 57.7 MPa, which was experimentally validated at 52.6 MPa, representing a relative difference of 8.8%. However, the optimized scaffold exhibited a relatively low porosity of approximately 17%, motivating subsequent architectural modification. To address this limitation without altering the optimized processing conditions, bioinspired longitudinal channels were incorporated into the scaffold architecture. A specific channel configuration achieved approximately 30% porosity and retained approximately 93% of the optimized compressive strength, while increasing permeability by approximately 310%. Preliminary in vitro studies further demonstrated endothelial cell attachment and infiltration within the channel-integrated scaffolds

title: The superite phase transition inducing microstructures and segregations during steel solidification
abstract: Based on classical concept, steels solidify through direct phase transition from liquid to solid, which produces final dendrites and microsegregation. The solidification evolution of three steels was investigated through in-situ laser confocal scanning microscope observation and synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction, together with microstructure characterization after solidification. A new superite phase was identified, which featured as a semi-solid containing limited long-range order with the same orientation. The liquid firstly transited to superite dendrites. Some superite phase transited to austenite grains with solute expelling, and the residual enriched superite phase subsequently transited to multi-phase mixtures. A general liquid-superite-solid phase transition process is revealed, which produces multiscale microstructures and segregations. The superite transition renews the formation mechanism on initial dendrite, dendritic segregation and solidification microstructures, which is crucial to control solidification microstructures and segregation.

title: FDTD analysis of positive-index plasma–metamaterials combining overdense plasma and high–permittivity ceramic inclusions
abstract: The efficiency of plasma-based material processing could be enhanced by producing larger plasma volumes with high electron density, n e . In most material plasma-processing technologies, plasmas are sustained by electromagnetic waves, such as microwaves at 2.45 GHz. However, when n e exceeds the critical density n e , c , the plasma permittivity becomes negative and transverse electromagnetic (TEM) waves cannot propagate through the plasma. This work demonstrates that the insertion of high-permittivity ceramic cylinders can balance the negative permittivity of the plasma, restoring electromagnetic wave propagation over larger distances through the plasma. The viability of this plasma metamaterial design was confirmed by finite-difference time-domain simulations of a square lattice of ceramic cylinders with relative permittivity ∊ r = 40 , a spatial period of 10 mm, and an overdense plasma density n e = 4 n e , c . Effective permittivity, permeability, and refractive index of the metamaterial were retrieved from the transmitted and reflected fields, confirming propagation for a positive refractive index. For a radius of the ceramic cylinders of 1.6 mm, the plasma–ceramic composite exhibits true metamaterial behavior at 2.45 GHz. This metamaterial design, which tailors microwave absorption, could enable the generation of larger, more homogeneous, high-density plasmas, opening routes to faster and more efficient plasma-based material processing.

title: Leveraging machine learning to predict oxidation kinetics in interconnect alloys for solid oxide cell applications
abstract: In energy conversion technologies, solid oxide cells (SOCs) play a vital role, operating as both fuel and electrolysis cells. In SOC stacks, metallic interconnects are crucial, as they enable electrical connectivity, oxidant/fuel gas distribution, and structural stability. Oxidation during service is a significant challenge, compromising the long-term durability of interconnect alloys. Machine learning (ML) models are employed to predict the oxidation kinetics of SOC interconnects, addressing the complex interactions between alloy design and operating conditions. A comprehensive dataset is gathered from the literature, incorporating key inputs including alloy chemistry, service temperature, and atmosphere composition. The natural logarithm of the parabolic oxidation rate constant, ln( k p ), is regarded as the prediction target. Seven models are developed and tuned, achieving R 2 values of 0.90–0.95. Experimental oxidation data from SS441 interconnects, oxidized in air at 750–850 °C for up to 1500 h, are used as unseen validation data to confirm the predictive capability of the models. The integration of a data-driven approach with oxidation kinetics analysis provides deeper insight into the interplay between alloy design, service conditions, and oxidation behavior. The results demonstrate ML as a powerful tool for optimizing interconnect materials in SOC applications.

title: Precipitate phase selection and grain boundary morphology in Cu-Ni-Si-Mn alloys: A machine-learning interatomic potential study
abstract: Alloys inevitably contain interphase boundaries, whose energetics govern nucleation processes and precipitate morphology. In Cu-Ni-Si alloys, Mn addition markedly changes grain boundary (GB) precipitation behavior. While GB precipitation of stable Ni 2 Si in Mn-free alloys is associated with degraded mechanical properties, Mn addition instead promotes film-shaped Mn 6 Ni 16 Si 7 (G-phase) precipitation, which is correlated to improved mechanical properties. However, the atomic origin of the contrasting GB phase selection and morphology remains unclear. Here we perform machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) calculations to investigate the effect of interphase-boundary atomic structure on GB precipitates in Cu-Ni-Si alloys with and without Mn. The MLIP calculations reliably reproduce DFT-level energetics for interfacial bonding and microstructural configurations, and further predict that Mn addition favors GB precipitation of Mn 6 Ni 16 Si 7 rather than Ni 2 Si. Experimentally, Mn-free alloys are observed to exhibit irregularly shaped Ni 2 Si precipitates with open-boundary-like Cu/Ni 2 Si interfaces, whereas Mn-added alloys exhibit film-like G-phase at GBs. Large-scale atomistic interface calculations reveal that the coherent interface structure between Cu and Ni 2 Si favors the formation of plate-like strained Ni 2 Si precipitates in the matrix. Upon coarsening and stress release, an out-of-phase coherent-like interface can form at GBs, generating a local repulsive region that gives rise to surface-like open-boundary structures and explains the irregular morphology of GB stable Ni 2 Si precipitates. In contrast, Cu/Mn 6 Ni 16 Si 7 interfaces remain predominantly incoherent with moderate boundary energies and no pronounced repulsive regime, thereby stabilizing continuous interfacial contact and explaining film-shaped GB precipitation.

title: Wide-angle and wideband microwave absorber based on a honeycomb structure integrated with geometrically tapered resistive patterns
abstract: Modern electromagnetic absorbers must maintain low reflection over wide angular and frequency ranges for practical applications. This article presents a novel honeycomb structure integrated with geometrically tapered resistive patterns (HS-GTRP) for wide-angle and wideband microwave absorption. By utilizing geometric variations to establish a continuous impedance gradient, the proposed structure achieves excellent impedance matching and stable absorption performance over a wide range of oblique incidence angles. An effective-medium model is first established to clarify the relationship between the geometry of the resistive patterns and the resulting tapered permittivity profile. Subsequently, a nonuniform transmission-line model based on a differential formulation is developed to calculate the reflectivity under oblique incidence. The calculated results agree well with the simulation results, validating the model and demonstrating wide-angle impedance matching. The proposed composite absorber, featuring stable geometrically tapered resistive patterns realized via screen printing, was fabricated and experimentally validated. The fabricated absorber exhibits reflectivity below -10 dB from 3.57 to 18 GHz for both TE and TM polarizations and maintains this performance up to an incidence angle of 45°. The good agreement among theoretical analysis, full-wave simulations, and measured results confirms the effectiveness of the proposed design strategy.

title: Achieving strength–ductility synergy in ultra-high-strength steels via multi-scale design: Nanoprecipitation, metastable austenite, and heterostructures
abstract: Ultra-high strength steels (UHSS) with ultimate tensile yield strengths exceeding 2 GPa, are essential for lightweight structural applications; however, their widespread deployment is severely constrained by the canonical strength–ductility trade-off. Achieving an exceptional strength-ductility synergy has thus become the primary focus in the development of these materials. This review provides a critical and systematic synthesis of recent microstructural designs engineered to overcome this bottleneck, focusing on three mutually reinforcing design pillars: (i) nanoscale precipitation engineering, which maximizes dislocation resistance via coherent, low-misfit particles while minimizing interfacial damage to retain essential plasticity; (ii) metastable austenite tailoring through chemical partitioning and thermomechanical processing, exploiting transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity (TRIP/TWIP) for sustained strain hardening, enhanced uniform elongation, and delayed necking; and (iii) heterogeneous architecture construction, leveraging hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) strengthening, geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation, back-stress hardening, and strain delocalization to achieve strength–ductility synergy. We critically evaluate advanced processing routes—such as quenching and partitioning (Q&P), deformation and partitioning (D&P), and additive manufacturing—as enabling tools for realizing these microstructural designs. Furthermore, we discuss the inherent synergies and competitions among these strategies. Finally, we outline a forward-looking perspective on multi-objective microstructural design, advanced multi-scale characterization, and data-driven optimization to push the strength–ductility frontier of UHSS.

title: Bioactive PCL/nSi-BMSCs composite scaffold regulates periosteal cell functions for neurovascularized bone regeneration
abstract: Proper innervation and vascularization are not only essential for maintaining bone homeostasis but also play a pivotal role in orchestrating efficient bone regeneration. Here, we investigate the regenerative potential of a polycaprolactone/Nanosilicates (PCL/nSi) scaffold loaded with bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), with a particular emphasis on its modulatory effects on periosteal cells (PCs) during bone repair, especially in neurovascular regeneration. We systematically evaluated the effects of this composite on PCs migration, osteogenesis, neurogenesis, and angiogenesis, and further explored the underlying molecular mechanisms. The composite exhibited excellent biocompatibility and markedly enhanced PCs proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation, primarily through activation of the PI3K-AKT signaling pathway. Beyond its osteogenic effects, the composite promoted angiogenic differentiation of endothelial cells (ECs) and upregulated neurogenic markers in PCs, thereby fostering a coordinated regenerative microenvironment. Collectively, these findings highlight the therapeutic promise of the PCL/nSi-BMSCs composite as a multifunctional and bioactive platform for bone tissue engineering capable of simultaneously supporting osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and neurogenesis.

title: Bioengineered targeted vesicle-gold nanorod hybrids for laser-responsive photothermal chemotherapy and on-demand drug release in metastatic melanoma in vivo
abstract: Problem: The development of multifunctional hybrid materials capable of integrating tumor targeting, controlled photothermal conversion, and stimulus-responsive drug release remains a major challenge for precision cancer therapy. Approach : Here, we report on a bioengineered hybrid material based on tumor-derived exosomes incorporating gold nanorods (AuNRs) functionalized with a thermoresponsive methotrexate (MTX) adduct. The resulting EXOS-AuNR-MTX architecture integrates the tumor-homing capability of exosomal vesicles with the NIR-responsive photothermal properties of AuNRs and thermally triggered drug release. Results : The hybrid nanomaterial retained strong NIR absorption, colloidal stability, and photothermal activity, while 808 nm irradiation generated localized heating and triggered MTX release. In B16F10 cells, laser activation significantly enhanced cytotoxicity. In a metastatic melanoma-bearing mouse model, repeated irradiation produced localized temperatures of 40–45 °C. Ex vivo molecular tracking confirmed delivery of the hybrid system to metastatic lung nodules. Although lung mass and tumor area remained unchanged, histological evaluation revealed increased apoptosis, reduced tumor cell proliferation, and reduced collagen type I deposition in the treated tumor sites. Conclusion : These findings establish a relationship between composition, properties and function, in which the engineered vesicle-gold nanorod architecture couples photothermal conversion with externally triggered drug release and localized therapeutic activity in metastatic melanoma for precision-controlled nanomedicine.

title: Next generation 3–3 interpenetrating piezoelectric phase composites: design principles, process-structure-property relationships, multifunctional performance, and emerging applications
abstract: In recent years, architectured interpenetrating piezoelectric phase composites (IP 2 Cs), a class of multifunctional materials with 3D co-continuous piezoelectric and passive networks have attracted significant interest due to their excellent electromechanical performance, structural integrity, and functional reliability compared to conventional piezocomposites. Despite recent advances in various constituent materials, architecture design, fabrication techniques, and topology optimization, the unified process-structure–property-performance framework for rational design of high-performance IP 2 Cs remains largely elusive. The present review comprehensively consolidates recent progress by critically assessing the marked influence of constituent materials, phase connectivity, interfacial engineering, architectured 3D networks, and advanced manufacturing strategies on electromechanical performance and multifunctional characteristics of IP 2 Cs. The review emphasizes mainly on mechanistic understanding and underlying mechanisms for enhanced 3–3 interpenetrating connectivity, mechanical stress transfer efficiency, electric field distribution, and polarization efficiency followed by various fabrication methods and their influence on performance characteristics. Recent progress in Pb-free piezoelectric systems, MXene-based composites, and stretchable architectures along their fabrication techniques and computation modelling are further discussed, thereby highlighting emerging opportunities and current challenges. The comprehensive inclusion of above aspects positions this materials design framework to provide critical insights and future design guidelines for developing next-generation IP 2 Cs for sensor, actuators, SHM, wearable electronics, and self-powered energy harvesting applications.

title: Orthotropy and aging effects on the nanomechanical properties of Perumytilus purpuratus nacre
abstract: Mollusks developed protective shells early in their evolutionary history, with nacre emerging as a highly optimized hierarchical structure that combines stiff aragonitic tablets with compliant organic interfaces to achieve remarkable toughness. Although its mechanical properties are well studied, the influence of aging on its nanomechanical response remains unclear. This study presents the first nanomechanical characterization of the Chilean bivalve Perumytilus purpuratus , evaluating age-related variations through nanoindentation, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM). Shells were classified into three groups representing different growth stages. Hardness (H) and elastic modulus (E) were measured in three orthogonal directions to assess anisotropy at the tablet scale, while SEM and AFM were used to characterize microstructure and deformation features. Results reveal pronounced orthotropic behavior, with higher modulus in the radial direction and higher hardness in the thickness direction. Age-related variations were direction-dependent and non-monotonic, with no evidence of intrinsic nanoscale degradation. SEM shows an increase in tablet size and aspect ratio with age, while AFM reveals enhanced pile-up in the thickness direction. These findings indicate that aging is governed by microstructural reorganization rather than intrinsic material changes, providing insights for bioinspired material design.

title: Abnormal grain growth mitigation during powder hot isostatic pressing in mechanical alloyed oxide dispersion strengthened alloys
abstract: Oxide dispersion strengthened (ODS) steels are promising structural material candidates for fast fission and fusion reactor in-vessel components owing to their excellent high temperature strength and resistance to several irradiation induced degradation mechanisms. These properties depend on the microstructural features such as grain structure and nano-oxide distributions, which are directly controlled by the powder manufacturing, mechanical alloying and consolidation processes. In fully ferritic ODS steels, where there is no phase transformation possibility, anisotropy during consolidation leading to heterogeneous mechanical properties remain a key concern. This is worsened by abnormal grain growth (AGG) that results in very elongated and heterogeneous shaped grains. Here, the effect of hot isostatic pressing (HIP) temperature on microstructural evolution was investigated. We reveal that high temperature HIP cycles can have a profound impact on ODS microstructures such as promoting nano-oxide coarsening and causing AGG. Using PM2000 (Fe-20Cr-5.5Al-0.3Y 2 O 3 ) as an exemplar we reveal that a dual-dwell HIP cycle, incorporating an initial low temperature hold can effectively relieve internal stresses, which minimises AGG and improves tensile ductility as compared to a similar single dwell HIP cycle

title: Synergistic effects of nano-TiO2 and KH550 modified glass fibers on fly-ash mortar properties: mechanical performance, durability, and microstructure
abstract: Glass fibers (GF) can reinforce cementitious materials, but GF-reinforced fly-ash mortar may suffer from weak interfacial bonding, poor fiber dispersion, and KH550 agglomeration. In this study, nano-TiO 2 and KH550 were used to prepare jointly modified GF (NKGF). Characterization identified anatase TiO 2 and a rougher fiber surface, together with spectral changes consistent with the possible formation of Ti–O–Si linkages. At an NKGF dosage of 2 wt%, the 28-day flexural and post-flexural compressive strengths increased by 50.1% and 18.1%, respectively, and the flexural-to-post-flexural compressive strength ratio reached 0.25. The mortar reached impermeability grade P11 and showed a mass loss of 0.09% and a strength loss of 4.20% after 25 freeze–thaw cycles. Replicated two-way ANOVA of the 28-day mechanical properties identified significant main effects of modification method and fiber content (p < 0.01). Overall, NKGF was associated with a more compact fiber–matrix interface and improved mechanical and durability performance. These findings provide a performance-based reference for developing high-performance mortar in which fly ash accounts for 20 wt% of the total binder mass.

title: Phase and morphology engineering toward promoting microwave absorption and magnetic hyperthermia of Sr–Fe–O-based nanostructures
abstract: To prepare scalable and practical materials with outstanding and reliable microwave absorbing and hyperthermia properties, a facile experimental scenario and repeatable results, the experimental procedures should be simplified and shortened. Accordingly, a one-pot method was architected, operating based on phase and morphology modification to improve microwave absorbing and hyperthermia performance. Hence, the substrates, capping agents, solvents, additives, and experimental scenarios were engineered to modify the phase and morphology. Urea, citric acid (CA), carbon microspheres (CMSs), ethylene glycol, glucose (Glu), and carbon nitride (CN) were applied as auxiliary agents, and complementary solvothermal sol–gel methods were designed to gain the best results. Intriguingly, a sustainable structure of Fe 3 O 4 , protected with Sr, was synthesized by modification of additives and experimental routes. Particularly, a green, environmentally friendly, sustainable, and capable absorbing matrix was prepared by esterification of extracted cellulose and citric acid. The fascinating maximum reflection loss (RL max ) and radar cross section (RCS) reduction were achieved. Phase and morphology engineering enhanced the magnetic and hyperthermia performance, yielding a specific absorption ratio (SAR) of 27.86 W/g at a concentration of 5 mg/mL. Significantly, the samples demonstrated moderate shielding effectiveness (SE), offering a practical solution to mitigate ambient electromagnetic pollution while remaining compatible with modern technological infrastructure.

title: Molecular dynamics study of liquid-solid cooperative deformation and apparent atomic migration driven by shear in semi-solid AZ91 alloy
abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to investigate the microstructural evolution and mechanical response of semi-solid AZ91 at 830, 850, and 870 K under shear rates of 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01 ps −1 . Temperature and shear rate jointly control the stability of the solid skeleton and the cooperative deformation of the liquid and solid phases. With increasing temperature, structural disorder increases, and atomic motion gradually shifts from short-range rearrangement constrained by the solid structure to long-range motion dominated by liquid flow. By combining the apparent migration coefficient with structure-resolved stress analysis, the relationship between microstructural evolution and load transfer was revealed. Lower shear rates favor the temporal accumulation of atomic motion and structural reconstruction, whereas higher shear rates promote interfacial atomic detachment and grain fragmentation. Structure-resolved stress analysis further shows that the stability of the crystalline skeleton directly affects load partitioning, with stress progressively redistributed toward the disordered region as skeleton degradation increases. These results collectively demonstrate that temperature and shear rate regulate atomic motion and structural evolution, thereby influencing stress redistribution and the evolution of load transfer mechanisms.

title: PhaseAuto: Machine-learning-aided identification of six phases in steel, including single-, double-, and triple-phase grains
abstract: Continuously evolving steel complexity makes grain-by-grain phase-identification critical for correlating microstructure and micromechanics through in-situ experimentation or modeling. Despite recent advances in machine-learning-aided phase-identification, no framework simultaneously (i) uses a ground truth with optimized objectivity, (ii) uses aligned SEM-EBSD data as inputs, (iii) identifies more than 4 steel phases, and (iv) recognizes double-/triple-phase grains. We obtain a reliable ground truth through semi-automated phase-identification of 6 phases using high-resolution aligned SEM-EBSD data of multi-phase steel grades. Critically, we identify both single-phase and double-/triple-phase grains, containing morphological features of multiple phases. The dataset is used to train a U-Net-based CNN within the framework PhaseAuto ( PH ase A nalysis from S EM- E BSD data, A utomated by U -Net T rained on O bjectivity-optimized data). PhaseAuto is the first framework that handles grains of single-/double-/triple-phase constitution, by recognizing them during ground truth generation, isolating them for training, and accurately identifying them during validation. For single-phase grains, PhaseAuto achieves 95.4% area-weighted grain-based-accuracy, surpassing previous works while distinguishing 6 unique phases. We demonstrate PhaseAuto on SEM-DIC bending of multi-phase high-strength steel, revealing micromechanical connections between strain and phase constitution, and showing that double-/triple-phase grains not only share morphological features of two phases, but also exhibit intermediate plastic deformation, all enabled by fast and accurate phase-identification.

title: Flame-retardant type and loading as design parameters governing the structure–property behavior of flexible polyurethane foams
abstract: Flexible polyurethane (PU) foams are widely used in various applications for their low density and favorable acoustic behavior, but their high flammability requires flame-retardant (FR) additives that can also alter their performance. This study compares three FR additives representing distinct physical states and modes of action — tributyl phosphate (TBP, liquid), melamine (MEL, solid, nitrogen-containing), and magnesium hydroxide (solid, inorganic) — incorporated into flexible open-cell PU foams at 1, 4, and 8 wt%. Foaming kinetics, density, compressive strength, sound absorption, and thermal degradation were evaluated before and after dry and wet aging (ASTM D3574 ). TBP acted mainly as a plasticizer, reducing compressive strength and mid-to-high-frequency sound absorption. Mg(OH) 2 improved thermal resistance and sound absorption at higher loadings but showed pronounced mechanical loss after wet aging. Melamine at 4 wt% gave the most balanced combination of mechanical, acoustic, and thermal performance, particularly after wet aging. An equal-domain multi-property screening analysis identified MEL 4 wt% and Mg(OH) 2 8 wt% as the two Pareto-efficient formulations; MEL 4 wt% provided the most balanced equal-weight response, whereas Mg(OH) 2 8 wt% became preferable when thermal performance was assigned greater priority. These findings support a multi-objective, aging-integrated approach to flame-retardant selection in acoustic polyurethane foam design.

title: A hybrid nanomodulator enables metabolic microenvironment remodeling for potent immunotherapy against lung adenocarcinoma
abstract: STING agonist-based immunotherapy holds considerable promise for cancer treatment, yet its efficacy against immunologically “cold” tumors such as lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains markedly limited. A major obstacle lies in the highly glycolytic tumor microenvironment (TME), where Warburg effect-driven metabolic competition deprives immune cells of adequate energetic support and thereby compromises their antitumor activity. Herein, we develop a metabolism regulation-based STING-activating hybrid nano-regulator (Que@ZnPDA) for sensitized immunotherapy against LUAD. Upon intravenous administration, Que@ZnPDA undergoes GSH-responsive disassembly in the TME to release quercetin (Que) and Zn 2+ . Que suppresses glycolysis through downregulating MCT4, whereas Zn 2+ inhibits mitochondrial complex IV activity to restrain oxidative phosphorylation, leading to concurrent disruption of energy-supplying pathways in tumor cells. The resulting energy depletion directly impairs tumor cell survival and relieves metabolic pressure within the TME. Meanwhile, Zn 2+ activates the cGAS-STING pathway, while glycolysis inhibition-induced TREX1 downregulation and mitochondrial damage further elevate cGAS expression, thus strengthening STING signaling and promoting cytokine secretion to reverse the immunosuppressive microenvironment. This metabolism regulation-based hybrid nano-regulator provides a promising strategy for LUAD immunotherapy.

title: Opacifier-colorant pairing in transparent photopolymer resins to optimize printing speed and resolution in masked stereolithography
abstract: Pigmented commercial masked stereolithography (mSLA) resins load strong photoblockers that lengthen the bottom exposure and shorten the lifespan of the consumer liquid crystal display (LCD) panel, whereas clear resins let the 405 nm light penetrate deep into the resin, producing axial over-curing and lateral swelling. This work addresses both limitations with a complementary-strength pairing rule: a strong inorganic opacifier (titanium dioxide) is paired with a weak organic dye (phthalocyanine blue), and a weak opacifier (zinc oxide) with a strong azo dye (diazo pyrazolone orange). The rule is implemented in a commercial transparent acrylate resin, and the cure behavior is described jointly by the Jacobs working curve and a kinetic power law. The extracted descriptors predict the dimensional fidelity of printed calibration parts under elevated exposure on a consumer LCD printer. Compared with a highly pigmented commercial reference, the optimized formulation prints about four times faster (bottom exposure near 50 s), cuts the Z-axis over-curing by 96% relative to the clear base to about 13 µm, holds the lateral swelling to a similar level, and retains a flexural modulus near 1.5 GPa. The pairing rule offers a transferable design principle for high-resolution, mechanically reliable, and printer-safe mSLA printing.

title: Synergistic effect of boron and cerium on precipitation behavior and hot workability of S31254 superaustenitic stainless steel
abstract: Due to the high contents of Cr and Mo in S31254 superaustenitic stainless steel (SASS), it exhibits precipitation sensitivity during hot working. Hot working cracking induced by this issue is a critical factor leading to the high processing difficulty of S31254 SASS. In the present work, hot working performance was evaluated via hot-compression-derived deformation uniformity and crack initiation susceptibility. The results show that the addition of B and Ce elements significantly inhibits the precipitation of the σ phase (σ phase area fraction decreases 68 %), effectively alleviating GB stress concentration and the subsequent aggravation of local precipitation. It also alleviates inadequate stress release induced by the pinning of σ phases at recrystallized GBs. Furthermore, B and Ce elements induce the formation of the Laves phase at recrystallized GBs. Compared with the brittle σ phase, the Laves phase exhibits a certain capacity for dislocation storage and enhances the dislocation transmission capability at GBs, thereby promoting coordinated deformation. This alloying regulation method fundamentally breaks the bottleneck of “precipitation-deformation inhomogeneity-formability deterioration” and ameliorates key microstructural factors governing hot-working performance for high Cr-Mo material systems where the σ phase serves as the primary precipitate during hot working.

title: An injectable self-healing hydrogel with pH-responsiveness for local analgesia and ROS scavenging in wound healing
abstract: Since tissue acidification in wounds is tightly linked to pain and inflammation, pH-responsive hydrogels are promising candidates for local analgesia and ROS scavenging in wound management. Herein, an injectable, self-healing and pH-responsive hydrogel crosslinked by coordination bonds between cerium ions and carboxylate moieties of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) is developed to encapsulate ropivacaine (Rop). The hydrogel features rapid matrix dissolution accompanied by fast release of both Rop and cerium ions under acidic conditions (pH 6.2), while providing sustained Rop release and extremely limited cerium ion release at physiological pH of 7.4. These features contribute to prominent antioxidant activity (ROS clearance rate ≥78%) under acidic conditions, and excellent cytocompatibility (cell viability ≥95%) at pH 7.4. Injecting the hydrogels into mouse plantar incisions resulted in prolonged analgesia (36 h) matching their Rop release feature, alongside excellent biosafety without impairing wound repair. Immunofluorescent assays demonstrate that such analgesic effects are realized by inhibiting the activation of TRPV1 + neurons in the DRG and neurons in the spinal dorsal horn. These findings provide an injectable, self-healing and pH-responsive hydrogel crosslinked by cerium ion coordination for local anesthetic loading and antioxidation in wound healing.

title: Engineered 3D DNA crystals: bridging molecular design to macroscopic precision materials
abstract: The rise of DNA nanotechnology has elevated DNA from its traditional role as a carrier of genetic information into a programmable material. As a unique class of DNA nanomaterials, engineered 3D DNA crystals combine molecular-level structural precision with macroscopic dimensions, thus creating the engineering utility of DNA single crystals beyond mere structural characterization. This review systematically summarizes the primary types of engineered 3D DNA crystals, strategies for optimizing their physical properties, methods for functional modification, and their applications. It provides an in-depth analysis of how different crystalline motif designs contribute to the enhancement of crystal performance and the expansion of functionality. Finally, the major challenges currently facing the field are discussed, and future directions for the development of engineered 3D DNA crystals are proposed.

title: Integrated kinetic–thermodynamic modelling of Fe-Al mineral transformations during high-pressure acid leaching of laterite ores at 265 °C
abstract: High-pressure acid leaching (HPAL) of laterite ores involves simultaneous mineral dissolution and secondary phase precipitation, both of which strongly influence metal extraction, acid consumption and scale formation. Existing models generally describe these phenomena independently, limiting their ability to predict the dynamic evolution of industrial HPAL systems. This work presents an integrated kinetic–thermodynamic–population balance framework that simultaneously models the dissolution of primary minerals (goethite and gibbsite) and the precipitation of secondary phases (hematite and H-alunite) during HPAL at 265 °C. Equilibrium speciation calculations were coupled with shrinking-core dissolution kinetics and population balance modelling to predict elemental concentrations, supersaturation, nucleation and crystal growth under different solid contents (22–30 wt%) and acid-to-ore ratios (0.25–0.45). The model accurately reproduced the experimental concentration profiles of Ni, Co, Mn, Mg, Fe and Al across the investigated operating conditions. The results demonstrate that increasing acid dosage enhances primary mineral dissolution while simultaneously promoting supersaturation and secondary phase precipitation. Hematite exhibited faster crystal growth, whereas H-alunite showed higher nucleation tendencies, highlighting distinct precipitation mechanisms in HPAL. The proposed framework predicts dissolution–precipitation interactions and provides mechanistic insights for optimising industrial HPAL operation by controlling process parameters to minimise precipitation leading to scale formation.

title: A flexible buckling beam based cross-coupled piezoelectric energy harvester for multi-directional vibrations
abstract: The existence of broad spectral content and multi-directionality in complex environmental vibrations poses major challenges for the application of piezoelectric energy harvesters. In this work, we propose a novel cross-coupled piezoelectric energy harvester (CCPEH) that synergistically integrates flexible buckling beams and a multi-directional coupling compliant mechanism. In particular, a spatial cross-coupling structure is developed with compliant mechanism and four symmetrically configured flexible buckling piezoelectric units, which mechanically induces multi-directional vibration modes across a wide resonant frequency range, capable of effectively collecting multi-directional vibration energy. The proposed design is analyzed from the electro-mechanical perspective and comprehensively evaluated by simulations. Furthermore, the flexible electroactive -phase PVDF films with micro-granular silver electrodes were prepared and systematically characterized via XRD, SEM, and EDS to establish the material properties supporting the functionality of the device. Combined with these material features, a prototype of the CCPEH is fabricated and experimentally validated under various vibrational scenarios with different orientations, demonstrating good capability of energy harvesting with a frequency band of 22–28.5 Hz and robust power outputs (up to 6.89 W) across the vibration angles from 0 360 degrees.

title: Surface functionalization regulated deposition of defect engineered black TiO2 on carbon fibers for lightweight broadband microwave absorption
abstract: Developing lightweight microwave absorbers with broadband absorption and attenuation remains challenging for radar stealth and electromagnetic protection. Carbon fibers (CFs) offer low density and a conductive framework, but their excessive conductivity and inert surface often lead to impedance mismatch and poor component integration. Here, we combine CF surface functionalization with liquid phase deposition and subsequent reduction treatment to construct black TiO 2 -coated carbon fibers (CF@TiO 2 -B) with coating morphology, interfacial characteristics, and defect states. Results show that the surface state of CFs primarily determines TiO 2 nucleation and coating continuity, whereas deposition temperature mainly affects early growth. γ-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (KH550) modification markedly increases nucleation sites and strengthens interfacial interactions, resulting in a uniform TiO 2 layer on the CF surface. The reduction treatment converts TiO 2 into defect-rich black TiO 2 containing abundant oxygen vacancies and Ti 3+ species, significantly enhancing electromagnetic attenuation through synergistic defect polarization, interfacial polarization, conductive dissipation, and impedance matching. Under optimized conditions, the CF@TiO 2 -B composite reaches a minimum reflection loss (RL min ) of − 58.53 dB and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth (EAB max ) of 3.76 GHz, together with radar cross-section reduction capability. These results establish a surface functionalization and defect engineering approach to regulate coating growth and electromagnetic dissipation in lightweight carbon fiber-based microwave absorbers.

title: Thickness-dependent microstructural transition and mechanical response in thin-walled LPBF-printed Inconel 718 structures
abstract: Thin-walled features are increasingly used in architected materials produced by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), yet the influence of geometric thickness on microstructure, defect formation, and mechanical behavior remains poorly understood. This study investigates the effect of thickness reduction in LPBF-fabricated Inconel 718 samples using optimized parameters, with a focus on interlayer rotation and contour scanning. Comparison between bulk samples and thin beams of varying thicknesses reveals that decreasing thickness promotes grain refinement. Texture analysis revealed a strengthening of the < 100 > crystallographic orientation along the build direction. Density measurements and microstructural observations showed increased porosity in the thinnest features, with a keyhole-like morphology consistent with localized heat accumulation associated with short scan vectors and constrained thermal conditions. Fine grains were preferentially observed in the contour-scanned regions, whose relative fraction increases as thickness decreases. Tensile tests showed increased variability and reduced ductility in the thinnest specimens, together with a trend toward a higher mean yield strength, to which grain refinement may contribute. The present results demonstrate that the transferability of bulk-optimized L-PBF parameters and bulk-derived mechanical properties to near-limit thin features cannot be assumed without geometry-specific validation.

title: Hierarchy of property gradients in dissimilar transient liquid phase bonds between wrought and additively manufactured alloys
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables the fabrication of complex, multi-material components, but functionally grading remains challenging due to interfacial defect and crack formation. In this study, transient liquid phase (TLP) bonding was used to join wrought Inconel 625 to AM Inconel 625, Nimonic 80A, stainless steel 316 L, and Haynes 25; specimens were fabricated via laser-powder directed energy deposition using a 1070 nm Yb-fiber laser. Bonds were produced at 1150 °C for 3 and 27 h to investigate the role of interfacial diffusion in microstructural evolution and mechanical performance. Characterization revealed alloy-dependent length scales associated with solidification and interdiffusion, which impacted microstructure and properties. While dense joints were found across all systems, Kirkendall porosity formed in the Inconel 625–316 L and Inconel 625-Haynes 25 bonds due to imbalanced diffusion fluxes. Spatially resolved stress–strain responses revealed that tensile strength gradients extend up to 2.7 mm from the joint, more than five times the width of composition and hardness gradients, which are confined within 500 µm of the interface. All bonds achieved >95 % joint efficiency, with 3-hour bonds exceeding 100 %. These results demonstrate the efficacy of TLP for producing high-quality dissimilar joints and the necessity of intermediate-scale test methods for evaluating graded material systems.

title: Unidirectional Cu filling of TGVs using highly-concentrated Cu-MSA electrolytes
abstract: Glass substrates have recently attracted considerable attention as next-generation semiconductor packaging platforms capable of replacing conventional Si interposers and organic substrates for AI accelerators and other advanced semiconductor packages. However, the commercialization of glass substrates is hindered by their low manufacturing yield and poor process productivity. Through-glass vias (TGVs) provide the essential vertical electrical interconnections in glass substrates and are typically formed by Cu electrodeposition. Among the representative TGV filling strategies, unidirectional filling effectively suppresses void formation but suffers from long filling times due to severe mass transport limitations. In this study, highly concentrated Cu-methanesulfonic acid (Cu-MSA) electrolytes were developed to achieve higher Cu ion concentrations than conventional Cu-H 2 SO 4 electrolytes and thereby accelerate unidirectional TGV filling. The physicochemical and electrochemical properties of the Cu-MSA electrolytes were systematically characterized, and a rapid screening method based on short-time electrode potential monitoring was established to determine the maximum operating current density of each electrolyte. Consequently, highly concentrated Cu-MSA electrolytes enabled defect-free unidirectional TGV filling with a 2.30-fold increase in process productivity compared with the conventional H 2 SO 4 -based electrolyte. These findings provide an effective strategy for improving the productivity of unidirectional TGV metallization.

title: Influence of cryogenic pretreatment and minimum quantity lubrication on grinding characteristics of additively manufactured Ti–64
