abstract: Additively manufactured (AM) Ti-64 alloys possess exceptional mechanical properties, however it becomes extremely challenging to finish it effectively via grinding. The present research successfully improved grindability of AM Ti-64 through a preliminary cryogenic treatment route, resulting in substantial modifications to its microstructure and mechanical properties. Surface grinding experiments were carried out under both dry and minimum quantity lubrication (MQL) conditions, specifically with a lubricant flow rate of 200 mL/h and an air pressure of 4.5 bar, utilising a reciprocating grinding machine equipped with a resin-bonded diamond wheel. The tested process variables included wheel speeds of 40-50 m/s, table speeds of 4 and 8 m/min, and incremental depths of cut up to 6 μm. A thorough comparative analysis evaluated the performance of cryo-treated AM Ti-64 during dry grinding, compared with untreated AM Ti-64 processed under both dry and MQL environments, examining key aspects including microstructural features, microhardness values, grinding force components and ratios, residual stress profiles, surface roughness parameters, and chip morphology. The findings clearly indicate that cryogenic pretreatment improves grindability of AM Ti-64. This work positions cryogenic treatment as a robust and viable pre-processing approach to address the persistent difficulties encountered in machining additively manufactured titanium alloys.

title: Geometry-driven combat helmet padding system enabling deformation-mode switching for blunt and ballistic protection
abstract: Combat helmet padding must attenuate fundamentally different blunt and ballistic impact loading, yet most existing systems are designed primarily for a single regime. This study presents OmniShield, a passive, geometry-driven, pre-curved buckling combat helmet padding designed to exhibit boundary-condition-dependent deformation modes under blunt and ballistic loading conditions. OmniShield was evaluated against commercial foam- and lattice-based padding systems. Helmet-level performance was assessed using a MICH helmet mounted on a Hybrid III 50th percentile head-neck assembly. Ballistic impacts were evaluated using 124-grain-9-mm-FMJ rounds at 1400±50ft/s at front, side, and rear locations, while blunt impacts were assessed using a linear impactor at the same locations and at 10, 14, and 17ft/s. High-speed imaging revealed distinct deformation modes of OmniShield under blunt and ballistic conditions. Under ballistic impacts, OmniShield reduced head peak linear acceleration (PLA) and Head Injury Criterion (HIC) by 20-36% and 46-69%, respectively, relative to foam-based padding, and by up to 21% and 45%, respectively, relative to the lattice padding. Under blunt impacts, OmniShield produced lower or comparable PLA and HIC across velocities and locations. These results demonstrate that geometry-programmed deformation can enable a single helmet padding architecture with effective multi-threat performance beyond conventional material-property-driven designs.

title: Microstructure, tensile, and fracture toughness properties study on a water-quenched as-cast Ti6Al4V-5Cu alloy at different temperatures
abstract: The influence of water quenching treatment on the microstructure, tensile properties, and fracture toughness of the as-cast Ti6Al4V-5Cu alloy at different temperatures was studied. Using scanning electron microscopy, the alloy exhibited different features of microstructure. Results showed that the fracture toughness of the Ti6Al4V-5Cu alloy decreases to 28 MPa·m 1/2 when the heat treatment temperature is increased from 740 to 920 °C. The highest fracture toughness, K Q value of 68.3 MPa·m 1/2 , was achieved on the 740 °C water-quenched alloy. The lowest fracture toughness, K IC value of 28 MPa·m 1/2 , was acquired on a water-quenched alloy at the α/β phase transformation temperature (T β ). With rising heat treatment temperature, the fracture toughness gradually increases and reaches 49.5 MPa·m 1/2 when the temperature is 940 °C. As a result, the fracture toughness of the water-quenched Ti6Al4V-5Cu alloy at different temperatures showed a decrease trend in the (α + β) phase region. The alloy exhibits high yield strength and ultimate tensile strength at 790 °C. After 790 °C, the ultimate tensile strength and yield strength of Ti6Al4V-5Cu are reduced, while the plasticity is greatly enhanced.

title: Synergistic enhancement of wear and corrosion resistance in laser-clad Ni60-Cr coatings via trace graphene-driven microstructural engineering
abstract: The pursuit of advanced surface engineering solutions to enhance both wear and corrosion resistance in medium-carbon steel substrates, such as 40Cr steel commonly utilized in critical mechanical components, poses a significant challenge for extending service life and reliability under harsh operating conditions. This study addresses this challenge by investigating the multifunctional performance enhancement of laser-clad Ni60-Cr coatings through the strategic incorporation of trace graphene (Gr). Composite powders with Gr contents of 0, 0.05, 0.1, and 0.15 wt% were deposited onto 40Cr steel using laser cladding. Systematic analysis has shown that incorporating 0.1 wt% Gr optimizes grain refinement, fosters a continuous carbide-rich eutectic network, and enhances solid solution strengthening through carbon dissolution. The resultant Ni60-Cr-0.1%Gr coating displayed a maximum microhardness of 551.1 HV, a 41% decrease in wear depth, a low steady-state friction coefficient of 0.46, and superior corrosion resistance, as indicated by a noble corrosion potential (−0.9876 V) and minimal corrosion current density (1.34 × 10 − 4 A/cm 2 ). These improvements are ascribed to the synergistic interplay of Hall-Petch strengthening, graphene-facilitated solid lubrication, the development of a stable Cr 2 O 3 -rich passive film, and Gr-induced barrier effects. Excessive Gr content (0.15 wt%) resulted in agglomeration and deterioration of properties. This study illustrates that minute amounts of graphene serve as a potent regulator of microstructure, offering a promising avenue for crafting high-performance coatings with integrated wear and corrosion protection for challenging engineering scenarios.

title: All-optical quantification of elastic, thermal, and optical anisotropy in highly oriented UHMWPE tapes
abstract: Polymer chain-oriented architectures offer a lightweight route to maximize mechanical performance and steer heat flow in one direction, while remaining soft and bendable. Yet their functionality is rarely described beyond a limited set of characteristics, such as tensile modulus or effective thermal conductivity. Here, we establish a tensor-level thermo-mechanical benchmark for solid-state-processed ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) tapes at draw ratios of 7 and 70 using contactless, all-optical techniques. Brillouin light scattering resolves direction-dependent acoustic phonon velocities in the gigahertz regime, which are converted into the full orthorhombic elastic tensor and engineering compliance matrix, yielding orientation-dependent Young’s moduli, shear moduli, and Poisson’s ratios together with the anisotropic refractive index. Complementary thermoreflectance measurements quantify thermal transport and reveal strongly anisotropic in-plane heat conduction with anisotropy ratios of about ten. The combined dataset shows that axial mechanical stiffening is not accompanied by a proportional increase in thermal-conductivity anisotropy in these hierarchical fibrillar tapes, highlighting the role of interdomain coupling and phonon scattering. More broadly, the results position chain-oriented UHMWPE as a rare insulating-material platform combining high, strongly anisotropic mechanical performance with directional heat transport, approaching the functionality otherwise associated with benchmark electrically insulating thermal conductors such as diamond, but in a lightweight, flexible form.

title: Intrinsic crack-tip plasticity dominates fracture resistance in a high-strength titanium alloy
abstract: High-strength titanium alloys are attractive lightweight materials for aerospace applications; however, the mechanisms governing their fracture toughness (K IC ) are still not well understood. Here, we show that the fracture toughness of a high-strength Ti-1500 alloy is dominated by intrinsic crack-tip plasticity, rather than by extrinsic crack-path tortuosity. Through quantitative analysis combined with EBSD and site-specific FIB/TEM characterizations, the effects of heat treatment and microstructure on crack-tip deformation and crack propagation were systematically clarified. The results show that the cooling mode after solution treatment is the most influential heat treatment variable, while the solution temperature also significantly affects the fracture toughness. K IC decomposition further reveals that intrinsic toughening accounts for more than 80% of the total fracture toughness. Superior fracture toughness is associated with a sufficiently developed crack-tip plastic zone, larger plastic work, and more uniform plastic strain, characterized by extensive dislocation activity, activation of non-basal slips in the α phase, and compatible strain accommodation between the α and β phases. In contrast, extrinsic toughening mainly arises from crack deflection, secondary cracking, and crystallography-dependent crack propagation, acting as a secondary modifier of the overall fracture toughness. These findings provide a basis for for designing high-strength titanium alloys with improved fracture resistance.

title: Programmable plasma sprayed Hydroxyapatite surface to Regulate apatite formation and prevent bacterial Physical shielding for bone implants
abstract: Hydroxyapatite (HA) modified implants are widely used due to bioactivity and osteoinductivity. However, apatite reprecipitation also encapsulates bacteria within surface microdeposits, shielding them from therapeutic ions and the host immune system, leading to persistent infection and implant failure. To overcome this problem, we dual ion-engineered gallium and zinc doped HA was deposited on titanium via plasma spraying, followed by heat treatment at various temperatures for 5 h. Heat treatment regulated the ZnO formation on the surface of the coating and governed apatite nucleation via a surface charge mechanism, thereby suppressing the bacteria-shielding apatite layer while concurrently increasing the coating adhesive strength and structural stability. The coating heat-treated at 500 ℃ inhibits 91% bacterial activity via a synergistic mechanism, the Zn 2+ mediated membrane disruption, ZnO-generated ROS, and Ga 3+ perturbation of bacterial iron metabolism. In vitro study verified the decent biocompatibility and osteogenic potential, including MC3T3-E1 cell proliferation, adhesion, and differentiation. In vivo evaluation also revealed excellent antibacterial activity, minimal inflammatory response, and enhanced angiogenesis around the implant. The (Ga,Zn)500 coating addresses a critical vulnerability of HA coated implants, which offers active bacterial protection and also promotes osseointegration and holds significant potential for enhancing implant performance and longitivty specially in infection-prone patients.

title: Attention-driven tab transformer for predicting tensile strength of friction stir welded aluminium alloys
abstract: Friction stir welding (FSW) of aluminium alloys has become an important solid-state joining process in advanced manufacturing; however, accurately predicting normalized tensile strength remains challenging because of the complex nonlinear interactions among welding process parameters. Conventional machine learning (ML) models often exhibit limited capability in learning contextual feature interactions from tabular welding datasets. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Tab Transformer Welding Parameter Attention Layer (TT-WPAL) framework that extends the conventional Tab Transformer by incorporating a dedicated welding parameter attention layer to strengthen contextual feature representation for FSW process data. In addition to the experimentally measured process parameters, namely rotational speed (RPM), welding speed, and tilt angle, three established thermomechanical descriptors, namely rotation–travel speed ratio (RTR), welding pitch (WP), and heat input index (HII), are incorporated to enhance feature representation. The framework was implemented using Python with TensorFlow/Keras and evaluated using a publicly available experimental dataset of aluminium alloy friction stir welds. The proposed model achieved an R 2 score of 0.98 with RMSE of 0.0303 (evaluated on normalized tensile strength after preprocessing) and demonstrated consistent predictive performance through five-fold cross-validation. Compared with conventional Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost, and KNN models evaluated in this study, the proposed framework achieved lower prediction errors and higher predictive accuracy. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an accurate and interpretable approach for predicting normalized tensile strength in friction stir welded aluminium alloy joints within the operating conditions represented by the available dataset.

title: Direct aging of laser powder bed fusion 17-4 PH stainless steel: Nanoscale precipitation and grain boundary segregation
abstract: Direct aging (DA) of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) 17-4 PH stainless steel bypasses solution annealing to achieve single-step precipitation hardening, but its effects on grain boundary (GB) chemistry remain poorly understood. Using atom probe tomography and electron backscatter diffraction, we characterise eight conditions spanning two processing environments (∼0.08 vs. ∼ 0.35 at.% N, differing concurrently in atomisation gas, LPBF platform, and scanning parameters), two laser power levels (∼130 and ∼ 170 W), and two states (as-built and DA at 480 °C, 1 h). As-built, Cu-rich precipitates (CRPs) localise exclusively at GBs, while Cu clustering pervades the matrix. The N-rich condition stabilises 2–5 % retained austenite, promotes extensive GB NbN precipitation, and yields smaller GB CRPs. DA triggers profuse intragranular CRP formation (∼5.5 vol%) in all conditions, with enhanced coarsening in the N-rich material (∼7 vs. ∼ 5 nm). Pronounced GB P segregation after DA is associated with the high-N processing condition, without establishing an isolated effect of N. Localised P segregation is also observed near an as-built lack-of-fusion pore. Although the densest builds reach 469 HV after DA, this GB P enrichment within the classical temper embrittlement regime represents a potential embrittlement risk requiring toughness validation before structural qualification.

title: Strain engineering of Hf2CO2 MXene for enhanced transport and photoresponse in nanodevices
abstract: MXenes have emerged as promising semiconductor materials for applications in nanoelectronics and optoelectronics. In this study, Hf 2 CO 2 MXene was systematically investigated to elucidate its intrinsic material properties, quantum transport behavior, and photoelectric response mechanisms. The Hf 2 CO 2 monolayer was identified as a stable semiconductor with a bandgap of 1.57 eV. Notably, this bandgap was modulated under biaxial tensile strain, increasing to 1.83 eV under 4 % strain and to 1.94 eV under 8 % strain. This material is predicted to retain dynamic, thermal, and mechanical stability throughout strain application. Additionally, strain engineering significantly enhanced device performance: the current density of the p–n junction diode reached 47 mA/mm, while the p–i–n junction field-effect transistor achieved a maximum current density of 1000 mA/mm at a gate voltage of − 4 V under 8 % strain. In terms of the photoresponse, Hf 2 CO 2 exhibited distinct absorption peaks in the green–blue and ultraviolet regions. Under strain modulation, the intrinsic photocurrent density of the phototransistor reached 1.2 mA/mm 2 , highlighting its potential for broadband photodetection and photovoltaic applications.

title: Construction of a macrophage-targeted nanoparticle-integrated bioactive composite scaffold preserving osteogenic capacity for sustained local antitubercular drug delivery
abstract: Osteoarticular tuberculosis, a critical clinical challenge featured by chronic Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, yields unsatisfactory therapeutic outcomes despite prolonged multidrug therapy and surgical interventions. Macrophages serve as key intracellular reservoirs for bacilli, promoting bacterial persistence and hindering bone regeneration. We developed a mannosamine-modified, macrophage-targeted Man-PLGA-PEG nanocarrier encapsulating anti-tuberculosis rifapentine (RPT), and integrated it with hydroxyapatite/β-tricalcium phosphate (HA/β-TCP) scaffold to fabricate a therapeutic composite. The nanomaterial’s physicochemical traits, targeting capacity, in vitro anti-mycobacterial activity and sustained drug release were systematically characterized. In vitro and in vivo experiments were performed to evaluate the composite’s osteogenic performance and biosafety. RPT@Man-PLGA-PEG nanoparticles displayed uniform spherical morphology (108.5 ± 7.6 nm, 13.6 ± 0.9% drug loading) and favorable sustained release. They enhanced macrophage uptake and intracellular antibacterial activity in vitro via PI3K/Akt/mTOR-mediated autophagy. Incorporation into HA/β-TCP scaffolds preserved high porosity and mechanical integrity, promoted rBMSC proliferation, migration and osteogenic differentiation, and supported robust in vivo bone regeneration comparable to the HA/β-TCP scaffold alone, with therapeutic-level local drug retention in bone tissue and no observable systemic toxicity under experimental conditions. Thus, RPT@Man-PLGA-PEG/HA/β-TCP composite retains HA/β-TCP scaffolds’ intrinsic osteogenic capacity while enabling macrophage-targeted antibacterial drug delivery, offering a promising and safe strategy for tuberculous bone defect repair.

title: PLLA-based magnetic composites from L-lactide ring-opening polymerization grafted on core-shell modified Mg,Zn spinel ferrites
abstract: In this work, a series of PLLA-based composites incorporating surface-modified spinel particles (ZMFO@VTMS) were successfully prepared through a direct and controlled polymerization route. The synthetic protocol enabled precise control of the inorganic content up to 37.4 wt% (VTMS40), yielding homogeneous materials with tailored microstructures. Thermal analyses revealed a clear transition in the crystallization behavior of PLLA from an interface-restricted regime at low particle contents (VTMS10-VTMS20) to a nucleation-dominated regime at intermediate composition (VTMS30), where the degree of crystallinity is higher and the rigid amorphous fractions (RAF) its minimum. This optimized microstructure also governed the functional response of the composites. Thermal and dielectric characterizations confirmed that the best thermal stability and lowest dielectric strength occur at the same critical composition (VTMS30), evidencing a strong interdependence between polymer chain dynamics, interfacial polarization and particle dispersion. Magnetic measurements demonstrated a progressive increase in saturation and remanent magnetization with increasing ZMFO@VTMS content, while the coercive field remained nearly constant, reflecting the effective embedding of the spinel phase within the polymer matrix.

title: Multifunctional composite electrospinning fiber membranes promote neurovascular-network regeneration for diabetic wound repair
abstract: The healing of diabetic wounds remains a formidable challenge due to local vascular impairment, peripheral neuropathy, and bacterial infection. With the escalating global prevalence of diabetes, the management of diabetic wound healing has garnered increasing clinical attention; however, existing wound dressings demonstrate limited efficacy in treating diabetic neurovascular lesions. In this context, we developed novel wound dressing for diabetic wounds by integrating electrospinning with vacuum-assisted deposition. Bacterial cellulose (BC) was loaded within the polyacrylonitrile (PAN) electrospinning fibers to construct porous reticular architecture, which significantly enhanced both the mechanical strength and hydrophilicity of the composite fibers. Furthermore, the electrospinning fibers were loaded with berberine, a therapeutic agent that confers antibacterial, antioxidant, and anti-aging properties, while simultaneously promoting collagen deposition and the regeneration of neurovascular networks. In the in vivo experiments, the composite fibers ameliorated the pathological microenvironment of diabetic wounds by promoting the expression of anti‑inflammatory factors and inhibiting the production of pro‑inflammatory factors. Collectively, this study presents a promising strategy for neurovascular regeneration in diabetic wound healing.

title: MXene-based composite hydrogel with synergistic crosslinking networks for multimodal wearable sensors
abstract: Flexible wearable sensors with multimodal sensing capabilities are urgently needed for personalized health monitoring and human–machine interaction. However, integrating high stretchability, excellent conductivity, and multiple stimulus responsiveness into a single hydrogel remains challenging. Herein, we develop a multifunctional MXene-based composite hydrogel PABSM (PVA, acrylic acid, borax, sodium alginate, and MXene) via one-pot free radical polymerization, incorporating poly(vinyl alcohol), acrylic acid, sodium alginate, bacterial cellulose, borax, and MXene nanosheets. The hydrogel features a synergistic crosslinking network comprising dynamic borate ester bonds, covalent crosslinks, hydrogen bonding, and electrostatic interactions. The PABSM hydrogel exhibits outstanding mechanical properties, high conductivity (1.27 S/m), and multimodal sensing capabilities, including strain sensitivity (gauge factor up to 1.96 over 0–1400 % strain) and thermal sensitivity (negative temperature coefficient of − 4.72 %/°C, R 2 = 0.995 ). The sensor demonstrates rapid response/recovery times (170 ms for pressure, 11 s/8.6 s for temperature), excellent cycling stability over 1000 cycles, and reliable monitoring of human motions including finger bending, wrist movement, knee flexion, and vocalization, with good biocompatibility. These properties position the PABSM hydrogel as a promising platform for wearable health monitoring, soft robotics, and human–machine interfaces.

title: A machine learning-mediated composition-microstructure-property multiscale mapping approach for the design of high-strength and high-toughness ductile cast iron
abstract: To overcome the strength–plasticity trade–off and the inefficiency of trial–and–error in ductile cast iron, we develop a machine–learning framework for inverse design from mechanical properties to composition via multiscale mapping. Using 336 experimental datasets with KNN imputation and outlier removal, we construct forward GBRT/RF models linking composition, microstructure, and properties, with SHAP analysis quantifying elemental effects. A two–stage inverse model (GBRT + RF) and Pareto optimization enable property–driven microstructure and composition design. Three designed alloys are experimentally validated. For the three experimentally validated designs, the absolute prediction errors are within 30 MPa for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and 0.5 % for elongation (EL), while the relative prediction errors are within 3 % and 9 %, respectively. Notably, Design 3 achieves UTS of 970 MPa and EL of 5.1 %—over 120 MPa higher than conventional normalized ductile iron while maintaining high ductility—attributed to synergistic strengthening from ultrafine grains (1.15 μm), strong〈111〉texture, and a ternary carbide network (Mo 2 C, Mn 7 C 3 , Fe 3 C). This framework offers an efficient, generalizable pathway for on–demand design of complex alloys.

title: 3D printed bioinspired chiral helical-vortex metastructures for broadband electromagnetic wave absorption
abstract: Conventional structural electromagnetic (EM) wave absorbers rely on inherent material losses and gradient design to optimize absorption performance. However, they inevitably face a fundamental trade-off between broadening the effective absorption bandwidth and achieving lightweight configurations. Inspired by the helical phyllotaxis of plants, a growth mechanism that maximizes light capture efficiency, this work proposes a bioinspired chiral helical-vortex metastructure featuring a graded solid fraction, continuously expanding helical laminae, and intrinsic chirality, which achieves impedance matching and broadband absorption through multiple internal reflections, prolonged EM propagation paths and polarization conversion. By combining a dielectric loss composite with rational structure, this multiscale optimization strategy enables broadband absorption with the reflection loss RL ≤ −10 dB covering 5.2–18 GHz, while exhibiting outstanding angular insensitivity at incidence angles of up to 45° and polarization insensitivity. This work demonstrates the great potential of bioinspired chiral structures for EM absorption, providing a promising design strategy for thin, broadband absorption metastructures with angular insensitivity and polarization insensitivity.

title: Toughness and ultimate strength of amorphous silica identified through a combined microbeam and phase-field approach
abstract: This work presents a new approach to evaluating the toughness, described by the critical energy release rate ($G_c$), and ultimate tensile strength ($\sigma_c$) of amorphous silica (SiO$_2$ glass), combining microbeam tests and phase-field calculations. The latter provides a numerical route to brittle fracture without prescribing explicit fracture surfaces \textit{a priori}, enabling crack initiation and propagation to be tracked. Single-notched microbeams and newly designed bone-shaped microbeams with a notch-free gauge section were fabricated by Focused Ion Beam (FIB) milling nd tested under bending in air, probing the brittle-fracture and strength-controlled regimes, respectively. Both geometries were modeled by Finite Element Analysis (FEA) coupled with a phase-field formulation. We found $G_c = 5.1$~J/m$^2$ (critical stressintensity factor $K_{IC} = 0.61$~MPa$\cdot$m$^{1/2}$), an intrinsic material length scale $\ell_c = 9.1$~nm, and $\sigma_c = 6.8$~GPa, consistent with previously reported brittleproperties of silica glass. Through a parametric study, we show the effect of notch geometry on the fracture response of the microbeams and the impact of dimensional measurement error on the determined toughness. Unlike conventional micromechanical methods that yield only $K_{IC}$, our combined microbeam geometries and phase-field approach simultaneously deliver $G_c$ and $\sigma_c$, bridging brittle-fracture characterization and the strength-controlled regimeinaccessible to toughness-only techniques.

title: Oxide interface-mediated plasticity and irradiation hardening behavior in Ni-free high-Mn ODS austenitic steel
abstract: Structural materials for magnetic confinement fusion reactors must simultaneously withstand neutron irradiation, maintain mechanical integrity across operating temperatures, and remain non-magnetic. Current candidates fail to meet all requirements: ODS ferritic steels are ferromagnetic and may suffer from low-temperature embrittlement, while conventional ODS austenitic steels contain Ni that severely activates under irradiation. Here, interface engineering in Ni-free Fe-30Mn-6Al-1Si ODS austenitic steel is demonstrated to simultaneously achieve room-temperature strength–plasticity (9 ± 1 % uniform elongation at 1267 ± 12 MPa yield strength), high-temperature performance (783 ± 10 MPa at 500 °C), and suppressed irradiation hardening at 0.1–0.2 dpa (one-fifth of non-ODS austenitic steel). A multimodal oxide distribution underpins this performance: fine particles (∼6 nm) provide Orowan strengthening and defect sink capacity, while large incoherent particles (>10 nm, ∼10 % lattice mismatch) generate stress concentrations triggering sequential 9R → stacking fault → deformation twin transformations in the high-SFE (∼64.4mJ/m 2 ) matrix. This interface-mediated mechanism activates deformation twinning independently of bulk composition or grain structure, while achieving defect sink strength comparable to ODS ferritic steels. These results demonstrate that engineering oxide size distribution—rather than oxide density alone—offers a design principle for reconciling defect-sink capacity with plastic deformability in extreme-environment structural materials.

title: In situ investigation of failure mechanisms in TGV interconnect structures under electrical loading
abstract: Abstract With the trend towards high-frequency, high-power-density packaging, through-glass vias (TGV) are considered a promising alternative to TSVs. However, their reliability under high current density, a critical concern for practical application, remains insufficiently studied. This work systematically investigates the failure mechanisms of TGV interconnect structures under electrical loads. In-situ electromigration experiments were conducted on daisy-chain TGV samples at current densities of 2.3×10 5 , 2.8×10 5 , and 3.0×10 5 A/cm 2 , with real-time resistance monitoring and cross-sectional SEM analysis. Distinct failure modes were identified: at the lowest density, failure was dominated by RDL/glass interfacial delamination with negligible resistance change; at the medium density, electromigration became apparent, accelerating void nucleation/growth and causing a linear resistance increase; at the highest density, severe thermo-mechanical coupling led to glass cracking at the TGV-RDL corner and RDL plastic deformation, resulting in an accelerated resistance rise. Complementary electro-thermo-mechanical finite element simulations revealed significant current crowding at the TGV-RDL corners, with local current density exceeding that at the narrowest via cross-section. The combined temperature field and geometric features jointly determined the stress concentration locations. This study clarifies the failure mechanisms of TGV and provides insights for the reliable design of high-current-density glass interposer packages.

title: Impact of processing-induced geometric imperfections on the compressive response of PBF-LB/M-fabricated Zr-based bulk metallic glass lattices
abstract: Bulk metallic glasses (BMGs) combine high strength, high hardness, and large elastic strain limits, but their structural use is limited by critical cooling requirements and poor damage tolerance. Here, Zr-based BMG body-centered cubic (BCC) lattices with relative densities of 1.58–7.26% were fabricated by laser powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M) and investigated by differential scanning calorimetry, quasi-static compression testing, fracture-surface analysis, micro-computed tomography (µCT), and finite-element (FE) modeling. The lattices remained predominantly amorphous, although the amorphous fraction decreased from above 90% for the thinnest struts to approximately 71% for the thickest. Compression testing showed an initial quasi-linear regime followed by either progressive cell-layer collapse or abrupt post-peak failure, depending on strut diameter. Analytical stiffness relations and nominal 1D beam and 3D solid FE models captured qualitative diameter trends but overestimated the as-built response. For one representative lattice, µCT measurements of 64 struts were used to quantify diameter scatter and centerline waviness for a 3D FE model. Diameter correction alone was insufficient, whereas incorporating µCT-derived waviness substantially improved predictions of apparent stiffness and the onset of macroscopic non-linearity. Thus, process-induced geometric imperfections must be considered for reliable prediction and design of PBF-LB/M BMG lattices.

title: Resolving room-temperature microscale fracture and plasticity of iron oxides along the iron ore reduction cascade via nanoindentation and microcantilever bending
abstract: Understanding the fundamental mechanical behaviour of iron oxide phases is essential for controlling attrition and fracture during iron ore reduction, particularly in hydrogen-based direct reduction systems. This study investigates the room temperature plasticity and fracture behaviour of single crystal hematite, magnetite, and Wüstite using nanoindentation and micro-cantilever fracture testing. Hematite exhibited the highest hardness, H and elastic modulus, E (H=18.5±0.5 GPa, E=281±3 GPa), followed by magnetite (H=8.7±0.5 GPa, E=165±3 GPa) and Wüstite (H=7.5±0.4 GPa, E=145±4 GPa), reflecting differences in slip activity along the iron oxide reduction sequence. Furthermore, fracture toughness was measured using notched microcantilevers aligned along low-index and high-index crystallographic planes in all three phases. For the low index-oriented case hematite showed increased fracture toughness owing to crack deviation and faceting while magnetite and Wüstite exhibited single plane cleavage fracture. Distinct changes in the deformation behaviour in terms of plasticity and cracking of the three iron oxides were evident from both methods. Further investigation of a magnetite–gangue interface, particularly relevant to low-concentration ores, revealed significantly reduced fracture toughness compared to the magnetite phase. Overall, these results provide a comprehensive set of mechanical properties of iron oxides for future material models predicting fracture and attrition during hydrogen-based direct reduction.

title: Topology-optimized chiral metamaterials for acoustic-mechanical co-optimization in waterborne mufflers achieving high load-bearing and noise reduction
abstract: This work proposes a compact waterborne muffler that simultaneously achieves low-frequency broadband noise reduction and high load-bearing capacity by embedding topology-optimized chiral metamaterials into a square expansion chamber. A density-based topology optimization framework combined with homogenization is developed to inversely design chiral lattices with low acoustic impedance and enhanced stiffness. Two independent optimization tasks are formulated. The first targets low acoustic impedance under characteristic-parameter constraints to verify the effectiveness of the inverse-design framework. The second retains acoustic impedance minimization as the objective while additionally imposing stiffness requirements through two constraint formulations. Quasi-static compression tests show that the optimized metamaterial achieves a stiffness of 92.83 MPa and a strength of 2.2 MPa. Water-circulating pipeline experiments further demonstrate that the resulting muffler maintains stable acoustic performance under hydrostatic pressures up to 2 MPa, with average transmission loss exceeding 9 dB over both 10–1000 Hz and 10–2000 Hz. Compared with representative existing metamaterials, the proposed chiral lattices achieve a favorable trade-off between low acoustic impedance and high stiffness, providing an effective route to compact, pressure-resistant waterborne mufflers with combined acoustic and mechanical performance.

title: Dopant effects on thermodynamic stability and oxygen vacancy formation in CaMnO3 perovskites for chemical-looping combustion
abstract: The thermodynamic properties and phase stability of doped CaMnO 3-δ perovskites have been investigated over a range of oxygen non-stoichiometry (δ), from 1/16 to 6/16, to assess their suitability as oxygen carriers for chemical-looping combustion. The computational framework combines machine-learning interatomic potentials for structural relaxation, cluster expansions for configurational energetics, phonon calculations for vibrational contributions, and Monte Carlo simulations for configurational entropy. Doping was explored at the A-site (Ce, Sr, La, Bi) and B-site (Ti, Fe, Si, Cr, Cu, Mo, Mg) at substitution levels ranging from 1/16 to 6/16. Phase stability was evaluated using multi-component equilibrium calculations based on thermodynamic data derived from the calculated enthalpy, entropy, and heat capacity. Ce and Sr (A-site), Fe and Ti (B-site), were identified as promising dopants. Ce and Ti enhanced the overall thermodynamic stability of CaMnO 3 , whereas Fe and Sr promoted oxygen vacancy formation, reflecting a trade-off between reducibility and thermodynamic stability. Where experimental data is available, these trends show good agreement with previously reported studies. These results demonstrate that targeted doping enables systematic tuning of thermodynamic behavior in CaMnO 3 -based perovskites, providing guidance for balancing thermodynamic stability and oxygen release in chemical-looping applications.

title: Asymmetric interfacial metallurgical evolution and mechanical-electrical response of ultrasonically welded Ni/Al/Ni multilayers
abstract: Ultrasonic welding of dissimilar multilayer metals is governed by complex structural constraints and non-uniform interfacial deformation, yet the fundamental mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. In this study, we systematically examine asymmetric interfacial evolution in ultrasonically welded Ni/Al/Ni multilayers, focusing on the interplay among localized thermomechanical fields across interfaces, metallurgical bonding, and electrical performance. Our results indicate that interface-specific boundary conditions and thermomechanical histories across the multilayer stack produce distinct thermal and deformation environments at 1/2 and 2/3 interfaces, resulting in non-synchronous bonding and a 23% disparity in T-peel strength. Dynamic recrystallization within the Al interlayer is shown to drive solid-state metallurgical bonding and enable the formation of continuous Al 3 Ni intermetallic layers under sub-melting conditions. Notably, the evolution of macroscopic apparent resistance can be interpreted as a dynamic trade-off between mechanical contact-area consolidation and localized intermetallic layer development: moderate bonding is associated with reduced resistance, whereas excessive IMC growth may increase interfacial resistivity. These findings clarify the impact of interface-specific behavior in multilayer ultrasonic welding and provide critical insights for optimizing high-performance battery interconnects.

title: Damage modelling of porous PBF-LB/M 316L stainless steel using crystal plasticity and cohesive zone method with RVE model
abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a microstructurally informed damage model that explicitly incorporates grains, melt pools, pores, and pre-existing cracks to quantify how defect morphology, porosity level, and orientation govern deformation and failure of products manufactured using laser-based powder bed fusion of metals (PBF‑LB/M). A representative volume element (RVE) framework, inspired by the experimental observations, was constructed using Voronoi tessellation for grain topology and melt pools modelled as overlapping cylinders. Cohesive elements inserted at melt-pool boundaries to represent weak interfaces. Appropriate RVE size identified via convergence analysis. Pore volume distributions were fitted with lognormal and Weibull functions, with Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics indicating superior lognormal fit. Parameterizable pore geometries were generated by an algorithm to create porous RVEs. The crystal plasticity and cohesive zone model parameters were calibrated to experimental stress–strain data, achieving close agreement. Simulations demonstrated that stress concentration and plastification initiate near pores, while damage preferentially nucleates and evolves at melt pool boundaries adjacent to pores, identifying pores and melt-pool boundaries as the most vulnerable zones. Orientation strongly affected properties: horizontally oriented RVEs exhibited higher yield and ultimate tensile strengths but lower elongation than build-direction RVEs. Increasing pores and previously defined cracks markedly reduced ductility and ultimate stress.

title: AI-driven X-ray CT image characterization for accelerating polymer composite design
abstract: Polymer composites offer highly tunable mechanical and thermal properties, but their design is often limited by the slow and labor-intensive characterization of microstructures from X-ray computed tomography (CT) data. An artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework, PocomAI, is presented for rapid polymer composite characterization and generation directly from X-ray CT images. PocomAI integrates multiple deep learning models to perform image segmentation, conditional 3D voxel-grid generation, super-resolution, 3D instance segmentation, voxel-to-mesh reconstruction, and homogenized property prediction within a unified workflow. Trained on a synthetic multimodal dataset of polymer composites containing discrete particulate fillers, the framework enables rapid reconstruction of composite microstructures and prediction of filler-phase volume fraction, Young’s modulus, and thermal conductivity. The generated microstructures show good morphological and property-level consistency with reference structures. Experimental validation using X-ray CT data further demonstrates that fine-tuned PocomAI generates statistically plausible 3D microstructures from limited sliced images, with homogenization-derived effective properties consistent with those of reference reconstructions. PocomAI is further integrated with a large language model to provide a user-friendly interface for stepwise guidance, automatic tool selection, and structured outputs. By reducing post-acquisition characterization time from hours to less than one minute, PocomAI provides an efficient framework for polymer composite design.

title: Strain-engineered functional oxide heterostructures for thermally enhanced resistive switching
abstract: Functional oxide heterostructures offer a versatile platform for next-generation electronics. Here, we report a strain-engineered SmNiO 3 /PMN-PT heterostructure that enables thermally enhanced resistive switching. Epitaxial SmNiO 3 films grown on (001)-oriented PMN-PT ferroelectric substrates via pulsed laser deposition exhibit high crystalline quality and smooth surfaces. Using electrostrain generated from the piezoelectric substrate, we achieve volatile resistance modulation of 5.4% under ± 12 kV/cm at room temperature, and a nonvolatile switching of 3.2% that is consistent with 109° ferroelastic domain switching. Moderate heating (70 °C) boosts the volatile modulation to 9.4% under the same field; at 90 °C, only 4 kV/cm yields a 5.7% change, demonstrating high low-field efficiency. These results suggest a clear strain-property relationship and demonstrate that the heterostructure integrates both volatile dynamic tuning and nonvolatile memory states. This work positions the SmNiO 3 /PMN-PT heterostructure as a promising functional material for further exploration in neuromorphic applications.

title: Shrinkage and viscous behavior during sintering of 3D extrusion printed 316 L stainless steel: Experiments and modeling
abstract: Sinter-based additive manufacturing such as 3D material extrusion (3DMEX) offers the opportunity to elaborate complex metal, ceramic or multi-material parts. However, after printing and debinding, significant shrinkage and distortions occur during the course of sintering, limiting the use of this technology. A model to predict such deformations is proposed based on dilatometric experiments performed to characterize the shrinkage and the viscous behaviors. The complex sintering behavior of 316L SS is influenced by a high residual carbon content which (1) increases the carbide content at GB and (2) postpones the δ-ferrite formation. After a fast initial shrinkage, the dissolution of carbides leads to a sudden transition from poly to monocrystalline character of the particles which slows down the sintering kinetics. A reacceleration is then observed with the formation of δ-ferrite. Based on this sintering scenario, a phenomenological sintering model is built. Viscosity during sintering is measured by cyclic loading dilatometry and fitted with an exponential law to model its evolution with temperature and density. The deflection of a slender part (I-shape sample) is well predicted by the FEM implementation of the developed model.

title: Corrosion and wear resistant yttria-stabilised zirconia (YSZ) coatings on stainless-steel via laser deposition
abstract: Yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) is a promising protective coating for stainless-steel, but its direct deposition has achieved limited success due to difficulties in forming dense coatings with strong interfacial bonding. In this study, laser deposition (LD) is applied to directly deposit YSZ on stainless-steel to address this challenge. A systematic optimisation of LD parameters is first conducted using surface inspection to identify defects, complemented by a data-driven segmentation approach to quantitatively characterise protrusions and depressions, and their spatial distribution. A parameter set (250 W, 900 mm/min) was identified to achieve defect-minimised surface quality. Microstructural characterisation revealed an interface with pronounced metallurgical bonding and substantial interfacial diffusion is achieved. The YSZ coating exhibits a hardness of 15.7 ± 0.5 GPa, approximately six-times that of stainless-steel, and a 4.7-fold improvement in wear resistance, attributing to the intrinsic hardness of YSZ and the strong interfacial bonding. Electrochemical analysis in 3.5 wt% NaCl reveals a ten-fold reduction in corrosion rate, with the corrosion current density decreasing from 0.41 ± 0.15 to 0.036 ± 0.009 µA cm −2 , indicating that the coating acts as an effective physical barrier. The findings confirm the feasibility of direct LD for producing dense, well-adhered YSZ coatings with reliable protective performance against wear and corrosion.

title: Buckling-Induced interlayer misalignment and support design in controlling Thin-Walled structure deformation in powder bed fusion
abstract: Thin-walled structures fabricated by powder bed fusion (PBF) often suffer from deformation defects due to residual stress accumulation during layer-wise deposition. In addition to conventional shrink lines caused by local overheating at structural transitions, abrupt buckling deformation may also induce interlayer misalignment in thin-walled structures. Using thin-walled square tubes as representative specimens, this study investigates the formation mechanism, prediction, and suppression of buckling-induced interlayer misalignment with reproducible patterns. A numerical framework based on the inherent strain method is employed to simulate deformation evolution during the fabrication process and to identify the conditions under which instability-induced misalignment occurs. Experimental validation using Ti6Al4V specimens shows good agreement with the predicted deformation patterns and misalignment locations. Comparative experiments with AlSi10Mg further demonstrate that the equivalent inherent strain level is closely associated with the severity of instability-induced deformation. In addition, the effectiveness of different support configurations is evaluated, showing that longitudinal support ribs significantly improve structural stability and suppress buckling-induced deformation. The findings provide insight into the formation of instability-related defects in PBF thin-walled structures and offer guidance for deformation control and support design in additive manufacturing.

title: Nanocoated probiotics by expressing PET hydrolase to efficiently regulate gut dysbiosis induced by nanoplastics
abstract: Nanoplastics represent emerging environmental contaminants that pose significant threats to human health. Current research on nanoplastics predominantly focuses on their environmental impact and ex situ degradation. A critical paradigm shift is needed toward developing strategies for their in vivo elimination and therapy. Addressing this gap, a living therapeutic agent based on Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) is engineered in this study for charge-enhanced adsorption and remediation of polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (nanoPET) in the gastrointestinal tract. This engineered probiotic, EcNp@PDA-PEI, is designed to express PET hydrolase for direct nanoPET biodegradation and coated by polydopamine-polyethyleneimine (PDA-PEI) for prolonging gut retention. The EcNp@PDA-PEI effectively reduces nanoPET uptake by Caco-2 cells, thereby alleviating cellular inflammation and gut barrier disruption. In a murine model of nanoPET-induced colitis, the EcNp@PDA-PEI robustly restores gut barrier integrity, mitigates inflammation, and recalibrates the dysregulated gut microbiota. This work presents a proof-of-concept demonstration of repurposing a PET-degradation system from environmental remediation toward preliminary biomedical exploration, providing a foundational basis for further investigations into nanoplastics-associated health risks

title: Supramolecular interaction-driven lipoic acid-based hydrogels for hemostasis and wound healing
abstract: Uncontrolled hemorrhage following severe trauma and diabetic infected wounds pose significant challenges to existing tissue adhesives, and the design of dressings for bedside hemorrhage control and prevention of traumatic infections represents an urgent medical need. In this study, a supramolecular adhesive hydrogel, LA/PLO/Ka, was prepared from lipoic acid (LA), poly-L-ornithine (PLO), and kaempferol (Ka) through LA ring-opening polymerization and reversible noncovalent interactions, including electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and hydrophobic association. Molecular dynamics simulations further unveiled the atomic details of the formation of the LA/PLO/Ka hydrogel via multimodal physical interactions. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the LA/PLO/Ka hydrogel possessed self-gelation ability, tissue adhesiveness, hemostatic capacity, favorable biocompatibility, and antibacterial activity. In terms of hemostasis, compared with commercially available hemostatic agents, the LA/PLO/Ka hydrogel exhibited reduced blood loss and shortened hemostasis time. Moreover, LA/PLO/Ka demonstrated superior performance in accelerating wound closure and promoting the healing of diabetic infected wounds. In conclusion, the LA/PLO/Ka hydrogel represents a promising candidate material for medical dressings, particularly for the management of hemorrhage and diabetic infected wounds.

title: A novel grind coating technology for in-situ utilization of metallic swarf waste particles: A multi-substrate proof-of-concept study
abstract: The growing need for sustainable surface engineering has increased interest in economical and environmentally responsible alternatives to conventional coating technologies. Many established deposition processes, including thermal spray techniques, rely on costly metallic powder feedstocks and specialized equipment, increasing both material and processing costs. In this context, Grind Coating is introduced as a simple direct-deposition approach in which swarf generated in situ during grinding is used as the coating feedstock. By avoiding pre-processed powders, this method enables coating formation directly from machining by-products, offering a simpler, less expensive, and potentially more sustainable route for surface modification. To assess substrate compatibility of the method, mild steel swarf was deposited on three different substrate classes: aluminium (metal), acrylic (polymer), and glass (ceramic). Well-adherent coatings were obtained on all substrates, with coating thickness in the range of 0.1 – 10 mm and microhardness values between ∼ 120 − 615HV, with the upper value representing a localized maximum. These results demonstrate the feasibility of producing thick, stable deposits on different substrate types using a waste-derived feedstock. The approach may be relevant for repair and refurbishment of damaged surfaces, as well as broader surface modification applications requiring thick deposits. By converting machining by-products into coatings, Grind Coating supports sustainable surface engineering and circular material use in manufacturing.

title: Design-of-experiments-guided process control of phase evolution and carrier polarity in SnOx thin-film transistors
abstract: Non-stoichiometric tin oxide, SnO x , offers a tunable oxide thin-film platform in which carrier polarity can switch between p-type, ambipolar, and n-type states, but this control requires navigating a narrow, coupled process window. Here, a design-of-experiments is employed to systematically map how oxygen partial pressure ( P O 2 ), annealing temperature ( T A ), and working pressure ( W P ) influence phase evolution and carrier-polarity transitions in sputtered SnO x thin-film transistors. SnO x films were deposited over P O 2 of 9.1–50.0% and W P of 1.9 –10 mTorr, exhibiting litharge-phase SnO at low P O 2 , mixed-phase SnO/SnO 2 at intermediate conditions, and rutile-phase SnO 2 at higher P O 2 . Optimized p-type SnO TFTs achieved a field-effect mobility of 12.6 cm 2 V -1 s −1 with I ON/OFF = 10 6 , while n-type SnO 2 TFTs reached 39.5 cm 2 V -1 s −1 with I ON/OFF = 10 7 . In the mixed-phase regime, ambipolar transport exhibited lower mobilities and weaker switching. Gate-bias stress measurements confirm that phase-pure devices maintain ΔV TH ≤ 0.36 V after 3600 s, whereas the mixed-phase channel is less stable. These findings demonstrate that coordinated control of P O 2 , W P and T A enable tunable phase evolution and carrier polarity from p-type to ambipolar to n-type in SnO x , providing a process-structure–property framework for the rational design of oxide TFTs.

title: Corrigendum to “Quantitative grain structure and texture analysis of hot-pressed ZrB2 via 3D EBSD” [Mater. Design 261 (2026) 115378]
Using AI to diagnose shrinkage in injection-molded products via monitoring PVT properties of amorphous polymers
abstract: Injection molding of amorphous polymers often suffers from shrinkage and warpage due to the complex rheological behavior of plastic melts, making parameter control like temperature and pressure challenging; traditionally, operators rely on trial-and-error based on experience, but this study advocates a systematic approach using sensors in the mold cavity to monitor temperature and pressure, converting data to specific volume via pressure–specific volume–temperature (PVT) relationships as a quality indicator. Employing design of experiments (DOE), the Taguchi method screens significant factors through signal-to-noise ratios, followed by response surface methodology (RSM) with central composite design (CCD) and Box–Behnken design (BBD) for optimization, while an artificial neural network (ANN) predicts quality with hyperparameters tuned by uniform design (UD). Results show the packing stage most impacts volumetric shrinkage; CCD proves more accurate than BBD due to better design point distribution, reducing shrinkage to 1.22%, with CCD's optimal packing time 0.4s shorter. ANN error decreased from 3.29% to 1.52% post-tuning, validating the method. Overall, integrating DOE and ANN effectively predicts and mitigates defects, enhancing process reliability over empirical methods.

title: The improvement of cycle quenching combining deep cryogenic treatment on the microstructures, strength-ductility and wear resistance of 40CrNiMoA steels
abstract: This work examines cyclic quenching (CQ) combining deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) on 40CrNiMoA steel. CQ (930 °C/2 min) refines prior austenite grains, with 2 passes (CQ2) reducing grain size from 9.3 to 4.6 μm. CQ2 improves yield strength (YS), ultimate tensile strength (UTS), and hardness by 71.9 %, 74.5 %, and 66.7 % vs. hot–rolled (HR), lowers wear rate by 25.1 %, but reduces elongation (TE) by 13.0 %. Subsequent DCT for 12–36 h shows peak performance at 24 h (CQ2-DCT24h). Versus CQ2, CQ2-DCT24h increases YS, UTS, TE, and hardness by 10.2 %, 11.0 %, 20.5 %, and 8.5 %, and decreases wear rate by 42.8 %, achieving YS = 1.86 GPa and UTS = 2.21 GPa. This simultaneous strength-ductility-wear improvement stems from higher dislocation density, fine precipitates (reducing lattice distortion), martensite refinement. Ultimately, CQ2-DCT24h outperforms HR with YS, UTS, TE, and hardness gains of 89.2 %, 93.6 %, 7.4 %, and 80.8 %, and a 57.2 % wear reduction. This work demonstrates that the CQ-DCT process effectively synergizes strength-ductility and wear resistance in high-strength steels.

title: Beyond structural recovery: impurity-associated magnetic response and ultra-low thermal expansion in electrodeposited Invar
abstract: Electrodeposited (ED) Invar alloys offer a bottom-up route for sub-10 μm precision manufacturing, but their far-from-equilibrium state results in anomalously high coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE). Here, we investigate why structural recovery alone is insufficient to restore ultra-low thermal expansion in ED Ni 36 Fe 64 Invar films. By comparing Ar and 5% H 2 /Ar annealing within one sample set, we correlate structural, chemical, magnetic, and thermal-expansion responses. Post-deposition annealing promoted phase transformation and grain coarsening in both atmospheres, yielding nearly identical phase fractions and grain sizes at 900 °C. Nevertheless, the CTE decreased from 1.75 ppm·K −1 after Ar annealing to 0.88 ppm·K −1 after H 2 annealing, with a minimum value of 0.68 ppm·K −1 . Temperature-dependent magnetization, residual-stress, and texture analyses showed no large atmosphere-dependent differences. In contrast, H 2 annealing was accompanied by C and S removal, 31% lower mean remanence, and a 16% lower mean low-field dM/dH. Although these magnetic descriptors do not resolve microscopic spin configurations, their concurrent evolution with chemical purification is consistent with changes in the magnetic response associated with the underlying spin environment. These observations support a proposed framework in which impurity-associated perturbations of the spin environment may influence magneto-volume compensation and thereby contribute to the recovery of ultra-low CTE.

title: Hierarchical polydopamine bridged LDH hybrid enables simultaneous fire safety and mechanical enhancement in epoxy composites
abstract: Epoxy thermosets are widely used in structural and electronic components but suffer from high flammability and toxic fume emission. Halogen-free flame retardants typically require high loadings and degrade mechanical properties, causing an unavoidable trade-off. Herein, a hierarchically structured LDH-DBS@PDA@PBA hybrid filler is rationally designed via multi-step interfacial manipulation to simultaneously improve fire safety and mechanical strength. DBS intercalation expands LDH galleries, while mussel-inspired polydopamine acts as a dual-function bridge to anchor uniform, confined NiCoFe Prussian blue analogue nanocrystals (50–70 nm) on LDH sheets. With only 7.5 wt% loading, the composite achieves a LOI of 33.1 % and UL-94 V-1 rating, while peak heat release rate, CO production, and smoke production decline by 70.3 %, 70.0 %, and 58.1 %, respectively, compared to neat epoxy. Impact and tensile strengths rise by 29.0 % and 11.2 %, overcoming the flame retardancy–mechanical performance compromise. The outstanding fire protection is attributed to a synergistic cascade of endothermic cooling, volatile dilution, and transition-metal-catalyzed carbonization, forming a dense, thermally insulating char barrier. This work provides a practical interfacial engineering strategy for high-performance epoxy composites in fire-critical applications.

title: MatSegNet: A new boundary-aware deep learning model for accurate carbide precipitate analysis in high-strength steels
abstract: Lower Bainite (LB) and Tempered Martensite (TM) are two common microstructures in modern high-strength steels. LB and TM can render similar mechanical properties for steels, yet LB is often considered superior to TM in resistance to hydrogen embrittlement. Such performance differences have conventionally been attributed to their distinction in certain microstructural features, particularly carbides. The present study developed, MatSegNet, a new contour-aware deep learning (DL) architecture. It is tailored for comprehensive segmentation and quantitative characterization of carbide precipitates with complex contours in high-strength steels, shown to outperform existing leading DL architectures. Based on MatSegNet, a high-throughput DL pipeline has been established for precise comparative carbide analysis in LB and TM. The results showed that statistically the two microstructures exhibit similarity in key carbide characteristics with marginal difference, cautioning against the conventional use of carbide orientation as a reliable means to differentiate LB and TM in practice. Through MatSegNet, this work demonstrated the potential of DL to play a critical role in enabling accurate and quantitative microstructure characterization to facilitate development of structure–property relationships for accelerating materials innovation.

title: Data-driven multi-parameter collaborative optimization of microstructure and electrical performance for inkjet-printed silver circuits
abstract: Inkjet printing (IJP), as a rapidly advancing additive manufacturing (AM) technology, offers a promising approach for the conformal fabrication of circuits. Nevertheless, the quality of circuits is heavily affected by process parameters and substantially determines the service performance of functional components. Unlike conventional experimental trial-and-error methods, this work adopts data-driven methodologies to accurately predict process parameters from measured data. Initially, a full-factorial experimental design was implemented to fabricate printed specimens. Subsequently, the correlations between process parameters-namely substrate temperature, printing speed, delay time, and number of layers and quality metrics, including line width (LW), line resistance (LR), and line thickness (LT), were modeled using long short-term memory (LSTM), bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and sparrow search algorithm-enhanced BiLSTM (SSA-BiLSTM) models. The main and interactive effects of parameters on line quality were then quantified and analyzed. Furthermore, the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) was utilized to identify and verify optimal parameter sets that minimize LW and LR while maintaining desirable LT performance. The results reveal that the SSA-BiLSTM model consistently outperforms both LSTM and BiLSTM models across all output responses, attaining the highest coefficients of determination (R 2 ) and the lowest root mean squared errors (RMSE) for LW (R 2 = 0.9466), LR (R 2 = 0.9782), and LT (R 2 = 0.9287). The optimized process parameters—substrate temperature of 68 ℃, printing speed of 1238 mm/min, 5 layers and an 8 ms delay time—proved to be both effective and reliable. Overall, the proposed data-driven framework significantly improves the manufacturing performance of IJP for microelectronic devices.

title: Experiment-driven machine learning prediction of mechanical properties of additively manufactured sparse-cell gyroid structures
abstract: Additively manufactured Gyroid structures have great potential for lightweight load-bearing and energy-absorbing applications. In this study, PEEK and PEEK-CF Gyroid thin-walled structures with different cell sizes and cell wall thicknesses were fabricated by fused deposition modeling and tested under quasi-static compression. The effects of structural parameters on compressive modulus, compressive strength, mass, energy absorption, and specific energy absorption were systematically investigated. The results show that increasing wall thickness and decreasing cell size both enhance the compressive and energy absorption performance. Three machine learning models were compared, including Gaussian process regression, extreme gradient boosting, and support vector regression. The optimized Gaussian process regression model achieved test R 2 above 0.97 for all five target properties. This work provides an efficient experiment-driven machine learning strategy for mechanical property prediction and design screening of additively manufactured Gyroid lightweight structures

title: Data-driven topology design and experimental validation of hyperelastic auxetic metamaterials
abstract: The design and fabrication of hyperelastic auxetic metamaterials are particularly challenging because of coupled material and geometric nonlinearities, structural instability, and internal self-contact under large deformation. These effects can cause premature buckling and reduce auxetic performance. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a data-driven topology design framework that integrates nonlinear finite element analysis with a learning-based generative model. The framework first prepares diverse auxetic candidates and evaluates their mechanical responses using a nonlinear model incorporating Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, geometric nonlinearity, and internal self-contact. High-performing designs are then selected by simultaneously minimizing the effective Poisson’s ratio and deformation asymmetry, and new candidates are generated through an iterative generation–evaluation–selection process. The optimized structure is fabricated by stereolithography using a commercial elastomeric resin and experimentally validated under quasi-static compression. Compared with an initial design candidate and a spline-like benchmark, the optimized specimen exhibits stronger auxetic behavior and lower global deformation asymmetry, maintaining measured effective Poisson’s ratios below over a broad strain range. Deformation observations further reveal coordinated unit-cell rotation followed by gradual contact-induced stiffening, resulting in symmetric and controllable deformation under large compression.

title: Microstructure evolution in nickel-based superalloy IN718 during cogging
abstract: Cogging is a hot open-die forging operation used to control the microstructure of cast and wrought Ni-based superalloys. However, the impact of cogging process variables on microstructural evolution has not been investigated in detail. In this work, a unique lab-scale rig has been used to physically simulate the cogging process on small samples (Ø 12 mm) of the superalloy IN718. These trials have been modelled using finite element analysis, and the resulting microstructures have been characterised in detail along the entire length of the cogged sample using large area EBSD mapping. These results show that grain size depends on strain path and cannot be predicted from total accumulated strain alone. Detailed characterisation reveals that a trimodal microstructure is generated during cogging. This structure comprises (i) unrecrystallised grains, (ii) dynamically recrystallised grains and (iii) post-dynamically recrystallised grains. The area fraction of the post-dynamically recrystallised grains is associated with the strain applied in the final forging blow. Since these post-dynamically recrystallised grains grow moderately large (≈55 μm) during the slow cooling which follows cogging, the strain applied in the final cogging bite has a strong impact on final grain size

title: Tailoring impact resistance and damage evolution in 7A62/7A52 aluminum alloy laminated plates through layer-number design
abstract: Layer architecture critically affects the flexural and impact performance of heterogeneous metallic laminates. Here, 2-, 4-, 8-, and 16-layer 7A62/7A52 aluminum alloy laminated plates were fabricated by accumulative roll bonding, and their flexural behavior, absorbed impact energy, ballistic performance, and failure mechanisms were investigated. The high-strength 7A62 and ductile 7A52 layers were alternately distributed through the thickness, with relatively straight interfaces and no evident necking or wavy instability. The 4-layer plate exhibited the best overall performance, achieving an absorbed impact energy of 48.4 J, 100%, 21%, and 27% higher than those of the 2-, 8-, and 16-layer plates, respectively. Under ballistic impact, all configurations failed through combined shear plugging, interfacial delamination, bending, and fragment spalling. The 4-layer plate dissipated 152.3 J of kinetic energy, exceeding the corresponding values of the 2-, 8-, and 16-layer plates by 61.0%, 19.5%, and 22.7%, respectively. Its superior performance arose from synergistic constituent-layer plasticity, coordinated interlayer deformation, and interfacial energy dissipation. Performance varied non-monotonically with layer number: an appropriate interface number balanced load transfer, deformation coordination, and energy dissipation, whereas excessive interfaces promoted delamination and fragmentation. These findings support the design of lightweight 7xxx-series aluminum alloy protective laminates.

title: Direction-dependent hardening in anisotropic FDM-printed ABS: Hill48 constitutive modeling with Taguchi-based optimization and fractographic validation
abstract: Raster-based deposition influences the mechanical response of fused deposition modeling (FDM)-printed acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS), yet prior Hill (1948)-based FDM models generally assume orientation-independent hardening. This study develops a custom UMAT subroutine for CalculiX, combining orthotropic elasticity, Hill anisotropic yielding, and direction-dependent post-yield hardening for ABS at 0°, 45°, and 90° raster orientations, calibrated via a Taguchi L9 design (27 specimens). Elastic stiffness, yield stress, and hardening modulus varied independently with orientation: hardening modulus decreased 34.5% from 0° to 90° (699.23 to 457.95 MPa), while yield stress was lowest at 0° despite its highest stiffness. The model reproduced experimental response within −4% to +16% at 0° and 90°, but showed a systematic deviation at 45° (−24% to +6%), not attributable to the plastic-strain calibration or hardening form, pointing instead to three-dimensional stress redistribution. Fractography corroborated this, showing localized ductile texture in the 0° specimen absent in the 90° block. Layer height was the only significant process-parameter driver of tensile strength (0° block); the Taguchi-predicted optimum generalized to an independent confirmation specimen (+6.5%). These results indicate that isotropic post-yield hardening, assumed in prior semi-crystalline-validated Hill-based FDM models, does not transfer to amorphous ABS.

title: Guest conformational rigidification and solid solution in a supramolecular cage compound: molecular dynamics, phase transition, ferroelectricity and fluorescence
abstract: The confinement of molecules within supramolecular cages provides a unique platform for modulating molecular motion. However, the precise role of a guest’s intrinsic conformational flexibility in its confined dynamics remains elusive. Here, we report the encapsulation of a conformationally rigidified tadpole-like molecule, 1-allyl-1H-imidazole (AIm), within a two-in-one supramolecular cage formed by p-tert-butylcalix [4] arene (BC), namely AIm@(BC) 2 . In contrast to the propyl-linked analogue (1-propyl-1H-imidazole, PIm), the allyl group in AIm exhibits reduced conformational flexibility. This subtle modification raises the activation energy for cage-confined motion from 0.27 eV to 0.30 eV and lowers the ferroelectric phase transition temperature from 192 K to 139 K—both changes are attributed mainly to the conformational rigidification of the AIm guest, which simultaneously increases the kinetic barrier for reorientation and diminishes the thermodynamic driving force for ordering. The rigidified guest also enhances fluorescence. Furthermore, forming a molecular solid solution between the two end-members disrupts long-range dipole coupling, converting conventional ferroelectricity into relaxor behavior with suppressed permittivity and broadened frequency dispersion. Collectively, this work establishes guest conformational rigidification and solid solution formation as two effective strategies to systematically tune molecular dynamics, phase transitions, and electrical/optical properties in a supramolecular cage system.

title: An oral montmorillonite nano-delivery system of purple radish anthocyanin for ulcerative colitis therapy
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, non-specific inflammatory bowel disease. Although natural anthocyanins have the potential to scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) and repair oxidative damage, their poor oral absorption and gastric stability limit their clinical application. This study firstly loaded purple radish anthocyanin (PRA) into montmorillonite (MMT) nano-interlayers to construct a novel oral nano-delivery system (PRA-MMT), and evaluated its therapeutic efficacy and mechanism against UC. The results showed that PRA-MMT exhibited excellent physicochemical stability. The impermeable nature of MMT endowed it with strong resistance to the harsh gastrointestinal environment, and its mucoadhesive property prolonged the intestinal retention time of PRA. In DSS-induced colitis in mice, PRA-MMT enabled sustained release of PRA, exerted anti-inflammatory and antioxidant functions, significantly repaired the intestinal barrier, and exhibited favorable biosafety. PRA-MMT effectively repaired the intestinal barrier through synergistic antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, providing a new strategy and experimental basis for UC therapy based on natural products and nanocarriers.

title: Tailored infill path design using surface mesh deformation: a strategy for boosting mechanical performance in fused filament fabrication
abstract: Infill path planning critically influences the mechanical performance and printability of parts fabricated by fused filament fabrication (FFF). Conventional contour-parallel and zigzag paths provide good manufacturability but are poorly adapted to complex load-transfer conditions, whereas stress-aligned paths may suffer from discontinuity and nonuniform spacing. This study proposes a tailored infill path design method based on surface mesh deformation. The framework integrates SIMP-based topology optimization and Gaussian-weighted mesh deformation to transform a regular orthogonal mesh into continuous and printable paths that may follow stress orientations. The bridge, hook, and tensile testing specimens have been manufactured to validate the effectiveness of this method. Compared with conventional 0/90° infill, the average maximum loads of bridge specimens with optimized infill paths increase by 51.9% at a deformation degree of 60%. In addition, for the hook specimens and tensile specimens with a hole in the middle, the compression and tensile strengths increase by 70.2% and 45.8% compared to classic zig-zag printing paths. Therefore, the proposed method significantly improves the mechanical properties of 3D printed thermoplastic components using surface mesh deformation.

title: Surface-functionalized plant-derived carbon soot nanoparticles with enhanced dispersion stability and biocompatibility as sustainable tattoo pigments
abstract: Synthetic tattoo inks contain toxic impurities introduced during the ink manufacturing process. Therefore, alternative color pigments with high biocompatibility and stability need to be developed. Plant-derived edible soot is a promising pigment for black tattoo inks; however, its hydrophobicity necessitates surface modification to ensure stabilization under physiological conditions. In this study, Pluronic-coated soot nanoparticles (PSNPs) were developed as novel biocompatible color pigments. PSNP127 (1:20), a pigment prepared using soot nanoparticles coated with Pluronic F127, exhibited a spherical morphology with an average diameter of 220 nm. A black dispersion containing PSNP127 maintained its coloration and particle size for four weeks without noticeable precipitation under physiological conditions, demonstrating enhanced stability. An in vitro analysis of PSNP127 revealed that it did not affect cell viability, morphology, or oxidative stress levels in fibroblasts. The PSNP127 pigment was successfully tattooed into the dorsal skin of rats in vivo , resulting in an intense black color. No degradation or histological changes were observed during the eight weeks of monitoring, demonstrating the good retention capacity and biocompatibility of PSNP127. Furthermore, hemolysis, skin sensitization tests, and acute immunotoxicity analyses demonstrated the potential of PSNP127 to serve as a stable and safe pigment for black tattoo inks

title: Process–microstructure–rheology linkage in industrial semi-solid processing: A shear-history-dependent Herschel–Bulkley framework
abstract: Semi-solid slurry rheology under industrial stirring conditions is strongly influenced by transient structural evolution that cannot be captured by classical steady-state constitutive models. The present study introduces a process-history-aware Herschel–Bulkley framework in which the yield stress, consistency index, and flow index evolve as functions of a structural parameter encoding the inherited shear history of EN AC 42,000 alloy slurry prepared using the RheoMetal™ process. The proposed framework substantially improves predictive capability compared with classical steady-state models ( versus ), reducing the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) from 45.8% to 10.5%. Independent validation further demonstrates predictive utility beyond the calibration boundary, yielding a MAPE of 29.4% under extrapolation conditions. Microstructural analysis supports the physical basis of . The shear-rate increment exhibits strong correlation with multi-scale particle dispersion quantified using Ripley’s function ( , ), supporting a physically grounded Process Microstructure Rheology relationship associated with transient structural evolution. These results suggest that rheological evolution in semi-solid slurry processing is governed not only by instantaneous shear rate, but also by the inherited structural state generated during prior processing history.

title: Spray-deployable microenvironment-adaptive nanozyme interface for anti-biofilm and redox-regulated chronic wound healing
abstract: Chronic wounds are characterized by persistent bacterial infection, oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration, which require dynamic therapeutic interventions throughout the healing process. Herein, we report a spray-deployable nanozyme hybrid multifunctional dressing (MHFD) based on Fe 3 O 4 /Au magnetic-gold nanozymes integrated into a polydopamine/phase-transition bovine serum albumin (PDA/PTB) interface. The PDA/PTB hybrid membrane not only stabilizes the catalytic interface and inhibits bacterial adhesion but also enhances nanozyme activity and photothermal responsiveness.
