Benefiting from the pH-responsive catalytic behavior of Fe 3 O 4 /Au nanozymes, the MHFD exhibits peroxidase (POD)-like activity under acidic infection conditions for efficient bacterial eradication, while switching to superoxide dismutase (SOD)-like activity under near-neutral conditions to alleviate oxidative stress and promote tissue repair. The synergistic effects of anti-adhesion, catalytic antibacterial activity, redox regulation, and photothermal enhancement enable effective control of the wound microenvironment. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that MHFD accelerates infection resolution, promotes macrophage polarization and collagen deposition, and significantly enhances chronic wound healing. This work provides a versatile interfacial engineering strategy for constructing multifunctional nanozyme-based therapeutic platforms.

title: A novel residual stress finite element method model based on anisotropic yield criterion for a rare earth magnesium alloy
abstract: To accurately predict the quenching residual stress (RS) in a rare-earth (RE) magnesium alloy conical forging, anisotropic characterizations were first performed on the material at both microstructural and macroscopic scales. The anisotropy is mainly reflected in the preferred orientation of grains, a distinct basal texture, and the axial yield strength (YS) being significantly higher than that in other directions. Based on these characterization results, a RS finite element method (FEM) model based on the anisotropic yield criterion was established. RS tests via the hole drilling method (HDM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) show that, compared with the traditional isotropic RS FEM, the prediction accuracy of the proposed model is improved by 7.32%. In addition, the HDM is more suitable for the RS test of magnesium alloys with obvious texture and anisotropy than the XRD method.

title: A biofunctionalizable collagen-nPVA interpenetrating network hydrogel for long-term resistance against cell-induced contraction
abstract: Collagen is widely used in tissue engineering due to its bioactivity and ability to support cell adhesion, migration, and differentiation. However, collagen-based in vitro tissues exhibit cell-mediated contraction, which can impair their applicability as microphysiological models or systems for regenerative purposes. Chemical or fiber-based strategies to limit contraction often compromise the bioactivity of collagen, introduce cytotoxic components, or result in mechanical and biological heterogeneity. Addressing these issues, we demonstrate an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) hydrogel based on collagen and norbornene-functionalized poly(vinyl alcohol). The synthetic network serves as a stabilizing backbone that greatly resists hydrogel contraction while preserving collagen bioactivity and further enabling biofunctionalization. Upon encapsulation of human dermal fibroblasts, the IPN strongly limits cell-mediated contraction for up to 21 days, while maintaining fibroblast behavior in terms of viability, metabolic activity and spreading capacity comparable to collagen. Furthermore, the IPN supports the attachment of human umbilical vein endothelial cells to the hydrogel surface, and sprouting from 3D cell spheroids into the matrix. Functionalization with a VEGF-mimetic peptide further enhanced early endothelial cell sprouting, demonstrating the system’s capacity for modular biofunctionalization. Collectively, these properties make this IPN a promising material allowing for long-term culture of 3D tissue constructs and tunable biofunctionalization.

title: Correlation of microstructural characteristics with the mechanical and electrical properties of low-temperature annealed copper-clad aluminum
abstract: Annealing is crucial for restoring the ductility of severely deformed copper-clad aluminum (CCA) conductors; however, it simultaneously drives intermetallic compound (IMC) growth at the Al/Cu interface, and the point at which the penalties of annealing outweigh the benefits remains unclear. To investigate this, CCA wires were annealed at 260–350 °C, lower temperatures than those used in most kinetic studies. Al 2 Cu and AlCu were formed at the earliest stage, whereas Al 4 Cu 9 was formed at the Cu-side interface only after an incubation period. Because the interfacial state depends on temperature and time, they were considered together in terms of the total IMC thickness, allowing different thermal histories to be compared on a common basis. The maximum elongation and a reduction in the rate of increase in conductivity were observed at an IMC thickness of approximately 2 µm; both transitions coincided with the first appearance of Al 4 Cu 9 rather than with any particular temperature or time. These transitions are consistent with contributions from the complex cubic structure of Al 4 Cu 9 and the accumulated thickness, which develop together. Therefore, the onset of the dominant brittle phase provides a criterion for annealing design, which is defined by the interfacial state rather than by temperature and time.

title: Protein delivery from calcium phosphate cements – influence of loading routes and compositional modifications on release behaviour and material properties
abstract: Calcium phosphate cements (CPC) are established bone graft substitutes and versatile local drug/protein delivery matrices, but the effects of simple, clinically conceivable loading routes on cement behaviour remain incompletely quantified. Using lysozyme, bovine serum albumin and foetal calf serum as model proteins with different experimental functions, we compared three low-complexity incorporation methods: mixing proteins as dry powder into a cement paste, post-setting adsorption by dip coating, or mixing the cement paste directly with a protein solution. In addition, calcium sulphate and/or mesoporous bioactive glass were added to the CPC to alter ionic environment and release behaviour. We assessed setting, initial mechanical properties and porosity, pH change, ion release (Ca, P, Si, Sr), protein release and retained protein activity, and interpreted results with multivariate regression, mixed-effects modelling and principal component analysis. Material composition primarily governed pH and ionic release signatures, whereas the preparation workflow and protein loading method showed the strongest association with protein release trajectories; protein type had comparatively small effects on release kinetics. In summary, we demonstrate that a range of parameters exist for converting CPC into a versatile delivery system with low-complexity workflows that are potentially translatable to clinical applications.

title: Materials design framework for mitigating thermal cracking in high-carbon martensitic steel via coordinated cryogenic treatment and tempering
abstract: Thermal cracking is triggered by frictional thermal shock in high-carbon martensitic steels used as work rolls for cold rolling. However, materials-design strategies that satisfy hardness requirements while mitigating thermal cracking remain underdeveloped. This study proposes a framework linking cryogenic treatment, tempering, retained austenite (RA), hardness, and fracture-related responses in a single material system. AISI 52100 steel was subjected to systematic cryogenic treatment and tempering to produce different RA fractions and associated pre-thermal shock material states while maintaining comparable post-tempering hardness. The quasi-static fracture resistance was evaluated using the critical stress intensity factor, whereas the thermal-crack susceptibility was assessed through frictional thermal-shock testing, microstructural characterization, and residual stress measurements. The quasi-static fracture resistance was primarily governed by hardness and showed limited dependence on the RA fraction. The thermal-crack susceptibility was generally higher in specimens with lower RA fractions. This observation is qualitatively consistent with the contribution from RA-related irreversible-strain accommodation, although other microstructural changes induced by cryogenic treatment may also contribute. The proposed framework provides a conceptual basis for interpreting the roles of hardness, RA fraction, and material states induced by cryogenic treatment and offers guidance for coordinating cryogenic treatment and tempering to mitigate thermal cracking while maintaining the required hardness

title: Multifunctional phase-change thermal interface composite integrating a natural cotton-derived NiFe2O4–carbon network with AlN
abstract: Highly integrated electronic systems require thermal interface materials (TIMs) that combine efficient heat transfer with thermal buffering, leakage resistance, electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, and mechanical stability. Here, a multifunctional phase-change TIM was developed by integrating a NiFe 2 O 4 -decorated carbonized cotton network with an AlN-containing stearic acid/butylene-based epoxy matrix. The carbonized cotton network contributed to phase-change-material confinement, auxiliary heat conduction, and support of the EMI-active phase, while AlN provided the primary thermal pathways. The composite exhibited a thermal conductivity of 3.54 W·m −1 ·K −1 , a melting latent heat of 83.1 J·g −1 , and an X-band EMI shielding effectiveness of 26.18 dB with a total shielding fraction of 99.76%. The latent heat decreased by only 2.25% after 50 consecutive DSC heating–cooling cycles. No evident leakage was observed under static heating up to 150 °C or after coupled thermal-compressive testing at 150 °C and 1 MPa for 1 h. The composite also showed a tensile strength of 17.7 MPa and a strain at break of 40.5%. During a 40 min CPU test, the final 5 min average core temperature was 75.8 °C, demonstrating sustained multifunctional thermal-management performance.

title: Rosmarinic acid-loaded proanthocyanidin self-assembled nanosystem for atherosclerosis therapy via regulating macrophage lipid metabolism and inhibiting phenotype transformation of VSMCs
abstract: Dysfunction of lipid metabolism in macrophages and phenotype transformation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) are key events in the advancement of AS. Thus, the novel strategies of coordinated regulation of lipid metabolism and inhibition of phenotype transformation of VSMCs can provide tools for AS therapy. In this study, a rosmarinic acid-loaded proanthocyanidin self-assembled nanosystem with hyaluronic acid modification (HA-PA@RA NPs) was developed to synergistically alleviate AS. In vitro results demonstrated that HA-PA@RA NPs regulated lipid metabolism by upregulating ABCA1/ABCG1in macrophage. Meanwhile, HA-PA@RA NPs inhibited phenotype transformation of VSMCs by upregulating alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) and smooth muscle 22 alpha (SM22α) while downregulating osteopontin (OPN) through the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. In vivo studies demonstrated that HA-PA@RA NPs prolonged circulation time and actively targeted diseased regions, effectively reducing plaque area and alleviating AS progression. Overall, HA-PA@RA NPs with high biocompatibility exerted synergistic effects on regulating macrophage lipid metabolism and inhibiting phenotype transformation of VSMCs. In summary, this nanodrug holds the potential for the clinical therapy of AS.

title: Effect of heat treatment on transformation behavior and functional properties of NiTiCu shape memory alloys: A review
abstract: NiTiCu shape memory alloys (SMAs) are increasingly studied because Cu addition can reduce transformation hysteresis, improve cyclic stability, and modify the martensitic transformation pathway relative to binary NiTi. However, these advantages are strongly dependent on manufacturing route and thermal history, since segregation, residual stress, porosity, and secondary phase formation can alter the effective matrix composition and functional response. This review examines heat treatment in NiTiCu SMAs, focusing on how thermal processing controls phase composition, precipitate evolution, transformation behavior, hysteresis, and mechanical and functional properties. The effects of Cu on phase stability and thermomechanical behavior are first discussed, followed by an overview of conventional and additive manufacturing routes that define the as-fabricated microstructure. Solution treatment, aging, and annealing are then reviewed as key strategies for homogenization, stress relief, precipitate control, and stabilization of transformation-mediated deformation. The review also highlights the value of CALPHAD modeling in identifying safe and effective heat treatment parameters for phase control and post-processing optimization.

title: Transient amorphous interfacial layers modulate early-stage corrosion of steels in supercritical CO2-saturated brine
abstract: Bulk Cr content is commonly considered an important factor influencing the corrosion resistance of steels in CO 2 -containing environments; however, its relationship with early-stage corrosion behavior is complicated by differences in alloy composition, microstructure, and evolving interfacial chemistry. Here, six commercial steels containing 0.07–16.78 wt% Cr were exposed to CO 2 -saturated 3.5 wt% NaCl brine at 10 MPa and 50 °C for 1–1000 h to establish the relationship among bulk alloy chemistry, early interfacial-layer evolution, and corrosion behaviour. Gravimetric measurements revealed a non-monotonic dependence of corrosion rate on Cr content. For example, after 100 h, P91 steel containing 8.38 wt% Cr exhibited a lower corrosion rate (0.039 mm/yr) than 13Cr steel containing 13.04 wt% Cr (0.069 mm/yr). X-ray diffraction, SEM/EDS, Raman spectroscopy, and cross-sectional STEM/SAED revealed distinct early interfacial chemistries among the steels. These surface layers were operationally categorized as Fe–C-enriched, Fe–O-rich, or Cr–O-enriched transient amorphous layers (TALs), depending on alloy type and exposure time. To evaluate how TAL chemistry influences interfacial reactivity, amorphous Fe–C, Fe–O, and Cr–O layers supported on Fe were modelled using density functional theory. Fe–C TALs showed the strongest adsorption of H 2 O, CO 2 , and H 2 CO 3 , whereas Cr–O TALs exhibited the weakest adsorption and the least favourable energetics for CO 2 -derived bicarbonate formation and decomposition. The experimentally observed corrosion trends and calculated interfacial energetics together indicate that early TAL chemistry provides a mechanistic descriptor beyond bulk Cr content alone. Promoting Cr–O-enriched interfacial layers may therefore offer a materials-design strategy for improving the corrosion resistance of steels used in CO 2 transport, injection, and storage systems.

title: Limit-position characterization of novel crossed star-shaped honeycombs under in-plane crushing
abstract: Auxetic metamaterials (AMs) exhibit excellent shear resistance and energy absorption properties; nevertheless, traditional star‑shaped honeycombs suffer from low initial stiffness, and limited attention has been paid to honeycomb metamaterial mechanical responses at the boundaries of feasible geometric design domains. To this end, this paper takes the crossed star-shaped honeycomb (CSSH) as a prototype and innovatively arranges the crossed inclined cell walls to their limit positions, designing three reinforced limit configurations: ECSSH-1/2/3. Quasi-static compression tests were conducted on PLA specimens produced via FDM 3D printing, whilst finite element models were established using ABAQUS to systematically analyse their in-plane crushing behaviour. The results indicate that the performance of the reinforced honeycombs has been significantly enhanced, with ECSSH-3 exhibiting a maximum increase in energy absorption of 271.5 % compared to the original CSSH; the opened angle ( θ 1 ) had a negligible effect on the deformation modes of the three ECSSH types across most of the investigated parameter space, except that ECSSH-3 may experience unstable collapse at θ 1 = 10°. Meanwhile, the inclined angle θ 2 significantly reduced structural stability, with ECSSH-3 being the most sensitive to θ 2 ; all reinforced honeycombs exhibited a two-stage deformation mechanism comprising star-shaped cell wall bending and rhombic lattice collapse. This two-step deformation mechanism degenerates into a single-step mode when θ 2 is ≥ 72.5° for both ECSSH-1 and ECSSH-3. ECSSH-1 exhibited the most stable deformation and the strongest negative Poisson’s ratio, whilst ECSSH-3 demonstrated the best compressive strength and energy absorption capacity. A comparison with existing expandable honeycomb structures confirms that this limit-position topology design can efficiently enhance energy absorption performance whilst reducing weight; the design approach can be extended to various types of honeycomb metamaterials.

title: A linear-nonlinear coupled symbolic framework for accurate property prediction: A case study on beta transus temperature of titanium alloys
abstract: In material property prediction, linear empirical formulas lack accuracy and ignore interactions, while nonlinear ML models are black–box and overlook linear contributions. To overcome these dual drawbacks, we propose a novel linear–symbolic regression framework that constructs a dual–layer formula by simultaneously coupling linear and nonlinear terms, thereby preserving the explicit linear effects while fully accounting for complex elemental interactions. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through a case study on the beta transus temperature prediction of titanium alloys. Extensive extrapolation tests show that our approach significantly outperforms traditional empirical formulas, linear regressions, and nonlinear ML models in terms of accuracy and generalizability on the present dataset. More importantly, this work offers a new paradigm for mining intricate nonlinear relationships in materials science without sacrificing the interpretable linear contribution of compositional features.

title: Tregs derived apoptotic bodies loaded with miR-483-3p for mitigating ferroptosis and inflammation in ischemic skin flaps via AGO1/NF-κB pathway
abstract: Background Ischemic random-pattern skin flaps (RPSFs) are widely used in clinics to reconstruct cutaneous wounds. However, RPSFs are limited by poor blood supply leading to inflammation and ferroptosis. This study developed regulatory T cells (Tregs) derived apoptotic bodies (T-ABs) loaded with miR-483-3p (T-ABs miR-483-3p ) to improve skin flaps viability. Methods The morphology of apoptotic bodies from TBHP-induced Tregs (T-ABs) and T-ABs encapsulated with miR-483-3p (T-ABs miR-483-3p ) was observed by TEM. RPSFs blood perfusion and temperature were evaluated by laser doppler flowmetry and infrared thermography. Immunofluorescence (IF) and western blotting (WB) were also employed to verify the mechanism by which T-ABs miR-483-3p influence RPSFs viability. Results T-ABs functioned as effective delivery vectors for miR-483-3p both in vitro and in vivo. T-ABs miR-483-3p treatment significantly enhanced RPSFs survival rate, blood perfusion, tissue temperature, and angiogenesis. The pro-survival effects were mediated by suppressing ferroptosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress through the miR-483-3p/AGO1/NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of AGO1 impaired RPSFs viability, while T-ABs miR-483-3p alleviated these injuries via the AGO1/NF-κB axis. Conclusion T-ABs exert potent pro-regenerative effects by delivering miR-483-3p to suppress AGO1, thereby mitigating NF-κB-mediated inflammation and ferroptosis. AGO1 may represent a potential therapeutic target for enhancing RPSFs regeneration, providing new insights for cutaneous regenerative medicine.

title: Multilayer weft knitted fabric design for balancing mechanical reinforcement and elastic recovery after heat pressing
abstract: Functional support fabrics provide mechanical restraint while preserving recoverable deformation. However, the role of multilayer knitted construction in distributing yarns selected for different material functions, and its implications for reinforcement and elastic recovery after heat pressing, requires further clarification. This study therefore examined the mechanical properties and elastic recovery of multilayer weft knitted fabrics after heat pressing. Three knitted structures incorporating two yarn combinations were investigated with untreated controls. Heat pressing produced partial inter-yarn bonding and a compact morphology. The full needle rib and back knit construction incorporating main nylon yarn and low-melting-point nylon achieved the highest bending stiffness (402.5 N·mm) and tensile load at 50% strain (442 N), with the latter 29.5 times that of the strongest untreated control. The bending stiffness showed a structural effect in the wale direction and a structure and yarn interaction in both bending directions. The alternating 1 × 1 tuck middle connection with elastic yarn retained the highest elastic recovery (58.27%), close to the control (59.80%), while tensile load at 50% strain increased from 11.54 to 198.12 N. The results provide a structural and material basis for balancing support enhancement with retained elastic recovery for future wearable supporters.

title: Quantitative evaluation of acoustic transmission characteristics of dental prosthetic materials for intraoral bone-conduction auditory assistive devices
abstract: Bone conduction hearing aids are classified into implantable and non-implantable types. Implantable devices offer high transmission efficiency but involve surgical risks, while non-implantable devices can be applied without surgery but suffer from reduced transmission efficiency due to soft tissue attenuation. This study proposes an intraoral bone conduction hearing assistance device integrable with dental prosthetics as a means of achieving transmission efficiency comparable to implantable devices without the surgical burden, and verifies its feasibility at a laboratory level. To this end, the frequency response characteristics of representative dental prosthetic materials were quantitatively measured and compared, confirming that acoustic vibration transmission characteristics vary distinctly depending on the type of housing material. While bone conduction transmission potential was confirmed in all evaluated materials, zirconia and dental resin exhibited relatively stable and high frequency response characteristics under the experimental conditions of this study. The frequency response data obtained for each material in this study provides foundational data that can be utilized in the design and material selection process for future intraoral bone conduction hearing assistance devices.

title: Corrigendum to “Thermal, electrical and magnetic properties of Cu-Doped CoSi2” [Mater. Des. 265 (2026) 115873]
Machine-learning-empowered knowledge mining for general design rules in high-performance intermetallic compound interconnects
abstract: The continued scaling of semiconductor devices demands the development of advanced interconnect materials beyond the limitations of conventional copper. Here, we propose a Data-Model-Knowledge co-mining learning framework to accelerate the discovery of high-performance intermetallic candidates. Cohesive energy and the key figure-of-merit parameter ρ 0 ×λ were systematically curated from literature to construct robust regression models. Pareto optimality analysis was employed to balance the dual objectives of high cohesive energy and low ρ 0 ×λ enabling the identification of optimal intermetallic candidates for interconnect applications. Furthermore, interpretable machine learning enabled the extraction of key descriptors, leading to a generalizable design rule: binary alloys with a valence electron count (VE) between 7.658 and 9.035 and a cohesive energy (CoE) exceeding 5.765 eV exhibit a greater than 90% likelihood of being identified as Pareto-optimal candidates. Validation using high throughput calculations shows that 62.5% of the predicted candidates outperform the benchmark IrRu and Rh. In addition, several high-potential intermetallics − including CoOs, Co 3 Os, Co 4 Os, Rh 3 Os, Ir 4 W, Rh 3 Ir, and Rh 4 Ru − were identified as potential interconnect materials. This data–model–knowledge framework establishes a transferable paradigm for materials informatics, enabling the transformation of high-dimensional data into actionable design rules and accelerating the discovery of advanced materials across diverse systems.

title: Rapid discovery of high thermal conductivity silicon nitride ceramics via synergistic integration of WGAN-GP and active learning
abstract: To address the low optimization efficiency of thermal conductivity in silicon nitride ceramics under multi-parameter coupling effects, this study proposes an optimization framework integrating generative adversarial network (GAN) data augmentation with active learning. Using five composition features and four process features as inputs, a high-precision thermal conductivity prediction model with R 2 = 0.92 was trained. Analysis using the SHAP method revealed the relationship between various features and thermal conductivity. Based on an active learning approach, a rapid screening was conducted for preparation schemes potentially exhibiting high thermal conductivity characteristics. Through only one experimental round guided by active learning, a silicon nitride ceramic with a thermal conductivity of 102 W·m −1 ·K −1 was obtained by SPS at 1900°C for 1 h. This represents a 20% improvement over the best sample in the initial dataset and demonstrates a clear efficiency advantage over conventional trial and error optimization or passive machine learning prediction. A series of characterizations confirmed the formation of elongated columnar β-Si 3 N 4 grains during sintering, along with their close intergranular bonding. The resulting β phase exhibits low lattice distortion and minimal lattice defects. This study provides an effective research approach for the optimized design of high thermal conductivity silicon nitride ceramics under small sample datasets.

title: Scale-dependent interplay between densification and deposition quality in MEX/M 17-4PH gyroid shell-TPMS
abstract: Mechanical performance in metallic TPMS structures fabricated by metal material extrusion (MEX/M) is commonly associated with densification, defect evolution, and microstructural development. However, it remains unclear whether their relative importance remains constant across different geometric configurations or changes as geometric constraints intensify. This study investigates 17–4 PH gyroid Shell-TPMS structures fabricated through filament-based fused filament fabrication (FFF) and rod-based bound metal deposition (BMD). Feedstock characteristics, deposition architecture, defect populations, microstructure, hardness, density-related metrics, and compressive performance were evaluated across multiple configurations. Statistical analysis revealed significant effects of manufacturing condition, geometric configuration, and their interaction on compressive performance ( p < 0.001). For moderate-to-thick-wall configurations, BMD exhibited the highest compressive performance, combining macro-porosity below 2 %, hardness values 15–25 % higher than FFF, and a peak stress of 26.63 ± 0.32 MPa. In contrast, a different trend was observed for the ultra-thin configuration (UL = 10 mm, RD = 0.082), where BMD exhibited a peak stress approximately 22 % lower than FFF fabricated with a 0.40 mm nozzle despite the more favorable defect, microstructural, and hardness characteristics associated with the BMD process chain. These results indicate a configuration-dependent interplay between consolidation-related and deposition-related characteristics, with deposition architecture becoming increasingly influential as geometric constraints intensify.

title: Nanomaterial-Enabled biosensors for Non-Invasive detection of urological Cancers: From urinary and blood biomarkers to Point-of-Care translation
abstract: Urological cancers—bladder, prostate, renal cell and upper tract urothelial carcinoma—carry a substantial share of the global cancer burden, yet their diagnosis and surveillance rely on procedures that are invasive, costly or poorly specific. Urothelial and prostatic tumors shed cells, nucleic acids, proteins and extracellular vesicles directly into urine, which can be collected non-invasively and repeatedly. This narrative review examines how nanomaterials—metallic, carbon-based, two-dimensional, semiconducting, magnetic, framework-based and enzyme-mimicking—enable biosensors for these analytes in urine and blood. We compare the nanomaterial families on stability, manufacturability and regulatory maturity as well as analytical performance, and survey electrochemical, optical, field-effect-transistor and microfluidic platforms, distinguishing evidence obtained in urological clinical samples from transferable concepts. Applying the Debye relation to urinary electrolyte data shows that sample-to-sample variation in ionic strength alone changes the screening length more than twofold. Of 36 platforms compiled, 22 measured a urological-cancer analyte in human samples and 17 compared patients with controls (median cohort 20); none has reported a prospective evaluation, and none is among the commercially available tests. Within this set, the binding constraints on translation are stability, manufacturing consistency and prospective clinical validation rather than detection limits.

title: Creep behavior mediated by intra-/intergranular particles in Al-Cu-Mg-Ag-Sc alloys
abstract: High-performance Al alloys mediated by dual particles are promising lightweight materials for improving the creep behavior. Here, the effect of Sc microalloying on coarse θ-Al 2 Cu particle distribution, nanoscale precipitates, and creep behavior in high-Cu Al-Cu-Mg-Ag alloys was investigated. Sc addition refines grains, drives θ-Al 2 Cu particles toward grain boundaries, and induces thermally stable V-phase and Al 3 Sc precipitates. The 0.3 wt% Sc alloy exhibits the best creep resistance under compression at 350 °C, outperforming the Sc-free and 0.6 wt% Sc alloys. In the diffusion creep regime, although abundant grain-boundary particles facilitate stress redistribution and impede vacancy diffusion, grain refinement still induces a detrimental transition from Nabarro-Herring to Coble creep, whose rate increase is only partially offset by these particles. In the dislocation creep regime, quasi–in situ EBSD results show that intragranular particles in the 0.3 wt% Sc alloy enhance strain heterogeneity and promote geometrically necessary dislocation accumulation, leading to higher internal stress and creep resistance. Additionally, prolonged creep causes vacancy accumulation and interfacial cavity formation at grain-boundary particles, impairing particle load transfer. These findings demonstrate that the creep resistance of Al alloys is governed not only by the thermally-stable internal resistance but also by the particle-distribution-dependent internal stress generated during creep.

title: A cosmic abundance perspective on refractory element selection in nickel-based superalloys
abstract: Modern nickel-based superalloys achieve exceptional high-temperature performance through refractory elements (W, Re, Ta), whose engineering demand far exceeds cosmic abundance. We introduce the Cosmic Criticality Index (CCI) to quantify this demand-abundance mismatch across eleven elements: it correlates strongly with melting point ( , 95% CI [0.686, 0.977], stable under leave-one-out resampling) and more modestly with solar-nebula condensation temperature ( , 95% CI [ , 0.88]). Partial-correlation analysis shows both associations share explanatory power with cosmic abundance itself ( for the CCI–melting-point association once abundance is controlled), consistent with a picture in which nucleosynthesis and condensation jointly govern abundance and thermodynamic refractoriness. We term this a “refractory element duality”, reflecting shared physical origins behind cosmic scarcity and engineering value rather than a contradiction. Tracing CCI across Generations 1–5, mean aggregate criticality increased 2.4-fold, with narrowing inter-alloy variation indicating convergence toward a consistent compositional strategy; the single-alloy sixth generation is reported for completeness only. Incorporating terrestrial recycling, an Effective CCI shows efficient Re recovery lowers its effective criticality by nearly 0.7 dex, partially offsetting its cosmic scarcity. CCI is a descriptive, statistically grounded framework complementing established terrestrial criticality metrics and offering a foundation for future, more prescriptive alloy-design extensions.

title: Effect of re-melting on residual stresses in Inconel 718 produced by additive manufacturing
abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) fabricated Inconel 718 undergoes harsh thermal cycles that lead to the accumulation of residual stresses, which in turn degrades geometric accuracy and results in the deterioration of mechanical properties. To alleviate these residual stresses, the re-melting strategy has been proposed. In this study, the influence of different re-melting energy densities, E V , on the microstructures and residual stresses of Inconel 718 was investigated. The residual stresses in the builds were assessed using an innovative specimen cutting method. While increasing the E V to up to 0.4 times the first-pass energy increases the RS, at energies ≥ 0.9–1.3 times the first-pass energy led to a more uniform texture, lower RS and minimal porosity. Further increase in the E V led to an increase in porosity and RS. Other mechanical properties, such as yield strength and ductility are insensitive to E V . These results are explained on the basis of changes in the melt pool geometry and thermal gradients with increasing E V . This study highlights the potential of using re-melting to alleviate residual stresses with minimal post-processing treatments.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived bioactive nanosystems and the design logic for antibiotic co-delivery against Helicobacter pylori
abstract: Helicobacter pylori eradication is increasingly compromised by multidrug resistance, gastric acid instability, mucus and biofilm barriers, protected bacterial niches, adverse effects and microbiome disruption. Nanotechnology enables programmable re-engineering of intragastric drug exposure through acid protection, mucus-transport modulation, stimuli-responsive release and synchronized co-delivery. Traditional Chinese Medicine–derived bioactives contribute mechanistically complementary anti-bacterial, anti-urease, anti-adhesive, anti-biofilm, anti-inflammatory and mucosa-protective functions. This Review critically appraises the evidence for combining these bioactives with antibiotics in nanocarriers: it classifies anti- Helicobacter pylori bioactives by chemical class, compiles representative nanosystems carrying Traditional Chinese Medicine bioactives with quantitative physicochemical and efficacy data, and appraises the quantitative basis of antibiotic–Traditional Chinese Medicine synergy. Crucially, genuine co-delivery—one carrier delivering a named antibiotic and a named bioactive—has not yet been achieved for Helicobacter pylori , and this Review therefore specifies what would be required to construct it. The strategy is contextualized against potassium-competitive acid blocker–based regimens and alternatives including phage and endolysin therapy, probiotics and vaccines. Translational barriers—safety, reproducibility, model validity, microbiome effects and regulatory complexity—are critically assessed, and network pharmacology and artificial intelligence–guided formulation are positioned as early-stage enablers. Clinically credible progress demands evidence-grounded platform selection, standardized quality control, predictive gastric models and rigorous clinical validation.

title: Strain-rate-dominated damage competition: microscopic origins and the dual effect in dynamic failure of metallic glasses
abstract: Elucidating the dynamic failure mechanism of advanced materials under extreme conditions remains a formidable challenge, owing to the intricate interplay between strain rate and stress state, compounded by the absence of a unifying mechanistic framework. Here, leveraging molecular dynamics simulations under quasi-isentropic loading, we unravel a strain-rate-governed competitive mechanism underpinning the spallation failure of metallic glasses. We identify an intrinsic dynamic toughening in Cu50Zr50 glass, accompanied by a strain-rate-relevant morphological transition from localized, unstable expansion of sparse voids to dispersed nucleation and kinetically constrained growth of a dense population of micro-voids. A dual strain rate effect of nucleation promotion and expansion suppression is believed to dictate this damage transition. At the microscale, elevated strain rates induce fragmentation of the medium-range-order, proliferating nucleation sites at structural heterogeneities, while simultaneously engendering strong mutual interference among displacement fields, thereby arresting the runaway expansion of any single void. This competition originates from the fundamental temporal disparity between the external loading characteristic time and the intrinsic relaxation time scale under ultrahigh strain rates. We further discuss the potential generality of this dual mechanism across distinct failure modalities of shear-dominated fracture. Synthesizing the role of stress state, we propose a unified conceptual framework of dynamic failure wherein the stress state dictates the primary failure carrier (voids versus shear bands), whereas the strain rate governs the spatial distribution of damage (localized versus dispersed). This framework offers a foundational physical paradigm for rationalizing the diverse spectrum of dynamic failure phenomena observed in metallic glasses.

title: Unveiling the synergistic impact of nanoclay on the mechanical performance of polyester nanocomposite coatings
abstract: Polyester coatings on pre-coated metal (PCM), typically crosslinked with hexamethoxymethyl melamine (HMMM), must provide both wear resistance and high formability. However, increasing hardness to improve wear resistance often reduces toughness, compromising formability. Although nanoclay incorporation has emerged as a promising strategy to mitigate this trade-off, its interactions with the polyester-HMMM network remain poorly understood. This study systematically evaluates the synergistic effects of surface-modified Lucentite (LU) nanoclay and HMMM on hardness ( H ), creep resistance, formability, and wear performance. LU-HMMM interactions produced a complex, non-linear influence that departed from classic rule-of-mixtures predictions. Low LU loadings (≤0.5 wt%) increased H by 5–12% and reduced creep. At higher LU loadings (3–5 wt%), however, hydroxyl groups on the LU consumed HMMM, reducing crosslinking and lowering H by 23–26%. At 30–40 wt% HMMM, excess crosslinker limited hardness gains from low LU additions. At moderate LU loadings (0.25–1 wt%), toughness improved without compromising hardness, overcoming the conventional hardness-toughness trade-off as LU-induced softening remained minimal, allowing nanoclay reinforcement and crack suppression. The highest wear resistance was achieved by coatings containing 0.25 wt% LU with 30 wt% HMMM and 3 wt% LU with 40 wt% HMMM, owing to an optimal balance of hardness, toughness, and surface roughness.

title: Comparative study on the surface integrity of Inconel 718 parts produced by laser powder bed fusion after different finishing techniques
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of four surface finishing methods – Glass Bead Blasting (GBB), Ceramic Cone Grinding (CCG), Dry Electropolishing (DEP), Abrasive Flow Machining (AFM) – on Inconel 718 samples produced via Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF). The assessment was conducted based on technical, geometric and economic criteria tailored for thin-walled aerospace applications. Following heat treatment (comprising stress relieving, hot isostatic pressing, solution annealing, double aging), the alloy achieved near-theoretical density, a recrystallized microstructure characterized by a 55% fraction of Ʃ3 twin boundaries, and precipitation hardening corresponding to a peak hardness of 428 HV10. At a test temperature of 425°C, despite variations in surface finishing techniques, the high density of Ʃ3 boundaries combined with high fracture toughness resulted in a high fatigue limit range (at R = 0.05) between 450 and 485 MPa. The CCG, DEP, and AFM methods reduced the surface roughness (Ra) to < 2 µm, shifting fatigue crack initiation sites from surface notches to subsurface crystallographic facets. The AFM method is the optimal solution for the criteria. The application of AFM resulted in a high fatigue strength of 475 MPa at 425°C, exhibiting minimal geometric distortion and the most favorable ratio of capital expenditure, operating expenses.

title: Mechanical characterization and machine learning prediction of Al 7079 hybrid composites reinforced with coconut shell ash and graphite
abstract: Aluminum matrix composites offer great potential as a lightweight structural material, but the sustainability and mechanical performance development is still ongoing. Additionally, extensive experimental characterization is costly and time-consuming. In this study, Al 7079 hybrid composites were manufactured with coconut shell ash and graphite as reinforcements using the stir casting method and extensively characterized in terms of mechanical properties using hardness, tensile, impact, and density tests. Microstructure characterization shows that the matrix composites achieved matrix—reinforcement bonding and uniform particle dispersion, resulting in increased hardness and tensile strength at the cost of impact energy and density. To complement the extensive experimental characterization, a machine learning-based data-driven framework was developed to predict hardness and tensile strength using physically meaningful input features based on the experimental results. Several regression algorithms were used, showing that lightweight interpretable machine learning methods can also accurately model structure—property relationships without complex model architectures. The insights from this study highlight the need to choose model complexity carefully concerning the dataset and input features. Overall, the machine learning workflow developed in this study allows for a cost-efficient yet interpretable approach to the sustainability and mechanical performance of aluminum matrix composites, thus saving extensive experimental work for optimization.

title: Rigid compatible kinematics and geometric response of boundary released helical origami
abstract: Helical origami structures exhibit coupled axial and rotational deformation, but conventional closed configurations restrict radial evolution due to circumferential constraints. This limitation reduces the geometric freedom available for programming their deformation behavior. In this work, a boundary released helical origami configuration is investigated through a rigid compatible kinematic framework. By relaxing the circumferential constraint, the proposed model establishes the coupling among structural height, circumferential radius, and helical rotation based on triangular facet compatibility. The results reveal that geometric parameters of the crease pattern regulate the accessible deformation regimes and determine the evolution of the crease rotational energy landscape. A geometric transverse response parameter is further introduced to characterize the axial-transverse coupling induced by geometric compatibility rather than material constitutive behavior. The predicted height-radius relationship is validated using paper prototypes, where the measured configurations agree well with the theoretical rigid compatible trajectory. This work provides a geometric design strategy for programming coupled deformation responses in reconfigurable origami structures.

title: Unveiling the Coupled effects of La/Gd substitution on phase transition, lattice defects, and growth mechanism in (La1-xGdx)2Zr2O7 TBCs by EB-PVD
abstract: This study systematically investigates the effects of La/Gd substitution ratio on the crystal structure, microstructural evolution, and elemental distribution of (La 1-x Gd x ) 2 Zr 2 O 7 (LGZ) thermal barrier coatings fabricated via three-step EB-PVD. Five kinds of duplex LGZ/YSZ coatings (x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9) were deposited on (Ni,Pt)Al bond-coated superalloy substrates. The coatings reveal a composition-driven structural transition from ordered pyrochlore to disordered defect-fluorite phase with increasing Gd, alongside lattice contraction and dislocation density variation. Columnar grain size increases monotonically with Gd content, evolving from fine columns with lamellar tips in La-rich compositions (x < 0.5) to coarse columns with pyramid tips in Gd-rich compositions (x > 0.5). This growth behavior results from La 3+ surface segregation and pinning that inhibit lateral growth, whereas Gd-rich compositions lack this effect, allowing normal diffusion and competitive growth. Furthermore, elemental mapping reveals pronounced hierarchical segregation of La perpendicular to the growth in La-rich coatings, due to the higher vapor pressure of lanthanum oxide and stronger La 3+ segregation tendency, while Gd remains relatively uniformly distributed due to its moderate volatility. These findings establish comprehensive processing-structure-composition relationships, providing fundamental guidance for tailoring microstructures and elemental distributions via compositional design in rare-earth zirconate TBCs.

title: Synergistic strengthening mechanisms of in-situ rolling and heat treatment on Ti–6Al–4V titanium alloy prepared by laser directed energy deposition
abstract: Ti–6Al–4V samples were fabricated via in-situ rolling-assisted laser directed energy deposition, and the effects of rolling load and heat treatment on microstructure and tensile properties were studied. In-situ rolling induces plastic deformation of columnar grains and promote recrystallization during layer-by-layer accumulation, reducing average grain size from 469 μm at 0 kN to 133 μm at 10 kN, thereby resulting in a largely equiaxed grain structure, although a small fraction of elongated grains may still remain. An increased number of grain boundaries hinders dislocation movement, and the resulting higher dislocation density significantly enhances the strength of the titanium alloy. After stress-relief annealing, the formation of fine dot-like β phase reduces stress concentration at the α/β interfaces, enhancing ductility. Further grain size reduction helps maintain excellent strength. After solution aging treatment, coarse lamellar α and fine secondary α phases form, and the heat treatment at 940°C diminishes the dislocation and grain boundary strengthening gained from in-situ rolling but improves ductility by creating a more homogeneous lamellar structure. By combining in-situ rolling with subsequent heat treatment, the Ti–6Al–4V thin-wall/block components with excellent mechanical properties can be realized.

title: The optimized treatment strategy of dihydrolipoic acid-gold nanoclusters in burn wound care and macrophage polarization
abstract: Severe inflammation following a burn injury hampers tissue regeneration, and prolonged exposure to metallic nanomaterials raises safety concerns. However, bioinstructive scaffold surfaces have the potential to address these challenges effectively. Here, we engineered a functional delivery system by incorporating dihydrolipoic acid-capped gold nanoclusters (DHLA@AuNCs) into a porous lyophilized silk fibroin (SF) scaffold to provide sustained local nanocluster release and temporally defined exposure. Transmission electron microscopy showed ultrasmall DHLA@AuNCs without apparent aggregation, while the scaffold exhibited an interconnected porous architecture with an average pore size of 24.56 ± 3.73 μm. DHLA@AuNCs were released, reaching approximately 50 nM during days 3–5, a concentration shown to be well tolerated and biologically active in macrophages. DHLA@AuNCs predominantly suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophage activation rather than directly promoting an M2-like phenotype. Short-period DHLA@AuNC/SF exposure enhanced granulation tissue formation, collagen deposition, and neovascularization while reducing inflammation and apoptosis. DHLA@AuNCs primarily suppressed interferon-γ-induced pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization and attenuated IRF1/CXCL10-associated inflammatory signaling. These findings establish a functional link between scaffold-mediated DHLA@AuNC presentation, controlled exposure duration, macrophage regulation, and tissue regeneration, supporting DHLA@AuNC/SF as a material-based strategy for burn wound repair.

title: Enhanced creep resistance in nickel-based alloys via healing δ-phase precipitation at cavities
abstract: The creep resistance of Ni-based superalloys is fundamentally limited by the nucleation and growth of grain boundary cavities. This study presents an indepth experimental and computational study of self-healing strategy in a novel Ni-based alloy system, assisted cavity-growth retardation of creep cavities via site-specific precipitation of healing phase. The underlying mechanism, involving the formation of δ-Ni 3 Nb phase specifically at damage sites and its role in impeding cavity propagation, is systematically investigated. The higher healing-potential alloy (SH-High) consistently exhibits superior creep rupture life compared to lower-potential counterpart (SH-Low) across multiple stress levels, with a life exceeding approximately 40 h. Quantitative microstructural characterization reveals that SH-High develops small, elliptical cavities under high-stress creep, while SH-Low forms larger, irregular morphologies, with advanced microscopy confirming site-specific δ-phase precipitation at cavity edges. Benchmarked against a commercial non-self-healing alloy (SH-No) under identical thermomechanical conditions, SH-High alloy achieves significantly extended creep life at low stress, which correlates with markedly reduced average cavity size and cavity growth rate suppressed. Strain gradient-driven crystal plasticity simulations further elucidate the micromechanical mechanism: healing precipitates disrupt and discretize the localized deformation zones around cavities, introducing additional heterogeneous interfaces, which improve deformation coordination and effectively redistribute local stress–strain fields, collectively delaying crack propagation and coalescence.

title: Flow-accelerated corrosion of laser cladded 316L SS/X70 steel via LP-DED technique: surface and passive film characterisation in CO2-saturated oilfield environment
abstract: Laser surface cladding (LSC) via laser powder-directed energy deposition (LP-DED) improves the corrosion resistance of structural steels in aggressive environments. This study evaluates SS316L clads fabricated under varying laser parameters against flow-accelerated corrosion (FAC) in CO 2 -saturated simulated oilfield water. EBSD, electrochemical measurements, and post-FAC characterisation (SEM, 3D profilometry, XPS) establish links between microstructure, passive film stability, and degradation mechanisms. The clad produced at 300 W and 1200 mm/min shows a heterogeneous microstructure and poor corrosion resistance (C.R: 235.5 µm/Y), with severe localised attack, pitting, microcracking, and high surface roughness. XPS results point to a thin, unstable passive film and chromium depletion, driving repeated breakdown/repassivation cycles and rapid material loss. The clad fabricated at 500 W and 720 mm/min instead shows a refined, uniform microstructure and markedly better corrosion resistance (C.R: 23.5 µm/Y), attributed to a stable, chromium-rich passive film, lower defect density, and stronger metallurgical bonding. This optimised clad reduces the corrosion rate by nearly 10× compared to the lower-power condition and by over 140× compared to the API 5 L X70 substrate (C.R ≈ 3413.5 µm/Y), indicating a substantial gain in service life. Process parameters clearly govern clad quality and corrosion durability in corrosive environments.

title: Transition of toughening mechanisms governed by austenite deformation temperature in low-carbon martensitic stainless steel
abstract: To investigate the transition of toughening mechanisms governed by austenite deformation temperature, thermomechanical processing of 13Cr4Ni low-carbon martensitic stainless steel was systematically conducted. Microstructural analyses demonstrate that the deformed austenite state dictates the subsequent martensitic lath morphology and crack resistance. Deformation at 150 °C triggers intense variant selection and shear bands, provoking severe strain localization and a drastic low-temperature toughness deterioration via delamination fracture. In the warm-deformation regime, lath morphology controls crack-arrest capability. Rolling at 280 °C yields an interlocked lath configuration that effectively deflects cracks, whereas deformation at 400 °C is associated with a unidirectionally aligned lath configuration and stronger local strain/dislocation heterogeneity, reducing crack-arrest capability. At 650 °C, recovery-related substructure evolution and local boundary adjustment improve deformation compatibility and enhance crack-tip plastic accommodation. At 900 °C, the mixed morphology consisting of elongated prior-austenite grains and locally equiaxed grains, together with the increased fraction of high-angle boundaries, enhances crack-path tortuosity and boundary-mediated crack deflection. These results demonstrate that increasing deformation temperature drives a transition in fracture-control mechanism from strain-localization-induced embrittlement to lath-configuration-controlled crack propagation and finally to crack-tip-plasticity and boundary-network-mediated toughening.

title: Effective straight-segment length governs CNT/Cu thermal coupling in composites containing meandering CNTs
abstract: Copper composites reinforced with aligned carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are promising advanced heat-dissipation materials for semiconductor devices. In this study, finite volume method simulations were performed to systematically investigate the effects of CNT morphology and interface characteristics on the overall thermal conductivity of CNT/Cu composites. The simulations modeled CNT/Cu composites containing meandering CNTs with a characteristic length ranging from 0.1 to 40 μm, isolating the effects of CNT length, curvature, orientation, intrinsic thermal conductivity, and CNT/Cu interfacial thermal conductance. Results demonstrated that the effective straight-segment length (ESSL) of CNTs is the dominant factor governing heat transport. At short ESSLs, heat is conducted separately through the CNTs and the Cu matrix, resulting in a thermally decoupled state. However, increasing the ESSL triggers the transition to a thermally coupled state in which the CNTs effectively participate in heat transport, markedly enhancing the overall thermal conductivity. The critical ESSL required to achieve this thermally coupled state is closely related to the characteristic thermal transfer length. These findings establish structural guidelines for optimizing CNT networks to achieve maximum thermal performance in next-generation electronics.

title: Influence of crack initiation mechanisms on fatigue life dispersion in inconel 718 DA over a large temperature range
abstract: An analysis of 6035 direct-aged (DA) Inconel 718 fatigue tests examined fatigue life variability and its relationship with crack initiation mechanisms, across temperatures of 20, 200, 350, 450, 550, and . Fatigue life distributions displayed bimodal pattern between 200 and , consistent with two distinct lognormal populations, although formal mixture-distribution modelling was not performed. In the high cycle fatigue regime (HCF), scatter reached at least 1.5 decades and varied with temperature and stress amplitude. This scatter was statistically associated with temperature-dependent crack initiation mechanisms. Forging process factors may also have contributed, and a causal relationship was not established. Surface non-metallic inclusion (NMI) initiation predominated in the low-cycle fatigue (LCF) regime. In HCF, the predominant initiation site varied with temperature: surface crack initiation at , internal grain dominated at 200 and , and internal NMI occurred at 550 and . A mixed surface/internal competition was observed at coinciding with increased scatter. A qualitative comparison between crack initiation feature sizes and microstructural dimensions suggested that crack initiation occurred near the upper tail of the microstructural size distribution. A modified Murakami approach was applied to assess defect size and location effects on fatigue life.

title: Towards high performance and long-term stability: Strategies and challenges for zirconia ceramic stabilizers
abstract: Zirconia ceramics are critical in aerospace, biomedicine, and mechanical engineering due to their high hardness, strength, biocompatibility, and chemical stability. However, their long-term reliability faces low-temperature degradation (LTD), posing an irreconcilable trade‑off among strength, toughness, and aging resistance. This paper systematically reviews recent progress across three dimensions: defect engineering and stabilization, microstructural tailoring and mechanical optimization, and multilevel LTD protection strategies. Importantly, it explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence in breaking the trade‑off: machine learning interatomic potentials bridge first‑principles accuracy with large‑scale molecular dynamics; graph neural networks and active learning improve search efficiency in high‑dimensional compositional spaces by over an order of magnitude; and intelligent diagnostic frameworks combining nondestructive testing and deep learning enable dynamic prediction of degradation. The paper identifies that future breakthroughs hinge on the deep integration of fundamental mechanistic understanding, cross‑scale structural design, and AI‑driven rational paradigms. It also calls for standardized, open‑shared materials databases to support the shift from trial‑and‑error to data‑driven systems engineering, thereby offering a theoretical and practical roadmap for next‑generation high‑performance, long‑life zirconia‑based materials.

title: Polyphenols in infectious dental diseases: therapeutic applications and emerging material-based strategies
abstract: Infectious dental diseases, including dental caries, pulpitis, apical periodontitis, and periodontitis, represent a major global health burden and are characterized by complex interactions among pathogenic microorganisms, host immune responses, and tissue destruction. Although conventional treatments can reduce microbial load, their long-term efficacy is often limited by recurrent infection, antimicrobial resistance, dysregulated inflammation, and insufficient tissue regeneration, underscoring the urgent need for alternative strategies. To address this limitatiopns, polyphenols, a diverse class of dietary bioactive compounds with phenolic structures, have gained increasing attention due to their antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and regenerative properties. Beyond their intrinsic bioactivities, recent advances in biomaterials have enabled polyphenols to be incorporated into delivery systems or utilized as functional building blocks for hydrogels, self-assembled nanoplatforms, metal-phenolic networks, and multifunctional coatings, thereby improving their stability, bioavailability, and therapeutic performance. This review summarizes recent advances in the application of polyphenols for infectious dental diseases and highlights their emerging roles as direct bioactive agents, encapsulated therapeutics, and functional biomaterial building blocks. Collectively, these multifunctional strategies underscore the considerable potential of polyphenols for developing next-generation therapies for infectious dental diseases.

title: Full-field reconstruction of noisy DIC displacement fields beyond reliable measurement regions via a measurement-conditioned physics-informed neural network
abstract: This study presents a measurement-conditioned physics-informed framework for denoising digital image correlation (DIC) displacement fields within reliably measured regions and mechanically constrained completion where data are missing or unreliable. Spatial coordinates and a small number of selected DIC displacements are used as case-conditioning inputs to distinguish multiple field cases within a single network. Displacement-data fidelity constrains the measured region, while quasi-static equilibrium and boundary conditions constrain the data-excluded regions; both regions share a continuous network representation. Strain and stress fields are derived from the reconstructed displacement field through automatic differentiation and linear-elastic constitutive relations. The approach is evaluated using two finite-element-based DIC-like examples with 10% Gaussian noise and an experimental fatigue-crack-growth dataset for an AA2024-T3 M(T) specimen. The numerical examples provide clean references for quantitative assessment, while the experimental example examines applicability to measured DIC data. An ablation study comparing MSE, MAE, Huber, and Huber with self-adaptive weighting examines the influence of data-fidelity loss and adaptive point-wise weighting. The results demonstrate noise suppression within measured regions and spatial reconstruction near specimen boundaries, holes, and crack-affected regions excluded from the data-fidelity loss.

title: Contact characteristics of double-nut ball screws under the coupling of combined loads and screw bending
abstract: The double-nut ball screw (DNBS) is a critical rolling component in mechanical transmission systems. However, under complex working conditions, the coupling of axial-radial combined loads and screw bending leads to uneven load distribution and accelerated local wear, seriously affecting the positioning accuracy and service life of the transmission system. To accurately predict wear and service life, establishing a DNBS load distribution model that reflects multi-load coupling effects is essential. This paper proposes a DNBS contact load distribution model (CLM) considering the coupling between axial-radial load and screw bending. By incorporating nut displacement calculation and screw bending analysis, the CLM enables a more accurate representation of ball-raceway contact behavior under axial-radial load, yielding the full-ball contact loads. This model is validated through simulations and experiments. Further numerical analyses reveal how geometric deviations and nut position affect DNBS load distribution, identifying the evolution of the maximum contact load region. Finally, the influence of uneven radial load on the contact characteristics is examined. This study provides key theoretical support for wear and life prediction of DNBS.

title: Parametric geometrical framework for flattened tubular braided composite preforms: analytical formulations and micro-computed tomography assessment
abstract: Flattening transforms tubular braided preforms into closed, non-circular architectures that are not represented adequately by conventional cylindrical or planar braid models. This study develops a parametric analytical framework for generating three-dimensional yarn centerlines of flattened tubular braids using elliptical and race-track cross-sectional representations. The formulations use a closed arc-length coordinate and incorporate yarn number, braid angle, axial pitch, yarn-family direction, phase shift, and over–under displacement, with mathematical capability for 1/1, 2/2 and 3/3 interlacement patterns. The framework was assessed using one 32-yarn 2/2 specimen and one 16-yarn 1/1 specimen reconstructed by micro-computed tomography. Because specimen-level braid angle and flattened dimensions were used as model inputs, the assessment is conditional on measured geometry. For the 2/2 specimen, pooled centerline errors were 0.0856 mm for the elliptical model and 0.2569 mm for the race-track model. For the 1/1 specimen, the corresponding values were 0.2270 and 0.1666 mm. The lower-error representation therefore differed between the two tested configurations. Because the specimens also differed in yarn number, braid pattern, and morphology, these results do not establish a general model-selection criterion. The generated centerlines were transferred to complete solid-yarn computer-aided models for subsequent numerical analyses.

title: The effect of primary carbides on the fatigue properties and crack initiation mechanism of M50 bearing steel
abstract: Large-sized primary carbides have become the main factor inducing fatigue failure in M50 steel. This study systematically investigates the distinct roles of M2C and MC primary carbides in determining the rotating-bending fatigue properties of M50 steel through a combination of fatigue testing, microstructural characterization and finite element (FE) simulation. Statistical analysis of crack initiation sites reveals that M2C carbides induce fatigue failure at smaller sizes (8.85-20.61 μm) than MC carbides (18.82-36.99 μm), indicating their greater harmfulness. Empirical formulae correlating fatigue life with carbide size and stress amplitude are established, showing excellent agreement between predicted and experimental values. FE simulations demonstrate that the sharp-edged, rod-like morphology of M2C carbides leads to significantly higher stress concentration factors (up to 1.64) than those of ellipsoidal MC carbides (up to 1.36). Fracture surface characterization indicates that for both carbides, fatigue cracks initiate inside the primary carbides adjacent to the carbide-matrix interface and preferentially propagate within the carbide. In the early stage, when the crack propagates into the martensite matrix, the microstructure does not undergo significant changes, indicating that the formation of the fine granular area (FGA) is due to the mutual extrusion of the microstructures between the two sides of the crack.

title: Resource-aware direct ink writing of lunar regolith simulant pastes through milling-controlled rheology and activator reduction
abstract: Lunar construction requires processing routes that reduce imported consumables while retaining application-relevant printability and performance. This study developed a two-stage strategy for direct ink writing of alkali-activated CUG-LRS-1 pastes. In Stage I, milling for 1, 4, and 10 h yielded D 50 values of 25, 6, and 0.9 μm, respectively. Without a rheology modifier, prolonged milling enhanced viscosity recovery and time-dependent structural build-up. The 0.9 μm paste exhibited an apparent structural build-up rate, A thix , of 1.424 Pa/min, a printing window of 45–145 min, and a maximum of 43 layers before collapse. In Stage II, reducing the activator from 9 to 5 wt% (44.4%) produced 71.4% viscosity recovery and 32 layers before collapse. At 28 days, flexural strength decreased from 6.48 to 5.99 MPa, while compressive strength decreased from 45.03 to 15.15 MPa. XRD showed that the crystalline phases persisted, whereas FTIR and SEM revealed a less developed amorphous network and a less continuous matrix after activator reduction. Overall, milling history governed the time-dependent printing window, while activator dosage set the trade-off among material input, buildability, and strength. The results support application-specific formulation rather than maximizing strength alone.

title: Dilute Zn alloying in biodegradable Mg wires: microstructure, mechanical performance, and degradation behavior
abstract: Dilute Mg-Zn wires are of interest for biodegradable small-bone fixation as magnesium degradation can support bone healing, while low zinc additions may provide biological benefit without compromising biocompatibility. The influence of Zn content below the room-temperature solubility limit was assessed in Mg-Zn wires intended for resorbable implant applications. Mg-0.4Zn, Mg-0.6Zn, Mg-0.8Zn, and Mg-1.5Zn alloys were processed by single-step direct hot extrusion into thin wires and characterized via correlative microstructural analysis, tensile testing, bending experiments, and in vitro degradation. All compositions achieved a recrystallized equiaxed grain size of 5.0–5.9 µm and exhibited ultimate tensile strengths of 246–256 MPa with elongations of 23–28 %. Zn content had only a limited effect on grain size and ultimate tensile strength, whereas the 0.2 % proof stress was higher for Mg-0.4Zn and Mg-0.6Zn, which exhibited a pronounced sharp yield point. Bending of Mg-0.6Zn and Mg-1.5Zn was governed mainly by extrusion texture and preserved reversible plasticity through twinning and detwinning. Simulated body fluid caused rapid, localized degradation and loss of mechanical integrity within 7 days, whereas an application-relevant medium (DMEM + FBS) resulted in slower degradation and higher retained strength. These findings support dilute Mg-Zn wires as a material platform for future resorbable bone fixation devices

title: Architecting core–shell Si3N4@CuO interfaces to resolve nanoparticle agglomeration and dramatically elevate the shear strength of Sn58Bi solders
abstract: To address the issues of agglomeration and weak interfacial bonding of Si 3 N 4 particles within the solder, core–shell structures were introduced to enhance the performance of the Si 3 N 4 particles. A series of Si 3 N 4 @CuO x (SC x ) particles ( x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4) was prepared by coating CuO thin films onto the Si 3 N 4 particles, and the effects of these SC x particles on the properties of Sn58Bi solder were evaluated through experimental characterization. Experimental results indicated that SC particles, while retaining the advantages of Si 3 N 4 NPs, were also embedded more uniformly within the solder matrix. This led to the introduction of more grain boundaries and dislocations, thereby improving the microstructure and mechanical performance of the solder joints. However, a higher Cu content in the SC particles led to their accumulation above the intermetallic compound (IMC) layer, adversely affecting joint properties. Among all the tested samples, the Sn58Bi-SC3 solder joint exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a shear strength of 67.9 MPa, a 62.8% increase over the SC particle-free solder joint.

title: A high-modification monophasic hyaluronic acid hydrogel promotes aged-skin regeneration associated with mitochondrial bioenergetic and redox recovery
abstract: Current cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers face an application-dependent trade-off among persistence, mechanical compliance, tissue integration, and regenerative activity. Here, a 20 mg/mL high-modification monophasic HA hydrogel (HM-HA) was developed by combining extensive BDDE modification with homogenization and compared with two commercial biphasic fillers. HM-HA exhibited a degree of modification of 30%, compared with 22% and 21% for CP-1 and CP-2, while its storage modulus at 5 Hz was approximately 330 Pa versus 920 and 950 Pa. Its swelling factor was approximately 3.4 versus 2.6 and 2.8, and complete degradation in an accelerated hyaluronidase assay occurred at 6 h versus 5 h. In D-galactose-induced cellular senescence, HM-HA reduced ROS-associated fluorescence by 54% and decreased SA-β-gal-positive cells from more than 80% to 25% (p < 0.0001). In aged rats, HM-HA maintained a coherent implant contour for 28 days, restored collagen to the normal level (p > 0.05), and induced less inflammation and fibrous encapsulation than the commercial comparators. Transcriptomic, redox, and mitochondrial analyses associated HM-HA treatment with extracellular-matrix remodeling, improved antioxidant defense, and recovery of mitochondrial function. Collectively, monophasic network engineering combined high chemical modification with compliant mechanics and short-term structural persistence while supporting tissue regenerative responses.

title: Coupled optimization of soft-magnetic, electrical, and mechanical properties through controlled nanocrystallization in Fe-P-B-C amorphous alloys
abstract: Fe-based amorphous alloys are promising for high-frequency motor cores owing to their intrinsically low core loss. However, annealing required for magnetic optimization can induce nanocrystallization, leading to trade-offs among saturation magnetization, electrical resistivity, and mechanical reliability. Here, a quantitative framework is established to correlate crystallized volume fraction ( V c ) and nanograin size with the coupled evolution of magnetic, electrical, and mechanical properties in Fe-P-B-C amorphous alloys by varying the P/B ratio and annealing temperature. A bendable Fe 86 P 6 B 6 C 2 amorphous alloy (94.6 wt% Fe), annealed 40 K below the onset of primary crystallization, exhibits ultralow coercivity (1.9 A/m), high saturation magnetization (1.734 T), high electrical resistivity (154.8 μΩ·cm), and reliable tensile behavior with a high Weibull modulus (14.2). This balance is associated with a continuous, high-resistivity amorphous matrix containing uniformly dispersed α-Fe nanocrystals that are predominantly smaller than 5 nm. Further nanocrystallization increases saturation magnetization but causes an abrupt resistivity drop near V c of ∼26%, whereas tensile reliability deteriorates at ∼6%, revealing distinct microstructural thresholds governing electromagnetic and mechanical trade-offs. Supported by performance-cost analysis, these findings establish a threshold-guided strategy for designing affordable Fe-based soft magnetic alloys with balanced performance for next-generation high-frequency electrical machines.

title: Cold plasma-induced fragmentation and surface modification of polystyrene microplastics in aqueous systems
abstract: Cold plasma offers a reagent-free route for modifying persistent polymer particles, but fragmentation must be distinguished from chemical destruction. Here, polystyrene microplastics were examined in a recirculating air-plasma water reactor at 22–40 °C. A 1 μm fraction (1 mg L −1 ) was used for time-resolved analysis, while a 10 μm fraction (100 mg L −1 ) provided a supplementary qualitative assessment under a different polymer loading. Dynamic light scattering, turbidity, flow cytometry, electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy showed progressive particle-size redistribution, loss of spherical morphology, surface roughening, and moderate spectral changes consistent with surface modification. For the 1 μm suspension, the mean hydrodynamic diameter decreased from approximately 1.02 μm to 94 nm within 20 min. An empirical first-order fit described the diameter redistribution (k app approximately 0.12 min −1 ), but this parameter does not represent an intrinsic chemical degradation rate. The 10 μm particles showed slower transformation into lower-micrometre fractions; direct quantitative size comparison is limited by the different initial polymer loadings and the upper measurement range of dynamic light scattering. The results demonstrate fragmentation and surface modification rather than mineralization and support considering cold plasma as a potential pretreatment before downstream separation or further oxidation.

title: Spatiotemporal control of drug release on implant surfaces for simultaneous infection inhibition and osseointegration
abstract: Permanent orthopedic and dental implants fail through two mechanistically linked yet temporally distinct pathways: early bacterial colonization that matures into biofilm-protected infection, and insufficient long-term bone anchorage. Because contaminating bacteria and host cells compete for the same freshly implanted surface, a coating optimized only for antibacterial potency frequently compromises osteogenesis, whereas a purely osteoconductive surface invites colonization. This review argues that resolving this conflict requires controlling not merely what an implant releases, but precisely when and where it releases it. We define spatiotemporal control as the engineering of a distinct release program for each anatomical region of a device, and use that criterion to separate genuinely spatiotemporal designs from static dual-function, purely temporal and purely spatial coatings. Against the biological timeline and the two-zone anatomy of peri-implant healing, we compare temporal architectures, region-specific functionalization, and integrated platforms in which macrophage-centered osteoimmunomodulation couples early antibacterial defense to late bone formation, and we set out the quantitative, preclinical and regulatory barriers that still separate these designs from clinical use.

title: Surface acoustic wave-assisted printing of complex three-dimensional magnetic impeller for motion control
abstract: Magnetic components are widely utilized in soft robotics, their precise geometry and strong magnetic responsiveness are generally essential. The fabrication of magnetic components is technically challenging, conventional fabrication methods struggle to simultaneously achieve complex structures and programmable patterning of embedded magnetic fillers. Herein, an approach using surface acoustic wave (SAW)-induced magnetic microparticle’s patterning and stepwise layered photopolymerization is presented for the printing of complex magnetic components. By dynamically adjusting photocuring region, complex magnetic components like magnetic impeller with spatially controlled magnetic particles’ arrangement and magnetic-moment alignment was printed as a function demonstrator. Under rotating magnetic field, the printed impeller exhibited stable combined planar motion with tunable orbital radius and rotational speed, successfully completing a 320 mm trajectory through a maze in 66 s. Additionally, leveraging tailored 3D geometry and programmed magnetic particle alignment, magnetic impeller can achieve the movement along a tube under the propulsion of an axially translating magnetic field, typically at 40 mT magnetic field intensity, stable motion over an axial velocity range of 3.30–23.44 mm/s can be obtained. The results demonstrated that our printing process can be used to print complex magnetic components with the potential for advanced soft robotics applications.

title: 3D-Printed architected fillers in soft composite matrices: A systematic framework for geometry-dependent mechanical characterisation
abstract: A fundamental gap persists in composite materials science: how do fillers behave mechanically in the 300–1000 µm regime? This size range is largely inaccessible, trapped between colloidal synthesis and conventional machining. Using digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing, we fabricated cubes and tetrapods at two size classes (0.03–0.05 mm 3 and 1 mm 3 ) and embedded them into polydimethylsiloxane matrices spanning a 6.5-fold stiffness range.
