Experiments were conducted on body-centered cubic (BCC). Error of the equivalent properties of conformal lattice was reduced to 2.16%. High precision predicted displacement field was achieved, and the maximum displacement error was reduced to 2–3%. Consistent vibration mode form was obtained with a natural frequency error of less than 1%. Computation time was shortened by 2–3 orders of magnitude, and the analysis of large-scale conformal lattice structure which cannot be handled by conventional FE models, was enabled by the proposed method.

title: Optical, dielectric, and conductivity properties of Bi2O3/Fe2O3-doped PVOH/SA nanocomposites for potential optoelectronic applications
abstract: The development of polymer nanocomposites with tailored optical, electrical, and dielectric properties is important for emerging optoelectronic and energy-storage technologies. In this study, PVOH/SA-Bi 2 O 3 /Fe 2 O 3 nanocomposite films were prepared by a simple solution-casting method using different concentrations of Bi 2 O 3 /Fe 2 O 3 nanoparticles (0.0, 0.5, 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 wt%). The structural, optical, electrical, and dielectric properties of the resulting films were systematically investigated. X-ray diffraction confirmed the incorporation of the hybrid nanoparticles and revealed a reduction in polymer crystallinity, while FT-IR analysis indicated intermolecular interactions and hydrogen bonding between the polymer matrix and nanofillers. Increasing the Bi 2 O 3 /Fe 2 O 3 content enhanced the optical absorption and absorption coefficient and reduced the direct and indirect optical band gaps from 4.68 to 3.87 eV and from 3.83 to 3.01 eV, respectively. The AC conductivity increased from 1.98 × 10 −11 to 1.87 × 10 −9 S/cm at 100 Hz. The dielectric constant also increased with nanoparticle loading, consistent with enhanced interfacial polarization and charge accumulation. These findings demonstrate that Bi 2 O 3 /Fe 2 O 3 incorporation provides an effective means of tuning the optical, dielectric, and electrical properties of PVOH/SA nanocomposites.

title: Elemental powder blending with graphene nanoplatelets for laser beam powder bed fusion of Cu–Ni–Si alloys
abstract: Copper alloys are challenging to process by near-infrared laser beam powder bed fusion (LB-PBF) owing to high reflectance and thermal conductivity. Here, we demonstrate graphene-assisted elemental powder blending as a compositionally flexible feedstock strategy for Cu–Ni–Si(–Cr) alloys. Trace graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs), introduced before elemental alloying additions, reduced powder reflectance while maintaining compositional flexibility. FLOW-3D simulations using absorptivity inputs derived from measured powder reflectance showed that higher absorptivity promoted deeper Cu melt-pool formation. Multiple compositions achieved relative and areal densities exceeding 99.6 %, while the baseline alloy attained a yield strength of 212 ± 4 MPa and uniform elongation of 23.8 ± 1.3 %. Microstructural analysis revealed dislocation-cell structures without evidence of dominant Ni–Si precipitation. STEM-EELS, HRTEM and Raman spectroscopy indicated locally modified GNP-derived carbon with retained sp 2 /graphitic character. Excess GNP reduced densification despite lowering reflectance further, highlighting the importance of a practical addition window. Powder reused once without sieving retained near-full density but exhibited reduced tensile properties. These findings establish a practical route to dense, compositionally tunable Cu alloys using conventional near-infrared LB-PBF.

title: Experimental investigation and modeling of local deformation heterogeneity and continuous dynamic recrystallization in ZM21 alloy during electrically assisted tensile deformation
abstract: Electrically assisted forming (EAF) involves complex electro-thermo-mechanical coupling and heterogeneous local deformation, which may influence continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) behavior of magnesium alloys at elevated temperatures. However, the coupling between local deformation heterogeneity and the CDRX mechanism during EAF remains insufficiently understood. In this study, the local deformation characteristics and CDRX behavior of ZM21 alloy during EAF were investigated through a combination of experiments and modeling. The results revealed pronounced deformation heterogeneity, particularly in the gauge-center region, where increasing local strain rate and current density were accompanied by flow softening, progressive grain refinement, and distinctive low-angle grain boundary (LAB) evolution. Based on these observations, a CDRX-EAF framework was developed by incorporating dislocation evolution, grain boundary evolution, and electrically assisted deformation behavior. The framework reproduced the principal trends in flow behavior, grain size evolution, and LAB fraction evolution under various deformation conditions. It also captured regional differences in CDRX progression under a representative condition. Model-predicted dislocation evolution further suggests that the coupled evolution of local strain rate and current density is associated with the distinctive LAB evolution and regional CDRX behavior. These results provide insight into the relationship between local electro-thermo-mechanical histories and microstructural evolution during EAF.

title: Neutron scattering reveals magnetic field-induced microparticle restructuring in densely packed magnetoactive elastomers
abstract: Magnetoactive elastomers (MAEs) exhibit large magnetic-field-dependent changes in mechanical and surface properties, yet the underlying particle-scale mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. In this work, ultra-small-angle neutron scattering (USANS) is used to probe in situ filler-particle restructuring in MAEs under applied magnetic fields. Measurements on thin-film samples with 30~wt\% and 75~wt\% carbonyl iron particles access structural correlations in the range of 0.2–30~\textmu m.Analysis using multilevel Guinier–Porod models reveals hierarchical structuring and concentration-dependent characteristic length scales, while also revealing limitations related to size polydispersity, structure factors, and magnetic scattering. Field-dependent measurements show, for the first time, anisotropic changes in the scattering signal, with distinct behavior parallel and perpendicular to the applied field. Intermediate length-scale changes are attributed to particle rearrangement, whereas high-$q$ features are dominated by magnetic scattering.Monte Carlo simulations with dipolar interactions reproduce the measured anisotropy and indicate that particle displacements are small and only weakly anisotropic. This suggests that particle chaining is unlikely under moderate magnetic field strengths (<300~kA/m) and given mechanical constraints.These results demonstrate the potential of USANS to probe mesoscale restructuring in MAEs and provide insight into the interplay between particle organization, magnetic interactions, and elastic deformations.

title: Dual-functional triamine treatment of SnO2 electron transport layer for simultaneous improvement of efficiency and stability in perovskite solar cells
abstract: The superior properties of tin oxide (SnO 2 ) such as its low temperature for synthesis and deposition, high transparency, high chemical and UV-stability, and high electron mobility, has introduced it as a promising electron transport layer (ETL) in planar perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, its high defect density and the deeper conduction band (CB) energy level are considered as the challenges for this application. In this work, diethylenetriamine (DETA) is employed as an ion chelation agent to effectively passivate defects on the SnO 2 ETL surface and at the SnO 2 /perovskite interface, utilizing its three high-potential functional groups (primary and secondary amines) to coordinate with undercoordinated sites and neutralize charged traps. Surface modification with DETA leads to a substantial improvement in device performance, increasing the power conversion efficiency from 13.90% to 15.02% in P3HT-based devices and from 15.05% to 17.76% in Spiro–OMeTAD-based devices. The lone pair electrons in the amine groups can passivate defects by interacting with oxygen vacancies, while simultaneously influencing the perovskite layer by increasing grain size and reducing pinholes. Additionally, the treated devices exhibit enhanced dark, light, and thermal stability, highlighting the effectiveness of DETA modification for advancing SnO 2 -based PSCs.

title: Study on material rebound characteristics of shotcrete: A review
abstract: Reducing material rebound while improving deposition efficiency and the quality of the sprayed layer remains a key challenge in shotcrete engineering. This review systematically examines shotcrete rebound characteristics at the macro-level, meso-level and micro-level. Particular attention is given to a central unresolved issue: reported optimum rebound-control parameters vary substantially among studies, while the mechanistic links between macroscopic process/material variables and particle-scale impact–adhesion behavior remain insufficiently established. First, the effects of spraying processes, material composition, and environmental conditions on rebound are critically analyzed, with emphasis on their condition dependence and underlying mechanisms. Second, the rebound mechanisms of aggregate particles and concrete jet flow upon impact are discussed, together with their relationships to mesoscopic accumulation behavior and microstructural evolution of the deposited layer. The need to establish quantitative cross-scale links among process parameters, rheological properties, impact mechanics, interfacial retention, and macroscopic rebound is further highlighted. Finally, future research priorities and the feasibility of engineering “shotcrete zero-rebound” are discussed. This review provides a cross-scale framework for understanding shotcrete rebound and offers theoretical guidance for low-rebound material design, process optimization, and improved engineering performance.

title: A magnesium-engineered nanoporous MXene/GelMA hydrogel platform for photothermal eradication of bacteria and accelerated bone healing
abstract: Bone defect repair remains clinically challenging because of insufficient osteogenic regeneration and the potential risk of postoperative infection. Developing multifunctional biomaterials that integrate osteogenic regulation with antibacterial potential is highly desirable. In this study, a magnesium-engineered nanoporous MXene/GelMA hydrogel, termed nMX/Gel, was constructed by incorporating microwave-assisted combustion engineered nMX into a GelMA hydrogel matrix. Compared with conventional MXene/GelMA hydrogel (MX/Gel), nMX/Gel exhibited enhanced photothermal performance under 1064 nm near-infrared irradiation. In vitro antibacterial assays showed that nMX effectively inhibited the growth of Escherichia coli and S. aureus upon near-infrared irradiation, confirming its photothermal antibacterial potential. Furthermore, nMX/Gel showed favorable cytocompatibility and promoted MC3T3-E1 cell proliferation. In addition, nMX/Gel significantly upregulated the expression of osteogenesis-related genes, including ALP, RUNX2, and OPN, in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. In a rat femoral defect model, micro-CT, histological staining, and immunohistochemical analyses further confirmed that nMX/Gel markedly enhanced new bone formation, collagen deposition, and the expression of osteogenic markers OCN and OPN. Overall, this designed nMX/Gel hydrogel provides a promising multifunctional biomaterial strategy for bone defect repair by combining enhanced osteogenic activity with photothermal antibacterial potential.

title: Origin of thermal-expansion anomalies in Mo-containing high-entropy diborides: A machine-learning interatomic potential study of MoB2 and (Mo,Nb,Zr,Ta,Ti)B2
abstract: Mo-containing high-entropy diborides (HEBs) show processing-dependent thermal expansion: pressure-densified samples expand monotonically, whereas pressureless-sintered ones show an apparent c-axis contraction above 873 K, an effect attributed to incomplete chemical homogenisation. We identify its origin with active-learned machine-learning interatomic potentials for (Mo,Nb,Zr,Ta,Ti)B 2 and MoB 2 , validated against density-functional theory and literature data. The anomaly originates in the metastable AlB 2 -type end-member α-MoB 2 , a kinetically trapped local free-energy minimum whose c-axis expands at a third of the HEB rate (≈3 × 10 −6 K −1 against 9–10 × 10 −6 K −1 ) while remaining positive. Presence of other metals removes the anomaly in the homogeneous solid solution, which expands almost isotropically. When homogenisation is incomplete, coherent Mo-rich domains accumulate 2–3 GPa of mismatch stress and microcrack beyond a few micrometres; their progressive decoupling on heating lowers the average lattice parameter c, appearing in diffraction as a contraction. Chemical homogeneity therefore controls the microcrack-free thermal expansion of Mo-bearing HEBs.

title: Quantifying ceramic hollow sphere network connectivity in bimodal aluminum matrix syntactic foams: Linking 3D architecture to crack propagation
abstract: Aluminum matrix syntactic foams reinforced with ceramic hollow spheres (CHSs) were investigated to determine how the three-dimensional connectivity of the large-sphere subnetwork influences early crack trajectories under compression. Four bimodal configurations containing 7.0 mm and 2.4 mm CHSs at volume ratios of 4:1, 2:1, 1:1, and 1:2 were fabricated by infiltration casting and examined by micro-computed tomography before and during compressive loading. The large CHSs were reconstructed in three dimensions, and their spatial organization was evaluated using agglomerative hierarchical clustering with complete linkage. The dendrograms revealed a characteristic transition between local and inter-cluster length scales at approximately 6–7 mm. These length scales were subsequently used to evaluate network connectivity through connected component analysis. The large CHS rich 4:1 configuration formed a dominant sample-scale connected network, associated with the experimentally observed diagonal crack trajectory. In contrast, decreasing the large CHS content produced progressively more fragmented networks and predominantly lateral crack propagation. The results demonstrate that hierarchical length scale analysis combined with quantitative network descriptors provides a physically interpretable link between three-dimensional filler architecture and observed failure behavior. The proposed framework provides a computationally simple basis for evaluating reinforcement configurations and for future design-oriented control of failure paths in syntactic foams.

title: Ecodesign of solar panels mitigating temperature gradients and hotspots
abstract: Conventional photovoltaic modules rely on crosslinked polymer encapsulants that cause localized overheating and ultimately limit end-of-life recyclability. This study presents an effective encapsulation design based on an inert liquid material that 1) enables easy separation of the module components for reuse and 2) redistributes heat within the module. Conventional photovoltaic modules rely on crosslinked polymer encapsulants that cause localized overheating and ultimately limit end-of-life recyclability. This contribution focuses on an ecodesign for solar panels based on liquid dimethylpolysiloxane (PDMS). This novel encapsulation mitigates temperature gradients and suppresses hotspot formation, one of the challenges in silicon modules. Thermal imaging reveals a more uniform heat distribution in liquid-encapsulated cells compared to conventional ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA)-based structures, despite similar intrinsic thermal conductivities. These results highlight the critical role of convective and interfacial heat transfer mechanisms, which are absent in solid encapsulation systems. Outdoor testing under harsh Nordic conditions for 260 days demonstrates stable device performance (initial 17.66%, after aging 18.26%), confirming that liquid encapsulation can also provide effective environmental protection. Most importantly, the non-crosslinked nature of the encapsulant allows complete module disassembly via a simple approach, preserving material quality for reuse. The material recovery with this encapsulation is shown to be effective while requiring less than 1% of that needed for conventional approaches. This liquid encapsulation offers improved thermal regulation, which could extend device lifetime, and enable full end-of-life recyclability.

title: Self-evolving digital twin with federated reinforcement learning for autonomous process–property optimization in polymer nanocomposite manufacturing systems
abstract: Rapid growth of polymer nanocomposite manufacturing demands intelligent systems capable of accurately predicting multi-property behavior and autonomously optimizing process conditions across heterogeneous industrial environments. Existing Digital Twin (DT) and machine learning approaches often suffer from centralized data dependency, limited generalization under non-IID conditions, and an inability to adaptively optimize process parameters in real time. To address these constraints, this study proposes a Self-Evolving Digital Twin framework integrating a Neural Adaptive Fusion Transformer (NAF-Transformer), FedAdam-based federated learning, and a Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) reinforcement learning agent. The model is implemented using Python, PyTorch, Gym, NumPy, and executed on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. The system is trained on the Nanocomposites Properties Dataset (Kaggle), comprising key manufacturing inputs such as filler loading, temperature, mixing time, and curing conditions. The proposed DT demonstrates exceptional predictive performance, achieving R 2 = 0.978 and RMSE = 0.085, outperforming state-of-the-art FL–DT studies by 12–18% accuracy improvement. Federated aggregation enhances global model generalization by 10% compared to local DTs, while the TD3 agent optimizes process parameters such as temperature and mixing time, resulting in material property improvements of up to 15.3% in tensile strength, 10.2% in modulus, and 7.5% in thermal stability. The unified DT–FedAdam–TD3 architecture enables adaptive model updating, data-local federated learning, and autonomous multi-objective optimization. Overall, this study introduces a powerful, scalable, DT framework capable of continuous self-evolution, offering a significant leap beyond existing predictive or rule-based control strategies in polymer nanocomposite manufacturing.

title: Exosome-loaded hydrogel by optimizing cellular functions to enhance diabetic wound healing
abstract: Wound healing is a clinically critical process often hindered by persistent inflammation, reduced cellular regenerative capacity, and impaired tissue repair. Exosomes, as nanosized vesicles enriched with bioactive molecules such as growth factors, proteins and miRNAs, hold great promise for promoting tissue regeneration. However, their clinical translation is significantly hindered by challenges such as rapid clearance, structural instability and transient therapeutic effects. To address these limitations, we developed an injectable exosome-integrated hydrogel (Exo@CSGA-HA) for local encapsulation and sustained delivery of exosomes. This hydrogel was constructed by crosslinking gallic acid-modified chitosan (CSGA) with aldehyde-functionalized hyaluronic acid (HA-ALD), endowing the platform with intrinsic antioxidant and antibacterial properties. Crucially, the resulting Exo@CSGA-HA hydrogel exhibits excellent mechanical strength, tissue adhesion, and self-healing capabilities and enables prolonged local delivery of exosome-associated components. In vivo results revealed that Exo@CSGA-HA hydrogel significantly promoted diabetic wound repair, characterized by enhanced healing rates, increased collagen deposition, and extensive neovascular formation. Mechanistically, the hydrogel provides an antioxidant microenvironment favorable to the delivered exosomes and wound-resident cells, while its treatment is also associated with increased TGF-β expression. This dual-action approach significantly enhances extracellular matrix synthesis (type I and type III collagen), promotes rapid re-epithelialization, and facilitates robust dermal remodeling. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of Exo@CSGA-HA hydrogel in promoting diabetic wound repair.

title: Evolutionary machine learning for thermophysical property modeling and materials design of CNT–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids
abstract: Hybrid nanofluids incorporating carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and metal oxide nanoparticles have emerged as advanced functional nanomaterials for thermal management because of their tunable thermophysical properties and synergistic nanoparticle interactions. However, the strong nonlinear dependence of their density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and specific heat capacity on nanoparticle composition and concentration complicates accurate property prediction and materials design. In this study, an evolutionary machine learning framework is developed to establish composition–property relationships for aqueous CNT–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids. A multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) coupled with a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to optimize the network architecture and learning parameters and to predict four key thermophysical properties, namely density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and specific heat capacity. The predictive performance of the evolutionary GA–MLPNN model is systematically benchmarked against Gaussian process regression (GPR) and classification and regression tree (CART) models. The results demonstrate that GA–MLPNN provides highly accurate predictions for all investigated properties, achieving correlation coefficients above 0.998 for density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity and reaching 0.9999 for specific heat capacity. The analysis further reveals distinct composition–property relationships: nanoparticle volume fraction is the principal factor controlling density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity, whereas the specific heat capacity is strongly associated with the thermal capacity contributions of the constituent phases. These results demonstrate that evolutionary learning can effectively capture the complex property landscape of CNT–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids and provide an efficient route for thermophysical property estimation without extensive additional experimentation. The proposed framework establishes a materials-oriented computational strategy for screening and designing hybrid nanofluids with tailored thermophysical properties for advanced thermal-management and energy-related applications.

title: Macrophage-targeted engineered extracellular vesicles released from GelMA hydrogel for diabetic wound healing via regulating macrophage heterogeneity
abstract: The impaired healing of chronic diabetic wounds caused by excessive inflammation presents a significant clinical challenge. In this study, we constructed macrophage-targeted extracellular vesicles modified with dextran sulfate (DS-EVs) using MGL-guided bioorthogonal click chemistry and embedded these engineered DS-EVs within GelMA hydrogel to generate an injectable wound therapeutic dressing. In vitro results demonstrated that DS-EVs targeted and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 to regenerative M2 phenotypes, exerting anti-inflammation and angiogenesis effects. Proteomic and transcriptomic sequencing revealed the excellent effects of DS-EVs in repairing chronic diabetic wounds through the delivery of microRNA(miR)-221, which further suppressed CXCR3 production and suppress the CXCL10/NF-κB signaling pathway. In vivo results demonstrated that DS-EVs accelerated diabetic wound healing by promoting neovascularization and alleviating persistent inflammation. Collectively, this work identifies DS-EVs as an effective therapeutic strategy for chronic diabetic wounds, which functions by dual regulation of angiogenesis and macrophage phenotypic switching to remodel the diabetic wound microenvironment.

title: Shape design of stretching- and bending-dominated lattice columns for Wire-and-Arc Additive Manufacturing
abstract: Wire-and-Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) enables the fabrication of lattice meso-elements made of spatial networks of thin branches. In stretching-dominated lattices, members primarily carry loads through axial tension and compression, providing high stiffness-to-weight ratios that are well-suited for lightweight structural components requiring high rigidity. In contrast, bending-dominated lattices deform mainly through flexural actions. Although less efficient in terms of stiffness, they are more deformable and therefore advantageous in other applications. In this contribution, an energy-based computational framework is implemented to automatically design shape-optimized lattice columns for robotic fabrication. The lattice geometry is described through a low-dimensional Hermite-spline parametrization, which is explicitly constrained by WAAM overhang and printability limits, enabling automation-ready shape generation without manual redesign. A minimum compliance optimization procedure is employed to generate stretching-dominated lattice spatial structures, whereas a compliance-constrained maximization of the bending contribution to the overall strain energy is devised to achieve bending-dominated layouts. The numerical studies on meso-columns under central and eccentric loads, together with a WAAM-produced prototype, demonstrate the feasibility of the digital design and fabrication workflow for a new generation of steel structures.

title: Zn-Ce nanocomposites reprogram macrophages via ROS scavenging and autophagy promotion for enhanced diabetic burn wound healing
abstract: Diabetic burns represent one of the most challenging wound types in clinical dermatology, with delayed healing primarily attributed to excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and impaired autophagy within the wound microenvironment. High ROS causes mitochondrial damage, while suppressed autophagy prevents clearance of damaged mitochondria, creating a cycle that promotes pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization and hinders healing. To target both pathways, we developed zinc-cerium composite nanoparticles (Zn-Ce NPs) via hydrothermal doping. These NPs were designed to combine cerium’s ROS-scavenging and zinc’s autophagy-enhancing properties, alleviating oxidative stress, improving mitochondrial quality, and shifting macrophages from M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 phenotypes. Our results demonstrate that Zn-Ce NPs significantly reduce intracellular ROS levels, enhance autophagic flux, facilitate the clearance of damaged mitochondria while promoting a shift toward fusion-dominated mitochondrial dynamics, and ultimately induce M2 macrophage polarization. Conditioned media from treated macrophages enhanced HUVEC migration and tube formation. In diabetic mice with dorsal burns, topical Zn-Ce NPs reduced inflammation, stimulated angiogenesis and collagen deposition, and accelerated wound closure. The nanosystem effectively breaks the ROS-autophagy dysfunction cycle, reprograms the wound microenvironment, and promotes repair. This dual-functional strategy—simultaneously scavenging ROS and restoring autophagy—represents a promising approach for treating diabetic burns, offering potential clinical translation in managing chronic wounds.

title: Engineering design of thermoplastic-based ternary hybrid composites with tunable electromagnetic shielding and microwave absorption performance
abstract: This study reports the engineering design and performance validation of thermoplastic ternary hybrid composites for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and microwave absorption. Using a complete mixture design, acrylonitrile–butadiene–styrene (ABS) was reinforced with nanosized graphite (nGra), carbonyl iron (Fe), and carbon black (CB) at a fixed 30 wt% total loading. Composites were manufactured via industrially relevant melt mixing and compression molding to systematically map processability and mechanical response to functional outcomes. Electromagnetic attenuation was evaluated using complementary rectangular waveguide (X-band) and coaxial transmission line (broadband) techniques, highlighting the critical influence of measurement geometry on observed performance. Driven by synergistic conductive network formation, a binary nGra/CB (15/15 wt%) composite achieved an EMI shielding effectiveness of 45 dB at 10 GHz (thickness of 2.5 mm, 18 dB/mm) while maintaining some mechanical properties and processability under tested conditions. Furthermore, hybrid systems incorporating Fe demonstrated tunable microwave absorption, achieving reflection losses below −16 dB over the 8–17 GHz range, which was further enhanced through experimentally validated multilayer architectures. By correlating complex electromagnetic properties with statistical mixture evaluation, this work establishes clear engineering pathways for designing manufacturable, thermoplastic-based, and multifunctional composites suitable for advanced aerospace, stealth, and electronic applications.

title: Gradient structure-mediated regulation of phase transformation behavior and elastocaloric effect in TiNiCu shape memory alloys
abstract: To address the challenge of simultaneously optimizing adiabatic temperature change, cooling efficiency, and cyclic stability in TiNiCu shape memory alloys, a spatially controllable gradient-microstructure design strategy is adopted. Laser surface treatment is employed to construct gradient structures in cold-rolled TiNiCu alloys, and the correlations among microstructural evolution, phase transformation behavior, mechanical response, and elastocaloric effect are systematically investigated. The typical microstructure can be generally divided into a surface coarse-grained region formed by laser treatment, an internally transitioned fine-grained region within the heat-affected zone, and a cold-rolled deformed matrix in the core. The deeply modified gradient structure leads to asynchronous thermally induced martensitic transformation behavior and promotes plateau-type stress-induced martensitic transformation behavior. Moreover, different gradient configurations show distinct advantages in adiabatic temperature change and cooling efficiency. At 3 % strain, the deeply modified gradient structure exhibits the highest adiabatic temperature change, remaining stable at approximately 13.5 K after cycling, whereas the moderately modified gradient structure shows the highest coefficient of performance, remaining stable at 14.7 after cycling. These results demonstrate that gradient-structure design can effectively regulate the phase transformation behavior, mechanical response, and elastocaloric response of TiNiCu alloys, and provide a viable microstructural design route for the targeted optimization of elastocaloric properties.

title: Effect of calcium content on the bioactivity, degradation, and osteogenic activity of multi-ion loaded SBA-15 rods
abstract: SBA-15-based materials have attracted considerable attention for skeletal tissue regeneration owing to their tunable structure, high surface area, versatile functionalization capability, and osteogenic potential. In this study, SBA-15 particles loaded with multiple therapeutic ions were successfully synthesized using varying calcium (Ca 2+ ) contents and fixed phosphate (PO 4 3- ) and copper (Cu 2+ ) concentrations. Physicochemical characterization confirmed the incorporation and homogeneous distribution of the loaded species while preserving the structural integrity and textural properties of SBA-15. Elevated carbon levels detected in the modified samples may originate from residual carbon-containing species associated with the Cu/L-ascorbic acid (AsAc) complex. Bioactivity increased with Ca 2+ content, promoting the rapid formation of crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAp)-like structures upon immersion in simulated body fluid (SBF). Following 30 days in TRIS-HCl, the multi-ion-loaded materials exhibited controlled degradation and the development of additional nanoporosity, while the persistence of PO 4 3- species suggested strong interactions with the SBA-15 framework. Although cell proliferation was lower than that of the control group, LDH assays confirmed the absence of cytotoxic effects. Notably, all ion-loaded systems promoted enhanced osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by significantly increased ALP activity. These findings highlight multi-ion-loaded SBA-15 systems as promising bioactive and biodegradable platforms for ion-mediated bone and dental tissue engineering applications.

title: Ginseng-derived nanoparticles enhance budesonide therapy and attenuate systemic toxicity in experimental asthma
abstract: Asthma is a prevalent chronic respiratory disease that imposes a substantial global health burden. Inhaled corticosteroids, such as budesonide (BUD), remain a cornerstone of asthma management; however, long-term treatment may be associated with systemic adverse effects, including metabolic disturbances, osteoporosis, and alterations in immune-related parameters. Plant-derived natural nanoparticles have recently emerged as promising biocompatible nanocarriers with intrinsic biological activities. In this study, we developed a ginseng-derived nanoparticle-based budesonide delivery system (BUD@GDNPs) to improve asthma therapy. The therapeutic efficacy of BUD@GDNPs was evaluated in two murine models of allergic asthma. Compared with free BUD, BUD@GDNPs more effectively alleviated airway inflammation, as evidenced by reduced eosinophil infiltration and decreased expression of Th2-associated cytokines. Importantly, long-term administration of BUD@GDNPs markedly attenuated BUD-associated systemic adverse effects, including disturbances in glucose metabolism and trabecular bone loss. In contrast, free BUD treatment induced splenic atrophy and reduced lymphocyte levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, whereas these alterations were substantially attenuated in mice receiving BUD@GDNPs. Collectively, these findings suggest that GDNPs represent a bioactive nanocarrier that enhances the therapeutic efficacy of BUD while attenuating its adverse effects, providing a promising strategy to improve the therapeutic index of corticosteroid therapy for asthma.

title: On the inhomogeneous microstructure and mechanical properties of an AA6060 aluminum alloy produced by additive friction stir deposition
abstract: A multiple-layer AA6060 deposit was manufactured by additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) and the co-relation between inhomogeneous microstructure and mechanical performance was quantitatively established by analyzing the grain size, dislocation density, and precipitates from the bottom to the top layers of the as-built deposit. The findings reveal that the top layers of the build exhibited 40% higher hardness/yield strength (~ 66.7 HV/87 MPa) compared to the middle/bottom layers (~39.2 HV/52 MPa), albeit with slight reduction in elongation. The spatially dependent mechanical properties were primarily governed by precipitate evolution: the top layers contain a high number of nano Mg2Si strengthening precipitates (~130 nm), whereas the middle and bottom layers consist of predominantly coarse Si-rich particles (~320 nm). Quantitative analysis indicates that the transformation of nano-precipitates results in nearly 30 MPa reduction in yield strength of bottom layers. The evolution of strengthening phase is primarily attributed to the significant variation of thermal residence time with the deposition height, which directly influences the in-situ precipitation and growth of Si-rich phase at substructures. This work will provide insights into the formation mechanism of inhomogeneous microstructure and mechanical properties of AFSD-Al alloys, aiding the engineering control of mechanical property homogeneity of AFSD fabricated components.

title: Design and structural engineering of natural polysaccharide-based biomaterials for macrophage functional modulation in ulcerative colitis
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disorder driven by profound innate immune dysregulation, wherein intestinal macrophages exhibit robust functional plasticity shaped by local microenvironmental cues. Recalibrating these aberrant macrophage programs is critical for durable UC therapy. Natural polysaccharides have emerged as highly promising biopolymers due to their exceptional structural diversity, inherent biocompatibility, and capacity for chemical modification. Unlike conventional broad-spectrum drugs, these macromolecular biomaterials act as context-dependent modulators whose physicochemical properties, such as molecular weight, spatial conformation, and active group modifications, directly dictate their immunoregulatory performance. Furthermore, formulating polysaccharides into advanced delivery systems, such as mucoadhesive hydrogels and targeted nanoparticles, optimizes their physical interaction with macrophages in the inflamed mucosa. Experimental evidence reveals that these engineered polysaccharide matrices fine-tune macrophage functional states by orchestrating complex material-cell crosstalk, specifically integrating the TLR4/NF-κB, JAK/STAT, Notch, and Autophagy-NLRP3 inflammasome axes. This review synthesizes current insights into the structure–property-function relationships of polysaccharide-based biomaterials in targeting macrophage heterogeneity in UC. By proposing a conceptual design framework centered on material-driven immune rewiring, we highlight the translational potential of these functional polymers for restoring intestinal homeostasis and outline future directions for precision mucosal engineering and advanced biomaterial formulation.

title: Atomistic insights into coupled hygrothermal-salinity degradation of carbon fiber-epoxy interfaces
abstract: Carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) structures in marine environments are continuously exposed to coupled humidity, salinity, and temperature, which progressively deteriorate carbon fiber-epoxy interfacial integrity. However, a unified atomistic understanding of environment-driven, multimode interfacial failure remains limited. Here, we employ a quantitative molecular dynamics (MD) strategy to evaluate interfacial degradation, avoiding arbitrarily prescribed moisture contents. Saturated uptake states in pure water and saline solution (simplified seawater) are generated via grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) sorption to account for model-specific free volume. We then examine the coupled evolution of interfacial nanostructure, diffusion kinetics, and mechanical response over an elevated temperature range. Moisture/saline uptake reduces interfacial compactness, while the interfacial solution content increases with temperature. Water forms and reorganizes hydrogen-bond networks with polar epoxy groups, weakening adhesion and nonbonded interactions. In saline environments, ions promote hydration-shell formation and competitively occupy polar sites, reducing and redistributing matrix-related hydrogen bonds and further degrading interfacial interactions. At fixed absorbed compositions, heating from 298 to 354 K reduces saline-interface tensile and shear strength retention from 74.62% to 61.69% and 69.43% to 64.98%, respectively. Overall, humidity and salinity primarily weaken nonbonded interactions and promote lubrication-assisted sliding, whereas temperature accelerates deterioration by enhancing segmental mobility and structural relaxation.

title: Dual enzyme-powered nanomotors for cascade-amplified sonodynamic therapy of prostate cancer
abstract: The clinical application of sonodynamic therapy (SDT) remains limited by the intrinsic hypoxic tumor microenvironment and sonosensitizer accumulation, while starvation therapy suffers from enzymatic activity in vivo . To address these challenges, we developed a cascade enzyme‑loaded extracellular vesicle platform (EV@TCG) derived from RM‑1 cells, co‑encapsulating the sonosensitizer TCPP with glucose oxidase (GOx) and catalase (CAT) via electroporation. The GOx/CAT cascade reaction depletes endogenous glucose for starvation therapy while generating oxygen that both relieve hypoxia and enhance the diffusive motion of EVs. The self‑generated oxygen serves as a substrate for TCPP‑mediated SDT, producing abundant reactive oxygen species (ROS) under ultrasound irradiation, while the enzyme‑catalysis‑enhanced cellular internalization and tumor accumulation. This synergistic mechanism improves oxidative stress, consumes glutathione and adenosine triphosphate, and elicits potent antitumor efficacy in prostate cancer models with a favorable safety profile. The EV@TCG platform thus addresses the critical limitations of hypoxia and passive diffusion, offering a robust and safe strategy for integrating cascade bio-catalysis, self‑propulsion, and sonodynamic therapy in cancer treatment

title: Anhydrous orthorhombic WO3 versus WO3·1/3H2O: a comparative experimental and first-principles study of structural, vibrational, electronic, optical, and thermodynamic properties
abstract: Anhydrous orthorhombic WO 3 and WO 3 ·⅓H 2 O were investigated by combining X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy with density functional theory (DFT) and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT), in order to compare their structural, vibrational, electronic, optical, and thermodynamic properties within a single, numerically converged framework. The samples were prepared by sol–gel and hydrothermal routes, respectively, and their orthorhombic structures were confirmed by Rietveld refinement. Energy–volume calculations yield bulk moduli of approximately 155 and 86 GPa for the anhydrous and hydrated models, respectively. The calculated Raman spectra reproduce the main bending and stretching bands of the tungsten–oxygen framework, whereas the explicit-hydrogen WO 3 ·⅓H 2 O model predicted O–H stretching (∼3532 and 3619 cm −1 ) modes outside the measured Raman range. In both structures, the valence-band maximum is O-2 p -derived and the conduction-band minimum W-5 d -derived. Anhydrous WO 3 has a direct gap at Γ, whereas the hydrated model has an indirect gap; the PBE, PBE+SOC, and HSE06 gaps are 0.894, 1.167, and 2.848 eV for WO 3 and 2.366, 2.596, and 3.657 eV for WO 3 ·⅓H 2 O. The gap difference between the two models decreases from 1.47 eV (PBE) to 0.81 eV (HSE06), revealing a strong dependence on the exchange–correlation treatment. Both models exhibit an anisotropic optical response concentrated in the ultraviolet, and the high-frequency O–H modes of the hydrated model delay the approach of the heat capacity to the Dulong–Petit limit. Because the samples were obtained by different routes and the models differ in both composition and structure, these results are discussed as structure–property differences between the two phases rather than as effects of hydration alone.

title: Experiment based mathematical model to assess liquid transfer and performance of fibre based hygiene wipes in disinfection of hard surfaces
abstract: For an efficient use of biocides the requested reduction in viability of microorganisms should be achieved with minimum consumption of biocidal product. In a new test protocol the liquid transfer from a wipe to a test surface has been determined as function of wiping length. The experimentally determined liquid transfer was approximated by an exponential decay function, which enables prediction of the liquid transfer per area as function of wiping length. From the test the characteristic parameters m 0 the total transferable amount of water and k a liquid transfer constant can be extracted. The liquid transfer from a wipe to the hard surface in terms of mass per area can be calculated as function of the wiping length. The capacity limit of a wipe will depend on concentration and type of biocide in solution, wipe characteristics and properties of hard surface. Prediction of a capacity limit for a chosen sanitation concept below which the amount of applied biocide falls under the minimal inhibitory amount is possible. Knowledge about liquid transfer capacity of a wipe assures reliable results in disinfection, minimises the risk of biocide and antibiotic resistance and prevents use of an unnecessary high surplus of biocidal products.

title: Temperature-dependent mechanical response and deformation mechanisms of AZ91 magnesium matrix composites with graphene: A molecular dynamics study
abstract: AZ91(Mg-9Al-1Zn, wt.%) magnesium matrix composites exhibit excellent mechanical properties with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) as the reinforcing phase. Although the addition of GNPs can improve the mechanical properties of AZ91 alloy at room temperature, the deformation behavior of the composite across a broad temperature range (from low to high temperatures) requires further investigation. In this paper, the molecular dynamics (MD) simulation method was utilized to systematically investigate the compressive deformation behavior of AZ91/GNPs composites from 100 K to 600 K, exploring the internal relationships among temperature, microstructure, and mechanical properties. The results indicate that as the temperature increases, both the yield strength and compression modulus decline gradually, with reductions of approximately 38 % and 15 % at 600 K relative to 100 K. Atomic-scale analysis reveals a pronounced temperature dependence of the plastic deformation mechanism: twin-assisted deformation dominates at low temperatures, while dislocation slip becomes the primary mechanism at elevated temperatures. Additionally, high temperature conditions promote phase structure transformation and dislocation nucleation. This study reveals the deformation behavior of AZ91/GNPs composites under different thermodynamic conditions at the atomic scale, providing a significant theoretical reference for further understanding the mechanical response mechanism of the material in complex environments.

title: Microstructural degradation and damage-dependent creep behavior of heterogeneous porous geomaterials after freeze–thaw treatment
abstract: The long-term durability of porous soft rocks in cold-region mines is severely threatened by the synergistic degradation of freeze-thaw (F-T) weathering and creep loading. To investigate the influence of freeze-thaw cycle (FTC) frequency and freezing temperature on the creep behavior and damage evolution of weak-layer materials, this study performed F-T cycling, scanning electron microscopy, and uniaxial creep tests on sandy mudstone. The results reveal a distinct damage-creep coupling mechanism governed by progressive microstructural degradation. Under equivalent stress levels, increasing F-T frequency and decreasing temperatures monotonically amplify the instantaneous strain, total creep strain, and steady-state creep rates. A key finding is that the ratio of long-term strength to uniaxial compressive strength remains stable at approximately 70%, aligning closely with the crack-initiation stress regardless of F-T history. As damage accumulates, the failure mode transitions from brittle shear to complex tensile-shear composite fracture, characterized by increased primary crack density and a significant reduction in structural integrity. By defining an environmental damage variable based on elastic modulus degradation, an improved creep constitutive model was established. The model exhibits high fidelity in characterizing F-T induced weakening, providing a physics-based framework for assessing the stability of soft rock structures in high-altitude cold regions.

title: Squaraine-based J-aggregation for photoacoustic imaging-guided photothermal therapy
abstract: Organic small molecules have attracted growing interest in phototheranostics due to their capacity to unify diagnostic and therapeutic functionalities within a singular molecular framework. Here, we report a new squaraine (SQ) J-aggregate (SQ NPs) as a phototheranostic system for imaging guided photothermal therapy (PTT). The J-aggregate induced a significant redshift, enabling effective matching with the near-infrared (NIR)-I biological window. SQ NPs demonstrated favorable photothermal performance with high photostability and a notable photothermal conversion efficiency (PCE) of 62%. In vitro studies indicated that SQ NPs exhibit low dark cytotoxicity but induce potent cancer cell killing upon 808 nm laser irradiation. Following intravenous (i.v.) administration into Colon26 tumor-bearing mice, SQ NPs showed effective tumor accumulation through the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, enabling photoacoustic imaging (PAI) for precise tumor delineation. Furthermore, the J-aggregates combined with 808 nm laser treatment generated rapid and localized temperature elevation (ΔT ≈ 20 °C), achieving complete macroscopic tumor regression during the 14-day observation period with minimal systemic side effects. Histological analysis confirmed no apparent damage to major organs, indicating good biocompatibility. This work establishes squaraine-based J-aggregates as a versatile and effective organic phototheranostic platform, opening new avenues for precision cancer treatment.

title: Microstructural relaxation and enhanced mechanical performance of electric current-assisted Cu–Cu bonding
abstract: Copper-to-copper (Cu–Cu) direct bonding is a promising interconnection technology for advanced semiconductor packaging, but achieving reliable joints typically requires high thermal budgets. In this study, electric current-assisted Cu–Cu bonding was investigated as a processing strategy for forming high-strength interconnections under reduced thermal budgets, while the associated mechanical performance and microstructural evolution were systematically analyzed. Cross-sectional focused ion beam (FIB) observations and shear strength measurements confirmed metallurgical Cu–Cu joint formation at temperatures as low as 120 °C. Notably, the current-assisted joint formed at 200 °C/40 A exhibited a higher mean nominal shear strength than the 300 °C/0 A thermal-only reference joint despite the markedly reduced bonding temperature. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis showed that room-temperature current-only treatment produced pronounced reductions in defect-associated lattice distortion, particularly in the bulk and low-angle grain boundary (LAGB)-adjacent regions. These results demonstrate treatment-duration- and location-dependent microstructural relaxation under current-only treatment and support its relevance to Cu–Cu bond development. Overall, these results establish a process–microstructure–mechanical performance correlation and highlight the potential of current-assisted bonding for low-temperature Cu–Cu interconnection using conventional, unmodified electroplated Cu.

title: Functional shape memory polymers and composites: from material design to applications
abstract: Functional shape memory polymers (SMPs) and their composites (SMPCs) combine programmable deformation with mechanical, thermal, electrical, optical, magnetic, or self-healing functions, but their engineering performance is governed by coupled material and processing constraints. This review critically examines the relationships among molecular design, network architecture, functional fillers, additive manufacturing routes, printed structures, and service functions. Crosslink density, switching domains, reversible bonds, and rigid backbones are compared in terms of their effects on strength, deformability, recovery stress, creep, and thermal stability. The interactions between filler-enabled electrothermal, photothermal, and magnetic actuation and the rheological, interfacial, and optical requirements of direct ink writing, fused deposition modeling, and digital light processing are then assessed. Reported systems are evaluated according to printability, mechanical performance, actuation efficiency, functional integration, and application-specific reliability rather than isolated peak values, with attention to programming and testing conditions. The analysis identifies recurring trade-offs: reinforcement can restrict deformation, stronger stimulus conversion can narrow the printing window, and increasingly complex architectures can reduce manufacturing robustness. From these comparisons, conditional structure–processing–property–function design principles are identified, emphasizing process-specific formulation, filler loading compatible with processing, control of actuation and bond-exchange conditions, and coordinated material–architecture optimization toward reliable, cyclically stable, and application-ready functional SMP and SMPC systems.

title: Damped harmonic hygrothermoelastic response of a voided half space with four transport lags
abstract: This study investigates the harmonic hygrothermoelastic response of an isotropic half-space containing distributed voids. A two-dimensional boundary-value model couples perturbations in displacement, temperature, moisture concentration, and void fraction. Separate phase lags for heat flux, temperature gradient, moisture flux, and concentration gradient extend the classical Fourier and Fick transport laws. We prescribe a sinusoidal surface temperature consistent with the normal-mode representation. The governing equations yield coupled longitudinal modes and a shear mode that decay with depth. Modal amplitudes are determined by the prescribed temperature, zero normal moisture flux, and vanishing void and mechanical tractions. The solutions describe the spatial distributions of temperature, moisture, void fraction, displacement, and stress. Comparisons among classical transport, heat-flux relaxation, and the four-phase-lag model illustrate the influence of delayed transport on these fields. Varying each lag separately identifies distinct thermal and moisture transport effects on the coupled response. The formulation specifies a coupled boundary-value system for examining the effects of delayed transport under damped harmonic excitation; numerical verification must use the corrected equations and boundary conditions. The calculated profiles describe the coupled response to an exponentially decaying sinusoidal surface temperature.

title: A mild photothermal polysaccharide-based hydrogel with multifunctional pro-healing properties enables rapid sutureless repair of colon perforation
abstract: Colon Perforation (CP) can cause severe intra-abdominal infections that may progress to sepsis, compromising intestinal barrier functions. This can trigger systemic inflammatory responses and multiple organ dysfunction through mechanisms like bacterial translocation, reactive oxygen species production, and inflammatory factor release. To address these issues, we developed a photothermal responsive hydrogel. This hydrogel facilitates rapid closure of CP and exhibits superior antibacterial, antioxidant, and angiogenic properties. It modulates the local microenvironment and promotes macrophage M1-to-M2 polarization, reducing inflammation, stimulating angiogenesis and tissue regeneration, and accelerating CP healing. Furthermore, the hydrogel not only promotes rapid closure and efficient repair of colon perforations but also markedly prevents abdominal adhesion formation. By leveraging immunomodulation, bacterial clearance, tissue regeneration, and remodeling of the perforation-surrounding microenvironment, this innovative material offers an effective therapeutic solution for CP, exhibiting substantial clinical promise.

title: A mitochondria-inspired siCysLTR1 nanoplatform for modulating macrophage-associated signaling in vascular calcification
abstract: Coronary artery calcification, a hallmark of advanced atherosclerosis, lacks effective treatment due to its complex pathogenesis involving macrophage-mediated inflammation and metabolic dysregulation. Our data support a pathway in which LT-C4 exposure is associated with KLF2 redistribution and loss, together with NCOA4-related ferritin degradation. These changes were accompanied by labile iron accumulation and metabolic reprogramming. We engineered a biomimetic nanoparticle loaded with CysLTR1 siRNA (MNPs@siCysLTR1). The formulation improved macrophage uptake in vitro. In ApoE KO mice with dietary-induced vascular calcification, MNPs@siCysLTR1 accumulated in CD68 + macrophage-rich plaque regions; this regional colocalization does not establish exclusive cell-specific targeting. Treatment reduced vascular calcification and circulating inflammatory markers. Conditioned-medium experiments linked LT-C4-treated macrophages to vascular smooth muscle cell mineralization, which was attenuated by the formulation. Under the current dosing regimen, preliminary safety findings were acceptable. Treatment reduced CysLTR1 signals in plaque macrophage-rich regions and increased the KLF2 nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. These findings support further investigation of CysLTR1-directed nanodelivery for vascular calcification.

title: Selective dissolution-induced mechanical damage in Cu/Nb laminated composites revealed by in-situ acoustic emission monitoring
abstract: Cu/Nb laminated composites combine high electrical conductivity with mechanical strength, but their environmental reliability under selective phase dissolution remains insufficiently understood. In this study, corrosion-induced damage in Cu/Nb laminated composites was investigated in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution using potentiodynamic anodic polarization, in-situ optical microscopy, acoustic emission (AE) monitoring, and post-corrosion microstructural characterization. Pure Cu was examined as a reference to separate Cu-dominated electrochemical behavior from damage specific to the laminated architecture. The Cu/Nb laminates exhibited polarization behavior similar to pure Cu, indicating that the electrochemical response was mainly governed by Cu dissolution and CuCl-based passivation. However, after passivation-film breakdown, short-duration high-frequency AE events appeared only in the Cu/Nb laminates. Cross-sectional observations revealed that selective dissolution of Cu produced subsurface cavities beneath the Nb layers, leading to local Nb-layer deformation, collapse, and crack initiation. Time-frequency analysis confirmed that these transient signals were distinct from low-frequency periodic signals associated with the electrochemical measurement system. These results demonstrate that selective Cu dissolution can mechanically destabilize corrosion-resistant Nb layers and that AE monitoring can detect such transient corrosion-deformation coupling in laminated metallic composites.

title: Integrated thermal analysis modelling for induction-assisted directed energy deposition of Ti–6Al–4V
abstract: Directed energy deposition (DED) combined with in-situ induction heating (ISIH) offers a promising route to actively tailor the thermal field during large-scale metal additive manufacturing to effectively control residual stress to mitigate distortion and premature failure. However, the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood due to the strongly coupled and spatially varying thermal-electromagnetic interactions involved in the process. In this work, an efficient induction heat source modelling strategy has been developed for a locally designed induction coil and integrated with a laser heat-source model to enable thermal analysis of ISIH-assisted DED of Ti–6Al–4V over different build heights. The model retains fixed heat-distribution parameters while introducing height-dependent power partitioning between the deposited wall and the substrate, allowing it to reproduce experimentally measured temperature fields and capture the reduced thermal gradients observed relative to conventional DED. These results demonstrate the capability of ISIH to moderate thermal gradients and provide a thermal basis for assessing its potential influence on residual-stress development. Furthermore, the proposed model provides a physically informed description of deposition-height-dependent induction heating behaviour, enabling part-scale ISIH-DED thermal simulations with substantially reduced computational cost.

title: Flexural characterization of metallic sandwich beams with a novel 3D DAH core: a scalable fabrication and ANN-driven design approach
abstract: The growing demand for lightweight, high-performance structural components in aerospace and automotive industries, necessitates the development of optimized metallic sandwich panels. While conventional cellular cores offer favorable stiffness-to-weight ratios, their flexural load-bearing capacity and structural integrity are often constrained by geometric limitations and complex, costly manufacturing processes. To address these critical gaps, this paper introduces a novel, cost-effective, assembly-based fabrication methodology for metallic sandwich beams utilizing a three-dimensional Double-Arrow Head (3D-DAH) core geometry. This innovative architecture is engineered to deliver superior flexural stiffness, enhanced structural strength, and outstanding load-bearing capacity under transverse loading. Following the fabrication and experimental validation of the proposed beams under three-point bending conditions, a systematic parametric investigation employing a factorial experimental design generated a robust dataset of 180 finite element simulations. This dataset was utilized to train an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to accurately predict the highly nonlinear relationships between geometric parameters and the structure’s mechanical response. Complementing the computational insights, the finite element modeling and experimental validation revealed distinct failure regimes—geometry-dominated versus local buckling-dominated—providing insights into the progressive collapse mechanisms. These findings offer a comprehensive methodology for designing and optimizing high-performance metallic sandwich panels with tailored flexural properties, paving the way for the scalable manufacturing of advanced load-bearing structures.

title: An integrated process of fine particle peening and plasma nitrocarburizing for improved the surface properties of 16Cr3NiWMoVNbE aviation gear steel
abstract: To improve the wear resistance of a new-generation aviation gear steel, fine particle peening (FPP), plasma nitrocarburizing (PNC), and their integrated process were used with 16Cr3NiWMoVNbE. The surface integrity, microstructural evolution, and tribological behavior of the treated specimens were systematically investigated. The results indicated that the grain refinement, high dislocation density, and abundant low-angle grain boundaries introduced by FPP promoted the diffusion of C and N atoms during the subsequent PNC process, leading to the formation of a denser modified layer. The integrated treatment produced the highest surface hardness and excellent compressive residual stress among all treated specimens. And the integrated treatment exhibited the lowest wear volume and rate with a 90% reduction relative to UNT specimen. These results demonstrate that the integrated process can improve the surface properties of 16Cr3NiWMoVNbE aviation gear steel.

title: Designing metal-organic framework-growth factor interfaces for stage-matched chronic wound repair: from molecular binding to composite architectures
abstract: Chronic wounds are sustained by coupled failures in inflammation control, infection resolution, redox homeostasis, protease regulation, and angiogenesis, which destabilize growth factors (GFs) and disrupt the temporal sequence of repair. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a designable route to address this problem because metal-node chemistry, linker composition, pore and defect structure, particle architecture, and composite processing can be coordinated within one platform. This Review develops a structure-interface-function framework for MOF-enabled GF regulation in chronic wound repair. We examine how surface adsorption, biomineralization-derived framework encapsulation, and confinement within accessible hierarchical pore domains control GF loading, conformational protection, release, and post-release activity; how responsive framework transformation and bioactive ion exposure couple microenvironment remodeling with endogenous or exogenous GF signaling; and how hydrogels, nanofibers, microneedles, and multilayer scaffolds translate nanoscale interactions into spatially and temporally organized therapy. Direct GF delivery is distinguished from indirect signaling regulation, and current evidence is evaluated against requirements for interface-resolved characterization, coupled release modeling, reproducible processing, wound-relevant exposure assessment, and long-term safety. These design principles position MOFs as programmable regenerative interfaces rather than passive protein reservoirs.

title: New families of two-dimensional materials emerging from MXene compositions
abstract: MXenes are traditionally described as two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal carbides and nitrides in which carbon or nitrogen layers are sandwiched between outer transition-metal layers. Here, we investigate the possibility of an inverted atomic arrangement, coined XMene, in which the X atoms occupy the outermost atomic planes. Using spin-polarized density functional theory, we systematically examined 112 bare MXene compositions spanning M 2 X and M 3 X 2 stoichiometries, 14 transition metals (Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Y, Zr, Nb, Mo, La, Lu, Hf, Ta, and W), two X species (C and N), and both ABC and ABA stacking sequences. The propensity toward inversion was assessed through X-vacancy/X-adatom defect formation energies and inversion energies comparing conventional MXenes and fully inverted XMenes. A strong compositional dependence was identified. M 3 C 2 MXenes universally favour MXene structures, whereas other compositions may exhibit thermodynamically favourable inversion, or even a tendency to form non-hexagonal phases. Among all the studied phases, the XMenes one was predicted for be the most stable for the Nb 2 N, Ta 2 N, Ta 3 N 2 , Mo 3 N 2 , W 3 N 2 , and Mn 3 N 2 compositions. For several others, inversion does not yield an ideal XMene but instead drives the formation of previously unexplored low-energy 2D phases with rectangular or square symmetry. Specifically, group-3 M 2 X compounds favour rectangular structures, while group-6 and Mn-based M 2 X compounds favour square structures. Despite the substantial structural transformations, all predicted XMenes and reconstructed phases remain metallic, while exhibiting diverse magnetic behaviour. These results establish XMenes as a new class of MXene-derived 2D materials and demonstrate that layer inversion can serve as a mechanism for generating competing low-energy phases. The findings provide a possible explanation for the discrepancy between the large number of theoretically predicted MXenes and the comparatively small number realized experimentally, particularly among nitride compositions.

title: The role of sintering atmosphere in properties formation of Fe-based soft magnetic composites
abstract: This study systematically investigates the influence of sintering atmosphere on the structure and functional properties of Fe/MgO soft magnetic composites (SMC). Through comprehensive characterisation of samples processed under varying pressing pressures and sintering temperatures, we demonstrate distinct qualitative and quantitative differences between oxidative (air) and protective (N 2 ) environments. Our results reveal that air-sintered samples exhibit enhanced resonant frequencies and electrical resistivity, whereas nitrogen-sintered samples show better magnetic softness, characterised by reduced coercivity and increased permeability. At the same time, the character of the influence on losses is complex, depending on both the annealing temperature and the pressing pressure. Microstructural analysis further elucidates the role of atmospheric conditions in oxide formation and distribution within the composite matrix. The findings provide fundamental insights for optimising the fabrication parameters of SMCs. By establishing correlations between sintering atmosphere, microstructure, and functional properties, this work enables the rational design of processing protocols to tailor SMCs performance for specific applications.

title: Dual gradient microcellular TPU fabricated via coupled concentration-temperature gradient fields: structure, performance, and optimization
abstract: Microcellular thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) inherently combines high elasticity and toughness with a three-dimensionally controllable microcellular structure, delivering superior compression resilience, energy dissipation, and acoustic/thermal insulation. The introduction of functional gradient structures can overcome the performance trade-offs inherent to microcellular TPU with uniform structure materials (MTUS), enabling synergistic optimization of mechanical load-bearing capacity and multifunctionality. However, existing studies have focused predominantly on single cell size gradients, leaving the synergistic and precise control of dual gradients in both cell size and cell density largely unexplored. This study reports a foaming strategy based on coupled temperature-concentration fields to fabricate microcellular TPU with gradients structure materials (MTGS). Integration of an N 2 -assisted volume recovery process provides an effective strategy to suppress post-foaming shrinkage and improve the dimensional stability of high-performance elastomer foams. Compared with MTUS, the MTGS exhibit significantly enhanced compression strength, resilience, and energy-absorption capacity, while simultaneously providing excellent high-frequency sound insulation and precisely tunable thermal insulation. Furthermore, multi-physics simulations via COMSOL Multiphysics were performed to establish how the mathematical profile of the gradients dictate mechanical performance. These findings provide a practical and precise toolkit for designing high-performance gradient polymers.

title: Oxidation behavior and mechanisms of LSPwC-treated DD6 superalloy at 650 °C and 1000 °C
abstract: LSPwC introduces a rough, porous remelted layer and a gradient-deformed layer—both critically affecting oxidation. This study systematically examines the high-temperature oxidation resistance of single-crystal superalloy DD6 (Ni–4.4Cr–5.7Al, wt%) under three surface conditions: untreated, LSPwC-treated, and polished LSPwC (remelted layer removed). At 1000 °C, LSPwC reduces mass gain by 18% versus untreated; at 650 °C, it increases mass gain by 26%. In contrast, polished LSPwC shows superior resistance at both temperatures—due to removal of the detrimental remelted layer. At 1000 °C, LSPwC-induced dislocations accelerate continuous α-Al 2 O 3 scale formation. Although the remelted layer initially enhances oxygen ingress, it is quickly blocked by a continuous α-Al 2 O 3 layer, resulting in mass gain lower than untreated. Among all variants, polished LSPwC delivers the best oxidation resistance: it retains the beneficial dislocation substructure while eliminating the harmful remelted layer. At 650 °C, sluggish diffusion hinders continuous oxide scale formation. Dislocations then promote only isolated Cr 2 O 3 nuclei, while the remelted layer exacerbates oxidation—making LSPwC perform the worst. Polishing to remove the remelted layer while preserving dislocations results in optimal oxidation resistance of the polished LSPwC. These results show that combining LSPwC with polishing synergistically optimizes oxidation resistance—a promising strategy for extending turbine blade tenon life.

title: An injectable ROS-responsive hyaluronic acid hydrogel delivering Coptis chinensis-derived nanovesicles for diabetic wound microenvironment reprogramming
abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are trapped in a nonhealing state by excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), persistent inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and defective extracellular matrix remodeling. Although plant-derived nanovesicles provide scalable and biocompatible therapeutic cues, their direct application is hindered by rapid diffusion, enzymatic degradation, and poor local retention. Here, an injectable ROS-responsive hyaluronic acid hydrogel is engineered as a microenvironment-adaptive depot for localized delivery of Coptis chinensis -derived nanovesicles (CCNVs). The hydrogel, constructed from phenylboronic acid-functionalized methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA-PBA), integrates injectability, wound conformity, and ROS-triggered degradation. Under oxidative stress, cleavage of PBA-containing linkages accelerates matrix disassembly and enables on-demand CCNV release. Released CCNVs are efficiently internalized by fibroblasts and endothelial cells, enhancing migration, proliferation, and angiogenic tube formation in vitro . In a streptozotocin-induced diabetic full-thickness wound model, HAMA-PBA@CCNVs accelerate wound closure, re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and neovascularization while promoting CD163-positive macrophage polarization and suppressing iNOS-associated inflammatory activation. This ROS-adaptive biomaterial platform integrates responsive delivery with botanical nanovesicle bioactivity for chronic wound repair.

title: Correlation of microstructural evolution and hardness response in heavy-ion irradiated nanocrystalline tungsten
abstract: Nanocrystalline materials exhibit high resistance to displacement damage because their high density of grain boundaries acts as defect sinks. Here, bulk nanocrystalline tungsten (NCW) was fabricated and investigated through experiments and simulations to elucidate the correlation between microstructural evolution and hardness response, exploring its potential for plasma-facing materials for fusion reactors. Following heavy-ion irradiation, NCW exhibited lower dislocation loop and void number densities than coarse-grained tungsten (CGW), although this advantage was weakened with increasing dose at an elevated temperature, owing to irradiation-enhanced grain growth. Simulations revealed that grain boundary migration was primarily driven by thermal spikes. NCW exhibited unexpected irradiation softening, in contrast to the conventional irradiation hardening in CGW. This originates from the competition between grain growth-induced softening and defect accumulation-induced hardening, with the former dominating. A model was developed to correlate hardness with defect accumulation and grain growth, thereby decoupling their respective contributions. With increasing irradiation dose, grain growth-induced softening in NCW increased from 6.5 GPa to 11.1 GPa, whereas defect accumulation-induced hardening increased from 1.2 GPa to 1.9 GPa. These findings provide insights into the radiation effects of NCW and highlight grain boundary energy reduction as a promising strategy for improving the irradiation stability of nanocrystalline materials.

title: Non-monotonic regulation of the intrinsic mechanical properties of electrodeposited FeNiCo alloys by Co content
abstract: Electrodeposited FeNiCo films (0–51.61 at.% Co) were studied by in-situ micropillar compression, first-principles SQS calculations and nanoindentation finite-element modelling. Yield strength and strain-hardening capacity vary non-monotonically with Co content but peak at different compositions: yield strength at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 , strain hardening and high-strain flow stress at (FeNi) 66 Co 34 , so the stress–strain curves cross. A Hall–Petch decomposition using TEM and X-ray grain sizes shows that grain refinement accounts for most of the initial rise in yield strength but only about 38% of its subsequent fall; the grain-size-corrected strength still peaks at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 and follows the calculated shear modulus. The calculated bulk modulus rises monotonically, whereas the shear and Young’s moduli peak at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 ( G = 100.95 GPa, +16% over the Co-free alloy). Density-of-states and Bader analyses associate this maximum with balanced charge partitioning among Fe, Co and Ni; a charge-dispersion index is minimal at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 and varies together with the shear modulus across the seven models ( r = −0.91, suggestive rather than conclusive). A finite-element model whose only composition-dependent inputs are the micropillar yield strength and hardening exponent reproduces the measured rise-then-fall of hardness ( r = 0.99). These results give a plausible electronic-structure basis for FeNiCo compositional design.
