title: Targeted nanomedicine for ischemic cardiomyopathy
abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The therapeutic efficacy of conventional pharmacological interventions is constrained by poor bioavailability, limited myocardial targeting capacity, and systemic adverse effects. Nanomedicine has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enhancing drug stability, prolonging blood circulation time, and enabling precise delivery to diseased tissues. In the setting of ischemic cardiomyopathy, active targeting approaches-particularly those functionalized with tannic acid and cardiac-targeting peptides-have been extensively investigated to boost the delivery efficiency of therapeutic agents and halt disease progression. Moreover, the ischemic microenvironment (IME), characterized by inflammation, redox imbalance, and enzymatic dysregulation, not only drives pathological progression but also creates unique opportunities for site-specific therapeutic intervention. Systematic comprehension and evaluation of these targeting strategies are critical to advancing the clinical translation of myocardium-targeted nanomedicines. In this review, we summarize recent advances in myocardium-targeted nanotherapeutic strategies, with a special focus on tannic acid-based systems, cardiac-targeting peptides, reductive microenvironment-responsive platforms, and enzyme-responsive delivery approaches. We also discuss the current limitations and future perspectives of such strategies, aiming to offer insights into the rational design and clinical development of next-generation therapeutics for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

title: Comparative mechanical, microstructural, durability performance and life cycle assessment of pectin and inulin versus xanthan gum in loam soil stabilization
abstract: Microbial xanthan gum (XG) is a well-known stabilizer for loam soil, however plant-derived biopolymers such as pectin and inulin may offer better performance due to their distinct stabilization mechanisms. This study therefore compares these plant-derived biopolymers with XG to evaluate their effects on the strength, durability, microstructure, and LCA of loam soil, using treated samples tested after 1, 7, 28, 56, and 90 days by UCS, ultrasonic pulse velocity, F-T cycles, and microstructural analyses. Compared with inulin and XG, 1% pectin after 28 days provided the highest compressive strength, increasing the strength of loam from 230 to 5102 kPa. Pectin also exhibited the best performance under F-T cycling. This improvement was associated with the formation of a dense hydrogel network that coated mineral surfaces and reduced pore spaces. Although pectin provided the greatest mechanical and durability enhancements, the comparative LCA showed that inulin achieved the highest overall environmental performance, with MPPI scores of 0.67, 0.60, and 0.50 for inulin, XG, and pectin, respectively, under scenario S2. These results indicate that pectin and inulin can improve the performance of loam soil compared with XG; however, inulin emerged as the best performing biopolymer when structural integrity and environmental sustainability were considered simultaneously.

title: Strain-ratio-dependent low-cycle fatigue and localized deformation of bake-hardened HR420 steel
abstract: Manufacturing history can substantially alter the cyclic response of automotive bake-hardened steels, yet the role of strain ratio in this processing–structure–property link remains insufficiently resolved. Here, as-received HR420 steel and specimens subjected to 4% pre-straining followed by bake hardening were examined under strain-controlled low-cycle fatigue at three strain amplitudes and at strain ratios R ε = − 1 and 0. Cyclic hysteresis, fatigue life, three-dimensional digital image correlation, and fracture-side electron backscatter diffraction were combined to identify localization and crack-path characteristics. Bake hardening produced an amplitude-dependent response: it restrained early localized plasticity and improved fatigue resistance at low amplitude, whereas at high amplitude it intensified strain localization and accelerated damage accumulation. Positive mean strain under R ε = 0 promoted directional slip accumulation and more crystallographically guided transgranular cracking than fully reversed cycling. A Chaboche-type cyclic elastoplastic damage model and EBSD-informed crystal-plasticity simulations were used to interpret the observed specimen- and grain-scale responses. The results establish a processing–microstructure–fatigue relationship for formed and bake-hardened HR420 steel.

title: Exploring flexible sensing strategies toward embodied intelligence
abstract: The field of embodied intelligence emphasizes the adaptive development of systems through interactions with their environments, with perceptual capabilities acting as a core enabler. Accordingly, flexible sensors are increasingly integrated into embodied intelligence systems, owing to their conformability to complex morphologies and adaptability to dynamic movements. Despite the great potential of such sensors, improving their performance to further advance embodied intelligence presents cross-disciplinary challenges. This article reviews flexible sensing strategies for embodied intelligence at both the device and system levels, highlighting the path toward the synergy between hardware and software. The foundational elements underpinning the advancement of flexible sensors in embodied intelligence are introduced from both hardware and software perspectives. At the device level, various approaches for developing flexible sensors are examined for enhancing their mechanical performance and augmenting their functionalities. At the system level, the integration of flexible sensors into embodied intelligence systems is analyzed with respect to implementation approaches and the resultant intelligent behaviors. Finally, the future outlook of flexible sensing strategies for embodied intelligence systems is discussed.

title: Microstructure-informed constrained multi-objective optimization for process–structure–property design of WAAM 316L stainless steel
abstract: Process design in wire arc additive manufacturing requires the cross-scale balancing of microstructural refinement and mechanical performance under geometric constraints. This work integrates finite element–cellular automaton grain-size predictions with measured hardness and bead width through quadratic response surfaces and constrained Pareto optimization for 316L stainless steel. Infrared thermography and electron backscatter diffraction supported thermal–microstructural predictions at selected conditions. Grain coarsening at equal nominal line energy highlighted the additional influence of interpass thermal state. Grain refinement and hardness favoured distinct process conditions, defining a narrow nominal Pareto front that was not truncated by the 6–8 mm bead-width constraint. Validation tests at three conditions supported the local trade-off in the measured means. The nominal knee at 20.25 V, 10.19 mm/s travel speed, 5.06 m/min wire feed rate and 85.10 °C interpass temperature yielded measured grain size, hardness and bead width of 149.47 μm, 169.74 HV and 6.47 mm, respectively. However, changes in surrogate structure shifted the predicted knee grain size by more than the nominal front’s grain-size span. Predictive uncertainty and significant lack of fit further limited confidence in its precise location. The framework supports experimentally assessed process screening while quantifying uncertainty and model dependence of the selected compromise.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning-Assisted design of refractory High-Entropy alloys with balanced strength and plasticity
abstract: The vast compositional space of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) makes it challenging to identify compositions with balanced room temperature strength and plasticity. Here, an interpretable machine-learning-assisted strategy is developed to predict yield strength and fracture strain using separate regression models. The optimized LightGBM and random forest models achieve test-set R 2 values of 0.80 and 0.84 for yield strength and fracture strain, respectively. Descriptor-based SHAP analysis identifies property-dependent predictive associations, while an auxiliary composition-based model provides elemental SHAP information to inform the composition search bounds. Three designed alloys exhibit room temperature yield strengths of 1310–1430 MPa and fracture strains of 15.8–21.7%. Among them, Nb 30 Mo 17 Ta 24 Hf 15 Zr 14 (A2) achieves a yield strength of 1370 MPa and a fracture strain of 18.0%. Additional compression tests at 1000 °C show that this alloy exhibits a yield strength of approximately 940 MPa and reaches a true compressive strain of at least 35% without fracture. TEM and EDS observations reveal Zr-Hf-rich particles near locally curved dislocations, suggesting a possible contribution of particle-dislocation interactions to deformation resistance. These findings support interpretable machine learning as a tool for identifying RHEAs with balanced room temperature strength and plasticity and highlight the promising compressive performance of the A2 alloy at 1000 °C.

title: Design of patient-specific metamaterial orthopedic implants enabled by field-driven lattice grading for additive manufacturing
abstract: Stress shielding caused by stiffness mismatch between metallic femoral stems and bone contributes to bone resorption and implant loosening after total hip arthroplasty. This study presents a patient-specific computational framework integrating topology optimization (TO), continuous field-driven lattice grading, automated design exploration, and biomechanical evaluation. A Ti-6Al-4V stem was optimized under peak static physiological loading to generate a spatial density field, which was continuously mapped to architecture-specific geometric parameters. The same TO-derived field was used as a common mechanical control field for three distinct architectures: strut-based Diamond, TPMS-based Gyroid, and stochastic Voronoi, under identical anatomical and loading conditions. A Python-based constrained full-factorial design-of-experiments workflow explored architecture-specific parameters against a common intact-femur stiffness target, enabling controlled comparison of how different lattice representations realize the same patient-specific optimization objective. The optimized stems achieved 53–57% porosity, intact-femur-like deformation, pore sizes predominantly within 500–1050 μm, and surface-to-volume ratios of 2.011–3.45 mm −1 . Compared with the solid stem, graded architectures reduced stiffness by 41–49% and Gruen-zone stress shielding from 55 to 75% to 18–36%, while maintaining stresses below the Ti-6Al-4V yield strength. The framework enables systematic architecture-dependent design and biomechanical evaluation of patient-specific graded porous implants.

title: Study on droplet impact, spreading and infiltration behavior, and granule binding mechanisms in binder jet 3D printing
abstract: Binder jet 3D printing (BJ-3DP) offers unique advantages for fabricating personalized pharmaceutical formulations, but its process control is limited by insufficient understanding of droplet-powder interactions. In this study, a high-speed visualization platform was established to investigate droplet impact behavior on pharmaceutical powder beds. The effects of powder properties, powder-bed density, Weber number ( We ), and ink composition on impact dynamics and agglomerate formation were systematically evaluated. The results showed that powder characteristics and bed density jointly determined the interaction mode. A higher powder-bed density suppressed bed collapse, accelerated penetration, and promoted the formation of dense and uniform agglomerates. We was identified as an important parameter affecting spreading, penetration, and cratering, while viscous dissipation, wettability, solvent evaporation, and powder-bed resistance also contributed to the overall behavior. Low- We droplets favored stable spreading–penetration and uniform agglomeration, whereas high- We droplets induced splashing, prolonged penetration, and reduced deposition precision. Ink composition further regulated droplet behavior through surface tension, wettability, evaporation, and ink-powder compatibility. Overall, this study proposes a mechanism-based and semi-quantitative framework for understanding how local droplet-powder interactions may guide formulation design and process-window determination in pharmaceutical BJ-3DP.

title: Ratcheting in AHSS under cyclic fatigue: Strain rate dependent nonlinear kinematic hardening plasticity and metaheuristic optimization
abstract: To optimum characterize material properties and predict cyclic ratcheting in advanced high strength multiphase steel sheets, a series of quasi-static/dynamic uniaxial tensile/compressive tests, along with asymmetric cyclic load- and displacement-controlled tension–compression experiments on DP590, DP780, DP980 dual phase steels, and TRIP980, is conducted using a high-speed digital image correlation (DIC) camera to measure strain accumulation. Since, the hardening criterion significantly affects cyclic creep and life, and yield size of TRIP steels are notably sensitive to stress rate, a non-linear Chaboche-type kinematic hardening rule is developed to capture the influence of loading frequency on the ratchetting under low cycle fatigue. To identify the model parameters with minimal computational cost, a multi-objective, multi-stage metaheuristic calibration procedure is proposed and implemented in MATLAB, incorporating the genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and pattern search methods. The implemented hardening law and obtained optimal constants predict the effects of mean stress relaxation, load ratio and strain rate in good agreements with experimental data. Moreover, complex stress state validation is performed by comparing central hole (notched) monotonic experiment with corresponding finite element analysis (FEA) via UserMat subroutine. The results verify that the presented approach predicts the effect of notch and cutout within acceptable accuracy.

title: Salvianolic Acid-A/Gemcitabine loaded hydrogel reprograms the immunosuppressive microenvironment and inhibits bladder cancer progression by targeting mTOR/STAT3/IL-10 pathway
abstract: The clinical management of bladder cancer, particularly intravesical chemotherapy, is severely hampered by rapid drug wash-out and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. To address these limitations, we developed an injectable thermosensitive PLGA-PEG-PLGA hydrogel co-loaded with salvianolic acid A (SAA) and gemcitabine (GEM) as a localized drug delivery system. The hydrogel exhibited a rapid sol–gel transition at physiological body temperature and enabled sustained co-release of GEM and SAA for over 13 days in physiological media. As a proof-of-concept (PoC), localized administration of the co-loaded hydrogel in a subcutaneous murine bladder cancer model significantly augmented the therapeutic efficacy of GEM while reducing the required chemotherapy dosage. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that SAA suppressed tumor-derived IL-10 sretion via the mTOR/STAT3 axis, thereby blocking M2 macrophage polarization and enhancing pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage infiltration. This targeted immune reprogramming restructured the M2-predominant immunosuppressive macrophage microenvironment into a pro-inflammatory state, consequently enhancing cellular GEM uptake by tumor cells. Overall, this dual-drug hydrogel platform integrates localized sustained release with macrophage-targeted microenvironment reprogramming, offering a promising strategy for synergistic chemo-immunotherapy against bladder cancer.

title: Influence of residual deformation fields on microstructural evolution during powder metallurgy hot isostatic pressing
abstract: The objective of this study is to understand how deformation fields and residual defects influence microstructure evolution during powder metallurgy hot isostatic pressing (PM-HIP). For this, gas-atomized Fe-10Cr-6.1Al powders are consolidated at 750°C and 1050°C at 100 MPa and 150 MPa for 3 h. The lower consolidation temperature corresponds to a kinetically intermediate stage of PM-HIP evolution, enabling observation of dynamic consolidation mechanisms through parametric effects. Numerous low-angle grain boundaries are observed at intermediate stages of the consolidation process. Results show that strain energy (from entrained low-angle grain boundaries and contact stresses) drives rapid recovery and recrystallization at the early stages of PM-HIP. But as strain energy is dissipated through defect annihilation and relaxation of contact stresses, microstructural evolution slows, and grain growth dominates the later stages of PM-HIP. In PM-HIP microstructure, isolated fine-grained particle artifacts are observed, which remain relatively undeformed, potentially due to delayed recovery-recrystallization kinetics associated with initial microstructure and/or localized stress and strain variations. This work reveals that residual deformation fields, together with PM-HIP processing parameters, can be used to kinetically trap the consolidated microstructure at desired stages along the recovery-recrystallization-grain growth process. Harnessing this concept enables us to design controlled material microstructure through advanced manufacturing.

title: Dislocation substructure evolution in type 304 stainless steel under high temperature non-proportional creep-fatigue loading
abstract: The macroscopic mechanical responses and microscopic deformation mechanisms under non-proportional loading conditions were systematically investigated for a type 304 stainless steel at 600 °C. The effects of strain paths, strain rates, and holding periods on the microstructural evolution were evaluated through transmission electron microscopy. The results show that the non-proportional loading forces the activation of multiple non-coplanar slip systems, inducing an additional hardening effect compared to proportional loading. Lamellar laths, labyrinth structures, deformation twins, and dislocation cells can be observed under different loading conditions. Furthermore, time dependent creep effects significantly enhance dynamic recovery, leading to marked cell coarsening and advanced dynamic carbide precipitation along the boundaries. The interaction between non-proportional loading and high temperature creep profoundly dictates microstructural evolution, underscoring the critical necessity of accounting for external operational factors in real applications.

title: Chemical short-range order as a conditional modifier of deformation and damage in void-containing high-entropy alloys under high-strain-rate loading
abstract: Chemical short-range order (SRO) can markedly affect the mechanical response of high-entropy alloys (HEAs), but its role in void-containing alloys under high-strain-rate loading remains unclear. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and a data-driven surrogate model were combined to investigate the tensile response of Al 0.3 FeCoCrNi HEAs with pre-existing nanoscale voids. The results reveal a coupling effect between structural defects and local chemical ordering. The size of pre-existing voids dominates yield onset, peak strength and damage evolution by intensifying stress concentration and promoting earlier plasticity. By contrast, SRO acts as a conditional atomic-scale modifier. For smaller voids, SRO improves tensile resistance by reducing active dislocation nucleation sites, confining early plastic zones, and promoting sessile reactions including Lomer-Cottrell locks and Hirth dislocations. This effect becomes less pronounced for larger voids, where deformation is increasingly governed by void-induced stress concentration. Temperature further constrains the SRO effect: SRO promotes twinning and organized planar-defect evolution at 300 K, whereas thermal activation suppresses twinning and causes diffuse post-yield defect accumulation at 1200 K. The proposed surrogate model provides an efficient mapping of the stress response and damage evolution across the studied parameter space. These findings identify SRO as a conditional design parameter for tuning defect tolerance in HEAs.

title: Role of interlaminar deformation mismatch in cure-induced stress evolution and distortion response of CFRP laminates
abstract: Cure-induced residual stress and distortion critically affect the dimensional accuracy and service performance of autoclave-cured carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates. However, the role of interlaminar deformation mismatch in residual stress and distortion remains insufficiently quantified. A three-dimensional sequentially coupled thermo–chemo–mechanical finite element model was developed, and interlaminar deformation mismatch was quantified from differences in stress-free thermal and cure-shrinkage strains between adjacent plies using a scalar mismatch index. The model accounts for cure exotherm, viscoelasticity, ply anisotropy, tooling constraints, and demolding, and its predictions agree well with published benchmark results. During cooling, the deformation mismatch between the 0° and 90° plies increases from about 5 × 10 −3 to above 12 × 10 −3 , contributing to a marked increase in the local through-thickness stress, which reaches approximately 27 MPa. For [ 0 / θ / θ / 0 ] laminates, the mismatch index increases with θ , thereby contributing to the corresponding increase in peak residual stress, whereas laminate–tool friction and curing pressure have limited effects on the overall stress distribution. Free-boundary effects promote local stress concentration, while unbalanced through-thickness mismatch in asymmetric laminates promotes warpage after demolding. These results identify interlaminar deformation mismatch as a dominant mechanism contributing to cure-induced residual stress and distortion.

title: Modifying structure and properties of CoCrCuxNiMoy (x = 0, 0.1, y = 0.1, 0.5, 1) MPEAs by chemical composition and laser-surface treatment
abstract: In this work, the structure and selected properties like corrosion resistance and hardness of CoCrCu x NiMo y (x = 0, 0.1, y = 0.1, 0.5, 1) alloys in the as-cast state and after laser surface treatment were characterized. The structural investigations confirmed that with a higher molybdenum addition, the ability to form a dual-phase structure composed of the FCC and the intermetallic phase increases, which leads to a decrease in corrosion resistance, but increases hardness. The addition of copper turned out to be beneficial for a single-phase CoCrCu 0.1 NiMo 0.1 alloy due to the best electrochemical parameters ( R p = 244 kΩcm 2 , j corr = 0.55 μA/cm 2 − as-cast state, R p = 320 kΩcm 2 , j corr = 0.04 μA/cm 2 − after laser surface treatment). In the dual-phase alloys, the FCC phase was enriched in copper, which led to higher Volta potential differences that promoted corrosion. Laser surface treatment resulted in grain refinement in the structure. Single-phase CoCrNiMo 0.1 alloy after laser surface treatment showed improved corrosion resistance and increased hardness compared to the as-cast state form. However, the CoCrCu 0.1 NiMo 0.1 alloy after laser surface treatment was characterized by the presence of copper-rich precipitates resulting lower corrosion resistance. The improvement in corrosion resistance and increased hardness depended on the share of the FCC and intermetallic phase.

title: Nb-mediated carbide transformation and tailored He+ irradiation damage in aged Ni-12Mo-7Cr alloy
abstract: Molten salt reactors employ GH3535-type Ni-Mo-Cr alloys, yet high-temperature He + irradiation induces severe He swelling and hardening that degrade service performance. This work investigates how 2 wt% Nb addition modifies carbide precipitation and irradiation responses in aged Ni-12Mo-7Cr alloys using first-principles calculations, electron microscopy and nanoindentation. DFT calculations yield a more negative formation energy for NbC (−0.55 eV/atom) than for Mo 2 C (−0.12 eV/atom), consistent with the observed transition from Mo-rich M 2 C to Nb-rich MC. The MC precipitates formed semi-coherent interfaces with the γ matrix, with an average misfit-dislocation spacing of 1.33 nm, and occurred as chains along parts of the grain boundaries. At 1.0 × 10 17 ions/cm 2 , the 2 wt% Nb alloy exhibited a lower measured mean swelling (1.9 % vs. 2.4 %) and a lower irradiation-hardening increment (0.94 vs. 1.25 GPa) under the present experimental conditions. Smaller local bubbles and wider bubble-depleted zones were observed near MC/γ interfaces and MC-modified grain boundaries. The overall irradiation response reflects the combined effects of residual solute Nb, localized carbide-related interfaces, and grain-boundary structure. This study offers experimental support for tailoring carbides to improve irradiation tolerance of Nb-alloyed Ni-Mo-Cr alloys.

title: A comparative study of transformer models and recurrent neural networks for path-dependent composite materials
abstract: Accurate modeling of Short Fiber Reinforced Composites (SFRCs) remains computationally expensive for full-field simulations. Data-driven surrogate models using artificial neural networks have been proposed as an efficient alternative to numerical modeling, where Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are increasingly being used for path-dependent multiscale modeling. However, recently, transformer models have been developed and they offer scalability and efficient parallelization, yet have not been systematically compared with RNNs in this field. In this study, we perform a systematic comparison between RNNs and transformer models trained on sequences of homogenized response of SFRC. We study the effect of two types of hyperparameters, namely architectural hyperparameters (such as the number of GRU layers, hidden size, number of attention heads, and encoder blocks) and training hyperparameters (such as learning rate and batch size). Both sets of hyperparameters are tuned using Bayesian optimization. We then analyze scaling laws with respect to dataset size and inference accuracy in interpolation and extrapolation regimes. Results show that while transformer models remain competitive in terms of accuracy on large datasets, the RNNs demonstrate better accuracy on small datasets. Furthermore, under extrapolation, the RNN is more accurate, while the transformer is seven times faster at inference when evaluating complete sequences offline.

title: Microstructural fatigue damage mechanisms in the coarse-grained heat-affected zone of A514 welded joints from a multi-scale perspective
abstract: The CGHAZ is the fundamental mechanical weak link of A514 high-strength steel welded joints. Traditional nominal stress methods fail to capture its localized degradation, leading to unsafe fatigue life predictions. To address this empirical limitation, this study proposes a novel multi-scale fatigue evaluation paradigm coupling macroscopic thermodynamic energy dissipation with mesoscopic dislocation dynamics. Through in-situ infrared thermography and EBSD tracking under cyclic loading, a highly synchronized bilinear bifurcation phenomenon was discovered across multiple scales. Macroscopically, the steady-state temperature increment exhibits a thermodynamic bifurcation at a stress amplitude of 436.86 MPa. Microscopically, the evolution of geometrically necessary dislocations reveals corresponding crystallographic thresholds at 437.89 MPa. This astonishing cross-scale numerical agreement unveils the physical essence of the fatigue limit by demonstrating that the macroscopic thermal energy bifurcation is intrinsically driven by the avalanche-like collapse of internal dislocation structures caused by cyclic-hardening exhaustion. Compared to the traditional S-N curve method (450 MPa) , this physically rigorous multi-scale method provides a more accurate and conservative life prediction, establishing a robust theoretical framework for the anti-fatigue design of welded structures under extreme conditions.

title: Phase prediction of high-entropy alloys via transfer learning with domain adaptation and oversampling
abstract: Accurate phase prediction is critical for customized high-entropy alloys (HEAs) design. Machine learning has been widely adopted to improve their phase classification accuracy, but limited samples and phase imbalance remain challenging. Herein, we developed a deep learning-based transfer learning scheme from sputtered-state to as-cast alloys. Domain adaptation method together with a multi-kernel MMD loss function is embedded to align feature distributions across different fabrication processes, and SMOTE oversampling is employed to balance the sample sizes of various phase categories between the source and target domains. For as-cast Al-Co-Cr-Cu-Fe-Ni-Mn alloy system, the developed model achieves 94 % in both precision and recall for four phase types-FCC, BCC, FCC + BCC and IM-outperforming traditional ML models by 15.6 % and 30.6 %, respectively. Validation using independent external samples also demonstrates its generalization capability. SHAP analysis reveals the influence patterns of empirical parameters and elements on HEAs phase formation. Composition-phase mapping confirm the dominant role of Al in IM formation and identifiy that Cr significantly stabilizes the FCC phase in Al-free alloys. Further experimental validation across the four phase types corroborates the model’s superior predictive performance. This work provides an effective recipe for HEAs phase prediction and lays a methodological foundation for cross-process knowledge transfer in alloy design.

title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
abstract: We present a high-dimensional neural network potential (HDNNP) for the martensitic phase of the NiTi shape-memory alloy trained to density functional theory (DFT) data. A central aspect of this work is the systematic validation of the potential with respect to the underlying DFT reference method for key properties governing structural evolution, including equilibrium crystal structures, elastic constants, generalized-stacking fault energies, and vibrational spectra. The HDNNP accurately describes the relative stability of the B19$^\prime$ and B33 phases, including subtle energy differences on the order of meV/atom. The predicted stacking-fault energy landscape is strongly anisotropic and reveals a preferential shear pathway, providing atomistic insight into deformation and twinning mechanisms. Finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations further enable the investigation of unconstrained structural evolution as a function of temperature. Overall, the developed HDNNP provides a robust basis for atomistic simulations of the complex structural and functional behavior of martensitic NiTi systems containing hundreds of thousands of atoms on nanosecond time scales.

title: An elastic core/shell nanofiber cardiac patch with Prussian Blue nanozymes and ultrasound responsive NO donor for myocardium infarction therapy
abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) is characterized by excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and insufficient nitric oxide (NO), driving progressive cardiac dysfunction. Here we develop an elastic core/shell nanofiber cardiac patch (PCL–B/SF–PB) to address this by integrating ultrasound (US)–responsive NO delivery with catalytic ROS scavenging. The patch loaded BNN6 and Prussian Blue nanozyme (PB) for ROS elimination. Under US irradiation, the coordinated action of NO release and ROS scavenging synergistically alleviates oxidative stress and enhances NO bioactivity. In vitro , this cooperative system promotes endothelial cell function, and protects H9C2 cardiomyocytes from oxidative damage by preserving mitochondrial integrity. In a mouse MI model, PCL-B/SF-PB implantation combined with US treatment significantly elevated local NO levels while reducing ROS and its reaction with NO. This dual-functional strategy attenuated cardiomyocyte apoptosis, promoted neovascularization, reduced fibrosis, and improves cardiac function, with no systemic toxicity. Our findings demonstrate that spatiotemporally controlled NO release coupled with catalytic ROS scavenging PB provides a potent synergistic strategy for MI therapy.

title: AI-enabled knowledge mapping of microfluidics research: Scientometric analysis and sentence-transformer-based bertopic modeling
abstract: Over the past decade, microfluidics research has expanded rapidly across disciplines, creating a need for comprehensive data-driven synthesis. Here, we present an AI-enabled knowledge map of microfluidics research from 2014 to 2024 using a Scopus-indexed corpus (N = 18,907). We analyzed bibliometric indicators, VOSviewer-based collaboration and keyword co-occurrence networks, and temporal profiles of dominant materials and applications. To capture semantic structure beyond bibliographic metadata, transformer-based topic modeling (BERTopic) was applied to a filtered subset of English-language articles and reviews with sufficient textual metadata (n = 14,026). This enabled the extraction of coherent research themes, quantification of topic dynamics, and identification of emerging research fronts using an EmergingScore framework. The results show sustained publication and citation growth, with Lab on a Chip identified as a prominent journal in the field. The United States and China dominate research output, while increasing multi-country publications indicate growing global collaboration. Materials profiling shows the continued prominence of paper/cellulose and PDMS, the sustained relevance of glass as a platform material, and the emergence of hydrogels and 3D-printed resins. Biosensing and bioanalytical applications remain prevalent, followed by cancer/tumor modeling and point-of-care diagnostics. Topic robustness was evaluated against random baselines and benchmarked against Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) using coherence and distinctiveness metrics

title: Bridging the gap in craniomaxillofacial bone defects: between clinical practice, experimental developments and shifts in bone-tissue engineering strategies
abstract: Craniomaxillofacial bone defects represent a global public health issue, as well as a major challenge for biomaterials design, as the facial skeleton is involved in essential functions (e.g. mastication, phonation) while shaping individual identity through facial aesthetics. The clinical demand for autograft alternatives has driven the development of synthetic substitutes; yet, none have achieved comparable clinical success, and translation into commercially viable products remains a critical bottleneck that limits the emergence of innovative solutions. Unlike broader reviews focused on biomaterial classes or biological material manipulation, this work aims at clearing out the considerable grey area that persists between novel experimental developments, established surgical procedures and commercial synthetic biomaterials for craniomaxillofacial defects through a comparative assessment of their performances and limitation. Particular attention is given to extracellular–matrix–mimicking biomaterials and in situ bone-tissue engineering, which offer the prospect of reducing the complexity, cost, and regulatory burden associated with cell-based therapies. Building on our current understanding of cell-biomaterials interactions, this work proposes biomimetic design guidelines for next-generation acellular biocomposites, emphasizing how biological mechanisms affect engineered biomaterials and how these interactions ultimately shape clinical outcomes. Finally, advanced manufacturing technologies are discussed as a promising avenue towards innovative and clinically translatable substitutes for craniomaxillofacial defects.

title: Tailoring alkali-activated red mud–waste glass binders through an effective silicate modulus: The influence of partial glass dissolution on network polymerisation and strength
abstract: Conventional silicate modulus calculations may overestimate the reactive silica available when solid silica sources are used in alkali-activated binders because only a fraction dissolves during activation. This study introduces an effective silicate modulus ( M s , e f f ) that incorporates the measured three-day silica dissolution efficiency ( η = 0.32) of waste glass powder (WGP) to guide its use in reducing commercial sodium silicate demand in alkali-activated red mud binders. Mixtures combining four target M s , e f f values (1.0–2.5) and four WGP replacement levels (0–40 wt%) were activated with 10 M NaOH at a constant externally supplied Na 2 O equivalent of 5 wt% and liquid-to-binder ratio of 0.5, followed by curing at 70 °C for 24 h. Reaction, microstructural, thermal, and mechanical characteristics were evaluated. WGP addition accelerated the reaction and increased the silicon content of the reacted matrix. At M s , e f f = 2.0 , the mixture containing 40 % WGP reached a 28-day compressive strength of 21.10 MPa, compared with 11.85 MPa for the WGP-free mixture, corresponding to an improvement of 78.1 %, while using 43.2 % less commercial sodium silicate and 68.1 % less sodium silicate per unit compressive strength. Within the investigated conditions, M s , e f f provides a composition-based framework for incorporating partially dissolving waste silica while reducing dependence on manufactured silicate activators.

title: Explainable machine learning framework for design and performance optimization of MOF-TFN FO membranes
abstract: The escalating need for efficient and sustainable water-treatment solutions has placed MOF-incorporated TFN FO membranes at the forefront of membrane research thanks to their notable potential for seawater desalination and wastewater treatment, largely due to their capacity for high Water Flux (Jw) coupled with suppressed Reverse Solute Flux (Js). Still, a persistent and often frustrating challenge lies in navigating the inherent trade-off between Jw and Js. In this study, we turn to machine learning (ML) for a more systematic membrane design and performance optimization strategy. Beyond prediction, we sought to open the “black box” and understand why certain membrane compositions and operating conditions lead to better outcomes. Through Pearson correlation analysis, SHAP-based feature importance, single- and two-variable PDPs, DML causal-effect heterogeneity analysis, and feature-guided uncertainty-aware stepwise PSO we identified not only which structural and operational parameters matter most, but also how they interact—sometimes in non-intuitive ways. The main contribution of this study lies in integrating all these techniques into a complete ML framework, which not only delivers robust, data-driven performance predictions for MOF-TFN FO membranes, but also provides actionable guidance for their design and optimization, reinforcing the value of ML as a tool for innovation in membrane technology

title: Factors determining the enzymatic degradation of PLA/PHBV blends
abstract: Blends of poly(lactic acid) and poly(hydroxybutyrat-co-valerate) were prepared in the entire composition range to compensate the deficiencies of the components and prepare materials with optimal properties including biodegradability. The polymers were homogenized by extrusion and then injection molded into plates with different thickness to study its effect on enzymatic degradation. Five enzymes were selected for the preliminary study, and then degradation was followed as a function of time. Many factors influence the degradation of injection-molded specimens. Besides composition, the crystallinity and structure of PHBV proved to be the main factors determining the rate and extent of degradation. Structure is very complex including skin-core morphology, orientation, surface area, and the differences in the structure of injection molded and cut surfaces. PLA and PHBV are immiscible, and their blends have a heterogeneous dispersed structure, but the interaction of the two components is not negligible, and thus influences both structure and degradation. Enzymatic degradation proceeds in three steps and the modeling of degradation kinetics together with the analysis of the dependence of the parameters helps the identification and understanding of the factors influencing degradation. In this study, basically only PLA degrades in the blends and the presence of PHBV controls its degradation.

title: Thermosensitive PEGylated niosome-loaded dissolving microneedles for localized co-delivery of gemcitabine and paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains a major clinical challenge due to its aggressiveness and limited therapeutic options. This study developed a hierarchical nano-micro platform for localized gemcitabine (Gem) and paclitaxel (PTX) co-delivery using PEGylated thermosensitive niosomes integrated into dissolving microneedles (DMNs). Niosomes (∼150 nm) prepared by thin-film hydration exhibited a phase transition at 41–42 °C and were incorporated into bilayer PVA/PVP DMNs fabricated by micromolding. The arrays demonstrated mechanical strength up to 200 N and 84% dissolution within 60 s. Ex vivo studies confirmed skin penetration of approximately 1100 μm. Under acidic pH and mild hyperthermia (pH 6.5, 42 °C), drug release exceeded 97% within 192 h. Entrapment efficiencies reached 74% for Gem and 80% for PTX. In MDA-MB-231 cells, co-loaded niosomes exhibited greater cytotoxicity than single-drug formulations and free drugs, particularly under hyperthermic conditions. Flow cytometry revealed 77% total apoptosis, while real-time PCR showed upregulation of BAX (7.77-fold) and P53 (11.5-fold) and downregulation of BCL2 and MMP-2 (p < 0.0001). The platform remained stable for three months. This thermosensitive niosome-in-DMN system offers a promising minimally invasive strategy for localized, stimuli-responsive chemotherapy against TNBC

title: A strategy for considering material anisotropy and nonlinearity in translaminar fracture prediction of 3D-printed notched PLA plates with cross-ply layups
abstract: This study aims to investigate the fracture behavior of additively manufactured polylactic acid (PLA) notched three-point bending (TPB) specimens with a cross-ply layup under Mode I loading. Notched specimens with various tip radii are prepared using fused deposition modeling (FDM) technique and tested for Mode I fracture under TPB. Subsequently, a simplified notch fracture toughness (NFT) prediction approach is proposed by combining the virtual isotropic material concept (VIMC) with the modified equivalent material concept (MEMC). This approach indirectly considers the effects of material anisotropy and nonlinearity through equivalent material representations. NFT values are estimated using mean stress (MS), maximum tangential stress (MTS), and averaged strain energy density (ASED) criteria, as well as extended finite element method (XFEM) coupled with a cohesive zone model (CZM). Incorporating MEMC improves predictions in most cases; however, VIMC-MEMC-ASED approach shows reduced prediction accuracy for U-notched specimens, indicating a geometry-dependent limitation of this particular formulation. VIMC-MEMC-MS approach provides the most accurate estimates with average discrepancies of 0.6% for U-notches and 1.3% for RV-notches. Qualitative microscopy observations further indicate that, although crack growth follows the notch bisector at the macroscopic scale, differences in notch geometry are associated with observable differences in fracture-surface morphology and microscopic crack-growth features.

title: Application of compressive stress during high-speed laser welding to mitigate transverse hot cracking in a 6000-series aluminum alloy
abstract: The industrial applicability of laser welding for joining sheets made from high-strength aluminum alloys is often limited by the formation of transverse hot cracks in the weld seam, which reduces the mechanical performance of the joint. Previous studies have attributed transverse hot cracking to insufficient feeding of melt into the intergranular region due to a drop in static pressure in the melt pool. To address this issue, we propose using a clamping device to counteract the static pressure drop by applying uniaxial mechanical compressive stress transverse to the welding direction to compress the area around the melt pool. The release of transverse compressive stress during welding of a 6000-series aluminum alloy was experimentally monitored with a force sensor. The local transverse strain was simultaneously analyzed by means of digital image correlation. The findings demonstrate that the release of transverse compressive stress during welding increases the local transverse compressive strain. Using metallographic analysis, a decrease in the number of transverse hot cracks in the weld seam by a factor of up to four was observed when a transverse compressive stress of –30 MPa was applied, as compared to the compressive stress of –0.5 MPa present under the standard clamping conditions.

title: Development of anisotropic sintering analytical model and numerical simulation for stainless steel 316 L fabricated by material extrusion additive manufacturing
abstract: Material extrusion (MEX) processing, utilizing a composite filament formulated with a mixture of highly filled metal and binder, can be served as an economical and efficient method for creating dense metal components. As a key step, sintering plays a decisive role in controlling the dimensional accuracy and structural integrity of the final parts. Consequently, there is a growing need to gain an in-depth understanding on the anisotropic shrinkage that occurs during sintering. In this work, a novel analytical model based on sintering continuum theory and three-dimensional dilatometry test was developed to comprehensively decipher the anisotropic shrinkage behavior of stainless steel (SS) 316 L during MEX. Such an anisotropic phenomenological model can help elucidate the temperature-dependent diffusion mechanisms throughout sintering, enabling a rapid identification method of parameters and the prediction of porosity evolution. The error between numerical simulation prediction and experimental results for three-dimensional deformation was less than 10 %. The anisotropic sintering shrinkage mechanism was thoroughly elucidated from the perspectives of both anisotropic viscous behavior and heat transfer theory. The findings in this work will provide insights into the anisotropic sintering mechanisms of MEX-built SS 316 L, paving the way for the shape-property optimization of metal parts created through sintering-based AM.

title: Cross-attentive PINN modeling of Cu-Ni interdiffusion in variable thickness Sn-2.5Ag solder joints
abstract: The aim of this study is to unravel the coupled effects of under-bump metallization (UBM) configuration, solder joint thickness, and joining sequence on interfacial intermetallic compound (IMC) formation, Cu-Ni cross-diffusion kinetics, and long-term reliability in microelectronic solder joints-a critical challenge for three-dimensional integrated circuit packaging. Symmetric Cu/Sn-2.5Ag/Cu, Ni/Sn-2.5Ag/Ni, and asymmetric Cu/Sn-2.5Ag/Ni copper pillar microbumps were fabricated and subjected to thermal cycling tests (TCTs, − 55 ∘ C to 125 ∘ C , up to 1000 cycles), with asymmetric joints processed via two pathways: Cu-first (Path I) and Ni-first (Path II). Characterization revealed (Cu,Ni) 6 Sn 5 at both interfaces in Cu-based joints, Ni 3 Sn 4 in Ni-based systems, and path- and height-dependent (Cu,Ni) 6 Sn 5 variation in asymmetric joints. Kirkendall voids formed extensively in Cu 3 Sn of symmetric Cu/Cu joints but were suppressed in asymmetric configurations, indicating superior reliability. To elucidate cross-diffusion mechanisms, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) simulated coupled solute transport in liquid solder across variable thicknesses and boundary concentrations. Building on these solutions, CuNiCrossDiffusionLLM-a transformer-inspired cross-attention interpolation framework with natural language query reasoning enabled rapid, physically consistent predictions of concentration fields, fluxes, and uphill diffusion without retraining. The framework shows that Cu-Ni cross-interaction accelerates diffusion fronts relative to self-diffusion, with thinner layers exhibiting intensified fluxes and pronounced uphill diffusion, where Cu’s steeper gradient drives stronger Ni uphill transport near zero-flux planes. These findings explain accelerated IMC growth in thinner joints and establish a digital-twin platform for parametric design, process optimization, and reliability assessment, bridging fundamental diffusion physics with engineering applications.

title: Injectable functionalized viscoelastic hydrogel for promoting microstructural reconstruction of rotator cuff tendon-bone insertion
abstract: Effective reconstruction of the tendon-to-bone interface (TBI) is a significant challenge in rotator cuff tear (RCT) repair, primarily due to the inability of current methods to regenerate the native enthesis structure. In this study, we developed and compared two multifunctional hydrogels designed to enhance enthesis healing: a silk fibroin-based SHO hydrogel (SF/HAMA/ODOHA) and a synthetic PHO hydrogel (4-arm PEGMA/HAMA/ODOHA). Both hydrogels incorporate dopamine-modified hyaluronic acid (ODOHA) for wet adhesion through catechol-mediated bonding and are functionalized with the E7 peptide to promote mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) recruitment and osteo-induction. Using a surgically created rabbit infraspinatus tear model, we found that hydrogel-treated repairs yielded superior micro-CT, histological, and biomechanical outcomes compared to direct suturing. Histological staining indicated enhanced continuity and fibrocartilage-like matrix formation at the repair interface, while biomechanical testing revealed improvements in failure parameters. In vitro analyses showed changes in markers related to osteogenic, chondrogenic, and tenogenic differentiation. These findings warrant further investigation of the hydrogels for tendon-to-bone repair, although they do not demonstrate complete reconstruction of the native enthesis or efficacy in chronic or large rotator cuff tears. The SHO formulation indicated promising repair outcomes, though the synergistic interaction between ODOHA and E7 remains unproven.

title: Two-dimensional cellular material optimization for additive manufacturing of sandwich panels
abstract: Mass reduction for aerospace structures is critical to reduce rocket launch costs. With this aim, we propose a two-dimensional cellular material optimization to stiffen sandwich panels via cellular redistribution within the core based on the Voronoï tesselation. A blackbox optimizer maximizes the panel stiffness by controlling local cellular density using a weight map and the weighted Voronoï stippling technique. The stiffest configuration was printed using Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF) along with a standard hexagonal honeycomb panel with a similar mass for comparison purposes. Both panels, simply supported on their edges were subject to a central load. The measured stiffness and maximal load in the elastic regime increased by 58% and 71% after optimization, respectively. The developed optimization algorithm is applied to the sandwich panel representing the demonstrator of a lunar rover's frame to minimize the maximal shear stress in its core during the launch environment. Starting with a centroidal Voronoï tesselation (CVT) configuration, the structure achieved a 65% reduction in maximal shear stress with an 11% reduction in core mass. By enabling localized control over cellular density with constant wall thickness compatible with FFF, the developed methodology offers a framework for the next generation of mass-optimized, high-performance aerospace structures.

title: Gyroid-primitive TPMS scaffold combinations for porous canine hip stems: structural, hemodynamic, and biomechanical evaluation
abstract: Additive manufacturing has enabled the development of porous biomimetic implants designed to better replicate the mechanical and fluidic characteristics of native bone while reducing stress shielding associated with conventional solid implants. This study investigated the structural and hemodynamic performance of Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) based porous scaffolds for potential application in load-bearing bone implants. TPMS Gyroid and Primitive architectures were combined at different weighing coefficients to generate nine weighted scaffold configurations. Their mechanical performance was evaluated through axial compression simulations and experiments, while computational fluid dynamics was used to assess permeability, wall shear stress and flow characteristics. Selected scaffolds were subsequently incorporated into canine hip stem models and evaluated under physiological loading conditions using finite element analysis (FEA). The results demonstrated that Gyroid-dominant architectures exhibited mechanical and permeability characteristics closer to those of native bone. The 90% Gyroid - 10% Primitive (i.e. G90P10) hip stem showed the lowest stress shielding while maintaining micromotion within the range favorable for bone growth. Fatigue analysis indicated adequate structural safety, with all porous hip stems exhibiting ideal fatigue life and safety factors Although further experimental and in vivo validation is required, the study establishes a systematic computational framework for the design and preclinical assessment of TPMS based porous implants and proposes novel porous hip stem configurations as potential alternatives to conventional solid stems.

title: Accumulative extrusion bonding of Cu/Nb multilayered tubes: Process design and realization
abstract: Accumulative extrusion bonding (AEB) is a severe plastic deformation process capable of producing multilayered metallic architectures with ultrafine grains and high densities of sharp internal interfaces. In this work, AEB was applied to copper and niobium (Cu and Nb) to produce a novel multilayered tubular product. Two-layer Cu/Nb tubes were experimentally fabricated at 55% and 66% radial deformation, and four-layer Cu/Nb tubes were fabricated at 55% radial deformation, establishing a practical AEB route for Cu/Nb bimetallic tubes. The experimental route included surface preparation by acetone cleaning and scratch brushing, stacking with a controlled slip fit, extrusion, expansion, and intermediate annealing. Peel testing was performed to ensure the quality of bonding. Results in terms of measured interfacial bond strength showed that increasing radial deformation from 55% to 66% approximately doubled the measured average peel strength from 2.6 to 5.3 N/mm, although different die-half angles were used. Additionally, axisymmetric finite element (FE) plasticity simulations were performed in ABAQUS to evaluate the effects of key extrusion parameters including deformation, die half-angle, and coefficient of friction on through-wall equivalent plastic strain and extrusion force. Predicted strain distributions and processing loads helped assess process sensitivity and refine the practical AEB route for Cu/Nb tube fabrication.

title: Asiatic acid-based injectable nanohydrogel attenuates osteoarthritis by disrupting CCL17-associated macrophage–chondrocyte crosstalk
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease-causing pain and disability. To identify anti-inflammatory agents, we screened natural compounds and found asiatic acid (AA) effective against inflammatory macrophage activation, yet its poor solubility and bioavailability limit use. To overcome this, AA was polymerized into poly(asiatic acid) (PAA), self-assembled into nanoparticles (PAA NPs), and further modified with folic acid (FA-PAA NPs) for macrophage targeting. These NPs were incorporated into a hydroxypropyl chitin hydrogel (HPCH) to form an injectable sustained-release platform (FA-PAA@HPCH). This system showed good injectability, temperature-responsive gelation, and prolonged release. FA modification markedly enhanced uptake by inflammatory macrophages. FA-PAA@HPCH suppressed pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, favored an anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype, and reduced ROS. Antibody microarray analysis identified reduced CCL17 secretion, while transcriptomic analysis implicated TNF-related signaling as a candidate pathway associated with treatment. Recombinant CCL17 partially reversed the protective effects on chondrocytes, supporting a contribution of CCL17 to macrophage–chondrocyte inflammatory communication. In an ACL transection‑induced OA model, FA-PAA@HPCH alleviated synovial inflammation, preserved cartilage, improved subchondral bone, and showed favorable biocompatibility under the tested conditions. Collectively, this study supports further investigation of CCL17-associated inflammatory communication and an AA-based immunomodulatory hydrogel strategy for OA treatment.

title: Enhancement of strength–ductility balance in heterogeneous nanostructured Cu–Zn alloys by texture control and dense mechanical twinning during early-stage rolling
abstract: Rectangular specimens cut from hot-extruded Cu–Zn alloy bars were subjected to unidirectional rolling and rotational rolling. In rotational rolling, the specimens were rotated 90° around the rolling direction once or three times before further rolling to a total reduction of 90%. The effects of the rolling process design on texture evolution, mechanical twinning, heterogeneous nanostructure (HN-structure) formation, and mechanical properties were investigated. At 50% reduction, the fraction of grains containing Σ3 twin boundaries, including retained annealing and deformation twins, increased from 66% for unidirectional rolling to 77% and 85% for one and three rotations, respectively. This increase was associated with rotation-induced texture reorientation toward twinning-favorable orientations. After 90% reduction, all specimens contained HN-structures consisting of eye-shaped twin domains, shear bands, and low-angle lamellae. The three-time rotationally rolled specimen exhibited higher twin-domain number density and apparent area fraction, along with an ultimate tensile strength of 820 MPa and a fracture strain of 10%. Digital image correlation revealed local strain partitioning in the unidirectionally rolled specimen. Loading–unloading–reloading tests indicated higher estimated heterogeneous deformation-induced stress after three rotations. These results suggest that early-stage texture modification effectively promotes mechanical twinning and improves the tensile performance of HN-structured materials.

title: Deciphering the passivation mechanism of Ti‑35421 alloy: linking microstructure to passive film properties via the point defect model
abstract: Passivation behavior of near-β titanium alloys is critically influenced by the microstructure. However, the mechanistic link between microstructure and passive film property remains inadequately understood. The present work investigated the passive behavior of Ti-35421 alloy with different α-phase morphologies through microstructural (SEM/TEM/EBSD) and electrochemical calculations from the perspective of Point Defect Model (PDM). The results showed that passive film of Ti alloy with α lath+equiaxed structure showed superior protective quality over α lamellar and α lath+secondary structures, which was consistent with the oxygen-vacancy flux within the passive film. At a film-formation potential of 0.6 V SCE , Ti-35421 alloy with α lath+equiaxed structure had an apparent donor density of 1.37 × 10 26 m −3 , an adopted high-field vacancy diffusivity of 5.64 × 10 −22 m 2 ·s −1 and a calculated field-driven vacancy flux J P of 4.01 × 10 14 m −2 ·s −1 . The α lath+equiaxed structure presented the lowest dislocation density and the highest metal/film interface potential drop, which facilitates the lowest donor density and the smallest vacancy flux, thereby explaining its superior corrosion resistance. The associated microstructural and defect-transport trends provide a PDM-consistent interpretation of the passivation mechanism of Ti‑35421 Alloy.

title: Substructure–enabled dynamic strain aging and κ-carbide nano-precipitation in a high-SFE Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steel
abstract: Classical theories predict that dynamic-strain-aging (DSA) should be strongly suppressed in high stacking-fault-energy (SFE) Fe–Mn–Al–C steels, because narrow, temperature-sensitive stacking-fault widths limit solute–dislocation interaction times. Contrary to these expectations, we demonstrate that a high-SFE lightweight steel exhibits pronounced DSA from 100-to-500 °C, a regime traditionally considered unlikely. Despite serrated-flow and negative strain-rate-sensitivity, the alloy retains remarkably stable ductility and work-hardening capability, revealing a fundamentally non-classical DSA response that is not governed by conventional stacking-fault-mediated solute–dislocation interactions. Electron-backscatter-diffraction shows rapid formation of a boundary-rich substructure consisting of dense low-angle-boundaries and refined subgrains that concentrate mobile dislocations at interfaces. This deformation-generated-network acts as a fast-diffusion scaffold that enables stress-assisted pipe and boundary diffusion of interstitial and substitutional solutes, activating a DSA mechanism independent of stacking-fault-mediated interactions. Transmission electron microscopy and selected-area diffraction reveal ordering-like nanoscale domains consistent with deformation-assisted short-range-ordering near 300 °C and a transition to κ-carbide(L′1 2 ) nanoprecipitation above 500 °C, indicating that deformation-induced solute redistribution associated with the DSA regime may facilitate subsequent κ-phase formation at higher temperatures. These findings uncover a previously unreported substructure-assisted DSA mechanism in high-SFE steels, explain the coexistence of strong DSA and sustained ductility, and establish a mechanistic link between warm-temperature DSA, dynamic ordering, and κ-carbide precipitation.

title: Gas-mediated surface design of medical latex catheters by microwave jet plasma: Coupling chemistry, morphology, and wettability
abstract: Medical latex catheters are widely used for urinary drainage, but their predominantly nonpolar surfaces exhibit limited aqueous wettability, motivating modification to facilitate aqueous-solution spreading during subsequent functionalization or coating. Plasma-induced wetting improvement is often associated with oxygen enrichment, yet whether oxygen content alone explains gas-dependent differences remains unclear. Here, latex catheter surfaces were treated using 2.45 GHz atmospheric-pressure microwave jet plasma with air, O 2 , N 2 , and Ar. Contact-angle measurements, scanning electron microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy linked wettability with morphology and chemical states. At 120 W, 120 s, 12 mm, and 13 L/min, air produced the lowest water contact angle of 27.65 ± 2.76 ∘ within 5 min. Air and Ar yielded similar O/C ratios but different contact angles, with air showing a larger apparent bound-oxygen contribution from O 1 s fitting. O 2 caused pronounced fissures and localized peeling without increasing retained surface oxygen. All groups exhibited hydrophobic recovery over 72 h, with air-treated specimens approaching the untreated reference. Air therefore provided the strongest initial wetting improvement within the tested window, while total oxygen enrichment alone could not explain the gas-dependent response. These findings support considering retained chemical states alongside morphology and aging when designing hydrophilic latex surfaces.

title: Predicting grain growth evolution under complex thermal profiles with deep learning through thermal descriptor modulation
abstract: Predicting microstructure evolution during thermomechanical treatment is essential for determining the final mechanical properties of a material, yet conventional simulations based on Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) remain computationally expensive. Our prior Deep Learning (DL) framework using Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) has proven effective in accelerating grain growth prediction, though its applicability was limited to constant-temperature or single-rate thermal profiles. As the model was trained exclusively under constant thermal conditions, it cannot account for the thermal history dependence of grain boundary kinetics, fundamentally limiting its applicability to the time-varying thermal profiles characteristic of industrial heat treatment processes. This study extends the previous framework by incorporating Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) for thermal conditioning to predict grain growth under complex, time-varying thermal profiles. The model was trained on a large dataset of grain growth evolution under thermal profiles with heating and cooling rates ranging from 0.01 kelvin per second to 10 kelvin per second. The results demonstrate that the proposed thermal conditioning mechanism enables the model to capture the influence of variable thermal profiles on grain boundary migration kinetics. Across the three test scenarios of increasing complexity, the model achieved a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of up to 0.93 and mean grain size error below 3.2%. Despite the architectural extensions, inference time remains on the order of seconds per prediction sequence, preserving the computational advantage over PDE-based simulations.

title: Balancing barrier consumption and interfacial delamination in Ni-barriered Bi2Te3 thermoelectric joints
abstract: Ni is widely used as a barrier layer in Bi 2 Te 3 -based thermoelectric devices, establishing the joints that connect thermoelectric legs with electrodes. This study demonstrates that the thickness of the nickel (Ni) diffusion barrier is one of the decisive parameter controlling this trade-off by governing the fundamental interfacial failure mode. Through a combination of accelerated aging (up to 120 h at 200 ℃), microstructural analysis, and thermo-mechanical characterization, we reveal a thickness-dependent change: thin barriers (<9.11 μm) fail by consumption of Ni barrier and severe interdiffusion, however, the thick-layer barrier layer (>11.10 μm) failed due to the deterioration of interface bonding, causing the Ni barrier to peel off and resulting in a sharp decline in shear strength. The range is valid for isothermal aging at 200 ℃ without applied temperature gradient, compressive load, or current. The thermoelectric conversion efficiency exhibits a gradual decrease with thickness increasing, attributed to increased resistance. Crucially, this work reveals the thickness-triggered difference of failure modes at the interface of Bi 2 Te 3 -based thermoelectric devices and establishes the interplay among diffusion barrier effectiveness, mechanical integrity, and electrical performance degradation.

title: A machine-learning-based shear lag model for accurate analysis of the bending behavior of sandwich beams
abstract: The bending behavior of sandwich beams is significantly affected by the shear deformation of the soft core layer, which transfers normal stress between the upper and lower hard surface layers. However, due to prior assumptions about deformation distribution or difficulty in accurately describing boundary conditions, existing bending theories cannot accurately predict the mechanical behavior. In this paper, a machine-learning-based shear lag model is proposed, which aims to predict stress and deformation fields using a physics-informed neural networks method, without priori assumptions or closed-form boundary conditions. It shows that all stress and deformation predictions are in good agreement with finite element simulation results (with errors less than 10%), with better accuracy than the existing Newmark shear lag model. Furthermore, either a larger modulus difference or a smaller thickness difference between surface and core layers not only increases the normal stress in the hard surface layer, but also reduces bending stiffness, which is beneficial for improving the load transfer efficiency and toughness. Comparing with finite element results, the applicability of the model for modulus and thickness ratios of the surface/core layers is ultimately clarified. This study provides a reliable theoretical tool for guiding the design of sandwich structures with ideal properties.

title: Microsphere-in-gel material design for improved delivery of α-terpineol in periodontitis: A pilot pre-clinical study
abstract: Aim This study aimed to fabricate and evaluate α-terpineol (AT) loaded microsphere (mAT)-embedded gel (mATs-G) for the treatment of periodontal infections. Methods α-Terpineol-loaded ethyl cellulose microspheres were prepared by a modified solvent evaporation method, and subsequently embedded in a chitosan-HPMC gel to form a hybrid depot. The system was characterized within a structure–property framework, including percentage yield, surface morphology, drug loading and encapsulation efficiency, mucoadhesive behaviour, rheological properties, and in vitro release kinetics. The influence of the microsphere-in-gel architecture on functional performance was evaluated in vitro and in vivo . Results FTIR study confirmed compatibility of AT and the tested excipients. Experimental mATs were spherical, with smooth surfaces, 11.8 ± 1.2% (w/w) AT loading, 89.85 ± 2.3% (w/w) loading efficiency, 77 ± 1.5% (w/w) mucoadhesion with sustained release of AT over 24 h. mATs-G showed good spreadability (6.2 ± 2.2 g·cm/s), extrudability (76.72 ± 0.8%), and viscosity (39,534 ± 2.1 cP). mATs-G showed effective antibacterial activity (ZOI, MBC) against periodontal bacteria, marked improvement in vivo , and docking predicted α-terpineol-protein interactions. Conclusion The microsphere-in-gel system is a promising periodontal delivery platform with sustained and localized release and antibacterial activity. Additional preclinical studies are needed to further validate its efficacy and safety

title: Endpoint compatibility and attachment dependent strain in morphing skins under prescribed rotation
Stimuli-responsive microneedles for rheumatoid arthritis: from responsive drug delivery to immunomodulation and osteochondral protection
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) causes synovial inflammation and progressive cartilage and bone damage despite advances in disease-modifying treatment. Microneedle systems offer a minimally invasive route across the skin barrier, while stimulus-responsive carriers may regulate release, activation or transport. This review critically maps the locations and mechanisms of responsive modules, including reactive-oxygen-species-labile linkages, acid-dissolving inorganic inclusions, adenosine-triphosphate-sensitive deoxyribonucleic acid assemblies and externally controlled delivery. It distinguishes genuine stimulus-dependent release from antioxidant action, biomimetic targeting, sustained delivery and device-controlled transport. Evidence from preclinical arthritis studies indicates changes in inflammatory pathways, immune-cell phenotypes and selected osteochondral endpoints, although mechanistic controls and direct joint pharmacokinetic measurements remain inconsistent. Skin insertion, carrier release and joint drug exposure represent separate experimental steps; improvement in disease scores or micro-computed tomography does not independently establish cartilage regeneration or antigen-specific tolerance. We propose a materials-design and translational evaluation framework combining chemical validation, mechanical insertion tests, drug-specific exposure accounting, mechanism-matched controls, structural outcomes, repeat-dose safety and product quality. No therapeutic human RA microneedle study was identified; clinical applications remain prospective adjuncts rather than established alternatives to systemic treatment.

title: Dynamic evolution of TiC nanoparticles into hierarchical reinforcement architecture for strengthening LPBF-fabricated GH4099 superalloy
abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) has emerged as a promising manufacturing technology for producing geometrically complex GH4099 Ni-based superalloy components. However, simultaneously achieving high strength and excellent ductility remains a major challenge. In this study, an in-situ microstructural engineering strategy was developed by controlling the hierarchical evolution of TiC particles during LPBF processing. Statistical analysis revealed that the TiC nanoparticles evolved into a multiscale reinforcement architecture comprising nanoscale, submicron, and microscale particles. This optimized hierarchical TiC distribution altered the solidification behavior by refining the columnar grain structure, weakening the crystallographic texture, increasing the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries, and promoting more uniform strain accommodation. Collectively, these synergistic microstructural modifications increased the yield strength of the as-built alloy by 40%, with nanoscale TiC precipitation accounting for 99.8% of the total σPS. This work provided new insights into the formation mechanism and strengthening effects of hierarchical TiC distributions during LPBF while offering a practical strategy for tailoring the as-built microstructure of high-performance Ni-based metal matrix composites.

title: Osteon topography-mimetic β-TCP/PCL membrane loaded with alendronate for the bidirectional regulation of guided bone regeneration
abstract: Alveolar bone resorption, a hallmark of periodontitis, stems from an inflammation-induced imbalance in bone metabolism marked by excessive osteoclastogenesis and suppressed osteogenesis. Current guided bone regeneration (GBR) membranes lack bidirectional modulation, failing to achieve synergistic pro-osteogenic and anti-osteoclastogenic effects. Here, we engineered an alendronate-loaded osteon-mimetic β-TCP/PCL membrane (ALN@M-TCP/PCL) using soft lithography and melt-casting. This membrane integrates concentric microgrooves, uniformly dispersed β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP) particles, and an alendronate (ALN) coating. The membrane exhibited a biphasic, staged release of ALN and Ca 2+ characterized by an early burst followed by sustained delivery over 3–5 weeks. In vitro, it promoted osteogenesis in MC3T3-E1 monocultures while strongly inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. In an osteoblast–osteoclast co-culture model, the membrane reshaped paracrine crosstalk: the altered secretory factors suppressed osteoclast differentiation by lowering the RANKL/OPG ratio and reciprocally stimulating osteogenesis through elevated BMP-2 and oncostatin M (OSM). In vivo, ALN@M-TCP/PCL maximized new bone volume and osteocalcin (OCN) deposition while minimizing TRAP-positive osteoclast accumulation. By coupling biomimetic topography with targeted pharmacological cues, this membrane enables bidirectional intervention in bone metabolism, offering a promising strategy for alveolar bone regeneration in osteoclast-hyperactive microenvironments.

title: Cytosine-guanine hydrogen-bonded HA/PEG dual-network hydrogels for lung cancer organoid culture and drug response evaluation
abstract: Matrigel remains the default matrix for tumor organoid culture, yet its undefined composition, batch variability, and purely elastic mechanics limit mechanistic studies of how the extracellular matrix regulates drug response. We report a chemically defined dual-network hydrogel constructed from thiolated hyaluronic acid derivatives bearing cytosine and guanine (HA-SH-HMDA-C/G) and four-arm polyethylene glycol vinyl sulfone (4-PEG-VS). Reversible cytosine-guanine base pairing, layered onto covalent thiol-vinyl sulfone crosslinks, endows the network with tunable stress relaxation while preserving structural integrity. The hybrid gel showed moderate gelation (∼15 min at 2.5% w/v), ∼40% swelling, interconnected porosity, and markedly attenuated stress relaxation (∼6.2% versus ∼ 18.9% modulus decay at 3.0% w/v over 1,000 s), and excellent cytocompatibility and hemocompatibility (hemolysis < 5%). Non-small cell lung cancer organoids (A549, PC9) in the hybrid gel matched Matrigel in morphology, growth, cytoskeletal organization, and EGFR/CD44 expression. Across four agents, 3D organoids showed significantly elevated IC50 versus 2D cultures; IC50 values were comparable to or lower than those in Matrigel, consistent with reduced drug sequestration in the defined matrix. Five patient-derived organoid lines established in the hybrid gel retained the histopathology and marker expression of matched parental tumors. This work establishes a xeno-free platform linking dynamic matrix mechanics to drug response evaluation.
